# API reference: `acme_client`

[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/acme-client.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/acme-client/)
[![Python versions](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/acme-client.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/acme-client/)
[![Docs](https://readthedocs.org/projects/acme-client/badge/?version=stable)](https://acme-client.readthedocs.io/en/stable/?badge=stable)
[![Typed](https://img.shields.io/badge/typing-PEP%20561-informational)](https://peps.python.org/pep-0561/)

This page documents the public API of `acme_client` **3.x**. Anything not listed here — every name that starts with an underscore, and the whole `acme_client._internal` package — is private and may change in a patch release. Type hints in the signatures are the source of truth: if this page and the hints disagree, the hints win and this page has a bug, so please [tell us](https://github.com/acme/acme-client-python/issues/new?template=docs.yml&labels=docs,good+first+issue&title=%5Bdocs%5D+) about it.

Module overview
---------------

| Name | Kind | Summary |
|:-----|:----:|:--------|
| [`Client`][acme_client.Client] | class | Synchronous client, thread-safe |
| [`AsyncClient`][acme_client.AsyncClient] | class | `asyncio` client with the same surface |
| [`paginate()`][acme_client.paginate] | function | Iterate over every item of a list endpoint |
| [`configure_logging()`][acme_client.configure_logging] | function | Opinionated logging setup for scripts and notebooks |
| `acme_client.errors` | module | Exception hierarchy, see [Exceptions](#exceptions) |
| `acme_client.types` | module | `TypedDict`s and enums for request/response payloads |

Install with `pip install acme-client`, or `pip install "acme-client[http2]"` to get HTTP/2 through `h2`.

## Client

```python
class acme_client.Client(
    token: str | None = None,
    *,
    base_url: str = "https://api.acme.example.com",
    timeout: float | httpx.Timeout | None = 10.0,
    max_retries: int = 3,
    user_agent: str | None = None,
    transport: httpx.BaseTransport | None = None,
    **httpx_kwargs: Any,
)
```

The main entry point. A `Client` owns a connection pool, so create one and reuse it.
Creating a client per request works, but it is slow and will eventually exhaust file
descriptors on a busy worker.[^threads]

**Parameters**

- **token** (*str \| None*) – API token. When omitted it is read from the `ACME_TOKEN`
  environment variable; if that is unset as well, [`ConfigurationError`](#exceptions) is raised.
- **base_url** (*str*) – Override for self-managed installations, e.g. `https://acme.internal.example.net`.
- **timeout** (*float \| httpx.Timeout \| None*) – Seconds, or a full `httpx.Timeout`. `None` disables timeouts completely, which you almost never want.
- **max_retries** (*int*) – Retries for idempotent requests on connection errors, `429` and `5xx` responses. Back-off is exponential with full jitter, capped at 30 s. Set max_retries to 0 to turn retries off.
- **user_agent** (*str \| None*) – Appended to the default `acme-client/3.x python/3.y` string.
- **transport** (*httpx.BaseTransport \| None*) – Custom transport; mostly useful in tests together with `httpx.MockTransport`.
- **\*\*httpx_kwargs** – Any other keyword arguments are passed straight to `httpx.Client` (for example `proxies` or `verify`).

**Raises**

- **ConfigurationError** – no token could be found, or `base_url` is not an absolute `https://` URL.

!!! tip "Use it as a context manager"
    `Client` supports `with Client() as client: ...`, which closes the pool deterministically.
    Long-running services can call [`client.close()`][acme_client.Client.close] on shutdown instead.

#### `Client.fetch(url, *, timeout=None)`

Low-level escape hatch: performs an authenticated `GET` against any path and returns the decoded JSON body.

```python
def fetch(self, url: str, *, timeout: float | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]: ...
```

Parameters
:   **url** (*str*) – Absolute URL, or a path relative to `base_url` such as `/v1/projects`.
:   **timeout** (*float \| None*) – Per-call override of the client timeout.

Returns
:   *dict[str, Any]* – the decoded JSON body.

Raises
:   [`NotFound`][acme_client.errors.NotFound] – the resource doesn't exist.
:   [`RateLimited`][acme_client.errors.RateLimited] – retries were exhausted.

#### `Client.projects.list(*, status=None, q=None, limit=20)`

Returns the first page of projects as a [`Page`][acme_client.Page]. A `Page` is iterable and has
`.has_more` and `.next_cursor`; use [`paginate()`](#paginate) when you want every item. Note that
`len(page)` is the size of *this* page only — the dunder \_\_len\_\_ never triggers a request.

```pycon
>>> from acme_client import Client
>>> client = Client(token="acme_pat_test")
>>> page = client.projects.list(status="active", limit=2)
>>> [p.name for p in page]
['Website relaunch', 'Mobile app 2.0']
>>> page.has_more
True
>>> page.next_cursor  # opaque, don't parse it
'eyJpZCI6InByal8wMUhROVpUMUFBIn0='
```

- **status** (*str \| Sequence[str] \| None*) – `"active"`, `"paused"`, `"archived"`, or several of them.
- **q** (*str \| None*) – Case-insensitive substring filter on name and slug.
- **limit** (*int*) – Page size, 1–100.

#### `Client.projects.create(name, *, slug=None, visibility="private", template_id=None, idempotency_key=None)`

Creates a project and returns a [`Project`][acme_client.types.Project].
If `idempotency_key` is not given, one is generated automatically (a UUID4) so that the built-in
retries are safe. Pass your own key if you retry at a higher level, e.g. from a task queue.

#### `Client.get_project(project_id)`

!!! warning "Deprecated since 2.3"
    Use [`client.projects.get()`][acme_client.resources.Projects.get] instead. `get_project()` will be
    removed in **4.0**. It emits a `DeprecationWarning` on every call, which Python hides by default
    unless you run with `-W default` or under pytest.

```python
# before
project = client.get_project("prj_01HV3Q4ZK8")
# after
project = client.projects.get("prj_01HV3Q4ZK8")
```

***

## AsyncClient

```python
class acme_client.AsyncClient(token: str | None = None, *, base_url: str = ..., timeout: float | httpx.Timeout | None = 10.0, max_retries: int = 3, **httpx_kwargs: Any)
```

Same parameters and the same resource namespaces as [`Client`][acme_client.Client], but every
method is a coroutine. Close it with `await client.aclose()`, or use `async with`.

```python
import asyncio
from acme_client import AsyncClient

async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncClient() as client:
        a, b = await asyncio.gather(
            client.projects.get("website-relaunch"),
            client.projects.get("mobile-app-2-0"),
        )
        print(a.status, b.status)

asyncio.run(main())
```


## Functions

### paginate

```python
def paginate(fn: Callable[..., Page[T]], /, *args: Any, page_size: int = 100, **kwargs: Any) -> Iterator[T]
```

Calls *fn* repeatedly, following `next_cursor`, and yields every item. Extra positional
arguments (\*args) and keyword arguments (\*\*kwargs) are passed to *fn* unchanged on every call — except `cursor` and `limit`, which `paginate` manages itself and will overwrite (a warning is logged if you pass them anyway).

```pycon
>>> from acme_client import paginate
>>> names = [p.name for p in paginate(client.projects.list, status="active")]
>>> len(names)
137
```

There is also `apaginate()` for [`AsyncClient`][acme_client.AsyncClient], which returns an async iterator; use it with `async for`.

### configure_logging

```python
def configure_logging(level: int | str = "INFO", *, json: bool = False, redact: bool = True) -> None
```

- **level** – passed to `logging.basicConfig`.
- **json** (*bool*) – emit one JSON object per line (handy in containers).
- **redact** (*bool*) – mask tokens and `Authorization` headers. Turning this off is only meant for local debugging; _never_ ship it.

## Exceptions

All exceptions live in `acme_client.errors` and are re-exported from the package root.

    AcmeError
     ├── ConfigurationError
     └── APIError
          ├── BadRequest           (400)
          ├── AuthenticationError  (401)
          ├── PermissionDenied     (403)
          ├── NotFound             (404)
          ├── Conflict             (409)
          ├── RateLimited          (429)
          └── ServerError          (5xx)

| Exception | HTTP status | Useful attributes | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `AcmeError` | — | | Base class; catch this if you don't care about the details |
| `ConfigurationError` | — | | Raised at construction time, never during a request |
| `APIError` | any | `.status`, `.code`, `.message`, `.request_id` | Always include `request_id` in support tickets |
| `PermissionDenied` | 403 | `.required_scope` | e.g. `"projects:write"` |
| `Conflict` | 409 | `.code` | `slug_taken`, `idempotency_key_reused`, `last_owner` |
| `RateLimited` | 429 | `.retry_after` (*float*, seconds) | Only raised once `max_retries` is exhausted |
| `ServerError` | 500–599 | | Retried automatically for idempotent requests |

```python
import time

from acme_client import Client
from acme_client.errors import Conflict, RateLimited

client = Client()
try:
    client.projects.create("Website relaunch", slug="website-relaunch")
except Conflict as exc:
    if exc.code != "slug_taken":
        raise
except RateLimited as exc:
    time.sleep(exc.retry_after)
```

## Types
`acme_client.types` contains plain `TypedDict`s (for payloads you build) and frozen dataclasses (for objects the API returns). The dataclasses accept unknown fields and keep them in `.extra`, so a newer server never breaks an older client — this is deliberate, please don't "fix" it.[^compat]

Project
:   `id`, `name`, `slug`, `status` (`ProjectStatus`), `owner` (`User`), `settings`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `archived_at`

User
:   `id`, `email`, `display_name`

ProjectStatus
:   `ACTIVE`, `PAUSED`, `ARCHIVED` — a `str` enum, so `ProjectStatus.ACTIVE == "active"` is `True`.

[^threads]: `Client` is thread-safe. `AsyncClient` is **not** safe to share between event loops.

[^compat]: The policy is written down in `CONTRIBUTING.md` under *Forward compatibility*.

    In short: the client must never raise because the server sent a field it doesn't know about,
    and enums fall back to a plain `str` for values added after the client was released.

- **timeout** (*float \| httpx.Timeout \| None*) – Seconds, or a full `httpx.Timeout`. `None` disables timeouts completely, which you almost never want.
- **max_retries** (*int*) – Retries for idempotent requests on connection errors, `429` and `5xx` responses. Back-off is exponential with full jitter, capped at 30 s. Set max_retries to 0 to turn retries off.
- **user_agent** (*str \| None*) – Appended to the default `acme-client/3.x python/3.y` string.
- **transport** (*httpx.BaseTransport \| None*) – Custom transport; mostly useful in tests together with `httpx.MockTransport`.
- **\*\*httpx_kwargs** – Any other keyword arguments are passed straight to `httpx.Client` (for example `proxies` or `verify`).

**Raises**

- **ConfigurationError** – no token could be found, or `base_url` is not an absolute `https://` URL.

!!! tip "Use it as a context manager"
    `Client` supports `with Client() as client: ...`, which closes the pool deterministically.
    Long-running services can call [`client.close()`][acme_client.Client.close] on shutdown instead.

#### `Client.fetch(url, *, timeout=None)`

Low-level escape hatch: performs an authenticated `GET` against any path and returns the decoded JSON body.

```python
def fetch(self, url: str, *, timeout: float | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]: ...
```

Parameters
:   **url** (*str*) – Absolute URL, or a path relative to `base_url` such as `/v1/projects`.
:   **timeout** (*float \| None*) – Per-call override of the client timeout.

Returns
:   *dict[str, Any]* – the decoded JSON body.

Raises
:   [`NotFound`][acme_client.errors.NotFound] – the resource doesn't exist.
:   [`RateLimited`][acme_client.errors.RateLimited] – retries were exhausted.

#### `Client.projects.list(*, status=None, q=None, limit=20)`

Returns the first page of projects as a [`Page`][acme_client.Page]. A `Page` is iterable and has
`.has_more` and `.next_cursor`; use [`paginate()`](#paginate) when you want every item. Note that
`len(page)` is the size of *this* page only — the dunder \_\_len\_\_ never triggers a request.

```pycon
>>> from acme_client import Client
>>> client = Client(token="acme_pat_test")
>>> page = client.projects.list(status="active", limit=2)
>>> [p.name for p in page]
['Website relaunch', 'Mobile app 2.0']
>>> page.has_more
True
>>> page.next_cursor  # opaque, don't parse it
'eyJpZCI6InByal8wMUhROVpUMUFBIn0='
```

- **status** (*str \| Sequence[str] \| None*) – `"active"`, `"paused"`, `"archived"`, or several of them.
- **q** (*str \| None*) – Case-insensitive substring filter on name and slug.
- **limit** (*int*) – Page size, 1–100.

#### `Client.projects.create(name, *, slug=None, visibility="private", template_id=None, idempotency_key=None)`

Creates a project and returns a [`Project`][acme_client.types.Project].
If `idempotency_key` is not given, one is generated automatically (a UUID4) so that the built-in
retries are safe. Pass your own key if you retry at a higher level, e.g. from a task queue.

#### `Client.get_project(project_id)`

!!! warning "Deprecated since 2.3"
    Use [`client.projects.get()`][acme_client.resources.Projects.get] instead. `get_project()` will be
    removed in **4.0**. It emits a `DeprecationWarning` on every call, which Python hides by default
    unless you run with `-W default` or under pytest.

```python
# before
project = client.get_project("prj_01HV3Q4ZK8")
# after
project = client.projects.get("prj_01HV3Q4ZK8")
```

***

## AsyncClient

```python
class acme_client.AsyncClient(token: str | None = None, *, base_url: str = ..., timeout: float | httpx.Timeout | None = 10.0, max_retries: int = 3, **httpx_kwargs: Any)
```

Same parameters and the same resource namespaces as [`Client`][acme_client.Client], but every
method is a coroutine. Close it with `await client.aclose()`, or use `async with`.

```python
import asyncio
from acme_client import AsyncClient

async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncClient() as client:
        a, b = await asyncio.gather(
            client.projects.get("website-relaunch"),
            client.projects.get("mobile-app-2-0"),
        )
        print(a.status, b.status)

asyncio.run(main())
```


## Functions

### paginate

```python
def paginate(fn: Callable[..., Page[T]], /, *args: Any, page_size: int = 100, **kwargs: Any) -> Iterator[T]
```

Calls *fn* repeatedly, following `next_cursor`, and yields every item. Extra positional
arguments (\*args) and keyword arguments (\*\*kwargs) are passed to *fn* unchanged on every call — except `cursor` and `limit`, which `paginate` manages itself and will overwrite (a warning is logged if you pass them anyway).

```pycon
>>> from acme_client import paginate
>>> names = [p.name for p in paginate(client.projects.list, status="active")]
>>> len(names)
137
```

There is also `apaginate()` for [`AsyncClient`][acme_client.AsyncClient], which returns an async iterator; use it with `async for`.

### configure_logging

```python
def configure_logging(level: int | str = "INFO", *, json: bool = False, redact: bool = True) -> None
```

- **level** – passed to `logging.basicConfig`.
- **json** (*bool*) – emit one JSON object per line (handy in containers).
- **redact** (*bool*) – mask tokens and `Authorization` headers. Turning this off is only meant for local debugging; _never_ ship it.

## Exceptions

All exceptions live in `acme_client.errors` and are re-exported from the package root.

    AcmeError
     ├── ConfigurationError
     └── APIError
          ├── BadRequest           (400)
          ├── AuthenticationError  (401)
          ├── PermissionDenied     (403)
          ├── NotFound             (404)
          ├── Conflict             (409)
          ├── RateLimited          (429)
          └── ServerError          (5xx)

| Exception | HTTP status | Useful attributes | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `AcmeError` | — | | Base class; catch this if you don't care about the details |
| `ConfigurationError` | — | | Raised at construction time, never during a request |
| `APIError` | any | `.status`, `.code`, `.message`, `.request_id` | Always include `request_id` in support tickets |
| `PermissionDenied` | 403 | `.required_scope` | e.g. `"projects:write"` |
| `Conflict` | 409 | `.code` | `slug_taken`, `idempotency_key_reused`, `last_owner` |
| `RateLimited` | 429 | `.retry_after` (*float*, seconds) | Only raised once `max_retries` is exhausted |
| `ServerError` | 500–599 | | Retried automatically for idempotent requests |

```python
import time

from acme_client import Client
from acme_client.errors import Conflict, RateLimited

client = Client()
try:
    client.projects.create("Website relaunch", slug="website-relaunch")
except Conflict as exc:
    if exc.code != "slug_taken":
        raise
except RateLimited as exc:
    time.sleep(exc.retry_after)
```

## Types
`acme_client.types` contains plain `TypedDict`s (for payloads you build) and frozen dataclasses (for objects the API returns). The dataclasses accept unknown fields and keep them in `.extra`, so a newer server never breaks an older client — this is deliberate, please don't "fix" it.[^compat]

Project
:   `id`, `name`, `slug`, `status` (`ProjectStatus`), `owner` (`User`), `settings`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `archived_at`

User
:   `id`, `email`, `display_name`

ProjectStatus
:   `ACTIVE`, `PAUSED`, `ARCHIVED` — a `str` enum, so `ProjectStatus.ACTIVE == "active"` is `True`.

[^threads]: `Client` is thread-safe. `AsyncClient` is **not** safe to share between event loops.

[^compat]: The policy is written down in `CONTRIBUTING.md` under *Forward compatibility*.

    In short: the client must never raise because the server sent a field it doesn't know about,
    and enums fall back to a plain `str` for values added after the client was released.

---
# roles/nginx/tasks/main.yml
#
# Installs + configures nginx (distro package OR source build), drops the vhosts,
# hardens a couple of defaults and makes sure the thing actually answers on :80.
#
# Owner: web-platform (ping #ops-web before touching the vhost logic, it is load-bearing)
# NOTE: handlers live in ../handlers/main.yml -- "reload nginx" runs `nginx -t` first.


- name: Include OS-specific variables
  include_vars: "{{ item }}"
  with_first_found:
    - "{{ ansible_distribution | lower }}-{{ ansible_distribution_major_version }}.yml"
    - "{{ ansible_os_family | lower }}.yml"
    - default.yml
  tags: [ nginx,config ]

- name: Include OS-specific install tasks (RedHat / Suse live in their own files)
  include_tasks: "{{ ansible_os_family | lower }}.yml"
  when: not nginx_install_from_source | bool
  tags:
  - nginx
  - packages


- name:    Install nginx and helper packages
  ansible.builtin.package:
     name: "{{ item }}"
     state: present
  loop:
     - nginx
     - "{{ 'python3-passlib' if nginx_basic_auth_users | length > 0 else 'python3' }}"
     - logrotate
     # ssl-cert gives us the snakeoil pair for the catch-all vhost
     - ssl-cert
  when:
    - not nginx_install_from_source | bool
    - ansible_os_family == 'Debian'
  register: nginx_pkg_result
  until: nginx_pkg_result is succeeded
  retries: 3
  delay: 10
  tags: [ nginx, packages ]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source build -- only the edge boxes need brotli + headers-more.
# FIXME(jk): move this into its own role, it is getting out of hand
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
- name: Build nginx from source
  when:
    - nginx_install_from_source | bool
    - ansible_distribution_major_version is version('20', '>=')
  tags: ['nginx', "source-build"]
  block:
    -   name: Install build dependencies
        apt:
          name: "{{ nginx_build_deps }}"
          state: present
          update_cache: yes
          cache_valid_time: 3600

    -   name: Download nginx {{ nginx_source_version }} tarball
        get_url:
          url: "https://nginx.org/download/nginx-{{ nginx_source_version }}.tar.gz"
          dest: /usr/local/src/nginx-{{ nginx_source_version }}.tar.gz
          checksum: "sha256:{{ nginx_source_sha256 }}"
          mode: 0644

    -   name: Unpack source
        unarchive:
          src: /usr/local/src/nginx-{{ nginx_source_version }}.tar.gz
          dest: /usr/local/src/
          remote_src: yes
          creates: /usr/local/src/nginx-{{ nginx_source_version }}/configure

    -   name: Configure and compile (takes ~6 min on the t3.small boxes, be patient)
        shell: >-
          ./configure --prefix=/etc/nginx --sbin-path=/usr/sbin/nginx
          --modules-path=/usr/lib/nginx/modules --conf-path=/etc/nginx/nginx.conf
          --with-http_ssl_module --with-http_v2_module --with-http_realip_module
          {% for mod in nginx_extra_modules %}--add-dynamic-module=/usr/local/src/{{ mod }} {% endfor %}
          && make -j{{ ansible_processor_vcpus | default(2) }}
          && make install
        args:
          chdir: /usr/local/src/nginx-{{ nginx_source_version }}
          creates: /usr/sbin/nginx

  rescue:
    - name: Source build failed - grab the tail of autoconf.err
      command: tail -n 50 /usr/local/src/nginx-{{ nginx_source_version }}/objs/autoconf.err
      register: nginx_autoconf_err
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: false

    - name: Fail loudly
      fail:
        msg: "nginx source build failed on {{ inventory_hostname }}: {{ nginx_autoconf_err.stdout_lines | default([]) | join(' / ') }}"

  always:
  - name: Clean up the build tree
    file:
      path: /usr/local/src/nginx-{{ nginx_source_version }}
      state: absent
    when: nginx_cleanup_build_dir | default(true)


- name: Ensure config directories exist
  file:
    path: "{{ item.path }}"
    state: directory
    owner: root
    group: "{{ item.group | default('root') }}"
    mode: "{{ item.mode | default('0755') }}"
  loop:
  - { path: /etc/nginx/conf.d }
  - { path: /etc/nginx/sites-available }
  - { path: /etc/nginx/sites-enabled }
  - { path: /etc/nginx/snippets }
  - { path: "{{ nginx_log_dir }}", group: adm, mode: '0750' }
  - {path: /var/cache/nginx,mode: "0700"}
  loop_control:
    label: "{{ item.path }}"

- name: Check whether somebody dropped a hand-edited nginx.conf.local
  stat:
    path: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf.local
  register: nginx_local_conf

- name: Render main nginx.conf
  template:
    src: nginx.conf.j2
    dest: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: 0644
    backup: yes
    validate: 'nginx -t -c %s'
  when: not nginx_local_conf.stat.exists   # hand-edited -> leave it alone (see #1182)
  notify: reload nginx
  tags: [ nginx,config ]

- name:   Hide nginx version in error pages and the Server header
  lineinfile:
    path: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
    regexp: '^#?\s*server_tokens'
    line: "    server_tokens off;"
    insertafter: '^http \{'
    state: present
  notify: reload nginx
      # ^ only really matters for the source build, the template already sets it

- name: Deploy vhost configs
  template:
    src: "{{ item.template | default('vhost.conf.j2') }}"
    dest: "/etc/nginx/sites-available/{{ item.server_name }}.conf"
    mode: '0644'
  loop: "{{ nginx_vhosts }}"
  loop_control: { label: "{{ item.server_name }}" }
  when: item.state | default('present') == 'present'
  notify: reload nginx
  tags:
    - nginx
    - vhosts

- name: Enable vhosts
  file:
    src: /etc/nginx/sites-available/{{ item.server_name }}.conf
    dest: /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/{{ item.server_name }}.conf
    state: link
  loop: "{{ nginx_vhosts }}"
  loop_control: { label: "{{ item.server_name }}" }
  when:
  - item.enabled | default(true) | bool
  - item.state | default('present') == 'present'
  notify: reload nginx

- name: Remove distro default site
  file:
    path: "{{ item }}"
    state: absent
  with_items:
    - /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default
    - /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
  when: nginx_remove_default_vhost
  notify: reload nginx

- name: Write upstreams.conf
  copy:
    dest: /etc/nginx/conf.d/upstreams.conf
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0644"
    content: |
      # {{ ansible_managed }}
      # generated from nginx_upstreams -- do NOT edit on the box
      {% for up in nginx_upstreams %}
      upstream {{ up.name }} {
      {%   if up.strategy is defined %}
          {{ up.strategy }};
      {%   endif %}
      {%   for srv in up.servers %}
          server {{ srv }}{% if up.max_fails is defined %} max_fails={{ up.max_fails }}{% endif %};
      {%   endfor %}
          keepalive {{ up.keepalive | default(32) }};
      }

      {% endfor %}
  notify:
    - validate nginx config
    - reload nginx

- name: Create htpasswd files for the basic-auth protected vhosts
  community.general.htpasswd:
    path: /etc/nginx/.htpasswd-{{ item.0.name }}
    name: "{{ item.1.user }}"
    password: "{{ item.1.password }}"
    owner: root
    group: www-data
    mode: 0640
  loop: "{{ nginx_basic_auth_users | subelements('users') }}"
  loop_control:
     label: "{{ item.0.name }}/{{ item.1.user }}"
  no_log: TRUE

- name: Logrotate config
  template: src=logrotate.j2 dest=/etc/logrotate.d/nginx owner=root group=root mode=0644

- name: Open 80/443 in ufw
  ufw:
    rule: allow
    port: "{{ item }}"
    proto: tcp
    comment:
  loop: [ '80', '443' ]
  when: nginx_manage_firewall | default(false)

- name: Remind people about the manual cert step
  debug:
    msg: Certificates for the public vhosts are issued by cert-manager on the k8s ingress, NOT here; this role only installs snakeoil certs for the catch-all.
  when: nginx_show_cert_reminder | default(false)

- name: Make sure nginx is enabled and running
  service:
    name: nginx
    state: started
    enabled: yes

# Flush handlers here so the health check below hits the *new* config.
- meta: flush_handlers

- name: Sanity-check the rendered config
  assert:
    that: [
        "nginx_worker_connections | int >= 1024",
        "nginx_vhosts | length > 0",
        "nginx_client_max_body_size is match('^[0-9]+[kKmMgG]?$')"
      ]
    fail_msg: "nginx_worker_connections too low or no vhosts defined for {{ inventory_hostname }} - check group_vars/web.yml"
    success_msg: All good
    quiet: true

- name: Health check - catch-all vhost answers
  uri:
    url: "http://127.0.0.1:{{ nginx_listen_port | default(80) }}/nginx-health"
    status_code: [200, 204]
    return_content: no
  register: nginx_health
  until: nginx_health.status in [200, 204]
  retries: 5
  delay: 3
  changed_when: false
  tags: [ nginx , healthcheck ]

          url: "https://nginx.org/download/nginx-{{ nginx_source_version }}.tar.gz"
          dest: /usr/local/src/nginx-{{ nginx_source_version }}.tar.gz
          checksum: "sha256:{{ nginx_source_sha256 }}"
          mode: 0644

    -   name: Unpack source
        unarchive:
          src: /usr/local/src/nginx-{{ nginx_source_version }}.tar.gz
          dest: /usr/local/src/
          remote_src: yes
          creates: /usr/local/src/nginx-{{ nginx_source_version }}/configure

    -   name: Configure and compile (takes ~6 min on the t3.small boxes, be patient)
        shell: >-
          ./configure --prefix=/etc/nginx --sbin-path=/usr/sbin/nginx
          --modules-path=/usr/lib/nginx/modules --conf-path=/etc/nginx/nginx.conf
          --with-http_ssl_module --with-http_v2_module --with-http_realip_module
          {% for mod in nginx_extra_modules %}--add-dynamic-module=/usr/local/src/{{ mod }} {% endfor %}
          && make -j{{ ansible_processor_vcpus | default(2) }}
          && make install
        args:
          chdir: /usr/local/src/nginx-{{ nginx_source_version }}
          creates: /usr/sbin/nginx

  rescue:
    - name: Source build failed - grab the tail of autoconf.err
      command: tail -n 50 /usr/local/src/nginx-{{ nginx_source_version }}/objs/autoconf.err
      register: nginx_autoconf_err
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: false

    - name: Fail loudly
      fail:
        msg: "nginx source build failed on {{ inventory_hostname }}: {{ nginx_autoconf_err.stdout_lines | default([]) | join(' / ') }}"

  always:
  - name: Clean up the build tree
    file:
      path: /usr/local/src/nginx-{{ nginx_source_version }}
      state: absent
    when: nginx_cleanup_build_dir | default(true)


- name: Ensure config directories exist
  file:
    path: "{{ item.path }}"
    state: directory
    owner: root
    group: "{{ item.group | default('root') }}"
    mode: "{{ item.mode | default('0755') }}"
  loop:
  - { path: /etc/nginx/conf.d }
  - { path: /etc/nginx/sites-available }
  - { path: /etc/nginx/sites-enabled }
  - { path: /etc/nginx/snippets }
  - { path: "{{ nginx_log_dir }}", group: adm, mode: '0750' }
  - {path: /var/cache/nginx,mode: "0700"}
  loop_control:
    label: "{{ item.path }}"

- name: Check whether somebody dropped a hand-edited nginx.conf.local
  stat:
    path: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf.local
  register: nginx_local_conf

- name: Render main nginx.conf
  template:
    src: nginx.conf.j2
    dest: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: 0644
    backup: yes
    validate: 'nginx -t -c %s'
  when: not nginx_local_conf.stat.exists   # hand-edited -> leave it alone (see #1182)
  notify: reload nginx
  tags: [ nginx,config ]

- name:   Hide nginx version in error pages and the Server header
  lineinfile:
    path: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
    regexp: '^#?\s*server_tokens'
    line: "    server_tokens off;"
    insertafter: '^http \{'
    state: present
  notify: reload nginx
      # ^ only really matters for the source build, the template already sets it

- name: Deploy vhost configs
  template:
    src: "{{ item.template | default('vhost.conf.j2') }}"
    dest: "/etc/nginx/sites-available/{{ item.server_name }}.conf"
    mode: '0644'
  loop: "{{ nginx_vhosts }}"
  loop_control: { label: "{{ item.server_name }}" }
  when: item.state | default('present') == 'present'
  notify: reload nginx
  tags:
    - nginx
    - vhosts

- name: Enable vhosts
  file:
    src: /etc/nginx/sites-available/{{ item.server_name }}.conf
    dest: /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/{{ item.server_name }}.conf
    state: link
  loop: "{{ nginx_vhosts }}"
  loop_control: { label: "{{ item.server_name }}" }
  when:
  - item.enabled | default(true) | bool
  - item.state | default('present') == 'present'
  notify: reload nginx

- name: Remove distro default site
  file:
    path: "{{ item }}"
    state: absent
  with_items:
    - /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default
    - /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
  when: nginx_remove_default_vhost
  notify: reload nginx

- name: Write upstreams.conf
  copy:
    dest: /etc/nginx/conf.d/upstreams.conf
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0644"
    content: |
      # {{ ansible_managed }}
      # generated from nginx_upstreams -- do NOT edit on the box
      {% for up in nginx_upstreams %}
      upstream {{ up.name }} {
      {%   if up.strategy is defined %}
          {{ up.strategy }};
      {%   endif %}
      {%   for srv in up.servers %}
          server {{ srv }}{% if up.max_fails is defined %} max_fails={{ up.max_fails }}{% endif %};
      {%   endfor %}
          keepalive {{ up.keepalive | default(32) }};
      }

      {% endfor %}
  notify:
    - validate nginx config
    - reload nginx

- name: Create htpasswd files for the basic-auth protected vhosts
  community.general.htpasswd:
    path: /etc/nginx/.htpasswd-{{ item.0.name }}
    name: "{{ item.1.user }}"
    password: "{{ item.1.password }}"
    owner: root
    group: www-data
    mode: 0640
  loop: "{{ nginx_basic_auth_users | subelements('users') }}"
  loop_control:
     label: "{{ item.0.name }}/{{ item.1.user }}"
  no_log: TRUE

- name: Logrotate config
  template: src=logrotate.j2 dest=/etc/logrotate.d/nginx owner=root group=root mode=0644

- name: Open 80/443 in ufw
  ufw:
    rule: allow
    port: "{{ item }}"
    proto: tcp
    comment:
  loop: [ '80', '443' ]
  when: nginx_manage_firewall | default(false)

- name: Remind people about the manual cert step
  debug:
    msg: Certificates for the public vhosts are issued by cert-manager on the k8s ingress, NOT here; this role only installs snakeoil certs for the catch-all.
  when: nginx_show_cert_reminder | default(false)

- name: Make sure nginx is enabled and running
  service:
    name: nginx
    state: started
    enabled: yes

# Flush handlers here so the health check below hits the *new* config.
- meta: flush_handlers

- name: Sanity-check the rendered config
  assert:
    that: [
        "nginx_worker_connections | int >= 1024",
        "nginx_vhosts | length > 0",
        "nginx_client_max_body_size is match('^[0-9]+[kKmMgG]?$')"
      ]
    fail_msg: "nginx_worker_connections too low or no vhosts defined for {{ inventory_hostname }} - check group_vars/web.yml"
    success_msg: All good
    quiet: true

- name: Health check - catch-all vhost answers
  uri:
    url: "http://127.0.0.1:{{ nginx_listen_port | default(80) }}/nginx-health"
    status_code: [200, 204]
    return_content: no
  register: nginx_health
  until: nginx_health.status in [200, 204]
  retries: 5
  delay: 3
  changed_when: false
  tags: [ nginx , healthcheck ]

# group_vars/all.yml

# Last big cleanup: 2024-02 (jk) -- dropped the CentOS 7 leftovers.


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- app ---
app_name:     acme
app_version:  1.10        # FIXME: YAML reads this as the float 1.1 -> artifact URL 404s. Quote it!! (see #2210)
app_build: "1.10.4+build.317"
app_user: "{{ app_name }}"
app_group:    "{{ app_name }}"
app_home: "/opt/{{ app_name }}"
app_port: 8080
app_admin_port:   8081
app_env: production
app_debug: no
app_log_level: "info"
app_max_open_files: 1e5          # TODO: check the template renders 100000 and not 100000.0
app_feature_mask: 0x1F
app_umask: 0027
backup_window: 02:30             # HH:MM local time, consumed by the backup role
app_description: Acme order management backend, deployed as a single fat jar behind nginx
  with a local postgres replica for the read-heavy reporting queries.
deploy_notify_message: "Deployed {{ app_name }} {{ app_build }} to {{ app_env }} by {{ lookup('env', 'USER') | default('ci', true) }} - details at https://ci.acme.example/job/acme-deploy/"

app_logs:
  - name: app
    path: "{{ app_home }}/logs/app.log"
    rotate: 14
  - name: access
    path: "{{ app_home }}/logs/access.log"
    rotate: 30
    compress: yes
  - name: gc
    path: "{{ app_home }}/logs/gc.log"
    rotate: 5
    size: 100M
    compress: off


# JVM. Heap = half the RAM but never above 8g (G1 pauses get ugly above that on our boxes)
java_home: /usr/lib/jvm/temurin-17-jdk-amd64
java_opts: >-
  -Xms512m
  -Xmx{{ [ (ansible_memtotal_mb * 0.5) | int, 8192 ] | min }}m
  -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200
  -Xlog:gc*:file={{ app_home }}/logs/gc.log:time,uptime:filecount=5,filesize=20m
  -Djava.security.egd=file:/dev/./urandom
  -Dspring.profiles.active={{ app_env }}

# ------------------------------------------------------------- users ---
admin_users:
    jkowalski:
        uid: 2001
        shell: /bin/zsh
        groups: [ sudo,adm, docker ]
        ssh_keys:
            - "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIHk2b1m3Jx0rRk3pWqYlq7Cq0yWmXo8k1JqD2y7vS3aB jk@laptop"
            - "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIM1e9fQ2z8kQwVf3mY0bS5aC9xTnL4pH7rJdW2eGk6uE jk@yubikey"
    mnguyen:
        uid: 2002
        shell: /bin/bash
        groups:
        - sudo
        - docker
        ssh_keys:
        - ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAADAQABAAABgQC7xZ9mR4pT2wL8kV1nB6cY3hJ5sD0fG8aQ2eW4rT6yU9iO1pL3kJ7hG5fD2sA4qW6eR8tY0uI2oP4aS6dF8gH0jK2lZ4xC6vB8nM0= mnguyen@acme
        state: present
    ops-bot:
        uid: 2100
        shell: /usr/sbin/nologin     # deploy key only, no interactive logins
        groups: []
        ssh_keys: []
    old-contractor:
        state: absent
        uid: ~
        # remove this entry once the account is gone everywhere (`getent passwd old-contractor`)

# ---------------------------------------------------------- firewall ---
firewall_enabled: yes
firewall_default_policy: deny
firewall_rules:
  - { port: 22, proto: tcp, from: "10.20.0.0/16", comment: "ssh from the VPN range only" }

   net.core.somaxconn: 4096

   net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse: 1
   vm.swappiness: 10

   fs.inotify.max_user_watches: 524288
   kernel.panic: 10
   net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6: "{{ 0 if enable_ipv6 | bool else 1 }}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------- secrets ---
db_host: db-primary.internal.acme.example
db_port: 5432
db_name: "{{ app_name }}_prod"
db_user: "{{ app_name }}"
db_password: !vault |
          $ANSIBLE_VAULT;1.1;AES256
          62313365396662343061393464336163383764373764613633653634306231386433626436623361
          6134333665353966363534333632666535333761666131620a663537646436643839616531643561
          63396265333966386166373632626539326166353965363262633030333630313338646538316634
          3061366335303633310a376465386366643230616565336436383462363635303730316535346539
          3135
smtp_relay: smtp.eu.mailgun.org:587
smtp_user: postmaster@mg.acme.example
smtp_password: !vault |
          $ANSIBLE_VAULT;1.1;AES256
          39386537643830306563383365343736353065653965383363613232613133623335336336373962
          3637363562316132366634366134373331333062646263370a346133663039376131353235646136
          61366266663463393934303736663734323266636231343737393838633363313966633161626365
          6466373839653134630a323733356163626234313139656565623432336538633034393565656630
          6438

# -------------------------------------------------------- time / net ---
timezone: Etc/UTC
ntp_servers: [ 0.de.pool.ntp.org, 1.de.pool.ntp.org,2.de.pool.ntp.org ]
ntp_fallback_servers: [
    time.cloudflare.com,
    "time.google.com"
  ]
enable_ipv6: no
selinux_state: permissive
proxy_env: { http_proxy: ~, https_proxy: ~,no_proxy: "localhost,127.0.0.1,.internal.acme.example" }
swap_size_mb: null      # null = no swap file; set e.g. 2048 on the tiny staging boxes
dns_search_domains:
- internal.acme.example
- acme.example
packages_extra: []
packages_absent:
  - telnet
  - rsh-client
  - nis

motd_banner: |+
  ****************************************************************
   {{ inventory_hostname }} ({{ app_env | upper }})
   Managed by Ansible - manual changes WILL be overwritten.
   Questions: #ops-help on Slack, runbooks at https://runbooks.acme.example
  ****************************************************************


# --------------------------------------------------------- logrotate ---
logrotate_config: |
  # {{ ansible_managed }}
  {% for log in app_logs %}
  {{ log.path }} {
      {{ 'daily' if log.size is not defined else 'size ' ~ log.size }}
      rotate {{ log.rotate | default(7) }}
      missingok
      notifempty
  {% if log.compress | default(true) | bool %}
      compress
      delaycompress
  {% endif %}
      copytruncate
      su {{ app_user }} {{ app_group }}
  }
  {% endfor %}

# -------------------------------------------------------- monitoring ---
monitoring_cidr: 10.20.9.0/24
node_exporter_version: 1.7.0
node_exporter_enabled_collectors: [systemd , processes, "textfile"]
node_exporter_textfile_dir: /var/lib/node_exporter/textfile
promtail_enabled: TRUE
promtail_loki_url: "https://loki.monitoring.acme.example/loki/api/v1/push"
promtail_extra_labels:
  env: "{{ app_env }}"
  dc: fra1
  role:
  team: 'platform'

---
# roles/nginx/handlers/main.yml
#
# Handler ORDER matters: Ansible runs handlers in the order they are DEFINED in this
# file, not in the order they were notified. So keep it like this:
#   1. validate config         (fail the play before we reload a broken config)
#   2. reload systemd          (unit files changed)
#   3. restart / reload nginx  (+ php-fpm)
#   4. restart app, then wait for it
#
# Need a handler to fire mid-play? Put
#     - meta: flush_handlers
# in the tasks (tasks/main.yml does exactly that right before the health check).


- name: validate nginx config
  command: nginx -t
  changed_when: false
  listen: "validate web config"

- name: reload systemd
  ansible.builtin.systemd:
    daemon_reload: yes


# legacy k=v style -- the old site.yml playbooks still notify "restart nginx", leave it
- name: restart nginx
  service: name=nginx state=restarted
  listen: "restart web stack"

- name: reload nginx
  ansible.builtin.systemd:
      name: nginx
      state: reloaded
  when: nginx_service_enabled | default(true) | bool
  listen:
    - "reload web stack"
    - nginx config changed

-   name:  restart php-fpm
    service:
        name: "php{{ php_version }}-fpm"
        state: restarted
    when: php_enabled | default(false)
    listen: restart web stack

- name: restart postgresql
  service:
    name: postgresql
    state: restarted
  throttle: 1          # one node at a time, the replicas need to catch up
  # run_once: true     # NO. that only restarted the first host -- see INC-2291
  listen: [ "restart db" ,  postgres config changed ]

- name: reload postgresql
  become: yes
  become_user: postgres
  command: "pg_ctlcluster {{ postgresql_version }} main reload"
  changed_when: True

- name: restart app
  systemd:
    name: "{{ app_name }}"
    state: restarted
    daemon_reload: no
  listen:
  - restart app stack
  - "app config changed"

- name: wait for app
  wait_for:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: "{{ app_port }}"
    delay: 5
    timeout: 120
    state: started
    msg: "{{ app_name }} did not come back on port {{ app_port }} within 120s - check `journalctl -u {{ app_name }} -n 200`"
  listen: restart app stack



- name: restart rsyslog
  service: name=rsyslog state=restarted

- name: reload firewall
  command: ufw reload
  when: firewall_enabled | default(true)
  # changed_when: false   <- deliberately left out so it shows up in the recap

- name: restart node_exporter
  service:
    name: node_exporter
    state: restarted
  when:      # TODO(mn): node_exporter_enabled | bool once every host has the var

- name: clear nginx cache
  file:
    path: /var/cache/nginx/proxy_temp/
    state: absent
  notify: restart nginx   # handlers CAN notify other handlers (ansible >= 2.2)

- name: restart haproxy
  service: { name: haproxy, state: restarted }
  when: "'lb' in group_names"
  listen:   restart web stack

  # NOTE: there is intentionally no "restart docker" handler here. Restarting
  # dockerd on the web boxes kills the sidecars; do it by hand in a maintenance window.
...

# acmectl CLI reference #

[![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/acme/acmectl?sort=semver&display_name=tag)](https://github.com/acme/acmectl/releases/latest) [![Homebrew](https://img.shields.io/homebrew/v/acmectl)](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/acmectl) [![Scoop](https://img.shields.io/scoop/v/acmectl?bucket=extras)](https://scoop.sh/#/apps?q=acmectl&s=0&d=1&o=true)

`acmectl` is the command-line client for the Acme platform. This page is the complete
reference for **acmectl 3.4**. The same text is available offline via
`acmectl help <command>`, and as `man acmectl-<command>` if you installed the
Homebrew or `.deb` package.

## Synopsis

```text
acmectl [global flags] <command> [<subcommand>] [flags] [args...]
```

Commands at a glance:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`login`](#acmectl-login) / `logout` | Authenticate against an Acme host |
| [`deploy`](#acmectl-deploy) | Roll out a new revision of a service |
| [`logs`](#acmectl-logs) | Stream or search service logs |
| [`projects`](#acmectl-projects) | List, create and archive projects |
| [`config`](#acmectl-config) | Read and write CLI configuration |
| [`completion`](#shell-completion) | Generate shell completion scripts |

## Global flags
Global flags are accepted by every command. They _should_ come before the command name (`acmectl -o json projects list`); putting them after the command works for most commands, but not all of them.[^order]

`-c`, `--config <path>`
:   Path to the config file. Default: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/acme/config.toml`, falling back to `~/.config/acme/config.toml` (or `%APPDATA%\acme\config.toml` on Windows).

`-p`, `--profile <name>`
:   Profile from the config file to use. Overrides `ACME_PROFILE`.

`-o`, `--output <format>`
:   One of `table` (the default when stdout is a terminal), `json` (the default otherwise), `yaml`, `jsonl`, `name`, or `template=<go template>`. With `template=` you get the full Go `text/template` language plus the [Sprig](https://masterminds.github.io/sprig/) function library, e.g. `-o 'template={{range .}}{{.id}}{{"\t"}}{{.name | upper}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}'`, which is powerful, occasionally baffling, and the main reason the much simpler `name` format exists at all — if all you need is IDs for a shell loop, use `-o name`.

`-v`, `--verbose`
:   Increase log verbosity. Repeat it for more: `-vv` logs every HTTP request, `-vvv` also logs bodies (with tokens redacted).

`-q`, `--quiet`
:   Only print errors.

`--no-color`
:   Disable ANSI colours. `NO_COLOR=1` is honoured too.

`--timeout <duration>`
:   Network timeout such as `30s` or `2m`. Default: `60s`.

## acmectl login

```text
acmectl login [--token-stdin] [--sso] [--host <url>]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|:-----|:-------:|:------------|
| `--token-stdin` | `false` | Read a personal access token from stdin instead of opening a browser |
| `--sso` | `false` | Use the SSO device-code flow |
| `--host` | `https://api.acme.example.com` | API host, for self-managed installations |

1. Interactive login (opens your browser):

   ```console
   $ acmectl login
   ! First copy your one-time code: 4F2A-9C1B
   Press Enter to open acme.example.com in your browser...
   ✓ Logged in as lea.moreau (profile "default")
   ```

2. In CI, with the token stored as a secret:

   ```bash
   echo "$ACME_TOKEN" | acmectl login --token-stdin --host https://acme.corp.example.net
   ```

`acmectl logout` removes the stored credentials for the current profile. Add `--all` to remove every profile's credentials.

## acmectl deploy

```text
acmectl deploy [flags] <service> [<image>]
acmectl deploy status <service>
acmectl deploy promote <service>
acmectl deploy rollback <service> [--to <revision>]
```

Deploys a new revision of `<service>`. When `<image>` is omitted the image of the current revision is reused, which is handy for config-only changes. The command waits until the rollout is healthy (or `--timeout` passes) and streams events in the meantime; press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> to stop watching — the rollout itself carries on in the background, and `acmectl deploy status <service>` picks it up again.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
|------|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--env` | `-e` | string | `staging` | Target environment |
| `--set` | | `key=value`, repeatable | | Override a config value; nested keys use dots, e.g. `--set 'db.pool.max=20'` |
| `--set-file` | | `key=path` | | Like `--set`, but reads the value from a file |
| `--strategy` | | `rolling\|blue-green\|canary` | `rolling` | Rollout strategy |
| `--canary-weight` | | int | `10` | Percentage of traffic sent to the canary |
| `--wait` | | bool | `true` | Wait for the rollout to finish |
| `--dry-run` | | `none\|client\|server` | `none` | Validate without applying anything |

Examples:

1. Deploy a specific image to production:

   ```bash
   acmectl deploy -e production checkout ghcr.io/acme/checkout:1.42.0
   ```

2. Canary with 5% of the traffic, then promote it:

   ```bash
   acmectl deploy checkout --strategy canary --canary-weight 5
   acmectl deploy promote checkout
   ```

3. Change a setting without building a new image:

   ```bash
   acmectl deploy checkout \
     --set 'feature_flags.new_cart=true' \
     --set-file 'tls.cert=./certs/checkout.pem'
   ```

## acmectl logs

```text
acmectl logs <service> [-f] [--since <duration>] [--grep <regex>] [--instance <id>]
```

`-f`, `--follow`
:   Keep streaming new lines until interrupted.

`--since <duration>`
:   Only show lines newer than this (`10m`, `2h`, `1d`). Default: `15m`.

`--grep <regex>`
:   RE2 syntax. Case-sensitive unless you prefix the pattern with `(?i)`.

`--instance <id>`
:   Only one instance; get the IDs from `acmectl deploy status`.

## acmectl projects

```text
acmectl projects list    [--status active|paused|archived] [--limit N]
acmectl projects create  <name> [--visibility private|internal]
acmectl projects archive <project>
```

Here `|` means "one of" — it's not a shell pipe :)

## acmectl config

`acmectl config get <key>`, `acmectl config set <key> <value>` and `acmectl config list`. Keys use dots (`defaults.env`, `output.color`). Unknown keys are rejected unless you pass `--force`, so that typos don't silently create settings that do nothing.

## Shell completion

=== "bash"

    ```bash
    acmectl completion bash | sudo tee /etc/bash_completion.d/acmectl > /dev/null
    ```

=== "zsh"

    ```zsh
    acmectl completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_acmectl"
    autoload -U compinit && compinit
    ```

=== "fish"

    ```fish
    acmectl completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/acmectl.fish
    ```

=== "PowerShell"

    ```powershell
    acmectl completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
    ```

Restart your shell afterwards.[^completion]

## Environment variables

| Variable | Equivalent flag | Notes |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `ACME_TOKEN` | — | Takes precedence over stored credentials; handy in CI |
| `ACME_HOST` | `--host` | |
| `ACME_PROFILE` | `--profile` | |
| `ACME_OUTPUT` | `--output` | |
| `ACME_CONFIG` | `--config` | |
| `NO_COLOR` | `--no-color` | Any non-empty value |
| `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` | | Standard proxy variables, see <https://pkg.go.dev/net/http#ProxyFromEnvironment> |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|-----:|:--------|
| 0 | Success |
| 1 | Generic error |
| 2 | Invalid usage (unknown flag, missing argument) |
| 3 | Not authenticated, or the token expired |
| 4 | Resource not found |
| 5 | Conflict, e.g. a deployment is already in progress |
| 10 | Rollout failed its health checks and was rolled back |
| 124 | Timed out waiting (see `--timeout`) |
| 130 | Interrupted with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> |

[^order]: Since 3.2, `deploy`, `logs` and `projects` accept global flags anywhere on the line; `config` and `completion` still don't, because their arguments are passed through verbatim.
[^completion]: The system bash 3.2 on macOS is not supported. Install bash 5 with Homebrew (`brew install bash bash-completion@2`).

# dotfiles #

my dotfiles. there are many like them, but these ones are mine :)

Managed with [GNU Stow](https://www.gnu.org/software/stow/) because I tried chezmoi
and yadm and the bare-repo-with-an-alias trick and kept coming back to the simplest thing.
Mostly Arch on the desktop, macOS on the work laptop, the
occasional Debian VPS. Things are *supposed* to work on all three but no
promises — PRs welcome, issues less so.

![screenshot of my desktop](img/desktop-2024.png "sway + waybar + foot, gruvbox-ish")

***

## what's in here ##

* `zsh/` — zshrc, aliases, a handful of functions
* `fish/` — I keep switching back and forth, don't judge
+ `nvim/` — neovim config, lua, lazy.nvim
+ `tmux/`
* `git/` — gitconfig with delta as the pager, global gitignore
* `sway/`, `waybar/`, `foot/`, `mako/` (linux only)
* `bin/` — random scripts. some of them are terrible.
    * `bin/wttr` — weather in the terminal
    * `bin/gc-branches` — deletes merged branches, asks first
    + `bin/ocr-screenshot` — grim + slurp + tesseract, surprisingly useful

## install ##

1) clone it somewhere. I use `~/.dotfiles`:

        git clone --recursive https://github.com/jdoe/dotfiles.git ~/.dotfiles

2) install stow (`pacman -S stow` / `brew install stow` / `apt install stow`)
3) stow whatever you want:

```sh
cd ~/.dotfiles
stow -v zsh git nvim tmux
# linux only
stow -v sway waybar foot mako
```

4) open nvim once and let lazy.nvim do its thing. it'll complain about a missing
   `stylua` — ignore it or `cargo install stylua`

thats it. there's also a `bootstrap.sh` that does all of the above *and* installs
packages, but read it first, it __will__ overwrite things.

    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jdoe/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | less
    # if you're brave:
    # curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jdoe/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | sh

___

## shell

zsh with no framework (oh-my-zsh made startup take 600ms, now it's ~40ms).
the prompt is [starship](https://starship.rs). history is shared between sessions,
deduped, and 100k lines long because disk is cheap.

some aliases I actually use:

```sh
alias g='git'
alias gs='git status -sb'
alias ll='eza -lah --git --group-directories-first'
alias k='kubectl'
alias please='sudo $(fc -ln -1)'   # :^)
```

the fish config is roughly equivalent:

```fish
abbr -a g git
abbr -a gs 'git status -sb'
function mkcd --description 'mkdir + cd'
    mkdir -p $argv[1]; and cd $argv[1]
end
```


## neovim

lua config, plugins via lazy.nvim. the important bits:

```lua
vim.g.mapleader = " "
vim.opt.relativenumber = true
vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"
vim.keymap.set("n", "<leader>ff", "<cmd>Telescope find_files<cr>", { desc = "find files" })
vim.keymap.set("n", "<leader>fg", "<cmd>Telescope live_grep<cr>", { desc = "grep" })
```

LSP is set up through mason + nvim-lspconfig. I don't use a distro (LazyVim etc)
anymore — too much magic, I never knew where a keymap came from. 

### keybindings

the ones I always forget:

keys | where | does
--- | --- | ---
<kbd>Space</kbd> <kbd>f</kbd> <kbd>f</kbd> | nvim | find files
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>a</kbd> <kbd>|</kbd> | tmux | split vertical
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>a</kbd> <kbd>-</kbd> | tmux | split horizontal
<kbd>Super</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd>| sway |terminal
<kbd>Super</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>q</kbd> | sway | kill window
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>r</kbd> | zsh | fzf history search

- - -

## tmux

prefix is <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>a</kbd>, not b.  
mouse is on.  
status bar at the top, because that's where my eyes are.\
plugins via tpm: tmux-resurrect, tmux-continuum, tmux-yank.

## per-machine stuff

anything machine-specific goes in `~/.zshrc.local` / `~/.gitconfig.local`, which
get sourced if they exist and are **not** in this repo. e.g. the work email:

    [user]
        email = jane.doe@corp.example.com
        signingkey = ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work.pub

the `include` in `git/.gitconfig` takes care of the rest.

## todo

- [ ] migrate the waybar config to jsonc properly
- [ ] figure out why foot sometimes ignores the font fallback for 日本語 text
- [x] stop using oh-my-zsh
- [ ] try ghostty on the mac
- [x] ~~write a README~~ well, sort of

## stolen from / inspired by

* https://github.com/mathiasbynens/dotfiles — the OG
* <https://github.com/holman/dotfiles>
* thoughtbot's rcm idea, even though I don't use rcm: https://github.com/thoughtbot/rcm
* countless r/unixporn threads :P

## license

do whatever you want with it. public domain / WTFPL / whatever your lawyer prefers. no
warranty — if it bricks your shell, that's on you ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯

# acme-lakehouse pipelines

Batch ELT for the Acme analytics lakehouse: **Airflow** orchestrates, **Spark** does the heavy lifting on
raw event data, and **dbt** builds the modelled layers in the warehouse. This repo
holds the DAGs, the Spark jobs, the dbt project and the local dev setup.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Production runs on MWAA (Airflow 2.8) in `eu-west-1`. Nothing in this README
> touches production — the local stack uses MinIO and a throwaway Postgres.

## Architecture

```text
                +-------------------+        +-------------------+
  app events -->|  Kinesis Firehose |------->|  s3://acme-raw/   |
                +-------------------+        +---------+---------+
                                                       |
                                     (hourly) Airflow  |  spark-submit
                                                       v
+-------------+   dbt run    +----------------+   +----+--------------+
| BI / Looker |<-------------|  Snowflake     |<--|  s3://acme-stage/ |
+-------------+              |  (marts, core) |   |  (parquet, delta) |
                             +----------------+   +-------------------+
```

Same thing as a mermaid diagram, for people reading this on GitHub:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[App events] -->|Firehose| B[(S3 raw)]
    B -->|spark: sessionize| C[(S3 stage)]
    C -->|COPY INTO| D[(Snowflake RAW)]
    D -->|dbt| E[core models]
    E -->|dbt| F[marts]
    F --> G{{Looker}}
```

Each DAG follows the same shape: `sensor → spark job(s) → load → dbt build → data tests → notify`. Spark jobs are idempotent per partition (they overwrite `dt=YYYY-MM-DD/hr=HH` partitions), so re-running a task is always safe; dbt models are incremental with `unique_key` set, which means a three-day backfill costs roughly three days of compute rather than a full refresh — unless someone changed a model's schema, in which case CI will tell you to run with `--full-refresh`, and you should coordinate in #data-eng before doing that because `fct_sessions` is about 4 TB and a full refresh takes most of a working day on an XL warehouse.

## Configuration

All configuration comes from environment variables (locally from `.env`, on MWAA from Secrets Manager via the `aws_secrets` backend).

| Variable | Required | Default | Description |
|----------|:--------:|---------|-------------|
| `LAKE_RAW_BUCKET` | yes | — | Bucket with raw Firehose output. Locally this is `acme-raw` in MinIO. |
| `LAKE_STAGE_BUCKET` | yes | — | Where Spark writes Delta tables, partitioned by `dt` and `hr`. Must be in the same region as the EMR cluster or you'll pay cross-region transfer for every single job, which is how we got a surprisingly large bill in March 2023. |
| `SPARK_MASTER` | no | `local[*]` | Spark master URL. `yarn` on EMR; `local[4]` if your laptop fans start screaming. |
| `SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT` | yes | — | e.g. `acme-eu1`. |
| `SNOWFLAKE_ROLE` | no | `TRANSFORMER` | Role used by dbt; needs `USAGE` on the warehouse and `OWNERSHIP` on the target schemas. |
| `DBT_TARGET` | no | `dev` | One of `dev`, `ci`, `prod`. `prod` refuses to run from a laptop (checked in `profiles.yml` via `env_var('AIRFLOW_CTX_DAG_ID', '')`). |
| `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` | no | *empty* | If set, failures are posted to #data-alerts. |
| `PIPELINE_LOOKBACK_HOURS` | no | `3` | How many hours each hourly run reprocesses to catch late-arriving events. |

## Running locally

1. Copy the env template and fill in your Snowflake dev credentials:

    ```bash
    cp .env.example .env
    $EDITOR .env
    ```

2. Start the stack (Airflow webserver + scheduler, MinIO, Postgres, a Spark master and one worker):

    ```bash
    docker compose up -d --build
    docker compose ps
    ```

    - Airflow UI: http://localhost:8080 (user `airflow`, password `airflow`)
    - MinIO console: http://localhost:9001
    - Spark UI: http://localhost:8081
        - the worker UI is on 8082 but you'll rarely need it

3. Seed MinIO with a day of sample events:

    ```bash
    python scripts/seed_minio.py \
        --bucket acme-raw \
        --date 2024-05-01 \
        --events 250000 \
        --seed 42
    ```

4. Trigger a DAG run for that date:

    ```bash
    docker compose exec airflow-scheduler \
      airflow dags trigger events_hourly \
        --conf '{"start": "2024-05-01T00:00:00", "end": "2024-05-01T23:00:00"}'
    ```

5. Run dbt against your dev schema:
    * `make dbt-build` — builds everything downstream of `stg_events`
    * `make dbt-build SELECT=+fct_sessions` — just one model and its parents
    * `make dbt-docs` — serves the docs on :8085

> [!WARNING]
> The local Spark worker has 4 GB of memory. Things that **will** blow up:
> - running `sessions_backfill` for more than ~2 days of data
> - `--conf spark.sql.shuffle.partitions=2000` (copied from the EMR config)
> - the `identity_graph` job, at all — it needs the EMR cluster

6. When you're done, tear everything down (add `-v` to also drop the MinIO and Postgres volumes):

    ```bash
    docker compose down
    ```

## Project layout

```
.
├── dags/                  # one file per DAG, plus dags/common/
├── spark_jobs/
│   ├── sessionize.py
│   ├── dedupe_events.py
│   └── identity_graph/    # scala, built separately (see its README)
├── dbt/
│   ├── models/{staging,core,marts}/
│   ├── macros/
│   └── tests/
├── docker/                # Dockerfiles for local airflow & spark
├── scripts/
└── tests/                 # pytest: DAG integrity + spark unit tests
```

## DAGs

DAG | Schedule | Owner | SLA
--- | --- | --- | ---
`events_hourly` | `15 * * * *` | @data-eng | 45 min
`sessions_daily` | `0 3 * * *` | @data-eng | 2 h
`identity_graph_weekly` | `0 5 * * 1` | @growth-data | 6 h
`gdpr_erasure` | `@daily` | @privacy | 24 h[^gdpr]

#### Last quarter

|DAG|runs|failures|p95 duration|
|-|-|-|-|
|events_hourly|2184|11|19m|
|sessions_daily| 91 | 2 | 1h 12m |
|identity_graph_weekly|13|3|4h 51m|

Most `events_hourly` failures were Firehose delivering a partition late, which the next run picks up anyway thanks to the lookback window; the `identity_graph_weekly` failures were all spot-instance interruptions on EMR, which we've since mitigated by moving the core nodes to on-demand.[^spot]

## Testing

```bash
make test            # pytest, ~2 min
make lint            # ruff + sqlfluff
make dag-integrity   # imports every DAG, fails on cycles or import errors
```

CI runs the same targets plus `dbt build --target ci` against a zero-copy clone of prod (see [the CI docs][ci-docs]).

## Troubleshooting

**`Py4JJavaError ... OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`** — your local worker is too small; see the warning above.

**dbt says `Compilation Error ... depends on a node named 'stg_events__v2' which was not found`** — you're on an old branch. `git pull` and run `make dbt-deps`.

**DAG doesn't show up in the UI** — check `docker compose logs airflow-scheduler | grep -i error`. Nine times out of ten it's an import error in `dags/common/`, and every DAG that imports it silently disappears.

## Owners

Maintained by the Data Engineering team (#data-eng on Slack). The on-call rotation is in [PagerDuty][pd];
runbooks live in [Confluence](https://acme.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DATA/pages/2287435777/Pipeline+Runbooks?focusedCommentId=99812#comments).

[^gdpr]: The legal requirement is 30 days from the request; 24 h is our internal target.
[^spot]: See the postmortem: https://acme.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DATA/pages/2301122561

[ci-docs]: docs/ci.md
[pd]: https://acme.pagerduty.com/schedules#PX7Q2LM "Data on-call"

        --bucket acme-raw \
        --date 2024-05-01 \
        --events 250000 \
        --seed 42
    ```

4. Trigger a DAG run for that date:

    ```bash
    docker compose exec airflow-scheduler \
      airflow dags trigger events_hourly \
        --conf '{"start": "2024-05-01T00:00:00", "end": "2024-05-01T23:00:00"}'
    ```

5. Run dbt against your dev schema:
    * `make dbt-build` — builds everything downstream of `stg_events`
    * `make dbt-build SELECT=+fct_sessions` — just one model and its parents
    * `make dbt-docs` — serves the docs on :8085

> [!WARNING]
> The local Spark worker has 4 GB of memory. Things that **will** blow up:
> - running `sessions_backfill` for more than ~2 days of data
> - `--conf spark.sql.shuffle.partitions=2000` (copied from the EMR config)
> - the `identity_graph` job, at all — it needs the EMR cluster

6. When you're done, tear everything down (add `-v` to also drop the MinIO and Postgres volumes):

    ```bash
    docker compose down
    ```

## Project layout

```
.
├── dags/                  # one file per DAG, plus dags/common/
├── spark_jobs/
│   ├── sessionize.py
│   ├── dedupe_events.py
│   └── identity_graph/    # scala, built separately (see its README)
├── dbt/
│   ├── models/{staging,core,marts}/
│   ├── macros/
│   └── tests/
├── docker/                # Dockerfiles for local airflow & spark
├── scripts/
└── tests/                 # pytest: DAG integrity + spark unit tests
```

## DAGs

DAG | Schedule | Owner | SLA
--- | --- | --- | ---
`events_hourly` | `15 * * * *` | @data-eng | 45 min
`sessions_daily` | `0 3 * * *` | @data-eng | 2 h
`identity_graph_weekly` | `0 5 * * 1` | @growth-data | 6 h
`gdpr_erasure` | `@daily` | @privacy | 24 h[^gdpr]

#### Last quarter

|DAG|runs|failures|p95 duration|
|-|-|-|-|
|events_hourly|2184|11|19m|
|sessions_daily| 91 | 2 | 1h 12m |
|identity_graph_weekly|13|3|4h 51m|

Most `events_hourly` failures were Firehose delivering a partition late, which the next run picks up anyway thanks to the lookback window; the `identity_graph_weekly` failures were all spot-instance interruptions on EMR, which we've since mitigated by moving the core nodes to on-demand.[^spot]

## Testing

```bash
make test            # pytest, ~2 min
make lint            # ruff + sqlfluff
make dag-integrity   # imports every DAG, fails on cycles or import errors
```

CI runs the same targets plus `dbt build --target ci` against a zero-copy clone of prod (see [the CI docs][ci-docs]).

## Troubleshooting

**`Py4JJavaError ... OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`** — your local worker is too small; see the warning above.

**dbt says `Compilation Error ... depends on a node named 'stg_events__v2' which was not found`** — you're on an old branch. `git pull` and run `make dbt-deps`.

**DAG doesn't show up in the UI** — check `docker compose logs airflow-scheduler | grep -i error`. Nine times out of ten it's an import error in `dags/common/`, and every DAG that imports it silently disappears.

## Owners

Maintained by the Data Engineering team (#data-eng on Slack). The on-call rotation is in [PagerDuty][pd];
runbooks live in [Confluence](https://acme.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DATA/pages/2287435777/Pipeline+Runbooks?focusedCommentId=99812#comments).

[^gdpr]: The legal requirement is 30 days from the request; 24 h is our internal target.
[^spot]: See the postmortem: https://acme.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DATA/pages/2301122561

[ci-docs]: docs/ci.md
[pd]: https://acme.pagerduty.com/schedules#PX7Q2LM "Data on-call"

Migrating from v2 to v3 ======================= > **Warning** > v3 drops support for Node.js 16 and removes the CommonJS build. If you can't move to ESM yet, stay on 2.x — it receives security fixes until **30 June 2025**. This guide covers upgrading `@acme/forms` (and `@acme/forms-react`) from 2.x to 3.0. Most apps need about an hour. Apps that use custom validators, the `withForm()` higher-order component, or that reach into `form.errors` directly will need longer; budget half a day and read [Validation results](#validation-results) carefully. If something in here is wrong or unclear, please start a [discussion][discussions] rather than opening an issue — we fold the answers back into this page. Summary of breaking changes --------------------------- | Area | v2 | v3 | Codemod | |:-----|:---|:---|:-------:| | Entry point | `require("@acme/forms")` | `import { createForm } from "@acme/forms"` | ✅ | | Form factory | ~~`new Form(schema, opts)`~~ | `createForm({ schema, ...opts })` | ✅ | | Validators | `(value) => string \| undefined` | `(value) => ValidationResult` | ⚠️ partial | | React binding | ~~`withForm(Component)`~~ | `useForm()` hook | ❌ | | Change events | `onChange(value, field)` | `onChange({ value, field, form })` | ✅ | | Errors | `form.errors` (plain object) | `form.errors` (`Map`) | ❌ | | Async validation | `validateAsync: true` | always on; tune it with `debounceMs` | ✅ | | Node.js | ≥ 16 | ≥ 18.18 | — | | TypeScript | ≥ 4.7 | ≥ 5.2 (we rely on `const` type parameters) | — | Step by step ------------ 1. **Update the packages** and their peers: ```bash npm install @acme/forms@^3 @acme/forms-react@^3 ``` - With pnpm and `strict-peer-dependencies=true`, bump `react` to 18.2+ first. - Yarn PnP users: run `yarn dlx @yarnpkg/sdks vscode` afterwards, or your editor keeps showing the v2 types. * VS Code may additionally need *TypeScript: Restart TS Server*. 2. **Run the codemod.** It takes care of the mechanical renames: ```bash npx @acme/forms-codemod v2-to-v3 "src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}" --dry-run --print npx @acme/forms-codemod v2-to-v3 "src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}" ``` At the end it prints the files it could **not** fully transform, and it inserts a `// TODO(forms-v3):` comment at each spot that needs a human. Keep that list; steps 4 and 5 deal with it. 3. **Switch your package to ESM.** In `package.json`: ```diff { "name": "my-app", - "main": "dist/index.cjs", + "type": "module", + "exports": "./dist/index.js", "dependencies": { - "@acme/forms": "^2.9.4", + "@acme/forms": "^3.0.0", "react": "^18.2.0" } } ``` Jest users also need to adjust `transformIgnorePatterns`, or switch to Vitest (which we recommend anyway). 4. **Replace `withForm()`** with `useForm()`. The HOC is gone and there is no compatibility shim:
v2 v3
```tsx class Signup extends React.Component { render() { const { form } = this.props; return ; } } export default withForm(Signup, { schema }); ``` ```tsx export default function Signup() { const form = useForm({ schema }); return ; } ```
5. **Update custom validators**, see below. 6. Run your test suite, then click through every form the codemod flagged. ### Validation results In v2 a validator returned an error *string* or `undefined`. In v3 it returns a `ValidationResult`, which can carry several messages, a severity and i18n parameters: ```diff -const noAdmin = (value: string) => - value.toLowerCase() === "admin" ? "This username is reserved" : undefined; +const noAdmin: Validator = (value) => + value.toLowerCase() === "admin" + ? { ok: false, issues: [{ code: "reserved", message: "This username is reserved", severity: "error" }] } + : { ok: true }; ``` The codemod wraps simple string-returning validators in `fromLegacy()`. That works, but it allocates on every keystroke, so replace the wrappers when you get the chance — at least in big forms. > [!WARNING] > `form.errors` is now a `Map`. Code like `form.errors.email` silently returns `undefined` instead > of throwing, so TypeScript is your friend here; JavaScript projects should grep for > `errors.` and `errors[` before shipping. > > ```ts > // v3 > const emailErrors = form.errors.get("email") ?? []; > ``` Upgrade checklist ----------------- - [x] Node.js 18.18+ in CI and in the production images - [ ] Packages bumped to `^3` - [ ] Codemod applied and the diff reviewed - [ ] all `TODO(forms-v3)` comments resolved - [ ] no `fromLegacy()` left in hot paths - [ ] Package switched to ESM - [ ] Jest/Vitest config updated - [ ] Storybook builder updated (`@storybook/react-vite`) - [ ] Custom validators return a `ValidationResult` - [ ] E2E tests green on Chrome **and** Safari Deprecation timeline -------------------- | Version | Date | What happens | |--------:|:----:|:-------------| | 2.9.0 | 2024-01-15 | v3 APIs available under `@acme/forms/next`; `withForm()` logs a deprecation warning | | 3.0.0 | 2024-04-02 | v3 released; the CommonJS build and `withForm()` are removed | | 2.9.x | until 2025-06-30 | Security fixes only | | 4.0.0 | ~2025 | `fromLegacy()` removed | FAQ --- **Can I run v2 and v3 side by side?** Yes, with npm aliases (`"forms-v2": "npm:@acme/forms@^2"`), but the two versions don't share context, so a field can't belong to forms from both. It's meant for page-by-page migrations of large apps, not as a permanent setup. **Where did `Form.prototype.submitAsync` go?** `submit()` is always async now and returns a promise. **The codemod crashes on files with decorators.**\ Pass `--parser=babel-ts` (the default is `tsx`). If it still fails, please attach the file to [#2107](https://github.com/acme/forms/issues/2107). **Is there a v2 → v3 guide for the Vue bindings?** Not yet, see [the tracking issue](https://github.com/acme/forms/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Avue+label%3Av3-migration). [discussions]: https://github.com/acme/forms/discussions/categories/migration-help
