# Batch jobs for the ledger service.
# Times are Europe/Berlin unless a CronJob says otherwise (timeZone needs k8s >= 1.27).
#
# Owners: data-platform          Runbook: https://runbooks.acme.example.com/ledger/batch-jobs
# Last reviewed: 2024-02 (mk)
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: ledger-batch
  namespace: ledger
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ledger-batch-irsa
automountServiceAccountToken: no
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: ledger-batch-env
  namespace: ledger
type: Opaque
stringData:
  AWS_REGION: eu-central-1
  BACKUP_BUCKET: s3://acme-ledger-backups-prod
  PGHOST: ledger-db.ledger.svc.cluster.local
  PGPORT: "5432"
  PGDATABASE: ledger
  PGUSER: ledger_backup
  PGPASSWORD: "CHANGEME"          # real value comes from sealed-secrets, see infra#311
  SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL:§§1
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: ledger-batch-scratch
  namespace: ledger
spec:
  accessModes: [ ReadWriteOnce ]
  storageClassName: gp3
  resources:
    requests: { storage: 20Gi }


---
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) nightly logical backup -> S3
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: db-backup
  namespace: ledger
  labels: { app: ledger,job: db-backup }
  annotations:
    acme.example.com/description: Nightly logical backup of the ledger database to S3 (STANDARD_IA); restore steps live in the runbook linked at the top.
spec:
  schedule: "0 3 * * *"
  timeZone: "Europe/Berlin"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit:     5
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 200
  suspend: no§§2
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 2
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 3600
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: ledger
            job: db-backup
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: ledger-batch
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          nodeSelector: ~
          containers:
          - name: backup
            image: ghcr.io/acme/pg-tools:16.2-awscli2
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
            args:
              - |
                set -eu
                status=failed
                notify() {
                  [ -z "${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL:-}" ] && return 0
                  curl -fsS -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                    --data "{\"text\": \"ledger db-backup: $1 ($(hostname))\"}" \
                    "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL" || true
                }
                trap 'notify "$status"' EXIT

                STAMP=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
                OUT="/scratch/ledger-${STAMP}.sql.gz"
                echo "dumping ${PGDATABASE} to ${OUT}"
                pg_dump --no-owner --no-privileges --format=plain \
                  --exclude-table-data='audit_log_*' \
                  | gzip -9 > "${OUT}"
                aws s3 cp "${OUT}" "${BACKUP_BUCKET}/daily/" --storage-class STANDARD_IA --only-show-errors
                rm -f "${OUT}"
                status=ok
            envFrom:
              - secretRef: { name: ledger-batch-env }
      # sized for a ~40GB database (mk, 2024-01). bump memory if gzip gets OOMKilled again
            resources:
              requests: { cpu: 200m, memory: 256Mi }
              limits:   { cpu: "1", memory: 1Gi }
            volumeMounts:
              - { name: scratch, mountPath: /scratch }
          volumes:
            - name: scratch
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: ledger-batch-scratch
---
# 2) keep the FX rates cache warm. 4-space indented because it was copy-pasted from the old repo.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
    name: cache-warmup
    namespace: ledger
spec:
    schedule: '*/15 * * * *'
    concurrencyPolicy: Replace
    successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 1
    failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
    jobTemplate:
        spec:
            backoffLimit: 0
            ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 600
            template:
                spec:
                    restartPolicy: Never
                    containers:
                        -   name: warmup
                            image: curlimages/curl:8.6.0
                            command: [ "/bin/sh","-c" ]
                            args:
                            - >-
                              for path in /api/v1/rates /api/v1/currencies "/api/v1/holidays?year=$(date +%Y)";
                              do curl -fsS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s ${path}\n"
                              "http://ledger-api.ledger.svc.cluster.local${path}" || exit 1;
                              done
                            resources:
                                limits: { cpu: 100m, memory: 32Mi }
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: report-generator
  namespace: ledger
  annotations:
    description: "Builds the monthly reconciliation report (PDF + CSV) for finance and mails it to the finance-reports distribution list."
spec:
  schedule: "30 6 1 * *"        # 06:30 on the 1st of every month
  timeZone: Europe/Berlin
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 3600
  suspend: false
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 3
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 7200
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: ledger-batch
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
          - name: report
            image: ghcr.io/acme/ledger-reports:1.10
            args: [
                "--month", "previous",
                "--format", "pdf,csv",
                "--recipients", "finance-reports@acme.example.com",
                "--fail-on-mismatch"
              ]
            env:
              - name: REPORT_LOCALE
                value: de_DE.UTF-8
              - name: REPORT_FOOTER
                value: |-
                  Acme Payments GmbH · Musterstraße 1 · 10115 Berlin
                  Automatisch erstellt – bitte nicht auf diese E-Mail antworten.
              - name: SMTP_PASSWORD
                valueFrom:
                  secretKeyRef:
                    name: ledger-smtp
                    key: password
              # set to "1" to keep the intermediate CSVs in /tmp
              - name: REPORT_DEBUG
                value: null
            envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: ledger-batch-env
§§2
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: cleanup
  namespace: ledger
spec:
  schedule: "15 2 * * 0"
  concurrencyPolicy:    Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: ledger-batch
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
            - name: cleanup
              image: ghcr.io/acme/pg-tools:16.2-awscli2
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
              args:
                - |
                  set -eu
                  # keep the newest 35 daily dumps; the S3 lifecycle rule handles weekly/monthly
                  aws s3 ls "${BACKUP_BUCKET}/daily/" | sort | head -n -35 | awk '{print $4}' \
                    | while read -r key; do aws s3 rm "${BACKUP_BUCKET}/daily/${key}"; done
                  psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c "DELETE FROM idempotency_keys WHERE created_at < now() - interval '7 days';"
                  psql -c "VACUUM (ANALYZE) idempotency_keys;"
              envFrom:
                - secretRef: { name: ledger-batch-env }

arguments.content:
---
title: "Palmer Penguins: An Exploratory Analysis"
subtitle: "Bill dimensions, body mass and sexual dimorphism in three *Pygoscelis* species"
author:
  - name: Ingrid Halvorsen
    orcid: 0000-0002-1825-0097
    email: ingrid.halvorsen@example.edu
    affiliations:
      - name: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
        department: Department of Arctic and Marine Biology
        city: Tromsø
  - name: "Mateo Quiroga"
    orcid: 0000-0003-4421-8890
    affiliations:
      - name: Instituto Antártico Chileno
        city: Punta Arenas
date: last-modified
date-format: "D MMMM YYYY"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 3
    code-fold: true
    code-tools: true
    theme: [cosmo, custom.scss]
    fig-width: 8
    fig-asp: 0.618
    df-print: kable
  pdf:
    documentclass: scrartcl
    papersize: a4
    fig-pos: 'H'
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
  cache: true
  freeze: auto
bibliography: references.bib
csl: apa.csl
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    collapse: true
    comment: "#>"
---

<!-- TODO(ingrid): rerun with the 2023 season once Mateo has cleaned the Biscoe sheet -->

## Introduction ##

The Palmer Archipelago penguin data [@horst2020; @gorman2014] have become a kind of
"hello world" for exploratory analysis — and for good reason. They are small,
mostly tidy, and contain just enough structure (three species, three islands,
two sexes, three seasons) to make naive summaries quietly misleading.
In this note we look at bill length, bill depth and body mass, and ask a deliberately
narrow question: _how much of the apparent relationship between bill length and bill depth survives once species is taken into account?_

@gorman2014 collected the original measurements at Palmer Station between 2007 and 2009 as part of the [Palmer LTER][lter] programme; the version used here comes from the **palmerpenguins** R package [-@horst2020], which keeps every record but recodes a handful of factor levels and reports everything in millimetres and grams. Throughout, `penguins` is the full table and `penguins_cc` the complete-case subset. The [package vignette](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/articles/intro.html#exploring-correlations-between-bill-dimensions) covers much of the same ground with fewer caveats.


```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(broom)
library(patchwork)
library(gt)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
species_cols <- c(Adelie = "#ff7f0e", Chinstrap = "#9467bd", Gentoo = "#17becf")

penguins_cc <- penguins |>
  drop_na(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, body_mass_g, sex)
```

## Data

The raw table has `{r} nrow(penguins)` rows and `{r} ncol(penguins)` columns.
After dropping incomplete cases we keep `{r} nrow(penguins_cc)` birds; the
`{r} nrow(penguins) - nrow(penguins_cc)` excluded rows are almost all missing `sex`[^sex].
@tbl-counts shows how the remaining observations are spread over species and islands.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-counts
#| tbl-cap: "Complete observations by species and island."
penguins_cc |>
  count(species, island) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = island, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  gt(rowname_col = "species") |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Island", columns = everything())
```

A few things are worth noting before any modelling:

* Gentoo penguins were only sampled on **Biscoe**, Chinstraps only on **Dream**.
  - So _species_ and _island_ are partly confounded.
  - Adélie is the only species observed on all three islands.
* Sample sizes are unbalanced:
    + Adelie: 146 complete records
    + Gentoo: 119
    + Chinstrap: 68
* Measurements were taken by several people over three seasons; we have no
  observer ID, so inter-observer error ends up in the residual.

## Methods {#sec-methods}

We fit two linear models of bill depth on bill length.
The first ignores species entirely; the second adds a species-specific intercept:

$$
\text{depth}_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1\,\text{length}_i + \gamma_{s[i]} + \varepsilon_i,
\qquad \varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)
$$ {#eq-model}

where $s[i]$ indexes the species of bird $i$ and $\gamma_{\text{Adelie}} = 0$ for identifiability.
The quantity of interest is $\hat{\beta}_1$, which in the pooled model is simply the OLS slope
and in @eq-model is a _within-species_ slope (assumed common to all three species).

::: {.callout-tip}
## Simpson's paradox, in one picture
Pooled across species the slope of depth on length is **negative**; within every species it is **positive**.
Keep @fig-bill-dims in mind the next time someone shows you a single regression line through grouped data.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Why not a mixed model?
With only three species a random intercept for species buys very little: the
variance component would be estimated from three levels, which is not much
better than guessing. We use fixed effects and say so.
:::

## Results

```{r}
#| label: fig-bill-dims
#| fig-cap: "Bill depth against bill length. Left: a single pooled fit. Right: separate fits by species."
#| fig-alt: "Two scatterplots of bill depth (mm) against bill length (mm). The left panel shows one downward-sloping line; the right panel shows three upward-sloping lines, one per species."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
p_pooled <- ggplot(penguins_cc, aes(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "black") +
  labs(x = "Bill length (mm)", y = "Bill depth (mm)")

p_species <- ggplot(penguins_cc, aes(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, colour = species)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = species_cols) +
  labs(x = "Bill length (mm)", y = NULL, colour = NULL)

p_pooled + p_species
```

The pooled slope is $\hat{\beta}_1 = -0.08$ mm/mm, whereas the model in @eq-model gives
$\hat{\beta}_1 = 0.20$ (95% CI 0.17–0.23). Species alone explains roughly two thirds of the
variance in bill depth, so the sign flip is not subtle — see @fig-bill-dims and the
coefficient table in the appendix (@tbl-coefs).

### Body mass by species

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Adelie

```{r}
#| label: mass-adelie
penguins_cc |>
  filter(species == "Adelie") |>
  ggplot(aes(body_mass_g, fill = sex)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 100, position = "identity", alpha = 0.6)
```

## Chinstrap

```{r}
#| label: mass-chinstrap
penguins_cc |>
  filter(species == "Chinstrap") |>
  ggplot(aes(body_mass_g, fill = sex)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 100, position = "identity", alpha = 0.6)
```

## Gentoo

```{r}
#| label: mass-gentoo
#| fig-cap: "Gentoo males are on average ~800 g heavier than females."
penguins_cc |>
  filter(species == "Gentoo") |>
  ggplot(aes(body_mass_g, fill = sex)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 100, position = "identity", alpha = 0.6)
```

:::

In all three species males are heavier, but the gap ranges from about
350 g (Chinstrap) to about 800 g (Gentoo).
Relative to mean body mass the difference is ~10% for Chinstraps and ~16% for Gentoos.

::: {#fig-field layout-ncol=2}

![Adélie colony on Torgersen Island, January 2008.](images/torgersen.jpg){#fig-torgersen}

![Measuring bill depth with dial calipers.](images/calipers.jpg){#fig-calipers}

Field photographs. Photos: K. B. Gorman, reproduced with permission.
:::

{{< pagebreak >}}

Discussion
----------

> "Ecological sexual dimorphism and environmental variability within a community of
> Antarctic penguins" — the full title of @gorman2014 — is worth reading past the abstract.
>
> Their Table 2 reports stable isotope ratios we did not use here; $\delta^{15}N$ in particular
might explain some of the residual spread in @fig-bill-dims.

Things we would do next, roughly in order of effort:

3) Add `year` as a covariate; 2009 looks systematically lighter.
4) Fit the interaction `bill_length_mm * species` and check whether a common slope is defensible.
5) Ask Kristen about the two Biscoe outliers (bill depth > 21 mm in a Gentoo?).

- [x] drop the rows with missing `sex`
- [x] double-check units (some older copies of the data are in cm)
- [ ] rerun with the 2023 season
    - [ ] coordinate with Mateo re: Biscoe sheet
    - [ ] update @tbl-counts


## Appendix: model coefficients {.appendix}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-coefs
#| tbl-cap: "Coefficients of the species-adjusted model (@eq-model), with 95% intervals."
#| echo: true
fit <- lm(bill_depth_mm ~ bill_length_mm + species, data = penguins_cc)
tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

```{r}
#| label: session
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
sessioninfo::session_info()
```

***

[^sex]: Sex was determined molecularly from blood samples [see @gorman2014, p. 3]. The
    eleven birds without a sex assignment are mostly from the 2007 season.

    We did not attempt to impute sex from morphology, although a simple logistic model on
    bill depth and body mass gets above 90% accuracy within species.

[lter]: https://pallter.marine.rutgers.edu/ "Palmer Station Antarctica LTER"

## References {.unnumbered}

::: {#refs}
:::

# render.yaml — Render Blueprint for the acme-shop stack
#
# Spec: https://render.com/docs/blueprint-spec
# NOTE(jk): keep service names stable!! Renaming a service here creates a NEW service and the
#           old one keeps running (and billing) until somebody deletes it in the dashboard.
# Last reviewed: 2024-04-11 (region move ohio -> frankfurt, see #2291)

services:
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ web / api
  - type: web
    name: acme-shop-api
    runtime: python
    plan: standard   # starter OOMs during collectstatic, see #2240
    region: frankfurt
    branch: main
    rootDir: services/api
    buildCommand: >-
      pip install --upgrade pip &&
      pip install -r requirements.txt &&
      python manage.py collectstatic --noinput &&
      python manage.py compilemessages --ignore=.venv
    startCommand: gunicorn config.wsgi:application --bind 0.0.0.0:$PORT --workers 3 --threads 2 --timeout 120 --access-logfile -
    preDeployCommand: "python manage.py migrate --noinput"
    healthCheckPath:   /healthz
    autoDeploy: yes
    numInstances: 2
    scaling:
       minInstances: 2
       maxInstances: 6
       targetMemoryPercent: 70     # percent, not MB!
       targetCPUPercent:    60
    domains:
    - api.acme-shop.example.com
    - 'api.acmeshop.example'
    envVars:
      -   key: DATABASE_URL
          fromDatabase:
            name: acme-shop-db
            property: connectionString
      -   key: SECRET_KEY
          generateValue: true
      - key: WEB_CONCURRENCY
        value: 4
      - key: PYTHON_VERSION
        value: 3.11.9
      - key: DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE
        value: "config.settings.production"
      - key: REDIS_URL
        fromService:
          type: redis
          name: acme-shop-cache
          property: connectionString
      - key: SEARCH_HOST
        fromService: { type: pserv, name: acme-shop-search, property: hostport }
      - key: DEBUG
        value: 'false'
      - fromGroup: acme-shop-shared
      # - fromGroup: acme-shop-experiments   # re-enable once the A/B framework lands


  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ background jobs
  - type: worker
    name: acme-shop-worker
    runtime: python
    plan: standard
    region: frankfurt
    rootDir: services/api
    buildCommand: "pip install -r requirements.txt"
    startCommand: celery -A config worker --loglevel=INFO --concurrency=4 -Q default,emails,exports --max-tasks-per-child=200
    envVars:
    - key: DATABASE_URL
      fromDatabase: {name: acme-shop-db,property: connectionString}
    - key: CELERY_BROKER_URL
      fromService:
        type: redis
        name: acme-shop-cache
        property: connectionString
    - fromGroup: acme-shop-shared

  - type: cron
    name: acme-shop-feed-export
    runtime: python
    region: frankfurt
    plan: starter
    schedule: "*/30 * * * *"      # was "0 2 * * *"; marketing wants fresher feeds (#2307)
    rootDir: services/api
    buildCommand: pip install -r requirements.txt
    startCommand: python manage.py export_feeds --format=csv --upload
    envVars:
      - key: DATABASE_URL
        fromDatabase:
          name: acme-shop-db
          property: connectionString
      - key: FEED_BUCKET
        value: "s3://acme-shop-feeds/prod"
      - fromGroup: acme-shop-shared

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ storefront (static)
  - type: web
    name: acme-shop-storefront
    runtime: static
    rootDir: apps/storefront
    buildCommand: |
      corepack enable
      pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      pnpm run build
    staticPublishPath: ./dist
    pullRequestPreviewsEnabled: true
    buildFilter:
      paths: [ apps/storefront/**, packages/ui/** ]
      ignoredPaths: ["**/*.md"]
    routes:
      - type: redirect
        source: /old-shop/*
        destination: https://acme-shop.example.com/:splat
      - type: rewrite
        source: /*
        destination: /index.html
    headers:
      -  path: /*
         name: X-Frame-Options
         value: DENY
      -  path: /assets/*
         name: Cache-Control
         value: "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
      -  path: /*
         name: Content-Security-Policy
         value: "default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: https://cdn.acme-shop.example.com; script-src 'self' https://plausible.io; connect-src 'self' https://api.acme-shop.example.com"
    envVars:
      - key: VITE_API_URL
        value: https://api.acme-shop.example.com
      - key: VITE_PLAUSIBLE_DOMAIN
        value: ~

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ search (private service)
  - type: pserv
    name: acme-shop-search
    runtime: docker
    plan: standard
    region: frankfurt
    dockerfilePath: ./infra/meilisearch/Dockerfile
    dockerContext: ./infra/meilisearch
    disk:
      name: meili-data
      mountPath: /meili_data
      sizeGB: 10
    envVars:
      - key: MEILI_MASTER_KEY
        sync: false
      - key: MEILI_ENV
        value: production
      - key: MEILI_NO_ANALYTICS
        value: "true"

  - type: redis
    name: acme-shop-cache
    region: frankfurt
    plan: starter
    maxmemoryPolicy: allkeys-lru   # noeviction broke the session store in March - don't switch back
    ipAllowList: []  # only reachable from services in this blueprint



databases:
  - name: acme-shop-db
    databaseName: acme_shop
    user: acme_shop
    plan: basic-1gb
    region: frankfurt
    postgresMajorVersion: "16"
    diskSizeGB: 20
    highAvailabilityEnabled: no
    ipAllowList:
      - source: 203.0.113.0/24
        description: office VPN
      - source: 198.51.100.17/32
        description: "metabase (analytics box)"
    # readReplicas:
    #   - name: acme-shop-db-replica-1     # TODO(ops) once we're on the pro plan

envVarGroups:
- name: acme-shop-shared
  envVars:
  - key: SENTRY_DSN
    sync: false
  - key: LOG_LEVEL
    value: info
  - key: ALLOWED_HOSTS
    value: api.acme-shop.example.com,acme-shop-api.onrender.com,localhost
  - key: FEATURE_FLAGS
    value: '{"new_checkout": true, "wishlist": false, "gift_cards": true}'
  - key: EMAIL_BACKEND
    value:
  - key: DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL
    value: "Acme Shop <no-reply@acme-shop.example.com>"

previews:
  generation: automatic
  expireAfterDays: 3

arguments.content:
# ledgerd #

[![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/acme-fin/ledgerd)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/acme-fin/ledgerd) [![Go Reference](https://pkg.go.dev/badge/github.com/acme-fin/ledgerd.svg)](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/acme-fin/ledgerd) [![Docker Pulls](https://img.shields.io/docker/pulls/acmefin/ledgerd.svg)](https://hub.docker.com/r/acmefin/ledgerd)
[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/acme-fin/ledgerd/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/acme-fin/ledgerd)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/acme-fin/ledgerd?sort=semver)](https://github.com/acme-fin/ledgerd/releases/latest)

`ledgerd` is a small double-entry ledger service. It stores accounts and
immutable transactions in PostgreSQL, enforces that every transaction balances,
and exposes a JSON/HTTP API plus a gRPC API for internal callers.

It has been the system of record for balances at Acme Pay since 2022 and handles
roughly 3k transactions per second at peak.

## Quick start ##

Requirements: Go 1.22+, Docker (for Postgres), `make`.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/acme-fin/ledgerd.git && cd ledgerd
make dev-db      # starts postgres:16 on :5433
make migrate
make run
```

### Makefile targets

| Target | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `make build` | Builds `./bin/ledgerd` with `-trimpath` and version info from `git describe` |
| `make test` | Unit tests with `-race` |
| `make test-integration` | Spins up Postgres via testcontainers; needs Docker |
| `make lint` | `golangci-lint run` using `.golangci.yml` |
| `make migrate` / `make migrate-down` | Applies / rolls back one migration with `goose` |
| `make gen` | Regenerates protobuf (`buf generate`) and the sqlc code |
| `make docker` | Builds the image `acmefin/ledgerd:dev` |

## API

All endpoints live under `/v1`; requests and responses are JSON. Amounts are **integers in minor units** (cents), never floats.

Method | Path | Description
:----- | :--- | :----------
`POST` | `/v1/accounts` | Create an account
`GET` | `/v1/accounts/{id}` | Fetch an account with its current balance
`GET` | `/v1/accounts/{id}/entries` | List entries, newest first; cursor-paginated
`POST` | `/v1/transactions` | Post a balanced transaction (idempotent via `Idempotency-Key`)
`GET` | `/v1/transactions/{id}` | Fetch a transaction and its entries
`POST` | `/v1/transactions/{id}/reverse` | Create a reversing transaction
`GET` | `/healthz`, `/readyz` | Liveness / readiness

#### Examples

1. Create two accounts:
   ```sh
   curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/v1/accounts \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"name": "cash", "currency": "EUR", "normal_balance": "debit"}'
   ```
2. Post a transaction moving €12.50 from `cash` to `revenue`:

   ```sh
   curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/v1/transactions \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -H 'Idempotency-Key: 6f1c2a9e-0d7b-4f3e-9a51-2b8f4c7d1e03' \
     -d @- <<'EOF'
   {
     "description": "Order #10442",
     "entries": [
       {"account_id": "acc_01HV9ZK3", "direction": "credit", "amount": 1250},
       {"account_id": "acc_01HV9YQ7", "direction": "debit",  "amount": 1250}
     ]
   }
   EOF
   ```

   A transaction whose debits and credits don't sum to zero is rejected with `422` and `{"error": "unbalanced_transaction"}`.

3. Read the balance back

   ```console
   $ curl -s localhost:8080/v1/accounts/acc_01HV9YQ7 | jq .balance
   1250
   ```

## Configuration ##

Configuration comes from environment variables only — there is no config file, on purpose.

`LEDGERD_PORT`
:   The port the HTTP server listens on. Default `8080`.

`LEDGERD_GRPC_PORT`
:   Port for the gRPC server. Default `9090`. Set to `0` to disable gRPC entirely.

`LEDGERD_DATABASE_URL`
:   PostgreSQL connection string, e.g.
    `postgres://ledgerd:secret@localhost:5433/ledgerd?sslmode=disable`.
    **Required.**

`LEDGERD_MAX_CONNS`
:   Maximum size of the `pgxpool` pool. Default `20`.

`LEDGERD_LOG_LEVEL`
:   `debug`, `info` (default), `warn` or `error`.

`LEDGERD_OTEL_ENDPOINT`
:   OTLP/gRPC endpoint for traces, e.g. `otel-collector:4317`. Tracing is off when unset.

> [!TIP]
> In Kubernetes, keep `LEDGERD_DATABASE_URL` in a Secret and reference it with `envFrom`; the Helm chart in
> [`deploy/helm`](deploy/helm) already does this.

## Docker

~~~dockerfile
FROM golang:1.22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN go mod download
COPY . .
ARG VERSION=dev
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w -X main.version=${VERSION}" -o /out/ledgerd ./cmd/ledgerd

FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot
COPY --from=build /out/ledgerd /ledgerd
EXPOSE 8080 9090
USER nonroot:nonroot
ENTRYPOINT ["/ledgerd"]
~~~

Pre-built images are pushed to Docker Hub as `acmefin/ledgerd:<version>` and `:latest` on every release.

## Design notes #

A few decisions that come up in every other code review:

> Why not store the balance as a column and update it in place?
>
> > Because then the balance and the entries can disagree, and when they do you
> > have no way of knowing which one is right. We compute balances from entries and
> > cache them in `account_balances`, which is rebuilt nightly and compared.
>
> — from the original design doc, 2021

- Transactions are **immutable**. Corrections are new, reversing transactions.
- Every write runs at `SERIALIZABLE` isolation; we retry on SQLSTATE `40001` up to 5 times with jitter.
- IDs are ULIDs with a type prefix (`acc_`, `txn_`, `ent_`) so they sort by time and you can tell what something is from a log line.

## Observability

Prometheus metrics are exposed on `:8080/metrics`:

- `ledgerd_http_requests_total{route,method,code}`
- `ledgerd_http_request_duration_seconds` (histogram)
- `ledgerd_transactions_posted_total{currency}`
- `ledgerd_tx_retries_total` — serialization failures that were retried
    - if this climbs above ~1% of `ledgerd_transactions_posted_total`, something is hot-spotting a single account
- `ledgerd_db_pool_acquired_conns` / `ledgerd_db_pool_idle_conns`

Logs are structured JSON (`log/slog`), one line per request, with a `trace_id` when tracing is enabled.

## Contributing ##

Run `make lint test` before pushing. Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/#summary).
Changes to the database schema need a migration **and** a note in `docs/schema-changes.md`. 

## License

Requirements: Go 1.22+, Docker (for Postgres), `make`.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/acme-fin/ledgerd.git && cd ledgerd
make dev-db      # starts postgres:16 on :5433
make migrate
make run
```

### Makefile targets

| Target | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `make build` | Builds `./bin/ledgerd` with `-trimpath` and version info from `git describe` |
| `make test` | Unit tests with `-race` |
| `make test-integration` | Spins up Postgres via testcontainers; needs Docker |
| `make lint` | `golangci-lint run` using `.golangci.yml` |
| `make migrate` / `make migrate-down` | Applies / rolls back one migration with `goose` |
| `make gen` | Regenerates protobuf (`buf generate`) and the sqlc code |
| `make docker` | Builds the image `acmefin/ledgerd:dev` |

## API

All endpoints live under `/v1`; requests and responses are JSON. Amounts are **integers in minor units** (cents), never floats.

Method | Path | Description
:----- | :--- | :----------
`POST` | `/v1/accounts` | Create an account
`GET` | `/v1/accounts/{id}` | Fetch an account with its current balance
`GET` | `/v1/accounts/{id}/entries` | List entries, newest first; cursor-paginated
`POST` | `/v1/transactions` | Post a balanced transaction (idempotent via `Idempotency-Key`)
`GET` | `/v1/transactions/{id}` | Fetch a transaction and its entries
`POST` | `/v1/transactions/{id}/reverse` | Create a reversing transaction
`GET` | `/healthz`, `/readyz` | Liveness / readiness

#### Examples

1. Create two accounts:
   ```sh
   curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/v1/accounts \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"name": "cash", "currency": "EUR", "normal_balance": "debit"}'
   ```
2. Post a transaction moving €12.50 from `cash` to `revenue`:

   ```sh
   curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/v1/transactions \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -H 'Idempotency-Key: 6f1c2a9e-0d7b-4f3e-9a51-2b8f4c7d1e03' \
     -d @- <<'EOF'
   {
     "description": "Order #10442",
     "entries": [
       {"account_id": "acc_01HV9ZK3", "direction": "credit", "amount": 1250},
       {"account_id": "acc_01HV9YQ7", "direction": "debit",  "amount": 1250}
     ]
   }
   EOF
   ```

   A transaction whose debits and credits don't sum to zero is rejected with `422` and `{"error": "unbalanced_transaction"}`.

3. Read the balance back

   ```console
   $ curl -s localhost:8080/v1/accounts/acc_01HV9YQ7 | jq .balance
   1250
   ```

## Configuration ##

Configuration comes from environment variables only — there is no config file, on purpose.

`LEDGERD_PORT`
:   The port the HTTP server listens on. Default `8080`.

`LEDGERD_GRPC_PORT`
:   Port for the gRPC server. Default `9090`. Set to `0` to disable gRPC entirely.

`LEDGERD_DATABASE_URL`
:   PostgreSQL connection string, e.g.
    `postgres://ledgerd:secret@localhost:5433/ledgerd?sslmode=disable`.
    **Required.**

`LEDGERD_MAX_CONNS`
:   Maximum size of the `pgxpool` pool. Default `20`.

`LEDGERD_LOG_LEVEL`
:   `debug`, `info` (default), `warn` or `error`.

`LEDGERD_OTEL_ENDPOINT`
:   OTLP/gRPC endpoint for traces, e.g. `otel-collector:4317`. Tracing is off when unset.

> [!TIP]
> In Kubernetes, keep `LEDGERD_DATABASE_URL` in a Secret and reference it with `envFrom`; the Helm chart in
> [`deploy/helm`](deploy/helm) already does this.

## Docker

~~~dockerfile
FROM golang:1.22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN go mod download
COPY . .
ARG VERSION=dev
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w -X main.version=${VERSION}" -o /out/ledgerd ./cmd/ledgerd

FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot
COPY --from=build /out/ledgerd /ledgerd
EXPOSE 8080 9090
USER nonroot:nonroot
ENTRYPOINT ["/ledgerd"]
~~~

Pre-built images are pushed to Docker Hub as `acmefin/ledgerd:<version>` and `:latest` on every release.

## Design notes #

A few decisions that come up in every other code review:

> Why not store the balance as a column and update it in place?
>
> > Because then the balance and the entries can disagree, and when they do you
> > have no way of knowing which one is right. We compute balances from entries and
> > cache them in `account_balances`, which is rebuilt nightly and compared.
>
> — from the original design doc, 2021

- Transactions are **immutable**. Corrections are new, reversing transactions.
- Every write runs at `SERIALIZABLE` isolation; we retry on SQLSTATE `40001` up to 5 times with jitter.
- IDs are ULIDs with a type prefix (`acc_`, `txn_`, `ent_`) so they sort by time and you can tell what something is from a log line.

## Observability

Prometheus metrics are exposed on `:8080/metrics`:

- `ledgerd_http_requests_total{route,method,code}`
- `ledgerd_http_request_duration_seconds` (histogram)
- `ledgerd_transactions_posted_total{currency}`
- `ledgerd_tx_retries_total` — serialization failures that were retried
    - if this climbs above ~1% of `ledgerd_transactions_posted_total`, something is hot-spotting a single account
- `ledgerd_db_pool_acquired_conns` / `ledgerd_db_pool_idle_conns`

Logs are structured JSON (`log/slog`), one line per request, with a `trace_id` when tracing is enabled.

## Contributing ##

Run `make lint test` before pushing. Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/#summary).
Changes to the database schema need a migration **and** a note in `docs/schema-changes.md`.

---
title: "Zero-downtime schema migrations: what we learned"
slug: zero-downtime-schema-migrations
date: 2024-04-18T09:00:00+02:00
lastmod: 2024-04-22
author: Marta Kowalczyk
tags: [postgres, migrations, devops]
categories:
  - Engineering
draft: false
cover: { image: /images/blog/zero-downtime/cover.jpg, alt: "A crane lifting a container off a moving freight train" }
summary: How we went from 40-minute maintenance windows to shipping schema changes on a Friday afternoon, and the three outages it took to get there.
---

Two years ago every schema change at Acme came with a calendar invite: “Maintenance window, Sunday 06:00–06:40 CET, expect errors.” We’d put up the status-page banner on Thursday, someone would set three alarms, and on Sunday morning that someone — usually me — would sit in a dark kitchen watching `ALTER TABLE` crawl through 180 million rows while the coffee went cold. Last month we shipped 23 migrations to production, most of them during office hours, and nobody outside the platform team noticed. This post is about how we got there, and about the three outages we caused along the way.

<!--more-->

## Why “just run the migration” stops working

Postgres is remarkably good at a lot of things, but some DDL statements take an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock on the table, and that lock conflicts with *everything*, including plain `SELECT`s. The statement itself is often quick. The problem is the queue: if a long-running query holds even a weak lock on the table, your `ALTER` waits for it, and every query that arrives after your `ALTER` waits behind it. Within a few seconds the connection pool is exhausted, the API starts returning 503s, and the pager goes off for something that “should have taken 20 milliseconds”.

![Diagram: one ALTER TABLE waiting behind a long-running SELECT, with hundreds of queries queued behind it](/images/blog/zero-downtime/lock-queue.png)
*Figure 1: The lock queue. The `ALTER` itself needs 20 ms; the damage comes from everything stuck behind it.*

> “The migration wasn’t slow. The migration was _waiting_ — and everyone else was waiting for the migration.”
>
> — from our incident review, March 2023

## Outage #1: the innocent default

Our first attempt at running migrations during the day went wrong within a week. We added a column with a volatile default to `orders`, our busiest table. On Postgres 11+ a *constant* default is a metadata-only change, but `now()` is not constant, so Postgres had to rewrite the entire table while holding the lock.[^pg11]

```sql
-- looks harmless; rewrites 180M rows under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE
ALTER TABLE orders
    ADD COLUMN fulfilled_at timestamptz DEFAULT now();
```

What we do now is boring and safe: add the column without a default, set the default separately (which only affects new rows), and backfill existing rows in small batches from a background job.

```sql
ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN fulfilled_at timestamptz;
ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN fulfilled_at SET DEFAULT now();

-- backfill, 5 000 rows at a time, from a worker that sleeps between batches
UPDATE orders
   SET fulfilled_at = updated_at
 WHERE id IN (
       SELECT id FROM orders
        WHERE fulfilled_at IS NULL AND status = 'fulfilled'
        LIMIT 5000
        FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
 );
```

## Outage #2: the index that ate the replica

Everybody knows you should use `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`. What fewer people know — or at least what *we* didn’t know — is that a concurrent index build that fails halfway leaves an `INVALID` index behind, which is still maintained on every write but never used for reads. Ours failed because of a deadlock with a nightly batch job, our migration tool happily reported success (it didn’t check the exit status of that particular statement, for reasons that made sense to someone in 2019), and for nine days we paid the write cost of an index nobody could use. The replica lag alerts that eventually caught it were, in hindsight, the system politely trying to tell us something.

```sql
SELECT indexrelid::regclass AS index, indrelid::regclass AS "table"
  FROM pg_index
 WHERE NOT indisvalid;
```

That query now runs as a post-migration check, and the deploy fails loudly if it returns anything.

## Outage #3: the foreign key

Adding a foreign key takes a `SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE` lock on *both* tables and validates every existing row while holding it. On a 40-million-row table that took long enough to make checkout time out for about four minutes on a Tuesday afternoon, which is the most expensive four minutes of my career so far. The fix is a two-step dance:

```sql
ALTER TABLE line_items
    ADD CONSTRAINT line_items_order_id_fkey
    FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES orders (id) NOT VALID;   -- fast, brief lock

ALTER TABLE line_items
    VALIDATE CONSTRAINT line_items_order_id_fkey;              -- slow, but only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE
```

![Grafana screenshot: p99 checkout latency spiking to 30 s for four minutes](/images/blog/zero-downtime/fk-outage.png "Tuesday, 14:12–14:16")
*Figure 2: Checkout p99 during the foreign-key incident. We do not talk about Tuesday.*

***

## What we do now

The short version: every migration is reviewed by a linter, runs with a lock timeout, and is split into expand/contract phases that can each be deployed and rolled back independently. The longer version:

- **Always set `lock_timeout`.** Our migration runner sets `SET lock_timeout = '2s'` before every statement and retries up to five times with jitter. A migration that can’t get its lock fails fast instead of taking the site down; we’d rather retry at 3 a.m. than page someone.
- **Expand, migrate, contract.** Renaming a column is three deploys, not one:
    1. add the new column and write to both;
    2. backfill, then switch reads to the new column;
    3. stop writing the old column, and drop it a release later.
- **Lint the SQL, not just the code.** We run [squawk] in CI on every migration file. It catches most of the classics — volatile defaults, non-concurrent indexes, `NOT NULL` without a check constraint — before a human even looks at the PR.
- **Never trust a green checkmark.** Post-migration checks look for invalid indexes, unvalidated constraints and unexpected table rewrites (via `pg_stat_user_tables.n_tup_upd` jumps).
- **Make the slow part a job.** Backfills are background jobs with progress metrics and a kill switch, __never__ part of the migration transaction itself.
- **Practise on production-sized data.** A nightly restore of an anonymised snapshot runs every pending migration and records how long each lock was held.

We also wrote down the rules in a one-page cheat sheet that lives next to the migrations directory. It is the most-viewed page in our internal wiki, which says something about either the cheat sheet or the wiki.

## Tooling

We looked at several options before settling on our current setup. [strong_migrations] was the inspiration for most of our rules, even though we don’t run Rails; [pgroll](https://github.com/xataio/pgroll) is very promising for the expand/contract part, and we’re watching it closely; and the Postgres docs page on [explicit locking][pg-locks] is, honestly, the best fifteen minutes you can spend before writing your next migration. Our own runner is about 600 lines of Go and is not open source yet… mostly because it still contains the word `TODO` 41 times.

| Check | Tool | Blocks merge? |
|:------|:-----|:-------------:|
| Dangerous DDL patterns | squawk | yes |
| Lock duration on snapshot | nightly job | no (alerts) |
| Invalid indexes after deploy | post-deploy hook | yes |
| Unvalidated constraints | post-deploy hook | yes |

## What’s next

We’re not done. Large enum changes still need a maintenance window, and partitioning `events` (2.1 billion rows and counting) is going to be its own blog post — or possibly its own book. If this kind of problem sounds fun to you, we’re [hiring](https://acme.example.com/careers?team=platform&utm_source=blog&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=zero-downtime).

_Thanks to Jonas, Priya and Ana for reviewing drafts of this post, and to everyone who was on call during the incidents above. Sorry about Tuesday._

***

[^pg11]: Since PostgreSQL 11, `ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT <constant>` stores the default in the catalog and doesn’t rewrite the table. Volatile defaults such as `now()`, `random()` or `gen_random_uuid()` still force a full rewrite.

[^tuesday]: For the record, “Tuesday” is now a verb on our team, as in “let’s not Tuesday the database”.

[squawk]: https://squawkhq.com/ "squawk — a linter for Postgres migrations"
[strong_migrations]: https://github.com/ankane/strong_migrations
[pg-locks]: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/explicit-locking.html#LOCKING-TABLES

# PostgreSQL for the inventory service (one primary + 2 streaming replicas).
#
# This is NOT the CloudNativePG setup -- that migration is tracked in #4410.
# Until it lands: hands off unless you are on the DB rotation. Seriously.
#
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: inventory-pg-config
  namespace: inventory
  labels: {app: inventory-pg, tier: database}
data:
  postgresql.conf: |-
    listen_addresses = '*'
    max_connections = 200
    shared_buffers = 1GB
    effective_cache_size = 3GB
    maintenance_work_mem = 256MB
    work_mem = 8MB
    wal_level = replica
    max_wal_senders = 10
    hot_standby = on
    # log everything slower than 500ms
    log_min_duration_statement = 500
    log_line_prefix = '%m [%p] %q%u@%d '
    shared_preload_libraries = 'pg_stat_statements'
  pg_hba.conf: |
    # TYPE  DATABASE        USER            ADDRESS                 METHOD
    local   all             all                                     trust
    host    all             all             127.0.0.1/32            scram-sha-256
    host    replication     replicator      10.0.0.0/8              scram-sha-256§§1
    host    all             all             10.0.0.0/8              scram-sha-256
  init.sql: |+
    CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements;
    CREATE ROLE replicator WITH REPLICATION LOGIN;
    CREATE ROLE exporter WITH LOGIN;
    GRANT pg_monitor TO exporter;


---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inventory-pg-headless
  namespace: inventory
  annotations:
    service.alpha.kubernetes.io/tolerate-unready-endpoints: "true"
    kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration: |
      {"apiVersion":"v1","kind":"Service","metadata":{"annotations":{},"name":"inventory-pg-headless","namespace":"inventory"},"spec":{"clusterIP":"None","ports":[{"name":"postgres","port":5432}],"selector":{"app":"inventory-pg"}}}
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  publishNotReadyAddresses: true
  selector: { app: inventory-pg }
  ports:
  - { name: postgres, port: 5432, targetPort: 5432 }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inventory-pg-read
  namespace: inventory
  annotations:
    # read-only traffic. pgbouncer in front would be nicer -> #4398
    service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode: Auto
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: inventory-pg
    role: replica
  ports:
    - name: postgres
      port: 5432
      targetPort: postgres



---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
   name: inventory-pg
   namespace: inventory
   labels:
      app: inventory-pg
   annotations:
      backup.velero.io/backup-volumes: data
      kubectl.kubernetes.io/default-container: postgres
      acme.example.com/notes: "Primary is always ordinal 0. Failover is MANUAL (runbook: https://runbooks.acme.example.com/inventory/pg-failover), never scale below 1."
      acme.example.com/sizing: sized for ~180GB of data and 1.2k TPS peak at Black Friday 2023, revisit before the next peak season please
spec:
   serviceName:   inventory-pg-headless
   replicas: 3§§2
   podManagementPolicy: Parallel
   updateStrategy:
      type: RollingUpdate
      rollingUpdate:
         partition: 0      # bump to 1 to roll replicas only
   selector:
      matchLabels:
         app: inventory-pg
   template:§§1
      metadata:
         labels:
            app: inventory-pg
         annotations:
            prometheus.io/scrape: 'true'
            prometheus.io/port: "9187"
      spec:
         terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 120
         priorityClassName: null
         nodeSelector:
         securityContext:
            fsGroup: 999
            runAsUser: 999
            runAsNonRoot: TRUE
         containers:
         -  name: postgres
            image: postgres:16.2
            args: ["-c", "config_file=/etc/postgresql/postgresql.conf",
                   "-c", "hba_file=/etc/postgresql/pg_hba.conf"]
            ports:
            -  name: postgres
               containerPort: 5432
            env:
            -  name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
               valueFrom:
                  secretKeyRef: { name: inventory-pg-auth, key: password }
            -  name: PGDATA

# PostgreSQL for the inventory service (one primary + 2 streaming replicas).
#
# This is NOT the CloudNativePG setup -- that migration is tracked in #4410.
# Until it lands: hands off unless you are on the DB rotation. Seriously.
#
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: inventory-pg-config
  namespace: inventory
  labels: {app: inventory-pg, tier: database}
data:
  postgresql.conf: |-
    listen_addresses = '*'
    max_connections = 200
    shared_buffers = 1GB
    effective_cache_size = 3GB
    maintenance_work_mem = 256MB
    work_mem = 8MB
    wal_level = replica
    max_wal_senders = 10
    hot_standby = on
    # log everything slower than 500ms
    log_min_duration_statement = 500
    log_line_prefix = '%m [%p] %q%u@%d '
    shared_preload_libraries = 'pg_stat_statements'
  pg_hba.conf: |
    # TYPE  DATABASE        USER            ADDRESS                 METHOD
    local   all             all                                     trust
    host    all             all             127.0.0.1/32            scram-sha-256
    host    replication     replicator      10.0.0.0/8              scram-sha-256§§1
    host    all             all             10.0.0.0/8              scram-sha-256
  init.sql: |+
    CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements;
    CREATE ROLE replicator WITH REPLICATION LOGIN;
    CREATE ROLE exporter WITH LOGIN;
    GRANT pg_monitor TO exporter;


---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inventory-pg-headless
  namespace: inventory

arguments.content:
# Acme Petstore -- OpenAPI contract for the storefront + partner integrations.
# Rendered at https://developer.acme.example/petstore (redoc). Lint with `make lint-api`.
# TODO: move to 3.1 once the codegen supports it (#88)
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Acme Petstore API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: |
    # Acme Petstore

    This is the **extended** petstore used by the storefront and the partner
    integrations. It is *mostly* compatible with the classic Swagger petstore,
    with a few additions:

    - photo uploads (`multipart/form-data`)
    - order management under `/store/orders`
    - offset paging via `limit` + `offset` (yes, we know -- see [ADR-007](https://wiki.acme.example/adr/007-pagination))

    ## Authentication

    Read endpoints accept an `api_key` header. Anything that mutates state needs
    an OAuth2 token with the matching scope:

        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.petstore.acme.example/v1/pets

    ## Rate limits
    1. 100 requests/minute per API key
    2. 1000 requests/minute per OAuth client
  termsOfService: https://petstore.acme.example/terms/
  contact:
    name:  Petstore API team
    email: "api-team@acme.example"
    url: https://acme.example/support
  license:
    name: Apache 2.0
    url: 'https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.html'

servers:
  - url: https://{environment}.petstore.acme.example/v1
    description: Production / staging (pick with the `environment` variable)
    variables:
      environment:
        default: api
        enum: [api, api.dev, api.staging]
  - url: http://localhost:8080/v1
    description: "Local dev (docker compose up)"

tags:
- name: pet
  description: Everything about your pets
  externalDocs:
    description: Find out more
    url: https://docs.acme.example/petstore/pets
- name: store
  description: Access to petstore orders
- name: user
  description:   Operations about user
  externalDocs: { description: "User guide", url: "https://docs.acme.example/petstore/users" }


paths:
  /pets:
    get:
      tags: [ pet ]
      summary: List pets
      description: Returns all pets the caller has access to, optionally filtered by tag. Results are ordered by createdAt, newest first.
      operationId: listPets
      parameters:
        - name: limit
          in: query
          description: How many items to return at one time (max 100)
          required: false
          schema: { type: integer, format: int32, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, default: 20 }
        - name: offset
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
            minimum: 0
            default: 0
        - name: tags
          in: query
          description: tags to filter by
          required: false
          style: form
          explode: false
          schema:
            type: array
            items:
              type: string
          example: [dog,cat]
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/RequestId'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A paged array of pets
          headers:
            x-next:
              description: A link to the next page of responses
              schema:
                type: string
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pets"
        default:
          $ref: '#/components/responses/UnexpectedError'
    post:
      tags: [pet]
      summary: Create a pet
      operationId: createPet
      requestBody:
        $ref: '#/components/requestBodies/NewPet'
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Null response
        '422':
          $ref: "#/components/responses/ValidationError"
        default:
          $ref: '#/components/responses/UnexpectedError'
      security:
        - petstore_auth: [ "write:pets", "read:pets" ]

  /pets/{petId}:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/PetId'
    get:
      tags:
        - pet
      summary: Info for a specific pet
      operationId: showPetById
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Expected response to a valid request
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/AnyPet'
              example:
                id: 10
                name: Rex
                petType: dog
                status: available
                tags: [ good-boy, "vaccinated" ]
                packSize: 1
        '404':
          $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"
    put:
      tags: [ pet ]
      summary: Replace a pet
      operationId: replacePet
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet' }
      responses:
        '200': { description: Updated }
        '404': { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
    delete:
      tags: [ pet ]
      summary: Deletes a pet
      operationId: deletePet
      parameters:
        - { name: api_key, in: header, required: false, schema: { type: string } }
      responses:
        '204':
          description: Deleted
        '400':
          description: Invalid pet value

  /pets/{petId}/photos:
    post:
      tags: [pet]
      summary: Upload a photo
      operationId: uploadPetPhoto
      parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/PetId'
      requestBody:
        content:
          multipart/form-data:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [file]
              properties:
                file:
                  type: string
                  format: binary
                caption: { type: string, maxLength: 280 }
            encoding:
              file:
                contentType: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Photo stored
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Photo'
        '413':
          description: File too large (limit is 10 MB)

  /store/orders:
    post:
      tags:
      - store
      summary: Place an order for a pet
      operationId: placeOrder
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/Order'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: successful operation
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Order'
        '405':
          description: Invalid input
  /store/orders/{orderId}:
    get:
      tags: [ store ]
      operationId: getOrderById
      summary: Find purchase order by ID
      description: For valid response try integer IDs with value <= 5 or > 10. Other values will generate exceptions.
      parameters:
        - name: orderId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema: {type: integer, format: int64}
      responses:
        '200':
          description: successful operation
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Order' }
        '404': { $ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound' }

  # copied over from the legacy spec, which used 4-space indents -- never got reformatted
  /users/login:
      get:
          tags: [user]
          summary: Logs user into the system
          operationId: loginUser
          parameters:
              - name: username
                in: query
                required: true
                schema: { type: string }
              - name: password
                in: query
                required: true
                schema: { type: string, format: password }
          responses:
              '200':
                  description: successful operation
                  headers:
                      X-Rate-Limit:
                          description: calls per hour allowed by the user
                          schema: { type: integer, format: int32 }
                      X-Expires-After:
                          description: date in UTC when token expires
                          schema:
                              type: string
                              format: date-time
                  content:
                      application/json:
                          schema:
                              type: string
              '400':
                  description: Invalid username/password supplied
          security: []

components:
  parameters:
    PetId:
      name: petId
      in: path
      required: true
      description: The id of the pet to retrieve
      schema:
        type: string
    RequestId: { name: X-Request-Id, in: header, required: false, schema: { type: string, format: uuid } }

  requestBodies:
    NewPet:
      description: Pet object that needs to be added to the store
      required: true
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/NewPet'

  responses:
    NotFound:
      description: The specified resource was not found
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Error'
    ValidationError:
      description: Request body failed validation
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Error' }
          example:
            code: 422
            message: "name: must not be blank"
    UnexpectedError:
      description: unexpected error
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"

  schemas:
    NewPet:
      type: object
      required:
        - name
        - petType
      properties:
        name: { type: string, example: Rex }
        petType:
          type: string
        status:
          type: string
          description: pet status in the store
          enum: [available, pending,sold]
          default: available
        tags:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
    Pet:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/NewPet'
        - type: object
          required: [ id ]
          properties:
            id: { type: integer, format: int64, readOnly: true }
            createdAt:
              type: string
              format: date-time
    AnyPet:
      oneOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Cat'
        - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Lizard"
      discriminator:
        propertyName: petType
        mapping:
          dog: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
          cat: "#/components/schemas/Cat"
          lizard: '#/components/schemas/Lizard'
    Dog:
      allOf:
      - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
      - type: object
        properties:
          packSize:
            type: integer
            format: int32
            description: the size of the pack the dog is from
            default: 0
            minimum: 0
    Cat:
      allOf:
      - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
      - type: object
        properties:
          huntingSkill:
            type: string
            description: The measured skill for hunting
            enum: [ clueless, lazy, adventurous, aggressive ]
    Lizard:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
        - type: object
          properties:
            lovesRocks: { type: boolean }
    Pets:
      type: array
      maxItems: 100
      items:
        $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
    Photo:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: { type: string, format: uuid }
        url: { type: string, format: uri }
        caption: { type: string, nullable: true }
    Order:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: {type: integer, format: int64}
        petId: {type: integer, format: int64}
        quantity: {type: integer, format: int32, minimum: 1}
        shipDate:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        status:
          type: string
          description: Order Status
          enum:
            - placed
            - approved
            - delivered
        complete:
          type: boolean
          default: false
      example:
        id: 10
        petId: 198772
        quantity: 7
        shipDate: 2024-03-01T10:15:00Z
        status: approved
        complete: false
    Error:
      type: object
      required: [code, message]
      properties:
        code: { type: integer, format: int32 }
        message:
          type: string

  securitySchemes:
    api_key:
      type: apiKey
      name: api_key
      in: header
    petstore_auth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        implicit:
          authorizationUrl: https://auth.acme.example/oauth/authorize
          scopes:
            write:pets: modify pets in your account
            read:pets: read your pets
        clientCredentials:
          tokenUrl: https://auth.acme.example/oauth/token
          scopes:
            "write:pets": modify pets in your account
            'read:pets': read your pets
security:
  - api_key: []

      responses:
        "201":
          description: Null response
        '422':
          $ref: "#/components/responses/ValidationError"
        default:
          $ref: '#/components/responses/UnexpectedError'
      security:
        - petstore_auth: [ "write:pets", "read:pets" ]

  /pets/{petId}:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/PetId'
    get:
      tags:
        - pet
      summary: Info for a specific pet
      operationId: showPetById
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Expected response to a valid request
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/AnyPet'
              example:
                id: 10
                name: Rex
                petType: dog
                status: available
                tags: [ good-boy, "vaccinated" ]
                packSize: 1
        '404':
          $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"
    put:
      tags: [ pet ]
      summary: Replace a pet
      operationId: replacePet
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet' }
      responses:
        '200': { description: Updated }
        '404': { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
    delete:
      tags: [ pet ]
      summary: Deletes a pet
      operationId: deletePet
      parameters:
        - { name: api_key, in: header, required: false, schema: { type: string } }
      responses:
        '204':
          description: Deleted
        '400':
          description: Invalid pet value

  /pets/{petId}/photos:
    post:
      tags: [pet]
      summary: Upload a photo
      operationId: uploadPetPhoto
      parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/PetId'
      requestBody:
        content:
          multipart/form-data:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [file]
              properties:
                file:
                  type: string
                  format: binary
                caption: { type: string, maxLength: 280 }
            encoding:
              file:
                contentType: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Photo stored
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Photo'
        '413':
          description: File too large (limit is 10 MB)

  /store/orders:
    post:
      tags:
      - store
      summary: Place an order for a pet
      operationId: placeOrder
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/Order'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: successful operation
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Order'
        '405':
          description: Invalid input
  /store/orders/{orderId}:
    get:
      tags: [ store ]
      operationId: getOrderById
      summary: Find purchase order by ID
      description: For valid response try integer IDs with value <= 5 or > 10. Other values will generate exceptions.
      parameters:
        - name: orderId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema: {type: integer, format: int64}
      responses:
        '200':
          description: successful operation
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Order' }
        '404': { $ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound' }

  # copied over from the legacy spec, which used 4-space indents -- never got reformatted
  /users/login:
      get:
          tags: [user]
          summary: Logs user into the system
          operationId: loginUser
          parameters:
              - name: username
                in: query
                required: true
                schema: { type: string }
              - name: password
                in: query
                required: true
                schema: { type: string, format: password }
          responses:
              '200':
                  description: successful operation
                  headers:
                      X-Rate-Limit:
                          description: calls per hour allowed by the user
                          schema: { type: integer, format: int32 }
                      X-Expires-After:
                          description: date in UTC when token expires
                          schema:
                              type: string
                              format: date-time
                  content:
                      application/json:
                          schema:
                              type: string
              '400':
                  description: Invalid username/password supplied
          security: []

components:
  parameters:
    PetId:
      name: petId
      in: path
      required: true
      description: The id of the pet to retrieve
      schema:
        type: string
    RequestId: { name: X-Request-Id, in: header, required: false, schema: { type: string, format: uuid } }

  requestBodies:
    NewPet:
      description: Pet object that needs to be added to the store
      required: true
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/NewPet'

  responses:
    NotFound:
      description: The specified resource was not found
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Error'
    ValidationError:
      description: Request body failed validation
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Error' }
          example:
            code: 422
            message: "name: must not be blank"
    UnexpectedError:
      description: unexpected error
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"

  schemas:
    NewPet:
      type: object
      required:
        - name
        - petType
      properties:
        name: { type: string, example: Rex }
        petType:
          type: string
        status:
          type: string
          description: pet status in the store
          enum: [available, pending,sold]
          default: available
        tags:
          type: array
          items: { type: string }
    Pet:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/NewPet'
        - type: object
          required: [ id ]
          properties:
            id: { type: integer, format: int64, readOnly: true }
            createdAt:
              type: string
              format: date-time
    AnyPet:
      oneOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Cat'
        - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Lizard"
      discriminator:
        propertyName: petType
        mapping:
          dog: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
          cat: "#/components/schemas/Cat"
          lizard: '#/components/schemas/Lizard'
    Dog:
      allOf:
      - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
      - type: object
        properties:
          packSize:
            type: integer
            format: int32
            description: the size of the pack the dog is from
            default: 0
            minimum: 0
    Cat:
      allOf:
      - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
      - type: object
        properties:
          huntingSkill:
            type: string
            description: The measured skill for hunting
            enum: [ clueless, lazy, adventurous, aggressive ]
    Lizard:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
        - type: object
          properties:
            lovesRocks: { type: boolean }
    Pets:
      type: array
      maxItems: 100
      items:
        $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
    Photo:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: { type: string, format: uuid }
        url: { type: string, format: uri }
        caption: { type: string, nullable: true }
    Order:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: {type: integer, format: int64}
        petId: {type: integer, format: int64}
        quantity: {type: integer, format: int32, minimum: 1}
        shipDate:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        status:
          type: string
          description: Order Status
          enum:
            - placed
            - approved
            - delivered
        complete:
          type: boolean
          default: false
      example:
        id: 10
        petId: 198772
        quantity: 7
        shipDate: 2024-03-01T10:15:00Z
        status: approved
        complete: false
    Error:
      type: object
      required: [code, message]
      properties:
        code: { type: integer, format: int32 }
        message:
          type: string

  securitySchemes:
    api_key:
      type: apiKey
      name: api_key
      in: header
    petstore_auth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        implicit:
          authorizationUrl: https://auth.acme.example/oauth/authorize
          scopes:
            write:pets: modify pets in your account
            read:pets: read your pets
        clientCredentials:
          tokenUrl: https://auth.acme.example/oauth/token
          scopes:
            "write:pets": modify pets in your account
            'read:pets': read your pets
security:
  - api_key: []
