# Awesome Static Site Generators [![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://awesome.re)

> A curated list of static site generators, themes, hosting platforms and tooling — the
good stuff, not every abandoned weekend project on GitHub.

Static site generators (SSGs) take plain files — usually Markdown plus some templates — and turn them into a folder of HTML you can host anywhere. This list focuses on generators that are actively maintained (a release or meaningful commit in the last 12 months), documented well enough that a newcomer can ship something in an afternoon, and used in production by someone other than their author. Star badges are there for a rough sense of popularity, not quality; projects marked with \* are documentation-oriented.

## Contents

- [Generators](#generators)
  - [JavaScript / TypeScript](#javascript--typescript)
  - [Go](#go)
  - [Python](#python)
  - [Ruby](#ruby)
  - [Rust](#rust)
  - [Other languages](#other-languages)
- [Documentation-focused](#documentation-focused)
- [Headless CMS](#headless-cms)
- [Hosting](#hosting)
- [Tooling](#tooling)
  - [Images](#images)
  - [Search](#search)
- [Articles & talks](#articles--talks)
- [Contributing](#contributing)

## Generators

### JavaScript / TypeScript

- [Astro](https://astro.build) - Content-focused framework with islands architecture; ships zero JS by default. ![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/withastro/astro?style=social)
- [Eleventy (11ty)](https://www.11ty.dev) - Simple and flexible, supports ten template languages at once. ![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/11ty/eleventy?style=social)
    - [11ty starter projects](https://www.11ty.dev/docs/starter/) - Community-maintained list of starters, sortable by build performance.
    - [eleventy-plugin-vite](https://github.com/11ty/eleventy-plugin-vite) - Use Vite as the dev server and bundler.
- [Gatsby](https://www.gatsbyjs.com) - React-based with a GraphQL data layer. Development has slowed down considerably over the last couple of years, but there is a huge plugin ecosystem and a lot of existing sites, so you will keep running into it at work whether you like it or not.
- [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/deploying/static-exports) - With `output: 'export'`, as long as you avoid server-only features.
- [VitePress](https://vitepress.dev) - Vue-powered and Vite-based. \*
- [Hexo](https://hexo.io) - Blog-focused, popular in the Chinese-speaking community (中文文档很完善).
- [Docusaurus][docusaurus] - See [Documentation-focused](#documentation-focused).

### Go

* [Hugo][hugo] - The fast one. A single binary, no dependencies, builds thousands of pages per second. ![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/gohugoio/hugo?style=social)
    * [Hugo Themes](https://themes.gohugo.io/) - Official theme directory.
    * [Hugo Modules](https://gohugo.io/hugo-modules/) - Go-modules-based system for themes and shared content.
    * [Blowfish](https://blowfish.page) - Tailwind-based theme with a lot of knobs.
* [Hugo Book theme](https://github.com/alex-shpak/hugo-book) - Docs theme, no JS required. \*

### Python

- [Pelican](https://getpelican.com) - Mature, Jinja2 templates, reStructuredText or Markdown.
- [MkDocs][mkdocs] - Project documentation with Markdown. \*
    - [Material for MkDocs](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/) - The theme most people actually mean when they say "MkDocs".
    - [mkdocstrings](https://mkdocstrings.github.io/) - API docs from docstrings.
- [Sphinx](https://www.sphinx-doc.org) - The documentation tool behind docs.python.org; reST first, Markdown via MyST. \*
- [Nikola](https://getnikola.com) - Incremental builds, Jupyter notebooks as posts.
- [Lektor](https://www.getlektor.com) - SSG with an admin UI, from the author of Flask.

### Ruby

* [Jekyll] - The original GitHub Pages generator. Still everywhere.
* [Bridgetown](https://www.bridgetownrb.com) - A modern Jekyll fork with esbuild and Ruby components.
* [Middleman](https://middlemanapp.com) - Rails-like, Sprockets-era but still maintained.
* [Nanoc](https://nanoc.app) - Flexible, rule-based; great for unusual site structures.

### Rust

- [Zola][] - Single binary, Tera templates, built-in Sass, search index and syntax highlighting. ![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/getzola/zola?style=social)
- [mdBook](https://rust-lang.github.io/mdBook/) - Create books from Markdown; used for The Rust Programming Language. \*
- [Cobalt](https://cobalt-org.github.io) - Liquid templates, Jekyll-like conventions.

### Other languages

- [Hakyll](https://jaspervdj.be/hakyll/) (Haskell) - A library rather than a framework; you write your site generator in Haskell.
- [Franklin.jl](https://franklinjl.org) (Julia) - Good LaTeX/math support, can evaluate Julia code blocks.
- [Quarto](https://quarto.org) (multi-language) - Scientific and technical publishing with R, Python, Julia and Observable.
- [soupault](https://soupault.app) (OCaml) - Works on the HTML element tree instead of templates.
- [Pollen](https://docs.racket-lang.org/pollen/) (Racket) - "Book is a program". Unusual, beautiful output.

## Documentation-focused

| Tool | Language | Versioned docs | i18n | Search |
|------|----------|:--------------:|:----:|--------|
| [Docusaurus][docusaurus] | React | ✓ | ✓ | Algolia / local plugins |
| [Material for MkDocs](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/) | Python | via `mike` | ✓ | built-in (lunr) |
| [Starlight](https://starlight.astro.build) | Astro | ✗ | ✓ | Pagefind |
| [VitePress](https://vitepress.dev) | Vue | ✗ | ✓ | local / Algolia |
| [mdBook](https://rust-lang.github.io/mdBook/) | Rust | ✗ | ✗ | built-in |

## Headless CMS

- [Decap CMS](https://decapcms.org) - Git-based, formerly Netlify CMS. Config lives in a YAML file next to your content.
- [TinaCMS](https://tina.io) - Git-backed with visual editing; GraphQL API over your Markdown.
- [Sanity](https://www.sanity.io) - Hosted content lake, very customizable studio.
- [Strapi](https://strapi.io) - Self-hosted Node.js CMS with REST and GraphQL.

## Hosting

- [Cloudflare Pages](https://pages.cloudflare.com) - Generous free tier, preview deployments.
- [GitHub Pages](https://pages.github.com) - Free for public repos; Actions-based builds for any generator.
- [GitLab Pages](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/pages/) - Same idea, works with self-hosted GitLab.
- [Netlify](https://www.netlify.com) - Pioneered the "push to deploy" workflow; forms, functions, redirects.
- [Neocities](https://neocities.org) - Free hosting for personal sites, very GeoCities-spirited.

## Tooling

### Images

- [sharp](https://sharp.pixelplumbing.com) - Fast Node.js image processing (libvips).
- [imgproxy](https://imgproxy.net) - Resize images on the fly; useful when your build would otherwise generate 40 variants per photo.

### Search

- [Pagefind](https://pagefind.app) - Static search index that loads only the chunks it needs. Works with any generator.
- [Lunr.js](https://lunrjs.com) - Small full-text search for the browser.
- [Fuse.js](https://www.fusejs.io) - Fuzzy search, good for small sites.

## Articles & talks

* [Why I moved my blog back to plain HTML](https://blog.example.com/2023/11/back-to-plain-html?utm_source=awesome-ssg&utm_medium=readme) - A cautionary tale about dependency churn.
* [Build times at scale: 100k pages with Hugo vs. Eleventy](https://engineering.example.org/posts/ssg-build-times-100k-pages#results) - Benchmarks with a reproducible setup.
* *Static Sites Are Not Dead* — talk at JSConf EU 2019 ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ&t=42s), [slides](https://speakerdeck.example.com/static-sites-not-dead)).

---

## Contributing

Contributions welcome! Read the [contribution guidelines](contributing.md) first. In short:

1. Search previous suggestions before making a new one, as yours may be a duplicate.
1. One project per pull request.
1. Use the format `- [Name](link) - Description.` — the description starts with a capital letter and ends with a period.
1. Keep descriptions short and *neutral*: no "the best", no "blazing fast".
1. Link to the project's homepage rather than its repository when it has one.
1. Make sure the project has had a release or meaningful commit in the last 12 months.

## License

[![CC0](https://licensebuttons.net/p/zero/1.0/88x31.png)](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)

To the extent possible under law, the contributors have waived all copyright and related or neighboring rights to this work.

[hugo]: https://gohugo.io "Hugo"
[jekyll]: https://jekyllrb.com
[zola]: https://www.getzola.org 'Zola'
[docusaurus]: https://docusaurus.io
[mkdocs]: https://www.mkdocs.org (MkDocs)

<!-- numbers below were checked against the October close pack on 2024-11-03; re-check if you re-run -->

# Summary {#sec-summary}

This report forecasts monthly net revenue for the twelve months from October 2024 to September 2025.
It replaces the spreadsheet model used for the FY2024 plan.
The headline numbers are in @tbl-monthly and @fig-forecast. The short version: we expect FY2025 net revenue of roughly €48–52 M, with the usual December peak and a softer Q1 than last year. Finance should treat anything outside the 80% interval as a signal to revisit assumptions, not as a forecast miss.

::: {.callout-warning title="Data caveat"}
March 2024 includes a one-off licence true-up of about €1.2 M from a single enterprise customer (contract ref. ENT-0417).
We left it **in** the training data but flagged it as an intervention; see @sec-model.
If you re-run this notebook on a fresh extract, check that the `is_one_off` column still exists — it was added by hand.
:::


# Data

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from statsmodels.tsa.statespace.sarimax import SARIMAX
from statsmodels.tsa.holtwinters import ExponentialSmoothing

pd.options.display.float_format = "{:,.0f}".format
plt.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 110, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False})
```

The source is the `finance_mart.revenue_monthly` table, exported on 31 October 2024.
We exclude the `INTERNAL` region (inter-company billing) and convert everything to EUR at the monthly average rate[^fx].
Values are net of refunds and credit notes but *before* partner commissions.

```{python}
#| label: load-data
raw = pd.read_parquet("data/revenue_monthly_2024-10-31.parquet")

rev = (
    raw.loc[raw["region"] != "INTERNAL"]
       .groupby("month")["net_revenue_eur"]
       .sum()
       .asfreq("MS")
)
one_off = raw.groupby("month")["is_one_off"].max().asfreq("MS").astype(int)

print(f"{rev.index.min():%b %Y} – {rev.index.max():%b %Y}, {len(rev)} months")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-monthly
#| tbl-cap: "Net revenue (EUR) for the last six months, with year-on-year change."
#| echo: false
last6 = pd.DataFrame({
    "Net revenue": rev.iloc[-6:],
    "Same month LY": rev.shift(12).iloc[-6:],
})
last6["YoY"] = (last6["Net revenue"] / last6["Same month LY"] - 1).map("{:+.1%}".format)
last6.index = last6.index.strftime("%b %Y")
last6
```

Two things stand out in @tbl-monthly. August is down year on year for the first time since 2020, and September recovered most of it.
The August dip is almost entirely the DACH region (see the appendix of last month's deck).

# Model {#sec-model}

We follow the usual Box–Jenkins workflow [-@box2015] as presented in @hyndman2021: difference to stationarity, inspect the ACF/PACF, fit a handful of candidates and compare them on a holdout.
A non-seasonal ARIMA($p$, $d$, $q$) model can be written compactly with the backshift operator $B$:

$$\phi(B)(1-B)^d y_t = \theta(B)\varepsilon_t$$ {#eq-arima}

where $\phi$ and $\theta$ are polynomials of order $p$ and $q$, and $\varepsilon_t$ is white noise.
The seasonal version multiplies in seasonal polynomials of period $m = 12$:

$$
\phi(B)\,\Phi(B^{m})\,(1-B)^{d}(1-B^{m})^{D}\, y_t = \theta(B)\,\Theta(B^{m})\,\varepsilon_t
$$ {#eq-sarima}

Candidates were chosen by hand, informed by the ACF and by `auto_arima` from **pmdarima** (which we don't use in production because it pins an old numpy).
We hold out the last 12 months, refit on the full series for the final forecast, and score on MAPE because that is what Finance reports.
See @hyndman2021 [chap. 9] for why MAPE is a questionable choice for series with values near zero; ours are nowhere near zero, so we live with it [@hyndman2021, chap. 9].

```{python}
#| label: fit-models
#| output: false
train, test = rev.iloc[:-12], rev.iloc[-12:]
exog_train, exog_test = one_off.iloc[:-12], one_off.iloc[-12:]

def mape_of(pred):
    return float(np.mean(np.abs((test - pred) / test)))

snaive = rev.shift(12).iloc[-12:]
ets = ExponentialSmoothing(train, trend="add", seasonal="add", seasonal_periods=12).fit()
sarima = SARIMAX(train, exog=exog_train, order=(1, 1, 1), seasonal_order=(0, 1, 1, 12)).fit(disp=False)

scores = {
    "Seasonal naïve": mape_of(snaive),
    "ETS(A,A,A)": mape_of(ets.forecast(12)),
    "SARIMA(1,1,1)(0,1,1)12": mape_of(sarima.forecast(12, exog=exog_test)),
}
mape = scores["SARIMA(1,1,1)(0,1,1)12"]
```

| Model                    |     AIC | MAPE (holdout) | Notes                              |
|:-------------------------|--------:|---------------:|:-----------------------------------|
| Seasonal naïve           |       — |           9.8% | benchmark only |
| ETS(A,A,A)               | 1,412.3 |           6.1% |  |
| SARIMA(1,1,1)(0,1,1)~12~ | 1,398.7 |       **4.9%** | chosen; one-off dummy passed as `exog` |
| Prophet (defaults) | n/a | 7.4% | over-smooths December, and nobody wants to maintain the holiday calendar |

: Model comparison on the 12-month holdout (Oct 2023 – Sep 2024). {#tbl-models}

The SARIMA model wins on every metric we looked at (@tbl-models), with a holdout MAPE of `{python} f"{mape:.1%}"`. That's good enough for planning, though not for anything that pays commission.


# Forecast

::: {#fig-forecast}

```{python}
#| echo: false
final = SARIMAX(rev, exog=one_off, order=(1, 1, 1), seasonal_order=(0, 1, 1, 12)).fit(disp=False)
fc = final.get_forecast(12, exog=np.zeros((12, 1)))
ci80, ci95 = fc.conf_int(alpha=0.20), fc.conf_int(alpha=0.05)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4))
rev.loc["2021":].plot(ax=ax, color="0.2", lw=1.5, label="Actual")
fc.predicted_mean.plot(ax=ax, color="C0", lw=2, label="Forecast")
ax.fill_between(ci95.index, ci95.iloc[:, 0], ci95.iloc[:, 1], color="C0", alpha=0.15, label="95%")
ax.fill_between(ci80.index, ci80.iloc[:, 0], ci80.iloc[:, 1], color="C0", alpha=0.30, label="80%")
ax.set_ylabel("Net revenue (EUR)")
ax.legend(frameon=False, ncol=4, loc="upper left")
```

Monthly net revenue: actuals since January 2021 and the twelve-month forecast with 80% and 95% prediction intervals.
:::

Reading @fig-forecast:

1. The December peak is forecast at about €5.6 M, similar to last year.
2. January–March are forecast **below** last year. This is the seasonal MA term doing its job after a weak Q1 2024, not a judgement call.
3. Intervals widen quickly; by September 2025 the 95% interval spans about ±€1.4 M.

## What this forecast does *not* include

- Price changes. The list-price increase planned for April 2025 is **not** modelled.
    - If it goes ahead, add roughly 2–3% from May onwards (Finance has the elasticity estimate).
    - If it slips to Q3, ignore this bullet.
- New products. The "Teams" tier launches in Q2; there is no history to learn from.
- FX. Everything is in EUR at historical rates. USD exposure is ~18% of revenue, GBP ~7%.

___

# Next steps

- [ ] Move the extract into the scheduled pipeline (ticket [DATA-2291][data-2291])
- [ ] Replace the hand-made `is_one_off` flag with a proper adjustments table
- [x] Agree MAPE as the reporting metric with Finance (done 28 Oct)
- [ ] Revisit in January with Q1 actuals

> **Reviewer note (M. Okafor, 1 Nov):** the holdout is a single year that includes the one-off.
> Consider rolling-origin evaluation [@hyndman2021, sec. 5.10] before the next planning cycle.
>
> Also: please stop calling it "the model". There are four.

[^fx]: Monthly average ECB reference rates, pulled from the `fx_rates` table. We do not hedge in this model; the treasury team's hedging programme is out of scope.

[data-2291]: https://jira.example.com/browse/DATA-2291 "Schedule revenue extract"

# References {.unnumbered}

::: {#refs}
:::

---
# AWS Amplify build settings (monorepo)
# https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/userguide/monorepo-configuration.html
#
# Two Next.js apps live in this repo:
#     apps/web     customer-facing site     (Amplify app: acme-web)
#     apps/admin   internal back-office     (Amplify app: acme-admin)
# Amplify picks the entry whose appRoot matches AMPLIFY_MONOREPO_APP_ROOT.
# Don't rename an appRoot without changing that env var in BOTH Amplify consoles.
version: 1
env:
  variables:
    NODE_OPTIONS: --max-old-space-size=8192
    NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"
    PNPM_VERSION:    8.15.5
    TURBO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: 1
    SENTRY_UPLOAD:     TRUE
applications:
  - appRoot: apps/web
    frontend:
      phases:
        preBuild:
          commands:
            - nvm use 20
            - corepack enable
            - corepack prepare pnpm@$PNPM_VERSION --activate
            - pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
        build:
          commands:
            - env | grep -e NEXT_PUBLIC_ >> .env.production
            - env | grep -e SENTRY_ >> .env.production || true
            - pnpm --filter @acme/web... run build
            # - pnpm run build:analyze     # only when chasing bundle size
        postBuild:
          commands:
          - |
            if [ "$AWS_BRANCH" = "main" ] && [ "$SENTRY_UPLOAD" = "true" ]; then
              npx @sentry/cli sourcemaps upload --org acme --project web .next/static
            else
              echo "skipping sourcemap upload for branch $AWS_BRANCH"
            fi
      artifacts:
        baseDirectory: .next
        files:
          - '**/*'
      cache:
        paths:
          - node_modules/**/*
          - .next/cache/**/*
          - "node_modules/.pnpm/**/*"
      buildPath: /
    test:
      phases:
        preTest:
          commands:
            - pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
            - pnpm add -D mocha mochawesome mochawesome-merge mochawesome-report-generator
        test:
          commands:
            - 'npx start-test "pnpm --filter @acme/web start" http://localhost:3000 "npx cypress run --reporter mochawesome --reporter-options reportDir=cypress/report/mochawesome-report,overwrite=false,html=false,json=true,timestamp=mmddyyyy_HHMMss"'
        postTest:
          commands:
            - npx mochawesome-merge cypress/report/mochawesome-report/mochawesome*.json > cypress/report/mochawesome.json
      artifacts:
        baseDirectory: cypress
        configFilePath: '**/mochawesome.json'
        files:
          - '**/*.png'
          - '**/*.mp4'
    customHeaders:
      - pattern: '**/*'
        headers:
          - key: 'Strict-Transport-Security'
            value: 'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload'
          - key: "X-Content-Type-Options"
            value: nosniff
          - key: Content-Security-Policy
            value: "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://www.googletagmanager.com; img-src 'self' data: https://images.acme.example.com; frame-ancestors 'none'"
      - pattern: '/_next/static/*'
        headers:
        - key: Cache-Control
          value: public, max-age=31536000, immutable


  -   appRoot: apps/admin
      frontend:
         phases:
            preBuild:
               commands: [ nvm use 20, corepack enable, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile ]
            build:
               commands: [
                   "env | grep -e NEXT_PUBLIC_ >> .env.production",
                   "pnpm --filter @acme/admin... run build"
                 ]
         artifacts:
            baseDirectory: .next
            files: [ '**/*' ]
         cache:
            paths:
               - node_modules/**/*
               - .next/cache/**/*
         buildPath:
    # admin has no cypress suite yet (TODO: ADM-112)
      customHeaders:
        - pattern: '**/*'
          headers:
            - { key: X-Robots-Tag, value: "noindex, nofollow" }
            - { key: X-Frame-Options,value: DENY }
            - {key: Referrer-Policy, value: no-referrer}

# Q3 2024 planning — Platform team

**Date:** Thu 2024-06-27, 14:00–16:10 CEST (ran 40 min over, sorry)  
**Where:** Room "Lovelace" + Zoom (link in the calendar invite)  
**Notes:** @jkowalski (first half), @amina-r (second half)  
**Status:** draft, please correct anything I got wrong directly in this doc

## Attendees

- @mrossi (EM, facilitating)
- @amina-r
- @jkowalski
- @t.nguyen — joined ~14:35
- @sofia.l (PM)
- @dkim (SRE, guest for item 3)
- absent: @pbauer (OOO), @lchen (sick)

## Agenda

1. Q2 retro: what shipped / what didn't (15 min)
2. OKR draft review (30 min)
3. Postgres 16 upgrade — go / no-go
4. On-call load & the pager situation
5. Hiring update
6. AOB

---

## 1. Q2 retro

- shipped
  - multi-region read replicas (finally!!)
  - new deploy pipeline, p50 ~35% faster, p95 basically unchanged
    - p50 win is mostly the docker layer cache, see PLAT-1182
    - p95 is dominated by the integration-test stage, which nobody owns
  - self-serve feature flags v1, adoption 11 teams out of 19
- didn't ship
  - cost dashboards — blocked on the finance data export, *again*
    - finance says end of July; @sofia.l is skeptical
  - k8s 1.29 upgrade, moved to Q3
  - runbook cleanup (nobody picked it up, which tells us something)
- went well: pairing on the replica work, fewer "quick questions" in #platform
  since we started the office hours
- went badly: three P2 incidents caused by config drift between staging & prod,
  two of them on a Friday

> "We keep saying staging is 'basically prod'. It isn't. It's prod's younger
> sibling that never cleans its room." — @t.nguyen

TODO: @jkowalski link the three incident docs here

---

## 2. OKR draft

Draft from @mrossi, discussed line by line. Numbers are the proposed targets, not commitments yet.

Objective | Key result | Baseline | Target | Owner
--- | --- | --- | --- | ---
O1 Reliable deploys | KR1 change failure rate | 14% | < 8% | @amina-r
O1 | KR2 p95 deploy time | 31 min |18 min| @jkowalski
O2 Cheaper infra | KR1 compute spend vs Q2 | 100% | 88% | @t.nguyen
O2 | KR2 % of services with cost labels | 41% | 95% | @sofia.l
O3 Happier on-call | KR1 pages / week (median) | 23 | ≤ 10 | @mrossi
O3 | KR2 runbooks for top-20 alerts | 6 | 20 | ???

Discussion:
- O2/KR1 might be too aggressive; @t.nguyen thinks 92% is realistic w/o
  touching the data platform, 88% only if we also move the batch jobs to spot
  - @dkim: spot for batch is fine, we did it at my last company, but you need
    checkpointing or you'll eat the retries
  - agreed to keep 88% as stretch, 92% as the "committed" number
- O3/KR2 has no owner. Nobody volunteered. Awkward silence. Moving on.
- @sofia.l asked whether "happier on-call" can be measured at all; proposal: add
  a 2-question survey after each rotation. People were lukewarm but nobody objected.

**Decision:** OKRs go to the dept. review on 07-03 with the changes above. O3/KR2
owner to be assigned by @mrossi before then.

---

## 3. Postgres 16 upgrade

@dkim presented the plan (slides in the shared drive, "pg16-upgrade-v3-FINAL-really.pdf").

- approach: logical replication to a new PG16 cluster, then switch over
  - est. downtime: < 60 s for the switchover itself
  - rollback = reverse replication, tested in staging twice
- risks
  - extensions: `pg_partman` needs a version bump first; `timescaledb` not used anymore
    (but the extension is still installed in 2 DBs?? → check)
  - sequences are not replicated by logical replication → must sync manually right
    before the switchover; script exists, see PLAT-1240
  - the analytics team's long-running queries — they need a heads-up 2 weeks in advance
- open question: do we do all 14 clusters in Q3 or just the 4 critical ones?

> @amina-r: "If we only do four we'll be running two major versions for half a
> year, and that's how we ended up on 12 in the first place."
>
> @dkim: "Fair. But four done properly beats fourteen done in a rush."

**Decision:** go for the 4 critical clusters in Q3 (`orders`, `billing`, `identity`, `catalog`),
remaining 10 in Q4. @dkim owns the plan, @amina-r is the platform counterpart.

---

## 4. On-call load

Short version: it's bad. Median 23 pages/week over the last 6 rotations; 60%+ are
from 5 alerts, and 3 of those 5 are flapping disk-space alerts on the CI runners.

* proposal (@mrossi): one "alert hygiene" day per sprint, whole team
* counter-proposal (@jkowalski): just delete the CI runner alerts, we have autoscaling
  - concern: we had a real disk-full outage on runners in March
  - compromise: convert them to tickets instead of pages
* someone (I didn't catch who) suggested an "alert budget" per team; parked for now

**Decision:** CI-runner disk alerts become non-paging tickets as of next week. Alert
hygiene day: try it twice, then decide.

---

## 5. Hiring

- 1 senior SRE req open; 2 candidates in final round, decision expected next week
- backend req is frozen until Q4 (company-wide, not our call)
- @sofia.l: please, please do the interview training if you haven't — we have only 3 trained interviewers

## 6. AOB

- offsite in September: Lisbon vs. Kraków vs. "anywhere with decent coffee" — poll in Slack
- @t.nguyen out 08-05 → 08-23

---

## Action items

- [ ] @jkowalski — link the 3 config-drift incident docs in these notes (**2024-06-28**)
- [ ] @mrossi — find an owner for O3/KR2 before the dept. review (**2024-07-02**)
- [x] @sofia.l — send updated OKR draft to the team (done during the meeting, thanks!)
- [ ] @dkim + @amina-r — PG16: final plan for the 4 critical clusters (**2024-07-12**)
  - [ ] check why the `timescaledb` extension is still installed in `reporting` and `legacy_api`
  - [ ] announce the maintenance plan to the analytics team (**≥ 2 weeks before**)
- [ ] @t.nguyen — draft spot-instance plan for batch jobs incl. checkpointing (**2024-07-19**)
- [ ] @mrossi — convert CI-runner disk alerts to tickets
- [ ] everyone — interview training, if not done yet

Next meeting: mid-quarter check-in, **Thu 2024-08-15**, same room.

  - new deploy pipeline, p50 ~35% faster, p95 basically unchanged
    - p50 win is mostly the docker layer cache, see PLAT-1182
    - p95 is dominated by the integration-test stage, which nobody owns
  - self-serve feature flags v1, adoption 11 teams out of 19
- didn't ship
  - cost dashboards — blocked on the finance data export, *again*
    - finance says end of July; @sofia.l is skeptical
  - k8s 1.29 upgrade, moved to Q3
  - runbook cleanup (nobody picked it up, which tells us something)
- went well: pairing on the replica work, fewer "quick questions" in #platform
  since we started the office hours
- went badly: three P2 incidents caused by config drift between staging & prod,
  two of them on a Friday

> "We keep saying staging is 'basically prod'. It isn't. It's prod's younger
> sibling that never cleans its room." — @t.nguyen

TODO: @jkowalski link the three incident docs here

---

## 2. OKR draft

Draft from @mrossi, discussed line by line. Numbers are the proposed targets, not commitments yet.

Objective | Key result | Baseline | Target | Owner
--- | --- | --- | --- | ---
O1 Reliable deploys | KR1 change failure rate | 14% | < 8% | @amina-r
O1 | KR2 p95 deploy time | 31 min |18 min| @jkowalski
O2 Cheaper infra | KR1 compute spend vs Q2 | 100% | 88% | @t.nguyen
O2 | KR2 % of services with cost labels | 41% | 95% | @sofia.l
O3 Happier on-call | KR1 pages / week (median) | 23 | ≤ 10 | @mrossi
O3 | KR2 runbooks for top-20 alerts | 6 | 20 | ???

Discussion:
- O2/KR1 might be too aggressive; @t.nguyen thinks 92% is realistic w/o
  touching the data platform, 88% only if we also move the batch jobs to spot
  - @dkim: spot for batch is fine, we did it at my last company, but you need
    checkpointing or you'll eat the retries
  - agreed to keep 88% as stretch, 92% as the "committed" number
- O3/KR2 has no owner. Nobody volunteered. Awkward silence. Moving on.
- @sofia.l asked whether "happier on-call" can be measured at all; proposal: add
  a 2-question survey after each rotation. People were lukewarm but nobody objected.

**Decision:** OKRs go to the dept. review on 07-03 with the changes above. O3/KR2
owner to be assigned by @mrossi before then.

---

## 3. Postgres 16 upgrade

@dkim presented the plan (slides in the shared drive, "pg16-upgrade-v3-FINAL-really.pdf").

- approach: logical replication to a new PG16 cluster, then switch over
  - est. downtime: < 60 s for the switchover itself
  - rollback = reverse replication, tested in staging twice
- risks
  - extensions: `pg_partman` needs a version bump first; `timescaledb` not used anymore
    (but the extension is still installed in 2 DBs?? → check)
  - sequences are not replicated by logical replication → must sync manually right
    before the switchover; script exists, see PLAT-1240
  - the analytics team's long-running queries — they need a heads-up 2 weeks in advance
- open question: do we do all 14 clusters in Q3 or just the 4 critical ones?

> @amina-r: "If we only do four we'll be running two major versions for half a
> year, and that's how we ended up on 12 in the first place."
>
> @dkim: "Fair. But four done properly beats fourteen done in a rush."

**Decision:** go for the 4 critical clusters in Q3 (`orders`, `billing`, `identity`, `catalog`),
remaining 10 in Q4. @dkim owns the plan, @amina-r is the platform counterpart.

## 4. On-call load

Short version: it's bad. Median 23 pages/week over the last 6 rotations; 60%+ are
from 5 alerts, and 3 of those 5 are flapping disk-space alerts on the CI runners.

* proposal (@mrossi): one "alert hygiene" day per sprint, whole team

  - compromise: convert them to tickets instead of pages
* someone (I didn't catch who) suggested an "alert budget" per team; parked for now

**Decision:** CI-runner disk alerts become non-paging tickets as of next week. Alert
hygiene day: try it twice, then decide.

arguments.content:
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  CI — acme/platform monorepo
#
#  lint / typecheck / unit / e2e for every workspace package touched by a change.
#  Turbo remote cache is shared with the Vercel team (see TURBO_* below).
#  Ping #dev-infra before touching the matrix -- branch protection matches jobs by *name*.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main,'release/**' ]
    paths-ignore:
    - '**.md'
    - 'docs/**'
    - .changeset/**
    - "LICENSE"
  pull_request:
    types:
      - opened
      - synchronize
      - reopened
      - ready_for_review
  merge_group:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      debug:
        description: 'Open a tmate session when a job fails'
        type: boolean
        required: false
        default: false

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read     # dorny/paths-filter needs this on PRs

env:
  TURBO_TOKEN:    ${{ secrets.TURBO_TOKEN }}
  TURBO_TEAM:     ${{ vars.TURBO_TEAM }}
  TURBO_REMOTE_ONLY:      true
  NODE_OPTIONS: --max-old-space-size=4096
  FORCE_COLOR: "1"
  PNPM_VERSION:   8.15.4
  # HUSKY: 0      # not needed anymore, husky v9 skips itself when CI=true
  DO_NOT_TRACK: 1


jobs:
  changes:
    name: Detect changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      packages:  ${{ steps.filter.outputs.packages }}
      web:       ${{ steps.filter.outputs.web }}
      e2e:       ${{ steps.filter.outputs.e2e }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
      id: filter
      with:
        # keep in sync with the "inputs" globs in turbo.json  (FIXME: generate this from turbo.json?)
        filters: |
          packages:
            - 'packages/**'
            - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
          web:
            - 'apps/web/**'
            - 'packages/ui/**'
          e2e:
            - 'apps/**'
            - 'e2e/**'


  lint:
    name: Lint
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.packages == 'true' || github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0     # turbo --filter=...[origin/main] needs the history
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.PNPM_VERSION }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: 'pnpm'
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: ESLint + Prettier (affected packages only)
        run: pnpm turbo run lint format:check --filter="...[origin/${{ github.base_ref || 'main' }}]"
      # - name: Stylelint
      #   run: pnpm -r --parallel exec stylelint "**/*.css"
      #   (disabled until the design-system migration lands, see #1873)

  typecheck:
    name: Typecheck
    needs: [changes]
    if: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.packages == 'true' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
      with: { version: "${{ env.PNPM_VERSION }}" }
    - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version-file: .nvmrc
        cache: pnpm
    - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
    - run: pnpm turbo run typecheck --continue



  test:
    name: Unit (node ${{ matrix.node }}, ${{ matrix.os }}, ${{ matrix.shard }})
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.packages == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 25
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental == true }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: [ 18, 20,22 ]
        os:   [ubuntu-latest , windows-latest]
        shard: [1/3, 2/3, 3/3]
        experimental: [false]
        exclude:
          # node 18 + windows + vitest threads = random segfaults, see #2291
          - os: windows-latest
            node: 18
        include:
          -   node: 23
              os: ubuntu-latest
              shard: 1/1
              experimental: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.PNPM_VERSION }}
      - name: Setup node ${{ matrix.node }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache:   pnpm

      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline
      - name: Test
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # only packages affected since main (plus their dependents)
          pnpm turbo run test --filter=...[origin/main] -- \
            --shard=${{ matrix.shard }} \
            --reporter=default --reporter=junit \
            --outputFile.junit=reports/junit-${{ matrix.node }}-${{ strategy.job-index }}.xml
        env:
          TZ: UTC
          VITEST_MAX_THREADS:   4

      - name: Upload test reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: junit-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.node }}-${{ strategy.job-index }}
          path: '**/reports/junit-*.xml'
          retention-days: 05
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          # tmate only when explicitly requested via workflow_dispatch
      - name: Debug session
        if: ${{ failure() && inputs.debug }}
        uses: mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3
        with:
          limit-access-to-actor: true

  e2e:
    name: E2E (Playwright)
    needs: [changes, test]
    if: >-
      needs.changes.outputs.e2e == 'true' &&
      github.event.pull_request.draft != true
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    timeout-minutes: 40
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: acme
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: acme
          POSTGRES_DB:    acme_e2e
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U acme"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      redis:
         image: redis:7
         ports: [ '6379:6379' ]
         options: --health-cmd "redis-cli ping" --health-interval 10s --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 5 --health-start-period 5s
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://acme:acme@localhost:5432/acme_e2e
      REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379/0
      BASE_URL: http://localhost:3000
      PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH: ~/.cache/ms-playwright
      SENTRY_DSN:
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
      with:
        version: ${{ env.PNPM_VERSION }}
    - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: 20
        cache: pnpm
    - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
    - run: pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium
    - name: Migrate + seed
      run: |
        pnpm --filter @acme/db run migrate:deploy
        pnpm --filter @acme/db run seed -- --profile e2e
    - name: Start app & wait for it
      run: |
        pnpm turbo run start --filter=@acme/web --filter=@acme/api > app.log 2>&1 &
        for i in $(seq 1 90); do
          curl -fsS "$BASE_URL/api/health" > /dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0
          sleep 1
        done
        echo "::error::app did not come up within 90s"; tail -n 200 app.log; exit 1
    - name: Run e2e
      run: pnpm exec playwright test --project=chromium --reporter=github,html
    - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
      with:
        name: playwright-report
        path: |
          playwright-report/
          app.log
        retention-days: 7


  build:
    name: Build
    needs: [lint, typecheck, test]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.PNPM_VERSION }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm turbo run build --filter="./apps/*" --summarize
      - name: Upload build output
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-${{ github.sha }}
          path: |
            apps/web/.next/
            !apps/web/.next/cache
            apps/api/dist/
          retention-days: 05
      - name: Notify Slack on failure
        if: ${{ failure() && github.event_name == 'push' }}
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1.26.0
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL:  ${{ secrets.SLACK_CI_WEBHOOK }}
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_TYPE: INCOMING_WEBHOOK
        with:
          payload: |
            {"text": ":red_circle: CI failed on `${{ github.ref_name }}` (${{ github.actor }}): ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}",
             "username": "ci-bot", "icon_emoji": ":rotating_light:"}

  # Single required status check for the branch ruleset. If you rename this job,
  # update Settings > Rules > "main" as well or every PR will hang forever.
  ci-ok:
    name: CI OK
    if: always()
    needs: [ lint, typecheck,test, e2e, build ]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All required jobs passed (or were skipped)
        run: |
          echo '${{ toJSON(needs) }}' | jq -e 'all(.[]; .result == "success" or .result == "skipped")'

---
title: "Quarterly Sales Report — Q2 2024"
subtitle: "Region: EMEA · internal, please do not forward"
author: "Analytics Team (prepared by M. Okafor)"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 3
    toc_float:
      collapsed: false
      smooth_scroll: false
    number_sections: true
    df_print: paged
    code_folding: hide
    theme: flatly
    highlight: tango
params:
  region: "EMEA"
  quarter: 2
  fiscal_year: 2024
  fx_usd: 1.0813
editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: console
  markdown:
    wrap: sentence
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 5,
  fig.align = "center",
  dpi = 150
)

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
eur <- label_dollar(prefix = "€", big.mark = ",", accuracy = 1)
```

```{r load-data, cache=TRUE}
sales <- readr::read_csv(
  here::here("data", "sales_fy2024.csv"),
  col_types = readr::cols(order_date = readr::col_date("%Y-%m-%d"))
)
targets <- readxl::read_xlsx(here::here("data", "targets_fy24.xlsx"), sheet = "Q2")

q2 <- sales |>
  filter(region == params$region,
         lubridate::quarter(order_date) == params$quarter)

total_rev   <- sum(q2$net_revenue)
prev_rev    <- 11873420   # Q1 close, per Finance memo No. 3
growth_pct  <- (total_rev - prev_rev) / prev_rev
n_orders    <- nrow(q2)
n_customers <- n_distinct(q2$customer_id)
aov         <- total_rev / n_orders
```

<!-- MO 2024-07-09: numbers are from the 2024-07-08 extract. Re-knit after the July close
     in case Finance restates anything (they did last quarter, twice). -->


# Executive summary #

Net revenue for `r params$region` in Q`r params$quarter` `r params$fiscal_year` came to `r eur(total_rev)`, i.e. `r percent(growth_pct, accuracy = 0.1)` above Q1. This is the strongest quarter since the 2022 price change, although approx. one third of the uplift comes from two framework agreements signed in the last week of May.
Both deals were closed by Dr. Patel's team in Frankfurt; without them, growth would have been closer to 4% vs. the 6% we had planned.
The number of active customers rose to `r comma(n_customers)` (Q1: 1,412), while the average order value stayed roughly flat at `r eur(aov)`. For the group consolidation, which Acme Holdings Inc. reports in dollars to its U.S. shareholders, the headline figure is `r scales::dollar(total_rev * params$fx_usd)`; the unconverted amount, `r scales::dollar(total_rev)`, is what appears in the board pack with the € sign stripped (yes, really).

Three caveats up front.
First, April includes a one-off correction of €212k for invoices that were double-counted in March (see Finance memo No. 3 of 12 April).
Second, the UK entity migrated to the new ERP on 3 June at 4 p.m. CET, so a handful of orders
placed that evening were booked in early July.
We expect the effect to be small, but it is not zero!
Third, FX: all figures are converted at the monthly average rate published by Treasury, not at the transaction-date rate, which matters mostly for TRY and PLN (cf. the methodology note in the appendix).

> **TL;DR for the leadership call:** we beat the revenue target, mostly thanks to two deals that will not repeat in Q3. Margin is slightly below plan.
>
> The pipeline for Q3 looks _thin_ in the partner channel and __healthy__ in direct.
> See *Risks and next steps* before anyone commits to the H2 number.
>
> > Forwarded from the regional VP (11 July): "Please make sure the deck says clearly that the framework deals are one-offs. Last year the board extrapolated Q2 and we spent all of Q4 explaining why we missed."



# Revenue trend

```{r revenue-trend, fig.cap="Monthly revenue by channel, Q2 2024."}
q2 |>
  mutate(month = lubridate::floor_date(order_date, "month")) |>
  group_by(month, channel) |>
  summarise(revenue = sum(net_revenue), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(month, revenue, fill = channel)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 20) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = eur) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Net revenue", fill = "Channel")
```

Fig. 1 shows the usual pattern: April is soft, May is strong and June flattens out. Easter fell on 31 March this year, so the April dip is smaller than in 2023. Online grew in every single month.
The partner channel is lumpy, as always, because a handful of distributors place quarterly stocking orders; e.g. Brenntag-Nord alone accounted for €0.9m in May.
Direct sales were down 3% in June vs. May. That is within normal variation and we would not read much into it... but see the pipeline comments below.

Compared with Q2 2023 (Fig. 2 in last year's report), the mix has shifted towards online by roughly four percentage points.
Our working assumption, following Okafor et al. (internal analysis, 2023), is that about half of this shift is substitution from direct
rather than new demand. Nobody has tested that properly yet.

## Top products

```{r top-products, results='asis'}
top10 <- q2 |>
  group_by(sku, product_name) |>
  summarise(units = sum(quantity), revenue = sum(net_revenue), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(revenue, n = 10)

kable(top10, format = "html", digits = 0,
      col.names = c("SKU", "Product", "Units", "Revenue (EUR)"),
      caption = "Top 10 products by net revenue, EMEA, Q2 2024") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) |>
  print()
```

The 300-series still makes up six of the top ten. Hand-maintained KPI table below (Finance asked for exactly this format, sorry):

| KPI | Q2 actual | Target | Δ vs. target | Comment |
|:----|----------:|-------:|:------------:|:--------|
| Net revenue | `r eur(total_rev)` | €12.4m | +2.1 % | Includes the two framework deals; excluding them we are approx. 1.8 % *below* target |
| Orders | `r comma(n_orders)` |9,800| −4.0 % |Fewer, larger orders (partner channel) |
|Active customers| `r comma(n_customers)` | 1,450 | +3.2 % | Definition changed in April, see `customer_active_flag` in `finance_mart.dim_customer` |
| Gross margin | 41.7 % | 42.0 % | −0.3 pp | FX headwind (TRY, PLN); freight surcharges on the Rotterdam route |
| Returns rate| 2.9 % | ≤ 3.0 % | ok | |

## Regional breakdown {.tabset}

<!-- tabs only work in the HTML output; in the Word export the three sections simply follow each other -->

### EMEA

```{r region-emea, fig.height=4}
q2 |>
  count(country, wt = net_revenue, name = "revenue", sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 12) |>
  ggplot(aes(reorder(country, revenue), revenue)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2C7FB8") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = eur) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

Germany, France and the Netherlands account for 58% of EMEA revenue, up from 55% a year ago. Growth in the Nordics was driven by a single customer (Fjord Logistikk AS), so treat the +31% with care.
Southern Europe is flat.
Mr. Rossi's comment in the June forecast call ("Italy is waiting for the incentive scheme, nothing more.") still seems right to us. Société Lumière and Müller & Söhne GmbH both moved their orders from June into July.

### Americas

Shown for context only.
The Americas numbers are owned by the Austin team and are reported separately (their Q2 deck is linked at the bottom). Revenue was up 2.4% q/q.

### APAC

APAC had a weak quarter (−5.8% q/q). Most of the decline is Japan, where the yen lost approx. 7% vs. the euro over the quarter; in local currency Japan actually grew slightly.
Is this an FX story or a demand story? Mostly FX, we think.

- - -

# Channel mix and pipeline

The share of online revenue keeps creeping up, from 27% in Q2 2023 to 31% this quarter. A few observations, roughly in order of importance:

1. **Online.** Conversion improved after the checkout redesign went live on 22 April. Bounce rate on product pages fell from 48% to 41%, although part of that is a tracking change (the consent banner now loads asynchronously). We would like to see one more quarter before calling it structural.
2. **Partners.** Stocking orders are lumpy, e.g. two distributors ordered six months of stock in May.
   Two distributors in Poland have asked for extended payment terms (90 days vs. the usual 60). Finance has not decided yet.
3. **Direct.** Average deal size was €48k, about the same as in Q1. Win rate against our main competitor improved to 38% (Q1: 33%), which Sales attributes to the new bundle pricing; we have not been able to verify this independently.

The weighted pipeline for Q3 stands at €13.1m, i.e. approx. 1.05× the Q3 target. Historically we needed at least 1.2× coverage to hit the number, so this is tight.

* Pipeline by stage (weighted, € m):
  - Qualified: 4.2
  - Proposal: 5.0
      + of which deals > €250k: 2.1
      + of which renewals: 0.8
  - Negotiation: 3.9
* Slippage from Q2 into Q3: €1.4m across 23 opportunities.
    - Most of these are in DACH.
    - Three are flagged "customer budget freeze". One of them (opportunity No. 4471) has now been pushed four quarters in a row.

***

# Risks and next steps

Things that could move the Q3 number, as discussed with Prof. Lindqvist (our external advisor) on 4 July:

4) FX exposure in TRY, which is unhedged above €2m. A further 10% depreciation would cost us approx. €150k in reported revenue.
5) The ERP migration in France, currently planned for 2 September. If it slips, it slips into the busiest month of the quarter… not ideal.
6) The price increase on the 300-series (+4.5%, effective 1 August). Customers were notified in June. So far only two have objected in writing.

Next steps:

- [x] Share draft with the Regional VPs (done 9 July)
- [ ] Re-run after the July close and update the FX table
- [ ] Turn the Americas tab into a real comparison — currently just text
  - [ ] ask Austin for their extract (J. Álvarez)
- [ ] Agree the "active customer" definition with Finance and CRM Ops



Appendix {-}
========

Data notes
----------

The extract is taken from the `sales_fy2024` table in the warehouse (schema `finance_mart`), filtered to `region == "EMEA"` and `order_status %in% c("invoiced", "paid")`. Returns are netted against the original order month, not the month in which they were received.[^returns] Customer counts use the definition introduced in April 2024: a customer is *active* if they placed at least one invoiced order in the trailing twelve months.

The FX methodology follows Treasury's guideline (see the [FX policy on the intranet](https://intranet.acme-corp.example/finance/treasury/policies/fx-translation-methodology-v3.pdf?version=3.2&lang=en#section-4)), which in turn is based on IAS 21.
For background, Smith et al. (2019) give a readable overview of the trade-offs between average and spot rates.

Related reports: the [Q1 report][q1], the [Americas Q2 deck][amer], and the [pricing memo][pricing].

___

**Questions?** Ask in #sales-analytics on Slack
or e-mail analytics@acme-corp.example\
Office hours: Tuesdays and Thursdays, 2–3 p.m. CET

[^returns]: This differs from the U.S. reporting package, where returns are booked in the month they are received. The difference was approx. €40k in Q2.

[q1]: https://reports.acme-corp.example/sales/emea/2024-q1.html "Q1 2024 EMEA report"
[amer]: https://acme.sharepoint.example/sites/sales-americas/Shared%20Documents/Q2-2024/Americas_Q2_review_FINAL_v7.pptx
[pricing]: https://intranet.acme-corp.example/pricing/memos/2024-06-300-series-increase

# backup-operator: CRD + RBAC + an example Backup.
#
# Source of truth is acme/backup-operator/config/crd (controller-gen v0.14.0), but the CRD below
# was hand-patched because controller-gen can't express the cron pattern. Regenerate with care
# and re-apply the patch from hack/crd-schedule-pattern.patch afterwards.
---
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
    name: backups.ops.acme.example.com
    annotations:
        controller-gen.kubebuilder.io/version: v0.14.0
        api-approved.kubernetes.io: "unapproved, experimental-only"
spec:
    group: ops.acme.example.com
    names:
        kind: Backup
        listKind: BackupList
        plural: backups
        singular: backup
        shortNames: [ bk,bkp ]
        categories:
        - acme
        - all
    scope: Namespaced
    versions:
    -   name: v1alpha1
        served: true
        storage: true
        subresources:
            status: {}
        additionalPrinterColumns:
        -   name: Schedule
            type: string
            jsonPath: .spec.schedule
        -   name: Phase
            type: string
            jsonPath: .status.phase
        -   name: Last Backup
            type: date
            jsonPath: .status.lastSuccessfulTime
        -   name: Age
            type: date
            jsonPath: .metadata.creationTimestamp
        schema:
            openAPIV3Schema:
                description: Backup describes a scheduled logical or physical backup of a database instance managed by the backup-operator, including retention and storage target settings.
                type: object
                required: [spec]
                properties:
                    apiVersion:
                        type: string
                    kind:
                        type: string
                    metadata:
                        type: object
                    spec:
                        type: object
                        required:
                            - schedule
                            - target
                            - storage

arguments.content:
# Decap CMS (formerly Netlify CMS) configuration
# Served from /admin/ — see static/admin/index.html
# Docs: https://decapcms.org/docs/configuration-options/
#
# !! Editors: please don't rename field `name`s — they map 1:1 to front matter keys
#    in content/**. Renaming one silently drops the data on the next save.

backend:
  name: git-gateway
  branch: main
  squash_merges: true
  commit_messages:
    create: 'Create {{collection}} “{{slug}}”'
    update: 'Update {{collection}} “{{slug}}”'
    delete: 'Delete {{collection}} “{{slug}}”'
    uploadMedia: '[skip ci] Upload “{{path}}”'
    deleteMedia: "[skip ci] Delete “{{path}}”"
    openAuthoring: '{{message}}'

# run `npx decap-server` next to `hugo server` and flip this on for local editing (no auth)
local_backend: true

publish_mode: editorial_workflow
media_folder: "static/images/uploads"
public_folder: "/images/uploads"
media_library:
  name: uploadcare
  config:
    publicKey: demopublickey      # FIXME: real key lives in the Netlify env, this is the demo one
    multiple: true
    previewStep: TRUE

site_url: https://www.acme-coffee.example.com
display_url:  https://www.acme-coffee.example.com
logo_url: https://www.acme-coffee.example.com/images/logo-cms.svg
locale: 'en'
show_preview_links: yes
search: true


i18n:
   structure: multiple_folders
   locales: [en, de, fr]
   default_locale: en

slug:
  encoding: "ascii"
  clean_accents: true
  sanitize_replacement: "_"


collections:
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ journal / blog
  - name: "blog"
    label: "Blog"
    label_singular: "Post"
    description: >-
      Long-form articles for the Journal section. Posts with "Draft" switched on are never
      published, even after the PR is merged — check the toggle before you hit Publish.
    folder: "content/blog"
    create: true
    i18n: true
    slug: "{{year}}-{{month}}-{{day}}-{{slug}}"
    preview_path: "journal/{{slug}}"
    summary: "{{title}} — {{commit_date}}"
    sortable_fields: ['commit_date', 'title', "date", author]
    view_filters:
      - label: Drafts
        field: draft
        pattern: true
      - {label: "Posts from 2024", field: date, pattern: '2024'}
    view_groups:
      - label: Year
        field: date
        # first four characters of the ISO date
        pattern: \d{4}
    fields:
      - { label: "Title", name: "title", widget: "string", i18n: true }
      - {label: "Publish Date", name: "date", widget: "datetime", format: "YYYY-MM-DD", date_format: "DD.MM.YYYY", time_format: false}
      - { label: "Draft",   name: "draft",  widget: "boolean", default: true }
      - {label: Tags, name: tags, widget: list, default: [news]}
      - label: "Featured image"
        name: "image"
        widget: "image"
        required: false
        choose_url: true
        media_library:
          config:
            multiple: false
      - {
          label: "Excerpt",
          name: "excerpt",
          widget: "text",
          required: false,
          hint: "Shown on the journal index and in social cards. Keep it under 160 characters or Google cuts it off mid-sentence.",
          i18n: true
        }
      - label: "Author"
        name: "author"
        widget: "relation"
        collection: "authors"
        search_fields: ["name", 'email']
        value_field: "{{slug}}"
        display_fields: ["{{name}} ({{email}})"]
      - label: Body
        name: body
        widget: markdown
        i18n: true
        buttons: [bold, italic, link, heading-two, heading-three, quote, bulleted-list, numbered-list]
        editor_components: [image, code-block]
        modes: [ rich_text,raw ]


  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ authors
  - name: authors
    label: Authors
    folder: content/authors
    create: true
    identifier_field: name
    slug: "{{fields.name}}"
    editor:
       preview: false
    fields:
      -   {label: Name, name: name, widget: string}
      -   {label: "E-mail", name: email, widget: string,
           pattern: ['^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$', "Must be a valid e-mail address"]}
      -   {label: Avatar, name: avatar, widget: image, required: false}
      -   label: Bio
          name: bio
          widget: markdown
          minimal: true
          required: false
          hint:

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ pages
  - name: pages
    label: Pages
    folder: content/pages
    create: true
    i18n:
      structure: multiple_files
    fields:
      - {label: Title, name: title, widget: string, i18n: true}
      - label: Slug
        name: slug
        widget: string
        pattern: ['^[a-z0-9-]+$', "Must be lowercase letters, numbers, dashes"]
        hint: >-
          Used in the URL, e.g. "opening-hours" becomes /opening-hours/. Changing it after
          publishing breaks inbound links unless you also add a redirect in netlify.toml.
      - {label: "SEO title",name: seo_title, widget: string, required: false, default: ''}
      - {label: "SEO description", name: seo_description, widget: text, required: false,
         hint: 'Leave empty to fall back to the first paragraph. 150-160 characters works best for search results.'}
      - label: Body
        name: body
        widget: markdown

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ settings (single files)
  - name: settings
    label: Site settings
    delete: false
    editor:
        preview: false
    files:
    - label: "General"
      name: general
      file: "data/settings.yml"
      fields:
        - {label: Site title, name: title, widget: string}
        - {label: Tagline, name: tagline, widget: string, required: false}
        - label: Opening hours
          name: hours
          widget: list
          summary: '{{fields.day}}: {{fields.open}}–{{fields.close}}'
          fields:
            - {label: Day, name: day, widget: select, options: [Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun]}
            - {label: Opens, name: open, widget: string, default: "08:00"}
            - {label: Closes, name: close, widget: string, default: "18:00"}
        - label: Contact
          name: contact
          widget: object
          collapsed: true
          fields:
            - {label: Phone, name: phone, widget: string}
            - {label: Email, name: email, widget: string}
            - {label: Address, name: address, widget: text}
    - label: "Navigation"
      name: navigation
      file: data/navigation.yml
      fields:
        - label: Main menu
          name: main
          widget: list
          fields:
            - {label: Label, name: label, widget: string}
            - {label: URL, name: url, widget: string}
            - label: Children
              name: children
              widget: list
              required: false
              fields:
                - {label: Label, name: label, widget: string}
                - {label: URL, name: url, widget: string}
        - label: Footer links
          name: footer
          widget: list
          field: {label: Link, name: link, widget: string}
    # - label: "Announcement bar"     # parked until the redesign ships (ACME-431)
    #   name: announcement
    #   file: data/announcement.yml
    #   fields:
    #     - {label: Text, name: text, widget: string}
    #     - {label: Visible, name: visible, widget: boolean, default: false}

arguments.content:
# Release pipeline for `acmectl`
#
# Triggered by pushing a tag like v1.4.0 / v1.5.0-rc.1, or manually from the Actions
# tab (handy for re-running a botched release -- delete the draft release first!).
#
#   artifacts : tar.gz for linux + macOS, zip for windows, SHA256SUMS
#   publishes : GitHub release, Homebrew tap (stable only)
---
name: Release

on:
    push:
        tags: ['v*.*.*']
    workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
            version:
                description: Version to release without the leading v, e.g. 1.4.0 or 1.5.0-rc.1 (must match Cargo.toml and the tag you pushed)
                required: true
                type: string
            prerelease: { type: boolean, default: false }
            dry-run:
                description: "Build everything but don't publish anything"
                type: boolean
                default: no

permissions: { contents: write, packages: write, id-token: write }

env:
    BIN_NAME: acmectl
    CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
    # bump when the release notes template changes
    NOTES_TEMPLATE_VERSION: '2'
    MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET: 10.13
    # set to 'true' once the new code-signing cert is in the org secrets (INFRA-882)
    SIGNING_ENABLED:


jobs:
    prepare:
        name: Prepare
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        outputs:
            version: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}
            tag: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}
            is_prerelease: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.is_prerelease }}
        steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - id: meta
              name: Compute version
              shell: bash
              run: |
                  set -euo pipefail
                  if [[ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
                      VERSION="${{ inputs.version }}"
                  else
                      VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
                  fi
                  echo "version=${VERSION}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  echo "tag=v${VERSION}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  # anything with a dash (1.5.0-rc.1) is a prerelease
                  if [[ "$VERSION" == *-* || "${{ inputs.prerelease }}" == "true" ]]; then
                      echo "is_prerelease=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  else
                      echo "is_prerelease=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  fi
            - name: Check Cargo.toml agrees
              run: |
                  CARGO_VERSION=$(grep -m1 '^version' Cargo.toml | cut -d '"' -f2)
                  if [ "$CARGO_VERSION" != "${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}" ]; then
                      echo "::error::Cargo.toml says $CARGO_VERSION but we're releasing ${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}"
                      exit 1
                  fi

    build:
        name: Build ${{ matrix.target }}
        needs: prepare
        runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
        strategy:
            fail-fast: true
            matrix:
                include:
                    - { os: ubuntu-latest, target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, archive: tar.gz }
                    - { os: ubuntu-latest,  target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl,   archive: tar.gz, cross: true }
                    - {os: ubuntu-latest, target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, archive: tar.gz, cross: true}
                    - { os: macos-13,       target: x86_64-apple-darwin,      archive: tar.gz }
                    - { os: macos-14 , target: aarch64-apple-darwin , archive: tar.gz }
                    - { os: windows-latest, target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, archive: zip,ext: .exe }
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
            with:
              targets: ${{ matrix.target }}
          - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
            with:
              key: ${{ matrix.target }}

          - name: Install cross
            if: matrix.cross
            run: cargo install cross --locked --git https://github.com/cross-rs/cross --rev 44011c8

          - name: Build
            shell: bash
            run: |
              set -euo pipefail
              CARGO=cargo
              [[ "${{ matrix.cross }}" == "true" ]] && CARGO=cross
              $CARGO build --release --locked --target ${{ matrix.target }}

          - name: Sign binary (windows)
            if: runner.os == 'Windows' && env.SIGNING_ENABLED == 'true'
            shell: pwsh
            env:
              SIGN_CERT_B64: ${{ secrets.WINDOWS_SIGN_CERT }}
              SIGN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.WINDOWS_SIGN_PASSWORD }}
            run: |
              $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
              [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes("cert.pfx", [Convert]::FromBase64String($env:SIGN_CERT_B64))
              & signtool.exe sign /fd SHA256 /tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 /f cert.pfx /p $env:SIGN_PASSWORD "target\${{ matrix.target }}\release\acmectl.exe"
              Remove-Item cert.pfx

          - name: Package
            shell: bash
            run: |
              set -euo pipefail
              VERSION="${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}"
              STAGE="${BIN_NAME}-${VERSION}-${{ matrix.target }}"
              mkdir -p "dist/$STAGE"
              cp "target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/${BIN_NAME}${{ matrix.ext }}" "dist/$STAGE/"
              cp README.md LICENSE-MIT LICENSE-APACHE CHANGELOG.md "dist/$STAGE/"
              cat > "dist/$STAGE/INSTALL.txt" <<EOF
              ${BIN_NAME} ${VERSION} (${{ matrix.target }})

              Copy the binary somewhere on your PATH, e.g. /usr/local/bin, then run
              '${BIN_NAME} --help' to get started.
              EOF
              cd dist
              case "${{ matrix.archive }}" in
                tar.gz) tar czf "$STAGE.tar.gz" "$STAGE" ;;
                zip)    7z a -tzip "$STAGE.zip" "$STAGE" > /dev/null ;;
                *)      echo "unknown archive type: ${{ matrix.archive }}" >&2; exit 1 ;;
              esac
              echo "ASSET=dist/$STAGE.${{ matrix.archive }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: dist-${{ matrix.target }}
              path: ${{ env.ASSET }}
              if-no-files-found: error

    checksums:
        name: Checksums
        needs: [prepare, build]
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
        -   uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
                pattern: dist-*
                path: dist
                merge-multiple: true
        -   name: SHA256SUMS
            working-directory: dist
            run: sha256sum -- * | tee SHA256SUMS
        -   uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
                name: checksums
                path: dist/SHA256SUMS



    release:
        name: GitHub release
        needs: [ prepare, build, checksums ]
        if: ${{ !inputs.dry-run }}
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
              with:
                  path: dist
                  merge-multiple: true
            - name: Extract release notes
              shell: bash
              run: |
                  # pull this version's section out of CHANGELOG.md
                  awk -v ver="${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}" '
                    /^## \[/ { if (found) exit; if (index($0, "[" ver "]")) found = 1; next }
                    found    { print }
                  ' CHANGELOG.md > RELEASE_NOTES.md
                  test -s RELEASE_NOTES.md || echo "See CHANGELOG.md for details." > RELEASE_NOTES.md
            - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
              with:
                  tag_name: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
                  name: "acmectl ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}"
                  body_path: RELEASE_NOTES.md
                  draft: false
                  prerelease: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.is_prerelease }}
                  fail_on_unmatched_files: true
                  files: |
                      dist/*.tar.gz
                      dist/*.zip
                      dist/SHA256SUMS
                  discussion_category_name: ~
                  generate_release_notes: false

    homebrew:
        name: Bump Homebrew formula
        needs: [prepare, release]
        # stable releases only -- rc/beta versions contain a dash
        if: ${{ !contains(needs.prepare.outputs.version, '-') }}
        runs-on: macos-latest
        env:
            HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN }}
            HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API:
            HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE: 1
        steps:
            - name: Bump formula
              uses: mislav/bump-homebrew-formula-action@v3
              with:
                  formula-name: acmectl
                  homebrew-tap: acme/homebrew-tap
                  base-branch: main
                  download-url: https://github.com/acme/acmectl/releases/download/${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}/acmectl-${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
                  commit-message: "{{formulaName}} {{version}}\n\nCreated by https://github.com/acme/acmectl/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }} — please don't edit this formula by hand, the next release overwrites it."
...

>
> > — paraphrasing basically every senior engineer, ever

# Snapshots, not diffs {background-image="img/branch.png" background-opacity="0.15"}

## A commit is a snapshot

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}
Every commit records the state of the **whole** project at that moment, plus:

- who made it
- when
- a message saying _why_
- a pointer to its parent commit(s)
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
![](images/snapshot.svg){fig-alt="A row of boxes, each a full copy of the project folder, connected by arrows pointing backwards in time."}
:::

::::

. . .

Git is clever about storage — unchanged files are not copied again — but you can *think* of it as a full copy every time.

## The three areas

| Area | What lives there | How it gets there |
|------|------------------|-------------------|
| Working tree | the files you're editing | you, in RStudio / VS Code |
| Staging area ("index") | changes you've picked for the next commit | `git add` |
| Repository | the history of commits | `git commit` |

::: aside
The staging area confuses everyone at first. It's a feature: it lets you commit *part* of your work.
:::

---

![](images/three-areas.svg){width="80%" fig-align="center"}

## Your first commit {.smaller}

```{.bash code-line-numbers="2-3"}
git init
git add clean_data.R README.md
git commit -m "Add data cleaning script"
git log --oneline
```

. . .

- Line 2 *stages* two files
- Line 3 records the snapshot, with a message

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
**Good commit messages** say _why_, not _what_: "Drop 2019 rows — sensor recalibrated" beats "update script".
:::

## Branches are just labels

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 8
gitGraph
   commit id: "init"
   commit id: "clean data"
   branch outliers
   checkout outliers
   commit id: "try IQR filter"
   commit id: "tune threshold"
   checkout main
   commit id: "fix typo"
   merge outliers
   commit id: "report v1"
```

A branch costs [41 bytes]{.fragment}. Make lots of them.

::: {.notes}
The 41 bytes thing: a branch is a file containing a 40-char SHA plus a newline.
Don't go down the SHA-256 rabbit hole if someone asks.
:::

## Working with a remote

1. `git clone` — get a copy
2. `git pull` — bring in other people's commits
3. `git push` — send yours

. . .

```bash
git switch -c fix/outlier-threshold
# ...edit, add, commit...
git push -u origin fix/outlier-threshold
```

Then open a pull request (GitHub) or merge request (GitLab). See the [guild's PR checklist](https://wiki.example.org/display/DSG/Pull+Request+Checklist?src=slides&version=7#before-you-ask-for-review).

---

## When things go wrong {background-color="black"}

::: {.incremental}
- "I committed to the wrong branch" → `git switch -c new-branch`, then reset the old one
- "I want to undo my last commit" → `git revert HEAD` (safe) or `git reset --soft HEAD~1` (local only!)
- "There's a merge conflict" → open the file, look for `<<<<<<<`, decide, `git add`, commit
- "I've made a mess" → `git reflog` remembers everything for ~90 days
:::

## Demo

{{< video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uR6G2v_WsRA width="100%" height="85%" >}}

::: {.notes}
If the wifi is bad, the recording is also in `demo/` on the shared drive.
:::

## Cheat sheet {.smaller}

| I want to…                       | Command                              |
|:---------------------------------|:-------------------------------------|
| see what changed                 | `git status`, `git diff`             |
| stage part of a file             | `git add -p`                         |
| see history                      | `git log --oneline --graph --all`    |
| throw away local edits to a file | `git restore path/to/file` |
| work on something new | `git switch -c my-branch` |

## Thanks! {background-color="#1e1e2e"}

- Slides: <https://guild.example.org/talks/git-for-the-rest-of-us>
- Exercises: `github.com/acme-guild/git-katas` (ask me for access)
- Next session (16 May): *Code review without tears*
