# acme/platform Monorepo for Acme's customer-facing web platform: the Next.js storefront, the admin dashboard, shared UI components, and a handful of internal libraries. Everything is TypeScript, managed with **pnpm workspaces** and **Turborepo**. ## Packages | Package | Version | Description | |:--------|:-------:|:------------| | [`apps/storefront`](apps/storefront) | — | Public storefront (Next.js 14, App Router) | | [`apps/admin`](apps/admin) | — | Internal admin dashboard (Vite + React) | | [`@acme/ui`](packages/ui) | ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@acme/ui?label=&color=0b7285) | Design-system components; Storybook at | | [`@acme/config-eslint`](packages/config-eslint) | ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@acme/config-eslint?label=) | Shared ESLint flat config | | [`@acme/config-ts`](packages/config-ts) | ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@acme/config-ts?label=) | `tsconfig` bases (`base.json`, `nextjs.json`, `library.json`) | | [`@acme/api-client`](packages/api-client) | ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@acme/api-client?label=) | Typed client generated from the OpenAPI spec in `apis/commerce.yaml` | | [`@acme/utils`](packages/utils) | `0.0.0` (private) | Grab-bag of helpers. Please don't add more stuff here 🙃 | ## Repository structure ``` platform/ ├── apps/ │ ├── admin/ │ └── storefront/ ├── packages/ │ ├── api-client/ │ ├── config-eslint/ │ ├── config-ts/ │ ├── ui/ │ └── utils/ ├── apis/ # OpenAPI specs (source of truth for api-client) ├── tooling/ │ └── scripts/ ├── turbo.json ├── pnpm-workspace.yaml └── package.json ``` ## Getting started You need Node 20 (see `.nvmrc`) and pnpm 9. The easiest way to get the right pnpm is Corepack: ```bash corepack enable pnpm install ``` > [!NOTE] > `pnpm install` runs a `postinstall` that generates `packages/api-client/src/gen/`. If that > step fails you're probably missing Java (needed by `openapi-generator-cli`) — see Troubleshooting below. ### Common commands ```bash pnpm dev # everything, in parallel pnpm -F storefront dev # just the storefront pnpm -F "@acme/ui" storybook pnpm build # turbo build, cached pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck pnpm test -- --watch # vitest pnpm -F admin add react-hook-form # add a dependency to one workspace pnpm -w add -D prettier # ...or to the root ``` Turbo caches task outputs locally in `node_modules/.cache/turbo` and remotely (Vercel Remote Cache) when `TURBO_TOKEN` is set, so the second `pnpm build` on an unchanged tree should finish in well under a second; if it doesn't, something in your environment is leaking into the task hash — usually an env var that isn't listed in `turbo.json` under `globalEnv` or the task's `env`, and `pnpm turbo run build --dry=json | jq '.tasks[].environmentVariables'` will tell you which one. To bypass the cache entirely, run `pnpm build --force`. > [!TIP] > Filter by what changed since `main` with `pnpm turbo run test --filter=...[origin/main]` — > that's what CI does. ## Conventions - Workspace names - apps: plain names (`storefront`, `admin`) - libraries: `@acme/*`, published to GitHub Packages - except `@acme/utils`, which is private and never published - Imports - never import from another package's `src/`; use its public entry point - inside a package, use the `#` subpath imports defined in its `package.json` - e.g. `import { cn } from "#lib/cn"` - Docs: when you need to show a template literal in Markdown, wrap it in double backticks, like `` `Hello ${name}` ``. > [!IMPORTANT] > Changes to anything in `packages/` need a changeset: run `pnpm changeset` and commit the generated file. > CI fails without one. A changeset is just a Markdown file with front matter: ````md --- "@acme/ui": minor "@acme/api-client": patch --- Add `` component. Usage: ```tsx ``` ```` ## Releasing Libraries are versioned with [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets). Apps are deployed continuously from `main` and aren't versioned. Release checklist (for whoever is on release duty that week): - [ ] Merge the "Version Packages" PR opened by the changesets bot - [ ] double-check that the generated CHANGELOG entries read well - [ ] confirm no `major` bump snuck in for `@acme/ui` without an RFC - [ ] Wait for the `release` workflow to publish to GitHub Packages - [ ] Bump `@acme/ui` in the storefront and admin (Renovate usually does this within the hour) - [x] ~~Post in #frontend~~ — automated by the workflow now - [ ] Redeploy Storybook if it didn't trigger on its own > [!CAUTION] > Never run `pnpm publish` locally. The workflow publishes with provenance and a scoped token; a local publish skips both and has, in the past, shipped a package with a `.env` file in it. > > If you think you need a manual publish, talk to the platform leads first. There is almost always another way.
Troubleshooting 1. **`ERR_PNPM_BAD_PM_VERSION`** — you're using a globally installed pnpm. Run ```bash npm uninstall -g pnpm corepack enable ``` 2. **`openapi-generator-cli: java: command not found`** — install a JRE: ```bash brew install --cask temurin@21 # macOS sudo apt install -y openjdk-21-jre-headless # Debian/Ubuntu ``` 3. **Turbo keeps replaying a stale build** Delete the local cache and rebuild: ```bash rm -rf node_modules/.cache/turbo pnpm build --force ``` 4. **Storybook fails with `Cannot find module '@acme/config-ts/base.json'`** after switching branches: run `pnpm install` again, the workspace links are stale.
## CI GitHub Actions, see `.github/workflows/`. The main workflow runs `lint`, `typecheck`, `test` and `build` for affected packages only.[^affected] Vercel creates preview deployments for both apps on every PR. ## Ownership `CODEOWNERS` maps directories to teams. Roughly: * `apps/storefront` — web-storefront * `apps/admin` — backoffice * `packages/ui` — design-systems * everything else — platform [^affected]: "Affected" is computed by Turborepo against the merge base with `main`. Changes to the root `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` or `turbo.json` mark *everything* as affected. That's intentional, if annoying: a lockfile change can change the behaviour of any package, and we'd rather run the full suite than find out in production.

---
# See https://pre-commit.com for more information
# See https://pre-commit.com/hooks.html for more hooks
#
# install:  pipx install pre-commit && pre-commit install --install-hooks -t pre-commit -t pre-push
# update:   pre-commit autoupdate --freeze     (then run `pre-commit run -a` BEFORE pushing the bump)

default_language_version:
    python: python3.11
    node: 20.11.0
default_stages: [pre-commit, pre-push]
minimum_pre_commit_version: '3.5.0'
fail_fast: false
exclude: |
    (?x)^(
        docs/_build/.*|
        vendor/.*|
        .*\.min\.(js|css)|
        src/acme/_vendored/.*|
        tests/fixtures/.*\.(json|ya?ml)
    )$

ci:
  autofix_commit_msg: '[pre-commit.ci] auto fixes from pre-commit.com hooks'
  autofix_prs: true
  autoupdate_branch: ''
  autoupdate_commit_msg: "[pre-commit.ci] pre-commit autoupdate"
  autoupdate_schedule: quarterly
  skip: [mypy, eslint]     # need network / node_modules -> they run in GH Actions instead
  submodules: false


repos:
-   repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v4.6.0
    hooks:

# Linear regression {#sec-linreg}

<!-- Split out of the old ch03 in March. Cross-refs to @sec-intro still assume 2nd-ed. numbering; check before the next build. -->

Linear regression is the workhorse of applied statistics, and most of the ideas in later
chapters — generalised linear models in @sec-glm, regularisation in @sec-regularisation —
are best understood as modifications of it.
We assume familiarity with the matrix notation introduced in @sec-intro.
For a gentler treatment see @james2021 [ch. 3]; for a Bayesian perspective that we will not pursue here, see @gelman2020.

## The model

We observe $n$ pairs $(x_i, y_i)$ with $x_i \in \mathbb{R}^p$ and $y_i \in \mathbb{R}$.
Stacking the $x_i^\top$ as rows of the *design matrix* $X \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p}$,
the linear model is

$$
y = X\beta + \varepsilon, \qquad \operatorname{E}[\varepsilon] = 0,\quad \operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon) = \sigma^2 I_n.
$$ {#eq-linmod}

The classical assumptions, which we refer to as A1–A4 throughout the book, are:

1. **Linearity.** $\operatorname{E}[y \mid X] = X\beta$.
2. **Full rank.** $\operatorname{rank}(X) = p$, so $X^\top X$ is invertible.
3. **Exogeneity.** $\operatorname{E}[\varepsilon \mid X] = 0$.
4. **Spherical errors.** $\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon \mid X) = \sigma^2 I_n$, i.e.
   errors are homoscedastic *and* uncorrelated.

A fifth assumption, normality of $\varepsilon$ (A5), is needed for exact finite-sample inference
but for nothing in @sec-ols-properties. Students routinely [over-weight A5 and under-weight A3]{.mark}; the exam
questions are written with that in mind.

::: {#def-ols}
## Ordinary least squares
The *ordinary least squares* (OLS) estimator of $\beta$ is the minimiser of the residual sum of squares,
$$
\hat\beta = \arg\min_{b \in \mathbb{R}^p} \; \lVert y - Xb \rVert_2^2 .
$$
:::

Setting the gradient to zero gives the *normal equations* $X^\top X \hat\beta = X^\top y$, and under A2

$$\hat\beta = (X^\top X)^{-1}X^\top y$$ {#eq-ols}

In practice nobody computes @eq-ols literally[^qr].

[^qr]: R's `lm()` uses a pivoted QR decomposition of $X$ (via LINPACK's `dqrdc2`, for
    historical reasons). This is both faster and numerically far more stable than forming
    $X^\top X$, whose condition number is the *square* of that of $X$.

    If you ever see code that calls `solve(t(X) %*% X)`, be suspicious.


## Properties of the OLS estimator {#sec-ols-properties}

Under A1–A3 the estimator is unbiased:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{E}[\hat\beta \mid X]
  &= (X^\top X)^{-1} X^\top \operatorname{E}[y \mid X] \\
  &= (X^\top X)^{-1} X^\top X \beta \\
  &= \beta ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-unbiased}

and adding A4 gives its covariance, $\operatorname{Var}(\hat\beta \mid X) = \sigma^2 (X^\top X)^{-1}$.
The natural estimator of $\sigma^2$ is $s^2 = \lVert y - X\hat\beta\rVert^2 / (n - p)$; dividing by $n-p$ rather than $n$ makes it unbiased.

::: {#thm-gauss-markov}
## Gauss–Markov
Under assumptions A1–A4, the OLS estimator $\hat\beta$ is the best linear unbiased estimator (BLUE) of $\beta$: for any other linear unbiased estimator $\tilde\beta = Cy$,
the matrix $\operatorname{Var}(\tilde\beta \mid X) - \operatorname{Var}(\hat\beta \mid X)$ is positive semi-definite.
:::

::: {.proof}
Write $C = (X^\top X)^{-1}X^\top + D$. Unbiasedness for all $\beta$ requires $DX = 0$. Then
$$
\operatorname{Var}(\tilde\beta \mid X) = \sigma^2 C C^\top = \sigma^2 (X^\top X)^{-1} + \sigma^2 D D^\top ,
$$
because the cross terms vanish when $DX = 0$. Since $DD^\top$ is positive semi-definite, the result follows.
:::

Two remarks, both of which trip up students every year:

- "Best" is within the class of **linear** **unbiased** estimators only.
    * Biased estimators such as ridge regression (@sec-regularisation) can, and often do, have lower mean squared error.
    * Non-linear unbiased estimators can beat OLS when the errors are heavy-tailed.
- The theorem says nothing about normality. You need A5 for $t$- and $F$-tests to be exact;
  without it they are only asymptotically valid.

## Inference

| Quantity | Estimator | Distribution under A1–A5 |
|---|---|---|
| $\beta_j$ | $\hat\beta_j$ | $\mathcal{N}\big(\beta_j,\ \sigma^2 [(X^\top X)^{-1}]_{jj}\big)$ |
| $\sigma^2$ | $s^2$ | $(n-p)\,s^2/\sigma^2 \sim \chi^2_{n-p}$ |
| $t$-statistic | $(\hat\beta_j - \beta_j)/\widehat{\operatorname{se}}(\hat\beta_j)$ | $t_{n-p}$ |

: Sampling distributions under the normal linear model. {#tbl-sampling}

@tbl-sampling is the whole of classical regression inference in three rows; everything printed
by `summary.lm()` is a consequence of it.


## A worked example

We use the `mtcars` data, which every R user has seen and which is therefore a good
place to make mistakes in public. We model fuel efficiency (`mpg`) on weight (`wt`,
in 1000 lb) and horsepower (`hp`).

```{r}
#| label: fit-mtcars
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
summary(fit)$coefficients |> round(3)
```

Each extra 1000 lb of weight is associated with `{r} round(coef(fit)["wt"], 2)` mpg,
holding horsepower fixed. Whether "holding horsepower fixed" is a meaningful counterfactual
for a 1970s car is a question for @sec-causal, not for this chapter.

```{r}
#| label: fig-residuals
#| fig-cap: |
#|   Diagnostic plots for the `mtcars` fit. Left: residuals against
#|   fitted values, with a loess smooth. Right: normal Q–Q plot of the
#|   standardised residuals.
#| fig-subcap:
#|   - "Residuals vs fitted"
#|   - "Normal Q–Q"
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| echo: false
plot(fit, which = 1, caption = "", sub.caption = "")
plot(fit, which = 2, caption = "", sub.caption = "")
```

The curvature in the left panel of @fig-residuals suggests that the relationship with
`hp` is not linear -- a log transform helps (Exercise 4.2).

### Influence and leverage ###

Some vocabulary, used loosely in software output and precisely here:

Leverage
:   The $i$-th diagonal element $h_{ii}$ of the hat matrix $H = X(X^\top X)^{-1}X^\top$.
    It depends only on $X$, never on $y$.

Studentised residual
:   $r_i = e_i / (s\sqrt{1 - h_{ii}})$, where $e_i$ is the raw residual.

Cook's distance
:   A combination of leverage and residual size that measures how far $\hat\beta$ moves
    when observation $i$ is deleted; @cook1977 suggested comparing it with an $F_{p,\,n-p}$ quantile.

> **A word of caution.** Rules of thumb like "$h_{ii} > 2p/n$ is high leverage" are just that.
> Look at the observations they flag; don't delete them automatically.

## Exercises

::: {.callout-caution collapse="true"}
## Exercise 4.1
Show that the residual vector $e = y - X\hat\beta$ is orthogonal to every column of $X$,
i.e. $X^\top e = 0$. What does this imply about $\sum_i e_i$ when the model contains an intercept?
:::

::: {.callout-caution collapse="true"}
## Exercise 4.2
Refit the `mtcars` model with `log(hp)` in place of `hp`.

a) Compare the residual plots with @fig-residuals.
b) Interpret the new coefficient. What is a "one-unit change" in $\log(\text{hp})$?
c) Is comparing $R^2$ between the two models meaningful? Why (not)?
:::

::: {.callout-caution collapse="true"}
## Exercise 4.3 ★
Prove that $H$ is symmetric and idempotent, and that $\operatorname{tr}(H) = p$.

*Hint:* use the cyclic property of the trace, $\operatorname{tr}(ABC) = \operatorname{tr}(CAB)$.
:::

Further reading
---------------

The treatment here follows the standard texts closely [see @gelman2020, pp. 33-35; also @james2021, ch. 3].
@seber2003 remains the most complete reference for the linear-algebraic side, and @harrell2015 is the
one to read before you fit a regression to data that matters[^harrell].

[^harrell]: Chapter 4 of @harrell2015 on "multivariable modeling strategies" in particular. The R package
    accompanying the book, **rms**, is worth learning even if you end up using `lm()` for everything.

___

Show that the residual vector $e = y - X\hat\beta$ is orthogonal to every column of $X$,

:::

Refit the `mtcars` model with `log(hp)` in place of `hp`.

a) Compare the residual plots with @fig-residuals.
b) Interpret the new coefficient. What is a "one-unit change" in $\log(\text{hp})$?
c) Is comparing $R^2$ between the two models meaningful? Why (not)?
:::

Prove that $H$ is symmetric and idempotent, and that $\operatorname{tr}(H) = p$.

*Hint:* use the cyclic property of the trace, $\operatorname{tr}(ABC) = \operatorname{tr}(CAB)$.

---------------

The treatment here follows the standard texts closely [see @gelman2020, pp. 33-35; also @james2021, ch. 3].

one to read before you fit a regression to data that matters[^harrell].

  annotations: {}
  # -- The name of the service account to use.

  name: ""

# -- Annotations added to every pod

# -- Labels added to every pod
podLabels: {}

# -- Pod-level security context
podSecurityContext: {}
  # fsGroup: 2000

# -- Container-level security context
securityContext: {}
  # capabilities:

service:
  # -- Service type
  type: ClusterIP

  annotations: {}

ingress:
  # -- Enable ingress
  enabled: false
  # -- IngressClass to use
  className: ""
  # -- Ingress annotations
  annotations: {}
    # kubernetes.io/ingress.class: nginx

        # -- Address the HTTP server binds to

        # -- Public base URL, used for redirects and links in e-mails

    # -- Namespace for the ServiceMonitor; defaults to the release namespace

# Changelog
All notable changes to `acme-sdk` will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
The Python and TypeScript SDKs share version numbers; entries tagged *(py)* or *(ts)* apply to only one of them.

## [Unreleased]
### Added
- `Client.with_options()` for per-request overrides of `timeout` and `max_retries` ([#1482](https://github.com/acme/acme-sdk/pull/1482))
- *(ts)* The ESM build is now tree-shakeable (`"sideEffects": false` in `package.json`)

### Changed
- Default `max_retries` raised from 2 to 3. Retries still only happen on
  connection errors, `408`, `409`, `429` and `5xx` responses.

## [3.2.0] - 2024-05-14
### Added
- Streaming helpers: `client.events.stream()` returns an async iterator of typed events.
  - supports `Last-Event-ID` resumption via `stream(resume_from=...)`
  - emits a `heartbeat` event every 15s, which is filtered out unless `include_heartbeats=True`
- `Webhook.verify()` accepts a list of secrets, so you can rotate without downtime ([#1440](https://github.com/acme/acme-sdk/issues/1440))
- *(py)* Type stubs for `acme_sdk.types.webhooks`

### Fixed
- Pagination iterators no longer request one extra, empty page when `has_more` is
false on the last page ([#1451](https://github.com/acme/acme-sdk/issues/1451))
- `AcmeError.__str__` included the request body, which could leak card numbers into logs. It now only includes the request ID. 

### Security
- Raised the `urllib3` lower bound to `>=2.2.2` (CVE-2024-37891).

## [3.1.1] - 2024-04-02
### Fixed
- *(ts)* A `fetch` polyfill was accidentally bundled into the Node 18+ build, adding ~40 kB.
- Retries ignored the `Retry-After` header when it was given as an HTTP date rather than as seconds.

## [3.1.0] - 2024-03-11
### Added
- `client.invoices.finalize()` and `client.invoices.void()`
- Idempotency keys are generated automatically for `POST` requests unless you pass `idempotency_key=None`
    - the generated key is a UUIDv4 and is logged at `DEBUG`
    - keys you pass explicitly are never modified
### Deprecated
- `client.invoices.close()` — use `finalize()` instead; `close()` will be removed in 4.0
### Fixed
- Timeouts passed as `httpx.Timeout` objects were silently replaced by the default ([#1398](https://github.com/acme/acme-sdk/issues/1398))

## [3.0.0] - 2024-01-22
### Changed
- **BREAKING:** The minimum Python version is now 3.9; the minimum Node version is 18.
- **BREAKING:** All list methods return auto-paginating iterators instead of a
  `Page` object. To get the old behaviour, call `.page()`:
  ```python
  page = client.customers.list(limit=50).page()
  for customer in page.data:
      ...
  ```
- **BREAKING:** Renamed `AcmeAPIError` → `APIError` and `AcmeConnectionError` → `APIConnectionError`.
  The old names remain as aliases until 4.0 and emit a `DeprecationWarning`.
- Response objects are now Pydantic v2 models *(py)* / readonly interfaces *(ts)*.

### Removed
- **BREAKING:** the `acme_sdk.legacy` module and the `api_base` global.
- Support for the `Acme-Version: 2021-06-01` header.

### Fixed
- Thread-safety issue when sharing one `Client` between threads with HTTP/2 enabled ([#1301](https://github.com/acme/acme-sdk/issues/1301), thanks @mkowalski)

## [2.6.0] - 2023-11-08
### Added
- `client.refunds` resource
- `ACME_LOG=debug` environment variable that logs requests and responses (with `Authorization` redacted)
### Changed
- The `User-Agent` now includes the runtime, e.g. `acme-sdk-python/2.6.0 CPython/3.12.0`

## [2.5.2] - 2023-10-17
### Fixed
- The `py.typed` marker was missing from the wheel. 

## [2.5.1] - 2023-10-03
### Fixed
- Regression in 2.5.0: `customer.metadata` was `None` instead of `{}` when empty.
### Security
- Don't follow redirects to a different host when an `Authorization` header is set.

## [2.5.0] - 2023-09-19
### Added
- Async client (`AsyncClient`) *(py)*
  - same surface as `Client`; every method is a coroutine
  - uses `httpx.AsyncClient` under the hood, pass your own via `http_client=`
      - handy for sharing a connection pool with the rest of your app
- Request/response hooks: `on_request`, `on_response`

## [2.4.0] - 2023-08-01
### Added
- Support for the `2023-07-15` API version.
### Changed
- Errors expose `.request_id` and `.status_code` as attributes instead of only in the message.
### Fixed
- Duplicate webhook deliveries when two events had the same `created` timestamp — this
  is the proper fix for the issue that 2.3.1 tried to address.

## [2.3.1] - 2023-07-12 [YANKED]
### Fixed
- Attempted fix for duplicate webhook deliveries. Yanked because it dropped
  events with identical timestamps; upgrade to 2.4.0.

## [2.3.0] - 2023-06-20
### Added
- Webhook signature verification helpers (`Webhook.construct_event`).
### Fixed
- Unicode in metadata values (e.g. `"café"`, `"東京"`) was double-encoded ([#842](https://github.com/acme/acme-sdk/issues/842))

## [2.2.0] - 2023-04-27
### Added
- `client.customers.search(query=...)` using the new search endpoint.
### Deprecated
- `client.customers.list(email=...)`. Use `search(query="email:'a@example.com'")`.

## [2.0.0] - 2023-02-06
### Changed
- **BREAKING:** A new `Client` class replaces the module-level functions:
  ```diff
  - import acme_sdk
  - acme_sdk.api_key = "sk_test_..."
  - acme_sdk.Customer.create(email="a@example.com")
  + from acme_sdk import Client
  + client = Client(api_key="sk_test_...")
  + client.customers.create(email="a@example.com")
  ```
- Switched the HTTP layer from `requests` to `httpx`.
### Removed
- Python 3.6 and 3.7 support.

## [1.2.0] - 2022-09-14
### Added
- `expand=` parameter on all retrieve methods.
- Automatic retries with exponential backoff (off by default; enable with `max_retries=2`).

## [1.1.0] - 2022-05-30
### Added
- Customers and invoices resources.
### Fixed
- Typo in `Charge.captured_at` (was `captued_at`). The old name still works but is undocumented.

## [1.0.0] - 2022-03-01
### Added
- First stable release. 🎉

## [0.9.0] - 2021-12-02
### Added
- Release candidate for 1.0; charges and payment intents only.

raw_arguments.content:
# Changelog
All notable changes to `acme-sdk` will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
The Python and TypeScript SDKs share version numbers; entries tagged *(py)* or *(ts)* apply to only one of them.

## [Unreleased]
### Added
- `Client.with_options()` for per-request overrides of `timeout` and `max_retries` ([#1482](https://github.com/acme/acme-sdk/pull/1482))
- *(ts)* The ESM build is now tree-shakeable (`"sideEffects": false` in `package.json`)

### Changed
- Default `max_retries` raised from 2 to 3. Retries still only happen on
  connection errors, `408`, `409`, `429` and `5xx` responses.

## [3.2.0] - 2024-05-14
### Added
- Streaming helpers: `client.events.stream()` returns an async iterator of typed events.
  - supports `Last-Event-ID` resumption via `stream(resume_from=...)`
  - emits a `heartbeat` event every 15s, which is filtered out unless `include_heartbeats=True`
- `Webhook.verify()` accepts a list of secrets, so you can rotate without downtime ([#1440](https://github.com/acme/acme-sdk/issues/1440))
- *(py)* Type stubs for `acme_sdk.types.webhooks`

### Fixed
- Pagination iterators no longer request one extra, empty page when `has_more` is
false on the last page ([#1451](https://github.com/acme/acme-sdk/issues/1451))
- `AcmeError.__str__` included the request body, which could leak card numbers into logs. It now only includes the request ID. 

### Security
- Raised the `urllib3` lower bound to `>=2.2.2` (CVE-2024-37891).

## [3.1.1] - 2024-04-02
### Fixed
- *(ts)* A `fetch` polyfill was accidentally bundled into the Node 18+ build, adding ~40 kB.
- Retries ignored the `Retry-After` header when it was given as an HTTP date rather than as seconds.

## [3.1.0] - 2024-03-11
### Added
- `client.invoices.finalize()` and `client.invoices.void()`
- Idempotency keys are generated automatically for `POST` requests unless you pass `idempotency_key=None`
    - the generated key is a UUIDv4 and is logged at `DEBUG`
    - keys you pass explicitly are never modified
### Deprecated
- `client.invoices.close()` — use `finalize()` instead; `close()` will be removed in 4.0
### Fixed
- Timeouts passed as `httpx.Timeout` objects were silently replaced by the default ([#1398](https://github.com/acme/acme-sdk/issues/1398))

## [3.0.0] - 2024-01-22
### Changed
- **BREAKING:** The minimum Python version is now 3.9; the minimum Node version is 18.
- **BREAKING:** All list methods return auto-paginating iterators instead of a
  `Page` object. To get the old behaviour, call `.page()`:
  ```python
  page = client.customers.list(limit=50).page()
  for customer in page.data:
      ...
  ```
- **BREAKING:** Renamed `AcmeAPIError` → `APIError` and `AcmeConnectionError` → `APIConnectionError`.
  The old names remain as aliases until 4.0 and emit a `DeprecationWarning`.
- Response objects are now Pydantic v2 models *(py)* / readonly interfaces *(ts)*.

### Removed
- **BREAKING:** the `acme_sdk.legacy` module and the `api_base` global.
- Support for the `Acme-Version: 2021-06-01` header.

### Fixed
- Thread-safety issue when sharing one `Client` between threads with HTTP/2 enabled ([#1301](https://github.com/acme/acme-sdk/issues/1301), thanks @mkowalski)

## [2.6.0] - 2023-11-08
### Added
- `client.refunds` resource
- `ACME_LOG=debug` environment variable that logs requests and responses (with `Authorization` redacted)
### Changed
- The `User-Agent` now includes the runtime, e.g. `acme-sdk-python/2.6.0 CPython/3.12.0`

## [2.5.2] - 2023-10-17
### Fixed
- The `py.typed` marker was missing from the wheel. 

## [2.5.1] - 2023-10-03
### Fixed
- Regression in 2.5.0: `customer.metadata` was `None` instead of `{}` when empty.
### Security
- Don't follow redirects to a different host when an `Authorization` header is set.

## [2.5.0] - 2023-09-19
### Added
- Async client (`AsyncClient`) *(py)*
  - same surface as `Client`; every method is a coroutine
  - uses `httpx.AsyncClient` under the hood, pass your own via `http_client=`
      - handy for sharing a connection pool with the rest of your app
- Request/response hooks: `on_request`, `on_response`

## [2.4.0] - 2023-08-01
### Added
- Support for the `2023-07-15` API version.
### Changed
- Errors expose `.request_id` and `.status_code` as attributes instead of only in the message.
### Fixed
- Duplicate webhook deliveries when two events had the same `created` timestamp — this
  is the proper fix for the issue that 2.3.1 tried to address.

## [2.3.1] - 2023-07-12 [YANKED]
### Fixed
- Attempted fix for duplicate webhook deliveries. Yanked because it dropped
  events with identical timestamps; upgrade to 2.4.0.

## [2.3.0] - 2023-06-20
### Added
- Webhook signature verification helpers (`Webhook.construct_event`).
### Fixed
- Unicode in metadata values (e.g. `"café"`, `"東京"`) was double-encoded ([#842](https://github.com/acme/acme-sdk/issues/842))

## [2.2.0] - 2023-04-27
### Added
- `client.customers.search(query=...)` using the new search endpoint.
### Deprecated
- `client.customers.list(email=...)`. Use `search(query="email:'a@example.com'")`.

## [2.0.0] - 2023-02-06
### Changed
- **BREAKING:** A new `Client` class replaces the module-level functions:
  ```diff
  - import acme_sdk
  - acme_sdk.api_key = "sk_test_..."
  - acme_sdk.Customer.create(email="a@example.com")
  + from acme_sdk import Client
  + client = Client(api_key="sk_test_...")
  + client.customers.create(email="a@example.com")
  ```
- Switched the HTTP layer from `requests` to `httpx`.
### Removed
- Python 3.6 and 3.7 support.

## [1.2.0] - 2022-09-14
### Added
- `expand=` parameter on all retrieve methods.
- Automatic retries with exponential backoff (off by default; enable with `max_retries=2`).

## [1.1.0] - 2022-05-30
### Added
- Customers and invoices resources.
### Fixed
- Typo in `Charge.captured_at` (was `captued_at`). The old name still works but is undocumented.

## [1.0.0] - 2022-03-01
### Added
- First stable release. 🎉

## [0.9.0] - 2021-12-02
### Added
- Release candidate for 1.0; charges and payment intents only.

# environment.yml — geo-ml research environment
#
#   mamba env create -f environment.yml
#   mamba env update -f environment.yml --prune
#   conda-lock -f environment.yml -p linux-64 -p osx-arm64      # regenerates conda-lock.yml
#
# Maintainer: Lena P. (@lpetrova) — ping before bumping CUDA / pytorch, the GPU nodes on the
# cluster are pinned to driver 535, which tops out at CUDA 12.2.
# Last full re-solve: 2024-05-02 on linux-64. osx-arm64 works if you drop the nvidia:: lines.

name: geo-ml

channels:
  - conda-forge
  - pytorch
  - nvidia
  # - defaults     # NO. mixing defaults + conda-forge gave us two libgdal builds (#311)
  - nodefaults

dependencies:
# --- core ------------------------------------------------------------------
- python=3.11
- pip>=23
- setuptools
- numpy>=1.24,<2.0       # rasterio 1.3 wheels are not numpy-2 ready yet
- pandas=2.2.*
- scipy>=1.11
- scikit-learn>=1.4
- xarray
- dask>=2024.4
- numba=0.59.*           # 0.60 segfaults in our UDFs on aarch64, see #344
- pyarrow>=15
- tqdm

# --- geo -------------------------------------------------------------------
- gdal=3.8
- geopandas>=0.14
- rasterio>=1.3.9
- shapely>=2
- pyproj
- rioxarray
- cartopy
- libgdal-arrow-parquet   # GeoParquet I/O; no longer pulled in by gdal itself since 3.8
-   "h3-py=3.7"
# --- deep learning ---------------------------------------------------------
- pytorch::pytorch=2.2
- pytorch::torchvision=0.17
- pytorch::pytorch-cuda=12.1
- nvidia::cuda-toolkit=12.1
- lightning=2.2
- torchmetrics
# --- notebooks / viz -------------------------------------------------------
- jupyterlab>=4
- ipykernel
- ipywidgets
- matplotlib>=3.8
- seaborn
- folium
- nodejs=20               # jupyterlab extensions need it at build time
# - r-base=4.3            # R interop experiment, see notebooks/99-r-bridge.ipynb
# - rpy2
# --- dev -------------------------------------------------------------------
- pytest
- pytest-cov
- pre-commit
- mypy
- pip:
    - -r requirements-dev.txt
    - --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121
    - git+https://github.com/acme/geo-utils.git@v0.4.1#egg=geo-utils
    - "black[jupyter]==24.3.0"
    - mlflow==2.12.1
    - torchgeo>=0.5.2
    - "segmentation-models-pytorch==0.3.3"
    - planetary-computer
    - pystac-client>=0.7
    - 'odc-stac==0.3.9'
      # editable install of this repo; keep it LAST so it resolves against everything above
    - -e .


variables:
   CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: "0"
   PROJ_NETWORK: ON
   GDAL_CACHEMAX: 512        # MB
   GDAL_HTTP_MULTIRANGE: YES
   GDAL_DISABLE_READDIR_ON_OPEN: EMPTY_DIR
   AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST: "YES"
   OMP_NUM_THREADS: 4
   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI: https://mlflow.internal.acme.example.com
   PYTHONHASHSEED: 0
   TORCH_HOME:
   HF_HOME: ~

prefix: /opt/conda/envs/geo-ml

arguments.content:
# action.yml — acme/setup-toolchain
#
# Composite action used by ~40 repos in the org. Breaking input changes => new major
# tag (v4); everything else ships as v3.x.y and the floating v3 tag gets moved.
#
#   - uses: acme/setup-toolchain@v3
#     with:
#       node-version-file: .nvmrc
#       registry-token: ${{ secrets.ACME_NPM_TOKEN }}
#
name: 'Setup Acme toolchain'
description: >-
  Installs Node.js, pnpm (via corepack) and the acme CLI, restores the pnpm store
  and the local turbo cache, and configures auth for the internal npm registry so
  that `pnpm install` works for packages in the @acme scope. Works on ubuntu-*,
  macos-* and windows-* runners; self-hosted runners need curl, tar and gh on PATH.
author: 'Acme Developer Infrastructure <dev-infra@acme.example.com>'
branding: { icon: 'package', color: "blue" }

inputs:
  node-version:
    description: "Node.js version spec (20, 20.x, lts/*). Ignored when node-version-file is set."
    required: false
    default: "20.x"
  node-version-file:
     description: Path to a file with the Node.js version to use, usually .nvmrc or .node-version (package.json is read via engines.node)
     required: 'false'
     default: ''
  pnpm-version:
    description: 'pnpm version. Empty = use "packageManager" from package.json'
    required: false
    default: ''
  acme-cli-version:
    description: Version of the acme CLI to install (without the v)
    required: false
    default: 2.14.0
  registry-url:
    description: "Registry for the @acme scope"
    required: false
    default: https://npm.pkg.github.com
  registry-token:
     description: |
       Token with read:packages for the @acme scope.
       In most repos this is secrets.ACME_NPM_TOKEN (org secret). GITHUB_TOKEN only
       works if the calling repo was granted access in the package settings.
     required: TRUE
  token:
    description: GitHub token used to download the acme CLI release asset
    required: false
    default: ${{ github.token }}
  cache:
    description: Restore / save the pnpm store
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  turbo-cache:
    description: Restore .turbo between runs (local cache only -- the remote cache is configured through TURBO_TOKEN)
    required: false
    default: yes
  cache-key-suffix:
    description: "Appended to the cache key, e.g. to bust a poisoned cache"
    required: false
    default: ''
  install:
    description: 'Run pnpm install after setup'
    required: false
    default: "true"
  install-args:
    description: Extra args for pnpm install
    required: false
    default: --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline
  working-directory:
    description: Where to run pnpm install
    required: false
    default: .
  always-auth:
    description: Set always-auth in .npmrc
    required: false
    default: 'false'
    deprecationMessage: "always-auth is ignored by npm >= 9 and will be removed in v4 of this action. Drop it from your workflow to silence this warning."
  # debug:  (moved to ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG, see CHANGELOG 3.6.0)

outputs:
  node-version:
    description: "The resolved Node.js version, e.g. v20.11.1"
    value: ${{ steps.node.outputs.node-version }}
  pnpm-store-path:
    description: Path of the pnpm content-addressable store
    value: ${{ steps.pnpm.outputs.store-path }}
  cache-hit:
    description: Whether the pnpm store was restored from an exact key match
    value: ${{ steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit }}
  acme-cli-path:
    value: ${{ steps.cli.outputs.path }}
    description: ~


runs:
  using: "composite"
  steps:
    -   name: Setup Node.js
        id: node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version-file == '' && inputs.node-version || '' }}
          node-version-file: ${{ inputs.node-version-file }}

    -   name: Setup pnpm
        id: pnpm
        shell: bash
        env:
          PNPM_VERSION: ${{ inputs.pnpm-version }}
        run: |-
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "$PNPM_VERSION" ]; then
            PNPM_VERSION=$(node -p "(require('./package.json').packageManager || 'pnpm@8.15.4').split('@')[1]")
          fi
          corepack enable
          corepack prepare "pnpm@${PNPM_VERSION}" --activate
          echo "store-path=$(pnpm store path --silent)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    -   name: Restore pnpm store
        id: cache
        if: inputs.cache == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ${{ steps.pnpm.outputs.store-path }}
            ~/.cache/Cypress
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-tool-${{ hashFiles('**/pnpm-lock.yaml', '**/package-lock.json') }}${{ inputs.cache-key-suffix }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-tool-
      # 'yes' is the documented default but older callers pass 'true' -- accept both
    -   name: Restore turbo cache
        if: inputs.turbo-cache == 'true' || inputs.turbo-cache == 'yes'
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}/.turbo
          key: turbo-${{ runner.os }}-${{ github.job }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
             turbo-${{ runner.os }}-${{ github.job }}-
             turbo-${{ runner.os }}-

    -   name: Install acme CLI
        id: cli

# action.yml — acme/setup-toolchain
#
# Composite action used by ~40 repos in the org. Breaking input changes => new major
# tag (v4); everything else ships as v3.x.y and the floating v3 tag gets moved.
#
#   - uses: acme/setup-toolchain@v3
#     with:
#       node-version-file: .nvmrc
#       registry-token: ${{ secrets.ACME_NPM_TOKEN }}
#
name: 'Setup Acme toolchain'
description: >-
  Installs Node.js, pnpm (via corepack) and the acme CLI, restores the pnpm store
  and the local turbo cache, and configures auth for the internal npm registry so
  that `pnpm install` works for packages in the @acme scope. Works on ubuntu-*,
  macos-* and windows-* runners; self-hosted runners need curl, tar and gh on PATH.
author: 'Acme Developer Infrastructure <dev-infra@acme.example.com>'
branding: { icon: 'package', color: "blue" }

inputs:
  node-version:
    description: "Node.js version spec (20, 20.x, lts/*). Ignored when node-version-file is set."
    required: false
    default: "20.x"
  node-version-file:
     description: Path to a file with the Node.js version to use, usually .nvmrc or .node-version (package.json is read via engines.node)
     required: 'false'
     default: ''
  pnpm-version:
    description: 'pnpm version. Empty = use "packageManager" from package.json'
    required: false
    default: ''
  acme-cli-version:
    description: Version of the acme CLI to install (without the v)
    required: false
    default: 2.14.0
  registry-url:
    description: "Registry for the @acme scope"
    required: false
    default: https://npm.pkg.github.com
  registry-token:
     description: |
       Token with read:packages for the @acme scope.
       In most repos this is secrets.ACME_NPM_TOKEN (org secret). GITHUB_TOKEN only
       works if the calling repo was granted access in the package settings.
     required: TRUE
  token:
    description: GitHub token used to download the acme CLI release asset
    required: false
    default: ${{ github.token }}
  cache:
    description: Restore / save the pnpm store
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  turbo-cache:
    description: Restore .turbo between runs (local cache only -- the remote cache is configured through TURBO_TOKEN)
    required: false
    default: yes
  cache-key-suffix:
    description: "Appended to the cache key, e.g. to bust a poisoned cache"
    required: false
    default: ''
  install:
    description: 'Run pnpm install after setup'
    required: false
    default: "true"
  install-args:
    description: Extra args for pnpm install
    required: false
    default: --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline
  working-directory:
    description: Where to run pnpm install
    required: false
    default: .
  always-auth:
    description: Set always-auth in .npmrc
    required: false
    default: 'false'
    deprecationMessage: "always-auth is ignored by npm >= 9 and will be removed in v4 of this action. Drop it from your workflow to silence this warning."
  # debug:  (moved to ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG, see CHANGELOG 3.6.0)

outputs:
  node-version:
    description: "The resolved Node.js version, e.g. v20.11.1"
    value: ${{ steps.node.outputs.node-version }}
  pnpm-store-path:
    description: Path of the pnpm content-addressable store
    value: ${{ steps.pnpm.outputs.store-path }}
  cache-hit:
    description: Whether the pnpm store was restored from an exact key match
    value: ${{ steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit }}
  acme-cli-path:
    value: ${{ steps.cli.outputs.path }}
    description: ~


runs:
  using: "composite"
  steps:
    -   name: Setup Node.js
        id: node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version-file == '' && inputs.node-version || '' }}
          node-version-file: ${{ inputs.node-version-file }}

    -   name: Setup pnpm
        id: pnpm
        shell: bash
        env:
          PNPM_VERSION: ${{ inputs.pnpm-version }}
        run: |-
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "$PNPM_VERSION" ]; then
            PNPM_VERSION=$(node -p "(require('./package.json').packageManager || 'pnpm@8.15.4').split('@')[1]")
          fi
          corepack enable
          corepack prepare "pnpm@${PNPM_VERSION}" --activate
          echo "store-path=$(pnpm store path --silent)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    -   name: Restore pnpm store
        id: cache
        if: inputs.cache == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ${{ steps.pnpm.outputs.store-path }}
            ~/.cache/Cypress
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-tool-${{ hashFiles('**/pnpm-lock.yaml', '**/package-lock.json') }}${{ inputs.cache-key-suffix }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-tool-
      # 'yes' is the documented default but older callers pass 'true' -- accept both
    -   name: Restore turbo cache
        if: inputs.turbo-cache == 'true' || inputs.turbo-cache == 'yes'
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}/.turbo
          key: turbo-${{ runner.os }}-${{ github.job }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
             turbo-${{ runner.os }}-${{ github.job }}-
             turbo-${{ runner.os }}-

    -   name: Install acme CLI
        id: cli
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.token }}
          ACME_CLI_VERSION: ${{ inputs.acme-cli-version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "${RUNNER_OS}" in
            Linux)   asset="acme-linux-amd64.tar.gz" ;;
            macOS)   asset="acme-darwin-universal.tar.gz" ;;
            Windows) asset="acme-windows-amd64.zip" ;;
          esac
          dest="${RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE}/acme/${ACME_CLI_VERSION}"
          mkdir -p "$dest"
          if [ ! -x "$dest/acme" ] && [ ! -f "$dest/acme.exe" ]; then
            gh release download "v${ACME_CLI_VERSION}" --repo acme/acme-cli --pattern "$asset" --dir "$dest"
            (cd "$dest" && (tar xzf "$asset" 2>/dev/null || unzip -oq "$asset"))
          fi
          echo "$dest" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          echo "path=$dest" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    -   name: Configure registry auth
        shell: bash
        env:
            NPMRC: ${{ runner.temp }}/.npmrc
            REGISTRY_URL: ${{ inputs.registry-url }}
        run: |
          host="${REGISTRY_URL#https://}"
          echo "@acme:registry=${REGISTRY_URL}" >> "$NPMRC"
          echo "//${host%/}/:_authToken=${{ inputs.registry-token }}" >> "$NPMRC"
          if [ "${{ inputs.always-auth }}" = "true" ]; then echo "always-auth=true" >> "$NPMRC"; fi
          echo "NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG=$NPMRC" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

    -   name: pnpm install
        if: inputs.install == 'true'
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
        run: pnpm install ${{ inputs.install-args }}

    -   name: Summary
        if: ${{ runner.debug == '1' }}
        shell: bash
        run: >
          echo "node $(node --version), pnpm $(pnpm --version),
          acme $(acme --version 2>/dev/null || echo n/a),
          cache-hit=${{ steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit || 'n/a' }}"

# Methods {#methods}

<!-- EVH: section order follows the outline agreed with Dr. Brenner on
2024-02-27. The old 3.5 (pilot study) moved to Appendix B. -->

This chapter describes the study area, the field sampling design, the
laboratory procedures and the statistical models used to test the
hypotheses set out in Chapter \@ref(intro). Where a procedure follows a
published protocol closely I only summarise it and refer to the original
description [e.g., @biggs1996; @steinman2017, pp. 213--225]; any deviations are described in full.
All analyses were run in R [@R-base] with the packages listed in
Appendix \@ref(software).

## Study area {#study-area}

The study was carried out in twelve second- and third-order streams in
the upper Kinzig and Murg catchments of the northern Black Forest, SW
Germany (Figure \@ref(fig:study-area)). Both catchments are underlain by
Triassic sandstone (Buntsandstein) and granite. Mean annual
precipitation is ca. 1,600--1,900 mm and mean annual air temperature
approx. 7.5 °C at 800 m a.s.l. (DWD station No. 4927, 1991--2020
normals). Land use is dominated by managed spruce--fir forest;
agriculture is restricted to small pastures on the valley floors.

(ref:fig-study-area-cap) Location of the twelve study reaches in the upper Kinzig and Murg catchments (Black Forest, SW Germany). Open circles: shaded reaches; filled circles: open-canopy reaches. Basemap © OpenStreetMap contributors.

```{r study-area, fig.cap='(ref:fig-study-area-cap)', out.width='80%', fig.align='center'}
knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures", "ch3", "study_area_map.pdf"))
```

Reaches were chosen from a pool of 31 candidate sites identified during
a reconnaissance survey in March 2021. The selection criteria were (i) a
wetted width of 2--6 m at base flow, (ii) no point-source inputs within
2 km upstream and (iii) safe access during high flows. Six reaches had a
closed riparian canopy (> 80 % cover, measured with a spherical
densiometer[^densiometer]) and six had been clear-cut or windthrown within the past
ten years, i.e. they were largely open (< 30 % cover). Paired reaches
were located in the same or in adjacent sub-catchments to minimise
differences in water chemistry, cf. @jones2018, who showed that
between-catchment variation in dissolved phosphorus can mask canopy
effects almost entirely.


## Sampling design {#sampling-design}

Each reach was visited on six occasions between April and September 2022
(Table \@ref(tab:sampling)). The field procedure was identical on every
visit:

1. On arrival, water temperature, conductivity and pH were recorded with
   a multiparameter probe (WTW Multi 3630 IDS, Xylem Inc., Weilheim) at
   the downstream end of the reach.
2. Five transects were laid out at equal distances along a 50 m reach.
   On each transect:
   - three cobbles (64--256 mm, *b*-axis) were selected at random
     positions using a random-number table, **not** by eye;
   - canopy cover was read with the densiometer facing upstream,
     downstream and towards both banks;
       * the four readings were averaged per transect;
       * on overcast days a second observer (Dr. Kowalski or the
         author) repeated the readings independently.
3. Periphyton was removed from a 4.9 cm² area on the upper surface of
   each cobble with a template and a stiff toothbrush, rinsed into a
   sample bottle with filtered stream water and made up to 50 mL. A
   \SI{5}{\milli\litre} aliquot was preserved in Lugol's solution for
   taxonomic analysis (not reported in this chapter, see Chapter 5).
4. Samples were kept dark and cool (ca. 4 °C) and filtered within 6 h
of collection.

```{r sampling}
tribble(
  ~Campaign, ~Dates,            ~Discharge, ~Notes,
  "C1",      "11--14 Apr 2022", "85--240",  "tail of snowmelt",
  "C2",      "16--19 May 2022", "40--130",  "",
  "C3",      "20--23 Jun 2022", "25--95",   "M4 repeated on 30 Jun (spate)",
  "C4",      "18--21 Jul 2022", "12--60",   "low flow; K3 and M2 partly dry",
  "C5",      "22--25 Aug 2022", "9--48",    "",
  "C6",      "19--22 Sep 2022", "30--110",  "leaf fall started at K2, K5"
) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE,
        col.names = c("Campaign", "Dates", "Discharge (L/s)", "Notes"),
        caption = "Sampling campaigns, dates and discharge range across reaches.") |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", font_size = 9)
```

> **Field note, 23 June 2022 (reach M4).** Bed partly mobilised after
> the storm of 21 June; three of the five tiles were gone and the other
> two were buried under ca. 5 cm of sand. Campaign C3 for M4 was
therefore repeated a week later, on 30 June.

## Laboratory analyses

Chlorophyll *a* was extracted in 90 % ethanol at 75 °C for 5 min,
followed by 24 h in the dark at 4 °C, and measured spectrophotometrically
with correction for phaeopigments [@jespersen1978]. Ash-free dry mass
(AFDM) was determined by drying a second filter at 105 °C to constant
mass and combusting it at 500 °C for 4 h. Dissolved nutrients (SRP,
NO~3~-N, NH~4~-N) were analysed by the central laboratory of the
Institute (Dr. M. Schäfer) by continuous-flow analysis; detection limits
were 2 µg L^-1^ for SRP and 5 µg L^-1^ for both nitrogen species. Values
below the detection limit were set to half the limit. This affected 7 %
of the SRP measurements but none of the nitrate values.

## Periphyton growth model {#growth-model}

Accrual of chlorophyll *a* on artificial substrata (unglazed ceramic
tiles, 4.7 × 4.7 cm) deployed for 35 days was described by a logistic
model, following @biggs1996 and @stevenson1996 [-@stevenson1996]:

\begin{equation}
  B(t) = \frac{K}{1 + \left(\frac{K - B_0}{B_0}\right) e^{-r t}}
  (\#eq:growth)
\end{equation}

where $B(t)$ is chlorophyll *a* biomass (µg cm^-2^) at time $t$ (days
since deployment), $B_0$ the initial biomass, $K$ the carrying capacity
and $r$ the intrinsic growth rate (d^-1^). Equation \@ref(eq:growth) was
fitted separately for each reach and deployment by nonlinear least
squares (`nls()` with the port algorithm), constraining $K$ to be
positive. Following @doe2020 [p. 45], fits with fewer than five non-zero
observations were discarded; this removed 4 of 72 deployments (viz. K3
in C1, M4 in C3, and M2 and M6 in C4). Where the logistic model failed to converge,
a Gompertz model was fitted instead, cf. Eq. 2.4 in Chapter
\@ref(background); the two give nearly identical estimates of $r$ when
$B_0 \ll K$ [@smith2019; @doe2020, p. 45].

\newpage

## Statistical analysis {-}

Differences between shaded and open reaches were tested with linear
mixed-effects models of the form

$$
\log(y_{ijk}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1\,\text{canopy}_i + \beta_2\,\text{campaign}_j + \beta_3\,(\text{canopy} \times \text{campaign})_{ij} + u_{\text{pair}} + u_{\text{reach}} + \varepsilon_{ijk}
$$

with random intercepts for reach pair and for reach nested in pair. The
response variables were (1) chlorophyll *a*, (2) AFDM, (3) the
autotrophic index (AFDM : chl *a*) and (4) the growth rate $r$ from
Eq. \@ref(eq:growth). Models were fitted by REML with **lme4**
[@bates2015]; *p*-values for the fixed effects were obtained with the
Kenward--Roger approximation. Model assumptions were checked visually
(residuals vs. fitted values, Q--Q plots), e.g. for heteroscedasticity
between campaigns. Where needed, a variance structure was added with
**nlme**, i.e. `varIdent(form = ~ 1 | campaign)`.

```{r model-example, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
m_chla <- lmer(log(chla) ~ canopy * campaign + (1 | pair/reach),
               data = periphyton, REML = TRUE)
anova(m_chla, ddf = "Kenward-Roger")
```

Effect sizes are reported as back-transformed ratios with 95 %
confidence intervals. I did not correct for multiple testing across the
four response variables, since they are strongly correlated and
represent different facets of the same hypothesis [cf. @gelman2012];
this decision is revisited in the Discussion (Section
\@ref(disc-limits)). As @jones2018 put it, "the canopy effect is either
large enough to see in every metric, or it is not there at all."



***

## Open issues (remove before submission) {-}

<!-- notes to myself and Dr. Brenner. Delete before the PDF goes to the committee! -->

- [x] Replace placeholder map with final version (QGIS export, 600 dpi)
- [ ] Check whether DWD station No. 4927 is really the closest one for
      the Murg reaches --- maybe use No. 3362 instead?
- [ ] Ask Prof. Ritter whether Kenward--Roger is OK for the
  growth-rate models (only 68 fits).
- [ ] Densiometer footnote: cite the manufacturer's manual or Lemmon
    (1956)?

[^densiometer]: Model-C convex spherical densiometer (Forestry
    Suppliers Inc., Jackson, MS, U.S.A.). Readings were converted to
    percent cover following the manufacturer's instructions, i.e. by
    multiplying the number of covered points by 1.04.

    Lemmon's original description (1956) uses a slightly different
    grid; the difference is negligible for canopy cover above ca. 20 %.

```

> **Field note, 23 June 2022 (reach M4).** Bed partly mobilised after
> the storm of 21 June; three of the five tiles were gone and the other
> two were buried under ca. 5 cm of sand. Campaign C3 for M4 was
therefore repeated a week later, on 30 June.

## Laboratory analyses

Chlorophyll *a* was extracted in 90 % ethanol at 75 °C for 5 min,
followed by 24 h in the dark at 4 °C, and measured spectrophotometrically
with correction for phaeopigments [@jespersen1978]. Ash-free dry mass
(AFDM) was determined by drying a second filter at 105 °C to constant
mass and combusting it at 500 °C for 4 h. Dissolved nutrients (SRP,
NO~3~-N, NH~4~-N) were analysed by the central laboratory of the
Institute (Dr. M. Schäfer) by continuous-flow analysis; detection limits
were 2 µg L^-1^ for SRP and 5 µg L^-1^ for both nitrogen species. Values
below the detection limit were set to half the limit. This affected 7 %
of the SRP measurements but none of the nitrate values.

## Periphyton growth model {#growth-model}

Accrual of chlorophyll *a* on artificial substrata (unglazed ceramic
tiles, 4.7 × 4.7 cm) deployed for 35 days was described by a logistic
model, following @biggs1996 and @stevenson1996 [-@stevenson1996]:

\begin{equation}
  B(t) = \frac{K}{1 + \left(\frac{K - B_0}{B_0}\right) e^{-r t}}
  (\#eq:growth)
\end{equation}

where $B(t)$ is chlorophyll *a* biomass (µg cm^-2^) at time $t$ (days
since deployment), $B_0$ the initial biomass, $K$ the carrying capacity
and $r$ the intrinsic growth rate (d^-1^). Equation \@ref(eq:growth) was
fitted separately for each reach and deployment by nonlinear least
squares (`nls()` with the port algorithm), constraining $K$ to be
positive. Following @doe2020 [p. 45], fits with fewer than five non-zero
observations were discarded; this removed 4 of 72 deployments (viz. K3
in C1, M4 in C3, and M2 and M6 in C4). Where the logistic model failed to converge,
a Gompertz model was fitted instead, cf. Eq. 2.4 in Chapter
\@ref(background); the two give nearly identical estimates of $r$ when
$B_0 \ll K$ [@smith2019; @doe2020, p. 45].

\newpage

## Statistical analysis {-}

Differences between shaded and open reaches were tested with linear
mixed-effects models of the form

$$
\log(y_{ijk}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1\,\text{canopy}_i + \beta_2\,\text{campaign}_j + \beta_3\,(\text{canopy} \times \text{campaign})_{ij} + u_{\text{pair}} + u_{\text{reach}} + \varepsilon_{ijk}
$$

with random intercepts for reach pair and for reach nested in pair. The
response variables were (1) chlorophyll *a*, (2) AFDM, (3) the
autotrophic index (AFDM : chl *a*) and (4) the growth rate $r$ from
Eq. \@ref(eq:growth). Models were fitted by REML with **lme4**
[@bates2015]; *p*-values for the fixed effects were obtained with the
Kenward--Roger approximation. Model assumptions were checked visually
(residuals vs. fitted values, Q--Q plots), e.g. for heteroscedasticity
between campaigns. Where needed, a variance structure was added with
**nlme**, i.e. `varIdent(form = ~ 1 | campaign)`.

```{r model-example, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
m_chla <- lmer(log(chla) ~ canopy * campaign + (1 | pair/reach),
               data = periphyton, REML = TRUE)
anova(m_chla, ddf = "Kenward-Roger")
```

Effect sizes are reported as back-transformed ratios with 95 %
confidence intervals. I did not correct for multiple testing across the
four response variables, since they are strongly correlated and
represent different facets of the same hypothesis [cf. @gelman2012];
this decision is revisited in the Discussion (Section
\@ref(disc-limits)). As @jones2018 put it, "the canopy effect is either
large enough to see in every metric, or it is not there at all."



***

- [ ] Ask Prof. Ritter whether Kenward--Roger is OK for the
  growth-rate models (only 68 fits).
- [ ] Densiometer footnote: cite the manufacturer's manual or Lemmon
    (1956)?

[^densiometer]: Model-C convex spherical densiometer (Forestry
    Suppliers Inc., Jackson, MS, U.S.A.). Readings were converted to
    percent cover following the manufacturer's instructions, i.e. by
    multiplying the number of covered points by 1.04.

    Lemmon's original description (1956) uses a slightly different
    grid; the difference is negligible for canopy cover above ca. 20 %.

    url: jdbc:postgresql://${DB_HOST:localhost}:${DB_PORT:5432}/${DB_NAME:orders}?ApplicationName=order-service&reWriteBatchedInserts=true
    username: ${DB_USER:orders}
    password:
    driver-class-name: org.postgresql.Driver
    hikari:
        maximum-pool-size: 20
        minimum-idle: 5
        connection-timeout: 30000     # ms

        max-lifetime: 1800000
        pool-name: OrderHikariPool
        leak-detection-threshold: 0   # set to 20000 when hunting connection leaks (#1187)

    open-in-view: false
    show-sql: no

        order_updates: true
        "[query.fail_on_pagination_over_collection_fetch]": true

  flyway:
    enabled: true
    locations: classpath:db/migration,classpath:db/seed
    baseline-on-migrate: yes
    baseline-version: 1.0
    out-of-order: false
    validate-on-migrate: TRUE

  kafka:
    bootstrap-servers: ${KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP:localhost:9092}
    client-id: order-service

      group-id: order-service
      auto-offset-reset: earliest
      enable-auto-commit: false
      key-deserializer: org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringDeserializer

      properties:
        spring.deserializer.value.delegate.class: org.springframework.kafka.support.serializer.JsonDeserializer
        spring.json.trusted.packages: "com.acme.*"
        spring.json.use.type.headers: false
    producer:
      acks: all
      retries: 3
      compression-type: zstd
      properties: { linger.ms: 20,batch.size: 65536, enable.idempotence: true }
    listener:
      ack-mode: record
      concurrency: 3

  jackson:
    serialization:
      write-dates-as-timestamps: false
      indent-output: off
    deserialization:
      fail-on-unknown-properties: false
    default-property-inclusion: non_null
    time-zone: UTC


server:
   port: 8080
   shutdown: graceful
   forward-headers-strategy: framework
   servlet:
      context-path: /api
   compression:
      enabled: true
      min-response-size: 1KB
      mime-types: text/html,text/xml,text/plain,text/css,text/javascript,application/javascript,application/json,application/problem+json
   error:
      include-message: always
      include-stacktrace: never
   tomcat:
      threads:
         max: 200
      accesslog:
         enabled: false

management:
  server:
    port: 8081      # separate port so the ingress never exposes actuator
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: "health,info,prometheus,metrics"
        exclude: 'env,beans'
      base-path: /actuator
  endpoint:
    health:
      show-details: when_authorized
      probes:
        enabled: true
      group:
        readiness:
          include: [ readinessState, db, kafka ]
        liveness:
          include: [livenessState]
  metrics:
    tags:
      application: ${spring.application.name}
      region: ${REGION:eu-central-1}
    distribution:
      percentiles-histogram:
        http.server.requests: true
      slo:
        http.server.requests: 50ms,100ms,250ms,500ms,1s
  tracing:
    sampling:
      probability: 0.1
  otlp:
    tracing:
      endpoint: http://otel-collector.observability:4318/v1/traces

logging:
  level:
    root: INFO
    com.acme: DEBUG
    com.acme.orders.client: TRACE    # TODO remove once the payment-gateway timeouts are understood (#1203)
    org.hibernate.SQL: WARN
    org.hibernate.orm.jdbc.bind: off
    org.apache.kafka: WARN
  pattern:
    console: "%d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS} %5p [%t] %-40.40logger{39} : %m%n"
    file:  '%d{ISO8601} %5p ${PID:- } --- [%15.15t] %-40.40logger{39} : %m%n'
  file:
    name: ~
  logback:
    rollingpolicy:
      max-file-size: 50MB
      max-history: 7

info:
  app:
    name: ${spring.application.name}
    description: |
      Order service: owns carts, orders and the checkout saga.
      Talks to payment-gateway (sync, REST) and to inventory (async, Kafka).
    owner: "team-checkout@acme.example.com"

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from itables import show

# Exported every 15 min by the `ops-export` CronJob (see deploy/k8s/cronjobs.yml)
df = pd.read_parquet("data/checkout_metrics_7d.parquet")
errors = pd.read_parquet("data/checkout_errors_7d.parquet")
slow = pd.read_parquet("data/checkout_slow_endpoints_24h.parquet")
deploys = pd.read_csv("data/deploys_7d.csv", parse_dates=["deployed_at"])

last_hour = df[df["ts"] >= df["ts"].max() - pd.Timedelta("1h")]
rpm = last_hour["requests"].sum() / 60
p99 = last_hour["latency_p99_ms"].median()
err_rate = last_hour["errors_5xx"].sum() / last_hour["requests"].sum()
slo_budget_left = 0.62  # FIXME: compute from the SLO export instead of hard-coding
```

import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_parquet("data/checkout_metrics_7d.parquet")
errors = pd.read_parquet("data/checkout_errors_7d.parquet")

deploys = pd.read_csv("data/deploys_7d.csv", parse_dates=["deployed_at"])

last_hour = df[df["ts"] >= df["ts"].max() - pd.Timedelta("1h")]
rpm = last_hour["requests"].sum() / 60
p99 = last_hour["latency_p99_ms"].median()
err_rate = last_hour["errors_5xx"].sum() / last_hour["requests"].sum()

arguments.content:
## kube-prometheus-stack overrides for the prod-eu-1 cluster.
## Upstream defaults: https://github.com/prometheus-community/helm-charts/blob/main/charts/kube-prometheus-stack/values.yaml
## Chart version is pinned in ../Chart.yaml (58.x). Read the upgrade notes before bumping -- CRDs are NOT upgraded by helm.
##

fullnameOverride: kps
# crds:
#   enabled: true

defaultRules:
  create: true
  rules:
    etcd: false               # managed control plane (EKS), nothing to scrape
    kubeScheduler: false
    kubeControllerManager: false
    kubeProxy: false
  additionalRuleLabels: { cluster: prod-eu-1,team: platform }


alertmanager:
  enabled: true
  config:
    global:
      resolve_timeout: 5m
      slack_api_url_file: /etc/alertmanager/secrets/alertmanager-slack/url
    route:
      receiver: 'null'
      group_by: ['alertname', 'job']
      group_wait: 30s
      group_interval: 5m
      repeat_interval: 4h
      routes:
        - receiver: 'null'
          matchers:
            - alertname = "Watchdog"
        - receiver: pagerduty
          matchers:
          - severity =~ "critical|page"
          continue: true
        - receiver: slack-platform
          matchers: [ 'severity =~ "warning|critical"', 'namespace =~ "kube-.*|monitoring|ingress-nginx"' ]
          group_by: [ alertname, namespace ]
        - receiver: slack-apps
          matchers:
            - team = "apps"
          mute_time_intervals: [ weekends ]
    inhibit_rules:
      - source_matchers: [ 'severity = "critical"' ]
        target_matchers: [ 'severity =~ "warning|info"' ]
        equal: [namespace, alertname]
    receivers:
      - name: 'null'
      - name: pagerduty
        pagerduty_configs:
          - routing_key_file: /etc/alertmanager/secrets/alertmanager-pagerduty/routing-key
            severity: '{{ if eq .CommonLabels.severity "page" }}critical{{ else }}{{ .CommonLabels.severity }}{{ end }}'
            send_resolved: true
      - name: slack-platform
        slack_configs:
          - channel: '#alerts-platform'
            send_resolved: true
            title: '[{{ .Status | toUpper }}] {{ .CommonLabels.alertname }}'
            title_link: 'https://grafana.acme.example.com/alerting/list?search={{ .CommonLabels.alertname }}'
            text: |-
              {{ range .Alerts -}}
              *{{ .Annotations.summary }}*
              {{ if .Annotations.description }}{{ .Annotations.description }}{{ end }}
              {{ if .Annotations.runbook_url }}:book: <{{ .Annotations.runbook_url }}|Runbook>{{ end }}
              *Labels:* {{ range .Labels.SortedPairs }}`{{ .Name }}={{ .Value }}` {{ end }}
              {{ end }}
      - name: slack-apps
        slack_configs:
        - channel: "#alerts-apps"
          title: '[{{ .Status | toUpper }}] {{ .CommonLabels.alertname }}'
          text: >-
            {{ .CommonAnnotations.summary }} — {{ len .Alerts }} alert(s),
            first fired {{ (index .Alerts 0).StartsAt.Format "15:04 MST" }}
    time_intervals:
      - name: weekends
        time_intervals:
          - weekdays: ['saturday', 'sunday']
  alertmanagerSpec:
    replicas: 2
    retention: 120h
    secrets: [ alertmanager-slack, alertmanager-pagerduty ]
    storage:
      volumeClaimTemplate:
        spec:
          storageClassName: gp3
          accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
          resources:
            requests:
              storage: 10Gi
    # externalUrl: https://alertmanager.acme.example.com
    resources:
      requests: { cpu: 50m, memory: 128Mi }
      limits:   { memory: 256Mi }

grafana:
    enabled: true
    # admin password for kind/dev clusters only; prod overrides it from the sealed secret
    adminPassword: prom-operator
    defaultDashboardsTimezone: browser
    ingress:
        enabled: true
        ingressClassName: nginx
        annotations:
            cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod
        hosts: [ grafana.acme.example.com ]
        tls:
            - secretName: grafana-tls
              hosts:
                  - grafana.acme.example.com
    sidecar:
        dashboards:
            enabled: true
            label: grafana_dashboard
            labelValue: "1"
            searchNamespace: ALL
            folderAnnotation: grafana_folder
            provider:
                foldersFromFilesStructure: true
        datasources:
            enabled: true
            defaultDatasourceEnabled: true
    grafana.ini:
        server:
            root_url: https://grafana.acme.example.com
        auth.generic_oauth:
            enabled: true
            name: Acme SSO
            allow_sign_up: true
            client_id: grafana
            client_secret: $__file{/etc/secrets/grafana-oauth/client-secret}
            scopes: openid profile email groups
            auth_url: https://login.acme.example.com/realms/acme/protocol/openid-connect/auth
            token_url: https://login.acme.example.com/realms/acme/protocol/openid-connect/token
            api_url: https://login.acme.example.com/realms/acme/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo
            role_attribute_path: contains(groups[*], 'grafana-admins') && 'Admin' || contains(groups[*], 'grafana-editors') && 'Editor' || 'Viewer'
        analytics:
            check_for_updates: false
            reporting_enabled: off
        users:
            viewers_can_edit: false
    additionalDataSources:
        - name: Loki
          type: loki
          uid: loki
          url: http://loki-gateway.logging.svc.cluster.local
          access: proxy
          jsonData:
              maxLines: 1000
              derivedFields:
                  - datasourceUid: tempo
                    matcherRegex: '"trace_id":"(\w+)"'
                    name: TraceID
                    url: "$${__value.raw}"
        - name: Tempo
          type: tempo
          uid: tempo
          url: http://tempo.tracing.svc.cluster.local:3100
          # jsonData:
          #   tracesToLogsV2: { datasourceUid: loki }
    persistence: { enabled: false }


prometheus:
  enabled: true
  ingress:
    enabled: false
  prometheusSpec:
    replicas: 2
    retention: 15d
    retentionSize: "45GB"
    scrapeInterval: 30s
    evaluationInterval: 30s
    externalLabels:
      cluster: prod-eu-1
      region: eu-central-1
    # pick up ServiceMonitors/PodMonitors/rules from every namespace, not just the release's
    ruleSelectorNilUsesHelmValues: false
    serviceMonitorSelectorNilUsesHelmValues: false
    podMonitorSelectorNilUsesHelmValues: false
    probeSelectorNilUsesHelmValues: false
    enableFeatures: [ exemplar-storage,memory-snapshot-on-shutdown ]
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 4Gi
      limits:
        memory: 8Gi
    storageSpec:
      volumeClaimTemplate:
        spec:
          storageClassName: gp3
          accessModes: [ "ReadWriteOnce" ]
          resources:
            requests: { storage: 50Gi }
    # remoteWrite:
    #   - url: https://mimir.acme.example.com/api/v1/push
    #     headers: { X-Scope-OrgID: prod-eu-1 }
    additionalScrapeConfigs:
      - job_name: kubernetes-pods-annotated
        honor_labels: true
        kubernetes_sd_configs:
          - role: pod
        relabel_configs:
          - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_scrape]
            action: keep
            regex: true
          - source_labels: [ __meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_path ]
            action: replace
            target_label: __metrics_path__
            regex: (.+)
          - source_labels: [__address__, __meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_port]
            action: replace
            regex: ([^:]+)(?::\d+)?;(\d+)
            replacement: $1:$2
            target_label: __address__
          - action: labelmap
            regex: __meta_kubernetes_pod_label_(.+)
          - source_labels: [
                __meta_kubernetes_namespace,
                __meta_kubernetes_pod_name
              ]
            separator: /
            target_label: instance
      - job_name: blackbox-http
        metrics_path: /probe
        params: { module: [http_2xx] }
        static_configs:
          - targets:
            - https://shop.acme.example.com/healthz
            - https://api.acme.example.com/v1/health
        relabel_configs:
          - { source_labels: [__address__], target_label: __param_target }
          - { source_labels: [__param_target], target_label: instance }
          - target_label: __address__
            replacement: blackbox-exporter.monitoring.svc:9115

prometheus-node-exporter:
  hostRootFsMount:
    enabled: true
    mountPropagation: HostToContainer
  tolerations:
  - operator: Exists
  extraArgs:
  - --collector.filesystem.mount-points-exclude=^/(dev|proc|sys|var/lib/docker/.+|var/lib/kubelet/.+)($|/)
  - --collector.netclass.ignored-devices=^(veth.*|cali.*|[a-f0-9]{15})$

nodeExporter:
  enabled: true
  # operatingSystems: { linux: { enabled: true }, darwin: { enabled: false } }

kubeStateMetrics:
  enabled: true

kube-state-metrics:
  metricLabelsAllowlist:
    - pods=[app.kubernetes.io/name,app.kubernetes.io/component]
    - deployments=[*]
  collectors: [ certificatesigningrequests, configmaps, cronjobs, daemonsets, deployments,
      endpoints, horizontalpodautoscalers, ingresses, jobs, leases, namespaces, nodes,
      persistentvolumeclaims, persistentvolumes, poddisruptionbudgets, pods, replicasets,
      secrets, services, statefulsets, storageclasses ]
  # selfMonitor:
  #   enabled: true

kubeEtcd:
  enabled: false
kubeScheduler: { enabled: false }
kubeControllerManager:
  enabled: no
kubeProxy:
  enabled: false

Trailmate release notes ======================= [![Download on the App Store](https://trailmate.example.com/badges/app-store.svg)](https://apps.apple.com/app/trailmate-hiking-maps/id1490123456?platform=iphone&l=en) [![Get it on Google Play](https://trailmate.example.com/badges/google-play.svg)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.acme.trailmate&hl=en&gl=US) User-facing changes to the **Trailmate** apps for iOS and Android. Server-side changes are tracked in [trailmate-api/CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/acme/trailmate-api/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md), the web planner has its own page at . Beta builds are announced in `#trailmate-beta` and go out through TestFlight and the Play Console internal track first. Version 5.4.0 (build 1203) -------------------------- _Released 2024-04-22 on iOS · 24 April 2024 on Android (staged rollout 10 % → 100 % by Apr 29)_ ### ✨ New * **Offline topo packs.** Download whole regions (up to 2 GB) for areas without signal — tap *Map → ⋯ → Download area*. Packs update in the background, on Wi‑Fi only. * iOS: uses `BGProcessingTask`, so updates may wait until the phone is charging. * Android: honours *Data Saver*; on Android 14 the download runs as a user-initiated data transfer job and shows a persistent notification. * Elevation profile now shows grade colouring (green < 5 %, amber 5–12 %, red > 12 %). * New languages: Português (Brasil), 日本語 and Čeština — thanks to our volunteer translators on [Weblate](https://hosted.weblate.org/projects/trailmate/app-strings/?utm_source=changelog&utm_medium=app&utm_campaign=5.4.0#information)! * Live Activity for active recordings * iOS: 16.1+ only, shows distance, elapsed time and the next waypoint * Android: the ongoing notification got the same layout (no Live Activities on Android, sorry) ### 🐛 Fixed * Recording no longer stops after ~45 min with the screen off on some Samsung devices ([#2290](https://github.com/acme/trailmate/issues/2290)). * Android: we now request `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION` explicitly and ask to be excluded from *Put unused apps to sleep*. * GPX import accepted files with a `` but no `` and then crashed. It now shows a proper error. * Distance units flipped back to km after changing the system language. (Reported by several people using the de-CH locale – merci vielmal!) * The ascent label showed `NaN m` for routes with a single point. * Fixed a memory leak when scrubbing the elevation chart quickly (iOS only). ### 🔧 Under the hood * Kotlin 1.9.23 / AGP 8.3; iOS deployment target raised to **15.0**. * Map tiles are cached for 30 days instead of 7 → roughly 40 % fewer tile requests. * Crash reporting moved from Crashlytics to our self-hosted Sentry. The opt-out still lives in *Settings → Privacy → Diagnostics*.


Offline packs and the new grade colours (Pixel 7, dark theme)

*** ## 5.3.1 — 2024-03-05 ### 🐛 Fixed * Hotfix: the app crashed on launch for people with more than 10 000 saved waypoints. Sorry about that! * iOS: the Core Data migration ran on the main thread and got killed by the watchdog after 20 s. * Android: Room migration 41 → 42 was missing an index; it's now created lazily on first use. * Share sheet showed an empty preview for routes with emoji in the name (e.g. "Sunrise 🏔️ loop"). *** ## 5.3.0 — 2024-02-11 ### ✨ New * **Route planner v2** with snapping to trails, roads or *freehand*. * Weather along the route: hourly forecast for the estimated arrival time at each waypoint. * Uses the new `/v2/forecast/along-route` endpoint and falls back to point forecasts on older servers. * Home-screen widgets: "Last hike" and "Weekly distance".
Android widgets follow Material You colours; iOS widgets support StandBy mode. ### 💥 Changed * The *Explore* tab is now called *Discover*. Muscle memory, we know… * Minimum Android version is now **8.0 (API 26)**. * Photos attached to waypoints are stored at max. 2048 px instead of full resolution; the originals stay in your photo library. ### 🐛 Fixed * The compass calibration prompt appeared every time the map was opened. * `Export → KML` produced invalid XML when a note contained `&` (it is now escaped as `&`). * VoiceOver announced the record button as "button, button". *** Version 5.2.0 (build 1150) -------------------------- Released Dec. 4th, 2023\ TestFlight build 1149 went out on Nov 28 for the Watch beta. ### ✨ New - Apple Watch companion app (**beta**) — start and stop recordings, see distance and pace on your wrist. - Heart-rate import from Health Connect / Apple Health. - Dark map style for night hikes 🌙. ### 🐛 Fixed - Track smoothing created spikes when GPS accuracy was worse than 50 m. - iOS: points with `horizontalAccuracy > 50` are dropped before smoothing. - Android: same filter, see `LocationFilter.kt`. - "Download failed (code -1009)" when switching from Wi‑Fi to cellular in the middle of a download. *** ## 5.1.2 - 2023/10/18 ## * Fixed: sync conflicts duplicated waypoints on Android 14 ([#2041](https://github.com/acme/trailmate/issues/2041), [#2044](https://github.com/acme/trailmate/issues/2044)). * Fixed: iPad split view cut off the bottom sheet. * Updated translations: de, fr, it, es, nl. ## 5.1.1 - 2023/09/30 ## * Fixed: the *Rate us* dialog popped up during an active recording. We're not __that__ desperate. ## 5.1.0 - 2023/09/26 ## ### ✨ New * iOS 17 support, including interactive widgets. * Android 14 support (predictive back gesture, partial photo access). * "Turnaround time" reminder — pick a time and Trailmate nudges you to head back before dark. ### 🐛 Fixed * Lots of small layout fixes for large text sizes (Dynamic Type / font scale 200 %). Older releases (4.x and earlier) are archived on the [releases page][releases]; the 4.0 rewrite from React Native to native Swift/Kotlin is described in detail in our blog post *"Why we rewrote Trailmate (and what we'd do differently)"*, which also explains why some settings were reset for people upgrading from 3.x and why offline maps from 3.x couldn't be migrated automatically. --- Known issues ------------ - [ ] Offline packs larger than 1.5 GB fail to unzip on some Xiaomi devices running MIUI 14 (#2301) - [ ] The Live Activity doesn't update while Low Power Mode is on (iOS limitation, Feedback FB13698012) - [x] ~~Recording stops on Samsung devices with aggressive battery saving~~ — fixed in 5.4.0 - [ ] Apple Watch app: - [ ] heart rate is sometimes missing for the first 2–3 minutes - [x] crash when the paired iPhone is locked (fixed in TestFlight build 1161) - [ ] no metric/imperial setting yet, it follows the iPhone ## Supported OS versions | App version | iOS | iPadOS | Android | Watch | |:------------|:-----:|:------:|--------:|:------| | 5.4.x | 15.0+ | 15.0+ | 8.0+ (API 26) | watchOS 9+ | | 5.3.x | 14.0+ | 14.0+ | 8.0+ (API 26) | watchOS 9+ | | 5.0 – 5.2 | 14.0+ | 14.0+ | 7.0+ (API 24) | watchOS 8+ *(beta)* | | 4.x | 13.0+ | 13.0+ | 6.0+ (API 23) | — | Older versions are no longer supported and will be rejected by the API after **30 June 2024**. Questions? Write to or see the [FAQ][faq]. Trailmate © 2019–2024 Acme Outdoor GmbH [faq]: https://trailmate.example.com/help/faq#which-devices-are-supported "Which devices are supported?"
