As shown in @fig-importance, the bare-soil SWIR bands (B11, B12) and the
late-summer NDVI minimum dominated, followed by elevation and the
topographic wetness index. Legacy soil maps contributed little once the
Sentinel-2 composites were included.

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

Our accuracies are comparable to those of other regional studies using
bare-soil composites, e.g. $R^2$ = 0.52–0.64 in @dematte2020 and 0.49 in @castaldi2019, though direct comparisons are hampered by differences in sampling depth, validation design and SOC range. Three caveats apply.

- First, the bare-soil composite is, by construction, biased towards
  fields that are ploughed in late summer.
    - Olive groves with permanent cover are under-represented, which likely explains the weaker performance there.
- Second, BD was measured on only 39% of sites; errors in the
  pedotransfer function propagate directly into stock estimates (@eq-stock).
- Third, the sampling period (2019–2022) includes two drought years, cf.
  the 2022 summer, when NDVI minima were unusually low.

> The question for MRV schemes is not whether remote sensing can replace
> soil sampling, but how few samples it lets us get away with.
>
> > We think the honest answer, for now, is "fewer, but not few".

## Acknowledgments {.unnumbered}

We thank the farmers of the Campiña cooperatives for access to their
fields, and Dr. R. Ortega for help with the BD measurements. This work
was funded by the Spanish Ministry of Science (grant PID2020-11xxxx) and
the BMBF project *SOC-Monitor*.

## Data availability {.unnumbered}

Code and derived data are available at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.0000000>; raw sample
coordinates are withheld at the request of landowners.

:::

kable(cv$tuning_grid)
```

    and land use. Using the published function of @alexander1980 instead
    changed mean stocks by less than 3%.

info:

    url: https://acme.example/support

    name: Apache 2.0

servers:

tags:
- name: pet
  description: Everything about your pets
  externalDocs:
    description: Find out more

- name: store
  description: Access to petstore orders
- name: user
  description:   Operations about user
  externalDocs: { description: "User guide", url: "https://docs.acme.example/petstore/users" }


paths:
  /pets:
    get:
      tags: [ pet ]
      summary: List pets
      description: Returns all pets the caller has access to, optionally filtered by tag. Results are ordered by createdAt, newest first.
      operationId: listPets
      parameters:
        - name: limit
          in: query
          description: How many items to return at one time (max 100)
          required: false
          schema: { type: integer, format: int32, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, default: 20 }
        - name: tags
          in: query
          description: tags to filter by
          required: false
          style: form
          explode: false
          schema:
            type: array
            items:
              type: string
          example: [dog,cat]
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/RequestId'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A paged array of pets
          headers:
            x-next: { description: Link to the next page, schema: { type: string } }
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                maxItems: 100
                items:
                  $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pet"
        default:
          $ref: '#/components/responses/UnexpectedError'
    post:
      tags: [pet]
      summary: Create a pet
      operationId: createPet
      requestBody:
        $ref: '#/components/requestBodies/NewPet'
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Null response
        '422':
          $ref: "#/components/responses/ValidationError"
      security:
        - petstore_auth: [ "write:pets", "read:pets" ]

  /pets/{petId}:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/PetId'
    get:
      tags:
        - pet
      summary: Info for a specific pet
      operationId: showPetById
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Expected response to a valid request
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/AnyPet'

                name: Rex
                petType: dog

      summary: Replace a pet
      operationId: replacePet
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content: { application/json: { schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet' } } }
      responses:
        '200': { description: Updated }
        '404': { $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound" }
    delete:
      tags: [ pet ]
      summary: Deletes a pet
      operationId: deletePet
      parameters:
        - { name: api_key, in: header, required: false, schema: { type: string } }
      responses:
        '204':
          description: Deleted

    post:
      tags: [pet]
      summary: Upload a photo
      operationId: uploadPetPhoto
      parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/PetId'
      requestBody:
        content:

            schema:

              required: [file]

                caption: { type: string, maxLength: 280 }
            encoding:
              file: { contentType: "image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp" }

        content:

          operationId: loginUser

                          schema: { type: integer, format: int32 }
                  content:
                      application/json:
                          schema:
                              type: string
              '400':
                  description: Invalid username/password supplied
          security: []

components:
  parameters:
    PetId:
      name: petId
      in: path
      required: true
      description: The id of the pet to retrieve
      schema: { type: string }
    RequestId: { name: X-Request-Id, in: header, required: false, schema: { type: string, format: uuid } }
  requestBodies:
    NewPet:
      description: Pet object that needs to be added to the store
      required: true
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/NewPet'
  responses:
    NotFound:
      description: The specified resource was not found
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Error'
    ValidationError:
      description: Request body failed validation
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Error' }
          example:
            code: 422
            message: "name: must not be blank"
    UnexpectedError:
      description: unexpected error
      content: { application/json: { schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error" } } }

  schemas:
    NewPet:
      type: object
      required:
        - name
        - petType
      properties:
        name: { type: string, example: Rex }
        petType: { type: string }
        status:
          type: string
          description: pet status in the store
          enum: [available, pending,sold]
          default: available
        tags: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
    Pet:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/NewPet'
        - type: object
          required: [ id ]
          properties:
            id: { type: integer, format: int64, readOnly: true }
            createdAt: { type: string, format: date-time }
    AnyPet:
      oneOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
        - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Cat"
      discriminator:
        propertyName: petType
        mapping:
          dog: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
          cat: "#/components/schemas/Cat"
    Dog:
      allOf:
      - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
      - type: object
        properties:
          packSize: { type: integer, format: int32, minimum: 0, default: 0 }
    Cat:
      allOf:
      - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
      - type: object
        properties:
          huntingSkill:
            type: string
            enum: [ clueless, lazy, adventurous, aggressive ]
    Order:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: {type: integer, format: int64}
        petId: {type: integer, format: int64}
        quantity: {type: integer, format: int32, minimum: 1}
        shipDate: { type: string, format: date-time }
        status:
          type: string
          enum:
            - placed
            - approved
            - delivered
        complete: { type: boolean, default: false }
      example:
        id: 10
        petId: 198772
        quantity: 7
        shipDate: 2024-03-01T10:15:00Z
        status: approved
    Error:
      type: object
      required: [code, message]
      properties:
        code: { type: integer, format: int32 }
        message: { type: string }

  securitySchemes:
    api_key:
      type: apiKey
      name: api_key
      in: header
    petstore_auth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        authorizationCode:
          authorizationUrl: https://auth.acme.example/oauth/authorize
          tokenUrl: https://auth.acme.example/oauth/token
          scopes:
            write:pets: modify pets in your account
            'read:pets': read your pets
security:
  - api_key: []

---
## GitLab Runner chart values -- shared k8s runners for the acme/platform group
## Chart: gitlab/gitlab-runner 0.62.x
## Docs:  https://docs.gitlab.com/runner/install/kubernetes.html
##
## We use an authentication token (glrt-...) created in the runner UI; the old registration-token flow is gone.
## The token lives in the `gitlab-runner-secret` secret, NOT here. Do not commit tokens. Yes, again.

image:
  registry: registry.gitlab.com
  image: gitlab-org/gitlab-runner
  # tag: alpine-v16.9.1

imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

# -- The GitLab server URL (with protocol) to register the runner against
gitlabUrl: https://gitlab.example.com/
runnerToken: ""
# runnerRegistrationToken: ""      # deprecated, removed in 17.0

unregisterRunners: true
terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 3600
concurrent: 10
shutdown_timeout: 0
checkInterval: 30
logLevel: info§§1
logFormat: json

## Prometheus metrics
metrics:
  enabled: true
  portName: metrics
  port: 9252
  serviceMonitor:
     enabled: true
     labels: { release: kps }
     interval: ""

sessionServer:
  enabled: false

rbac:
  create: true
  clusterWideAccess: false
  podSecurityPolicy: { enabled: false, resourceNames: [] }
  rules:
    - apiGroups: [""]
      resources: ["pods", "pods/exec", "secrets"]
      verbs: ["get","list","watch","create","patch","delete"]
    - apiGroups: [""]
      resources:
        - configmaps
        - pods/attach
        - pods/log
        - serviceaccounts
      verbs:   [ "get", "list", "watch", "create", "update", "patch", "delete" ]
    -   apiGroups: [ "" ]
        resources: [ services ]
        verbs: [ create,get ]
  serviceAccountAnnotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gitlab-runner-cache


runners:
  # Runner configuration, rendered into config.toml by the chart (passed through `tpl`).
  # https://docs.gitlab.com/runner/configuration/advanced-configuration.html
  config: |
    [[runners]]
      name = "k8s-shared-{{ .Release.Namespace }}"
      output_limit = 16384
      environment = ["FF_USE_FASTZIP=true", "FF_KUBERNETES_HONOR_ENTRYPOINT=true"]
      [runners.kubernetes]
        namespace = "{{ .Release.Namespace }}"
        image = "alpine:3.19"
        privileged = false
        poll_timeout = 600
        cpu_request = "500m"
        cpu_limit = "2"
        memory_request = "1Gi"
        memory_limit = "4Gi"
        service_cpu_request = "100m"
        helper_cpu_request = "50m"
        [runners.kubernetes.node_selector]
          "kubernetes.io/os" = "linux"
          "node.acme.example.com/pool" = "ci"
        [runners.kubernetes.node_tolerations]
          "dedicated=ci" = "NoSchedule"
        [[runners.kubernetes.volumes.empty_dir]]
          name = "docker-certs"
          mount_path = "/certs/client"
          medium = "Memory"
        [[runners.kubernetes.volumes.empty_dir]]
          name = "build-cache"
          mount_path = "/cache"
      [runners.cache]
        Type = "s3"
        Path = "runner"
        Shared = true
        [runners.cache.s3]
          ServerAddress = "s3.amazonaws.com"
          BucketName = "acme-gitlab-runner-cache"
          BucketLocation = "eu-central-1"
          AuthenticationType = "iam"

  executor: kubernetes
  tags: "k8s,docker,linux"
  runUntagged: false
  protected: no
  secret: gitlab-runner-secret
  cache: {}
  # cache:
  #   secretName: s3access       # only needed for access-key auth, we use IRSA

securityContext:
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
  runAsNonRoot: true
  privileged: false
  capabilities:
    drop: ["ALL"]

podSecurityContext:
  runAsUser: 100
  fsGroup: 65533

resources:
   limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 200m
   requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m

affinity: {}
nodeSelector: { kubernetes.io/os: linux }
tolerations: []
hostAliases: []
#  - ip: "10.10.0.15"
#    hostnames: [ "gitlab.example.com" ]

podAnnotations:
  cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false"
podLabels: {}
priorityClassName: ~§§2

envVars:
  - name: RUNNER_EXECUTOR
    value: kubernetes
  - name: CI_SERVER_TLS_CA_FILE
    value: null
  - name: KUBERNETES_POLL_TIMEOUT
    value: '600'
  # RUNNER_PRE_GET_SOURCES_SCRIPT is easier to read here than in config.toml
  - name: RUNNER_PRE_GET_SOURCES_SCRIPT
    value: >-
      git config --global http.postBuffer 524288000 &&
      git config --global core.compression 0



## Deprecated top-level keys kept around because old docs (and old MRs) still reference them
hpa: {}
service:
  enabled: false
  type: ClusterIP
...

arguments.content:
# Tutorial: deploy the Acme sample shop to Kubernetes

![Architecture of the sample shop: browser, ingress, frontend, API, PostgreSQL](./images/k8s-tutorial/architecture.png "Sample shop architecture")

In this tutorial you'll deploy the **Acme sample shop** — a small three-tier app — to a
local Kubernetes cluster created with [kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/), expose it through an
ingress controller, and roll out a new version without downtime. Budget about 45 minutes.

> [!NOTE]
> Everything here runs on your laptop. Nothing is deployed to a cloud account, and you can delete
> all of it in the [Cleanup](#cleanup) step.

## Prerequisites

- [ ] Docker 24+ (or Podman 4.7+ with the Docker-compatible socket enabled)
- [ ] `kind` 0.22+
- [ ] `kubectl` 1.29+
- [ ] `helm` 3.14+ — only for the optional monitoring step
- [x] About 4 GB of free RAM

Check your versions:

```bash
docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'
kind version
kubectl version --client
```

## Step 1: Create the cluster

1. Save the following cluster config as `kind-config.yaml`. It maps ports 80 and 443 on your
   machine into the cluster, so the ingress controller is reachable on `localhost`:

   ```yaml
   kind: Cluster
   apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
   name: shop
   nodes:
     - role: control-plane
       kubeadmConfigPatches:
         - |
           kind: InitConfiguration
           nodeRegistration:
             kubeletExtraArgs:
               node-labels: "ingress-ready=true"
       extraPortMappings:
         - containerPort: 80
           hostPort: 80
         - containerPort: 443
           hostPort: 443
     - role: worker
     - role: worker
   ```

2. Create the cluster:

   ```bash
   kind create cluster --config kind-config.yaml
   ```

   Expected output (abridged):

   ```text
   Creating cluster "shop" ...
    ✓ Ensuring node image (kindest/node:v1.29.2)
    ✓ Preparing nodes
    ✓ Writing configuration
    ✓ Starting control-plane
    ✓ Installing CNI
    ✓ Installing StorageClass
    ✓ Joining worker nodes
   Set kubectl context to "kind-shop"
   ```

3. Verify that all three nodes are `Ready`:

   ```bash
   kubectl get nodes
   ```

> [!TIP]
> If `kind create cluster` hangs at *Starting control-plane*, Docker Desktop probably has less
> than 4 GB of memory assigned. Raise it under **Settings → Resources** and try again.

## Step 2: Install the ingress controller

1. Apply the ingress-nginx manifest that is built for kind:

   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/controller-v1.10.0/deploy/static/provider/kind/deploy.yaml
   ```

1. Wait until the controller is ready:

   ```bash
   kubectl wait --namespace ingress-nginx \
     --for=condition=ready pod \
     --selector=app.kubernetes.io/component=controller \
     --timeout=120s
   ```

1. That's it. (Yes, every item above is numbered `1.` — Markdown renumbers them for you.)

## Step 3: Deploy the database

1. Create a namespace and the database credentials:

   ```bash
   kubectl create namespace shop
   kubectl -n shop create secret generic db-credentials \
     --from-literal=POSTGRES_USER=shop \
     --from-literal=POSTGRES_PASSWORD="$(openssl rand -hex 16)"
   ```

2. Apply the PostgreSQL manifest from the repository:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n shop apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/acme/sample-shop/v2.3.0/deploy/k8s/postgres.yaml
   ```

3. Wait for the pod; the first start takes a while because the volume is initialised:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n shop rollout status statefulset/postgres --timeout=180s
   ```

## Step 4: Deploy the API and the frontend

Continuing the numbering from the previous step:

4. Deploy the API. Save this as `api.yaml`:

   ```yaml
   apiVersion: apps/v1
   kind: Deployment
   metadata:
     name: api
     namespace: shop
   spec:
     replicas: 2
     selector:
       matchLabels: { app: api }
     template:
       metadata:
         labels: { app: api }
       spec:
         containers:
           - name: api
             image: ghcr.io/acme/sample-shop-api:2.3.0
             ports:
               - containerPort: 8080
             envFrom:
               - secretRef:
                   name: db-credentials
             readinessProbe:
               httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: 8080 }
               periodSeconds: 5
   ```

   and apply it with `kubectl apply -f api.yaml`.

5. Deploy the frontend, the two services and the ingress in one go:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n shop apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/acme/sample-shop/v2.3.0/deploy/k8s/frontend.yaml
   ```

6. Open <http://shop.localtest.me> in your browser. `localtest.me` resolves to `127.0.0.1`, so no
   `/etc/hosts` editing is needed.

![The sample shop's home page showing three products](./images/k8s-tutorial/shop-home.png)

> [!NOTE]

# Tutorial: deploy the Acme sample shop to Kubernetes

![Architecture of the sample shop: browser, ingress, frontend, API, PostgreSQL](./images/k8s-tutorial/architecture.png "Sample shop architecture")

In this tutorial you'll deploy the **Acme sample shop** — a small three-tier app — to a
local Kubernetes cluster created with [kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/), expose it through an
ingress controller, and roll out a new version without downtime. Budget about 45 minutes.

> [!NOTE]
> Everything here runs on your laptop. Nothing is deployed to a cloud account, and you can delete
> all of it in the [Cleanup](#cleanup) step.

## Prerequisites

- [ ] Docker 24+ (or Podman 4.7+ with the Docker-compatible socket enabled)
- [ ] `kind` 0.22+
- [ ] `kubectl` 1.29+
- [ ] `helm` 3.14+ — only for the optional monitoring step
- [x] About 4 GB of free RAM

Check your versions:

```bash
docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'
kind version
kubectl version --client
```

## Step 1: Create the cluster

1. Save the following cluster config as `kind-config.yaml`. It maps ports 80 and 443 on your
   machine into the cluster, so the ingress controller is reachable on `localhost`:

   ```yaml
   kind: Cluster
   apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
   name: shop
   nodes:
     - role: control-plane
       kubeadmConfigPatches:
         - |
           kind: InitConfiguration
           nodeRegistration:
             kubeletExtraArgs:
               node-labels: "ingress-ready=true"
       extraPortMappings:
         - containerPort: 80
           hostPort: 80
         - containerPort: 443
           hostPort: 443
     - role: worker
     - role: worker
   ```

2. Create the cluster:

   ```bash
   kind create cluster --config kind-config.yaml
   ```

   Expected output (abridged):

   ```text
   Creating cluster "shop" ...
    ✓ Ensuring node image (kindest/node:v1.29.2)
    ✓ Preparing nodes
    ✓ Writing configuration
    ✓ Starting control-plane
    ✓ Installing CNI
    ✓ Installing StorageClass
    ✓ Joining worker nodes
   Set kubectl context to "kind-shop"
   ```

3. Verify that all three nodes are `Ready`:

   ```bash
   kubectl get nodes
   ```

> [!TIP]
> If `kind create cluster` hangs at *Starting control-plane*, Docker Desktop probably has less
> than 4 GB of memory assigned. Raise it under **Settings → Resources** and try again.

## Step 2: Install the ingress controller

1. Apply the ingress-nginx manifest that is built for kind:

   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/controller-v1.10.0/deploy/static/provider/kind/deploy.yaml
   ```

1. Wait until the controller is ready:

   ```bash
   kubectl wait --namespace ingress-nginx \
     --for=condition=ready pod \
     --selector=app.kubernetes.io/component=controller \
     --timeout=120s
   ```

1. That's it. (Yes, every item above is numbered `1.` — Markdown renumbers them for you.)

## Step 3: Deploy the database

1. Create a namespace and the database credentials:

   ```bash
   kubectl create namespace shop
   kubectl -n shop create secret generic db-credentials \
     --from-literal=POSTGRES_USER=shop \
     --from-literal=POSTGRES_PASSWORD="$(openssl rand -hex 16)"
   ```

2. Apply the PostgreSQL manifest from the repository:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n shop apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/acme/sample-shop/v2.3.0/deploy/k8s/postgres.yaml
   ```

3. Wait for the pod; the first start takes a while because the volume is initialised:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n shop rollout status statefulset/postgres --timeout=180s
   ```

Continuing the numbering from the previous step:

4. Deploy the API. Save this as `api.yaml`:

   ```yaml
   apiVersion: apps/v1
   kind: Deployment
   metadata:
     name: api
     namespace: shop
   spec:
     replicas: 2
     selector:
       matchLabels: { app: api }
     template:
       metadata:
         labels: { app: api }
       spec:
         containers:
           - name: api
             image: ghcr.io/acme/sample-shop-api:2.3.0
             ports:
               - containerPort: 8080
             envFrom:
               - secretRef:
                   name: db-credentials
             readinessProbe:
               httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: 8080 }
               periodSeconds: 5
   ```

   and apply it with `kubectl apply -f api.yaml`.

5. Deploy the frontend, the two services and the ingress in one go:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n shop apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/acme/sample-shop/v2.3.0/deploy/k8s/frontend.yaml
   ```

6. Open <http://shop.localtest.me> in your browser. `localtest.me` resolves to `127.0.0.1`, so no
   `/etc/hosts` editing is needed.

![The sample shop's home page showing three products](./images/k8s-tutorial/shop-home.png)

> [!NOTE]
> On Apple Silicon, kind runs `arm64` nodes. The sample images are multi-arch, but if you build
> your own images you need to build for the right platform and load them into the cluster:
>
> ```bash
> docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 -t shop-api:dev ./api
> kind load docker-image shop-api:dev --name shop
> ```

### What just happened?

* The `Deployment` created a `ReplicaSet`, which created two pods.
  - each pod got a cluster-internal IP address
    + you can see them with `kubectl -n shop get pods -o wide`
  - the `api` Service load-balances across those addresses
* The `Ingress` routes requests for `shop.localtest.me` to the frontend Service.
  - the frontend calls the API through its Service name, `http://api:8080`
* The readiness probe keeps traffic away from pods that aren't ready yet.

## Step 5: Roll out a new version

1. Update the image:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n shop set image deployment/api api=ghcr.io/acme/sample-shop-api:2.4.0
   ```

2. Watch the rollout:

   - from a second terminal, run

         kubectl -n shop get pods -l app=api -w

     and keep it open; you'll see new pods start before the old ones terminate.
   - or simply run `kubectl -n shop rollout status deployment/api`.

3. If something goes wrong, roll back:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n shop rollout undo deployment/api
   ```

Expected output of `rollout status`:

```text
Waiting for deployment "api" rollout to finish: 1 out of 2 new replicas have been updated...
Waiting for deployment "api" rollout to finish: 1 old replicas are pending termination...
deployment "api" successfully rolled out
```

## Cleanup

Delete the whole cluster:

```bash
kind delete cluster --name shop
```

## Next steps

+ Add metrics with the [kube-prometheus-stack Helm chart](https://github.com/prometheus-community/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/kube-prometheus-stack#configuration).
+ Read about [rolling update parameters](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/#rolling-update-deployment) (`maxSurge`, `maxUnavailable`).
+ Try the same deployment on a managed cluster: see our guide at https://docs.acme.example.com/tutorials/sample-shop/managed-kubernetes?provider=all&step=1
+ Found a mistake in this tutorial? [Open an issue](https://github.com/acme/sample-shop/issues/new?labels=docs%2Ctutorial&template=docs_bug.md).

---
# site.yml -- top-level playbook for the acme web platform
#
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/production site.yml --diff
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging site.yml --tags web --limit web-02
#
# Plays run in this order: all hosts -> db -> web -> monitoring (imported at the very bottom).
# Don't reorder without talking to #infra first; the db play assumes the base packages exist.

- name: Prepare all hosts
  hosts: all
  become: yes
  gather_facts: true
  vars:
    ntp_servers:
      - 0.de.pool.ntp.org
      - 1.de.pool.ntp.org
    admin_group: "{{ 'wheel' if ansible_os_family == 'RedHat' else 'sudo' }}"
    deploy_user:    deploy
    deploy_home: "/home/{{ deploy_user }}"
    swap_size_mb: 2048
    unattended_upgrades_enabled: yes§§1
  pre_tasks:
    - name: Update apt cache
      apt: update_cache=yes cache_valid_time=3600
      when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"
      changed_when: false

    - name: Make sure python3-apt is present (the apt module needs it on minimal images)
      ansible.builtin.raw: test -e /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/apt || (apt-get -y update && apt-get install -y python3-apt)
      when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"
      changed_when: false
  roles:
    - role: common
      tags: [common, base]
    - role: users
      vars:
        users_admins: "{{ vault_admin_users | default([]) }}"
      tags:
      - users
    - { role: nginx, when: "'web' in group_names", tags: ['web'] }
    - role: geerlingguy.ntp
      ntp_manage_config: true
      ntp_timezone: Etc/UTC
    # - role: fail2ban       # disabled, fights with crowdsec -- see INFRA-512


- name: Database servers
  hosts: db
  become: true
  serial: 1
  max_fail_percentage: 0
  gather_facts: no
  vars_files:
    - vars/postgres.yml
    - "vars/{{ env | default('staging') }}/secrets.yml"
  environment:
    PGPASSWORD: "{{ vault_postgres_admin_password }}"
    LC_ALL: C.UTF-8
  tasks:
    - name: Gather minimal facts (gather_facts is off for speed)
      ansible.builtin.setup:
        gather_subset: [ '!all', '!min', distribution,memory ]

    - name: Upgrade PostgreSQL minor version
      block:
        - name: Stop pgbouncer so clients fail fast instead of hanging
          ansible.builtin.service:
            name: pgbouncer
            state: stopped

        - name: Install postgresql packages
          ansible.builtin.apt:
            name:
              - "postgresql-{{ pg_version }}"
              - "postgresql-contrib-{{ pg_version }}"
              - python3-psycopg2
            state: latest
            update_cache: yes
          register: pg_pkgs
          notify: restart postgresql

        - name: Check replication lag before continuing
          ansible.builtin.command: >
            psql -U postgres -tAc
            "SELECT COALESCE(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp()), 0)::int"
          register: repl_lag
          changed_when: false
          failed_when:
            - repl_lag.rc != 0
            - repl_lag.stdout | int > 30
          when:
            - inventory_hostname in groups['db_replicas']
            - not (skip_lag_check | default(false) | bool)
      rescue:
        - name: Tell the humans
          community.general.slack:
            token: "{{ vault_slack_token }}"
            channel: "#ops-alerts"
            msg: "DB upgrade failed on {{ inventory_hostname }}: {{ ansible_failed_result.msg | default('unknown error') }}"
          delegate_to: localhost
          become: false

        - name: Abort the play
          ansible.builtin.fail:
            msg: Aborting, see slack for details. Nothing has been restarted on the remaining hosts.
      always:
        - name: Start pgbouncer again
          ansible.builtin.service: { name: pgbouncer, state: started }

    - name: Run pending migrations (once)
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        set -euo pipefail
        cd /opt/acme/current
        ./bin/migrate --check || ./bin/migrate up --lock-timeout 30s
      args:
        executable: /bin/bash
      run_once: true
      delegate_to: "{{ groups['db_primary'][0] }}"
      register: migrate_out
      changed_when: "'no pending migrations' not in migrate_out.stdout"

  handlers:
    - name: restart postgresql
      ansible.builtin.service:
        name: "postgresql@{{ pg_version }}-main"
        state: restarted



- name: Web servers
  hosts: web
  become: TRUE
  serial: "30%"
  tasks:
  - name: Take host out of the load balancer
    ansible.builtin.uri:
      url: "https://lb-api.acme.example.com/v1/pools/web/members/{{ inventory_hostname }}"
      method: PATCH
      body_format: json
      body: { state: draining }
      headers:
        Authorization: "Bearer {{ vault_lb_api_token }}"
      status_code: [200, 204]
    delegate_to: localhost
    become: no

  - name: Deploy application release
    ansible.builtin.unarchive:
      src: "https://artifacts.acme.example.com/acme-web/acme-web-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz"
      dest: /opt/acme/releases/
      remote_src: yes
      owner: "{{ deploy_user | default('deploy') }}"
      mode: 0755
    notify:
      - reload php-fpm
      - reload nginx

  - name: Warm up caches on every web node
    ansible.builtin.uri:
      url: "http://{{ item }}:8080/internal/warmup"
      timeout: 120
    loop: "{{ groups['web'] }}"
    run_once: true
    delegate_to: localhost
    # TODO(mk): this hammers all nodes at once, add throttle once we're on ansible-core 2.15

  - name: Put host back into the load balancer
    ansible.builtin.uri:
      url: "https://lb-api.acme.example.com/v1/pools/web/members/{{ inventory_hostname }}"
      method: PATCH
      body_format: json
      body: '{"state": "active"}'
      headers: { Authorization: "Bearer {{ vault_lb_api_token }}" }
    delegate_to: localhost
    become: no

  handlers:
  - name: reload nginx
    ansible.builtin.service: name=nginx state=reloaded
  - name: reload php-fpm
    ansible.builtin.service:
      name: php8.2-fpm
      state: reloaded


- import_playbook: monitoring.yml

---
title: Contributing to the docs
description: How to write, preview and submit changes to the Acme Platform documentation.
---

# Contributing to the documentation

The docs at **docs.acme.dev** are built with [MkDocs](https://www.mkdocs.org/) and the
[Material for MkDocs](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/) theme. Every page
is a Markdown file under `docs/`, and every change goes through a pull request,
just like code. Typos and one-line fixes can be made straight from GitHub — click
the :material-pencil: icon at the top of any page.

!!! tip "Preview locally"

    You don't need to install anything globally. From the repository root, run:

    ```bash
    python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
    pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
    mkdocs serve --dirtyreload
    ```

    Then open <http://127.0.0.1:8000>. Pages reload on save; if the navigation
    doesn't pick up a new page, stop the server with ++ctrl+c++ and start it again.

## Where things live

```text
docs/
├── index.md
├── getting-started/
│   ├── install.md
│   └── first-project.md
├── guides/              # task-oriented how-tos
├── reference/           # partly generated, see below
├── includes/
│   ├── abbreviations.md
│   └── supported-platforms.md
└── assets/images/
mkdocs.yml               # nav, theme, plugins
.vale.ini                # prose linting
```

Files under `docs/reference/cli/` are **generated** by `make docs-cli` from the `--help`
output; edit the Go source in `cmd/acme/` instead, or your change will be overwritten.

## Voice and tone ##

We write for busy engineers who arrived from a search engine and want to get
something done. Lead with the task, not the background. Use the second person
("you"), the active voice and the present tense. Prefer short sentences: if a
sentence needs two commas and a semicolon, it probably wants to be two sentences.
Avoid words that judge difficulty — *simply*, *just*, *easy*, _obviously_ —
because what's easy for you is the thing someone else has been stuck on for an hour.

Be precise about UI labels and use the exact capitalisation shown on screen, in
**bold**: "Select **Project settings** › **Webhooks**". Code, file names, CLI flags
and anything a reader might copy go in `inline code`. We use American spelling
in prose (color, behavior) but keep identifiers exactly as they are in the product,
e.g. the `colour_scheme` setting from the 2019 API, which we can't rename.

Don't promise the future. "Coming soon" ages badly; link to the public roadmap issue instead.


## Do and don't

| Do | Don't |
|:---|:------|
| Start procedures with a verb: "Create a token", "Run `acme login`". | Start with "In order to be able to create a token, you will first need to make sure that…" |
| Use realistic but obviously fake values: `ACME_TOKEN=acme_pat_EXAMPLE1234`, `project_id: demo-123`. | Paste anything that looks like a real secret, even an expired one — the secret scanner will (rightly) block your PR. |
| Link to the reference for every flag you mention, e.g. [`--dry-run`](../reference/cli/acme_deploy.md#dry-run). | Use "see below" or "click here" as link text. |
| Show a command and a trimmed sample of its output in separate blocks. | Mix `$` prompts and output in one block without the `console` info string. |
| Reserve `!!! warning` and `!!! danger` for data loss and security issues. | Wrap every second paragraph in an admonition; readers learn to skip them. |
| Write `a \| b` when you need a literal pipe inside a table cell. | Type a bare pipe in a cell and wonder why the table suddenly has an extra column. |

## Admonitions, tabs and other extensions

We enable `admonition`, `pymdownx.details`, `pymdownx.superfences`,
`pymdownx.tabbed`, `attr_list`, `md_in_html`, `abbr`, `pymdownx.keys` and
`pymdownx.snippets`. This is the syntax you will need most often:

````markdown
!!! note "Optional custom title"

    The body is indented by **four** spaces. It can contain lists,
    tables and code blocks:

    ```yaml
    retries: 3
    ```

??? info "Collapsed by default"

    Use `???+` instead to make it collapsible but expanded on page load.

=== "macOS"

    ```bash
    brew install acme
    ```

=== "Linux"

    ```bash
    curl -fsSL https://get.acme.dev | sh
    ```
````

!!! warning

    The body **must** be indented by four spaces. With two spaces the text is
    silently rendered *outside* the box — the most common review comment we leave.

<!--
  TODO(docs-team): document the `blog` plugin once we decide whether release notes move there.
  Tracking: https://github.com/acme/platform/issues/4410
-->

## Images and diagrams

* Put screenshots in `docs/assets/images/<section>/` and name them after what they show (`webhook-settings-dialog.png`, not `Screenshot 2024-05-02 at 14.31.07.png`).
* Crop to the relevant part of the UI, use the light theme and a window width of 1280 px.
* Always write alt text, and set a width for anything wider than the text column:

  ![The webhook settings dialog with the secret field highlighted](../assets/images/webhooks/settings-dialog.png){ width="300" loading=lazy }

* Use Mermaid in a fenced block (```` ```mermaid ````) instead of exported PNGs, so
  diagrams stay editable.
    + Keep them under ~15 nodes.
    + If a diagram needs a legend, it is probably two diagrams.

## Submitting a change

1. Create a branch named `docs/<short-topic>`.
1. Make your edits, then run the linters:
    1. Prose: `vale docs/` (our rules live in `.github/vale/styles/Acme/`).
    2. Markdown: `markdownlint-cli2 "docs/**/*.md"`.
    3. Links: `lychee --offline docs/` — internal links only; external ones are checked nightly.
1. Preview with `mkdocs serve` (see the tip at the top of this page).
1. Open a pull request. The *docs-preview* workflow comments with a link like
   `https://pr-1234.docs-preview.acme.dev` after about three minutes.
1. Someone from @acme/docs reviews it within two working days.

Vale output looks like this:

    docs/guides/webhooks.md
     14:21  warning  Avoid 'simply'.                      Acme.Simplicity
     27:1   error    Use 'sign in' instead of 'login'     Acme.Terms
                     when it's a verb.

    ✖ 1 error, 1 warning and 0 suggestions in 1 file.

You can silence a rule for a paragraph with `<!-- vale Acme.Terms = NO -->` …
`<!-- vale Acme.Terms = YES -->`, but please explain why in the PR description.

## Keys, abbreviations and snippets

Write keyboard shortcuts with the `pymdownx.keys` syntax — ++ctrl+shift+p++ renders as
proper key caps and is read correctly by screen readers. Don't use raw `<kbd>` tags.

Abbreviations are defined once in `docs/includes/abbreviations.md` and appended to every page
automatically, so hovering over "HTML" or "SSO" shows a tooltip. To add one, edit that file:

```markdown
*[HTML]: Hyper Text Markup Language
*[SSO]: Single Sign-On
*[RBAC]: Role-Based Access Control
```

To reuse a block of text (for example the list of supported platforms) on several pages,
include it as a snippet instead of copy-pasting it:

```markdown
--8<-- "includes/supported-platforms.md"
```

***

Questions? Ask in `#docs` on Slack or open a [discussion](https://github.com/acme/platform/discussions/categories/docs?discussions_q=is%3Aopen+category%3ADocs+sort%3Atop).

--8<-- "includes/abbreviations.md"

*[HTML]: Hyper Text Markup Language
*[PR]: Pull Request
*[CI]: Continuous Integration

---
title: "Lab notebook — March 2024"
author: "Kenji Nakamura"
date: "Last knitted `r format(Sys.time(), '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')`"
output:
  github_document:
    html_preview: false
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 2
editor_options:
  markdown:
    wrap: sentence
    canonical: true
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.path = "figs/2024-03/", dpi = 200)
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
gel  <- read_excel("data/2024-03-11_gel_densitometry.xlsx", sheet = "lanes")
brad <- read_csv("data/2024-03-13_bradford.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

Project: expression and purification of His~6~-tagged **PfkB-like kinase (construct pKN-17)** for the thermal-shift and crystallisation trials.\
Supervisor: Prof. Albrecht. Day-to-day questions: Dr. Nguyen.
Bench: room 2.14, shelf C. Freezer box "KN-2024-A".

<!-- Reminder to self: canonical: true means RStudio's visual editor rewrites this file on save. Don't panic about the diffs. -->

## 2024-03-04 (Mon)

Transformed pKN-17 into *E. coli* BL21(DE3) (NEB cat. No. C2527, lot 10183). Heat shock 30 s at 42 °C, recovery 1 h in SOC, plated on LB + kanamycin (50 µg/mL).
Also plated the empty-vector control and a no-DNA control.

Plan for the week, roughly:
1. Mon: transformation
2. Tue: overnight culture, then 1 L expression culture
3. Thu: lysis + Ni-NTA
4. Fri/Mon: SDS-PAGE, Bradford, decide whether to scale up

Ordered fresh imidazole (Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, U.S.) because the old bottle is yellowish. Dr. Nguyen says it's fine for washing buffers but not for elution... I'm not convinced either way, so new bottle it is.
Also made 500 mL of 0.5 M EDTA stock, pH 8.0 (took forever to dissolve, as usual).

## 2024-03-05 (Tue)

Colonies! ca. 200 on the pKN-17 plate, none on the no-DNA control.
Picked 3 colonies into 5 mL LB + Kan, 37 °C, 220 rpm, in the morning. At 5 p.m. inoculated 1 L 2×YT (+ Kan) with 10 mL of the culture from colony No. 4, which had grown fastest.
OD~600~ readings:

| Time  | OD600 | Note |
|------:|:-----:|:-----|
| 17:00 | 0.08 | |
| 19:30 | 0.41 | |
| 20:15 | 0.68 | induced with 0.5 mM IPTG, moved to 18 °C |
| next day 09:00 | 3.9 | harvested, 4,000 × g, 20 min, 4 °C |

Induction at 18 °C overnight vs. 37 °C for 3 h: going with the cold induction because Kim et al. (2019) report that the protein is mostly insoluble at 37 °C. Their Fig. 2B is pretty convincing, although they used a different tag (GST) and a different strain.
Pellet stored at −80 °C.

## 2024-03-07 (Thu)

Lysis and Ni-NTA purification.
Pellet (approx. 6.2 g wet weight) resuspended in 40 mL lysis buffer, sonicated 6 × 30 s on ice, spun 30 min at 20,000 × g. Supernatant clear-ish; pellet large.

|:--|:--|:-:|--:|
| Lysis | 50 mM Tris, 300 mM NaCl, 10 mM imidazole, 1 mM `TCEP`, protease inhibitor (1 tablet / 50 mL) | 8.0 | 50 mL |

|Elution| as lysis but 250 mM imidazole | 8.0 | 15 mL |
| Dialysis | 25 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 0.5 mM `TCEP`, 5 % glycerol | 7.5 | 2 × 2 L |

1. Bound supernatant to 2 mL Ni-NTA resin for 1 h at 4 °C on a rotator.
2. Washed with 3 × 10 CV wash buffer.
   The flow-through from the second wash was still slightly yellow. Is that the resin or the protein? Kept a sample.
3. Eluted in 5 × 1 mL fractions. Fractions E2--E4 were visibly cloudy at first, then cleared up after ca. 20 min on ice!

  group_by(lane_label) |>
  summarise(mean_int = mean(intensity), sd_int = sd(intensity), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(lane_label = fct_inorder(lane_label)) |>
  ggplot(aes(lane_label, mean_int)) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey60") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_int - sd_int, ymax = mean_int + sd_int), width = 0.3) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Integrated intensity (a.u.)")

>

# Azure Pipelines — acme-toolkit (Python library)
# Schema: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/devops/pipelines/yaml-schema/
#
# NOTE: variables from the "acme-secrets" group are linked to Key Vault kv-acme-ci.
#       If a run fails with "variable not found", someone rotated a secret and forgot to re-link it.

name: $(Date:yyyyMMdd)$(Rev:.r)

trigger:
  batch: true
  branches:
    include: [ main, release/* ]
  tags:
    include:
    - v*
  paths:
    exclude:
      - docs/**
      - '*.md'
      - .github/*

pr:
  autoCancel: true
  drafts: false
  branches:
    include:
      - main
      - "release/*"

schedules:
- cron: "0 0 * * Sun"
  displayName: Weekly build (dependency drift check)
  branches:
    include: [main]
  always: true

resources:
  repositories:
    - repository: templates
      type: github
      name: acme/pipeline-templates
      endpoint: acme-github
      ref: refs/tags/v2.1.0

parameters:
  - name: runIntegration
    displayName: 'Run integration tests (needs the staging DB, ~25 min)'
    type: boolean
    default: false
  - name: pythonVersions
    type: object
    default: ['3.10', '3.11', '3.12']
  - name: publish
    displayName: Publish to PyPI
    type: boolean
    default: FALSE
  -   name: deployEnvironment
      displayName: Deploy docs to
      type: string
      default: staging
      values:
      - staging
      - production

variables:
  - group: acme-secrets
  - name: PIP_CACHE_DIR
    value: $(Pipeline.Workspace)/.pip
  - name: isMain
    value: ${{ eq(variables['Build.SourceBranch'], 'refs/heads/main') }}
  - name: isTag
    value: ${{ startsWith(variables['Build.SourceBranch'], 'refs/tags/v') }}
  -  name: PYTHONUNBUFFERED
     value: 1
  - name: system.debug
    value: false


stages:
- stage: Test
  displayName: Lint & test
  jobs:
  - job: Lint
    pool:
      vmImage: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - task: UsePythonVersion@0
      inputs: { versionSpec: '3.12' }
    - script: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        pip install ruff==0.4.4 mypy==1.10.0
        ruff check . --output-format=azure
        ruff format --check .
        mypy src/acme_toolkit
      displayName: Ruff + mypy

  - job: Test
    dependsOn: Lint
    strategy:
      matrix:
        Linux_Py310:
          imageName: 'ubuntu-latest'
          python.version: '3.10'
        Windows_Py311:
          imageName: windows-latest
          python.version: 3.11
        mac_Py312:
          imageName: macOS-latest
          python.version: "3.12"
        # Linux_Py313:
        #   imageName: ubuntu-latest
        #   python.version: '3.13'     # enable once numpy wheels exist
      maxParallel: 3
    pool:
      vmImage: $(imageName)
    timeoutInMinutes: 45
    steps:
      - task: UsePythonVersion@0
        inputs:
          versionSpec: '$(python.version)'
          addToPath: true
        displayName: 'Use Python $(python.version)'

      - task: Cache@2
        inputs:
          key: 'pip | "$(Agent.OS)" | requirements*.txt'
          restoreKeys: |
            pip | "$(Agent.OS)"
            pip
          path: $(PIP_CACHE_DIR)
        displayName: Cache pip

      - script: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip wheel
          pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
          pip install -e .
        displayName: Install

      - script: pytest -n auto --junitxml=junit/test-results.xml --cov=acme_toolkit --cov-report=xml --cov-report=html -m "not integration"
        displayName: pytest

      - task: PublishTestResults@2
        condition: succeededOrFailed()
        inputs:
          testResultsFiles: '**/test-*.xml'
          testRunTitle: 'Python $(python.version) on $(imageName)'

      - task: PublishCodeCoverageResults@2
        condition: and(succeeded(), eq(variables['Agent.OS'], 'Linux'))
        inputs:
          summaryFileLocation: $(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)/coverage.xml
          pathToSources:
          failIfCoverageEmpty: yes

  - ${{ if eq(parameters.runIntegration, true) }}:
    - job: Integration
      dependsOn: Test
      pool:
        vmImage: ubuntu-latest
      variables:
        - group: acme-staging-db
      steps:
        - script: pytest -m integration --junitxml=junit/integration.xml
          displayName: Integration tests
          env:
            DATABASE_URL: $(stagingDatabaseUrl)
            ACME_API_TOKEN: $(acmeApiToken)

  - ${{ each version in parameters.pythonVersions }}:
    - job: compat_${{ replace(version, '.', '_') }}
      displayName: Compat check (Python ${{ version }})
      dependsOn: []
      pool: { vmImage: ubuntu-latest }
      steps:
      - task: UsePythonVersion@0
        inputs:
          versionSpec: ${{ version }}
      - bash: python -c "import acme_toolkit, sys; print(acme_toolkit.__version__, sys.version)"
        displayName: Import smoke test



- stage: Deploy
  dependsOn: Test
  condition: and(succeeded(), or(eq(variables.isMain, true), eq(variables.isTag, true)))
  jobs:
    - deployment: DeployDocs
      displayName: Publish docs + package
      environment: acme-${{ parameters.deployEnvironment }}
      pool:
         vmImage: ubuntu-latest
      strategy:
         runOnce:
            deploy:
               steps:
                  - checkout: self
                    fetchDepth: 0
                  - template: steps/deploy.yml@templates
                    parameters:
                      appName: acme-toolkit-docs
                      slot: staging
                      buildCommand: "mkdocs build --strict"
                  - bash: |
                      set -euo pipefail
                      python -m pip install build twine
                      python -m build
                      twine check dist/*
                    displayName: Build sdist + wheel
                  - ${{ if eq(parameters.publish, true) }}:
                    - bash: twine upload --non-interactive --skip-existing dist/*
                      displayName: Upload to PyPI
                      env:
                        TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
                        TWINE_PASSWORD: $(pypiApiToken)
                  - powershell: |
                      Write-Host "Deployed $(Build.BuildNumber) to ${{ parameters.deployEnvironment }}"
                      if ($env:SYSTEM_DEBUG -eq "true") { Get-ChildItem Env: | Sort-Object Name }
                    displayName: Summary
                    condition: always()

          testRunTitle: 'Python $(python.version) on $(imageName)'

      - task: PublishCodeCoverageResults@2
        condition: and(succeeded(), eq(variables['Agent.OS'], 'Linux'))
        inputs:
          summaryFileLocation: $(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)/coverage.xml
          pathToSources:
          failIfCoverageEmpty: yes

  - ${{ if eq(parameters.runIntegration, true) }}:
    - job: Integration
      dependsOn: Test
      pool:
        vmImage: ubuntu-latest
      variables:
        - group: acme-staging-db
      steps:
        - script: pytest -m integration --junitxml=junit/integration.xml
          displayName: Integration tests
          env:
            DATABASE_URL: $(stagingDatabaseUrl)
            ACME_API_TOKEN: $(acmeApiToken)

  - ${{ each version in parameters.pythonVersions }}:
    - job: compat_${{ replace(version, '.', '_') }}
      displayName: Compat check (Python ${{ version }})
      dependsOn: []
      pool: { vmImage: ubuntu-latest }
      steps:
      - task: UsePythonVersion@0
        inputs:
          versionSpec: ${{ version }}
      - bash: python -c "import acme_toolkit, sys; print(acme_toolkit.__version__, sys.version)"
        displayName: Import smoke test



- stage: Deploy
  dependsOn: Test
  condition: and(succeeded(), or(eq(variables.isMain, true), eq(variables.isTag, true)))
  jobs:
    - deployment: DeployDocs
      displayName: Publish docs + package
      environment: acme-${{ parameters.deployEnvironment }}
      pool:
         vmImage: ubuntu-latest
      strategy:
         runOnce:
            deploy:
               steps:
                  - checkout: self
                    fetchDepth: 0
                  - template: steps/deploy.yml@templates
                    parameters:
                      appName: acme-toolkit-docs
                      slot: staging
                      buildCommand: "mkdocs build --strict"
                  - bash: |
                      set -euo pipefail
                      python -m pip install build twine
                      python -m build
                      twine check dist/*
                    displayName: Build sdist + wheel
                  - ${{ if eq(parameters.publish, true) }}:
                    - bash: twine upload --non-interactive --skip-existing dist/*
                      displayName: Upload to PyPI
                      env:
                        TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
                        TWINE_PASSWORD: $(pypiApiToken)
                  - powershell: |
                      Write-Host "Deployed $(Build.BuildNumber) to ${{ parameters.deployEnvironment }}"

                    condition: always()

arguments.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://goreleaser.com/static/schema.json
# vim: set ts=2 sw=2 tw=0 fo=cnqoj
#
# acmectl release configuration.
#   local dry run:  goreleaser release --snapshot --clean
#   CI:             goreleaser release --clean   (on tag push, see .github/workflows/release.yml)
# Needs GITHUB_TOKEN, HOMEBREW_TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN and cosign (keyless) in CI.

version: 2

project_name: acmectl

before:
  hooks:
    - go mod tidy
    - go generate ./...
    - ./scripts/completions.sh
    - ./scripts/manpages.sh

builds:
  - id: acmectl
    main: ./cmd/acmectl
    binary: acmectl
    env: [CGO_ENABLED=0]
    goos: [linux, darwin, windows, freebsd]
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
      - "386"
      - arm
    goarm: ["6", "7"]
    ignore:
      - goos: windows
        goarch: arm
      - goos: darwin
        goarch: "386"
      - { goos: freebsd, goarch: arm64 }
    ldflags:
      - -s -w -X main.version={{.Version}} -X main.commit={{.Commit}} -X main.date={{.Date}} -X main.builtBy=goreleaser
    flags: [-trimpath]
    mod_timestamp: "{{ .CommitTimestamp }}"


  # the agent needs cgo for the sqlite driver -> linux only, built with the zig cross toolchain
  -   id: acme-agent
      main: ./cmd/acme-agent
      binary: acme-agent
      env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=1
      - CC=zig cc -target x86_64-linux-musl
      goos: [ linux ]
      goarch: [ amd64 ]
      tags: [ sqlite_omit_load_extension,netgo ]
      ldflags:
        - -s -w -linkmode external -extldflags "-static"
        - -X github.com/acme/acmectl/internal/version.Version={{.Version}}
      skip: false

archives:
  - id: default
    format: tar.gz
    # this name template makes the OS and Arch compatible with the results of `uname`.
    name_template: >-
      {{ .ProjectName }}_
      {{- title .Os }}_
      {{- if eq .Arch "amd64" }}x86_64
      {{- else if eq .Arch "386" }}i386
      {{- else }}{{ .Arch }}{{ end }}
      {{- if .Arm }}v{{ .Arm }}{{ end }}
    format_overrides:
    - goos: windows
      format: zip
    files:
      - LICENSE*
      - README.md
      - CHANGELOG.md
      - completions/*
      - manpages/*
    builds_info:
       group: root
       owner: root
       mode: 0755

checksum:
  name_template: 'checksums.txt'
  algorithm: sha256

snapshot:
  version_template: "{{ incpatch .Version }}-next"

changelog:
  sort: asc
  use: github
  abbrev: -1
  filters:
    exclude:
      - '^docs:'
      - '^test:'
      - "^chore\\(deps\\):"
      - '^ci:'
      - Merge pull request
      - Merge branch
  groups:
    - title: Features
      regexp: '^.*?feat(\([[:word:]]+\))??!?:.+$'
      order: 0
    - title: "Bug fixes"
      regexp: '^.*?fix(\([[:word:]]+\))??!?:.+$'
      order: 1
    - title: 'Security'
      regexp: '^.*?sec(\([[:word:]]+\))??!?:.+$'
      order: 2
    - title: Others
      order: 999

nfpms:
  -
    id: packages
    package_name: acmectl
    file_name_template: "{{ .ConventionalFileName }}"
    vendor: Acme Inc.
    homepage: https://acme.example.com/acmectl
    maintainer: Acme Maintainers <maintainers@acme.example.com>
    description: |-
      acmectl is the command line interface for the Acme platform.
      It manages projects, deployments and secrets from your terminal.
    license: Apache-2.0
    formats: [deb, rpm, apk]
    bindir: /usr/bin
    section: utils
    priority: optional
    contents:
      - src: ./completions/acmectl.bash
        dst: /usr/share/bash-completion/completions/acmectl

      - src: ./completions/acmectl.zsh

        file_info:

    description: "Command line interface for the Acme platform"
    license: "Apache-2.0"
    commit_author:
      name: acme-releasebot
      email: releasebot@acme.example.com
    skip_upload:
    install: |
      bin.install "acmectl"
      bash_completion.install "completions/acmectl.bash" => "acmectl"
      zsh_completion.install "completions/acmectl.zsh" => "_acmectl"
      fish_completion.install "completions/acmectl.fish"
      man1.install "manpages/acmectl.1.gz"
    test: |
      system "#{bin}/acmectl version"

dockers:
  - image_templates:
    - "ghcr.io/acme/acmectl:{{ .Version }}-amd64"
    - "ghcr.io/acme/acmectl:latest-amd64"
    use: buildx
    dockerfile: Dockerfile.goreleaser
    goarch: amd64
    build_flag_templates:
      - "--pull"
      - "--platform=linux/amd64"
      - "--label=org.opencontainers.image.created={{.Date}}"
      - "--label=org.opencontainers.image.title={{.ProjectName}}"
      - "--label=org.opencontainers.image.revision={{.FullCommit}}"
      - "--label=org.opencontainers.image.version={{.Version}}"
      - "--label=org.opencontainers.image.source=https://github.com/acme/acmectl"
  - image_templates: ["ghcr.io/acme/acmectl:{{ .Version }}-arm64v8", "ghcr.io/acme/acmectl:latest-arm64v8"]
    use: buildx
    dockerfile: Dockerfile.goreleaser
    goarch: arm64
    build_flag_templates:
      - --pull
      - --platform=linux/arm64/v8
      - --label=org.opencontainers.image.created={{.Date}}
      - --label=org.opencontainers.image.version={{.Version}}

docker_manifests:
  - name_template: "ghcr.io/acme/acmectl:{{ .Version }}"
    image_templates:
      - "ghcr.io/acme/acmectl:{{ .Version }}-amd64"
      - "ghcr.io/acme/acmectl:{{ .Version }}-arm64v8"

signs:
  - cmd: cosign
    certificate: "${artifact}.pem"
    signature: "${artifact}.sig"
    args: ["sign-blob",
           "--output-certificate=${certificate}",
           "--output-signature=${signature}",
           "${artifact}",
           "--yes"]
    artifacts: checksum
    output: true

release:
  github:
    owner: acme
    name: acmectl
  draft: no
  replace_existing_draft: true
  prerelease: auto
  mode: append
  name_template: "v{{.Version}}"
  header: |
    ## acmectl {{ .Tag }} ({{ .Date }})

    Install with Homebrew: `brew install acme/tap/acmectl`, or grab a binary below.
  footer: |+
    ---
    **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/acme/acmectl/compare/{{ .PreviousTag }}...{{ .Tag }}

    _Released by goreleaser — questions go to #acmectl on Slack._


announce:
  skip: "{{gt .Patch 0}}"
  slack:
    enabled: true
    message_template: "acmectl {{ .Tag }} is out! Changelog: {{ .ReleaseURL }}"
    channel: "#releases"
    username: ''
    icon_emoji: ':rocket:'

arguments.content:
# Build, scan and deploy the `storefront` image.
#
#   push to main       -> build + scan + deploy staging
#   push tag v*        -> build + scan + deploy staging + (manual approval) production
#   workflow_dispatch  -> deploy an existing image tag to the chosen environment
#
# Required secrets: NPM_TOKEN, SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL
# AWS access is via OIDC (roles live in acme/infra, terraform/iam/github.tf)
name: docker-deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
    tags:
      - 'v*.*.*'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: Target environment
        type: choice
        required: true
        default: staging
        options: [staging, production]
      image-tag:
        description: 'Existing image tag to deploy (leave empty to build from the selected ref)'
        type: string
        required: false
  schedule:
    - cron: '30 2 * * *'  # nightly rebuild (picks up base image security fixes)

env:
    REGISTRY: ghcr.io
    IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
    HELM_RELEASE:     storefront
    HELM_CHART_VERSION: 2.7.1
    KUBECTL_VERSION: "v1.29.4"

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write
  security-events: write   # SARIF upload
  id-token: write          # OIDC -> AWS


jobs:
    build:
        name: Build & push
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || inputs.image-tag == ''
        outputs:
            version: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}
            digest:  ${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }}
            image:   ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        steps:
          - name: Checkout
            uses: actions/checkout@v4

          - name: Set up QEMU
            uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3
            with:
              platforms: arm64

          - name: Set up Buildx
            uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

          - name: Log in to GHCR
            uses: docker/login-action@v3
            with:
              registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
              username: ${{ github.actor }}
              password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

          - name: Docker metadata
            id: meta
            uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
            with:
              images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
              tags: |
                type=ref,event=branch
                type=semver,pattern={{version}}
                type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}}
                type=sha,prefix=sha-,format=short
                type=schedule,pattern=nightly-{{date 'YYYYMMDD'}}
                type=raw,value=latest,enable={{is_default_branch}}
              labels: |
                org.opencontainers.image.title=storefront
                org.opencontainers.image.vendor=Acme Inc.
                org.opencontainers.image.description=Acme storefront (Next.js frontend + BFF)

          - name: Build and push
            id: push
            uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
            with:
              context: .
              file: ./docker/Dockerfile
              platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
              push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
              tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
              labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
              cache-from: type=gha
              cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
              build-args: |
                NODE_VERSION=20.12.2
                NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api.acme.example.com
                GIT_SHA=${{ github.sha }}
              secrets: |
                "npm_token=${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}"
                "sentry_auth_token=${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}"
              provenance: false
              sbom: true



    scan:
        name: Trivy scan
        needs: build
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
            -   name: Run Trivy
                uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@0.20.0
                with:
                    image-ref: ${{ needs.build.outputs.image }}@${{ needs.build.outputs.digest }}
                    format: sarif
                    output: trivy-results.sarif
                    severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
                    exit-code: '1'
                    ignore-unfixed: true
                    vuln-type: "os,library"
                    timeout: 10m0s
            -   name: Upload SARIF
                if: always()
                uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
                with:
                    sarif_file: trivy-results.sarif
                    category: trivy

    deploy-staging:
        name: Deploy → staging
        needs: [build, scan]
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        environment: { name: staging, url: "${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}" }
        concurrency: deploy-staging
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
            with:
              role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gha-deploy-staging
              aws-region: eu-central-1
          - uses: azure/setup-kubectl@v4
            with: { version: "${{ env.KUBECTL_VERSION }}" }
          - uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
          - id: deploy
            name: helm upgrade
            run: |-
              aws eks update-kubeconfig --name acme-staging --region eu-central-1
              helm upgrade --install "$HELM_RELEASE" oci://ghcr.io/acme/charts/storefront \
                --version "$HELM_CHART_VERSION" \
                --namespace storefront --create-namespace \
                --values deploy/values-staging.yaml \
                --set image.tag=${{ needs.build.outputs.version }} \
                --set image.digest=${{ needs.build.outputs.digest }} \
                --wait --timeout 10m --atomic
              echo "url=https://staging.acme.example.com" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    deploy-production:
        name: Deploy → production
        needs: [build, scan, deploy-staging]
        if: >-
            startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') ||
            (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.environment == 'production')
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        environment:

# Build, scan and deploy the `storefront` image.
#
#   push to main       -> build + scan + deploy staging
#   push tag v*        -> build + scan + deploy staging + (manual approval) production
#   workflow_dispatch  -> deploy an existing image tag to the chosen environment
#
# Required secrets: NPM_TOKEN, SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL
# AWS access is via OIDC (roles live in acme/infra, terraform/iam/github.tf)
name: docker-deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
    tags:
      - 'v*.*.*'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: Target environment
        type: choice
        required: true
        default: staging
        options: [staging, production]
      image-tag:
        description: 'Existing image tag to deploy (leave empty to build from the selected ref)'
        type: string
        required: false
  schedule:
    - cron: '30 2 * * *'  # nightly rebuild (picks up base image security fixes)

env:
    REGISTRY: ghcr.io
    IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
    HELM_RELEASE:     storefront
    HELM_CHART_VERSION: 2.7.1
    KUBECTL_VERSION: "v1.29.4"

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write
  security-events: write   # SARIF upload
  id-token: write          # OIDC -> AWS


jobs:
    build:
        name: Build & push
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || inputs.image-tag == ''
        outputs:
            version: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}
            digest:  ${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }}
            image:   ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        steps:
          - name: Checkout
            uses: actions/checkout@v4

          - name: Set up QEMU
            uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3
            with:
              platforms: arm64

          - name: Set up Buildx
            uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

          - name: Log in to GHCR
            uses: docker/login-action@v3
            with:
              registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
              username: ${{ github.actor }}
              password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

          - name: Docker metadata
            id: meta
            uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
            with:
              images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
              tags: |
                type=ref,event=branch
                type=semver,pattern={{version}}
                type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}}
                type=sha,prefix=sha-,format=short
                type=schedule,pattern=nightly-{{date 'YYYYMMDD'}}
                type=raw,value=latest,enable={{is_default_branch}}
              labels: |
                org.opencontainers.image.title=storefront
                org.opencontainers.image.vendor=Acme Inc.
                org.opencontainers.image.description=Acme storefront (Next.js frontend + BFF)

          - name: Build and push
            id: push
            uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
            with:
              context: .
              file: ./docker/Dockerfile
              platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
              push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
              tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
              labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
              cache-from: type=gha
              cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
              build-args: |
                NODE_VERSION=20.12.2
                NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api.acme.example.com
                GIT_SHA=${{ github.sha }}
              secrets: |
                "npm_token=${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}"
                "sentry_auth_token=${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}"
              provenance: false
              sbom: true



    scan:
        name: Trivy scan
        needs: build
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
            -   name: Run Trivy
                uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@0.20.0
                with:
                    image-ref: ${{ needs.build.outputs.image }}@${{ needs.build.outputs.digest }}
                    format: sarif
                    output: trivy-results.sarif
                    severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
                    exit-code: '1'
                    ignore-unfixed: true
                    vuln-type: "os,library"
                    timeout: 10m0s
            -   name: Upload SARIF
                if: always()
                uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
                with:
                    sarif_file: trivy-results.sarif
                    category: trivy

    deploy-staging:
        name: Deploy → staging
        needs: [build, scan]
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        environment: { name: staging, url: "${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}" }
        concurrency: deploy-staging
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
            with:
              role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gha-deploy-staging
              aws-region: eu-central-1
          - uses: azure/setup-kubectl@v4
            with: { version: "${{ env.KUBECTL_VERSION }}" }
          - uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
          - id: deploy
            name: helm upgrade
            run: |-
              aws eks update-kubeconfig --name acme-staging --region eu-central-1
              helm upgrade --install "$HELM_RELEASE" oci://ghcr.io/acme/charts/storefront \
                --version "$HELM_CHART_VERSION" \
                --namespace storefront --create-namespace \
                --values deploy/values-staging.yaml \
                --set image.tag=${{ needs.build.outputs.version }} \
                --set image.digest=${{ needs.build.outputs.digest }} \
                --wait --timeout 10m --atomic
              echo "url=https://staging.acme.example.com" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    deploy-production:
        name: Deploy → production
        needs: [build, scan, deploy-staging]
        if: >-
            startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') ||
            (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.environment == 'production')
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        environment:
            name: production
            url: https://www.acme.example.com
        concurrency:
            group: deploy-production
            cancel-in-progress: false   # never cancel a prod rollout halfway through
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
            with:
              role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/gha-deploy-production
              aws-region: eu-central-1
              role-duration-seconds: 3600
          - uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
          - name: helm upgrade
            env:
              IMAGE_TAG: ${{ inputs.image-tag || needs.build.outputs.version }}
            run: |
              aws eks update-kubeconfig --name acme-prod --region eu-central-1
              helm upgrade --install "$HELM_RELEASE" oci://ghcr.io/acme/charts/storefront \
                --version "$HELM_CHART_VERSION" \
                --namespace storefront \
                --values deploy/values-production.yaml \
                --set image.tag="$IMAGE_TAG" \
                --set podAnnotations.deployedBy=${{ github.actor }} \
                --wait --timeout 15m --atomic --history-max 20
          # - name: Purge CDN
          #   run: ./scripts/purge-cdn.sh --zone storefront   # disabled, Fastly does it on deploy now

    notify:
        needs: [deploy-staging, deploy-production]
        if: always() && contains(needs.*.result, 'failure')
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - name: Post to Teams
            env:
              TEAMS_WEBHOOK: ${{ secrets.TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL }}
              RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
            run: >-
              curl -sS -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
              -d "{\"text\": \"storefront deploy failed ($GITHUB_REF_NAME): $RUN_URL\"}"
              "$TEAMS_WEBHOOK"
...

# Acme Open Source Code of Conduct #

<!-- Adapted for Acme from the Contributor Covenant 2.1. Last reviewed 2024-01-15 by the Community Working Group. Translations live in /docs/conduct/ -->

## Our pledge

We — the people who contribute to, maintain and lead Acme Open Source projects — want taking part in our communities to be a harassment-free experience for everyone. That holds regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, colour, religion, or sexual identity and orientation, and it holds whether you have been around for ten years or opened your very first pull request this morning.

We promise to act and interact in ways that keep our community open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive and healthy, in every place where that community meets: issue trackers and pull request reviews, chat rooms and mailing lists, video calls, meetups, and the hallway of a conference where somebody recognises the sticker on your laptop and comes over to say hello.

## Our standards

Things that help build a good environment:

* being patient and kind, especially with people who are new — to the project, to open source, or to programming
* assuming good intent, and asking before assuming
* giving feedback that is specific and actionable, and receiving it gracefully
  - e.g. "this loop is O(n²) for large inputs, could we use a map here?" rather than "this is slow"
  - explaining *why*, not only *what*
* owning our mistakes, apologising to the people affected, and learning from them
* putting the health of the community ahead of winning an argument

Things we will not accept:

- sexualised jokes, language or imagery, and unwelcome sexual attention or advances — in any channel, including direct messages
- insults, name-calling, deliberately inflammatory "just asking questions" trolling, and attacks on someone's identity or beliefs
- harassment of any kind, in public threads or in private
    - continuing to contact someone after they've asked you to stop
    - piling onto a person in an issue, a review or on social media
- sharing someone's personal details (home address, phone number, employer, legal name) without their explicit consent
- anything else a reasonable person would consider out of place in a professional setting



## Responsibilities

The moderation team is responsible for explaining and enforcing these standards. They will take fair and proportionate action in response to behaviour they consider inappropriate, threatening, offensive or harmful, and they will tell the people involved what was decided and why — unless doing so would put someone at risk.

Moderators may remove, edit or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues and other contributions that don't follow this Code of Conduct. They are expected to follow it themselves; a moderator who is involved in a reported incident steps aside from handling it.

## Scope

This Code applies in all community spaces (GitHub, the forum, Slack and Matrix, events), and also when someone represents an Acme Open Source project in public — for example when posting from an official social media account, or speaking at a conference as a maintainer.

## Reporting

If you experience or witness behaviour that breaks this Code, please tell us. You don't need to be sure it "counts".

**E-mail**  
conduct@acme.example.org — read only by the moderation team listed below.

**Web form**  
<https://acme.example.org/conduct/report?source=github&lang=en> (anonymous reports are possible).

**In person at events**  
Look for a volunteer with a green lanyard, or call the number printed on the back of your badge.

Current moderators:

| Name | Pronouns | Time zone | Languages |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amara Okafor | she/her | UTC+1 | English, Igbo |
| Jonas Weiß | he/him | UTC+1 | Deutsch, English |
| Hana Sato (佐藤 花) | she/they | UTC+9 | 日本語, English |

All reports are handled confidentially. We acknowledge every report within **two business days**.

___

## Enforcement guidelines

Moderators use the following ladder when deciding on consequences. It is a guide, not a script: serious incidents can go straight to step 3 or 4.

### 1. Correction

**Community Impact**: A one-off rude comment, unprofessional language, or a joke that made people feel unwelcome.

**Consequence**: A moderator contacts you privately, explains which part of this Code was affected and why, and may ask you to edit the comment or apologise in the thread.

### 2. Warning

**Community Impact**: A single serious incident, or a pattern of smaller ones.

**Consequence**: A formal written warning that spells out what happens next time. For a set period (usually 30 days) you should not interact with the people involved, including in unofficial spaces such as social media. Ignoring this may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.

### 3. Temporary ban

**Community Impact**: A serious violation, including sustained inappropriate behaviour after a warning.

**Consequence**: Removal from all community spaces for a fixed period, typically three to six months. During the ban you may not contact community members about the incident, including the people who reported it.

### 4. Permanent ban
**Community Impact**: A repeated pattern of violations, harassment of an individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of groups of people.

**Consequence**: Permanent removal from all Acme Open Source community spaces.

## Appeals

If you believe a decision was wrong, write to appeals@acme.example.org within 30 days. Appeals are reviewed by two members of the Community Working Group who were *not* involved in the original decision, and their answer is final.

## Attribution

This Code of Conduct is adapted from the [Contributor Covenant][], version 2.1, available at [https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html][v2.1]. The enforcement ladder was inspired by [Mozilla's code of conduct enforcement ladder][mozilla coc].

For answers to common questions, see the Covenant's [FAQ]. [Translations] are available as well; Acme-specific translations live in `docs/conduct/` and are maintained by volunteers (thank you, Lucía, Thắng and Ingrid!).

info:
  title: Acme Petstore API
  version: 1.0.0

    # Acme Petstore

    The **extended** petstore used by the storefront and partner integrations. It is
