# Marmot roadmap [![Project board](https://img.shields.io/badge/board-GitHub%20Projects-blue)](https://github.com/orgs/marmot-flags/projects/3/views/2?filterQuery=-status%3ADone) [![Community call](https://img.shields.io/badge/community%20call-1st%20Tuesday-6f42c1)](https://marmot.example.org/community#call) This is where Marmot is headed over the next few quarters. It is a statement of intent, **not** a promise: priorities shift as we learn, and dates are deliberately vague. If you want to influence it, the best way is to comment on (or 👍) the linked issues, or to join the monthly community call on the first Tuesday of each month at 17:00 UTC. We review this document at the start of every quarter and record what moved and why in the [history of this file](https://github.com/marmot-flags/marmot/commits/main/ROADMAP.md); nothing is removed silently — things we decide not to do are struck through with a short explanation, and everything that ships moves into the archive at the bottom, so the history stays readable for people who land here from a search engine years later. ## Legend | Symbol | Meaning | |:------:|---------| | ✅ | Done | | 🚧 | In progress | | 🗓️ | Planned, not started | | 🤔 | Exploring, needs design | | ~~struck~~ | Dropped (with a reason) | ___ ## 2025 Q1 ## ### Theme: reliability of the evaluation path Flag evaluation must keep working when the Marmot server is down. Today the server-side SDKs fall back to defaults after 30 s, which is… not great. - [ ] 🚧 **Local evaluation for server SDKs** ([#412](https://github.com/marmot-flags/marmot/issues/412)) - [x] rule engine extracted into the `marmot-eval` crate - [ ] Go SDK - [x] streaming updates via SSE - [ ] fall back to polling when proxies block SSE ([#431](https://github.com/marmot-flags/marmot/issues/431)) - [ ] Python SDK - [ ] Node SDK - [ ] 🗓️ Relay proxy with a persistent cache ([#455](https://github.com/marmot-flags/marmot/issues/455)) - [ ] 🗓️ Chaos tests for the flag-delivery pipeline ### Theme: experimentation - [ ] 🤔 Sequential testing (always-valid p-values) — design doc in progress[^seq] - [ ] 🗓️ CUPED variance reduction - [ ] needs pre-experiment metric snapshots - [ ] storage cost estimate for large tenants - [ ] retention policy - [ ] UI: show the variance reduction achieved per experiment - [ ] ~~Multi-armed bandits~~ — dropped for 2025, see [#390](https://github.com/marmot-flags/marmot/issues/390) for the discussion ### Theme: self-hosting * [x] Helm chart moved to the main repository * [ ] 🚧 Official Terraform provider * [x] flags and segments * [ ] environments and API keys * [ ] 🗓️ Documented backup/restore procedure (with a script that actually works) ## 2025 Q2 ## - [ ] 🗓️ **Audit log v2** — structured diffs instead of before/after JSON blobs - [ ] 🗓️ OpenFeature providers for .NET and PHP - [ ] 🤔 Flag lifecycle: automatically detect "stale" flags (100% rolled out for > 30 days) and open a cleanup PR in the linked repository - [ ] 🤔 Approvals ("four-eyes principle") for production flag changes - [ ] per-environment configuration - [ ] Slack/Teams notifications for pending approvals ## 2025 H2 and later Fuzzier, by design: 1. Edge evaluation (Cloudflare Workers, Fastly Compute) using the `marmot-eval` WASM build 2. Warehouse-native experiment analysis (BigQuery, Snowflake, ClickHouse) 3. A proper plugin system for custom targeting rules — *if* the Terraform provider work shows that people need it *** ## Progress | Area | Planned | Done | Progress | |:-----|--------:|-----:|---------:| | SDKs | 14 | 9 | 64% | | Experimentation | 8 | 2 | 25% | | Self-hosting & ops | 11 | 7 | 64% | | Docs | 6 | 6 | 100% | | **Total** | **39** | **24** | **62%** | Numbers are updated by hand, so they lag the [project board][board] by a week or two.
Archive: shipped in 2024 - ✅ **2024 Q4** — PostgreSQL 16 support; OpenFeature provider for Java; dark mode (finally) - ✅ **2024 Q3** — audit log export to S3/GCS; SCIM provisioning - ✅ **2024 Q2** — scheduled flag changes; prerequisite flags - ✅ **2024 Q1** — percentage rollouts by any attribute, not only `user_id` - ~~MySQL backend~~ — dropped in Q1 2024: not enough interest to justify a second storage engine
___ Have an idea that isn't on here? Open a [feature request][fr] — please describe the *problem* first and the solution second.\ Maintainers: Hanna Virtanen, Kofi Mensah, Lucía Fernández. [^seq]: Draft: . Feedback from people who have actually run sequential tests in production is very welcome. [board]: https://github.com/orgs/marmot-flags/projects/3 "Marmot project board" [fr]: https://github.com/marmot-flags/marmot/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml

---
title: "Interim Safety Summary: Study ACME-301"
subtitle: "Data cut-off 31 January 2024 — DSMB open session report"
author:
  - "Dr. A. Rivera, MD"
  - "B. Chen, PhD"
  - "S. O'Neill, MSc (Biostatistics)"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"
output:
  word_document:
    reference_docx: template.docx
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 2
  pdf_document:
    latex_engine: xelatex
    toc: true
    number_sections: true
params:
  data_cut: "2024-01-31"
  arm_labels: ["Placebo", "Low dose", "High dose"]
  show_listings: false
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 4, dpi = 300)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(haven)
library(knitr)

adsl <- read_sas("data/adam/adsl.sas7bdat") |>
  filter(SAFFL == "Y")
adae <- read_sas("data/adam/adae.sas7bdat") |>
  filter(TRTEMFL == "Y", ASTDT <= as.Date(params$data_cut))

adsl$TRT01A <- factor(adsl$TRT01A, levels = params$arm_labels)
adae <- adae |> left_join(select(adsl, USUBJID, TRT01A), by = "USUBJID")

n_randomized <- nrow(adsl)
pct_ae       <- 100 * n_distinct(adae$USUBJID) / n_randomized
n_sae        <- n_distinct(adae$USUBJID[adae$AESER == "Y"])
```

<!-- QC: checked by BC 2024-02-05 against the TLF shells v1.3. Two discrepancies in the AE table were traced to a MedDRA version mismatch (26.0 vs. 26.1) and fixed in ADAE. -->

# Purpose of this report

This report summarises the cumulative safety data from Study ACME-301, a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase II study of ACM-4410 in adults with moderate-to-severe chronic plaque psoriasis, for the open session of the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) meeting on 21 February 2024. Data are presented by treatment arm, pooled across sites, i.e. without unblinding of individual participants. As agreed in the DSMB charter (v2.0, section 6.3), efficacy data are **not** included in the open report; see the [protocol][prot] and the [statistical analysis plan][sap] for definitions.

As of the data cut-off (`r params$data_cut`), `r n_randomized` participants had been randomised and had received at least one dose of study drug (safety population). Enrolment is approx. 68% complete vs. the planned 270 participants. Recruitment at the U.S. sites has been slower than projected, mainly because of competing studies, while the EU sites are on track. Dr. Rivera has asked the CRO to open two additional sites in Poland (site No. 314 and No. 315) in March.

# Study population

```{r demographics, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
demo <- adsl |>
  group_by(TRT01A) |>
  summarise(
    N = as.character(n()),
    `Age, mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(AGE), sd(AGE)),
    `Female, n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", sum(SEX == "F"), 100 * mean(SEX == "F")),
    `BMI, mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(BMI), sd(BMI)),
    `PASI at baseline, median` = sprintf("%.1f", median(BASEPASI))
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-TRT01A, names_to = "Characteristic") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = TRT01A, values_from = value)

knitr::kable(demo, align = "lccc",
             caption = "Table 1. Baseline demographics (safety population)")
```

Baseline characteristics were broadly balanced across arms (Table 1). The high-dose arm had a slightly higher proportion of participants with prior biologic exposure (31% vs. 24% on placebo), which is well within what one would expect by chance with arms of this size, cf. the simulations in the SAP, Appendix C.

# Exposure

Median duration of exposure was 16.1 weeks (range 2.0–24.0). Twelve participants discontinued study drug early:

- Placebo: 5 (lack of efficacy: 3; withdrawal of consent: 2)
- Low dose: 3
    - adverse event: 1 (SAE No. 2, see below)
    - lost to follow-up: 2
- High dose: 4
    * adverse event: 2
    * relocation: 1 — the participant moved abroad and could not attend visits
    * other: 1

# Adverse events #

Overall, `r sprintf("%.1f%%", pct_ae)` of participants experienced at least one treatment-emergent adverse event (TEAE). The most frequent TEAEs by MedDRA preferred term were nasopharyngitis, headache and upper respiratory tract infection, with no clear dose-response pattern (Fig. 1). Injection-site reactions were reported more often with active treatment (e.g., 9.8% in the high-dose arm vs. 2.2% on placebo), as expected from the phase I data reported by Lindgren et al.[^phase1] All injection-site reactions were grade 1 or 2 and none led to discontinuation.

```{r ae-plot, fig.cap="Fig. 1. Most frequent TEAEs (≥ 5% in any arm) by treatment arm."}
adae |>
  distinct(USUBJID, TRT01A, AEDECOD) |>
  count(TRT01A, AEDECOD) |>
  group_by(AEDECOD) |>
  filter(max(n) / n_randomized * 3 >= 0.05) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, reorder(AEDECOD, n), fill = TRT01A)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "Participants", y = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

Grade ≥ 3 TEAEs (CTCAE v5.0) were infrequent:

| Category | Placebo | Low dose | High dose |
|:---------|:-------:|:--------:|:---------:|
| Any TEAE | 58 (64.4 %) | 61 (67.8 %) | 64 (71.1 %) |
| TEAE grade ≥ 3 | 3 (3.3 %) | 4 (4.4 %) |6 (6.7 %)|
|Serious AE (SAE)| 2 (2.2 %) | 2 (2.2 %) | 3 (3.3 %) |
| AE leading to discontinuation | 0 | 1 (1.1 %) | 2 (2.2 %) |
| Deaths | 0 | 0 | 0 |

_Note:_ the table above is hand-copied from TLF 14.3.1.1 (run of 2024-02-04); if it ever disagrees with the programmed output, the programmed output takes precedence.

## Serious adverse events

There were `r n_sae` participants with SAEs as of the data cut. All were reviewed by the medical monitor, Dr. Rivera, and none was assessed as related to study drug except SAE No. 2.

* **SAE No. 1** (placebo). Appendicitis on Day 43, appendectomy, recovered without sequelae. Not related.
* **SAE No. 2** (low dose). Drug-induced liver injury suspected on Day 57: ALT 6.2× ULN, bilirubin normal, i.e. Hy's law criteria were **not** met. Study drug was permanently discontinued and ALT normalised by Day 85. Assessed as *possibly related* by the investigator.
* **SAE No. 3** (high dose). Community-acquired pneumonia on Day 98, hospitalised for 4 days. Not related per the investigator; the sponsor's assessment is "unlikely related" given the timing.
* **SAE No. 4–7**: see the listings in the closed report (Appendix 2).

> **From the DSMB charter, section 7.2**
>
> The DSMB may recommend modification or termination of the study if the incidence of hepatic events meeting Hy's law criteria, or of grade 4 neutropenia, is judged to be substantially higher in either active arm than in the placebo arm.
>
> > In the absence of formal stopping boundaries for safety, such a judgement will take into account the totality of the data, e.g. the time course, reversibility and biological plausibility of a causal relationship.

Laboratory parameters
---------------------

Shifts from normal at baseline to grade ≥ 2 abnormalities were rare. Two participants in the high-dose arm had transient neutropenia (grade 2, absolute neutrophil count 1.0–1.5 × 10⁹/L) at Week 4, which resolved without dose interruption by Week 8. There were no cases of grade ≥ 3 neutropenia. Mean changes in lipids were small (LDL-C +0.12 mmol/L in the high-dose arm vs. −0.03 mmol/L on placebo) and are similar to those described for other drugs of the class, cf. Haddad et al. (2021).

Vital signs and ECG parameters showed no clinically meaningful changes. One participant (low dose) had a QTcF of 482 ms at Week 12, i.e. above the 480 ms threshold; the repeat ECG one hour later was 451 ms, and the participant continued treatment after review by the cardiologist, Dr. Weiss.

# Important protocol deviations

Important protocol deviations (n = 14) are listed below. Minor deviations are summarised in the closed report only.

1. Eligibility criteria not met (n = 3).
   - Two participants were randomised with a screening PASI of 11.5 and 11.8, below the required ≥ 12. Both were identified at the first monitoring visit. Per sponsor decision, they continued treatment.
   - One participant had a positive QuantiFERON test at screening that was misread as "indeterminate". Isoniazid prophylaxis was started on Day 22.
2. Dosing errors (n = 4), e.g. a missed dose at Week 8 due to a shipment delay at site No. 112 (Lyon). No participant received a higher dose than assigned.
3. Visits out of window (n = 6). Mostly over the Christmas holidays; none affected the primary endpoint assessment at Week 16.
4. Unblinding (n = 1). The site pharmacist at site No. 205 inadvertently opened an emergency unblinding envelope. Dr. Chen reviewed the case and confirmed that neither the treating investigator nor the participant was informed of the allocation.

\newpage

# Conclusions

No new safety signals were identified in this interim analysis. The overall incidence of TEAEs was similar across arms, the excess of injection-site reactions on active treatment is consistent with the phase I experience, and the single hepatic SAE did not meet Hy's law criteria. The study team therefore proposes that the DSMB recommend continuation of the study without modification.
The next interim review is planned at a data cut-off of 31 July 2024, or earlier if requested by the DSMB.

***

# Listings {-}

```{r listings, eval=params$show_listings}
adae |>
  filter(AESER == "Y") |>
  select(USUBJID, TRT01A, AEDECOD, ASTDY, AETOXGR, AEREL, AEOUT) |>
  arrange(TRT01A, USUBJID) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Listing 1. Serious adverse events (safety population)")
```

[^phase1]: Lindgren M, Okafor C, Barros J, et al. Safety and pharmacokinetics of ACM-4410 in healthy volunteers: a phase I, randomised, placebo-controlled study. *Br J Clin Pharmacol*. 2022;88(4):1712–1723.

[prot]: https://ctms.acme-pharma.example/studies/ACME-301/documents/protocol-amendment-3-v4.0-2023-09-14.pdf "Protocol, amendment 3"
[sap]: https://ctms.acme-pharma.example/studies/ACME-301/documents/SAP_v2.1_final_signed.pdf

Important protocol deviations (n = 14) are listed below. Minor deviations are summarised in the closed report only.

1. Eligibility criteria not met (n = 3).
   - Two participants were randomised with a screening PASI of 11.5 and 11.8, below the required ≥ 12. Both were identified at the first monitoring visit. Per sponsor decision, they continued treatment.
   - One participant had a positive QuantiFERON test at screening that was misread as "indeterminate". Isoniazid prophylaxis was started on Day 22.
2. Dosing errors (n = 4), e.g. a missed dose at Week 8 due to a shipment delay at site No. 112 (Lyon). No participant received a higher dose than assigned.
3. Visits out of window (n = 6). Mostly over the Christmas holidays; none affected the primary endpoint assessment at Week 16.
4. Unblinding (n = 1). The site pharmacist at site No. 205 inadvertently opened an emergency unblinding envelope. Dr. Chen reviewed the case and confirmed that neither the treating investigator nor the participant was informed of the allocation.

\newpage

# Conclusions

No new safety signals were identified in this interim analysis. The overall incidence of TEAEs was similar across arms, the excess of injection-site reactions on active treatment is consistent with the phase I experience, and the single hepatic SAE did not meet Hy's law criteria. The study team therefore proposes that the DSMB recommend continuation of the study without modification.
The next interim review is planned at a data cut-off of 31 July 2024, or earlier if requested by the DSMB.

***

# .github/workflows/integration.yml  (reusable)
#
# Usage from another repo:
#
#   jobs:
#     integration:
#       uses: acme/.github/.github/workflows/integration.yml@v2
#       with:
#         node-version: 20
#         matrix: '{"suite": ["api", "worker"]}'
#       secrets: inherit
#
# Changing an input's type is a breaking change for every caller -> bump to @v3.
name: integration (reusable)

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: Runner label, or a JSON array of labels for the self-hosted pools
        type: string
        default: ubuntu-latest
      node-version:
        type: number
        default: 20
      node-version-legacy:
        description: "Kept for callers that still pass a string. Remove after Q3."
        type: string
        default: "20"
      matrix:
        description: 'JSON matrix, e.g. {"suite": ["api", "worker"]}'
        type: string
        required: true
      run-integration:
        type: boolean
        default: true
      mysql-version:
        type: string
        default: '8.0'
      timeout:
        type: number
        default: 30
      working-directory:
        type: string
        required: false
        default: .
    secrets:
      NPM_TOKEN:
        required: true
      SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN:
        required: false
      DB_PASSWORD:
        description: Password for the throwaway mysql service (not really secret, it just keeps it out of the logs)
        required: false
    outputs:
      report-url:
        description: Link to the uploaded HTML report
        value: ${{ jobs.integration.outputs.report-url }}
      passed:
        value: ${{ jobs.summary.outputs.passed }}

jobs:
   lint-config:
     name: Validate inputs
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - name: matrix must be valid JSON with a "suite" key
         env:
           MATRIX: ${{ inputs.matrix }}
         run: echo "$MATRIX" | jq -e 'has("suite")' > /dev/null


   integration:
      name: integration (${{ matrix.suite }})
      needs: lint-config
      runs-on: ${{ startsWith(inputs.runner, '[') && fromJSON(inputs.runner) || inputs.runner }}
      if: inputs.run-integration && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || !github.event.pull_request.draft)
      timeout-minutes: ${{ inputs.timeout }}
      strategy:
         fail-fast: false
         matrix: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.matrix) }}
      container:
         image: ghcr.io/acme/ci-node:${{ inputs.node-version }}
         credentials: { username: "${{ github.actor }}", password: "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" }
         options: --user 1001
      services:
         mysql:
            image: mysql:${{ inputs.mysql-version }}
            env:
               MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD || 'root' }}
               MYSQL_DATABASE: app_test
            ports: ['3306:3306']
            options: >-
               --health-cmd="mysqladmin ping"
               --health-interval=10s
               --health-timeout=5s
               --health-retries=6
      outputs:
         report-url: ${{ steps.upload.outputs.artifact-url }}
      defaults:
         run:
            working-directory: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
      steps:
         - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         # no setup-node here: the ci-node image already ships node + pnpm
         - name: Install
           run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
           env:
              NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
         # - name: Wait for mysql
         #   run: npx wait-on tcp:mysql:3306 -t 60000
         - name: Should we run?
           id: skip
           if: "!contains(github.event.head_commit.message, '[skip ci]')"
           run: echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
         - name: Run ${{ matrix.suite }} suite
           if: steps.skip.outputs.run == 'true'
           run: |
              pnpm run test:integration --suite ${{ matrix.suite }} \
                 --reporter=html --reporter=junit \
                 --outputDir=reports/${{ matrix.suite }}
           env:
              DB_HOST: mysql
              DB_PORT: 3306
              DB_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD || 'root' }}
              SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
              NODE_ENV: test
         - name: Upload report
           id: upload
           if: "!cancelled()"
           uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
           with:
              name: report-${{ matrix.suite }}
              path: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}/reports/
              retention-days: 14


   summary:
     needs: integration
     if: always()
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     outputs:
       passed: ${{ steps.result.outputs.passed }}
     steps:
       - id: result
         run: |
           if [ "${{ needs.integration.result }}" = "success" ]; then
             echo "passed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           else
             echo "passed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           fi
       - name: Write summary
         run: >
           echo "Integration result: **${{ needs.integration.result }}**"
           >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
       - name: Footer
         shell: bash
         run: |+
           echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
           echo "_generated by acme/.github integration.yml_" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

...

# Security Policy

[![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/acme/lattice/badge)](https://securityscorecards.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/acme/lattice)
[![OpenSSF Best Practices](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/8123/badge)](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/8123)
[![SLSA 3](https://slsa.dev/images/gh-badge-level3.svg)](https://slsa.dev)

The Lattice maintainers take security seriously. Thank you for helping keep Lattice and its users safe!

<!-- Keep this file in sync with https://lattice.example.org/security/ (docs/security.md). Last update: 2024-06-10 -->

## Supported versions

We release security fixes for the following versions of **Lattice** (`acme/lattice`, the PostgreSQL-aware connection proxy):

| Version | Supported          | Security fixes until |
| :------ | :----------------: | -------------------: |
| 4.2.x   | :white_check_mark: | current release      |
| 4.1.x   | :white_check_mark: | 2025-03-31           |
| 4.0.x   | :x:                | 2024-09-30           |
| 3.x | :x: | 2023-12-31 |
| < 3.0 | :x: | — |

Only the latest patch release of a supported minor version gets fixes, so please upgrade to e.g. `4.1.7` before reporting something against `4.1.3`.

## Reporting a vulnerability

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues, discussions or pull requests.**
>
> A public report puts every Lattice deployment at risk until a fix is available.

Use one of these private channels instead:

1) **GitHub private vulnerability reporting** (preferred) — open the [Security tab](https://github.com/acme/lattice/security/advisories/new) and click *Report a vulnerability*.
2) **E-mail** security@lattice.example.org. Please encrypt with our [PGP key](#pgp-key) if the report contains exploit details.
3) No reply after 72 hours? Ping `@acme/lattice-security` in the [Matrix room](https://matrix.to/#/#lattice-security:matrix.org) — don't share details there, just say that you sent a report.

Please include as much of the following as you can:

* the type of issue (e.g. SQL injection through the query rewriter, authentication bypass, request smuggling)
* full paths of the source file(s) related to the issue
* the affected version, tag, or commit
* any special configuration required to reproduce it
    * e.g. `tls.mode = "passthrough"`, or a custom `auth_plugin`
    * your `lattice.toml` with secrets removed is ideal

   ```bash
   cp -r tooling/templates/library packages/my-lib
   ```

1. Add the package to the **Packages** table above and to `CODEOWNERS`.

`TURBO_TOKEN` / `TURBO_TEAM` | CI, optional locally | enables the remote cache
`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` | build | uploads source maps; builds work fine without it

Local overrides go in `.env.local` files, which are git-ignored. Never commit real tokens — `gitleaks` runs in a pre-commit hook and in CI.

arguments.content:
# Acme Petstore -- OpenAPI contract for the storefront + partner integrations.
# Rendered at https://developer.acme.example/petstore (redoc). Lint with `make lint-api`.
# TODO: move to 3.1 once the codegen supports it (#88)
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Acme Petstore API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: |
    # Acme Petstore

    The **extended** petstore used by the storefront and partner integrations. It is
    *mostly* compatible with the classic Swagger petstore, plus:

    - photo uploads (`multipart/form-data`) and order management under `/store/orders`
    - offset paging via `limit` + `offset` (yes, we know -- see [ADR-007](https://wiki.acme.example/adr/007-pagination))

    ## Authentication
    Read endpoints accept an `api_key` header; anything that mutates state needs an
    OAuth2 token with the matching scope:

        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.petstore.acme.example/v1/pets
  contact:
    name:  Petstore API team
    email: "api-team@acme.example"
    url: https://acme.example/support
  license:
    name: Apache 2.0
    url: 'https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.html'

servers:
  - url: https://{environment}.petstore.acme.example/v1
    description: Production / staging (pick with the `environment` variable)
    variables:
      environment:
        default: api
        enum: [api, api.dev, api.staging]
tags:
- name: pet
  description: Everything about your pets
  externalDocs:
    description: Find out more
    url: https://docs.acme.example/petstore/pets
- name: store
  description: Access to petstore orders
- name: user
  description:   Operations about user
  externalDocs: { description: "User guide", url: "https://docs.acme.example/petstore/users" }


paths:
  /pets:
    get:
      tags: [ pet ]
      summary: List pets
      description: Returns all pets the caller has access to, optionally filtered by tag. Results are ordered by createdAt, newest first.
      operationId: listPets
      parameters:
        - name: limit
          in: query
          description: How many items to return at one time (max 100)
          required: false
          schema: { type: integer, format: int32, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, default: 20 }
        - name: tags
          in: query
          description: tags to filter by
          style: form
          explode: false
          schema: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
          example: [dog,cat]
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A paged array of pets
          headers:
            x-next: { description: Link to the next page, schema: { type: string } }
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { type: array, maxItems: 100, items: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pet" } }
        default:
          $ref: '#/components/responses/UnexpectedError'
    post:
      tags: [pet]
      summary: Create a pet
      operationId: createPet
      requestBody:
        $ref: '#/components/requestBodies/NewPet'
      responses:
        "201": { description: Null response }
        '422':
          $ref: "#/components/responses/ValidationError"
      security:
        - petstore_auth: [ "write:pets", "read:pets" ]

  /pets/{petId}:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/PetId'
    get:
      tags:
        - pet
      summary: Info for a specific pet
      operationId: showPetById
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Expected response to a valid request
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/AnyPet'
              example:
                id: 10
                name: Rex
                petType: dog
                tags: [ good-boy, "vaccinated" ]
                packSize: 1
        '404':
          $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"
    put:
      tags: [ pet ]
      summary: Replace a pet
      operationId: replacePet
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content: { application/json: { schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet' } } }
      responses:
        '200': { description: Updated }
    delete:
      tags: [ pet ]
      summary: Deletes a pet
      operationId: deletePet
      parameters:
        - { name: api_key, in: header, required: false, schema: { type: string } }
      responses:
        '204':
          description: Deleted

  /pets/{petId}/photos:
    post:
      tags: [pet]
      summary: Upload a photo
      operationId: uploadPetPhoto
      parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/PetId'
      requestBody:
        content:
          multipart/form-data:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [file]
              properties:
                file: { type: string, format: binary }
                caption: { type: string, maxLength: 280 }
      responses:
        '201': { description: Photo stored }
        '413': { description: File too large (limit is 10 MB) }

  /store/orders:
    post:
      tags:
      - store
      summary: Place an order for a pet
      operationId: placeOrder
      requestBody:
        content: { application/json: { schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Order' } } }
      responses:
        '200':
          description: successful operation
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Order' }
        '405': { description: Invalid input }

  # copied over from the legacy spec (4-space indents) -- never got reformatted
  /users/login:
      get:
          tags: [user]
          summary: Logs user into the system
          operationId: loginUser
          parameters:
              - { name: username, in: query, required: true, schema: { type: string } }
              - name: password
                in: query
                required: true
                schema: { type: string, format: password }
          responses:
              '200':
                  description: successful operation
                  headers:
                      X-Rate-Limit:
                          description: calls per hour allowed by the user
                          schema: { type: integer, format: int32 }
                  content: { application/json: { schema: { type: string } } }
              '400':
                  description: Invalid username/password supplied
          security: []

components:
  parameters:
    PetId:
      name: petId
      in: path
      required: true
      schema: { type: string }
  requestBodies:
    NewPet:
      description: Pet object that needs to be added to the store
      required: true
      content: { application/json: { schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/NewPet' } } }
  responses:
    NotFound:
      description: The specified resource was not found
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Error'
    ValidationError:
      description: Request body failed validation
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Error' }
          example:
            code: 422
            message: "name: must not be blank"
    UnexpectedError:
      description: unexpected error
      content: { application/json: { schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error" } } }

  schemas:
    NewPet:
      type: object
      required:
        - name
        - petType
      properties:
        name: { type: string, example: Rex }
        petType: { type: string }
        status:
          type: string
          description: pet status in the store
          enum: [available, pending,sold]
          default: available
        tags: { type: array, items: { type: string } }
    Pet:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/NewPet'
        - type: object
          required: [ id ]
          properties:
            id: { type: integer, format: int64, readOnly: true }
            createdAt: { type: string, format: date-time }
    AnyPet:
      oneOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
        - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Cat"
      discriminator:
        propertyName: petType
        mapping:
          dog: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
          cat: "#/components/schemas/Cat"
    Dog:
      allOf:
      - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
      - type: object
        properties:
          packSize: { type: integer, format: int32, minimum: 0, default: 0 }
    Cat:
      allOf:
      - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
      - type: object
        properties:
          huntingSkill: { type: string, enum: [ clueless, lazy, adventurous, aggressive ] }
    Order:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: {type: integer, format: int64}
        petId: {type: integer, format: int64}
        quantity: {type: integer, format: int32, minimum: 1}
        shipDate: { type: string, format: date-time }
        status: { type: string, enum: [placed, approved, delivered] }
        complete: { type: boolean, default: false }
      example: { id: 10, petId: 198772, quantity: 7, shipDate: "2024-03-01T10:15:00Z", status: approved }
    Error:
      type: object
      required: [code, message]
      properties:
        code: { type: integer, format: int32 }
        message: { type: string }

  securitySchemes:
    api_key: { type: apiKey, name: api_key, in: header }
    petstore_auth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        authorizationCode:
          authorizationUrl: https://auth.acme.example/oauth/authorize
          tokenUrl: https://auth.acme.example/oauth/token
          scopes:
            write:pets: modify pets in your account
            'read:pets': read your pets
security:
  - api_key: []

--- title: Getting started description: "Install acmeflow, build your first pipeline and run it locally — in about ten minutes." hide: [navigation] tags: - Installation - Tutorial - first steps icon: material/rocket-launch --- # Getting started **acmeflow** is a small, Python-native workflow engine. You describe tasks as plain functions, wire them together into a pipeline, and run that pipeline on your laptop, in CI or on a cluster without changing a line of code. This page walks you through installing it, writing a first pipeline, running it, and looking at the result in the local UI; it should take about ten minutes, most of which is waiting for `pip`. !!! note This guide assumes you're comfortable with a terminal and have used `pip` before. On Windows, run the commands in PowerShell; they work the same unless noted otherwise. ## Requirements * Python **3.9 – 3.13** (CPython; PyPy works but isn't tested in CI)[^pypy] * about 200 MB of free disk space for the local metadata store * *optional:* Docker or Podman, for the containerized executor in [step 5](#first-pipeline) !!! warning "Python 3.8 is no longer supported" acmeflow 2.0 dropped support for Python 3.8, which reached end-of-life in October 2024. If you're stuck on it, pin the last compatible release: ```bash pip install "acmeflow<2" ``` ## Install === "pip" ```bash python -m pip install --upgrade acmeflow ``` Optional extras: `acmeflow[s3]`, `acmeflow[gcs]`, `acmeflow[k8s]` or simply `acmeflow[all]`. === "conda" ```bash conda install -c conda-forge acmeflow ``` The conda-forge package usually lags PyPI by a day or two. === "uv" ```bash uv tool install acmeflow # just the CLI, in its own environment uv add acmeflow # or as a dependency of your project ``` ??? tip "Using uv" [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/#standalone-installer) resolves and installs packages 10–100× faster than pip. If you added acmeflow with `uv add`, run the CLI as `uv run acmeflow …` so that it picks up the project's virtual environment. Check that it worked: ```console $ acmeflow --version acmeflow 2.3.1 (python 3.12.4, linux-x86_64) ``` ## Your first pipeline { #first-pipeline } 1. Create a project folder and initialise it: ```bash mkdir hello-flow && cd hello-flow acmeflow init --template minimal ``` This creates `flow.py`, `acmeflow.toml` and a hidden `.acmeflow/` directory for local state. 2. Replace the contents of `flow.py` with: ``` { .python title="flow.py" linenums="1" } from acmeflow import task, pipeline @task(retries=2) # (1)! def fetch(city: str) -> dict: import httpx r = httpx.get(f"https://api.example.com/weather?q={city}&units=metric") r.raise_for_status() return r.json() @task def summarize(data: dict) -> str: return f"{data['name']}: {data['main']['temp']:.1f} °C" @pipeline(schedule="0 7 * * *") # (2)! def morning_report(cities: list[str] = ["Berlin", "Lisbon", "Osaka"]): return [summarize(fetch(c)) for c in cities] ``` 1. Failed tasks are retried with exponential back-off: 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, … 2. A standard cron expression. Schedules only apply once the pipeline is *deployed* — `acmeflow run` ignores them. 3. Run it: ```bash acmeflow run flow.py:morning_report ``` You should see something like this: ```text ▶ morning_report run_id=01HZX3K9Q2 executor=local ✓ fetch[Berlin] 0.41s ✓ fetch[Lisbon] 0.38s ✓ fetch[Osaka] 0.52s ✓ summarize ×3 0.01s ✔ finished in 0.97s — 6/6 tasks succeeded ``` Press ++ctrl+c++ at any time to cancel. Running tasks receive `SIGTERM` and get 10 seconds to clean up. 4. Open the local UI to inspect the run: ```bash acmeflow ui --port 4200 ``` Then browse to . Click a task to see its inputs, outputs and logs. The UI only listens on `127.0.0.1` unless you pass `--host 0.0.0.0`. 5. Optionally, run the same pipeline in containers: ```bash acmeflow run flow.py:morning_report --executor docker --image python:3.12-slim ``` ???+ example "Passing parameters on the command line" Pipeline arguments automatically become CLI options: ```bash acmeflow run flow.py:morning_report --cities '["Nairobi", "Montréal", "São Paulo"]' ``` ## What just happened? A few things worth knowing before you go further: - Each task result is cached by a hash of its inputs and source code (1), so re-running the pipeline with the same cities is almost instant. - Independent tasks run in parallel (2); `summarize` only waits for its own `fetch`. - Everything is recorded in `.acmeflow/metadata.db`, a plain SQLite file you can query. { .annotate } 1. Disable it per task with `@task(cache=False)`, or globally with `ACMEFLOW_CACHE=off`. 2. The local executor uses a thread pool of `min(32, os.cpu_count() + 4)` workers. ## Next steps
- :material-book-open-variant:{ .lg .middle } __Concepts__ --- Tasks, pipelines, executors and the metadata store, explained. [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Read the concepts](concepts/index.md) - :material-cloud-upload:{ .lg .middle } __Deploy__ --- Ship pipelines to Kubernetes, AWS Batch or a plain VM with systemd. [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Deployment guide](deploy/index.md) - :material-puzzle:{ .lg .middle } __Integrations__ --- dbt, Spark, DuckDB, Slack alerts and more than 30 others. [:octicons-arrow-right-24: Browse integrations](integrations/index.md)
Stuck? Ask in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/acme/acmeflow/discussions?discussions_q=label%3Aquestion) or check the [troubleshooting page](troubleshooting.md)[^support]. [^pypy]: PyPy 3.10 passes the test suite, but some optional extras (notably `acmeflow[k8s]`) depend on packages without PyPy wheels. [^support]: Commercial support is available from Acme Inc. — see .

arguments.content:
---
title: Configuration reference
description: Every option you can set in acme.toml, on the command line, or through environment variables.
---

# Configuration

Acme reads its settings from **`acme.toml`** in the project root (the first one found walking up
from the current directory). Every setting can also be passed on the command line or through an
environment variable. Precedence, from highest to lowest:

    CLI flag  >  environment variable  >  acme.toml  >  built-in default

That's the order you'd expect, with one twist: _list_ settings are **replaced**, not merged,
when they come from a higher-precedence source. Setting `ACME_ENV_PASSTHROUGH=CI` therefore
*removes* everything you listed in the file.

!!! danger "Breaking change in 3.0"

    The configuration file was renamed from `.acmerc` (YAML) to `acme.toml`. Acme 3.x still
    reads `.acmerc`, but prints a deprecation warning on every run, and support will be removed
    in 4.0. Convert your file with:

    ```console
    $ acme config migrate --from .acmerc --to acme.toml
    ✔ wrote acme.toml (14 settings, 2 renamed)
    ```

    !!! note "Comments are not migrated"

        TOML and YAML comments don't map one-to-one, so `config migrate` drops them.
        Keep the old file around until you've copied over anything important.

## Example

```toml title="acme.toml"
# acme.toml — shared by every package in this repo
cache_dir   = "~/.cache/acme"
parallelism = 0                 # 0 = one worker per CPU
log_level   = "info"

[project]
name    = "storefront"
include = ["apps/*", "packages/*"]
exclude = ["**/node_modules", "**/dist"]

[remote_cache]
url       = "https://cache.example.com/v1"
token_env = "ACME_CACHE_TOKEN"
mode      = "read-write"

[env]
passthrough = ["CI", "GITHUB_*", "NODE_OPTIONS"]
set         = { TZ = "UTC", LANG = "C.UTF-8" }
```

## Overview

| Option | Type | Default | CLI flag | Environment variable |
|:-------|:----:|:--------|:---------|:---------------------|
| `cache_dir` | path | platform cache dir | `--cache-dir` | `ACME_CACHE_DIR` |
| `parallelism` | integer ≥ 0 | `0` | `-j`, `--jobs` | `ACME_PARALLELISM` |
| `log_level` | `trace` \| `debug` \| `info` \| `warn` \| `error` | `info` | `-v` / `-q` | `ACME_LOG` |
| `project.name` | string | directory name | — | `ACME_PROJECT_NAME` |
| `project.include` | list of globs | `["**"]` | `--include` | — |
| `remote_cache.url` | URL | *unset* | `--remote-cache` | `ACME_REMOTE_CACHE_URL` |
| `remote_cache.mode` | `"read-write"` \| `"read-only"` \| `"off"` | `"read-write"` | — | `ACME_REMOTE_CACHE_MODE` |
| `env.passthrough` | list of names or globs | `[]` | `--env-passthrough` | `ACME_ENV_PASSTHROUGH` |

## Top-level options

<!-- md:option cache_dir -->
### `cache_dir` { #cache-dir }

`cache_dir`
:   Directory where Acme stores task outputs, logs and the local metadata database.

    Relative paths are resolved against the directory that contains `acme.toml`, and `~` is
    expanded. Environment variables are **not** interpolated — use `ACME_CACHE_DIR` if you
    need that.

    ```toml
    cache_dir = "/mnt/fast-ssd/acme-cache"
    ```

    Default: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/acme`, falling back to `~/.cache/acme`; on macOS
    `~/Library/Caches/acme`; on Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\acme\cache`.

<!-- md:option parallelism -->
### `parallelism` { #parallelism }

`parallelism`
:   Maximum number of tasks that run at the same time. `0` means "one per logical CPU".

    Tasks marked `exclusive = true` always run alone, regardless of this value.

<!-- md:option log_level -->
### `log_level` { #log-level }

`log_level`
:   Verbosity of the console output. Each `-v` on the command line raises it by one step,
    each `-q` lowers it.
:   Per-module filters use the same syntax as `RUST_LOG`, e.g. `info,acme::cache=debug`.

## `[project]` { #project }

`name`
:   A human-readable name used in logs, the dashboard and remote-cache keys. Must match
    `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`.

`include`
:   Glob patterns, relative to the project root, of packages that belong to the workspace.

`exclude`
:   Patterns removed from the result of `include`, evaluated *after* it:

    ```toml
    include = ["apps/*", "packages/*", "tools/codegen"]
    exclude = ["packages/legacy-*"]
    ```

    Patterns use gitignore syntax: `*` doesn't cross directory boundaries, `**` does.

## `[remote_cache]` { #remote-cache }

!!! info "Optional"
    Without this section Acme only uses the local cache. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.

---
title: Configuration reference
description: Every option you can set in acme.toml, on the command line, or through environment variables.
---

# Configuration

Acme reads its settings from **`acme.toml`** in the project root (the first one found walking up
from the current directory). Every setting can also be passed on the command line or through an
environment variable. Precedence, from highest to lowest:

    CLI flag  >  environment variable  >  acme.toml  >  built-in default

That's the order you'd expect, with one twist: _list_ settings are **replaced**, not merged,
when they come from a higher-precedence source. Setting `ACME_ENV_PASSTHROUGH=CI` therefore
*removes* everything you listed in the file.

!!! danger "Breaking change in 3.0"

    The configuration file was renamed from `.acmerc` (YAML) to `acme.toml`. Acme 3.x still
    reads `.acmerc`, but prints a deprecation warning on every run, and support will be removed
    in 4.0. Convert your file with:

    ```console
    $ acme config migrate --from .acmerc --to acme.toml
    ✔ wrote acme.toml (14 settings, 2 renamed)
    ```

    !!! note "Comments are not migrated"

        TOML and YAML comments don't map one-to-one, so `config migrate` drops them.
        Keep the old file around until you've copied over anything important.

## Example

```toml title="acme.toml"
# acme.toml — shared by every package in this repo
cache_dir   = "~/.cache/acme"
parallelism = 0                 # 0 = one worker per CPU
log_level   = "info"

[project]
name    = "storefront"
include = ["apps/*", "packages/*"]
exclude = ["**/node_modules", "**/dist"]

[remote_cache]
url       = "https://cache.example.com/v1"
token_env = "ACME_CACHE_TOKEN"
mode      = "read-write"

[env]
passthrough = ["CI", "GITHUB_*", "NODE_OPTIONS"]
set         = { TZ = "UTC", LANG = "C.UTF-8" }
```

## Overview

| Option | Type | Default | CLI flag | Environment variable |
|:-------|:----:|:--------|:---------|:---------------------|
| `cache_dir` | path | platform cache dir | `--cache-dir` | `ACME_CACHE_DIR` |
| `parallelism` | integer ≥ 0 | `0` | `-j`, `--jobs` | `ACME_PARALLELISM` |
| `log_level` | `trace` \| `debug` \| `info` \| `warn` \| `error` | `info` | `-v` / `-q` | `ACME_LOG` |
| `project.name` | string | directory name | — | `ACME_PROJECT_NAME` |
| `project.include` | list of globs | `["**"]` | `--include` | — |
| `remote_cache.url` | URL | *unset* | `--remote-cache` | `ACME_REMOTE_CACHE_URL` |
| `remote_cache.mode` | `"read-write"` \| `"read-only"` \| `"off"` | `"read-write"` | — | `ACME_REMOTE_CACHE_MODE` |
| `env.passthrough` | list of names or globs | `[]` | `--env-passthrough` | `ACME_ENV_PASSTHROUGH` |

## Top-level options

<!-- md:option cache_dir -->
### `cache_dir` { #cache-dir }

`cache_dir`
:   Directory where Acme stores task outputs, logs and the local metadata database.

    Relative paths are resolved against the directory that contains `acme.toml`, and `~` is
    expanded. Environment variables are **not** interpolated — use `ACME_CACHE_DIR` if you
    need that.

    ```toml
    cache_dir = "/mnt/fast-ssd/acme-cache"
    ```

    Default: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/acme`, falling back to `~/.cache/acme`; on macOS
    `~/Library/Caches/acme`; on Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\acme\cache`.

<!-- md:option parallelism -->
### `parallelism` { #parallelism }

`parallelism`
:   Maximum number of tasks that run at the same time. `0` means "one per logical CPU".

    Tasks marked `exclusive = true` always run alone, regardless of this value.

<!-- md:option log_level -->
### `log_level` { #log-level }

`log_level`
:   Verbosity of the console output. Each `-v` on the command line raises it by one step,
    each `-q` lowers it.
:   Per-module filters use the same syntax as `RUST_LOG`, e.g. `info,acme::cache=debug`.

## `[project]` { #project }

`name`
:   A human-readable name used in logs, the dashboard and remote-cache keys. Must match
    `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`.

`include`
:   Glob patterns, relative to the project root, of packages that belong to the workspace.

`exclude`
:   Patterns removed from the result of `include`, evaluated *after* it:

    ```toml
    include = ["apps/*", "packages/*", "tools/codegen"]
    exclude = ["packages/legacy-*"]
    ```

    Patterns use gitignore syntax: `*` doesn't cross directory boundaries, `**` does.

!!! info "Optional"
    Without this section Acme only uses the local cache. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.

| Key | Required | Description |

| `url` | yes | Base URL of an Acme-compatible cache server (`https://` only, unless `allow_http = true`). |

`set`

**`ACME_CONFIG`**  
Path to a config file to use instead of searching for `acme.toml`.

**`ACME_NO_COLOR`** / **`NO_COLOR`**

arguments.content:
# docker-compose.yml -- local / staging stack for acme-shop
#
# Usage:
#   cp .env.example .env
#   docker compose up -d --build
#   docker compose exec web python manage.py createsuperuser
#
# NOTE: production runs on ECS, this file is NOT used there (see infra/ecs/*.json).
#       Keep service names stable, the nginx upstreams and .env.example rely on them.

name: acme-shop

x-app-defaults: &app-defaults
  restart: unless-stopped
  env_file: [.env]
  logging: &default-logging { driver: json-file, options: { max-size: "10m", max-file: '3' } }
  networks:
    - backend

x-healthcheck: &hc { interval: 10s, timeout: 5s, retries: 5, start_period: 30s }

x-django-image: &django-image
    image: ghcr.io/acme/acme-shop:${APP_VERSION:-latest}
    build:
        context: .
        dockerfile: docker/django/Dockerfile
        args:
            PYTHON_VERSION: 3.12
            POETRY_VERSION: "1.8.2"


services:

  nginx:
    image: nginx:1.25-alpine
    <<: *app-defaults
    depends_on:
      web:
        condition: service_healthy
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - 443:443
      - target: 8443
        published: 8443
        protocol: tcp
        mode: host
    volumes:
      - ./docker/nginx/conf.d:/etc/nginx/conf.d:ro
      - static:/var/www/static:ro
      - media:/var/www/media:ro
      - ./certs:/etc/nginx/certs:ro
    configs:
      - source: nginx_conf
        target: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
    networks:
    - frontend
    - backend

  web:
    <<: [*app-defaults, *django-image]
    command: >
      gunicorn acme_shop.wsgi:application
      --bind 0.0.0.0:8000
      --workers ${GUNICORN_WORKERS:-4}
      --timeout 120
      --access-logfile -
      --forwarded-allow-ips="*"
    environment:
      DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE: acme_shop.settings.docker
      DEBUG: "true"
      ENABLE_X: yes
      PORT: 8000
      SENTRY_DSN:
      SECRET_KEY: ${SECRET_KEY:?err}
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://acme:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-acme}@db:5432/acme
      CELERY_BROKER_URL: amqp://acme:${RABBITMQ_PASSWORD:-acme}@rabbitmq:5672//
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/1
      AWS_S3_ENDPOINT_URL: http://minio:9000
      EMAIL_URL: smtp://mailhog:1025
      ALLOWED_HOSTS: localhost,127.0.0.1,.acme.test
      DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_NUMBER_FIELDS: 1e4
      MAINTENANCE_WINDOW_START: 02:30
      AWS_PROFILE: ~
    labels:
      com.acme.description: "Django app server. Serves the storefront API and the
        admin; static files are served by nginx from the shared volume."
    expose:
      - "8000"
    healthcheck: { <<: *hc, test: ["CMD", "curl", "-fsS", "http://localhost:8000/healthz/"] }
    depends_on:
      db: { condition: service_healthy }
      redis:
        condition: service_started
      rabbitmq:
        condition: service_healthy
    volumes:
    - static:/app/static
    - media:/app/media
    secrets:
      - django_secret_key
    stdin_open: yes
    tty: TRUE
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
      resources:
        limits: { cpus: '0.50', memory: 512M }
        reservations:
          cpus: '0.25'
          memory: 256M
      update_config:
        parallelism: 1
        delay: 10s
        order: start-first


  worker:
    <<: [*app-defaults, *django-image]
    command:
      - celery
      - --app=acme_shop.celery:app
      - worker
      - --loglevel=INFO
      - --concurrency=${CELERY_CONCURRENCY:-4}
      - --queues=default,emails,thumbnails,exports
      - --max-tasks-per-child=200
      - --without-gossip
      - --without-mingle
    environment:
      - DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=acme_shop.settings.docker
      - C_FORCE_ROOT=false
      - DATABASE_URL=postgres://acme:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-acme}@db:5432/acme
      - CELERY_BROKER_URL=amqp://acme:${RABBITMQ_PASSWORD:-acme}@rabbitmq:5672//
    healthcheck:
      <<: *hc
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "celery -A acme_shop.celery:app inspect ping -d celery@$$HOSTNAME | grep -q pong"]
      interval: 60s
    depends_on: [db, rabbitmq, redis]
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits: {cpus: "1.0",memory: 1G}

  beat:
    <<: [*app-defaults, *django-image]
    command: [ "celery", "--app=acme_shop.celery:app", "beat",
               "--loglevel=INFO",
               "--scheduler=django_celery_beat.schedulers:DatabaseScheduler",
               "--pidfile=/tmp/celerybeat.pid" ]
    depends_on:
      - db
      - rabbitmq
    deploy:
      replicas: 1     # NEVER more than one beat, duplicate periodic tasks otherwise


  db:
    image: postgres:16.2-alpine
    <<: *app-defaults
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: acme
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-acme}
      POSTGRES_DB: acme
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
      POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: "--encoding=UTF8 --locale=C.UTF-8"
    healthcheck: { <<: *hc, test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"] }
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./docker/postgres/initdb.d:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    command: [
        "postgres",
        "-c", "max_connections=200",
        "-c", "shared_buffers=256MB",
        "-c", "log_min_duration_statement=500",
        "-c", "log_statement=ddl"
      ]
    shm_size: 256mb
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"   # localhost only, don't expose this on the staging box

  redis:
    image: redis:7.2-alpine
    <<: *app-defaults
    command: redis-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru --save 900 1 --save 300 10
    healthcheck:
      test: [ "CMD", "redis-cli", "ping" ]
      <<: *hc
    volumes: [ "redisdata:/data" ]

  rabbitmq:
    image: rabbitmq:3.13-management-alpine
    <<: *app-defaults
    hostname: rabbitmq    # rabbit stores its data per hostname, keep it fixed
    environment:
      RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER: acme
      RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS: ${RABBITMQ_PASSWORD:-acme}
      RABBITMQ_SERVER_ADDITIONAL_ERL_ARGS: "-rabbit log_levels [{connection,error},{default,warning}] disk_free_limit 2147483648 consumer_timeout 3600000"
    ports:
      - 15672:15672
    healthcheck:
      <<: *hc
      test: rabbitmq-diagnostics -q ping
      interval: 30s
    volumes:
      - rabbitdata:/var/lib/rabbitmq

  minio:
    image: quay.io/minio/minio:RELEASE.2024-04-18T19-09-19Z
    <<: *app-defaults
    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: acme
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:-acme-secret}
      MINIO_BROWSER_REDIRECT_URL: http://localhost:9001
    ports:
      - "9000:9000"
      - "9001:9001"
    volumes:
      - miniodata:/data
    healthcheck:
      <<: *hc
      test: ["CMD", "mc", "ready", "local"]

  # dev only, the staging box uses SES
  mailhog:
    image: mailhog/mailhog:v1.0.1
    logging: *default-logging
    ports: ["8025:8025"]
    networks: [backend]
    profiles: [dev]


volumes:
  pgdata:
  redisdata: {}
  rabbitdata:
  miniodata:
    driver: local
    driver_opts:
      type: none
      o: bind
      device: ${MINIO_DATA_DIR:-./data/minio}
  static:
  media:

networks:
  frontend:
  backend:
    driver: bridge
    ipam:
      driver: default
      config:
        - subnet: 172.28.0.0/16
          gateway: 172.28.0.1

secrets:
  django_secret_key:
    file: ./secrets/django_secret_key.txt
  postgres_password:
    environment: POSTGRES_PASSWORD

configs:
  nginx_conf:
    file: ./docker/nginx/nginx.conf

    command:
      - celery
      - --app=acme_shop.celery:app
      - worker
      - --loglevel=INFO
      - --concurrency=${CELERY_CONCURRENCY:-4}
      - --queues=default,emails,thumbnails,exports
      - --max-tasks-per-child=200
      - --without-gossip
      - --without-mingle
    environment:
      - DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=acme_shop.settings.docker
      - C_FORCE_ROOT=false
      - DATABASE_URL=postgres://acme:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-acme}@db:5432/acme
      - CELERY_BROKER_URL=amqp://acme:${RABBITMQ_PASSWORD:-acme}@rabbitmq:5672//
    healthcheck:
      <<: *hc
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "celery -A acme_shop.celery:app inspect ping -d celery@$$HOSTNAME | grep -q pong"]
      interval: 60s
    depends_on: [db, rabbitmq, redis]
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits: {cpus: "1.0",memory: 1G}

  beat:
    <<: [*app-defaults, *django-image]
    command: [ "celery", "--app=acme_shop.celery:app", "beat",
               "--loglevel=INFO",
               "--scheduler=django_celery_beat.schedulers:DatabaseScheduler",
               "--pidfile=/tmp/celerybeat.pid" ]
    depends_on:
      - db
      - rabbitmq
    deploy:
      replicas: 1     # NEVER more than one beat, duplicate periodic tasks otherwise


  db:
    image: postgres:16.2-alpine
    <<: *app-defaults
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: acme
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-acme}
      POSTGRES_DB: acme
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
      POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: "--encoding=UTF8 --locale=C.UTF-8"
    healthcheck: { <<: *hc, test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"] }
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./docker/postgres/initdb.d:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    command: [
        "postgres",
        "-c", "max_connections=200",
        "-c", "shared_buffers=256MB",
        "-c", "log_min_duration_statement=500",
        "-c", "log_statement=ddl"
      ]
    shm_size: 256mb
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"   # localhost only, don't expose this on the staging box

  redis:
    image: redis:7.2-alpine
    <<: *app-defaults
    command: redis-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru --save 900 1 --save 300 10
    healthcheck:
      test: [ "CMD", "redis-cli", "ping" ]
      <<: *hc
    volumes: [ "redisdata:/data" ]

  rabbitmq:
    image: rabbitmq:3.13-management-alpine
    <<: *app-defaults
    hostname: rabbitmq    # rabbit stores its data per hostname, keep it fixed
    environment:
      RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER: acme
      RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS: ${RABBITMQ_PASSWORD:-acme}
      RABBITMQ_SERVER_ADDITIONAL_ERL_ARGS: "-rabbit log_levels [{connection,error},{default,warning}] disk_free_limit 2147483648 consumer_timeout 3600000"
    ports:
      - 15672:15672
    healthcheck:
      <<: *hc
      test: rabbitmq-diagnostics -q ping
      interval: 30s
    volumes:
      - rabbitdata:/var/lib/rabbitmq

  minio:
    image: quay.io/minio/minio:RELEASE.2024-04-18T19-09-19Z
    <<: *app-defaults
    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: acme
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD:-acme-secret}
      MINIO_BROWSER_REDIRECT_URL: http://localhost:9001
    ports:
      - "9000:9000"
      - "9001:9001"
    volumes:
      - miniodata:/data
    healthcheck:
      <<: *hc
      test: ["CMD", "mc", "ready", "local"]

  # dev only, the staging box uses SES
  mailhog:
    image: mailhog/mailhog:v1.0.1
    logging: *default-logging
    ports: ["8025:8025"]
    networks: [backend]
    profiles: [dev]


volumes:

  rabbitdata:

We also wrote down the rules in a one-page cheat sheet that lives next to the migrations directory. It is the most-viewed page in our internal wiki, which says something about either the cheat sheet or the wiki.

## Anatomy of a migration today

Here’s what renaming `customers.zip` to `customers.postal_code` looks like now. It’s three pull requests spread over about a week, and every one of them is boring on purpose:

1) **Expand.** Add the new column, plus a trigger that keeps both columns in sync while old and new code run side by side:

   ```sql
   ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN postal_code text;

   CREATE FUNCTION customers_sync_postal_code() RETURNS trigger AS $$
   BEGIN
     NEW.postal_code := COALESCE(NEW.postal_code, NEW.zip);
     NEW.zip         := COALESCE(NEW.zip, NEW.postal_code);
     RETURN NEW;
   END $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
   ```

2) **Migrate.** Backfill in batches, deploy the code that reads `postal_code`, and watch the dashboards for a day or two.
3) **Contract.** Drop the trigger, then — one release later, once we’re _really_ sure nothing reads it any more — drop `zip`.

The runner config that enforces the guard rails is tiny:

```yaml
# migrations/runner.yaml
lock_timeout: 2s
statement_timeout: 15m
retries: { max: 5, jitter: true }
checks:
  - invalid_indexes
  - unvalidated_constraints
  - table_rewrites
```

arguments.content:
Relay architecture
==================

*Status: living document · Owners: @acme/messaging-platform · Last reviewed: 2024-06-03*

Relay is the service that delivers every notification Acme sends — transactional e-mail,
SMS, mobile push and in-app messages. Product teams call one HTTP API (or publish to one
Kafka topic) and Relay takes care of templating, user preferences, rate limiting, provider
failover and delivery tracking.
This page describes how the pieces fit together. It's aimed at engineers who are about to
change Relay, and at on-call people who need a mental model at 3 a.m.; if you only want to
*send* notifications, read the [integration guide][integration] instead.

Goals and non-goals
-------------------

Goals, roughly in priority order:

1. Never lose a message that the API acknowledged with `202 Accepted`.
2. Respect user preferences and legal requirements (opt-outs, quiet hours, the
   `security` category that can't be muted) *before* anything is sent.
3. Deliver 99 % of transactional messages within 30 seconds, end to end.
4. Make it boring for product teams: one API, one schema, no provider SDKs in their code.

Non-goals: marketing campaigns and bulk sends (that's [Broadcast](https://wiki.acme.internal/display/MKT/Broadcast+platform+overview?src=relay-docs#ownership)),
chat or conversational messaging, and guaranteeing *exactly-once* delivery — the providers simply don't offer it.

## High-level view

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Producers
        A[Product services] -->|POST /v2/messages| GW(API gateway)
        B[Batch jobs] -->|relay.requests.v2| K[(Kafka)]
    end
    GW --> ING[Ingest API]
    ING --> K
    K --> R{Router}
    R -->|email| EW[Email worker]
    R -->|sms| SW[SMS worker]
    R -->|push| PW[Push worker]
    EW --> SES[(Amazon SES)]
    EW -. failover .-> SG[(SendGrid)]
    SW --> TW[(Twilio)]
    PW --> FCM[(FCM / APNs)]
    R <--> PREF[(Preference store)]
    EW & SW & PW --> EV[(delivery_events)]
```

Relay runs active/active in two AWS regions. Each region has its own Kafka cluster and
Postgres primary; the preference store is replicated, everything else is regional, and a message is
processed entirely in the region that accepted it.

![Relay deployment across two regions](img/relay-regions.svg "Active/active in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1")

## Components

* **Ingest API** (`relay-ingest`, Go)
    * Validates requests against the JSON schema in `schemas/message.v2.json`.
    * Assigns a ULID message ID and writes the message to the `outbox` table in the same
      transaction as the idempotency key.
        * Idempotency keys are kept for 24 h; a duplicate request returns `200` with the original ID.
        * Payloads over 256 KiB are rejected with `413` — attachments go through pre-signed S3 URLs.
* **Router** (`relay-router`, Go)
    * Resolves the recipient's channels from the preference store and the message `category`.
    * Applies per-tenant and per-recipient rate limits (Redis, sliding window).
        * Quiet hours: non-urgent messages are delayed until 08:00 in the recipient's time zone.
        * Limits are configured per tenant in `config/tenants/*.yaml`.
* **Channel workers** (`relay-email`, `relay-sms`, `relay-push`, Kotlin)
    * Render the template, call the provider, record the result.
    * Each worker keeps one circuit breaker per provider, see [ADR-0011][adr-11].
        * E-mail fails over from SES to SendGrid after 5 consecutive 5xx responses or 30 s of timeouts.
        * SMS has no automatic failover: Twilio is the only provider with sender IDs in all our markets.
* **Template service** — a thin CRUD service in front of S3 and a Postgres index. Templates are
  versioned and immutable once published.
* **Webhook receiver** (`relay-webhooks`) — accepts bounces, receipts and opens from the providers.

## Life of a message

1. A producer calls `POST /v2/messages` with an `Idempotency-Key` header.
The Ingest API validates the payload and stores it in `outbox`, together with the key.
2. The outbox publisher — a goroutine inside the Ingest pods, leader-elected through a Postgres
advisory lock — publishes the message to `relay.requests.v2`, keyed by recipient ID so that
all messages for one person are processed in order.
3. The Router consumes it, checks preferences and rate limits, and emits one record per
   channel to `relay.deliveries.<channel>`. Suppressed messages are recorded with status
   `suppressed` and a reason code.
4. A channel worker renders the template, calls the provider and writes a `delivery_events`
   row with status `sent`, `failed` or `deferred`.
5. Provider webhooks (bounces, delivery receipts, opens) arrive at `relay-webhooks` and are
appended to `delivery_events` as well. Nothing is ever updated in place.[^append-only]

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant P as Producer
    participant I as Ingest API
    participant DB as Postgres (outbox)
    participant K as Kafka
    participant R as Router
    participant W as Email worker
    participant S as Amazon SES
    P->>I: POST /v2/messages (Idempotency-Key)
    I->>DB: INSERT outbox + idempotency_keys (one tx)
    I-->>P: 202 Accepted {id}
    DB-->>K: outbox publisher
    K->>R: relay.requests.v2
    R->>K: relay.deliveries.email
    K->>W: consume
    W->>S: SendEmail
    S-->>W: 200 MessageId
    W->>DB: INSERT delivery_events (sent)
```

## Why an outbox?

> From the original design doc, *"Relay v2: exactly-once-ish delivery"* (March 2022):
>
> > We can't make provider calls exactly-once, but we can make sure we never lose a
> > message we acknowledged. Writing to Postgres and to Kafka within one request, without
> > a transaction spanning both, is the root cause of every "missing e-mail" incident in 2021.
> >
> > > Counter-point from the review (@k.osei): the outbox adds a hop and a table that grows
> > > forever. → Resolved: the publisher deletes rows once Kafka has acknowledged them.
>
> The outbox costs ~4 ms of extra p50 latency on ingest, which nobody has ever noticed.

## Architecture decision records

| ADR | Title | Status | Date |
|----:|:------|:------:|:-----|
| [0004][adr-4] | Kafka instead of SQS for the request bus | Accepted | 2021-11-08 |
| [0007](adr/0007-ulid-message-ids.md) | ULIDs for message IDs | Accepted | 2022-02-14 |
| [0011][adr-11] | Per-provider circuit breakers in channel workers | Accepted | 2022-09-30 |
| [0013](adr/0013-template-engine.md) | Replace Mustache with Handlebars | Superseded by 0019 | 2023-01-17 |
| [0019](adr/0019-mjml-templates.md) | MJML for e-mail templates, compiled at publish time | Accepted | 2023-10-02 |
| 0021 | Move the preference store from DynamoDB to Postgres | *Proposed* | 2024-05-21 |

## Failure modes

What happens when things break, in short:

- **Kafka unavailable** — Ingest keeps accepting requests; they pile up in `outbox` (we alert at 50 000 rows).
- **Postgres primary down** — Ingest returns `503`; producers are expected to retry with the same idempotency key.
- **Provider outage** — the circuit breaker opens, messages are `deferred` and retried with back-off for up to 6 h, then marked `failed`.
- **Preference store unreachable** — the Router *fails closed*: nothing except `security` messages is sent.

For the runbooks behind each of these, see the on-call handbook at https://runbooks.acme.internal/relay/ (VPN required).

***

## Glossary

**Channel** — a delivery medium: `email`, `sms`, `push` or `in_app`.  
**Category** — product-defined type of message (`account`, `billing`, `security`, …) that drives preference checks.  
**Suppression** — a decision *not* to send, e.g. because of an opt-out or a hard bounce.\
**Tenant** — an Acme business unit with its own sender domains and quotas.  
**Outbox** — the `outbox` table, see [Why an outbox?](#why-an-outbox)

[^append-only]: `delivery_events` is partitioned by day and never updated. The current status of a
    message is computed by the `message_status` materialized view, refreshed every 30 seconds.

    This makes webhook processing trivially idempotent — receiving the same bounce twice just
    inserts a duplicate row that the view ignores — at the cost of ~40 GB of storage per month.

    We considered event-sourcing the whole message lifecycle (ADR-0016, rejected) but decided
    it wasn't worth the operational complexity.

raw_arguments.content:
Relay architecture
==================

*Status: living document · Owners: @acme/messaging-platform · Last reviewed: 2024-06-03*

Relay is the service that delivers every notification Acme sends — transactional e-mail,
SMS, mobile push and in-app messages. Product teams call one HTTP API (or publish to one
Kafka topic) and Relay takes care of templating, user preferences, rate limiting, provider
failover and delivery tracking.
This page describes how the pieces fit together. It's aimed at engineers who are about to
change Relay, and at on-call people who need a mental model at 3 a.m.; if you only want to
*send* notifications, read the [integration guide][integration] instead.

Goals and non-goals
-------------------

Goals, roughly in priority order:

1. Never lose a message that the API acknowledged with `202 Accepted`.
2. Respect user preferences and legal requirements (opt-outs, quiet hours, the
   `security` category that can't be muted) *before* anything is sent.
3. Deliver 99 % of transactional messages within 30 seconds, end to end.
4. Make it boring for product teams: one API, one schema, no provider SDKs in their code.

Non-goals: marketing campaigns and bulk sends (that's [Broadcast](https://wiki.acme.internal/display/MKT/Broadcast+platform+overview?src=relay-docs#ownership)),
chat or conversational messaging, and guaranteeing *exactly-once* delivery — the providers simply don't offer it.

## High-level view

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Producers
        A[Product services] -->|POST /v2/messages| GW(API gateway)
        B[Batch jobs] -->|relay.requests.v2| K[(Kafka)]
    end
    GW --> ING[Ingest API]
    ING --> K
    K --> R{Router}
    R -->|email| EW[Email worker]
    R -->|sms| SW[SMS worker]
    R -->|push| PW[Push worker]
    EW --> SES[(Amazon SES)]
    EW -. failover .-> SG[(SendGrid)]
    SW --> TW[(Twilio)]
    PW --> FCM[(FCM / APNs)]
    R <--> PREF[(Preference store)]
    EW & SW & PW --> EV[(delivery_events)]
```

Relay runs active/active in two AWS regions. Each region has its own Kafka cluster and
Postgres primary; the preference store is replicated, everything else is regional, and a message is
processed entirely in the region that accepted it.

![Relay deployment across two regions](img/relay-regions.svg "Active/active in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1")

## Components

* **Ingest API** (`relay-ingest`, Go)
    * Validates requests against the JSON schema in `schemas/message.v2.json`.
    * Assigns a ULID message ID and writes the message to the `outbox` table in the same
      transaction as the idempotency key.
        * Idempotency keys are kept for 24 h; a duplicate request returns `200` with the original ID.
        * Payloads over 256 KiB are rejected with `413` — attachments go through pre-signed S3 URLs.
* **Router** (`relay-router`, Go)
    * Resolves the recipient's channels from the preference store and the message `category`.
    * Applies per-tenant and per-recipient rate limits (Redis, sliding window).
        * Quiet hours: non-urgent messages are delayed until 08:00 in the recipient's time zone.
        * Limits are configured per tenant in `config/tenants/*.yaml`.
* **Channel workers** (`relay-email`, `relay-sms`, `relay-push`, Kotlin)
    * Render the template, call the provider, record the result.
    * Each worker keeps one circuit breaker per provider, see [ADR-0011][adr-11].
        * E-mail fails over from SES to SendGrid after 5 consecutive 5xx responses or 30 s of timeouts.
        * SMS has no automatic failover: Twilio is the only provider with sender IDs in all our markets.
* **Template service** — a thin CRUD service in front of S3 and a Postgres index. Templates are
  versioned and immutable once published.
* **Webhook receiver** (`relay-webhooks`) — accepts bounces, receipts and opens from the providers.

## Life of a message

1. A producer calls `POST /v2/messages` with an `Idempotency-Key` header.
The Ingest API validates the payload and stores it in `outbox`, together with the key.
2. The outbox publisher — a goroutine inside the Ingest pods, leader-elected through a Postgres
advisory lock — publishes the message to `relay.requests.v2`, keyed by recipient ID so that
all messages for one person are processed in order.
3. The Router consumes it, checks preferences and rate limits, and emits one record per
   channel to `relay.deliveries.<channel>`. Suppressed messages are recorded with status
   `suppressed` and a reason code.
4. A channel worker renders the template, calls the provider and writes a `delivery_events`
   row with status `sent`, `failed` or `deferred`.
5. Provider webhooks (bounces, delivery receipts, opens) arrive at `relay-webhooks` and are
appended to `delivery_events` as well. Nothing is ever updated in place.[^append-only]

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant P as Producer
    participant I as Ingest API
    participant DB as Postgres (outbox)
    participant K as Kafka
    participant R as Router
    participant W as Email worker
    participant S as Amazon SES
    P->>I: POST /v2/messages (Idempotency-Key)
    I->>DB: INSERT outbox + idempotency_keys (one tx)
    I-->>P: 202 Accepted {id}
    DB-->>K: outbox publisher
    K->>R: relay.requests.v2
    R->>K: relay.deliveries.email
    K->>W: consume
    W->>S: SendEmail
    S-->>W: 200 MessageId
    W->>DB: INSERT delivery_events (sent)
```

## Why an outbox?

> From the original design doc, *"Relay v2: exactly-once-ish delivery"* (March 2022):
>
> > We can't make provider calls exactly-once, but we can make sure we never lose a
> > message we acknowledged. Writing to Postgres and to Kafka within one request, without
> > a transaction spanning both, is the root cause of every "missing e-mail" incident in 2021.
> >
> > > Counter-point from the review (@k.osei): the outbox adds a hop and a table that grows
> > > forever. → Resolved: the publisher deletes rows once Kafka has acknowledged them.
>
> The outbox costs ~4 ms of extra p50 latency on ingest, which nobody has ever noticed.

## Architecture decision records

| ADR | Title | Status | Date |
|----:|:------|:------:|:-----|
| [0004][adr-4] | Kafka instead of SQS for the request bus | Accepted | 2021-11-08 |
| [0007](adr/0007-ulid-message-ids.md) | ULIDs for message IDs | Accepted | 2022-02-14 |
| [0011][adr-11] | Per-provider circuit breakers in channel workers | Accepted | 2022-09-30 |
| [0013](adr/0013-template-engine.md) | Replace Mustache with Handlebars | Superseded by 0019 | 2023-01-17 |
| [0019](adr/0019-mjml-templates.md) | MJML for e-mail templates, compiled at publish time | Accepted | 2023-10-02 |
| 0021 | Move the preference store from DynamoDB to Postgres | *Proposed* | 2024-05-21 |

## Failure modes

What happens when things break, in short:

- **Kafka unavailable** — Ingest keeps accepting requests; they pile up in `outbox` (we alert at 50 000 rows).
- **Postgres primary down** — Ingest returns `503`; producers are expected to retry with the same idempotency key.
- **Provider outage** — the circuit breaker opens, messages are `deferred` and retried with back-off for up to 6 h, then marked `failed`.
- **Preference store unreachable** — the Router *fails closed*: nothing except `security` messages is sent.

For the runbooks behind each of these, see the on-call handbook at https://runbooks.acme.internal/relay/ (VPN required).

***

## Glossary

**Channel** — a delivery medium: `email`, `sms`, `push` or `in_app`.  
**Category** — product-defined type of message (`account`, `billing`, `security`, …) that drives preference checks.  
**Suppression** — a decision *not* to send, e.g. because of an opt-out or a hard bounce.\
**Tenant** — an Acme business unit with its own sender domains and quotas.  
**Outbox** — the `outbox` table, see [Why an outbox?](#why-an-outbox)

[^append-only]: `delivery_events` is partitioned by day and never updated. The current status of a
    message is computed by the `message_status` materialized view, refreshed every 30 seconds.

    This makes webhook processing trivially idempotent — receiving the same bounce twice just
    inserts a duplicate row that the view ignores — at the cost of ~40 GB of storage per month.

    We considered event-sourcing the whole message lifecycle (ADR-0016, rejected) but decided
    it wasn't worth the operational complexity.

[integration]: https://docs.acme.internal/relay/integration-guide "Relay integration guide"
[adr-4]: adr/0004-kafka-request-bus.md
[adr-11]: adr/0011-circuit-breakers.md "ADR-0011: circuit breakers"
