--- title: Yamark body-classes: yamark-home toc: false --- ::: {.hero-shell} ::: {.hero-copy} ::: {.hero-kicker} ![](assets/favicon.svg){.hero-mark} :::

A fast formatter for YAML and Markdown.

Yamark formats whole files and embedded content with the consistency we expect from code, keeping source readable and changes easy to review. ::: {.hero-actions} [Install](usage.qmd#install){.hero-button .primary} [See examples](examples.qmd){.hero-button} ::: ::: {.hero-command} Run directly from PyPI `uvx yamark format` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.workflow-strip} ::: {.workflow-item} **Format** Rewrite supported files in place. ::: ::: {.workflow-item} **Check** Use non-mutating CI and diff modes. ::: ::: {.workflow-item} **Embed** Format marked Markdown in YAML, Python, or R. ::: ::: {.workflow-item} **Recurse** Format nested YAML and Markdown inside fenced blocks. ::: ::: ## A quick example A short Markdown file with YAML front matter - a native document format for LLM work. It combines software-readable structure with natural language for prompts, skills, reference documents, and generated output. The Before pane shows the unformatted source; the After pane shows what `yamark format` writes back. :::: {.before-after} ::: {.before-after-pane #demo-before} **Before** ```markdown --- title: Why YAML + Markdown? description: The source languages of LLM work - structured fields for tools alongside instructions, examples, and context for models. tags: [llm,authoring,formats] --- # Why YAML + Markdown? ## When LLMs become part of a software system, YAML and Markdown start to feel like programming languages. YAML defines named fields tools can act on; Markdown carries the instructions, examples, and context that shape model behavior. Together they create a shared source file that stays readable to people and models, exposes explicit structure to software, produces clear diffs, and renders directly. Where the combination shines: - Agent skills and prompt files keep names, versions, and tool metadata beside the instructions they describe. - The Markdown body can carry code samples and nested structures with their own syntax and indentation. - Reference documents stay readable to authors and models without a separate source format or build step. - Tool inputs and model outputs survive chat, Git, and documentation pipelines as recognizable text. - One source can render as HTML or PDF and travel unchanged as agent context. ``` ::: ::: {.before-after-pane} **After** ```markdown --- title: Why YAML + Markdown? description: >- The source languages of LLM work - structured fields for tools alongside instructions, examples, and context for models. tags: [llm, authoring, formats] --- # Why YAML + Markdown? When LLMs become part of a software system, YAML and Markdown start to feel like programming languages. YAML defines named fields tools can act on; Markdown carries the instructions, examples, and context that shape model behavior. Together they create a shared source file that stays readable to people and models, exposes explicit structure to software, produces clear diffs, and renders directly. Where the combination shines: - Agent skills and prompt files keep names, versions, and tool metadata beside the instructions they describe. - The Markdown body can carry code samples and nested structures with their own syntax and indentation. - Reference documents stay readable to authors and models without a separate source format or build step. - Tool inputs and model outputs survive chat, Git, and documentation pipelines as recognizable text. - One source can render as HTML or PDF and travel unchanged as agent context. ``` ::: :::: Toggle soft wrap on the Before pane to inspect the input's physical lines. Yamark wraps and indents each region according to its own grammar. ```{=html} ``` ## Performance **On the benchmark host (Apple M4 Max, macOS arm64), Yamark recorded the lowest elapsed time in all four workloads:** 79–89 ms for each generated 4 MB file and 133 ms for 500 generated YAML files (50 MB). ====== --- title: Configuration description: Discovery and the complete yamark.toml schema. --- Yamark discovers `yamark.toml` from each formatted file's directory upward. It uses only the nearest file; it does not merge ancestor configs. Pass `--config path/to/yamark.toml` to use one explicit file for every selected path instead. Unknown keys and invalid values are errors. The top-level tables are `[format]`, `[template]`, `[embedded]`, and `[paths]`. ## `[format]` ```toml [format] wrap = "sentence:88" compact = true markdown_horizontal_rule = "***" ``` | Key | Type and values | Effect when present | | --- | --- | --- | | `wrap` | String: `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:`, or a positive integer. | Sets Markdown wrapping. An explicit `--wrap` value overrides it. | | `table_widths` | String: `"fit"` or `"preserve"`. | Sizes Markdown table columns from their contents by default, or retains source widths. An explicit `--table-widths` overrides it; document settings and scoped directives override that base setting. | | `compact` | Boolean. | Enables or disables eligible YAML block-to-flow compaction. `--compact` still enables compact mode when this is `false`. | | `markdown_horizontal_rule` | String: `"---"` or `"***"`. | Chooses the marker Yamark emits for normalized Markdown horizontal rules. | See [Formatting settings](reference-options.qmd) for built-in defaults and the other surfaces that expose these behaviors. ## `[template]` Template delimiters mark regions Yamark must preserve because rendering can change the host language. The defaults are `{{ }}`, `{% %}`, `{# #}`, and `<% %>`. | Key | Type | Effect | | --- | --- | --- | | `add_delimiters` | Array of `{ open, close }` tables. | Appends to the delimiters active at this layer, after `replace_delimiters` if both keys are present. | | `replace_delimiters` | Array of `{ open, close }` tables. | Replaces the delimiters active at this layer before any additions. | Add a delimiter pair: ```toml [template] add_delimiters = [ { open = "<<", close = ">>" } ] ``` Replace the defaults: ```toml [template] replace_delimiters = [ { open = "[[", close = "]]" } ] ``` Every entry must contain non-empty `open` and `close` strings. In Markdown paragraphs and supported prose containers, including lists and blockquotes, a complete single-line expression is one opaque word. Yamark preserves every byte inside it and wraps the surrounding prose normally. For example, `{{ render("keep this") }}` can occupy its own line or exceed the requested width, just like a long word. Function calls, quoted arguments, escaped quotes, and nested braces are supported. A closing delimiter inside a single- or double-quoted argument does not end the expression. For `{#` / `#}` comments, the first literal `#}` ends the token; quotes, apostrophes, and braces inside have no special meaning. Yamark only recognizes boundaries; it does not interpret or evaluate template languages. Configured openers take precedence over Markdown inline syntax. When several pairs match an opener, the first complete closing boundary ends the token. File directives apply to earlier content too, including nested Markdown blocks. A template-only source line does not preserve placement. With `--wrap sentence`: ```markdown Before {{ render("keep this") }} after. ``` becomes: ```markdown Before {{ render("keep this") }} after. ``` Wrapping still respects explicit hard breaks, blank lines, and block boundaries. Use `fmt: skip`, `fmt: off`/`fmt: on`, or `fmt: skip file` to preserve layout. Multiline expressions, templates nested in Markdown links or emphasis, and otherwise unsupported Markdown blocks retain their existing preservation policy. Template settings do not change how Yamark handles headings, tables, host-language eligibility, or standalone shortcode tokens. ## `[embedded]` Each child table maps a directive or fence name to a formatter that reads stdin and writes stdout. It accepts exactly one key: the required `formatter` key. ```toml [embedded.python] formatter = "ruff" [embedded.r] formatter = "air" [embedded.sql] formatter = { command = ["sqlfmt", "--filename", "{path}"], path_suffix = ".sql" } ``` `formatter` accepts either a built-in shorthand or a custom formatter table. """csvtidy -- normalise messy CSV exports.

Usage::

    csvtidy input.csv -o output.csv --delimiter ';'
"""
import csv
import io
import sys
import unicodedata
from typing import Iterable, Iterator

# fmt: markdown
# # How csvtidy cleans a file
#
# The cleaning steps are applied in this order, and each one can be switched off with a `--no-<step>` flag:
#
# 1. **Decode**: the input is decoded as UTF-8; if that fails we fall back to cp1252, which is what Excel on Windows produces in most western European locales.
# 2. **Strip**: leading and trailing whitespace is removed from every cell
# 3. **Normalise** unicode to NFC so that `é` typed on a Mac and `é` pasted from a PDF compare equal
# 4. **Header fix-up**:
#     * lower-case
#     * spaces and dashes become `_`
#     * duplicate names get a numeric suffix (`amount`, `amount_2`, ...)
#
# Rows that are completely empty after stripping are dropped.  


STEPS = ("strip", "normalise", "headers")


def decode(raw: bytes) -> str:
    try:
        return raw.decode("utf-8-sig")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return raw.decode("cp1252")


def fix_headers(names: Iterable[str]) -> list[str]:
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
    out = []
    for name in names:
        key = name.strip().lower().replace(" ", "_").replace("-", "_") or "column"
        if key in seen:
            seen[key] += 1
            key = f"{key}_{seen[key]}"
        else:
            seen[key] = 1
        out.append(key)
    return out


def clean_rows(rows: Iterable[list[str]], steps: tuple[str, ...] = STEPS) -> Iterator[list[str]]:
    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
        if "strip" in steps:
            row = [cell.strip() for cell in row]
        if "normalise" in steps:
            row = [unicodedata.normalize("NFC", cell) for cell in row]
        if i == 0 and "headers" in steps:
            row = fix_headers(row)

## The data

We'll use the built-in `cars` dataset, which records the speed of cars (in mph) and the distances taken to stop (in ft). The data were recorded in the 1920s, i.e. they're about a century old, so don't use them to plan your commute. There are `r nrow(cars)` observations.

  hosts: payments_batch
  become: yes
  gather_facts: True
  serial: "25%"
  max_fail_percentage: 10
  any_errors_fatal: false

  vars:
      app_name: settlement-worker
      app_user: "svc_settle"
      app_group: 'payments'
      install_root: "/opt/{{ app_name }}"
      release_tag: "{{ lookup('env', 'RELEASE_TAG') | default('v4.18.2', true) }}"
      artifact_base: "https://artifacts.acme-corp.example/repository/payments-releases"
      artifact_url: "{{ artifact_base }}/{{ app_name }}/{{ release_tag }}/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_tag }}-linux-amd64.tar.gz"
      jvm_heap:   2g
      cutover_date: 2026-11-30
      legacy_cutover: "2025-03-01"
      settlement_windows: [ "01:00", "07:00", "13:00",  "19:00" ]
      supported_currencies: [EUR, GBP, USD, CHF, SEK, NOK, DKK, PLN, CZK, HUF, RON, BGN, JPY, AUD, CAD, SGD, HKD]
      feature_flags: {dual_write: true, async_ack: False, strict_iban: "yes", batch_size: 500, ledger_shadow_mode: off}
      drain_timeout_seconds: "300"
      retry_budget: ~
      maintenance_contact:
      common_env: &common_env
        TZ: UTC
        LANG: "en_US.UTF-8"
        JAVA_HOME: /usr/lib/jvm/temurin-21-jdk
        MALLOC_ARENA_MAX: "2"
      # fmt: table
      firewall_rules:
        - {port: 8443, proto: tcp, src: 10.40.0.0/16, comment: "settlement API via internal LB"}
        - {port: 9102,proto: tcp, src: 10.40.12.0/24, comment: prometheus}
        - {port: 5701, proto: tcp, src: 10.40.30.0/24,   comment: "hazelcast cluster"}

  pre_tasks:
  - name: Check the release tag looks like a version
    ansible.builtin.assert:
      that:
        - release_tag is match('^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$')
        - "app_name | length > 0"
      fail_msg: "release_tag '{{ release_tag }}' does not look like a semantic version, refusing to deploy {{ app_name }} to {{ inventory_hostname }}"
      quiet:  true
    run_once: yes

  - name: Drain node in the settlement scheduler
    ansible.builtin.uri:
      url: "https://scheduler.payments.internal/api/v1/nodes/{{ inventory_hostname }}/drain"
      method: POST
      headers: { Authorization: "Bearer {{ scheduler_token }}", Content-Type: application/json, X-Change-Ticket: "{{ change_ticket | default('CHG-UNSET') }}" }
      body_format: json
      body: {reason: "rolling deploy {{ release_tag }}", grace_seconds: 300}
      status_code: [200, 202, 204]
    delegate_to: localhost
    register: drain_result
    retries: 5
    delay: 10
    until: drain_result.status in [200, 202, 204]

  tasks:
    - name: Service account
      block:
          - name: Ensure group exists
            ansible.builtin.group: {name: "{{ app_group }}", gid: 2300, system: true}
          - name: Ensure user exists
            ansible.builtin.user:
                name: "{{ app_user }}"
                group: "{{ app_group }}"
                uid: 2301
                shell: /sbin/nologin
                home: "{{ install_root }}"
                create_home: no
                comment: "Settlement worker service account (managed by Ansible - manual edits will be reverted on the next run)"
      tags: [users,   bootstrap]

    - name: Open firewall ports
      ansible.posix.firewalld:
        port: "{{ item.port }}/{{ item.proto }}"
        source: "{{ item.src }}"
        permanent: true
        immediate: true
        state: enabled
      loop: "{{ firewall_rules }}"
      loop_control: {label: "{{ item.port }} {{ item.comment }}"}

    - name: Download release artifact
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "{{ artifact_url }}"
        dest: "/tmp/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_tag }}.tar.gz"
        checksum: "sha256:{{ artifact_url }}.sha256"
        mode: "0640"
        timeout: 60
      register: artifact
          # Nexus occasionally answers 502 while the nightly blob-store compaction runs
      retries: 3
      until: artifact is succeeded

    - name: Unpack release
      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
        src: "/tmp/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_tag }}.tar.gz"
        dest: '{{ install_root }}/releases/'
        remote_src: yes
        owner: "{{ app_user }}"
        group: "{{ app_group }}"
        creates: "{{ install_root }}/releases/{{ release_tag }}/bin/{{ app_name }}"

    - name: Render application config
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: "{{ install_root }}/shared/application.yml"
        owner: "{{ app_user }}"
        group: "{{ app_group }}"
        mode: '0600'
        content: |
          server:
            port: 8443
            ssl: {enabled: true, key-store: /etc/pki/settle/keystore.p12}
          settlement:
            windows: {{ settlement_windows | to_json }}
            currencies: {{ supported_currencies | join(',') }}
            batch-size: {{ feature_flags.batch_size }}
          ledger:
            url: jdbc:postgresql://ledger-db.payments.internal:5432/ledger?sslmode=verify-full
            pool-size:    20
      notify: restart settlement-worker

    - name: Install systemd unit
      ansible.builtin.template:
        src: templates/settlement-worker.service.j2
        dest: /etc/systemd/system/settlement-worker.service
        mode: "0644"
      vars:
        unit_environment:
          <<: *common_env
          JAVA_OPTS: "-Xms{{ jvm_heap }} -Xmx{{ jvm_heap }} -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200 -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -Dsettlement.cutover={{ cutover_date }}"
          SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE: prod,batch
      notify:
      - reload systemd
      - restart settlement-worker

    - name: Run database migrations (first host of the first batch only)
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: >
          {{ install_root }}/releases/{{ release_tag }}/bin/settlement-worker migrate
          --url jdbc:postgresql://ledger-db.payments.internal:5432/ledger
          --baseline-on-migrate
          --target {{ release_tag | regex_replace('^v', '') }}
        chdir: "{{ install_root }}/releases/{{ release_tag }}"
      run_once: true
      register: migrate_out
      changed_when: "'Successfully applied' in migrate_out.stdout"
      when:
        - inventory_hostname == ansible_play_hosts_all[0]
        - not (skip_migrations | default(false) | bool)

    - name: Point the current symlink at the new release
      ansible.builtin.file:
        src: "{{ install_root }}/releases/{{ release_tag }}"
        dest: "{{ install_root }}/current"
        state:     link
        force: true
      notify: restart settlement-worker

  post_tasks:
    - name: Flush handlers before undraining
      ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers
    - name: Undrain node
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: "https://scheduler.payments.internal/api/v1/nodes/{{ inventory_hostname }}/undrain"
        method: POST
        headers: {Authorization: "Bearer {{ scheduler_token }}"}
        status_code: 204
      delegate_to: localhost

  handlers:
      - name: reload systemd
        ansible.builtin.systemd: { daemon_reload: true }
      - name: restart settlement-worker
        ansible.builtin.systemd:
          name: settlement-worker
          state: restarted
          enabled: TRUE

- name: Verify and announce
  hosts: localhost
  connection: local
  gather_facts: false
  vars:
    teams_webhook: "{{ vault_teams_webhook_payments }}"
  tasks:
    - name: Smoke test readiness on every batch host
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: "https://{{ item }}:8443/actuator/health/readiness"
        validate_certs: false
        return_content: true
      loop: "{{ groups['payments_batch'] }}"
      register: health
      failed_when: health.json.status != 'UP'

    - name: Post release note to the payments channel
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: "{{ teams_webhook }}"
        method: POST
        body_format: json
        body:
          title: "settlement-worker {{ release_tag }} deployed"
          # fmt: markdown
          text: "**Release {{ release_tag }}** of _settlement-worker_ is live on {{ groups['payments_batch'] | length }} batch hosts. Migrations ran on the first host only and the scheduler drain/undrain cycle completed without manual intervention.\n\n* Change ticket: {{ change_ticket | default('n/a') }}\n* Rollback: see *Rolling back a settlement release* in the payments-platform runbook"
      when: not ansible_check_mode

arguments.content:
# Local development stack for the Shipment Tracking platform (logistics-core team).
#   everything:        docker compose --profile full up -d
#   infra only:        docker compose up -d postgres redis kafka kafka-init
#
# NOTE: these credentials are for your laptop only. Never copy them into a shared environment.
version: "3.9"
name: "shiptrack-dev"

x-logging: &default-logging
  driver: "json-file"
  options: { max-size: "10m", max-file: "3" }

x-service-defaults: &service-defaults
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *default-logging
    networks: [ backend ]
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"

x-tracking-env: &tracking-env
  SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE: "local"
  DB_HOST: postgres
  DB_PORT: "5432"
  KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS: 'kafka:9092'
  OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: http://otel-collector:4317
  OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES: "deployment.environment=local,service.namespace=logistics,team=logistics-core"

services:
  postgres:
    <<: *service-defaults
    image: postgres:16.4-alpine
    container_name: shiptrack-postgres
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: shiptrack
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "localdev-only"
      POSTGRES_DB:    tracking
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    ports: ["5432:5432"]
    volumes:
    - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    - ./infra/postgres/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U shiptrack -d tracking"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  redis:
    <<: *service-defaults
    image: "redis:7.2"
    command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes", "--maxmemory", "256mb", "--maxmemory-policy", "allkeys-lru"]
    ports:
      - '6379:6379'
    volumes: [redisdata:/data]

  kafka:
        <<: *service-defaults
        image: bitnami/kafka:3.7
        hostname: kafka
        ports:
            - "9092:9092"
            - "9094:9094"
        environment:
            - KAFKA_CFG_NODE_ID=0
            - KAFKA_CFG_PROCESS_ROLES=controller,broker
            - KAFKA_CFG_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093,EXTERNAL://:9094
            - KAFKA_CFG_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092,EXTERNAL://localhost:9094
            - KAFKA_CFG_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP=CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT,EXTERNAL:PLAINTEXT,PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT
            - KAFKA_CFG_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=0@kafka:9093
            - KAFKA_CFG_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES=CONTROLLER
            - KAFKA_CFG_AUTO_CREATE_TOPICS_ENABLE=false
        volumes:
            - kafkadata:/bitnami/kafka
        # fmt: compact
        ulimits:
            nofile:
                soft: 65536
                hard: 65536
        healthcheck:
          test: kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --list || exit 1
          interval: 10s
          retries: 12

  kafka-init:
    image: bitnami/kafka:3.7
    depends_on: { kafka: { condition: service_healthy } }
    networks: [backend]
    restart: "no"
    entrypoint: [ "/bin/bash", "-c" ]
    command: |
      set -euo pipefail
      for topic in shipment.events.v2 shipment.eta.v1 carrier.webhooks.raw depot.scans.v3; do
        kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --create --if-not-exists \
          --topic "$${topic}" --partitions 6 --replication-factor 1
      done
      echo "topics ready"

  tracking-api:
    <<: *service-defaults
    build:
      context: ./services/tracking-api
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.dev
      args: {JAVA_VERSION: "21", GRADLE_OPTS: "-Dorg.gradle.daemon=false -Dorg.gradle.caching=true"}
    image: shiptrack/tracking-api:dev
    profiles: ["full", api]
    environment:
      <<: *tracking-env
      SERVER_PORT: 8080
      MANAGEMENT_SERVER_PORT: 8081
      TRACKING_CARRIER_POLL_INTERVAL: PT30S
      TRACKING_WEBHOOK_SECRET:
      JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS: >-
        -agentlib:jdwp=transport=dt_socket,server=y,suspend=n,address=*:5005
        -XX:+UseZGC -Xmx768m
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
      - 127.0.0.1:5005:5005     # remote debugger, loopback only
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      kafka-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      redis: {condition: service_started}
    labels:
      com.acme.team: "logistics-core"
      com.acme.cost-center: '4410'
      "com.acme.oncall": "https://oncall.acme-corp.example/schedules/logistics-core"
    deploy: {resources: {limits: {cpus: '1.50', memory: 1g}, reservations: {memory: 512m}}}

  route-optimizer:
    <<: *service-defaults
    image: ${REGISTRY:-registry.acme-corp.example}/logistics/route-optimizer:${ROUTE_OPT_TAG:-latest}
    profiles: [full]
    environment:
      <<: *tracking-env
      SOLVER_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS: 20
      SOLVER_THREADS: ${SOLVER_THREADS:-4}
      OSRM_URL: "http://osrm:5000"
      # the optimizer only reads ETAs, it never writes
      KAFKA_CONSUMER_GROUP: "route-optimizer-local"
    depends_on: [postgres, osrm]

  osrm:
    image: osrm/osrm-backend:v5.27.1
    profiles: [ full ]
    command: osrm-routed --algorithm mld /data/germany-latest.osrm
    volumes:
      - ./infra/osrm:/data:ro
    networks: [backend]

  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.108.0
    command: ["--config=/etc/otelcol/config.yaml"]
    volumes: ["./infra/otel/config.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml:ro"]
    ports: [ "4317:4317", "4318:4318", "13133:13133", "55679:55679" ]
    networks:
      - backend

  mailpit:   # catches outbound customer notification e-mails (http://localhost:8025)
    image: axllent/mailpit:v1.20
    ports: ['8025:8025', '1025:1025']
    networks: [backend]
    environment:
      MP_MAX_MESSAGES: 5000
      MP_SMTP_AUTH_ACCEPT_ANY: 1
      MP_SMTP_AUTH_ALLOW_INSECURE: "true"

volumes:
  pgdata:
  redisdata:
  kafkadata: {}

networks:
  backend:
    driver: bridge
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 172.28.0.0/16
          gateway: "172.28.0.1"

# NOTE: these credentials are for your laptop only. Never copy them into a shared environment.
version: "3.9"
name: "shiptrack-dev"

x-logging: &default-logging
  driver: "json-file"
  options: { max-size: "10m", max-file: "3" }

x-service-defaults: &service-defaults
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *default-logging
    networks: [ backend ]
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"

x-tracking-env: &tracking-env
  SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE: "local"
  DB_HOST: postgres
  DB_PORT: "5432"
  KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS: 'kafka:9092'
  OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: http://otel-collector:4317
  OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES: "deployment.environment=local,service.namespace=logistics,team=logistics-core"

services:
  postgres:
    <<: *service-defaults
    image: postgres:16.4-alpine
    container_name: shiptrack-postgres
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: shiptrack
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "localdev-only"
      POSTGRES_DB:    tracking
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    ports: ["5432:5432"]
    volumes:
    - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    - ./infra/postgres/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U shiptrack -d tracking"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  redis:
    <<: *service-defaults
    image: "redis:7.2"
    command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes", "--maxmemory", "256mb", "--maxmemory-policy", "allkeys-lru"]
    ports:
      - '6379:6379'
    volumes: [redisdata:/data]

  kafka:
        <<: *service-defaults
        image: bitnami/kafka:3.7
        hostname: kafka
        ports:
            - "9092:9092"
            - "9094:9094"
        environment:
            - KAFKA_CFG_NODE_ID=0
            - KAFKA_CFG_PROCESS_ROLES=controller,broker
            - KAFKA_CFG_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093,EXTERNAL://:9094
            - KAFKA_CFG_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092,EXTERNAL://localhost:9094
            - KAFKA_CFG_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP=CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT,EXTERNAL:PLAINTEXT,PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT
            - KAFKA_CFG_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=0@kafka:9093
            - KAFKA_CFG_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES=CONTROLLER
            - KAFKA_CFG_AUTO_CREATE_TOPICS_ENABLE=false
        volumes:
            - kafkadata:/bitnami/kafka
        # fmt: compact
        ulimits:
            nofile:
                soft: 65536
                hard: 65536
        healthcheck:
          test: kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --list || exit 1
          interval: 10s
          retries: 12

  kafka-init:
    image: bitnami/kafka:3.7
    depends_on: { kafka: { condition: service_healthy } }
    networks: [backend]
    restart: "no"
    entrypoint: [ "/bin/bash", "-c" ]
    command: |
      set -euo pipefail
      for topic in shipment.events.v2 shipment.eta.v1 carrier.webhooks.raw depot.scans.v3; do
        kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --create --if-not-exists \
          --topic "$${topic}" --partitions 6 --replication-factor 1
      done
      echo "topics ready"

  tracking-api:
    <<: *service-defaults
    build:
      context: ./services/tracking-api
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.dev
      args: {JAVA_VERSION: "21", GRADLE_OPTS: "-Dorg.gradle.daemon=false -Dorg.gradle.caching=true"}
    image: shiptrack/tracking-api:dev
    profiles: ["full", api]
    environment:
      <<: *tracking-env
      SERVER_PORT: 8080
      MANAGEMENT_SERVER_PORT: 8081
      TRACKING_CARRIER_POLL_INTERVAL: PT30S
      TRACKING_WEBHOOK_SECRET:
      JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS: >-
        -agentlib:jdwp=transport=dt_socket,server=y,suspend=n,address=*:5005
        -XX:+UseZGC -Xmx768m
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
      - 127.0.0.1:5005:5005     # remote debugger, loopback only
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      kafka-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      redis: {condition: service_started}
    labels:
      com.acme.team: "logistics-core"
      com.acme.cost-center: '4410'
      "com.acme.oncall": "https://oncall.acme-corp.example/schedules/logistics-core"
    deploy: {resources: {limits: {cpus: '1.50', memory: 1g}, reservations: {memory: 512m}}}

  route-optimizer:
    <<: *service-defaults
    image: ${REGISTRY:-registry.acme-corp.example}/logistics/route-optimizer:${ROUTE_OPT_TAG:-latest}
    profiles: [full]
    environment:
      <<: *tracking-env
      SOLVER_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS: 20
      SOLVER_THREADS: ${SOLVER_THREADS:-4}
      OSRM_URL: "http://osrm:5000"
      # the optimizer only reads ETAs, it never writes
      KAFKA_CONSUMER_GROUP: "route-optimizer-local"
    depends_on: [postgres, osrm]

  osrm:
    image: osrm/osrm-backend:v5.27.1
    profiles: [ full ]
    command: osrm-routed --algorithm mld /data/germany-latest.osrm
    volumes:
      - ./infra/osrm:/data:ro
    networks: [backend]

  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.108.0
    command: ["--config=/etc/otelcol/config.yaml"]
    volumes: ["./infra/otel/config.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml:ro"]
    ports: [ "4317:4317", "4318:4318", "13133:13133", "55679:55679" ]
    networks:
      - backend

  mailpit:   # catches outbound customer notification e-mails (http://localhost:8025)
    image: axllent/mailpit:v1.20
    ports: ['8025:8025', '1025:1025']
    networks: [backend]
    environment:
      MP_MAX_MESSAGES: 5000
      MP_SMTP_AUTH_ACCEPT_ANY: 1
      MP_SMTP_AUTH_ALLOW_INSECURE: "true"

volumes:
  pgdata:
  redisdata:
  kafkadata: {}

networks:
  backend:
    driver: bridge
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 172.28.0.0/16
          gateway: "172.28.0.1"

# CI for the payments-gateway service.
# Runs lint + tests on every PR, builds and pushes an image from main/tags, and deploys release branches to staging.
name: "CI / payments-gateway"

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, 'release/**' ]
    tags: ["v*.*.*"]
    paths-ignore:
    - 'docs/**'
    - "**/*.md"
  pull_request:
    branches:    [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: "Target environment for a manual deploy (staging deploys run automatically from release branches; production additionally requires a CAB-approved change ticket)"
        type: choice
        options: [staging, production]
        default: 'staging'
      change_ticket:
        description: ServiceNow change number, e.g. CHG0041234
        required: false
        type: string
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * 1-5'   # weekday nightly run for the dependency scan

permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write, packages: write, security-events: write }

concurrency:
  group: '${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}'
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
  JAVA_VERSION: "21"
  GRADLE_OPTS: -Dorg.gradle.daemon=false -Dorg.gradle.parallel=true -Dorg.gradle.workers.max=4
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository_owner }}/payments-gateway
  PACT_BROKER_BASE_URL: "https://pact.payments.internal"
  TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED: "true"

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint & static analysis
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: {fetch-depth: 0}
      - &setup-java
        name: Set up JDK
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ env.JAVA_VERSION }}
          cache: gradle
      - name: Spotless, Checkstyle and Error Prone
        run: ./gradlew spotlessCheck checkstyleMain errorproneMain --no-daemon --stacktrace

  test:
    name: "Test (${{ matrix.suite }}, PG ${{ matrix.postgres }})"
    needs: lint
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 40
    strategy:
        fail-fast: false
        matrix:
            os: [ubuntu-24.04]
            suite: [unit, integration, contract]
            postgres: ["15", "16"]
            exclude:
                - suite: unit
                  postgres: "15"
            include:
                - {suite: integration, postgres: "16", os: ubuntu-24.04-arm, experimental: true}
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental == true }}
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:${{ matrix.postgres }}
        env: {POSTGRES_USER: gateway, POSTGRES_PASSWORD: gateway, POSTGRES_DB: gateway_test}
        ports: ['5432:5432']
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U gateway"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - *setup-java
      - name: Run ${{ matrix.suite }} tests
        run: |
          ./gradlew ${{ matrix.suite }}Test \
            -Pdb.url=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/gateway_test \
            -Pdb.user=gateway -Pdb.password=gateway
      - name: Upload test reports
        if: ${{ always() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: reports-${{ matrix.suite }}-pg${{ matrix.postgres }}
          path: |
            build/reports/tests/
            build/test-results/
          retention-days: 14
      - name: Publish pacts
        if: matrix.suite == 'contract' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        run: ./gradlew pactPublish -Ppact.consumer.version=${{ github.sha }} -Ppact.tag=${{ github.ref_name }}
        env:
          PACT_BROKER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PACT_BROKER_TOKEN }}

  build-image:
    needs: [test]
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      digest: ${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
    - uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    - id: meta
      uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
      with:
        images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        tags: |
          type=ref,event=branch
          type=semver,pattern={{version}}
          type=sha,format=long
    - id: push
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
      with:
        context: .
        push: true
        tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
        labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
        cache-from: type=gha
        cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
        build-args: |
          GIT_SHA=${{ github.sha }}
          BUILD_DATE=${{ github.event.head_commit.timestamp }}
        # SBOM + provenance are required by the PCI image policy
        sbom: true
        provenance: mode=max

  deploy-staging:
    needs: build-image
    if: ${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/release/') || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.environment == 'staging') }}
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, payments-deployer]
    environment:
      name: staging
      url: https://gateway.staging.payments.internal
    steps:
      - name: Assume deploy role
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::412398765001:role/payments-gateway-deployer
          aws-region: eu-central-1
          role-duration-seconds: 1800
      - name: Helm upgrade
        run: >
          helm upgrade --install payments-gateway ./deploy/helm/payments-gateway
          --namespace payments --atomic --timeout 10m
          --set image.digest=${{ needs.build-image.outputs.digest }}
          --set podAnnotations.changeTicket=${{ inputs.change_ticket || 'auto' }}
      - name: "Notify #payments-releases"
        if: always()
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1.27.0
        with:
          channel-id: 'C04PAYREL'
          slack-message: "payments-gateway ${{ github.ref_name }} → staging: ${{ job.status }} (<${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}|run>)"
        env:
          SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN }}

# inventory-sync: pushes WMS stock levels into the order-promising cache.
# Hand-rendered from the platform golden-path template v3 -- do NOT run helm against this file.
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: logistics-inventory
  labels:
    team: logistics-core
    "istio-injection": enabled
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: inventory-sync-config
  namespace: logistics-inventory
data:
  SYNC_INTERVAL: "PT2M"
  WMS_BASE_URL: https://wms-gateway.logistics.internal/api/v4
  MAX_PARALLEL_DEPOTS: "12"
  FEATURE_PARTIAL_PALLETS: 'true'
  application.yaml: |
    inventory:
      depots: [DE-HAM-01, DE-MUC-02, NL-AMS-01, PL-WAW-03]
      reconcile:
        tolerance-units: 2
        quarantine-on-mismatch: true
    management:
      endpoints.web.exposure.include: health,info,prometheus
  logback.xml: |-
    <configuration>
      <appender name="JSON" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">
        <encoder class="net.logstash.logback.encoder.LogstashEncoder"/>
      </appender>
      <root level="INFO"><appender-ref ref="JSON"/></root>
    </configuration>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: inventory-sync
  namespace: logistics-inventory
  labels: &labels
    app.kubernetes.io/name: inventory-sync
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: order-promising
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: "platform-golden-path"
  annotations:
    platform.acme-corp.example/owner: "logistics-core@acme-corp.example"
    platform.acme-corp.example/runbook: https://wiki.acme-corp.example/display/LOG/inventory-sync+runbook
    platform.acme-corp.example/description: "Pulls stock snapshots from every regional WMS instance, reconciles them against the order-promising cache and publishes corrections to Kafka."
spec:
  replicas: 3
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate: {maxSurge: 1, maxUnavailable: 0}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: inventory-sync
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: *labels
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
        prometheus.io/port: "9102"
        prometheus.io/path: /actuator/prometheus
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: inventory-sync
      securityContext: { runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 10001, fsGroup: 10001, seccompProfile: { type: RuntimeDefault } }
      # fmt: off
      tolerations:
        - { key: "dedicated",  operator: "Equal",  value: "logistics", effect: "NoSchedule" }
        - { key: "spot",       operator: "Exists",                     effect: "NoSchedule" }
      # fmt: on
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: inventory-sync}
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: "registry.acme-corp.example/logistics/inventory-sync:2.14.0"
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          args: ["--spring.config.additional-location=file:/config/application.yaml", "--server.shutdown=graceful"]
          ports:
            - {name: http, containerPort: 8080}
            - {name: metrics, containerPort: 9102, protocol: TCP}
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef: {name: inventory-sync-config}
          env:
            - name: JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
              value: "-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 -XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError"
            - name: WMS_API_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: inventory-sync-secrets
                  key:  wms-api-token
            - name: POD_NAME
              valueFrom: {fieldRef: {fieldPath: metadata.name}}
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 250m, memory: 768Mi}
            limits:
              memory: 1Gi
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /actuator/health/readiness, port: http}
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /actuator/health/liveness
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 45
            failureThreshold: 3
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities: {drop: ["ALL"]}
          volumeMounts:
          - name: config
            mountPath: /config
            readOnly: true
          - {name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}
      volumes:
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: inventory-sync-config

# inventory-sync: pushes WMS stock levels into the order-promising cache.
# Hand-rendered from the platform golden-path template v3 -- do NOT run helm against this file.
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: logistics-inventory
  labels:
    team: logistics-core
    "istio-injection": enabled
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: inventory-sync-config
  namespace: logistics-inventory
data:
  SYNC_INTERVAL: "PT2M"
  WMS_BASE_URL: https://wms-gateway.logistics.internal/api/v4
  MAX_PARALLEL_DEPOTS: "12"
  FEATURE_PARTIAL_PALLETS: 'true'
  application.yaml: |
    inventory:
      depots: [DE-HAM-01, DE-MUC-02, NL-AMS-01, PL-WAW-03]
      reconcile:
        tolerance-units: 2
        quarantine-on-mismatch: true
    management:
      endpoints.web.exposure.include: health,info,prometheus
  logback.xml: |-
    <configuration>
      <appender name="JSON" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">
        <encoder class="net.logstash.logback.encoder.LogstashEncoder"/>
      </appender>
      <root level="INFO"><appender-ref ref="JSON"/></root>
    </configuration>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: inventory-sync
  namespace: logistics-inventory
  labels: &labels
    app.kubernetes.io/name: inventory-sync
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: order-promising
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: "platform-golden-path"
  annotations:
    platform.acme-corp.example/owner: "logistics-core@acme-corp.example"
    platform.acme-corp.example/runbook: https://wiki.acme-corp.example/display/LOG/inventory-sync+runbook
    platform.acme-corp.example/description: "Pulls stock snapshots from every regional WMS instance, reconciles them against the order-promising cache and publishes corrections to Kafka."
spec:
  replicas: 3
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate: {maxSurge: 1, maxUnavailable: 0}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: inventory-sync
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: *labels
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
        prometheus.io/port: "9102"
        prometheus.io/path: /actuator/prometheus
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: inventory-sync
      securityContext: { runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 10001, fsGroup: 10001, seccompProfile: { type: RuntimeDefault } }
      # fmt: off
      tolerations:
        - { key: "dedicated",  operator: "Equal",  value: "logistics", effect: "NoSchedule" }
        - { key: "spot",       operator: "Exists",                     effect: "NoSchedule" }
      # fmt: on
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: inventory-sync}
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: "registry.acme-corp.example/logistics/inventory-sync:2.14.0"
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          args: ["--spring.config.additional-location=file:/config/application.yaml", "--server.shutdown=graceful"]
          ports:
            - {name: http, containerPort: 8080}
            - {name: metrics, containerPort: 9102, protocol: TCP}
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef: {name: inventory-sync-config}
          env:
            - name: JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
              value: "-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 -XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError"
            - name: WMS_API_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: inventory-sync-secrets
                  key:  wms-api-token
            - name: POD_NAME
              valueFrom: {fieldRef: {fieldPath: metadata.name}}
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 250m, memory: 768Mi}
            limits:
              memory: 1Gi
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /actuator/health/readiness, port: http}
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /actuator/health/liveness
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 45
            failureThreshold: 3
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities: {drop: ["ALL"]}
          volumeMounts:
          - name: config
            mountPath: /config
            readOnly: true
          - {name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}
      volumes:
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: inventory-sync-config
            items: [{key: application.yaml, path: application.yaml}, {key: logback.xml, path: logback.xml}]
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir: {}
---

openapi: "3.1.0"
info:
  title: Acme Payments - Refunds & Payouts API
  version: '2.7.0'
  contact: {name: Payments API Guild, email: api-guild@acme-corp.example, url: "https://dev.acme-corp.example/payments"}
  license:
    name: Proprietary
    identifier: LicenseRef-Acme-Internal
  # fmt: markdown
  description: |
    The **Refunds & Payouts API** lets internal product teams initiate refunds against captured payments and schedule payouts to merchant bank accounts.  All amounts are expressed in _minor units_ (cents, pence, ...) and every mutating request __must__ carry an `Idempotency-Key` header.
    ## Conventions ##
    * Timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC.
    * Monetary amounts are integers in minor units; the currency is an ISO 4217 alpha-3 code.
    + Errors follow [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457 "Problem Details for HTTP APIs") problem details.
    ## Rate limits
    | Tier | Requests/min | Burst |
    |---|---:|--:|
    | internal-standard | 600 | 100 |
    | internal-batch | 3000 | 500 |

    Questions? Ask in `#payments-api` or open a ticket in the PAYAPI Jira project.
servers:
  - url: https://api.{region}.payments.internal/v2
    description: Internal production
    variables:
      region:
        default: eu
        enum: [eu, us, apac]
  - url: 'https://api.sandbox.payments.internal/v2'
    description: Sandbox (synthetic data, reset nightly at 02:00 UTC)
security:
  - oauth2: [ "refunds:write", "payouts:write" ]
  - mtls: []
tags:
- name: Refunds
  description: Return funds to the original payment instrument.
- name: Payouts
  description: "Move settled funds to a merchant's bank account."
paths:
  /refunds:
    post:
      tags: [Refunds]
      operationId: createRefund
      summary: Create a refund
      description: Creates a full or partial refund for a captured payment. Partial refunds may be issued repeatedly until the captured amount is exhausted; the API rejects any refund that would exceed it with `422`.
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/IdempotencyKey'
        - { name: X-Request-Origin, in: header, required: false, schema: { type: string, enum: [checkout, backoffice, dispute-automation] } }
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: "#/components/schemas/RefundRequest" }
            examples:
              partial:
                summary: Partial refund of a card payment
                value: {payment_id: pay_01J9Z3K4X8, amount: 1250, currency: EUR, reason: customer_request}
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Refund accepted
          headers:
            Location: {schema: {type: string, format: uri}}
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Refund'}
        "409": {$ref: '#/components/responses/Conflict'}
        422:
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unprocessable"
        default: {$ref: '#/components/responses/Problem'}
    get:
      tags: [ Refunds ]
      operationId: listRefunds
      summary: List refunds
      parameters:
        - name: payment_id
          in: query
          schema: {type: string, pattern: '^pay_[0-9A-Z]{10}$'}
        - name: created_after
          in: query
          schema: { type: string, format: date-time }
          example: 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/PageCursor"
        - {$ref: '#/components/parameters/PageSize'}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: A page of refunds
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [data, has_more]
                properties:
                  data: {type: array, items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Refund'}}
                  has_more: {type: boolean}
                  next_cursor: {type: [string, "null"]}
  /payouts/{payout_id}:
    parameters:
      - name: payout_id
        in: path
        required: true

    ## Conventions ##
    * Timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC.
    * Monetary amounts are integers in minor units; the currency is an ISO 4217 alpha-3 code.
    + Errors follow [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457 "Problem Details for HTTP APIs") problem details.
    ## Rate limits
    | Tier | Requests/min | Burst |

---
# Playbook for the EcoGen lab analysis server (ecogen-01.bio.example.edu)
#   * installs R + RStudio Server, Miniforge and the usual bioinformatics tools
#   * creates accounts for everyone in the lab
#   * mounts the sequencing share READ ONLY (we learned that one the hard way)
#
# Usage:   ansible-playbook -i inventory/lab.ini ecogen.yml -K
# Last touched by Tomás, 2024-02-12 -- ask in #computing before editing the user list!

- name:   "Configure EcoGen analysis server"
  hosts: analysis
  become: yes
  gather_facts: True
  vars:
      r_version: "4.3.2"
      rstudio_deb: 'rstudio-server-2023.12.1-402-amd64.deb'
      miniforge_prefix: /opt/miniforge3
      seq_mount: "/mnt/seqdata"
      nfs_server: 10.12.0.15
      lab_group: ecogen
      lab_gid: 2001
      proxy_url:            # only needed on the old campus network
      last_reviewed: 2024-02-12
      lab_members:
        - { name: tdiaz, fullname: "Tomás Díaz", shell: /bin/bash, admin: true }
        - {name: mokafor, fullname: "Miriam Okafor",shell: /bin/zsh, admin: false}
        - name: jlindqvist
          fullname: Johan Lindqvist
          shell: /bin/bash
          admin: no
        - {name: msc2024, fullname: 'MSc student (2024 intake)', shell: /bin/bash, admin: false}
      apt_packages: [build-essential, gfortran, libcurl4-openssl-dev, libssl-dev, libxml2-dev, libgdal-dev, libgeos-dev, libproj-dev, libudunits2-dev, cmake, git, htop, tmux, parallel, pigz]
      r_packages: ["tidyverse", "sf", "terra", "vegan", "lme4", "glmmTMB", 'DHARMa', "phyloseq", "BiocManager"]
      bioinfo_env:
        name: bioinfo
        channels: [conda-forge, bioconda]
        packages:
        - samtools=1.19
        - bwa
        - fastp
        - multiqc
        - 'bcftools>=1.18'
        - vsearch        # 16S amplicon stuff (Miriam)
        - cutadapt

  pre_tasks:
    - name: Refresh apt cache
      apt:
        update_cache: yes
        cache_valid_time: 3600

    - name: Use the campus proxy for apt
      copy:
        dest: /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/95proxy
        content: |
          Acquire::http::Proxy "{{ proxy_url }}";
          Acquire::https::Proxy "{{ proxy_url }}";
        mode: 0644
      when: proxy_url is not none and proxy_url | length > 0

  tasks:
  - name: Install system libraries (needed for sf, terra, xml2, curl ...)
    apt:
      name: "{{ apt_packages }}"
      state: present
      install_recommends: no

  - name: Create the lab group
    group:
        name: "{{ lab_group }}"
        gid: "{{ lab_gid }}"
        state: present

  - name: Create user accounts
    user:
      name: "{{ item.name }}"
      comment: "{{ item.fullname }}"
      shell: "{{ item.shell }}"
      groups: "{{ lab_group }}{{ ',sudo' if item.admin else '' }}"
      append: yes
      create_home: true
    loop: "{{ lab_members }}"
    loop_control: {label: "{{ item.name }}"}

  - name: Remember who is in the group (used by the quota report)
    set_fact:
      "{{ lab_group }}_usernames": "{{ lab_members | map(attribute='name') | list }}"

        # the export is read-only for us anyway, but mount it ro as well so nobody
        # writes intermediate files next to the raw reads again (looking at you, 2022)
  - name: Mount NFS shares
    mount:
      path: "{{ item.path }}"
      src: "{{ item.src }}"
      fstype: nfs
      opts: "{{ item.opts }}"
      state: mounted
    loop:
      - &seq_share
        path: "{{ seq_mount }}"
        src: "{{ nfs_server }}:/export/sequencing"
        opts: ro,hard,intr,noatime
      - <<: *seq_share
        path: /mnt/projects
        src: "{{ nfs_server }}:/export/projects"
        opts: "rw,hard,intr,noatime"

  - name: Install R from the CRAN apt repository
    when: ansible_distribution == "Ubuntu"
    block:
      - name: Add CRAN signing key
        apt_key:
          url: https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu/marutter_pubkey.asc
          state: present
      - name: Add CRAN repo
        apt_repository:
          repo: "deb https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu {{ ansible_distribution_release }}-cran40/"
          state: present
      - name: Install r-base
        apt: {name: "r-base={{ r_version }}*", state: present}

  - name: Install RStudio Server
    apt:
      deb: "https://download2.rstudio.org/server/jammy/amd64/{{ rstudio_deb }}"
    notify: restart rstudio

  - name: RStudio Server config
    copy:
      dest: /etc/rstudio/rserver.conf
      content: |
        # managed by ansible -- local edits will be overwritten!
        www-port=8787
        auth-required-user-group={{ lab_group }}
        session-timeout-minutes=0
      owner: root
      mode: '0644'
    notify: restart rstudio

  # slow!! ~25 min the first time because sf/terra compile from source
  - name: Install R packages site-wide
    command: >
      Rscript -e 'install.packages(c({{ r_packages | map("to_json") | join(", ") }}),
      repos = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/jammy/latest",
      Ncpus = {{ ansible_processor_vcpus }})'
    args:
      creates: /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/vegan

  - name: Install Miniforge
    shell: |-
      set -euo pipefail
      curl -fsSL -o /tmp/miniforge.sh https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge/releases/latest/download/Miniforge3-Linux-x86_64.sh
      bash /tmp/miniforge.sh -b -p {{ miniforge_prefix }}
      rm -f /tmp/miniforge.sh
    args:
      creates: "{{ miniforge_prefix }}/bin/mamba"
      executable: /bin/bash

  - name: Create the shared bioinformatics environment
    command: "{{ miniforge_prefix }}/bin/mamba create -y -n {{ bioinfo_env.name }} {{ bioinfo_env.channels | map('regex_replace', '^', '-c ') | join(' ') }} {{ bioinfo_env.packages | join(' ') }}"
    args:
      creates: "{{ miniforge_prefix }}/envs/{{ bioinfo_env.name }}"

  - name: Message of the day
    copy:
      dest: /etc/motd
      content: >+
        Welcome to ecogen-01. Raw reads live in /mnt/seqdata (read only).
        Please run big jobs with `nice` and keep your home directory under 200 GB.
        Questions go to #computing on Slack.

      mode: "0644"

  handlers:
    - name: restart rstudio
      service: {name: rstudio-server, state: restarted}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
- name: Nightly backup of home directories
  hosts: analysis
  become: true
  vars:
    backup_hour: '2'
    backup_target: "backup@nas02.bio.example.edu:/volume1/ecogen"
    rsync_excludes:   [".cache", ".local/share/Trash", "*.bam", "*.fastq.gz", ".conda/pkgs"]
  tasks:
    - name: Install rsync
      apt:  name=rsync state=present
    - name: Schedule nightly rsync
      cron:
        name: "nightly home backup"
        minute: "15"
        hour: "{{ backup_hour }}"
        job: "rsync -a --delete {{ rsync_excludes | map('regex_replace', '^(.*)$', '--exclude=\\1') | join(' ') }} /home/ {{ backup_target }}/home/ >> /var/log/home-backup.log 2>&1"
        user: root
      tags:
      - backup
      - cron

        mode: 0644
      when: proxy_url is not none and proxy_url | length > 0

  tasks:
  - name: Install system libraries (needed for sf, terra, xml2, curl ...)
    apt:
      name: "{{ apt_packages }}"
      state: present
      install_recommends: no

  - name: Create the lab group
    group:
        name: "{{ lab_group }}"
        gid: "{{ lab_gid }}"
        state: present

  - name: Create user accounts
    user:
      name: "{{ item.name }}"
      comment: "{{ item.fullname }}"
      shell: "{{ item.shell }}"
      groups: "{{ lab_group }}{{ ',sudo' if item.admin else '' }}"
      append: yes
      create_home: true
    loop: "{{ lab_members }}"
    loop_control: {label: "{{ item.name }}"}

  - name: Remember who is in the group (used by the quota report)
    set_fact:
      "{{ lab_group }}_usernames": "{{ lab_members | map(attribute='name') | list }}"

        # the export is read-only for us anyway, but mount it ro as well so nobody
        # writes intermediate files next to the raw reads again (looking at you, 2022)
  - name: Mount NFS shares
    mount:
      path: "{{ item.path }}"
      src: "{{ item.src }}"
      fstype: nfs
      opts: "{{ item.opts }}"
      state: mounted
    loop:
      - &seq_share
        path: "{{ seq_mount }}"
        src: "{{ nfs_server }}:/export/sequencing"
        opts: ro,hard,intr,noatime
      - <<: *seq_share
        path: /mnt/projects
        src: "{{ nfs_server }}:/export/projects"
        opts: "rw,hard,intr,noatime"

  - name: Install R from the CRAN apt repository
    when: ansible_distribution == "Ubuntu"
    block:
      - name: Add CRAN signing key
        apt_key:
          url: https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu/marutter_pubkey.asc
          state: present
      - name: Add CRAN repo
        apt_repository:
          repo: "deb https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu {{ ansible_distribution_release }}-cran40/"
          state: present
      - name: Install r-base
        apt: {name: "r-base={{ r_version }}*", state: present}

  - name: Install RStudio Server
    apt:
      deb: "https://download2.rstudio.org/server/jammy/amd64/{{ rstudio_deb }}"
    notify: restart rstudio

  - name: RStudio Server config
    copy:
      dest: /etc/rstudio/rserver.conf
      content: |
        # managed by ansible -- local edits will be overwritten!
        www-port=8787
        auth-required-user-group={{ lab_group }}
        session-timeout-minutes=0
      owner: root
      mode: '0644'
    notify: restart rstudio

  # slow!! ~25 min the first time because sf/terra compile from source
  - name: Install R packages site-wide
    command: >
      Rscript -e 'install.packages(c({{ r_packages | map("to_json") | join(", ") }}),
      repos = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/jammy/latest",
      Ncpus = {{ ansible_processor_vcpus }})'
    args:
      creates: /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/vegan

  - name: Install Miniforge
    shell: |-
      set -euo pipefail
      curl -fsSL -o /tmp/miniforge.sh https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge/releases/latest/download/Miniforge3-Linux-x86_64.sh
      bash /tmp/miniforge.sh -b -p {{ miniforge_prefix }}
      rm -f /tmp/miniforge.sh
    args:
      creates: "{{ miniforge_prefix }}/bin/mamba"
      executable: /bin/bash

  - name: Create the shared bioinformatics environment
    command: "{{ miniforge_prefix }}/bin/mamba create -y -n {{ bioinfo_env.name }} {{ bioinfo_env.channels | map('regex_replace', '^', '-c ') | join(' ') }} {{ bioinfo_env.packages | join(' ') }}"
    args:
      creates: "{{ miniforge_prefix }}/envs/{{ bioinfo_env.name }}"

  - name: Message of the day
    copy:
      dest: /etc/motd
      content: >+
        Welcome to ecogen-01. Raw reads live in /mnt/seqdata (read only).
        Please run big jobs with `nice` and keep your home directory under 200 GB.
        Questions go to #computing on Slack.

      mode: "0644"

  handlers:
    - name: restart rstudio
      service: {name: rstudio-server, state: restarted}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
- name: Nightly backup of home directories
  hosts: analysis
  become: true
  vars:
    backup_hour: '2'
    backup_target: "backup@nas02.bio.example.edu:/volume1/ecogen"
    rsync_excludes:   [".cache", ".local/share/Trash", "*.bam", "*.fastq.gz", ".conda/pkgs"]
  tasks:
    - name: Install rsync
      apt:  name=rsync state=present
    - name: Schedule nightly rsync
      cron:
        name: "nightly home backup"
        minute: "15"
        hour: "{{ backup_hour }}"
        job: "rsync -a --delete {{ rsync_excludes | map('regex_replace', '^(.*)$', '--exclude=\\1') | join(' ') }} /home/ {{ backup_target }}/home/ >> /var/log/home-backup.log 2>&1"
        user: root
      tags:
      - backup
      - cron

#

#   ansible-playbook -i inventory/hosts.ini site.yml --ask-vault-pass

# boxes: pi-01, pi-02 (pi 4, 4GB), pi-03 (3B+, the slow one), nuc (docker host)
# last big change: rebuilt pi-02 after its SD card died. again.

- name: base setup for every box
  hosts: all
  become:   yes
  gather_facts: True
  vars:
    timezone: "Europe/Amsterdam"
    admin_user: "{{ ansible_user }}"
    ssh_port:    22
    swap_size_mb: "1024"
    last_reviewed: 2024-03-09
    common_packages: &pkgs [vim, htop, tmux, git, curl, ncdu, "dnsutils", rsync, unattended-upgrades, apt-transport-https, 'lm-sensors']
    # overridden in host_vars/nuc.yml
    docker_users:
    - "{{ ansible_user }}"
    - 'backup'

  pre_tasks:
      - name: refresh apt cache if it is older than an hour
        apt:
            update_cache: yes
            cache_valid_time: 3600
        changed_when: False
        tags: [always]

  tasks:
    - name: install the usual suspects
      apt:
        name: *pkgs
        state: present
      tags: ['packages']

    - name: set timezone
      community.general.timezone:
        name: "{{ timezone }}"

    - name: hostname matches the inventory name
      hostname: {name: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"}

    - name: drop my dotfiles in
      copy:
        src: "files/dotfiles/{{ item }}"
        dest: /home/{{ admin_user }}/.{{ item }}
        owner: "{{ admin_user }}"
        group: "{{ admin_user }}"
        mode: "0644"
      loop: [ bashrc, tmux.conf, vimrc,   gitconfig ]

    - name: harden sshd a little
      lineinfile:
        path: /etc/ssh/sshd_config
        regexp: '{{ item.regexp }}'
        line: "{{ item.line }}"
        validate: '/usr/sbin/sshd -t -f %s'
      loop:
        - { regexp: '^#?PasswordAuthentication', line: 'PasswordAuthentication no' }
        - { regexp: '^#?PermitRootLogin',        line: 'PermitRootLogin no' }
        - {regexp: '^#?Port', line: "Port {{ ssh_port }}"}
      notify: restart ssh

    - name: unattended upgrades, reboot at 04:30 if needed
      copy:
        dest: /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/52homelab-upgrades
        mode: 0644
        content: |
          Unattended-Upgrade::Origins-Pattern {
                  "origin=Debian,codename=${distro_codename},label=Debian-Security";
                  "origin=Raspbian,codename=${distro_codename},label=Raspbian";
          };
          Unattended-Upgrade::Automatic-Reboot "true";
          Unattended-Upgrade::Automatic-Reboot-Time "04:30";

    - name: motd so I know which box I'm on
      copy:
        dest: /etc/motd
        content: |-

            {{ inventory_hostname | upper }}  ({{ ansible_facts['architecture'] }}, {{ ansible_memtotal_mb }} MB)
            managed by ansible -- local changes WILL be overwritten

#    - name: zram instead of a swap file on the 2GB pis
#      include_role:
#        name: zram
#      when: ansible_memtotal_mb < 2048

  handlers:
    - name: restart ssh
      service: name=ssh state=restarted


- name: docker host (the NUC)
  hosts: docker_hosts
  become: true
  vars:
      container_defaults: &container_defaults
          restart_policy: unless-stopped
          pull: true
          log_driver: json-file
          log_options: {max-size: "10m", max-file: "3"}
      pihole_webpassword: !vault |
          $ANSIBLE_VAULT;1.1;AES256
          36353064373262376563383664643536346631316431616438346230393337323835636532393335
          3166336465636339623466353231363034376463363438320a313464626264383337643239333735
          38306332353163666237633339363162343161373565313833626438303339376338373765313432
          6565336665353761370a653439346230383138373834386562373733613139396530623762313562
          3533
  tasks:
      - name: docker itself
        include_role:
            name: geerlingguy.docker
        vars:
            docker_install_compose_plugin:   true
            docker_users: "{{ docker_users }}"
        tags: docker

      - name: pihole
        community.docker.docker_container:
            <<: *container_defaults
            name: pihole
            image: "pihole/pihole:2024.07.0"
            ports: ["53:53/tcp", "53:53/udp", "8081:80/tcp"]
            env:
                TZ: "{{ timezone }}"

        community.docker.docker_container:
            <<: *container_defaults
            name: uptime-kuma
            image: louislam/uptime-kuma:1
            ports:
                - "3001:3001"
            volumes: ["/srv/kuma:/app/data"]

          ports: "{{ item.ports | default([]) }}"
          volumes: "{{ item.volumes | default(omit) }}"
        loop:
          - { name: homepage, image: "ghcr.io/gethomepage/homepage:latest", ports: ["3000:3000"], volumes: ["/srv/homepage:/app/config", "/var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro"] }

        loop_control: { label: "{{ item.name }}" }

  hosts: nas_clients
  become: yes
  vars:
    restic_repo: "sftp:backup@nas.lan:/volume1/restic/{{ inventory_hostname }}"
    restic_password:            # lives in group_vars/all/vault.yml
    healthchecks_uuid: ''
    backup_paths:

    backup_excludes: [ "*.tmp", "/srv/jellyfin/cache",   '/srv/**/node_modules', "/srv/pihole/etc/pihole-FTL.db" ]
  tasks:
    - block:
        - name: install restic
          apt: {name: restic, state: latest}

        - name: backup script
          template:
            src: templates/homelab-backup.sh.j2
            dest: /usr/local/bin/homelab-backup
            mode: '0750'

        - name: cron it (03:15 every night)
          cron:
            name: "restic nightly"
            minute: "15"
            hour: "3"
            job: "/usr/local/bin/homelab-backup >> /var/log/homelab-backup.log 2>&1"
      rescue:
        - name: complain loudly
          debug:
            msg: >
              Backup setup failed on {{ inventory_hostname }}. Check that the NAS is reachable
              and that the restic password is actually in the vault, otherwise this box will try
              every night at 03:15 and fail quietly, and you will only find out when you need a
              restore, which is the worst possible moment to find out.
      always:
        - name: ping healthchecks.io
          uri:
            url: "https://hc-ping.com/{{ healthchecks_uuid }}"
            method: GET
            timeout: 10
          ignore_errors: True
          when: healthchecks_uuid | length > 0

serosurv changelog ================== All notable changes to **serosurv** are documented in this file. We loosely follow [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/ "Keep a Changelog 1.1.0") and [semantic versioning][semver], although _honestly_ the 0.3.0 release broke the API without a major version bump (sorry to everyone whose scripts depended on the old two-vector interface of `seroprev()`; see the migration notes under 0.3.0). Dates are in ISO 8601 format and refer to the day the release was tagged, not the day it reached our r-universe. ## [Unreleased] ## ### Added * `adjust_prevalence()` gains `method = "bayes"`, which fits the hierarchical model of Gelman and Carpenter[^gc2020] so that the uncertainty in test sensitivity and specificity is propagated from the validation studies instead of being treated as known constants. Needs **cmdstanr** (>= 0.7.0), which is now listed under `Suggests`. * New example data `sero_toy`: a simulated serosurvey of 1,200 participants in 8 districts with a known true prevalence, mainly for teaching. + `plot_prevalence()` can facet by any grouping variable via `facet_by =`. ### Changed - The default interval for *unadjusted* prevalence is now Wilson instead of Wald. Wald intervals behave badly near 0 and 1, which is exactly where most serosurveys early in an outbreak live. - Minimum R version is now 4.1, because we use the native pipe `|>` internally. ### Fixed - `rogan_gladen()` no longer silently returns values outside $[0, 1]$; estimates are truncated to the unit interval and a warning is raised (#41, thanks to K. Asante for the report). - Column names containing underscores (age\_group\_5y and friends) were mangled in `plot_prevalence()` legends. ## [0.4.1] - 2024-03-18 ## Bug-fix release. If you used `weights =` together with `by =` in 0.4.0, **please re-run your analyses**: stratum weights were recycled in the wrong order whenever the grouping variable was a factor whose levels were not in alphabetical order. ### Fixed 1) Stratum weights are now matched by name, not by position (#38). 2) `seroprev()` printed "NaN%" for strata without positives; it now prints `0.0%` together with the exact (Clopper–Pearson) upper bound. 3) The vignettes build without internet access (the district shapefile now ships in `inst/extdata`). Effect of the fix on the bundled `sero_toy` data, adjusted prevalence in %: | District | 0.4.0 (wrong) | 0.4.1 |true value| |:--|--:|--:|:-:| | North | 12.4 | 8.1 | 8.0 | | Lakeside | 3.9| 6.6 |6.5| |Old Town | 21.0 | 20.7 | 21.2 | | *all districts* | 11.8 | 11.8 | 11.9 | ## [0.4.0] - 2024-01-29 ### Added * Post-stratification: `seroprev(..., poststrat = census_df)` reweights the sample to known population margins (age group × sex × district). Census margins for the three study countries are included as `census_ke`, `census_ug` and `census_tz`. * Support for **multiple assays** per sample: * `combine_assays(rule = "both")` – positive only if both assays are positive * `combine_assays(rule = "either")` * `combine_assays(rule = "sequential")` – the second assay is only run on samples that were positive on the first, which is the usual confirmatory algorithm in the field labs Sensitivity and specificity of the combined algorithm are derived assuming conditional independence of the assays, which is optimistic. See `vignette("assay-dependence")`. ### Changed * `seroprev()` returns a tibble with class `serosurv_est` instead of a plain list.\ Code that used `res$estimate` keeps working, code that used `res[[1]]` does not. * Arguments renamed for consistency with **epiR**: - `sens` → `se` - `spec` → `sp` - `n_val` → `n_validation` ### Deprecated * `seroprev_old()`, the pre-0.3 interface. It will be removed in 0.5.0 – *really* this time. * * * ## [0.3.0] - 2023-06-02 The version used for the analyses in our 2023 paper in __Epidemiology & Infection__. Dates are in ISO 8601 format and refer to the day the release was tagged, not the day it reached our r-universe. ## [Unreleased] ## ### Added * `adjust_prevalence()` gains `method = "bayes"`, which fits the hierarchical model of Gelman and Carpenter[^gc2020] so that the uncertainty in test sensitivity and specificity is propagated from the validation studies instead of being treated as known constants. --- layout: page title: "Contributing to ampliseq-lite" parent: "Pipelines" nav_order: 4 permalink: /pipelines/ampliseq-lite/contributing/ last_modified_date: 2024-05-02 tags: [snakemake,16S , how-to] --- # Contributing to ampliseq-lite # Thanks for helping out! `ampliseq-lite` is the Snakemake pipeline the Microbial Ecology group uses to get from demultiplexed 16S/ITS amplicon reads to an ASV table, a taxonomy table and a phylogenetic tree. It started as part of Lena's PhD and is now used by about a dozen people in three departments, so please read this page before opening a pull request -- it saves time for everybody, including you. > **TL;DR** > 1. Open an issue first for anything bigger than a typo. > 2. Work on a branch, never directly on `main`. > 3. Run the test dataset (`make test`) before you ask for a review. Contents: * [Reporting problems](#reporting-problems) * [Setting up a development environment](#setting-up) * [Code style](#code-style) + [Data policy](#data-policy) ← please read this one even if you skip everything else * [Pull requests](#pull-requests) Reporting problems ------------------ Before filing an issue please have a look at the [FAQ](docs/faq.md "Frequently asked questions") and at the closed issues, a surprising number of problems turn out to be caused by an outdated SILVA download. When you do open an issue, include - the exact command you ran, - your `config/config.yaml` (remove any paths that reveal sample or participant IDs!), - the **complete** log of the failing rule, which Snakemake writes to `logs//.log`, and - the output of `snakemake --version` and `mamba list -n ampliseq-lite`. We triage issues on Monday mornings at lab meeting and label them as follows: |label|meaning|who usually picks it up| |---|:---|---| | `bug` | wrong results or a crash | maintainers | |`good first issue`|small and well defined| anyone :) | | `taxonomy-db` | needs a new or updated reference database (SILVA, UNITE, GTDB) | Lena or Sam | | `wontfix` | out of scope, e.g. shotgun metagenomics (use nf-core/mag for that) | – | ## Setting up {#setting-up} You need [mamba](https://mamba.readthedocs.io/ "mamba documentation") (or conda >= 23.10, which uses the libmamba solver by default) and git. On the department cluster both are available after `module load mamba`. 1) Fork and clone the repository: ```bash git clone git@github.com:/ampliseq-lite.git cd ampliseq-lite ``` 2) Create the development environment. It contains snakemake, snakefmt, pytest and pre-commit on top of the runtime dependencies: ```bash mamba env create -f envs/dev.yaml mamba activate ampliseq-dev pre-commit install ``` 3) Run the small test dataset (6 mock-community samples, about two minutes on a laptop): make test If this fails on a fresh clone, that is a bug -- please tell us! ### A minimal config for development Point the pipeline at the test data with a small config file. Keys are case-sensitive and the pipeline does _not_ warn about unknown keys yet (see #57), so a typo in `max_ee` silently gives you the default: ```yaml samples: "tests/data/samples.tsv" primers: forward: GTGYCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA # 515F (Parada) reverse: "GGACTACNVGGGTWTCTAAT" # 806R (Apprill) trim: {min_length: 200, max_ee: [2,2], trunc_q: 2} taxonomy: database: silva-138.1 min_confidence: 0.8 threads: 4 ``` The expected-error filter discards a read when $\sum_i 10^{-Q_i/10}$ exceeds `max_ee`, where $Q_i$ is the Phred quality score at position $i$. ## Code style * Snakefiles are formatted with **snakefmt**, Python scripts with **ruff** and R scripts with **styler**. `pre-commit` runs all three, so normally you don't have to think about it. * One rule per output type. Rules that call R or Python should use the `script:` directive and not `shell: "Rscript ..."`, so the `snakemake` object is available inside the script. * Every rule needs `log:`, `conda:` and `benchmark:` directives. A rule without a log file __will__ be rejected in review; we have lost too many days to silent failures on the cluster. * Name rules with verbs: `trim_primers`, `learn_errors`, `assign_taxonomy`. Not `step3b`. A typical rule: ```python rule assign_taxonomy: input: seqs="results/asv/asv_seqs.fasta", db=config["taxonomy"]["database_path"], output: "results/taxonomy/asv_taxonomy.tsv", log: "logs/assign_taxonomy.log", benchmark: "benchmarks/assign_taxonomy.tsv" conda: "../envs/dada2.yaml" threads: 8 script: "../scripts/assign_taxonomy.R" ``` If a run hangs on the cluster, press Ctrl+C **once** and wait; Snakemake removes incomplete output files before it exits. ### Commit messages and the changelog Write a short summary line (max. ~60 characters) in the imperative mood, a blank line, then details if needed. Reference issues with `Fixes #12`. Good summary lines look like Add UNITE 9.0 database download rule Fix sample sheet parsing when sample IDs contain dots User-visible changes also get an entry under *Unreleased* in `CHANGELOG.md`, in this form: ```markdown ### Fixed * `trim_primers` no longer drops reads whose primer starts with a degenerate base (#61). + The taxonomy table now has one column per rank instead of a single `;`-separated string, which makes it much easier to read into phyloseq ``` ## Data policy
**Never commit sequencing reads, sample metadata containing participant information, or anything from the `restricted/` share.** Some projects (the infant gut cohort in particular) include human-associated samples covered by an ethics approval that does not allow sharing outside the university network.
If you accidentally commit something sensitive, __do not__ just delete it in a new commit -- it stays in the history. Tell Lena or Sam right away and we will rewrite the history and rotate whatever needs rotating. Nobody will be angry, it has happened before[^history]. Test data in `tests/data/` are subsampled from public mock communities ([ZymoBIOMICS][zymo]) and are fine to share. Pull requests ------------- Before requesting a review, tick these off in the PR description: - [ ] `make test` passes locally - [ ] new rules have `log:`, `conda:` and `benchmark:` - [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` has an entry under *Unreleased* - [x] you have read this document Reviews are usually done within a week. During the field season (May–August) it can take longer because half the group is out sampling lakes; ping us in the `#ampliseq` Slack channel if nothing happens. *** ### Authorship ### People who contribute substantially to the pipeline (new modules, major bug fixes, rewriting the docs) are invited as co-authors on the pipeline paper, with roles described using the [CRediT taxonomy][credit]. Smaller contributions are acknowledged in `AUTHORS.md`. If you think you should be on the list and aren't, just say so -- seriously. [^history]: Twice, actually. Once with a 4 GB FASTQ file, which GitHub refused anyway, and once with a metadata sheet. The second one is the reason this section exists. [zymo]: https://www.zymoresearch.com/collections/zymobiomics-microbial-community-standards [credit]: https://credit.niso.org/ "CRediT – Contributor Roles Taxonomy"
