# docker-compose.yml -- home automation box (the NUC in the hallway cupboard)
#
#   docker compose --env-file .env up -d
#   docker compose logs -f zigbee2mqtt      <- 90% of all debugging happens here
#
# NOTE: the zigbee stick is a Sonoff ZBDongle-P. Use the by-id path, NOT /dev/ttyUSB0,
#       it renumbers itself every time the UPS hiccups.

version: "3.8"   # obsolete, compose ignores it, but the old Portainer on the pi still wants it

x-common: &common
  restart: unless-stopped
  environment: &common-env
    TZ:   ${TZ:-Europe/Berlin}
    PUID: "${PUID:-1000}"
    PGID: "${PGID:-1000}"
  logging:
    driver: "json-file"
    options: { max-size: "10m", max-file: "3" }

x-healthcheck: &hc
    interval: 30s
    timeout: 10s
    retries: 3
    start_period: 40s

services:

  homeassistant:
    <<: *common
    container_name: homeassistant
    image: "ghcr.io/home-assistant/home-assistant:2024.6"
    network_mode: host
    privileged: true
    volumes:
      - ./homeassistant/config:/config
      - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
      - /run/dbus:/run/dbus:ro
    depends_on: [ mosquitto, influxdb ]
    healthcheck:
      <<: *hc
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-fsS", "http://localhost:8123/manifest.json"]
    labels:
      com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable: "false"   # HA updates are manual, there are breaking changes every month

  mosquitto:
    <<: *common
    image: eclipse-mosquitto:2.0.18
    container_name: mosquitto
    ports:
    - "1883:1883"
    - '9001:9001'
    volumes:
    - ./mosquitto/config:/mosquitto/config
    - ./mosquitto/data:/mosquitto/data
    - ./mosquitto/log:/mosquitto/log
    command: "mosquitto -c /mosquitto/config/mosquitto.conf"

  zigbee2mqtt:
    <<: *common
    image: koenkk/zigbee2mqtt:1.38.0
    container_name: zigbee2mqtt
    depends_on:
      mosquitto:
        condition: service_started
    ports: ["8080:8080"]
    volumes: [ "./zigbee2mqtt/data:/app/data", "/run/udev:/run/udev:ro" ]
    devices:
        - /dev/serial/by-id/usb-ITead_Sonoff_Zigbee_3.0_USB_Dongle_Plus_4c004e2c5e7f-if00-port0:/dev/ttyACM0
    environment:
      <<: *common-env
      ZIGBEE2MQTT_CONFIG_MQTT_SERVER: "mqtt://mosquitto:1883"
      ZIGBEE2MQTT_CONFIG_FRONTEND_PORT: 8080
      ZIGBEE2MQTT_CONFIG_PERMIT_JOIN: 'false'
      ZIGBEE2MQTT_CONFIG_ADVANCED_LOG_LEVEL:    warn

  nodered:
    <<: *common
    image: nodered/node-red:3.1-18
    container_name: nodered
    user: "1000:1000"
    ports:
      - 1880:1880
    volumes:
      - nodered-data:/data
    environment:
      <<: *common-env
      NODE_RED_CREDENTIAL_SECRET: ${NODE_RED_SECRET:?set NODE_RED_SECRET in .env}
    depends_on:
      - mosquitto

  influxdb:
    <<: *common
    image: influxdb:2.7-alpine
    container_name: influxdb
    ports: [ '8086:8086' ]
    volumes:
      - influx-data:/var/lib/influxdb2
      - ./influxdb/config:/etc/influxdb2
    environment:
      DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_MODE: setup
      DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_USERNAME: "admin"
      DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_PASSWORD: ${INFLUX_PASSWORD}
      DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_ORG: home
      DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_BUCKET: "homeassistant"
      DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_RETENTION: 52w
    healthcheck:
      <<: *hc
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://localhost:8086/health || exit 1"]

  grafana:
    <<: *common
    image: grafana/grafana-oss:10.4.2
    container_name: grafana

# docker-compose.yml -- home automation box (the NUC in the hallway cupboard)
#
#   docker compose --env-file .env up -d
#   docker compose logs -f zigbee2mqtt      <- 90% of all debugging happens here
#
# NOTE: the zigbee stick is a Sonoff ZBDongle-P. Use the by-id path, NOT /dev/ttyUSB0,
#       it renumbers itself every time the UPS hiccups.

version: "3.8"   # obsolete, compose ignores it, but the old Portainer on the pi still wants it

x-common: &common
  restart: unless-stopped
  environment: &common-env
    TZ:   ${TZ:-Europe/Berlin}
    PUID: "${PUID:-1000}"
    PGID: "${PGID:-1000}"
  logging:
    driver: "json-file"
    options: { max-size: "10m", max-file: "3" }

x-healthcheck: &hc
    interval: 30s
    timeout: 10s
    retries: 3
    start_period: 40s

services:

  homeassistant:
    <<: *common
    container_name: homeassistant
    image: "ghcr.io/home-assistant/home-assistant:2024.6"
    network_mode: host
    privileged: true
    volumes:
      - ./homeassistant/config:/config
      - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
      - /run/dbus:/run/dbus:ro
    depends_on: [ mosquitto, influxdb ]
    healthcheck:
      <<: *hc
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-fsS", "http://localhost:8123/manifest.json"]
    labels:
      com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable: "false"   # HA updates are manual, there are breaking changes every month

  mosquitto:
    <<: *common
    image: eclipse-mosquitto:2.0.18
    container_name: mosquitto
    ports:
    - "1883:1883"
    - '9001:9001'
    volumes:
    - ./mosquitto/config:/mosquitto/config
    - ./mosquitto/data:/mosquitto/data
    - ./mosquitto/log:/mosquitto/log
    command: "mosquitto -c /mosquitto/config/mosquitto.conf"

  zigbee2mqtt:
    <<: *common
    image: koenkk/zigbee2mqtt:1.38.0
    container_name: zigbee2mqtt
    depends_on:
      mosquitto:
        condition: service_started
    ports: ["8080:8080"]
    volumes: [ "./zigbee2mqtt/data:/app/data", "/run/udev:/run/udev:ro" ]
    devices:

      <<: *common-env
      ZIGBEE2MQTT_CONFIG_MQTT_SERVER: "mqtt://mosquitto:1883"

      ZIGBEE2MQTT_CONFIG_ADVANCED_LOG_LEVEL:    warn

    <<: *common

      - nodered-data:/data

      DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_PASSWORD: ${INFLUX_PASSWORD}
      DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_ORG: home
      DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_BUCKET: "homeassistant"

arguments.content:
# docker compose stack for the Freshwater Ecology Lab data platform
# Services: PostGIS (field data), RStudio, Jupyter, Shiny (public lake dashboard), MinIO (raw logger files)
#
#   start everything:     docker compose up -d
#   only the database:    docker compose up -d db
#   admin tools too:      docker compose --profile admin up -d
#
# NOTE: passwords come from .env which is NOT committed. Copy .env.example and fill it in.
version: "3.9"

x-logging: &default-logging
  driver: "json-file"
  options: { max-size: "10m", max-file: "5" }

x-common: &common
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *default-logging
    networks: [labnet]
    environment: &common-env
      TZ: "Europe/Stockholm"
      LAB_DATA_ROOT: /data

services:

  db:
    image: postgis/postgis:15-3.4
    <<: *common
    container_name: fieldlab-db
    environment:
      <<: *common-env
      POSTGRES_DB: fielddata
      POSTGRES_USER: "${POSTGRES_USER:-lab}"
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./db/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro   # creates the schemas + the read-only 'students' role
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-lab} -d fielddata"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout:  5s
      retries: 5
    shm_size: '1gb'

  rstudio:
    image: rocker/geospatial:4.3.2
    <<: *common
    environment:
      - PASSWORD=${RSTUDIO_PASSWORD}
      - ROOT=TRUE
      - DISABLE_AUTH=false
      - TZ=Europe/Stockholm
    ports: ["8787:8787"]
    volumes:
      - ./projects:/home/rstudio/projects
      - logger-raw:/data/raw:ro
      - type: bind
        source: ./renv-cache
        target: /renv/cache
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy

  jupyter:
    image: "quay.io/jupyter/scipy-notebook:2024-03-14"
    <<: *common
    user: root
    command: >
      start-notebook.py
        --ServerApp.token=''
        --ServerApp.password='${JUPYTER_PASSWORD_HASH}'
        --ServerApp.root_dir=/home/jovyan/work
    environment:
      NB_UID: 1000
      GRANT_SUDO: "yes"
      CHOWN_HOME: 'yes'
      JUPYTER_ENABLE_LAB: yes     # TODO does this still do anything?
    volumes: [ "./notebooks:/home/jovyan/work", "logger-raw:/data/raw:ro" ]
    ports:
      - 8888:8888

  shiny:
    build:
      context: ./dashboard
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
      args:
        R_VERSION: 4.3.2
        RENV_VERSION: "1.0.3"
    <<: *common
    container_name: lake-dashboard
    ports:
      - "3838:3838"
    environment:
      <<: *common-env
      DB_HOST: db
      DB_NAME: fielddata
      DB_USER: dashboard_ro
      DB_PASSWORD: ${DASHBOARD_DB_PASSWORD}
      SHINY_LOG_LEVEL: "INFO"
    depends_on: [db]
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits: {cpus: '2.0', memory: 4G}

  minio:
    image: minio/minio:RELEASE.2024-03-15T01-07-19Z
    <<: *common
    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - logger-raw:/data
    ports:
      - "9000:9000"
      - "9001:9001"

      # pulls the HOBO / YSI logger exports from the field laptops' sync folder.
      # Runs from cron on the host:  docker compose --profile ingest run --rm ingest
  ingest:
    build: ./ingest
    <<: *common
    restart: "no"
    entrypoint: ["/bin/bash", "-c"]
    command:
      - |
        set -e
        echo "[$(date -Is)] starting ingest"
        python -m ingest.sync --source /sync --bucket logger-raw
        python -m ingest.load --db "postgresql://$${POSTGRES_USER}:$${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/fielddata"
        echo "[$(date -Is)] done"
    volumes:
    - /srv/field-sync:/sync:ro
    environment:
      <<: *common-env
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-lab}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      MINIO_ENDPOINT: http://minio:9000
      LOGGER_TYPES: "hobo_u20,ysi_exo2,  onset_mx2202"
    profiles: ["ingest"]
    depends_on:
      db: {condition: service_healthy}
      minio:
        condition: service_started

  pgadmin:
      image: dpage/pgadmin4:8.4
      <<: *common
      environment:
          PGADMIN_DEFAULT_EMAIL: "admin@fieldlab.example.org"
          PGADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD: ${PGADMIN_PASSWORD}
          PGADMIN_CONFIG_SERVER_MODE: 'False'
      ports:
          - 5050:80
      profiles:
          - admin

volumes:
  pgdata:
  logger-raw:
  renv-cache: {}

networks:
  labnet:
    driver: bridge
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 172.28.0.0/16

arguments.content:
# CI for dicegoblin
#  - lint + tests on every push and PR
#  - on tags: build the docker image, push it to ghcr, then poke the homelab to pull it
name: "CI"

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, 'release/**' ]
    tags: ["v*.*.*"]
    paths-ignore:
      - '**.md'
      - docs/**
      - .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      deploy:
        description: "Deploy to the homelab after building? Only does anything on main, and only if the image actually built, so it's safe to tick this when you're just poking at things."
        type: boolean
        default: false
      log_level:
        description: 'log level for the smoke test'
        required: false
        default: "INFO"
        type: choice
        options: [DEBUG, INFO, WARNING]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 4 * * 1'   # monday 4am, catches dependency breakage before thursday's session

permissions: { contents: read }

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"
  IMAGE: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/dicegoblin
  DEFAULT_PYTHON: '3.12'

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
        # checkout first, obviously
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.DEFAULT_PYTHON }}
          cache: pip
      - run: pip install ruff==0.4.8 mypy types-PyYAML
      - name: ruff
        run: |
          ruff check .
          ruff format --check .
      - name: mypy (allowed to fail for now, the discord.py stubs are a mess)
        run: mypy dicegoblin.py --ignore-missing-imports
        continue-on-error: true

  test:
      needs: lint
      runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
      timeout-minutes: 15
      strategy:
          fail-fast: false
          matrix:
              os: [ubuntu-latest]
              python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12", '3.13']
              include:
                  - { os: windows-latest, python-version: "3.12" }
                  - {os: macos-latest, python-version: "3.12", experimental: true}
      continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental == true }}
      steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
            uses: actions/setup-python@v5
            with:
                python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
                allow-prereleases: true
          - name: install
            run: |
                python -m pip install --upgrade pip
                pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
          - name: pytest
            run: python -m pytest -q --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings --cov=dicegoblin --cov-report=xml --cov-report=term-missing tests/
            env:
                DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN: "not-a-real-token"
                DICEGOBLIN_LOG_LEVEL: ${{ inputs.log_level || 'INFO' }}
          - name: upload coverage
            if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && matrix.python-version == '3.12'
            uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
            with: {files: coverage.xml, fail_ci_if_error: false, token: "${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}"}

  docker:
    needs: [test]
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') || inputs.deploy }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    outputs:
      digest: ${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3      # pi-04 is arm64
    - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
    - uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        registry: ghcr.io
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    - id: meta
      uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
      with:
        images: ${{ env.IMAGE }}
        tags: |
          type=semver,pattern={{version}}
          type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}}
          type=raw,value=latest,enable={{is_default_branch}}
          type=sha,format=short

# CI for dicegoblin
#  - lint + tests on every push and PR
#  - on tags: build the docker image, push it to ghcr, then poke the homelab to pull it
name: "CI"

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, 'release/**' ]
    tags: ["v*.*.*"]
    paths-ignore:
      - '**.md'
      - docs/**
      - .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      deploy:
        description: "Deploy to the homelab after building? Only does anything on main, and only if the image actually built, so it's safe to tick this when you're just poking at things."
        type: boolean
        default: false
      log_level:
        description: 'log level for the smoke test'
        required: false
        default: "INFO"
        type: choice
        options: [DEBUG, INFO, WARNING]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 4 * * 1'   # monday 4am, catches dependency breakage before thursday's session

permissions: { contents: read }

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"
  IMAGE: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/dicegoblin
  DEFAULT_PYTHON: '3.12'

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
        # checkout first, obviously
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.DEFAULT_PYTHON }}
          cache: pip
      - run: pip install ruff==0.4.8 mypy types-PyYAML
      - name: ruff
        run: |
          ruff check .
          ruff format --check .
      - name: mypy (allowed to fail for now, the discord.py stubs are a mess)
        run: mypy dicegoblin.py --ignore-missing-imports
        continue-on-error: true

  test:
      needs: lint
      runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
      timeout-minutes: 15
      strategy:
          fail-fast: false
          matrix:
              os: [ubuntu-latest]
              python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12", '3.13']
              include:
                  - { os: windows-latest, python-version: "3.12" }
                  - {os: macos-latest, python-version: "3.12", experimental: true}
      continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental == true }}
      steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
            uses: actions/setup-python@v5
            with:
                python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
                allow-prereleases: true
          - name: install
            run: |
                python -m pip install --upgrade pip
                pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
          - name: pytest
            run: python -m pytest -q --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings --cov=dicegoblin --cov-report=xml --cov-report=term-missing tests/
            env:
                DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN: "not-a-real-token"
                DICEGOBLIN_LOG_LEVEL: ${{ inputs.log_level || 'INFO' }}
          - name: upload coverage
            if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && matrix.python-version == '3.12'
            uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
            with: {files: coverage.xml, fail_ci_if_error: false, token: "${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}"}

  docker:
    needs: [test]
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') || inputs.deploy }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    outputs:
      digest: ${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3      # pi-04 is arm64
    - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
    - uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        registry: ghcr.io
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    - id: meta
      uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
      with:
        images: ${{ env.IMAGE }}
        tags: |
          type=semver,pattern={{version}}
          type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}}
          type=raw,value=latest,enable={{is_default_branch}}
          type=sha,format=short
    - id: build
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
        push: true
        tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
        labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
        cache-from: type=gha
        cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

  deploy:
    needs: docker
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: homelab
      url: https://goblin.example.net/healthz
    steps:
      - name: tailscale
        uses: tailscale/github-action@v2
        with:
          oauth-client-id: ${{ secrets.TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          oauth-secret: ${{ secrets.TS_OAUTH_SECRET }}
          tags: tag:ci
      - name: pull + restart on the nuc
        run: >
          ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new deploy@nuc.tail1234.ts.net
          "cd /srv/dicegoblin && docker compose pull && docker compose up -d && docker image prune -f"
      - name: tell discord
        if: always()
        env:
          WEBHOOK: ${{ secrets.DISCORD_WEBHOOK }}
          STATUS:  ${{ job.status }}
        run: |-
          curl -sS -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "{\"content\": \"deploy of ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} finished: ${STATUS} :game_die:\"}" \
            "$WEBHOOK"

arguments.content:
# Runs R CMD check on the phenology package and rebuilds the analysis website.
# Adapted from the r-lib/actions v2 examples + extra steps for the targets pipeline.
# If the windows check fails because of sf/terra binaries, just re-run it. Usually works the 2nd time :(
name: R-CMD-check-and-site

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, master, 'release/**' ]
    paths-ignore:
      - '**.md'
      - "docs/**"
      - 'analysis/data-raw/**'
  pull_request:
    branches:    [main]
  schedule:
      # Mondays 06:17 UTC -- catches breakage from new CRAN/Bioc releases before lab meeting
    - cron:  '17 6 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      rebuild_cache:
        description: "Ignore the targets cache and rebuild every target from scratch (takes about 40 minutes, so only do this if something is really broken)"
        required: false
        default: 'false'
        type: choice
        options: ['false', 'true']

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  R_KEEP_PKG_SOURCE: yes
  GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  _R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_: false
  TARGETS_CACHE_VERSION: "v3"     # bump this to invalidate the cache

jobs:
  R-CMD-check:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.config.os }}
    name: ${{ matrix.config.os }} (R ${{ matrix.config.r }})
    timeout-minutes: 60

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config:
          # fmt: table
          - {os: macos-latest,   r: 'release'}
          - {os: windows-latest, r: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,   r: 'devel', http-user-agent: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,   r: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,   r: 'oldrel-1'}
          - {os: ubuntu-22.04, r: "4.1.3"}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-pandoc@v2

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          r-version: ${{ matrix.config.r }}
          http-user-agent: ${{ matrix.config.http-user-agent }}
          use-public-rspm: true

      - &sysdeps
        name: Install system deps for sf / terra (linux only)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libgdal-dev libgeos-dev libproj-dev libudunits2-dev

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
        with:
          extra-packages: any::rcmdcheck, local::.
          needs: check

      - uses: r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2
        with:
          upload-snapshots: true
          error-on: '"error"'
          args: 'c("--no-manual", "--as-cran")'

  site:
    needs: R-CMD-check
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      CDS_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CDS_API_KEY }}      # ERA5 temperature data from Copernicus
      TAR_PROJECT: main
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      with: {fetch-depth: 0}
    - *sysdeps
    - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
      with:
        use-public-rspm: true
    - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-renv@v2
    - uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2
      with:
        version: 1.4.550

    - name: Restore targets cache
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: |
          _targets/objects
          _targets/meta
        key: targets-${{ env.TARGETS_CACHE_VERSION }}-${{ hashFiles('_targets.R', 'R/**/*.R') }}
        restore-keys: |
          targets-${{ env.TARGETS_CACHE_VERSION }}-

    - name: Run targets pipeline
      shell: Rscript {0}
      run: |
        if (identical(Sys.getenv("REBUILD"), "true")) targets::tar_destroy(destroy = "objects", ask = FALSE)
        targets::tar_make(reporter = "timestamp")
        targets::tar_meta(fields = c(name, seconds, warnings)) |>
          dplyr::filter(!is.na(warnings)) |>
          print(n = Inf)
      env:
        REBUILD: ${{ github.event.inputs.rebuild_cache }}

    - name: Render site
      run: quarto render analysis/ --to html

    - name: Deploy to gh-pages
      if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
      uses: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.5.0
      with:
        branch: gh-pages
        folder: analysis/_site
        clean: true
        commit-message: >-
          Site rebuilt from ${{ github.sha }} by workflow run
          ${{ github.run_id }} (triggered by ${{ github.event_name }})

  coverage:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [R-CMD-check]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with: { use-public-rspm: true }
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
        with:
          extra-packages: "any::covr, any::xml2"
          needs: coverage
      - name: Test coverage
        run: |
          cov <- covr::package_coverage(quiet = FALSE, clean = FALSE, install_path = file.path(normalizePath(Sys.getenv("RUNNER_TEMP"), winslash = "/"), "package"))
          covr::to_cobertura(cov)
        shell: Rscript {0}
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          fail_ci_if_error: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' && true || false }}
          files: ./cobertura.xml
          plugin: noop
          disable_search: true
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}

arguments.content:
---
title: "Changelog"
description: All notable changes to @acme/shipment-tracking-sdk, the TypeScript client for the Shipment Tracking API used by the returns portal, the customer-service console and the depot dashboards.
hide: [toc]
tags: [logistics, sdk,  changelog]
---

Changelog
=========

All notable changes to `@acme/shipment-tracking-sdk` are documented in this file. The format is based on [Keep a Changelog][kac], and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning][semver] -- with one exception: anything exported from `@acme/shipment-tracking-sdk/internal` may change in a minor release without notice, because it is only meant for the tracking team's own frontends.

> [!TIP]
> Looking for the REST API rather than the SDK? The API has its own changelog in the [developer portal](https://dev.acme-corp.example/logistics/tracking/changelog "Tracking API changelog").

## [Unreleased]

### Added 
- `client.shipments.watch()` now accepts an `AbortSignal`, so React components can cancel the long-poll on unmount.
- A retry budget per client instance (`maxRetryBudget`), defaulting to 10 retries per 60 seconds.
+ Experimental: `client.depots.capacity()` for the depot capacity endpoint (behind the `depot-capacity` feature flag; ask in #logistics-platform for access).

### Fixed
* Time zones of `estimatedDelivery` were reported in the carrier's local time instead of UTC for **DPD** and **GLS** shipments.
* `listEvents()` silently dropped events with an unknown `type` instead of returning them as `UnknownEvent`.

## [5.0.0] - 2026-11-10 ##

This is a __major__ release. It removes the callback-based API that was deprecated in 4.0 and switches the default transport to `fetch`.  
Most consumers only need to change their imports; see the migration notes below.

> [!WARNING]
> Node.js 18 is no longer supported. The SDK now requires Node.js **20.11** or newer, or any evergreen browser.
> The Jest preset `@acme/shipment-tracking-sdk/jest` was removed as well.

### Breaking changes

1. Removed `TrackingClient#getShipment(id, callback)` and all other callback overloads. Use the promise-returning variants.
2. `Shipment.status` is now a string union (`"created" | "in_transit" | "out_for_delivery" | "delivered" | "exception" | "returned"`) instead of a numeric enum, so `status === 3` comparisons must be updated.
3. The default `baseUrl` changed from `https://tracking.acme-corp.example/api/v3` to `https://tracking.acme-corp.example/api/v4`. The v3 API will be switched off on 2027-03-31.
    * If you pin `baseUrl` explicitly, nothing changes for you.
    * If you rely on the default, test against v4 in staging first: the `eta` field moved into `delivery.eta`.

Migration example:

```diff
-import { TrackingClient, ShipmentStatus } from "@acme/shipment-tracking-sdk";
-client.getShipment(id, (err, shipment) => {
-  if (shipment.status === ShipmentStatus.Delivered) markDone(shipment);
-});
+import { TrackingClient } from "@acme/shipment-tracking-sdk";
+const shipment = await client.shipments.get(id);
+if (shipment.status === "delivered") markDone(shipment);
```

<details>
<summary>Full list of removed exports</summary>

| Export | Replacement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ShipmentStatus` (enum) | string union `ShipmentStatus` | type-only export now |
| `createLegacyClient()` | `new TrackingClient()` |  |
| `TrackingError.code` (number) | `TrackingError.reason` | e.g. `"RATE_LIMITED"`|
| `withRetries(fn, n)` | `retry` option | moved into client options \| per request |

</details>

### Changed
- The default request timeout is now 10 s (was 30 s).   Long-polling calls keep their own 55 s timeout.
- `User-Agent` now includes the calling service name when `serviceName` is set, e.g. `shipment-tracking-sdk/5.0.0 (returns-portal)`. This makes the tracking team's dashboards a lot more useful, so _please_ set it.
-  Bundle size dropped from 41 kB to 17 kB (min+gzip) after removing `axios`.   

### Deprecated
* `client.carriers.list({ includeInactive })` -- use `client.carriers.search()` instead; `includeInactive` will be removed in 6.0.

### Internal
1) Migrated the build from Rollup to tsup; the published package layout is unchanged.
2) CI now runs the contract tests against the tracking API's Pact broker on every merge request.
   1) Provider verification runs nightly instead of per commit.
   2) A failing verification blocks the release job, not the merge request.

***

## [4.9.2] - 2026-09-23

### Fixed
- The pagination cursor was not URL-encoded, which broke `listShipments()` for depots whose ID contains a `+` (only `AT-VIE+01` in practice).
- Fixed a memory leak in `watch()` when the server closed the connection with HTTP 204\
  (thanks to the returns-portal team for the heap snapshot).

## [4.9.1] - 2026-08-30
### Security
- Bumped `undici` to 6.19.8 to address CVE-2026-31337[^cve]. No API changes.

## [4.9.0] - 2026-08-04

### Added
3. `client.shipments.bulkGet(ids)` for up to 200 IDs per call.
4. An `onRateLimited` hook, called with the `Retry-After` value before the SDK backs off.

### Changed
* Internal: requests are now traced with OpenTelemetry when a global tracer provider is registered.  Spans are named `tracking.<resource>.<method>`, e.g. `tracking.shipments.get`, and carry the depot ID as the `acme.depot_id` attribute.

- - -

## [4.8.0] - 2026-06-12
### Added
- Support for the *Paketshop* pickup point type (`pickupPoint.kind === "parcel_shop"`).
- `formatTrackingUrl(shipment, { locale })` helper. It escapes the tracking number properly, so \*please\* stop building these URLs by hand.

### Removed
- Dropped the `dist/umd` bundle; nobody was loading it from the CDN any more[^umd].

___

Older releases (4.7.x and earlier) are listed in the [archived changelog](docs/CHANGELOG-4.x.md).

[^cve]: The vulnerability only affects clients that pass user-controlled headers to the SDK. None of our internal consumers do this, but the upgrade is mandatory under the platform security policy (SEC-POL-12, section 4.2).
[^umd]: We checked the CDN logs for the last 90 days before removing it: zero requests outside of our own synthetic monitoring.

---
title: "Changelog"
description: All notable changes to @acme/shipment-tracking-sdk, the TypeScript client for the Shipment Tracking API used by the returns portal, the customer-service console and the depot dashboards.
hide: [toc]
tags: [logistics, sdk,  changelog]
---

Changelog
=========

All notable changes to `@acme/shipment-tracking-sdk` are documented in this file. The format is based on [Keep a Changelog][kac], and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning][semver] -- with one exception: anything exported from `@acme/shipment-tracking-sdk/internal` may change in a minor release without notice, because it is only meant for the tracking team's own frontends.

> [!TIP]
> Looking for the REST API rather than the SDK? The API has its own changelog in the [developer portal](https://dev.acme-corp.example/logistics/tracking/changelog "Tracking API changelog").

## [Unreleased]

### Added 
- `client.shipments.watch()` now accepts an `AbortSignal`, so React components can cancel the long-poll on unmount.
- A retry budget per client instance (`maxRetryBudget`), defaulting to 10 retries per 60 seconds.
+ Experimental: `client.depots.capacity()` for the depot capacity endpoint (behind the `depot-capacity` feature flag; ask in #logistics-platform for access).

### Fixed
* Time zones of `estimatedDelivery` were reported in the carrier's local time instead of UTC for **DPD** and **GLS** shipments.
* `listEvents()` silently dropped events with an unknown `type` instead of returning them as `UnknownEvent`.

## [5.0.0] - 2026-11-10 ##

This is a __major__ release. It removes the callback-based API that was deprecated in 4.0 and switches the default transport to `fetch`.  
Most consumers only need to change their imports; see the migration notes below.

> [!WARNING]
> Node.js 18 is no longer supported. The SDK now requires Node.js **20.11** or newer, or any evergreen browser.
> The Jest preset `@acme/shipment-tracking-sdk/jest` was removed as well.

### Breaking changes

1. Removed `TrackingClient#getShipment(id, callback)` and all other callback overloads. Use the promise-returning variants.
2. `Shipment.status` is now a string union (`"created" | "in_transit" | "out_for_delivery" | "delivered" | "exception" | "returned"`) instead of a numeric enum, so `status === 3` comparisons must be updated.
3. The default `baseUrl` changed from `https://tracking.acme-corp.example/api/v3` to `https://tracking.acme-corp.example/api/v4`. The v3 API will be switched off on 2027-03-31.
    * If you pin `baseUrl` explicitly, nothing changes for you.
    * If you rely on the default, test against v4 in staging first: the `eta` field moved into `delivery.eta`.

Migration example:

```diff
-import { TrackingClient, ShipmentStatus } from "@acme/shipment-tracking-sdk";
-client.getShipment(id, (err, shipment) => {
-  if (shipment.status === ShipmentStatus.Delivered) markDone(shipment);
-});
+import { TrackingClient } from "@acme/shipment-tracking-sdk";
+const shipment = await client.shipments.get(id);
+if (shipment.status === "delivered") markDone(shipment);
```

<details>
<summary>Full list of removed exports</summary>

| Export | Replacement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ShipmentStatus` (enum) | string union `ShipmentStatus` | type-only export now |
| `createLegacyClient()` | `new TrackingClient()` |  |
| `TrackingError.code` (number) | `TrackingError.reason` | e.g. `"RATE_LIMITED"`|
| `withRetries(fn, n)` | `retry` option | moved into client options \| per request |

</details>

### Changed
- The default request timeout is now 10 s (was 30 s).   Long-polling calls keep their own 55 s timeout.
- `User-Agent` now includes the calling service name when `serviceName` is set, e.g. `shipment-tracking-sdk/5.0.0 (returns-portal)`. This makes the tracking team's dashboards a lot more useful, so _please_ set it.
-  Bundle size dropped from 41 kB to 17 kB (min+gzip) after removing `axios`.   

### Deprecated
* `client.carriers.list({ includeInactive })` -- use `client.carriers.search()` instead; `includeInactive` will be removed in 6.0.

### Internal
1) Migrated the build from Rollup to tsup; the published package layout is unchanged.
2) CI now runs the contract tests against the tracking API's Pact broker on every merge request.
   1) Provider verification runs nightly instead of per commit.
   2) A failing verification blocks the release job, not the merge request.

***

## [4.9.2] - 2026-09-23

### Fixed
- The pagination cursor was not URL-encoded, which broke `listShipments()` for depots whose ID contains a `+` (only `AT-VIE+01` in practice).
- Fixed a memory leak in `watch()` when the server closed the connection with HTTP 204\
  (thanks to the returns-portal team for the heap snapshot).

## [4.9.1] - 2026-08-30
### Security
- Bumped `undici` to 6.19.8 to address CVE-2026-31337[^cve]. No API changes.

## [4.9.0] - 2026-08-04

### Added
3. `client.shipments.bulkGet(ids)` for up to 200 IDs per call.
4. An `onRateLimited` hook, called with the `Retry-After` value before the SDK backs off.

### Changed
* Internal: requests are now traced with OpenTelemetry when a global tracer provider is registered.  Spans are named `tracking.<resource>.<method>`, e.g. `tracking.shipments.get`, and carry the depot ID as the `acme.depot_id` attribute.

- - -

## [4.8.0] - 2026-06-12
### Added
- Support for the *Paketshop* pickup point type (`pickupPoint.kind === "parcel_shop"`).
- `formatTrackingUrl(shipment, { locale })` helper. It escapes the tracking number properly, so \*please\* stop building these URLs by hand.

### Removed
- Dropped the `dist/umd` bundle; nobody was loading it from the CDN any more[^umd].

___

Older releases (4.7.x and earlier) are listed in the [archived changelog](docs/CHANGELOG-4.x.md).

[^cve]: The vulnerability only affects clients that pass user-controlled headers to the SDK. None of our internal consumers do this, but the upgrade is mandatory under the platform security policy (SEC-POL-12, section 4.2).
[^umd]: We checked the CDN logs for the last 90 days before removing it: zero requests outside of our own synthetic monitoring.

# miniflux on the k3s cluster (3x pi 4 + the old thinkpad as the "big" node)
# apply with:   envsubst < miniflux.yaml | kubectl apply -f -
# needs MINIFLUX_DB_PASSWORD and MINIFLUX_ADMIN_PASSWORD exported in the shell first
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: miniflux
  labels: {app.kubernetes.io/part-of: reading, homelab/backup: "true"}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: miniflux-secrets
  namespace: miniflux
type: Opaque
stringData:
  DATABASE_URL: "postgres://miniflux:${MINIFLUX_DB_PASSWORD}@miniflux-db:5432/miniflux?sslmode=disable"
  ADMIN_USERNAME: "admin"
  ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${MINIFLUX_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${MINIFLUX_DB_PASSWORD}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
    name: miniflux-config
    namespace: miniflux
data:
    RUN_MIGRATIONS: "1"
    CREATE_ADMIN: "1"
    POLLING_FREQUENCY: "30"        # minutes
    BATCH_SIZE: '50'
    BASE_URL: "https://rss.home.example.net/"
    LOG_DATE_TIME: "true"
    CLEANUP_ARCHIVE_READ_DAYS: "90"
    # postgres tuning for a pi with 4GB, copied from pgtune and then halved because it OOMed once
    postgresql.conf: |
        shared_buffers = 128MB
        effective_cache_size = 512MB
        work_mem = 4MB
        max_connections = 20
        # keep WAL small, the USB SSD thanks you
        wal_compression = on
        max_wal_size = 256MB
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: miniflux-db-data
  namespace: miniflux
  annotations:
    # 2 replicas, the third node is the thinkpad and it goes to sleep sometimes
    longhorn.io/number-of-replicas: "2"
spec:
  accessModes: [ "ReadWriteOnce" ]
  storageClassName: longhorn
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: miniflux-db
  namespace: miniflux
  labels: &db_labels
    app: miniflux
    component: db
spec:
  serviceName: miniflux-db
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels: *db_labels
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: *db_labels
    spec:
      nodeSelector: { kubernetes.io/arch: arm64 }
      containers:
      - name: postgres
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        args: ["-c", "config_file=/etc/postgresql/postgresql.conf"]
        env:
        - name: POSTGRES_USER
          value: miniflux
        - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef: {name: miniflux-secrets, key: POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
        - {name: PGDATA, value: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata}
        ports:
        - containerPort: 5432
          name: postgres
        readinessProbe:
          exec:
            command: [ "pg_isready", "-U", "miniflux" ]
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds:   10
        volumeMounts:
        - {name: data, mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data}
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/postgresql/postgresql.conf
          subPath: postgresql.conf
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: miniflux-db-data
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: miniflux-config
          items: [{key: postgresql.conf, path: postgresql.conf}]
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: miniflux
  namespace: miniflux
  labels: &web_labels {app: miniflux, component: web}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  revisionHistoryLimit: 3
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  selector:
    matchLabels: *web_labels
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: *web_labels
      annotations:
        # bump this to force a restart after editing the configmap
        homelab/restarted-at: "2024-06-02T21:14:00Z"
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: miniflux
          image: "miniflux/miniflux:2.1.3"
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
              name: http
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef: {name: miniflux-config}
            - secretRef:
                name: miniflux-secrets
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: "64Mi"}
            limits:
              memory: 256Mi
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /healthcheck, port: http}
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            failureThreshold: 3
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: miniflux, namespace: miniflux}
spec:
  selector:
    app: miniflux
    component: web
  ports:
    - {name: http, port: 80, targetPort: http}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: miniflux
  namespace: miniflux
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: "letsencrypt-prod"
    traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.entrypoints: websecure
    traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.middlewares: "kube-system-lan-only@kubernetescrd,kube-system-secure-headers@kubernetescrd"
    homelab/notes: >-
      Only reachable from the LAN and over tailscale. If you are reading this
      because the cert expired again, check that the DNS-01 token in the cert-manager namespace hasn't been rotated.
spec:
  ingressClassName: traefik
  tls:
  - hosts: [rss.home.example.net]
    secretName: miniflux-tls
  rules:
  - host: rss.home.example.net
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: miniflux
            port: {name: http}
---
# TODO: network policy so only traefik can talk to miniflux, and only miniflux to the db
# apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
# kind: NetworkPolicy
# metadata:
#   name: miniflux-db-only-from-web
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: miniflux-db-backup
  namespace: miniflux
spec:
  schedule: "30 3 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 2
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
          - name: pg-dump
            image: postgres:16-alpine
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
            args:
              - |
                set -eu
                FILE=/backup/miniflux-$(date +%Y%m%d).sql.gz
                pg_dump -h miniflux-db -U miniflux miniflux | gzip > "$FILE"
                find /backup -name 'miniflux-*.sql.gz' -mtime +14 -delete
            env:
              - name: PGPASSWORD
                valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: miniflux-secrets, key: POSTGRES_PASSWORD}}
            volumeMounts: [{name: backup, mountPath: /backup}]
          volumes:
          - name: backup
            nfs: {server: 192.168.1.20, path: /volume1/k3s-backups/miniflux}
...

# Manifests for the regional respiratory-virus nowcasting service
# Cluster: university research cloud (Rancher), namespace "nowcast"
# Apply with:   kubectl apply -f k8s/nowcast.yaml
#
# Maintainers: Epi Modelling Unit -- R. Haddad / J. Oyelaran
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: nowcast
  labels:
    team: epi-modelling
    cost-centre: "4410"     # must stay a string, the billing exporter chokes on numbers
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: nowcast-config
  namespace: nowcast
data:
  # model settings, read by both the API and the nightly refit job
  model.yaml: |
    pathogens: [influenza, rsv, sars-cov-2]
    delay_distribution:
      family: negative_binomial
      max_delay_days: 21
    nowcast:
      method: "epinowcast"
      chains: 4
      iter_sampling: 1000
      adapt_delta: 0.95
    regions: {source: "nuts2", exclude: [FRY1, FRY2, FRY3, FRY4, FRY5]}
  LOG_LEVEL: "info"
  FORECAST_HORIZON_DAYS: "14"
  TZ: Europe/Paris
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
    name: surveillance-credentials
    namespace: nowcast
type: Opaque
stringData:
    SURVEILLANCE_API_USER: "nowcast-bot"
    SURVEILLANCE_API_TOKEN: "REPLACE_ME"    # the real one lives in Vault, see README
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: model-outputs, namespace: nowcast}
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteMany"]
  storageClassName: cephfs
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 50Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nowcast-api
  namespace: nowcast
  labels: &api_labels
    app.kubernetes.io/name: nowcast-api
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: nowcast
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels: *api_labels
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: *api_labels
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: 'true'
        prometheus.io/port: "8000"
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: registry.epi.example.org/nowcast/api:2024.11.3
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        command: ["Rscript", "-e", "plumber::pr_run(plumber::pr('api/plumber.R'), host = '0.0.0.0', port = 8000)"]
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8000
          name: http
        envFrom:

# Contributing to payments-gateway #

Thanks for helping out!  `payments-gateway` sits in the card-data path of every checkout, which makes it part of our **PCI DSS** scope; that is the reason this guide is longer and stricter than the ones you may know from other internal repositories.  Please read it once end to end before opening your first merge request -- it will save you and your reviewers a few round trips.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Never paste real card numbers (PANs), CVCs or track data into issues, merge requests, test fixtures or Slack, not even "just once" for debugging.  Use the test cards listed in [`docs/test-cards.md`](docs/test-cards.md) instead.
> If it happens anyway, follow the [PAN exposure runbook][pan-runbook] **immediately**.

**Contents**

1) [Ground rules](#ground-rules)
2) [Setting up your environment](#setting-up-your-environment)
3) [Branches and commits](#branches-and-commits)
4) [Merge requests and reviews](#merge-requests-and-reviews)
5) [Releasing](#releasing)

## Ground rules

* Every change goes through a merge request with at least **two approvals**, one of them from a [code owner](CODEOWNERS "Who owns what").
* No direct pushes to `main` or `release/*` -- the branches are protected, and Compliance reviews the audit log every quarter.
+ Keep merge requests small. A good rule of thumb is fewer than 400 changed lines, excluding generated code and test fixtures.
* Changes that touch cryptography, tokenisation or key handling need an additional review from `@payments-security`.

## Setting up your environment

You will need:

- JDK 21 (Temurin) -- `sdk install java 21.0.5-tem`
- Docker Desktop or Colima with at least 6 GB of memory

- access to the `payments-dev` Vault namespace (request it in ServiceNow, catalogue item _Developer Vault Access_)

Then:

1. Clone the repository and install the git hooks:

   ```bash
   git clone git@git.acme-corp.example:payments/payments-gateway.git
   cd payments-gateway && ./scripts/install-hooks.sh
   ```

2. Start the dependencies (Postgres, Redis and the PSP simulator) with `docker compose up -d`.
3. Run the service with the `local` profile:

        ./gradlew bootRun --args='--spring.profiles.active=local'

4. Open <http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html> and send a test authorization with the Visa test card `4111 1111 1111 1111`.

If `docker compose` hangs on the PSP simulator under macOS, stop it with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> and restart Colima with more memory: `colima start --memory 8`.

## Branches and commits

We use short-lived feature branches off `main`. Release branches are cut by the release manager every second Tuesday, and hotfix branches are cut from the release branch they fix.

<!-- fmt: off -->
    main ──●────●────●─────────●────●──▶
            \         \       /
             feat/PAY-1234   release/2026.23 ──●── hotfix/PAY-1301   
<!-- fmt: on -->

Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/ "Conventional Commits 1.0.0"), with the Jira key as the scope:

```text
feat(PAY-1234): support network tokens for Mastercard MDES

Network tokens are requested lazily on the first recurring charge.
Refs: PAY-1190
```

| Type | When to use | Shows up in release notes? |
|:-----|:------------|:--:|
| `feat` | new behaviour visible to merchants or internal consumers | yes |
| `fix` | bug fix | yes |
| `perf` | performance improvement without a behaviour change | yes|
| `refactor` / `chore` / `test` | everything else | no |

## Merge requests and reviews

Before you assign reviewers, make sure that:

- [ ] the pipeline is green, including the `pci-static-analysis` job
- [x] new endpoints are documented in `openapi/gateway.yaml`
- [ ] database migrations are backwards compatible (expand / contract, see [ADR-0031][adr-31])
- [ ] logs do not contain cardholder data; run `./gradlew checkLogRedaction` to be sure

Use this template for the description (GitLab pre-fills it from `.gitlab/merge_request_templates/default.md`):

````markdown
##  What

Short summary of the change.   Link the Jira ticket: PAY-0000

## Why
*  context, links to incidents or ADRs

## How to test
1. step one
1. step two

## Risk
- [ ] touches card data  
- [ ] needs a feature flag
````

Reviewers should respond within **one working day**. If you need a faster review (incident, regulatory deadline), say so explicitly in the merge request and ping the `#payments-core` channel.  
Approvals are reset automatically when new commits are pushed.

## Releasing

The release pipeline is mostly automated: steps 1-3 (tagging, building the image and generating the release notes) happen when the release manager merges the release merge request.  Continue from step 4:

4. Check the generated release notes and remove anything internal-only.
5. Deploy to `staging` from the pipeline and run the PSP certification suite:

       ./gradlew certificationTest -Ppsp=adyen,worldpay,stripe

6. Request the production change in ServiceNow (standard change template `PAY-STD-DEPLOY`).
7. Deploy to production during the agreed window, then watch the __Gateway Golden Signals__ dashboard for 30 minutes.

___

Questions about this guide?  Ask in `#payments-core`, or raise an issue with the label ~"contributing guide"[^labels].

[^labels]: Yes, the tilde syntax is how GitLab references labels.  It renders as a coloured label chip in GitLab, but as plain text everywhere else, including the handbook.

[pan-runbook]: https://wiki.acme-corp.example/display/PAYSEC/PAN+exposure+runbook "PAN exposure runbook"
[adr-31]: docs/adr/0031-expand-contract-migrations.md

# platformctl [![pipeline status](https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/badges/main/pipeline.svg)](https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/-/commits/main) [![coverage report](https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/badges/main/coverage.svg "Line coverage on main")](https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/-/graphs/main/charts) [![classification: internal](https://img.shields.io/badge/classification-internal-orange)][classification] `platformctl` is the command-line front door to the **Acme Internal Developer Platform** (IDP). It provisions everything a new service needs on the golden path -- a Kubernetes namespace with sane defaults, a managed Postgres database, Kafka topics with ACLs, Vault policies, a Backstage catalog entry and the CI templates -- from a single `service.yaml` that lives next to your code. > [!NOTE] > `platformctl` replaces the old `svc-bootstrap` Jenkins job, which will be switched off on **31 January 2027**. See the [migration guide](docs/migrating-from-svc-bootstrap.md "Migrating from svc-bootstrap") if you still have services that were created with it. ## Contents ## * [Installation](#installation) * [Quick start](#quick-start) * [The service.yaml file](#the-serviceyaml-file) * [Tiers](#tiers) * [Commands](#commands) * [Configuration](#configuration) * [FAQ](#faq) ## Installation On a managed laptop the CLI is already installed by the _Developer Workstation_ profile and kept up to date by Jamf. Otherwise: 1. Make sure you are on the corporate VPN or in an office network. 2. Install it from the internal Homebrew tap: ```console $ brew tap acme/internal https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/homebrew-internal.git $ brew install platformctl ``` 3. Log in once. The token is cached in your OS keychain and refreshed automatically: platformctl login --sso Linux users can download a static binary from the [releases page][releases] instead. Windows is supported through WSL2 only. ## Quick start ```sh platformctl init --template java-service --name parcel-label-printer --team team-logistics-edge platformctl plan platformctl apply ``` `init` writes a `service.yaml` similar to this one: ```yaml apiVersion: platform.acme-corp.example/v1 kind: Service metadata: name: parcel-label-printer owner: team-logistics-edge tier: "2" tags: [logistics,printing , edge] spec: runtime: {language: java, version: 21} database: {engine: postgres, size: small, extensions: [pgcrypto, "pg_partman"], backups: {retention_days: 14, pitr: false}} kafka: topics: - name: label.print.requested.v1 partitions: 6 retention: "7d" - {name: label.print.completed.v1, partitions: 6, retention: 7d} expose: [ http ] ``` The service.yaml file --------------------- Every field is documented in the [schema reference](docs/schema.md). The ones people ask about most: + `metadata.owner` must be a team that exists in Backstage; personal owners are __not__ accepted. + `metadata.tier` controls the defaults for replicas, PodDisruptionBudgets and alerting (see [Tiers](#tiers)). + `spec.database.size` maps to a CloudNativePG instance class: `small` = 2 vCPU / 4 GiB, `medium` = 4 vCPU / 16 GiB, `large` = 8 vCPU / 32 GiB. ### Tiers | Tier | Example | Min. replicas | Paging | Change approval | |:---:|---|--:|:--|---| | 1 | payments-gateway, checkout | 3 | 24/7, 5 min | CAB | | 2 | parcel tracking, pricing | 2 | business hours | team lead | | 3 | internal tools, batch jobs | 1 | none | none| ## Commands | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `platformctl init` | Scaffolds `service.yaml`, `.gitlab-ci.yml` and a `catalog-info.yaml` from a template | | `platformctl plan` | Shows what would change, much like `terraform plan` \| `less` | | `platformctl apply` | Applies the plan. Tier 1 services need an approved change ticket: `--change CHG0041234` | | `platformctl destroy` | Tears everything down. Databases are snapshotted first and the snapshot is kept for 35 days | Press Ctrl + C during `apply` to abort; resources that were already created are rolled back unless you pass `--keep-partial`. ## Configuration Settings are read from, in order of precedence: command-line flags, environment variables, `~/.config/platformctl/config.yaml` and finally the defaults compiled into the binary. Variable | Default | Description --- | --- | --- `PLATFORMCTL_API` | `https://idp.acme-corp.example/api` | IDP API endpoint `PLATFORMCTL_CONTEXT` | `prod` | One of `dev`, `staging`, `prod` `PLATFORMCTL_NO_COLOR` | unset | Disable ANSI colours (also honours `NO_COLOR`)
Example config file ```yaml context: staging api: https://idp.staging.acme-corp.example/api defaults: {team: team-logistics-edge, template: java-service} ```
## FAQ **Why not just use Terraform directly?** You can, and the platform team does exactly that under the hood. But most product teams do not want to own 1,500 lines of HCL per service, keep provider versions in sync or remember that a tier 1 database needs point-in-time recovery enabled. `platformctl` encodes those decisions so that you do not have to. **Can I adopt an existing service?**\ Yes: `platformctl adopt --name ` imports existing resources into the IDP state. Expect a few manual fixes; the import report lists them. **Something is broken. Who do I talk to?** Post in `#platform-help` with the output of `platformctl doctor`. For outages use the `@platform-oncall` handle -- it pages whoever is on call. * * * Architecture ------------ ![High-level architecture: platformctl talks to the IDP API, which drives Crossplane, Vault and Backstage](docs/assets/architecture.png "platformctl architecture") The CLI is a thin client. All provisioning logic lives in the IDP API (`platform/idp-api`), which reconciles the desired state through Crossplane compositions[^xp]. The CLI itself only 1. validates `service.yaml` against the JSON schema, 2. renders a plan by calling `POST /v1/plans`, and 3. streams the apply log back to your terminal. ## License Internal use only. Copyright © 2024-2026 Acme Corp. See [LICENSE](LICENSE.md). [^xp]: We evaluated Terraform Cloud and Pulumi as the backend in 2024; the decision is recorded in [ADR-007](docs/adr/007-crossplane.md). [classification]: https://wiki.acme-corp.example/display/SEC/Data+classification [releases]: https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/-/releases "platformctl releases"

It provisions everything a new service needs on the golden path -- a Kubernetes namespace with sane defaults, a managed Postgres database, Kafka topics with ACLs, Vault policies, a Backstage catalog entry and the CI templates -- from a single `service.yaml` that lives next to your code. > [!NOTE] > `platformctl` replaces the old `svc-bootstrap` Jenkins job, which will be switched off on **31 January 2027**. See the [migration guide](docs/migrating-from-svc-bootstrap.md "Migrating from svc-bootstrap") if you still have services that were created with it. ## Contents ## * [Installation](#installation) * [Quick start](#quick-start) * [The service.yaml file](#the-serviceyaml-file) * [Tiers](#tiers) * [Commands](#commands) * [Configuration](#configuration) * [FAQ](#faq) ## Installation On a managed laptop the CLI is already installed by the _Developer Workstation_ profile and kept up to date by Jamf. Otherwise: 1. Make sure you are on the corporate VPN or in an office network. 2. Install it from the internal Homebrew tap: ```console $ brew tap acme/internal https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/homebrew-internal.git $ brew install platformctl ``` 3. Log in once. The token is cached in your OS keychain and refreshed automatically: platformctl login --sso Linux users can download a static binary from the [releases page][releases] instead. Windows is supported through WSL2 only. ## Quick start ```sh platformctl init --template java-service --name parcel-label-printer --team team-logistics-edge platformctl plan platformctl apply ``` `init` writes a `service.yaml` similar to this one: ```yaml apiVersion: platform.acme-corp.example/v1 kind: Service metadata: name: parcel-label-printer owner: team-logistics-edge tier: "2" tags: [logistics,printing , edge] spec: runtime: {language: java, version: 21} database: {engine: postgres, size: small, extensions: [pgcrypto, "pg_partman"], backups: {retention_days: 14, pitr: false}} kafka: topics: - name: label.print.requested.v1 partitions: 6 retention: "7d" - {name: label.print.completed.v1, partitions: 6, retention: 7d} expose: [ http ] ``` The service.yaml file --------------------- Every field is documented in the [schema reference](docs/schema.md). The ones people ask about most: + `metadata.owner` must be a team that exists in Backstage; personal owners are __not__ accepted. + `metadata.tier` controls the defaults for replicas, PodDisruptionBudgets and alerting (see [Tiers](#tiers)). + `spec.database.size` maps to a CloudNativePG instance class: `small` = 2 vCPU / 4 GiB, `medium` = 4 vCPU / 16 GiB, `large` = 8 vCPU / 32 GiB. ### Tiers | Tier | Example | Min. replicas | Paging | Change approval | |:---:|---|--:|:--|---| | 1 | payments-gateway, checkout | 3 | 24/7, 5 min | CAB | | 2 | parcel tracking, pricing | 2 | business hours | team lead | | 3 | internal tools, batch jobs | 1 | none | none| ## Commands | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `platformctl init` | Scaffolds `service.yaml`, `.gitlab-ci.yml` and a `catalog-info.yaml` from a template | | `platformctl plan` | Shows what would change, much like `terraform plan` \| `less` | | `platformctl apply` | Applies the plan. Tier 1 services need an approved change ticket: `--change CHG0041234` | | `platformctl destroy` | Tears everything down. Databases are snapshotted first and the snapshot is kept for 35 days | Press Ctrl + C during `apply` to abort; resources that were already created are rolled back unless you pass `--keep-partial`. ## Configuration Settings are read from, in order of precedence: command-line flags, environment variables, `~/.config/platformctl/config.yaml` and finally the defaults compiled into the binary. Variable | Default | Description --- | --- | --- `PLATFORMCTL_API` | `https://idp.acme-corp.example/api` | IDP API endpoint `PLATFORMCTL_CONTEXT` | `prod` | One of `dev`, `staging`, `prod` `PLATFORMCTL_NO_COLOR` | unset | Disable ANSI colours (also honours `NO_COLOR`)
Example config file ```yaml context: staging api: https://idp.staging.acme-corp.example/api defaults: {team: team-logistics-edge, template: java-service} ```
## FAQ **Why not just use Terraform directly?** You can, and the platform team does exactly that under the hood. But most product teams do not want to own 1,500 lines of HCL per service, keep provider versions in sync or remember that a tier 1 database needs point-in-time recovery enabled. `platformctl` encodes those decisions so that you do not have to. **Can I adopt an existing service?**\ Yes: `platformctl adopt --name ` imports existing resources into the IDP state. Expect a few manual fixes; the import report lists them. **Something is broken. Who do I talk to?** Post in `#platform-help` with the output of `platformctl doctor`. For outages use the `@platform-oncall` handle -- it pages whoever is on call. * * * Architecture ------------ ![High-level architecture: platformctl talks to the IDP API, which drives Crossplane, Vault and Backstage](docs/assets/architecture.png "platformctl architecture") The CLI is a thin client. All provisioning logic lives in the IDP API (`platform/idp-api`), which reconciles the desired state through Crossplane compositions[^xp]. The CLI itself only 1. validates `service.yaml` against the JSON schema, 2. renders a plan by calling `POST /v1/plans`, and 3. streams the apply log back to your terminal. ## License Internal use only. Copyright © 2024-2026 Acme Corp. See [LICENSE](LICENSE.md). [^xp]: We evaluated Terraform Cloud and Pulumi as the backend in 2024; the decision is recorded in [ADR-007](docs/adr/007-crossplane.md). [classification]: https://wiki.acme-corp.example/display/SEC/Data+classification [releases]: https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/-/releases "platformctl releases"

# mkdocs config for romsort.   `mkdocs serve` to preview, CI deploys with mike
site_name: romsort
site_description: "romsort - sort, rename and de-duplicate your ROM dumps using No-Intro / Redump DAT files, without uploading anything anywhere."
site_author: "Kit Okafor"
site_url: !ENV [SITE_URL, "https://kitokafor.github.io/romsort/"]
repo_url: https://github.com/kitokafor/romsort
repo_name: 'kitokafor/romsort'
edit_uri: edit/main/docs/
copyright: Copyright © 2022 - 2024 Kit Okafor — MIT licensed

theme:
  name: material
  custom_dir: overrides
  language: en
  logo: assets/cartridge.svg
  favicon: assets/favicon.png
  icon:
    repo: fontawesome/brands/github
    admonition: {note: octicons/tag-16, warning: octicons/alert-16, tip: octicons/light-bulb-16, example: octicons/beaker-16}
  font:
    text: "Inter"
    code: JetBrains Mono
  palette:
    # light
    - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: light)"
      scheme: default
      primary: deep purple
      accent: amber
      toggle:
        icon: material/weather-night
        name: Switch to dark mode
    # dark
    - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"
      scheme: slate
      primary:   deep purple
      accent: amber
      toggle: {icon: material/weather-sunny, name: "Switch to light mode"}
  features:
  - navigation.instant
  - navigation.tracking
  - navigation.tabs
  - navigation.sections
  - navigation.top
  - search.suggest
  - search.highlight
  - content.code.copy
  - content.code.annotate
  # - content.tabs.link     # breaks the tabs on the install page, look into it later
  - toc.follow

plugins:
    - search:
        lang: en
        separator: '[\s\-,:!=\[\]()"/]+|(?!\b)(?=[A-Z][a-z])|\.(?!\d)|&[lg]t;'
    - git-revision-date-localized:
        enable_creation_date: true
        type: timeago
        fallback_to_build_date: True
    - minify:
        minify_html: true
        htmlmin_opts: {remove_comments: true}
    - redirects:
        redirect_maps:
            'usage.md': 'guide/usage.md'
            "dats.md": "guide/dat-files.md"
    # - social          # needs cairo, which I could not get working on the CI runner
    # - privacy

markdown_extensions:
  - abbr
  - admonition
  - attr_list
  - def_list
  - footnotes
  - md_in_html
  - tables
  - toc:
      permalink: "¶"
      toc_depth: 3
  - pymdownx.details
  - pymdownx.highlight:
      anchor_linenums: true
      line_spans: __span
      pygments_lang_class: true
  - pymdownx.inlinehilite
  - pymdownx.snippets:
      base_path: [ "docs/_snippets", "." ]
      check_paths: true
  - pymdownx.superfences:
      custom_fences:
        - name: mermaid
          class: mermaid
          format: !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format
  - pymdownx.tabbed:
      alternate_style: true
  - pymdownx.tasklist: { custom_checkbox: true }
  - pymdownx.emoji:
      emoji_index: !!python/name:material.extensions.emoji.twemoji
      emoji_generator: !!python/name:material.extensions.emoji.to_svg
  - pymdownx.keys

extra:
  version:
    provider: mike
    default: latest
  generator: false
  analytics:
    provider: google
    property: !ENV GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_KEY
  social:
    - icon: fontawesome/brands/github
      link: https://github.com/kitokafor/romsort
    - {icon: fontawesome/brands/mastodon, link: "https://retro.social/@kit"}
    - {icon: fontawesome/brands/python, link: https://pypi.org/project/romsort/, name: romsort on PyPI}
  consent:
    title: Cookie consent
    description: >-
      I use cookies to see which pages people actually read, so I know what
      to improve. That's it, no ads. Feel free to say no.

extra_css: [stylesheets/extra.css, 'stylesheets/termynal.css']
extra_javascript:
  - javascripts/termynal.js
  - "https://unpkg.com/tablesort@5.3.0/dist/tablesort.min.js"
  - javascripts/tablesort.js

watch:
- src/romsort
- overrides

exclude_docs: |
  drafts/
  *.tmp.md
  _snippets/

not_in_nav: |
  /changelog-old.md

validation:
  omitted_files: warn
  absolute_links:    info
  unrecognized_links: warn

nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - 'Getting started':
    - Installation: getting-started/install.md
    - "Your first sort": getting-started/first-sort.md
  - Guide:
      - guide/usage.md
      - DAT files: guide/dat-files.md
      - Rename rules: guide/rename-rules.md
      - "Dedupe & 1G1R": guide/dedupe.md
      - Config file reference: guide/config.md
  - Systems:
    - systems/index.md
    - Nintendo: systems/nintendo.md
    - Sega: systems/sega.md
    - 'Sony (Redump)': systems/sony.md
  - FAQ: faq.md
  - Changelog: changelog.md
  - Contributing: https://github.com/kitokafor/romsort/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

arguments.content:
openapi: "3.0.3"
info:
  title: sprout
  version: '0.4.1'
  # fmt: markdown
  description: "Tiny HTTP API for the balcony watering controller (a Pi Zero 2 W, four 12V solenoid valves and some capacitive soil moisture sensors that are *mostly* calibrated).\n\nEverything runs on the LAN. There's no auth beyond an API key because the only clients are Home Assistant and my phone.\n\n- moisture values are percentages, 0 = bone dry, 100 = sitting in a cup of water\n- times are UTC unless a field says otherwise\n"
  contact: {name: Ines, url: "https://github.com/inesferreira/sprout"}
  license:
    name: MIT
servers:
  - url: http://{host}:{port}/api/v1
    description: "on the LAN"
    variables:
      host: { default: sprout.lan }
      port:
        default: "8000"
        enum: ["8000", "80"]

tags:
- name: zones
  description: Watering zones (one valve each)
- name: sensors
- name: schedule
  description: >-
    Cron-ish schedules. The controller skips a scheduled run if the zone's moisture is already above its target, so you can be generous here.

security:
  - apiKey: []

# shared error responses, merged into every path below
x-error-responses: &errors
  '401': {$ref: '#/components/responses/Unauthorized'}
  '404': {$ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound'}

paths:
  /zones:
    get:
      tags: [zones]
      summary: List all zones
      operationId: listZones
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Zone'}
              example:
                - {id: 1, name: "tomatoes", valve_gpio: 17, target_moisture: 45, state: idle}
                - {id: 2, name: herbs, valve_gpio: 27, target_moisture: 35, state: "watering"}
  /zones/{zoneId}:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ZoneId'
    get:
      tags: [ zones ]
      summary: Get one zone
      operationId: getZone
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Zone"
        <<: *errors
    patch:
      tags: [zones]
      summary: Update a zone
      description: Only the fields you send are changed. Sending `state` is not allowed, use the `/water` endpoint for that.
      operationId: updateZone
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/ZoneUpdate'}
      responses:
        '200':
          description: The updated zone
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Zone"}
        '422':
          description: Validation error, e.g. target_moisture outside 0..100
        <<: *errors
  /zones/{zoneId}/water:
    parameters:
    - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ZoneId'
    post:
      tags: [zones]
      summary: Water a zone now
      operationId: waterZone
          # fmt: markdown
      description: |
        Opens the zone's valve and starts the pump.
        * returns immediately (`202`), poll `GET /zones/{zoneId}` to see when it's done
        * if moisture is already above target this is a no-op unless `force` is true
        * the pump also has a hard 10 minute timeout in firmware, belt and braces
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                seconds:
                  type: integer
                  minimum: 1
                  maximum: 600
                  default: 30
                  description: How long to open the valve for. Capped at 10 minutes because I flooded the downstairs neighbour's balcony once.
                force: {type: boolean, default: false, description: "Water even if moisture is above target"}
      responses:
        '202':
          description: Accepted, valve is opening
        '409':
          description: Another zone is already watering (the pump can only feed one valve at a time)
        <<: *errors
  /sensors/readings:
    get:
      tags: [sensors]
      summary: Recent moisture readings
      operationId: listReadings
      parameters:
        - name: zone
          in: query
          schema: {type: integer}
        - name: since
          in: query
          description: ISO 8601 timestamp, defaults to 24 hours ago
          schema:
            type: string
            format: date-time
          example: 2024-05-01T06:30:00Z
        - {name: limit, in: query, schema: {type: integer, default: 100, maximum: 1000}}
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/Reading'

components:
  securitySchemes:
    apiKey:
      type: apiKey
      in: header
      name: X-Sprout-Key
  parameters:
    ZoneId:
      name: zoneId
      in: path
      required: true
      schema:
        type: integer
        minimum: 1
        maximum: 4
  responses:
    Unauthorized:
      description: Missing or wrong `X-Sprout-Key` header
    NotFound:
      description: "No such zone"
  schemas:
    Zone:
      type: object
      required: [id, name, valve_gpio, state]
      properties:
        id: {type: integer, readOnly: true}
        name:
          type: string
          maxLength: 32
        valve_gpio:
          type: integer
          description: BCM pin number, not the physical pin. Yes I mixed these up once. Yes the wrong valve opened.
        target_moisture: {type: integer, minimum: 0, maximum: 100, nullable: True}
        state:
          type: string
          enum: [idle, watering, cooldown, error, disabled]
        last_watered:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          nullable: true
          example: "2024-05-01T06:30:00Z"
        notes:
          type: string
          description: >+
            Free text, shown on the Home Assistant card.

    ZoneUpdate:
      type: object
      properties:
        name: {type: string, maxLength: 32}
        target_moisture: { type: integer, minimum: 0, maximum: 100 }
        enabled:
          type: boolean
      additionalProperties: false
    Reading:
      type: object
      properties:
        zone: {type: integer}
        at: {type: string, format: date-time}
        moisture: {type: number, format: float, example: 41.5}
        raw: {type: integer, description: Raw ADC value before calibration, example: 18234}
        battery_v:
          type: number
          example: 3.70
          deprecated: true
          description: |-
            Only the old ESP8266 sensor nodes report this.
            The wired ones on the Pi always return null.
