--- title: "Homelab Q3 2024: power, uptime & what broke" subtitle: 'A quarterly-ish review of the rack under the stairs' author: - name: Ines Ferreira url: https://ines.example.net date: 2024-10-06 date-modified: last-modified description: "Three months of smart-plug readings and Uptime Kuma exports, plus an honest accounting of every outage, including the two that were entirely my own fault." categories: [homelab, power, "self-hosting", uptime] format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 3 code-fold: true code-tools: True theme: [cosmo, custom.scss] fig-align: center execute: echo: false warning: false freeze: auto jupyter: python3 crossref: fig-prefix: Figure tbl-prefix: "Table" --- ## TL;DR {#sec-tldr} The rack drew **41.8 W on average** this quarter (down from 57 W in Q2), mostly because I finally retired the old Dell OptiPlex and moved everything onto the two N100 mini PCs. Uptime for the stuff the household actually notices (Home Assistant, Jellyfin, the Pi-hole) was above 99.5%, see @tbl-uptime, and the electricity bill impact is about €9 a month, which is less than a single streaming subscription so I'm calling that a win. ::: {.callout-note} All numbers come from two Shelly Plug S units logging to InfluxDB every 60 s, and from Uptime Kuma's SQLite database, which I copied off the NUC on 2024-10-01. The plugs claim ±1 W accuracy. I have not verified that and I don't really want to. ::: ![The rack under the stairs, mid-cable-management](images/rack-2024-09.jpg){#fig-rack fig-alt="A 10 inch rack on a shelf under the stairs with a patch panel, an 8 port switch, two mini PCs and a two-bay NAS, cables partly tidied with velcro" width="80%"} ```{python} #| label: setup #| include: false import pandas as pd import matplotlib.pyplot as plt power = pd.read_csv("data/power-q3.csv", parse_dates=["time"]) uptime = pd.read_csv("data/uptime-q3.csv") KWH_PRICE = 0.31 # EUR, fixed tariff until march ``` ## Power {#sec-power} @fig-power shows the daily average. The big dip in mid-August is the week the NAS spent at my parents' place for the offsite backup refresh, and the spike on 2024-09-14 is me running a Jellyfin library rescan *and* a ZFS scrub *and* compiling something, all at once, like an idiot. ```{python} #| label: fig-power #| fig-cap: "Daily average power draw of the rack, July to September 2024" #| fig-alt: "Line chart of daily mean watts, mostly flat around 40 W with a dip to 28 W in mid August and one spike to 71 W in mid September" #| fig-width: 8 #| fig-height: 3.5 daily = power.set_index("time").resample("D")["watts"].mean() ax = daily.plot(color="#7a5195") ax.set_ylabel("W") ax.set_xlabel("") plt.show() ``` The monthly cost works out as $$ \text{cost} = \bar{P} \cdot 24 \cdot 30 \cdot p_{\text{kWh}} \approx 41.8\,\text{W} \times 720\,\text{h} \times 0.31\,\text{€/kWh} $$ {#eq-cost} which is `{python} f"€{41.8 * 720 / 1000 * KWH_PRICE:.2f}"` per month. Plugging Q2's 57 W into @eq-cost gives roughly €12.70, so retiring the OptiPlex paid for one of the N100 boxes in about ~~two years~~ two and a half years. Ugh. The OptiPlex itself is now a very loud doorstop until I figure out what to do with it, suggestions welcome, no I will not run a Minecraft server on it. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="55%"} ### Per device | Device | Avg W | Peak W | Notes | |:--|--:|---:|---| | N100 #1 (proxmox) | 11.2 | 24.9 | runs HA, Pi-hole, kuma | | N100 #2 (docker) | 9.8 | 31.0 | Jellyfin with QSV transcoding | | Synology DS220+ | 14.1 | 22.3 | spins down at night, *mostly* | | switch + AP | 6.7|7.1| PoE for the AP | : Average and peak power per device {#tbl-power} ::: ::: {.column width="5%"} ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"} The NAS disks spinning down saves about 4 W overnight. Getting `hdparm -S` to stick across DSM updates is left as an exercise for future me. ::: ::: :::: ## Uptime {#sec-uptime} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Table ```{python} #| label: tbl-uptime #| tbl-cap: Uptime per service as measured by Uptime Kuma (HTTP checks every 60 s). Services marked with an asterisk are the ones anyone else in the house would notice. (uptime .assign(pct=lambda d: (100 * d.up / d.checks).round(2)) .sort_values("pct") [["service", "pct", "incidents"]]) ``` ### Chart ```{python} #| label: fig-uptime #| fig-cap: "Downtime minutes per service" #| fig-subcap: [ "All services", "Without the paperless outage"] #| layout-ncol: 2 for exclude in ([], ["paperless"]): d = uptime[~uptime.service.isin(exclude)] d.plot.barh(x="service", y="down_minutes", legend=False) plt.show() ``` ::: ## What broke {#sec-outages} 1. **Jul 12** – the Pi-hole died after an update and took DNS for the whole house with it. Household reaction: severe. Fix: a second Pi-hole on the NAS, see @sec-lessons. 2. **Aug 3** – paperless-ngx was down for ~19 hours because Redis ran out of memory; nobody noticed until I tried to find a receipt. 3. **Sep 14** – the power spike in @fig-power. Not an outage, just embarrassing. ::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"} ## The paperless outage, in detail Redis was configured with `maxmemory 64mb` because I copied a compose file from a blog post in 2021. paperless-ngx's task queue grew past that during a bulk import of ~1,400 scanned documents, Redis started evicting keys, and the consumer got stuck retrying the same task forever. The fix was one line. Finding it took an evening and a lot of {{< kbd Ctrl-C >}}. ::: ## Network, for reference ```{mermaid} %%| label: fig-network %%| fig-cap: "How things are wired (logically). The ISP router is in bridge mode." flowchart LR ISP[ISP router
bridge mode] --> OPN[OPNsense on N100 #1] OPN --> SW[8-port switch] SW --> AP[Wi-Fi AP] SW --> N2[N100 #2
docker] SW --> NAS[(DS220+)] OPN -. tailscale .-> PHONE[phones / laptop] ``` ## Lessons and next quarter {#sec-lessons} * Two DNS servers. Always two DNS servers. * Monitoring that nobody reads is not monitoring + Uptime Kuma now pushes to a Discord channel (the same server the dice bot lives on) + and to ntfy on my phone, but only for monitors tagged `critical` - Write down *why* a config value is what it is, future me does not remember[^redis] Plan for Q4: - [x] second Pi-hole - [ ] a UPS that actually talks to the NAS over USB (NUT) - [ ] move the Jellyfin metadata to the SSD - [ ] find out whether N100 #2 idles lower with `powertop --auto-tune` [^redis]: Case in point: the `maxmemory 64mb` line had a comment above it that just said `# important`. Thanks, 2021 me.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	# fmt: markdown
     3	"""Reconcile PSP settlement files against the internal ledger.
     4	
     5	This script is run by the **payments-ops** cron (`ops/cron/settlement.yaml`) every morning at 06:15 CET, after all payment service providers have dropped their settlement reports into the `s3://acme-pay-settlement-inbox` bucket.  It can also be run by hand when a PSP re-sends a corrected file.
     6	
     7	Usage
     8	-----
     9	
    10	    python reconcile_settlements.py --psp adyen --date 2026-11-16 --dry-run
    11	
    12	What it does:
    13	* downloads the settlement report for the given PSP and business date,
    14	* normalises every line into a `SettlementLine` (amounts in minor units),
    15	+ matches lines to ledger postings, see *Matching rules* below,
    16	* writes unmatched items to `recon.exceptions` and posts a summary to the payments-ops channel.
    17	
    18	Exit codes: `0` if everything matched, `3` if exceptions were found (not an error, but somebody has to look at them), `1` for anything else.
    19	"""
    20	from __future__ import annotations
    21	
    22	import argparse
    23	import csv
    24	import datetime as dt
    25	import io
    26	import logging
    27	import os
    28	import sys
    29	from collections import defaultdict
    30	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    31	from decimal import Decimal
    32	from pathlib import Path
    33	from typing import Iterable, Iterator
    34	
    35	import boto3
    36	import psycopg
    37	import requests
    38	import yaml
    39	
    40	log = logging.getLogger("recon")
    41	
    42	INBOX_BUCKET = os.environ.get("RECON_INBOX_BUCKET", "acme-pay-settlement-inbox")
    43	TEAMS_WEBHOOK = os.environ.get("RECON_TEAMS_WEBHOOK", "")
    44	
    45	# Defaults; override with --config path/to/recon.yaml (merged one level deep).
    46	DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML = """
    47	psp:
    48	  adyen:   {prefix: adyen/settlement, glob: "settlement_detail_report_batch_*.csv", delimiter: ","}
    49	  stripe:
    50	    prefix: stripe/payouts
    51	    glob: 'payout_reconciliation_*.csv'
    52	  worldpay: {prefix: worldpay/eod, glob: "*.EOD", delimiter: "|"}
    53	matching:
    54	  fuzzy_window_days: 1
    55	  batch_psps: [sepa_dd]
    56	notify:
    57	    channel: "#payments-ops"
    58	    mention_on_exceptions: ["@pay-oncall"]
    59	"""
    60	
    61	# fmt: markdown
    62	CONFIG_HELP = r"""
    63	## Configuration file
    64	
    65	The file passed with `--config` is merged **one level deep** into the defaults, so you only need to list what you want to change.  For example, to widen the fuzzy window for a PSP that is known to settle late and to silence the on-call mention:
    66	
    67	```yaml
    68	matching:
    69	    fuzzy_window_days:   3
    70	notify: {mention_on_exceptions: []}
    71	```
    72	
    73	Unknown top-level keys are rejected with exit code `1`, so typos do not go unnoticed.
    74	"""
    75	
    76	# fmt: markdown
    77	# ## Matching rules
    78	#
    79	# Matching runs in passes, from the most to the least specific.   A line matched in an earlier pass is never reconsidered, which keeps the result deterministic even when a PSP sends duplicate references.
    80	#
    81	# 1. **Exact** -- the PSP reference equals the ledger posting's `external_ref`.
    82	# 2. **Fuzzy** -- same merchant, currency and amount, value date within `fuzzy_window_days` days.
    83	#    Ties go to the earliest ledger posting.
    84	# 3. **Batch** -- for PSPs that settle in aggregate (looking at you, SEPA direct debit), compare per-merchant daily totals instead of individual lines.
    85	#
    86	# Anything left over becomes a row in `recon.exceptions` with reason `UNMATCHED`.
    87	
    88	
    89	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    90	class SettlementLine:
    91	    psp: str
    92	    psp_reference: str
    93	    merchant_id: str
    94	    currency: str
    95	    amount_minor: int
    96	    value_date: dt.date
    97	    fee_minor: int = 0
    98	
    99	
   100	@dataclass
   101	class ReconResult:
   102	    matched: list[tuple[SettlementLine, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
   103	    unmatched: list[SettlementLine] = field(default_factory=list)
   104	
   105	    @property
   106	    def exit_code(self) -> int:
   107	        return 3 if self.unmatched else 0
   108	
   109	    def totals_by_currency(self) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
   110	        totals: dict[str, list[int]] = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])
   111	        for line, _ in self.matched:
   112	            totals[line.currency][0] += line.amount_minor
   113	            totals[line.currency][1] += line.fee_minor
   114	        return {cur: (net, fees) for cur, (net, fees) in sorted(totals.items())}
   115	
   116	
   117	def load_config(path: Path | None) -> dict:
   118	    config = yaml.safe_load(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML)
   119	    if path is None:
   120	        return config
   121	    override = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
   122	    unknown = set(override) - set(config)
   123	    if unknown:
   124	        raise SystemExit(f"unknown config keys: {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
   125	    for key, value in override.items():
   126	        config[key] = {**config[key], **value}
   127	    return config
   128	
   129	
   130	def fetch_report(psp: str, business_date: dt.date, cfg: dict) -> Iterator[dict[str, str]]:
   131	    s3 = boto3.client("s3")
   132	    prefix = f"{cfg['psp'][psp]['prefix']}/{business_date:%Y/%m/%d}/"
   133	    for obj in s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket=INBOX_BUCKET, Prefix=prefix).get("Contents", []):
   134	        body = s3.get_object(Bucket=INBOX_BUCKET, Key=obj["Key"])["Body"].read().decode("utf-8-sig")
   135	        yield from csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(body), delimiter=cfg["psp"][psp].get("delimiter", ","))
   136	
   137	
   138	def to_minor(value: str | None) -> int:
   139	    return int(Decimal(value or "0").scaleb(2))
   140

#' ---
#' title: "Greenhouse sensors: summer 2024"
#' author: "Jo"
#' date: "2024-09-28"
#' format:
#'   html:
#'     code-fold: true
#'     embed-resources: true
#' ---
#'
#' Quick look at the three ESPHome sensor nodes in the greenhouse (well, polytunnel). Data comes out of Home Assistant's long-term statistics via the InfluxDB export, see `export.flux` in this folder.

#| label: setup
#| message:   false
#| warning: FALSE
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

# fmt: markdown
# ## Sensor nodes
#
# There are three nodes, all ESP32-C3 boards with an SHT31 for air temperature and humidity, plus a capacitive probe stuck in the soil of the middle bed:
#
# | node | location | notes |
# |------|----------|-------|
# | `gh-north` | north end, next to the door | gets a blast of cold air every time the door opens |
# | `gh-mid` | middle bed, 1m up | the "reference" one |
# | `gh-south` | south end, by the water butt | **in direct sun** from 2pm, afternoon readings are rubbish |
#
# The soil probes are uncalibrated, so I only ever look at the *relative* change.

#| label: load
#| cache: TRUE
readings <- read_csv("data/greenhouse-2024.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    time = with_tz(time, "Europe/London"),
    node = factor(node, levels = c("gh-north", "gh-mid", "gh-south"))
  ) |>
  filter(time >= ymd("2024-05-01"), time < ymd("2024-09-01"))

# the south node boot-looped for two days in July, drop those
readings <- readings |> filter(!(node == "gh-south" & between(time, ymd_hm("2024-07-09 10:00"), ymd_hm("2024-07-11 18:30"))))

# thresholds for the "hot days" counts below. Kept as YAML so the Home
# Assistant automation can read the exact same file.
thresholds_yaml <- r"(
hot:   35      # C, tomatoes stop setting fruit above this
cold: 4
humid: {max: 90, hours: 6}
alert_nodes: [gh-mid, "gh-north"]
)"
thresholds <- yaml::yaml.load(thresholds_yaml)

#| label: fig-daily
#| fig-cap: "Daily max/min air temperature per node. The grey band is the period with the shade net up."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height:  4.5
#| fig-alt: Daily maximum and minimum temperature for three nodes from May to August, maximums mostly between 25 and 40 degrees
daily <- readings |>
  mutate(day = as_date(time)) |>
  group_by(node, day) |>
  summarise(tmax = max(temp_c, na.rm = TRUE), tmin = min(temp_c, na.rm = TRUE), rh = mean(rh, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(daily, aes(day)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = ymd("2024-07-01"), xmax = ymd("2024-08-15"), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = tmax, colour = node)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = tmin, colour = node), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = thresholds$hot, colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "°C", colour = NULL)

# fmt: markdown
# ### Did the shade net help?
#
# Short answer: yes, a bit. Long answer: the comparison is confounded by July being cooler than June anyway, so the raw before/after numbers overstate it.  Comparing `gh-mid` against the outdoor sensor on the shed (not in this dataset, it's in a different InfluxDB bucket because past me is an idiot) the gap between inside and outside dropped from roughly 9 degrees to roughly 6.
#
# + days over 35C before the net: lots
# + days over 35C with the net: fewer
#    + but still some, mostly at the south end
# + tomatoes: did not care either way, they were delicious

#| label: tbl-hot-days
#| tbl-cap: Days per month where the max temperature went over the "hot" threshold, or the min went under the "cold" one
#| layout-ncol: 1
hot_days <- daily |>
  mutate(month = month(day, label = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(node, month) |>
  summarise(hot = sum(tmax > thresholds$hot), cold = sum(tmin < thresholds$cold), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = node, values_from = c(hot, cold), values_fill = 0)
knitr::kable(hot_days)

# fmt: markdown
#' ## Humidity
#'
#' Humidity is the one I actually care about, because of blight.  Anything above 90% for more than ~6 hours in a row counts as a "blight risk" period in the plot below, which is the same rule the Home Assistant automation uses to send me a notification and open the vent.
#'
#' * `gh-mid` is the one the automation listens to
#' * the vent motor is a cheap linear actuator, so "open" means "open-ish"

#| label: fig-humidity
#| fig-cap: "Daily mean relative humidity"
#| fig-subcap:
#| - "All nodes"
#| - 'gh-mid only'
#| layout-ncol: 2
ggplot(daily, aes(day, rh, colour = node)) + geom_line() + geom_hline(yintercept = thresholds$humid$max, linetype = "dotted")
ggplot(filter(daily, node == "gh-mid"), aes(day, rh)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue")

# fmt: markdown
summary_md <- "
## Greenhouse summary, summer 2024

The hottest day was **%s** at %.1f °C (node `%s`). There were %d days over %d °C in total, most of them in June before the shade net went up.

* humidity alerts: %d
* sensor dropouts longer than an hour: %d
"

hottest <- daily |> slice_max(tmax, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
msg <- sprintf(
  summary_md,
  format(hottest$day, "%d %B"), hottest$tmax, as.character(hottest$node),
  sum(daily$tmax > thresholds$hot), thresholds$hot,
  0L, 2L
)
writeLines(msg, "out/summary.md")

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
ntfy_message <- r"[
Greenhouse report for **summer 2024** is ready! Hottest node was `gh-south`, as always. The HTML version is on the NAS: <http://nas.lan/reports/greenhouse-2024.html>

- tomatoes: 14.2 kg (approx., the kitchen scale is not great)
- chillies: lots vs. last year's none. Next year: fewer chillies.
]"
httr2::request("https://ntfy.sh/jo-greenhouse") |>
  httr2::req_headers(Markdown = "yes", Title = "Greenhouse report") |>
  httr2::req_body_raw(ntfy_message) |>
  httr2::req_perform()

#| label: session
#| echo: false
#| include: !expr interactive()
sessionInfo()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# fmt: markdown
"""Reconcile PSP settlement files against the internal ledger.

This script is run by the **payments-ops** cron (`ops/cron/settlement.yaml`) every morning at 06:15 CET, after all payment service providers have dropped their settlement reports into the settlement inbox (synced from `s3://acme-pay-settlement-inbox`).  It can also be run by hand when a PSP re-sends a corrected file.

Usage
-----

    python reconcile_settlements.py --psp adyen --date 2026-11-16 --dry-run

What it does:
* reads the settlement report for the given PSP and business date,
* normalises every line into a `SettlementLine` (amounts in minor units),
+ matches lines to ledger postings, see *Matching rules* below,
* writes unmatched items to `recon.exceptions` and posts a summary to the payments-ops channel.

Exit codes: `0` if everything matched, `3` if exceptions were found (not an error, but somebody has to look at them), `1` for anything else.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import datetime as dt
import logging
import os
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable, Iterator

import psycopg
import requests
import yaml

log = logging.getLogger("recon")

INBOX_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("RECON_INBOX_DIR", "/srv/settlement-inbox"))
TEAMS_WEBHOOK = os.environ.get("RECON_TEAMS_WEBHOOK", "")

# Defaults; override with --config path/to/recon.yaml (merged one level deep).
DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML = """
psp:
  adyen:   {prefix: adyen/settlement, glob: "settlement_detail_report_batch_*.csv", delimiter: ","}
  worldpay: {prefix: worldpay/eod, glob: '*.EOD', delimiter: "|"}
matching:
  fuzzy_window_days: 1
notify:
    channel: "#payments-ops"
    mention_on_exceptions: ["@pay-oncall"]
"""

# fmt: markdown
CONFIG_HELP = r"""
## Configuration file

The file passed with `--config` is merged **one level deep** into the defaults, so you only need to list what you want to change.  For example, to widen the fuzzy window for a PSP that is known to settle late and to silence the on-call mention:

```yaml
matching:
    fuzzy_window_days:   3
notify: {mention_on_exceptions: []}
```

Unknown top-level keys are rejected with exit code `1`, so typos do not go unnoticed.
"""

# fmt: markdown
# ## Matching rules
#
# Matching runs in passes, from the most to the least specific.   A line matched in an earlier pass is never reconsidered, which keeps the result deterministic even when a PSP sends duplicate references.
#
# 1. **Exact** -- the PSP reference equals the ledger posting's `external_ref`.
# 2. **Fuzzy** -- same merchant, currency and amount, value date within `fuzzy_window_days` days.
#    Ties go to the earliest ledger posting.
# 3. **Batch** -- for PSPs that settle in aggregate (looking at you, SEPA direct debit), compare per-merchant daily totals instead of individual lines.
#
# Anything left over becomes a row in `recon.exceptions` with reason `UNMATCHED`.
MATCH_SQL = """
    SELECT posting_id FROM ledger.postings
    WHERE NOT reconciled
      AND (external_ref = %(ref)s
           OR (merchant_id = %(merchant)s AND currency = %(currency)s AND amount_minor = %(amount)s
               AND value_date BETWEEN %(earliest)s AND %(latest)s))
    ORDER BY external_ref = %(ref)s DESC, created_at
    LIMIT 1
"""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SettlementLine:
    psp: str
    psp_reference: str
    merchant_id: str
    currency: str
    amount_minor: int
    value_date: dt.date


@dataclass
class ReconResult:
    matched: list[tuple[SettlementLine, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    unmatched: list[SettlementLine] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def exit_code(self) -> int:
        return 3 if self.unmatched else 0


def load_config(path: Path | None) -> dict:
    config = yaml.safe_load(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML)
    if path is None:
        return config
    override = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
    if unknown := set(override) - set(config):
        raise SystemExit(f"unknown config keys: {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
    return {key: {**value, **override.get(key, {})} for key, value in config.items()}


def read_report(psp: str, business_date: dt.date, cfg: dict) -> Iterator[dict[str, str]]:
    psp_cfg = cfg["psp"][psp]
    for path in sorted((INBOX_DIR / psp_cfg["prefix"] / f"{business_date:%Y/%m/%d}").glob(psp_cfg["glob"])):
        with path.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as fh:
            yield from csv.DictReader(fh, delimiter=psp_cfg.get("delimiter", ","))


def normalise(psp: str, rows: Iterable[dict[str, str]]) -> list[SettlementLine]:
    return [
        SettlementLine(
            psp=psp,
            psp_reference=row["Psp Reference"].strip(),
            merchant_id=row["Merchant Account"],
            currency=row["Net Currency"],
            amount_minor=int(Decimal(row["Net Credit (NC)"] or "0").scaleb(2)),
            value_date=dt.date.fromisoformat(row["Booking Date"][:10]),
        )
        for row in rows
        if row.get("Type", "Settled") in {"Settled", "SettledBulk"}
    ]


def match(lines: list[SettlementLine], conn: psycopg.Connection, cfg: dict) -> ReconResult:
    # fmt: markdown
    # Passes 1 and 2 only.  The *batch* pass for `sepa_dd` is tracked in PAY-2210; until it lands, SEPA direct debit lines that settle in aggregate show up as exceptions and have to be cleared by payments-ops by hand.
    result = ReconResult()
    window = dt.timedelta(days=cfg["matching"]["fuzzy_window_days"])
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        for line in lines:
            params = {"ref": line.psp_reference, "merchant": line.merchant_id, "currency": line.currency, "amount": line.amount_minor}
            cur.execute(MATCH_SQL, params | {"earliest": line.value_date - window, "latest": line.value_date + window})
            if (row := cur.fetchone()) is None:
                result.unmatched.append(line)
            else:
                result.matched.append((line, row[0]))
    return result


def write_exceptions(conn: psycopg.Connection, unmatched: list[SettlementLine]) -> None:
    conn.cursor().executemany(
        "INSERT INTO recon.exceptions (psp, psp_reference, merchant_id, currency, amount_minor, value_date, reason)"
        " VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, 'UNMATCHED') ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING",
        [(u.psp, u.psp_reference, u.merchant_id, u.currency, u.amount_minor, u.value_date) for u in unmatched],
    )


def render_summary(result: ReconResult, psp: str, business_date: dt.date) -> str:
    totals: dict[str, int] = {}
    for line, _ in result.matched:
        totals[line.currency] = totals.get(line.currency, 0) + line.amount_minor
    rows = "\n".join(f"| {cur} | {total / 100:,.2f} |" for cur, total in sorted(totals.items()))
    # fmt: markdown
    return f"""
### Settlement reconciliation: {psp} / {business_date:%Y-%m-%d}

Matched **{len(result.matched)}** lines; **{len(result.unmatched)}** need attention.   Amounts are net of PSP fees, so they will not match the gross figures shown in the PSP portal.

| Currency | Net settled |
|---|--:|
{rows}

_Generated by reconcile_settlements.py at {dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc):%Y-%m-%d %H:%M} UTC._
"""


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    # fmt: markdown
    epilog = """
        Examples:

        * re-run yesterday's Adyen file without writing anything:
          `reconcile_settlements.py --psp adyen --date yesterday --dry-run`
        * reconcile a corrected Worldpay file that arrived late, with a wider fuzzy window: `reconcile_settlements.py --psp worldpay --date 2026-11-14 --config late-files.yaml`
        """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0], epilog=epilog, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--psp", required=True, choices=["adyen", "worldpay"])
    parser.add_argument("--date", default="yesterday", help="business date, YYYY-MM-DD or 'yesterday'")
    parser.add_argument("--config", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
    business_date = dt.date.today() - dt.timedelta(days=1) if args.date == "yesterday" else dt.date.fromisoformat(args.date)
    cfg = load_config(args.config)
    lines = normalise(args.psp, read_report(args.psp, business_date, cfg))
    log.info("loaded %d settlement lines for %s on %s", len(lines), args.psp, business_date)
    with psycopg.connect(os.environ["LEDGER_DSN"]) as conn:
        result = match(lines, conn, cfg)
        if not args.dry_run:
            write_exceptions(conn, result.unmatched)
    summary = render_summary(result, args.psp, business_date)
    if TEAMS_WEBHOOK and not args.dry_run:
        requests.post(TEAMS_WEBHOOK, json={"text": summary}, timeout=10).raise_for_status()
    else:
        print(summary)
    return result.exit_code


# %%
#| label: explore-exceptions
#| echo:   false
#| tags: [debug,  interactive]
#| fig-cap: "Unmatched settlement lines by currency for yesterday's Adyen file (interactive session only)"
if "ipykernel" in sys.modules:
    import pandas as pd

    _lines = normalise("adyen", read_report("adyen", dt.date.today() - dt.timedelta(days=1), load_config(None)))
    pd.DataFrame([vars(line) for line in _lines]).groupby("currency").amount_minor.sum().plot.bar()

# %%
if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

---
title: "Is the dice goblin cursed?"
subtitle:   "A totally serious statistical investigation of 4,000+ d20 rolls"
author: "Priya S."
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"
output:
    html_document:
        toc: yes
        toc_float: true
        code_folding: hide
        theme: flatly
params:
  bot_log: "data/rolls.csv"
  min_rolls: 30
editor_options:
  markdown:
    wrap: sentence
  chunk_output_type: console
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
rolls <- read_csv(params$bot_log)
```

## Background

Our D&D group uses a Discord bot (the "dice goblin", written by Ines, source at https://github.com/inesferreira/dicegoblin) for every single roll. Over the last few months Tom has become convinced that the goblin hates him specifically. His evidence: he rolled three natural 1s in a row on Thursday 14 March, i.e. the night his paladin nearly died. Is that suspicious? Not really! The probability of three 1s in a row on a fair d20 is 1 in 8000, which sounds tiny, but we roll a *lot* of dice. So I decided to settle this properly, with data vs. with yelling. Mr. Whiskers (Ines's cat, who walks across her keyboard during every session) is not considered a confounder.

## The data

The bot logs every roll to a CSV file (`rolls.csv`) with the user, the expression and each individual die. I only kept plain `d20` rolls, i.e. no advantage or disadvantage, because `2d20kh1` is not uniform (that's the whole point of it). That leaves `r nrow(rolls)` rolls from 6 players over 23 sessions. Session No. 5 is missing because the bot was down; Ines says it was "a Docker thing".

```{r d20-only}
d20 <- rolls %>% filter(expr == "d20") %>% mutate(face = as.integer(result))
nrow(d20)
```

## Is the die fair overall?

```{r overall-histogram, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Distribution of all plain d20 rolls. The dashed line is the expected count for a fair die.", fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
expected <- nrow(d20) / 20
ggplot(d20, aes(face)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#58508d") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = expected, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:20) +
  labs(x = "Face", y = "Count")
```

A chi-squared goodness-of-fit test is the obvious first step. With 20 faces there are 19 degrees of freedom, and the test statistic came out at `r round(chisq.test(table(d20$face))$statistic, 1)` with p = `r signif(chisq.test(table(d20$face))$p.value, 2)`. In plain English: no evidence at all that the die is unfair. The most common face was 17 and the least common was 9. Neither of those is a 1, Tom.

## But what about Tom specifically?

Fine. Let's look at each player separately (see Fig. 2 below). There is an obvious multiple-comparisons problem here, e.g. with six players the chance that at least one of them looks "unlucky" at the 5% level is approx. 26%, so I used a Bonferroni correction. Dr. Google tells me that's conservative. That is fine, conservative is what we want when the alternative hypothesis is "the goblin is cursed".

```{r per-player, fig.cap="Mean roll per player with 95% intervals. A fair d20 has a mean of 10.5."}
d20 %>%
  group_by(user) %>%
  filter(n() >= params$min_rolls) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(face), se = sd(face) / sqrt(n)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(reorder(user, mean), mean)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = mean - 1.96 * se, ymax = mean + 1.96 * se)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10.5, linetype = "dotted") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean d20 roll")
```

Results, in no particular order:

* **Tom** averaged 10.2 over 731 rolls. That is below 10.5! It is also completely normal. His three 1s in a row did happen, but so did Mags's four 20s in two sessions and nobody complained about that.
* **Priya** (me) averaged 10.9. I would like it noted that I did not tamper with the bot. I don't even know Python.
* **Dev** only has 88 rolls because he joined in May, so his interval is huge. Welcome, Dev!
* Everyone else was within 0.4 of 10.5.

| player | rolls | mean | nat 1s | nat 20s |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Tom | 731 | 10.2 | 41 | 33 |
| Priya | 702 | 10.9 | 30 | 38 |
| Mags | 688 | 10.6 | 33 | 37 |

## Streaks

The streak question is more interesting. How often should we see three 1s in a row from *someone* at the table? I simulated 10,000 campaigns of the same length as ours (same number of sessions, same rolls per player per session) with `sample(1:20, replace = TRUE)` and counted how many had at least one triple-1 streak. The answer was 41%. So, roughly a coin flip. Tom's streak is about as surprising as getting heads.[^sim]

```{r streaks, cache=TRUE}
set.seed(2024)
sim <- replicate(10000, {
  runs <- rle(sample(1:20, nrow(d20), replace = TRUE) == 1)
  any(runs$lengths[runs$values] >= 3)
})
mean(sim)
```

> Tom, reading a draft of this: "ok but what if the goblin knows when it's me". He then asked whether the bot could be "re-seeded with good vibes". It cannot. The bot uses `random.SystemRandom()`, which reads from the operating system, so there is nothing to re-seed!

## Conclusions

1. The dice goblin is not cursed. The `SystemRandom` source it uses (see `dicegoblin.py`, line 60 or so) is about as fair as it gets.
2. Tom is not cursed either. He is just a person who remembers his bad rolls. We all are!
3. Humans are terrible at judging randomness. This is well documented, see e.g. Tversky and Kahneman (1971), and it is also documented in every D&D group chat ever.

Next steps? ---
title: "Is the dice goblin cursed?"
subtitle:   "A totally serious statistical investigation of 4,000+ d20 rolls"
author: "Priya S."
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"
output:
    html_document:
        toc: yes
        toc_float: true
        code_folding: hide
        theme: flatly
params:
  bot_log: "data/rolls.csv"
  min_rolls: 30
editor_options:
  markdown:
    wrap: sentence
  chunk_output_type: console
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
rolls <- read_csv(params$bot_log)
```

## Background

Our D&D group uses a Discord bot (the "dice goblin", written by Ines, source at https://github.com/inesferreira/dicegoblin) for every single roll. Over the last few months Tom has become convinced that the goblin hates him specifically. His evidence: he rolled three natural 1s in a row on Thursday 14 March, i.e. the night his paladin nearly died. Is that suspicious? Not really! The probability of three 1s in a row on a fair d20 is 1 in 8000, which sounds tiny, but we roll a *lot* of dice. So I decided to settle this properly, with data vs. with yelling. Mr. Whiskers (Ines's cat, who walks across her keyboard during every session) is not considered a confounder.

## The data

The bot logs every roll to a CSV file (`rolls.csv`) with the user, the expression and each individual die. I only kept plain `d20` rolls, i.e. no advantage or disadvantage, because `2d20kh1` is not uniform (that's the whole point of it). That leaves `r nrow(rolls)` rolls from 6 players over 23 sessions. Session No. 5 is missing because the bot was down; Ines says it was "a Docker thing".

```{r d20-only}
d20 <- rolls %>% filter(expr == "d20") %>% mutate(face = as.integer(result))
nrow(d20)
```

## Is the die fair overall?

```{r overall-histogram, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Distribution of all plain d20 rolls. The dashed line is the expected count for a fair die.", fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
expected <- nrow(d20) / 20
ggplot(d20, aes(face)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#58508d") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = expected, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:20) +
  labs(x = "Face", y = "Count")
```

A chi-squared goodness-of-fit test is the obvious first step. With 20 faces there are 19 degrees of freedom, and the test statistic came out at `r round(chisq.test(table(d20$face))$statistic, 1)` with p = `r signif(chisq.test(table(d20$face))$p.value, 2)`. In plain English: no evidence at all that the die is unfair. The most common face was 17 and the least common was 9. Neither of those is a 1, Tom.

## But what about Tom specifically?

Fine. Let's look at each player separately (see Fig. 2 below). There is an obvious multiple-comparisons problem here, e.g. with six players the chance that at least one of them looks "unlucky" at the 5% level is approx. 26%, so I used a Bonferroni correction. Dr. Google tells me that's conservative. That is fine, conservative is what we want when the alternative hypothesis is "the goblin is cursed".

```{r per-player, fig.cap="Mean roll per player with 95% intervals. A fair d20 has a mean of 10.5."}
d20 %>%
  group_by(user) %>%
  filter(n() >= params$min_rolls) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(face), se = sd(face) / sqrt(n)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(reorder(user, mean), mean)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = mean - 1.96 * se, ymax = mean + 1.96 * se)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10.5, linetype = "dotted") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean d20 roll")
```

Results, in no particular order:

* **Tom** averaged 10.2 over 731 rolls. That is below 10.5! It is also completely normal. His three 1s in a row did happen, but so did Mags's four 20s in two sessions and nobody complained about that.
* **Priya** (me) averaged 10.9. I would like it noted that I did not tamper with the bot. I don't even know Python.
* **Dev** only has 88 rolls because he joined in May, so his interval is huge. Welcome, Dev!
* Everyone else was within 0.4 of 10.5.

| player | rolls | mean | nat 1s | nat 20s |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Tom | 731 | 10.2 | 41 | 33 |
| Priya | 702 | 10.9 | 30 | 38 |
| Mags | 688 | 10.6 | 33 | 37 |

## Streaks

The streak question is more interesting. How often should we see three 1s in a row from *someone* at the table? I simulated 10,000 campaigns of the same length as ours (same number of sessions, same rolls per player per session) with `sample(1:20, replace = TRUE)` and counted how many had at least one triple-1 streak. The answer was 41%. So, roughly a coin flip. Tom's streak is about as surprising as getting heads.[^sim]

```{r streaks, cache=TRUE}
set.seed(2024)
sim <- replicate(10000, {
  runs <- rle(sample(1:20, nrow(d20), replace = TRUE) == 1)
  any(runs$lengths[runs$values] >= 3)
})
mean(sim)
```

> Tom, reading a draft of this: "ok but what if the goblin knows when it's me". He then asked whether the bot could be "re-seeded with good vibes". It cannot. The bot uses `random.SystemRandom()`, which reads from the operating system, so there is nothing to re-seed!

## Conclusions

1. The dice goblin is not cursed. The `SystemRandom` source it uses (see `dicegoblin.py`, line 60 or so) is about as fair as it gets.
2. Tom is not cursed either. He is just a person who remembers his bad rolls. We all are!
3. Humans are terrible at judging randomness. This is well documented, see e.g. Tversky and Kahneman (1971), and it is also documented in every D&D group chat ever.

Next steps? I'd like to check whether people roll differently on their phone vs. on desktop (they shouldn't, the bot doesn't know), and whether rolls are more likely to get re-rolled ("my cat stepped on enter!!") after a low result. That second one isn't about the dice at all, it's about us. *Spoiler: it's Tom. It's always Tom.*

[^sim]: The simulation ignores that some rolls happen in quick bursts (e.g. fireball damage), which makes streaks slightly *more* likely in practice. So if anything, 41% is an underestimate. Sorry, Tom.

---

*Data: 23 sessions, Jan.–Jun. 2024. Code and data are at https://github.com/priyas/goblin-stats if you want to check my work. No goblins were harmed.*

#' ---
#' title:    "Occupancy of medium and large mammals in Kakamega forest fragments"
#' author: "Amani Wekesa"
#' date: '2024-04-09'
#' format:
#'   html:
#'     code-fold: true
#'     toc: true
#' bibliography: refs.bib
#' ---

#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning:   false
library(tidyverse)
library(unmarked)
library(AICcmodavg)
library(here)

set.seed(20240409)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11))

dh   <- read_rds(here("data", "derived", "detection_histories_2022.rds"))
covs <- read_csv(here("data", "site_covariates.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# fmt: markdown
#' ## Data
#'
#' We deployed `r nrow(covs)` camera stations (Browning Strike Force, 20 s between triggers) in the main forest block and in three fragments between June and September 2022, at least 1 km apart and as close as possible to the grid points of the 2016 TEAM survey so that the two surveys can be compared later.  Images were tagged in Timelapse by me and two field assistants; every record of a rare species was checked by a second person.
#'
#' * occasion length: 7 days, i.e. 8 occasions over the 56-day deployment
#' * stations that failed before day 28 were dropped (n = 3)
#' + all site covariates are standardised to mean 0 and SD 1 before fitting

#| label: covariates
covs_std <- covs |>
  mutate(
    across(c(dist_edge_m, canopy_pct, elev_m, dist_village_m), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)), .names = "{.col}_z"),
    fragment = factor(fragment, levels = c("Main block", "Kisere", "Malava", "Kaimosi"))
  ) |>
  arrange(station)

stopifnot(identical(covs_std$station, rownames(dh$golden_cat)))

# fmt: markdown
# ### Notes on model selection
#
# I fit the same candidate set for every species, which is not ideal for the rare ones (golden cat: 11 detections in total!) but keeps the chapter readable and was what my committee asked for in the 2023 progress meeting.  Detection is always modelled with effort, because cameras were not all active for the full occasion.
#
# 1. null model, `~1 ~1`
# 2. detection covariate only
# 3) edge, then edge + canopy, then the full model with fragment
#
# Model averaging over the whole set is done with `AICcmodavg::modavgPred()`, see Burnham & Anderson (2002), chapter 4.

species <- c("golden_cat", "blue_duiker", "bushpig", "civet", "genet")

fit_species <- function(sp) {
  umf <- unmarkedFrameOccu(
    y = dh[[sp]],
    siteCovs = covs_std |> select(ends_with("_z"), fragment),
    obsCovs = list(effort = dh$effort)
  )
  mods <- list(
    null    = occu(~1 ~1, data = umf),
    det     = occu(~effort ~1, data = umf),
    edge    = occu(~effort ~dist_edge_m_z, data = umf),
    habitat = occu(~effort ~dist_edge_m_z + canopy_pct_z, data = umf),
    full    = occu(~effort ~dist_edge_m_z + canopy_pct_z + dist_village_m_z + fragment, data = umf)
  )
  list(umf = umf, mods = mods, aic = aictab(mods, second.ord = TRUE))
}

fits <- set_names(species) |> map(fit_species, .progress = TRUE)

#| label: tbl-aic
#| tbl-cap: "AICc model selection table for each species. Only models with ΔAICc < 4 are shown."
fits |>
  map(\(f) as_tibble(f$aic)) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "species") |>
  filter(Delta_AICc < 4) |>
  select(species, model = Modnames, K, AICc, delta = Delta_AICc, weight = AICcWt) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

#| label: fig-edge
#| fig-cap: "Predicted occupancy probability against distance to the forest edge (model-averaged, 95% CI). Rug marks show the stations."
#| fig-subcap: ["Golden cat", "Blue duiker"]
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height:   3.5
newdat <- tibble(dist_edge_m = seq(0, 3000, by = 50)) |>
  mutate(
    dist_edge_m_z = (dist_edge_m - mean(covs$dist_edge_m)) / sd(covs$dist_edge_m),
    canopy_pct_z = 0, dist_village_m_z = 0, fragment = factor("Main block", levels = levels(covs_std$fragment))
  )

for (sp in c("golden_cat", "blue_duiker")) {
  pr <- modavgPred(fits[[sp]]$mods, newdata = as.data.frame(newdat), parm.type = "psi")
  p <- newdat |>
    mutate(psi = pr$mod.avg.pred, lo = pr$lower.CL, hi = pr$upper.CL) |>
    ggplot(aes(dist_edge_m, psi)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_rug(data = covs, aes(x = dist_edge_m), inherit.aes = FALSE, sides = "b", alpha = 0.5) +
    labs(x = "Distance to forest edge (m)", y = expression(hat(psi))) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1))
  print(p)
}

# numbers for the steering committee summary below
gc <- modavgPred(fits$golden_cat$mods, newdata = as.data.frame(newdat[1, ]), parm.type = "psi")
psi_gc <- round(gc$mod.avg.pred, 2)
lo_gc  <- round(gc$lower.CL, 2)
hi_gc  <- round(gc$upper.CL, 2)

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
committee_summary <- r"[
## Camera-trap results 2022 (summary for the steering committee)

Occupancy of the African golden cat at the forest edge was low (ψ = {psi_gc}, 95% CI {lo_gc}–{hi_gc}) and increased with distance into the forest. Blue duikers were detected at almost every station. Detection probability per 7-day occasion was low for all carnivores, i.e. a 56-day deployment is the minimum we would recommend for the 2023 season. Full results are in Table 3.2 of the thesis chapter.

**Recommendation:** keep the 2023 grid, but add ten stations in the Malava fragment where we currently have only four.
]"
cat(glue::glue(committee_summary))

# fmt: markdown
readme_txt <- r"---(
---
title: "Kakamega camera-trap detection histories, 2022"
creator:   [Amani Wekesa, "Kenya Wildlife Service – Western Conservation Area"]
license: CC-BY-4.0
temporal_coverage: {start: 2022-06-01, end: 2022-09-30}
---

# Detection histories, Kakamega 2022

This folder contains the detection histories used in Chapter 3. Each `.csv` file has one row per station and one column per 7-day occasion; `NA` means the camera was not working during that occasion.

Station coordinates are **not** included because of the poaching risk.  Ask KWS for access.
)---"

walk(species, \(sp) write_csv(as_tibble(dh[[sp]], rownames = "station"), here("data", "derived", paste0("dh_", sp, ".csv"))))
writeLines(readme_txt, here("data", "derived", "README.md"))

[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.0000000.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.0000000) [![License: CC BY 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-CC%20BY%204.0-lightgrey.svg)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) [![targets](https://github.com/reef-ecology/caribbean-reef-fish/actions/workflows/targets.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/reef-ecology/caribbean-reef-fish/actions) Caribbean reef fish surveys, 2009–2023 ======================================

Data and code for __"Two decades of change in Caribbean reef fish assemblages after the lionfish invasion"__ (Ramírez, Okafor & Thompson, *in review*). If you are a reviewer: hello! Everything you need to reproduce the figures and tables of the manuscript is in this repository, and the whole pipeline runs in about 25 minutes on a recent laptop (most of that time is spent fitting the hierarchical models in Stan). The repository is organised as a [research compendium](https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2017.1375986 "Marwick, Boettiger & Mullen (2018)"), i.e. an R-package-like structure in which the analysis code, the data and the manuscript live together and are versioned together. ## Contents ## ``` . ├── data-raw/ # survey sheets as entered by the dive teams (do not edit!) ├── data/ # cleaned data, created by data-raw/clean_surveys.R ├── R/ # functions used by the targets pipeline ├── analysis/ │ ├── _targets.R │ ├── config.yml │ └── manuscript.qmd └── renv.lock ``` ## Getting started You need R (>= 4.2), a working C++ toolchain for **cmdstanr**, and roughly 4 GB of free disk space. 1) Clone the repository and open `caribbean-reef-fish.Rproj` in RStudio. 2) Restore the package library: ```r install.packages("renv") renv::restore() cmdstanr::install_cmdstan(version = "2.34.1") ``` 3) Run the pipeline: ```r targets::tar_make() ``` Results end up in `analysis/outputs/`, and the manuscript is rendered to `analysis/manuscript.html`. #!/usr/bin/env python3

# fmt: markdown
"""
dicegoblin
==========

A small Discord bot for our Thursday night D&D group.  It rolls dice, keeps track of whose turn it is to bring snacks, and nags everyone about the next session so we stop having the "wait, is it this week??" conversation every single Wednesday.

Setup:
1. Create an application + bot user in the Discord developer portal and copy the token.
2. `export DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN=...` (or put it in a `.env` file next to this script)
3. `python dicegoblin.py --init` writes a default `dicegoblin.yaml`, then edit the channel ids in it
4. `python dicegoblin.py` and leave it running somewhere (mine lives on the homelab NUC, in docker)

Requirements:
*   Python 3.10+ (I use `X | None` everywhere, sorry)
*   discord.py >= 2.3 and PyYAML

A minimal config looks like this, everything else has defaults:

```yaml
prefix:   "!"
session: {day: thursday,   time: "19:30"}
channels:
    announcements: 123456789012345678
```

MIT licensed, do whatever you want with it. No warranty, *especially* not for natural 1s.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import os
import random
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import discord
import yaml
from discord.ext import commands, tasks

CONFIG_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("DICEGOBLIN_CONFIG", Path(__file__).with_name("dicegoblin.yaml")))

# fmt: markdown
# ## Dice syntax
#
# The roller understands the usual tabletop notation. It's case-insensitive and whitespace is ignored:
#
# | expression | what it does |
# |---|:--|
# | `d20` | one twenty-sided die |
# | `4d6kh3` | roll four d6 and keep the highest three (stat rolls) |
# | `2d20kl1` | disadvantage, keep the lowest |
# | `1d8+3`, `2d6 - 1` | flat modifiers |
#
# Anything else gets a goblin-themed error message.  Exploding dice (`!`) are on the todo list, but honestly nobody has asked for them yet and the regex is already ugly enough.
DICE_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<n>\d*)d(?P<sides>\d+)(?:k(?P<hl>[hl])(?P<keep>\d+))?(?P<mod>[+-]\d+)?$", re.IGNORECASE)  # fmt: skip


class DiceError(ValueError):
    pass


def roll(expr: str, rng: random.Random | None = None) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """Roll `expr` and return (total, pretty string for discord)."""
    rng = rng or random.SystemRandom()
    cleaned = expr.replace(" ", "").lower()
    m = DICE_RE.match(cleaned)
    if not m:
        raise DiceError(f"the goblin squints at `{expr}` and does not understand")
    n, sides = int(m["n"] or 1), int(m["sides"])
    if not 1 <= n <= 100 or sides not in (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 20, 100):
        raise DiceError("the goblin only owns normal dice (and at most 100 of them)")
    dice = [rng.randint(1, sides) for _ in range(n)]
    kept = sorted(dice, reverse=m["hl"] != "l")[: int(m["keep"] or n)]
    mod = int(m["mod"] or 0)
    total = sum(kept) + mod
    shown = ", ".join(f"**{d}**" if d in kept else f"~~{d}~~" for d in dice)
    return total, f"`{cleaned}` → [{shown}]{f' {mod:+d}' if mod else ''} = **{total}**"


# fmt: off
DEFAULT_CONFIG = """\
# dicegoblin.yaml -- written by `dicegoblin.py --init`
prefix:   "!"
timezone: Europe/London
session:
    day: thursday
    time: "19:30"     # keep the quotes, PyYAML reads 19:30 as a number otherwise
    remind_hours_before: [24, 2]
channels: {announcements: 0, rolls: 0}   # right click a channel -> Copy Channel ID
snack_rota:
- Priya
- Tom
- "Mags"
- Dev
quiet: no
"""
# fmt: on


def load_config(path: Path = CONFIG_PATH) -> dict:
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(DEFAULT_CONFIG)
    cfg.update(yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {})
    return cfg


# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
HELP_TEXT = """
**dicegoblin** knows the following commands. The prefix is configurable, these examples use `!`.

* `!roll 4d6kh3` – roll some dice. You can roll several at once: `!roll d20 d20 1d4+1`
* `!session` – when is the next session? The goblin does the timezone maths so you don't have to.
* `!snacks` – whose turn is it to bring snacks. `!snacks skip` moves on to the next person (e.g. if someone is ill).
*  `!goblin` – the goblin says something. It is not helpful.

Rolls go to the rolls channel if one is configured, otherwise they're posted right where you asked. Don't spam it please, Tom.
"""

# Sent once when the bot joins a server. Raw string because of the shrug.
# fmt: markdown
WELCOME = r"""
Hi! I'm the **dice goblin**. I roll dice, remember whose turn it is to bring snacks, and remind you about sessions.

Type `!help` to see what I can do. If something breaks, ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯ and poke whoever invited me.
"""

# fmt: markdown
REMINDER = """
:alarm_clock: **Session in {hours} hours!**
Starts {when}.   Bring your character sheet, your dice and, if it's your turn, __snacks__.
"""


class Goblin(commands.Bot):
    def __init__(self, cfg: dict) -> None:
        intents = discord.Intents.default()
        intents.message_content = True
        super().__init__(command_prefix=cfg["prefix"], intents=intents, help_command=None)
        self.cfg = cfg
        self.snack_index = 0

    async def setup_hook(self) -> None:
        self.reminder_loop.start()

    def next_session(self) -> dt.datetime:
        now = dt.datetime.now(ZoneInfo(self.cfg["timezone"]))
        day = ["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"].index(self.cfg["session"]["day"])
        hour, minute = map(int, str(self.cfg["session"]["time"]).split(":"))
        when = now.replace(hour=hour, minute=minute, second=0, microsecond=0) + dt.timedelta(days=(day - now.weekday()) % 7)
        return when if when > now else when + dt.timedelta(days=7)

    @tasks.loop(minutes=10)
    async def reminder_loop(self) -> None:
        channel = self.get_channel(self.cfg["channels"]["announcements"])
        if self.cfg["quiet"] or channel is None:
            return
        when = self.next_session()
        hours_left = (when - dt.datetime.now(when.tzinfo)).total_seconds() / 3600
        for h in self.cfg["session"].get("remind_hours_before", [24, 2]):
            # the loop runs every 10 minutes, so only fire inside one 10 minute window
            if h - 1 / 6 < hours_left <= h:
                await channel.send(REMINDER.format(hours=h, when=discord.utils.format_dt(when, "F")))


def build_bot(cfg: dict) -> Goblin:
    bot = Goblin(cfg)

    @bot.command(name="roll", aliases=["r"])
    async def roll_cmd(ctx: commands.Context, *exprs: str) -> None:
        lines = []
        for e in exprs[:10] or ["d20"]:
            try:
                lines.append(roll(e)[1])
            except DiceError as err:
                lines.append(str(err))
        target = bot.get_channel(cfg["channels"]["rolls"]) or ctx.channel
        await target.send(f"{ctx.author.mention}\n" + "\n".join(lines))

    @bot.command()
    async def snacks(ctx: commands.Context, action: str = "") -> None:
        rota = cfg["snack_rota"] or ["nobody, apparently"]
        bot.snack_index += action == "skip"
        await ctx.send(f"Snacks this week: **{rota[bot.snack_index % len(rota)]}**")

    @bot.command(name="help")
    async def help_cmd(ctx: commands.Context) -> None:
        await ctx.send(HELP_TEXT.replace("`!", f"`{cfg['prefix']}"))

    @bot.event
    async def on_guild_join(guild: discord.Guild) -> None:
        if guild.system_channel:
            await guild.system_channel.send(WELCOME)

    return bot


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="dicegoblin", description="D&D helper bot")
    parser.add_argument("--init", action="store_true", help="write a default config and exit")
    if parser.parse_args().init:
        if CONFIG_PATH.exists():
            sys.exit(f"{CONFIG_PATH} already exists, not overwriting it")
        CONFIG_PATH.write_text(DEFAULT_CONFIG, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"wrote {CONFIG_PATH}, now go and fill in the channel ids")
        return 0
    if not (token := os.environ.get("DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN")):
        sys.exit("DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN is not set")
    build_bot(load_config()).run(token)
    return 0


# %% [markdown]
# Scratchpad: the cell below only does anything with `GOBLIN_SCRATCH=1` set. It's for poking at the roller in the VS Code interactive window.

# %%
#| label: scratch-distribution
#| eval:    false
#| code-fold: True
#| tags: [scratch,dev]
#| fig-cap: '4d6kh3, 10k rolls'
if os.environ.get("GOBLIN_SCRATCH"):
    from collections import Counter

    counts = Counter(roll("4d6kh3", random.Random(42))[0] for _ in range(10_000))
    for total in sorted(counts):
        print(f"{total:>2} {'#' * (counts[total] // 40)}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

arguments.content: --- title: "Questing *Ixodes ricinus* nymphs along an altitudinal gradient in the Šumava mountains" author: - Petra Nováková - "Tomasz W. Zieliński" date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`" output: bookdown::html_document2: toc: yes toc_float: true number_sections: true fig_caption: yes bookdown::word_document2: default bibliography: [ticks.bib, packages.bib] csl: parasites-and-vectors.csl link-citations: yes editor_options: markdown: wrap: sentence canonical: true chunk_output_type: console --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE} knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 300) library(tidyverse) library(glmmTMB) library(DHARMa) library(here) drags <- read_csv(here("data", "drag_sampling_2022_2023.csv")) sites <- read_csv(here("data", "sites.csv")) n_sites <- nrow(sites) ``` # Introduction Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) and Lyme borreliosis are the two most important vector-borne diseases in central Europe, and both are transmitted mainly by nymphs of the castor bean tick, *Ixodes ricinus* (L.). In the Czech Republic the number of notified TBE cases has fluctuated between approx. 400 and 900 per year since the mid-1990s, with a record 847 cases reported in 2020. Over the same period ticks have been found at increasingly high altitudes, e.g. up to 1,300 m a.s.l. in the Krkonoše mountains [@Danielova2006; @Materna2008]. Is this upward shift a consequence of climate warming, of changes in host populations, or simply of more sampling effort at high altitudes? The answer matters for public health, because mountain areas are popular with hikers and vaccination coverage in the Czech population is still only about 30%. Several studies have described altitudinal patterns in tick abundance [@Jouda2004; @Gilbert2010; see also @Medlock2013, pp. 12--15], but most of them sampled only a few sites, and many used a single visit per site and year. Gilbert et al. (2010) concluded that "the upper altitudinal limit of *I. ricinus* is set by the length of the season in which questing is possible." Jouda et al. (2004) found the opposite pattern in one of their three years (cf. Fig. 2 in @Jouda2004), which they attributed to an unusually dry summer. We therefore ask three questions: (i) how does the density of questing nymphs change with altitude; (ii) is this relationship modified by microclimate, i.e. by the saturation deficit at ground level; and (iii) does it differ between years? The two study years were very different. 2022 was among the driest years on record, whereas the spring of 2023 was the wettest since 1961. Prof. Hönig (pers. comm.) called this contrast "almost a natural experiment". We agree, with some caveats (see Discussion). # Methods ## Study area The study was carried out in the Šumava National Park (SW Czech Republic) and its foothills under permit No. 2021/451 of the park administration. We selected `r n_sites` sites along four transects running from the Vltava valley (ca. 450 m a.s.l.) to the main ridge near Mt. Plechý (approx. 1,250 m a.s.l.); site characteristics are listed in Table \@ref(tab:sites). All sites were in mixed or coniferous forest with a herb layer dominated by *Vaccinium myrtillus*, *Oxalis acetosella* or grasses (*Calamagrostis* spp., *Deschampsia flexuosa*). Sites were at least 500 m apart. Mean annual temperature ranges from 7.5 °C at the lowest to 3.9 °C at the highest site. ## Tick sampling Questing ticks were collected by dragging a 1 m² white flannel cloth over the vegetation along 10 transects of 10 m per site (i.e. 100 m² per visit), checking the cloth after every 10 m. Each site was visited once a month from April to October in 2022 and 2023, always between 9:00 and 13:00 and never within 24 h of rain. All ticks were stored in 70% ethanol and identified to species and stage under a stereomicroscope using the key of Estrada-Peña et al. (2017). Larvae were counted but not analysed further. At each visit we measured air temperature and relative humidity 5 cm above the ground with a handheld meter and calculated the saturation deficit (SD) following Randolph & Storey (1999): $$ SD = \left(1 - \frac{RH}{100}\right) \cdot 4.9463 \cdot e^{0.0621\,T} $$ where $RH$ is relative humidity in % and $T$ is temperature in °C. **Field protocol card (laminated version)** 1. Drag 10 × 10 m. Check cloth after each 10 m. 2. Ticks → 70% EtOH, one tube per drag. 3. Record T and RH at 5 cm. Do NOT sample within 24 h of rain! ## Statistical analysis Nymph counts per visit were modelled with negative binomial GLMMs [`glmmTMB`, @Brooks2017] with altitude (scaled), SD, year and the altitude × year interaction as fixed effects, and site and month as random intercepts. Was a zero-inflated model necessary? We compared models with and without a zero-inflation component by AIC; the ZI model was not supported (ΔAIC = 1.8). Residuals were checked with DHARMa [@Hartig2022], which showed no overdispersion (dispersion test, p = 0.41). All analyses were done in R version `r getRversion()`. ```{r model} m_nb <- glmmTMB(nymphs ~ scale(altitude) * factor(year) + sd_hpa + (1 | site) + (1 | month), family = nbinom2, data = drags) m_zi <- update(m_nb, ziformula = ~1) sim <- simulateResiduals(m_nb, n = 1000) ``` # Results In total we collected 6,482 ticks, of which 5,911 (91.2%) were *I. ricinus* nymphs. Adults made up approx. 4% of the catch, and only 9 *Dermacentor reticulatus* were found, all at the two lowest sites. Nymph density declined steeply with altitude in both years (Fig. \@ref(fig:fig-altitude)), from a mean of 42.3 nymphs per 100 m² below 600 m to 3.1 per 100 m² above 1,000 m. The decline was steeper in 2022 than in 2023 (altitude × year interaction: z = 2.87, p = 0.004). Did nymphs simply quest less in the dry year? Partly: saturation deficit had a strong negative effect on counts (Table \@ref(tab:model-table)), but the altitude effect remained after accounting for it. ```{r fig-altitude, fig.cap="Mean density of questing *I. ricinus* nymphs per 100 m² against site altitude in 2022 (open circles) and 2023 (filled circles). Lines show model predictions with 95% confidence bands.", fig.width=7, fig.height=4} drags |> group_by(site, year) |> summarise(altitude = first(altitude), density = mean(nymphs), .groups = "drop") |> ggplot(aes(altitude, density, shape = factor(year))) + geom_point(size = 2) + scale_shape_manual(values = c(1, 16), name = NULL) + labs(x = "Altitude (m a.s.l.)", y = expression("Nymphs per 100 m"^2)) ``` Three further results are worth mentioning: - No nymphs were found above 1,150 m a.s.l. in 2022. In 2023 nymphs were found at all but one site, incl. the highest one (1,248 m). - The seasonal peak shifted from May at low sites to July at high sites. This is consistent with Materna et al. (2008) for the Krkonoše mts. - Larvae were extremely aggregated, e.g. 312 of 1,040 larvae came from a single drag in Aug. 2023. | Altitude band | Sites | Nymphs/100 m² (2022) | Nymphs/100 m² (2023) | |:---|---:|---:|---:| | < 600 m | 6 | 45.1 | 39.6 | | 600–900 m |8| 18.7 | 24.0 | | 900–1,100 m | 6 | 2.2 | 7.9 | | > 1,100 m | 4 | 0.0 | 1.4 | ```{r model-table} #| tab.cap: "Fixed effects of the negative binomial GLMM. Estimates are on the log scale." broom.mixed::tidy(m_nb, effects = "fixed") |> knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Fixed effects of the negative binomial GLMM. Estimates are on the log scale.") ``` # Discussion Our results support the view that the altitudinal limit of *I. ricinus* is not fixed but moves from year to year. In the wet year 2023, nymphs were found ca. 100 m higher than in 2022. Is the upward shift reported in the literature then an artefact? Not necessarily: a series of mild, wet years would produce exactly the pattern described by Daniel et al. (2003) and Materna et al. (2008). However, we cannot exclude that host density also changed; roe deer (*Capreolus capreolus*) numbers in the park increased by approx. 20% between 2015 and 2022 according to the park administration (unpubl. data)[^deer]. The so-called "edge effect", i.e. higher tick densities near forest edges, was not examined here! > Very windy, the cloth kept flipping over. Probably underestimates density at site 17. > --- field notebook, 14 June 2022 Two limitations should be kept in mind. First, drag sampling measures questing activity, not absolute abundance, and activity depends on weather (2022 vs. 2023 being an extreme example). Second, with only two years we cannot separate a trend from inter-annual variation. We are continuing the sampling in 2024 and 2025 with the same protocol. __Data availability:__ the data and code are archived at . [^deer]: Counts are based on winter track surveys. They are not corrected for detectability, so the 20% figure should be treated with caution. We thank Ing. J. Novák for providing them. # Acknowledgements {-} We thank the rangers of the Šumava NP for access to the sites, and M. Dvořáková, K. Beneš and L. Wagner for help with the field work in 2022–2023. Funded by the Czech Science Foundation (GAČR, project 22-00000S). # References {-}

#!/usr/bin/env python3

# fmt: markdown
"""
dicegoblin
==========

A small Discord bot for our Thursday night D&D group.  It rolls dice, keeps track of whose turn it is to bring snacks, and nags everyone about the next session so we stop having the "wait, is it this week??" conversation every single Wednesday.

Setup:
1. Create an application + bot user in the Discord developer portal and copy the token.
2. `export DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN=...` (or put it in a `.env` file next to this script)
3. `python dicegoblin.py --init` writes a default `dicegoblin.yaml`, then edit the channel ids in it
4. `python dicegoblin.py` and leave it running somewhere (mine lives on the homelab NUC, in docker)

Requirements:
*   Python 3.10+ (I use `X | None` everywhere, sorry)
*   discord.py >= 2.3 and PyYAML

A minimal config looks like this, everything else has defaults:

```yaml
prefix:   "!"
session: {day: thursday,   time: "19:30"}
channels:
    announcements: 123456789012345678
```

MIT licensed, do whatever you want with it. No warranty, *especially* not for natural 1s.
"""

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import os
import random
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import discord
import yaml
from discord.ext import commands, tasks

CONFIG_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("DICEGOBLIN_CONFIG", Path(__file__).with_name("dicegoblin.yaml")))

# fmt: markdown
# ## Dice syntax
#
# The roller understands the usual tabletop notation. It's case-insensitive and whitespace is ignored:
#
# | expression | what it does |
# |---|:--|
# | `d20` | one twenty-sided die |
# | `4d6kh3` | roll four d6 and keep the highest three (stat rolls) |
# | `2d20kl1` | disadvantage, keep the lowest |
# | `1d8+3`, `2d6 - 1` | flat modifiers |
#
# Anything else gets a goblin-themed error message.  Exploding dice (`!`) are on the todo list, but honestly nobody has asked for them yet and the regex is already ugly enough.
DICE_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<n>\d*)d(?P<sides>\d+)(?:k(?P<hl>[hl])(?P<keep>\d+))?(?P<mod>[+-]\d+)?$", re.IGNORECASE)  # fmt: skip


class DiceError(ValueError):
    pass


def roll(expr: str, rng: random.Random | None = None) -> tuple[int, str]:
    rng = rng or random.SystemRandom()
    cleaned = expr.replace(" ", "").lower()
    m = DICE_RE.match(cleaned)
    if not m:
        raise DiceError(f"the goblin squints at `{expr}` and does not understand")
    n, sides = int(m["n"] or 1), int(m["sides"])
    if not 1 <= n <= 100 or sides not in (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 20, 100):
        raise DiceError("the goblin only owns normal dice (and at most 100 of them)")
    dice = [rng.randint(1, sides) for _ in range(n)]
    kept = sorted(dice, reverse=m["hl"] != "l")[: int(m["keep"] or n)]
    mod = int(m["mod"] or 0)
    total = sum(kept) + mod
    shown = ", ".join(f"**{d}**" if d in kept else f"~~{d}~~" for d in dice)
    return total, f"`{cleaned}` → [{shown}]{f' {mod:+d}' if mod else ''} = **{total}**"


# fmt: off
DEFAULT_CONFIG = """\
# dicegoblin.yaml -- written by `dicegoblin.py --init`
prefix:   "!"
timezone: Europe/London
session:
    day: thursday
    time: "19:30"     # keep the quotes, PyYAML reads 19:30 as a number otherwise
    remind_hours_before: [24, 2]
channels: {announcements: 0, rolls: 0}   # right click a channel -> Copy Channel ID
snack_rota:
- Priya
- Tom
- "Mags"
- Dev
quiet: no
"""
# fmt: on

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
HELP_TEXT = """
**dicegoblin** knows the following commands. The prefix is configurable, these examples use `!`.

* `!roll 4d6kh3` – roll some dice. You can roll several at once: `!roll d20 d20 1d4+1`
* `!session` – when is the next session? The goblin does the timezone maths so you don't have to.
* `!snacks` – whose turn is it to bring snacks. `!snacks skip` moves on to the next person (e.g. if someone is ill).
*  `!goblin` – the goblin says something. It is not helpful.

Rolls go to the rolls channel if one is configured, otherwise they're posted right where you asked. Don't spam it please, Tom.
"""

# Sent once when the bot joins a server. Raw string because of the shrug.
# fmt: markdown
WELCOME = r"""
Hi! I'm the **dice goblin**. I roll dice, remember whose turn it is to bring snacks, and remind you about sessions.

Type `!help` to see what I can do. If something breaks, ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯ and poke whoever invited me.
"""

# fmt: markdown
REMINDER = """
:alarm_clock: **Session in {hours} hours!**
Starts {when}.   Bring your character sheet, your dice and, if it's your turn, __snacks__.
"""


class Goblin(commands.Bot):
    def __init__(self, cfg: dict) -> None:
        super().__init__(command_prefix=cfg["prefix"], intents=discord.Intents.all(), help_command=None)
        self.cfg, self.snack_index = cfg, 0

    async def setup_hook(self) -> None:
        self.reminder_loop.start()

    def next_session(self) -> dt.datetime:
        now = dt.datetime.now(ZoneInfo(self.cfg["timezone"]))
        day = ["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"].index(self.cfg["session"]["day"])
        hour, minute = map(int, str(self.cfg["session"]["time"]).split(":"))
        when = now.replace(hour=hour, minute=minute, second=0, microsecond=0) + dt.timedelta(days=(day - now.weekday()) % 7)
        return when if when > now else when + dt.timedelta(days=7)

    @tasks.loop(minutes=10)
    async def reminder_loop(self) -> None:
        channel = self.get_channel(self.cfg["channels"]["announcements"])
        when = self.next_session()
        hours_left = (when - dt.datetime.now(when.tzinfo)).total_seconds() / 3600
        for h in self.cfg["session"].get("remind_hours_before", [24, 2]):
            # the loop runs every 10 minutes, so only fire inside one 10 minute window
            if channel and not self.cfg["quiet"] and h - 1 / 6 < hours_left <= h:
                await channel.send(REMINDER.format(hours=h, when=discord.utils.format_dt(when, "F")))


def build_bot(cfg: dict) -> Goblin:
    bot = Goblin(cfg)

    @bot.command(name="roll", aliases=["r"])
    async def roll_cmd(ctx: commands.Context, *exprs: str) -> None:
        lines = []
        for e in exprs[:10] or ["d20"]:
            try:
                lines.append(roll(e)[1])
            except DiceError as err:
                lines.append(str(err))
        target = bot.get_channel(cfg["channels"]["rolls"]) or ctx.channel
        await target.send(f"{ctx.author.mention}\n" + "\n".join(lines))

    @bot.command()
    async def snacks(ctx: commands.Context, action: str = "") -> None:
        bot.snack_index += action == "skip"
        rota = cfg["snack_rota"] or ["nobody, apparently"]
        await ctx.send(f"Snacks this week: **{rota[bot.snack_index % len(rota)]}**")

    @bot.command(name="help")
    async def help_cmd(ctx: commands.Context) -> None:
        await ctx.send(HELP_TEXT.replace("`!", f"`{cfg['prefix']}"))

    @bot.event
    async def on_guild_join(guild: discord.Guild) -> None:
        if guild.system_channel:
            await guild.system_channel.send(WELCOME)

    return bot


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="dicegoblin", description="D&D helper bot")
    parser.add_argument("--init", action="store_true", help="write a default config and exit")
    if parser.parse_args().init:
        if CONFIG_PATH.exists():
            sys.exit(f"{CONFIG_PATH} already exists, not overwriting it")
        CONFIG_PATH.write_text(DEFAULT_CONFIG, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"wrote {CONFIG_PATH}, now go and fill in the channel ids")
        return 0
    if not (token := os.environ.get("DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN")):
        sys.exit("DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN is not set")
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(DEFAULT_CONFIG) | (yaml.safe_load(CONFIG_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {})
    build_bot(cfg).run(token)
    return 0


# %% scratchpad for the VS Code interactive window, only does anything with GOBLIN_SCRATCH=1
#| label: scratch-distribution
#| eval:    false
#| code-fold: True
#| tags: [scratch,dev]
#| fig-cap: '4d6kh3, 10k rolls'
if os.environ.get("GOBLIN_SCRATCH"):
    from collections import Counter

    counts = Counter(roll("4d6kh3", random.Random(42))[0] for _ in range(10_000))
    for total in sorted(counts):
        print(f"{total:>2} {'#' * (counts[total] // 40)}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

$
Dr. Okafor's team first suspected the new 3-D Secure challenge flow, i.e. the change that shipped in release v4.18.0 that morning; however, the timing did not m

## Timeline$

All times are CET. The timeline was reconstructed from PagerDuty, the `#inc-2026-1103` Slack channel and the gateway's audit log; where those sources disagree, 
$
| Time | Event |$
|---|---|$
## Root cause$
$
The HSM proxy keeps a fixed-size pool of TLS connections to the hardware security modules. When the HSM cluster's certificate was rotated at 13:35, all pooled c
$
> "We had a runbook for HSM certificate rotation, but it assumed the proxy would reconnect lazily. It does not. It reconnects everything at once."  $
> -- Mr. Lindqvist, in the incident channel at 15:12$
$
Several factors contributed:$
$
1. The rotation was scheduled during business hours (14:00 is our lowest-traffic hour on weekdays, but only for EU merchants).$
2. The proxy's pool metrics were not on any dashboard. They were only exposed via JMX, i.e., invisible to Grafana.$
3. The canary for the rotation checked HSM health, not end-to-end authorization latency. It passed.$

## TL;DR {#sec-tldr}

The rack drew **41.8 W on average** this quarter (down from 57 W in Q2), mostly because I finally retired the old Dell OptiPlex and moved everything onto the two N100 mini PCs. Uptime for the stuff the household actually notices (Home Assistant, Jellyfin, the Pi-hole) was above 99.5%, see @tbl-uptime, and the electricity bill impact is about €9 a month, which is less than a single streaming subscription so I'm calling that a win.

::: {.callout-note}
All numbers come from two Shelly Plug S units logging to InfluxDB every 60 s, and from Uptime Kuma's SQLite database, which I copied off the NUC on 2024-10-01.  
The plugs claim ±1 W accuracy. I have not verified that and I don't really want to.
:::

> Tom, reading a draft of this: "ok but what if the goblin knows when it's me".  
> He then asked whether the bot could be "re-seeded with good vibes". It cannot. The bot uses `random.SystemRandom()`, which reads from the operating system, so there is nothing to re-seed!

## Conclusions

1. The dice goblin is not cursed. The `SystemRandom` source it uses (see `dicegoblin.py`, line 60 or so) is about as fair as it gets.
2. Tom is not cursed either. He is just a person who remembers his bad rolls. We all are!
3. Humans are terrible at judging randomness. This is well documented, see e.g. Tversky and Kahneman (1971), and it is also documented in every D&D group chat ever.

Next steps? I'd like to check whether people roll differently on their phone vs. on desktop (they shouldn't, the bot doesn't know), and whether rolls are more likely to get re-rolled ("my cat stepped on enter!!") after a low result. That second one isn't about the dice at all, it's about us. *Spoiler: it's Tom. It's always Tom.*

[^sim]: The simulation ignores that some rolls happen in quick bursts (e.g. fireball damage), which makes streaks slightly *more* likely in practice. So if anything, 41% is an underestimate. Sorry, Tom.

---

*Data: 23 sessions, Jan.–Jun. 2024. Code and data are at https://github.com/priyas/goblin-stats if you want to check my work. No goblins were harmed.*

The Python file parses, and the R file passed a bracket and string balance check only, because R isn't installed here. I didn't run any formatter.

- **No `# fmt: yaml` directive:** that name would make the whole file fail with "unknown embedded formatter". In `python_script.py`, the YAML config string is instead wrapped in `# fmt: off` / `# fmt: on`, and the `# fmt: markdown` strings contain YAML front matter and a `yaml` fence.
- **Directive placement:** each directive sits after a blank line or code. A directive directly under another comment line, like a shebang or `# %% [markdown]`, is treated as plain text.

`github_workflow.yml` has an own-line `# fmt: table` above the matrix include list. The docs say the same-line form `config:  # fmt: table` is allowed, but `/workspace` rejects any trailing `# fmt:` comment in YAML. | `fmt: table` | Next | Align the next compatible sequence of flow mappings. |
| `fmt: compact table` | Next | Collapse eligible block mapping rows before aligning them. `fmt: table compact` and `fmt: table compact=true` are equivalent. |

`fmt: table` accepts only its default next-target scope. Compact directives
accept `next`, `from-here`, and `file`.

`compact`, `compact=true`, `compact=yes`, `compact=1`, and `compact true`
enable compaction. `compact=false`, `compact=no`, `compact=0`, and
`compact false` disable it. The separated form accepts only `true` or `false`.
