arguments.content:
# CI for the Riverton Open Data Portal
#
#  * validates every dataset descriptor under datasets/
#  * runs the harvester test-suite on several Python versions and OSes
#  * builds the static "explore" site and, on tags, publishes it to Pages

name: "CI"

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, 'release/**' ]
    paths-ignore: ['docs/**', '**/*.md', 'explore/static/**', '.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**', 'LICENSE', 'CITATION.cff']
  pull_request:
    branches:
    - main
  schedule:
      # Every Monday 04:30 UTC: re-validate the upstream department feeds
      - cron: '30 4 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dataset:
        description: Validate only this dataset slug (leave it empty to validate the whole catalogue, which takes about twenty minutes)
        required: false
        default: ""
      publish:
        description: "Publish the site after a successful build?"
        type: boolean
        default: False

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  PORTAL_ENV: ci
  CKAN_API_URL: https://data.riverton.gov/api/3/action
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"
  UV_VERSION: "0.4.30"
  FORCE_COLOR: "1"
  TZ: America/Chicago

jobs:

  validate-datasets:
    name: Validate dataset descriptors
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - &checkout
        name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Install validator
        run: pipx install "frictionless==5.18.0"

      - name: Validate
        # the dataset input is only set for manual runs
        run: |
          if [ -n "${{ github.event.inputs.dataset }}" ]; then
            frictionless validate "datasets/${{ github.event.inputs.dataset }}/datapackage.json"
          else
            for pkg in datasets/*/datapackage.json; do
              frictionless validate "$pkg" || exit 1
            done
          fi

  test:
    needs: validate-datasets
    name: Tests (${{ matrix.os }}, py${{ matrix.python-version }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental }}
    strategy:
       fail-fast: False
       max-parallel: 4
       matrix:
         os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-14]
         python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]
         experimental: [false]
         include:
           - { os: ubuntu-latest, python-version: "3.14-dev", experimental: true }
           - {os: ubuntu-24.04-arm,python-version: "3.12",experimental: true}
         exclude:
           # the 3.10 macOS runners keep timing out on the GDAL wheel
           - os: macos-14
             python-version: "3.10"
    steps:
      - *checkout
      - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
          allow-prereleases: true
          cache: 'pip'
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: >-
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip &&
          pip install -e ".[test,harvest]"
          --constraint requirements/constraints.txt
      - name:   Run tests
        run: pytest -q --maxfail=1 --cov=portal --cov-report=xml tests/
        env:
          CKAN_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CKAN_STAGING_KEY }}
          # Windows runners have no /tmp
          HARVEST_CACHE_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/harvest-cache
          HARVEST_OFFLINE:
      - name: Upload coverage
        if: ${{ matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && matrix.python-version == '3.12' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with: { files: coverage.xml , fail_ci_if_error: false }

  build-site:
    needs: [ test ]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      page_url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
    - *checkout
    - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: !!str 20
        cache: npm
        cache-dependency-path: explore/package-lock.json
    - name: Build the explore site
      working-directory: explore
      run: |
        npm ci
        npm run build -- --base-url "/" --site-url "https://data.riverton.gov"
    - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
      with:
        path: explore/_site
        retention-days: ~

  deploy:
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') || inputs.publish == true
    needs: build-site
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ needs.build-site.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deploy
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
      - name: Announce
        run: echo "Published ${{ github.ref_name }} on $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

# .github/workflows/site-and-autograder.yml
# Baut die Kurswebseite (Quarto), testet den Autograder gegen Beispielabgaben
# und deployt nach GitHub Pages.  Owner: @stat1010/tutoren
name:   "Kurswebseite & Autograder CI"

"on":
  push:
    branches: [ main, 'release/**' ]

    - "**.md"
    - 'docs/drafts/**'
  pull_request:

  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      deploy:
        description: "Nach dem Build auf GitHub Pages deployen? (yes/no)"
        required: false
        default: "no"
        type: choice
        options: ["yes", "no"]

        description: Nur eine Woche rendern, z.B. woche-07, leer lassen für das ganze Skript
        required: false

# fmt: compact
permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: True

env:
  TZ: Europe/Berlin
  LANG: de_DE.UTF-8
  QUARTO_VERSION: 1.6.40
  PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK: "1"
  PYTHONUTF8: '1'      # Umlaute in Dateinamen (Übung_03.ipynb) auf Windows
  COURSE:   STAT-1010

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Formatierung prüfen (YAML, Markdown)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - &checkout
        name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
      - run: uvx yamark format --check .

  autograder-tests:
    name: Autograder tests (${{ matrix.os }}, py${{ matrix.python }})
    needs: lint
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 25
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # fmt: table
        include:
          - {os: ubuntu-24.04, python: "3.11", otter: "6.0.2", experimental: false}
          - {os: ubuntu-24.04, python: "3.12", otter: "6.1.0", experimental: false}
          - {os: ubuntu-24.04,python: "3.13",otter: latest,experimental: true}
          - {os: macos-14, python: "3.12", otter: "6.1.0", experimental: false}
          - { os: windows-2022, python: "3.12", otter: "6.1.0", experimental: true }
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental }}
    steps:
      - *checkout
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
            python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
            cache: pip
      - name: Install grader + Beispielabgaben
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          if [ "${{ matrix.otter }}" = "latest" ]; then
            pip install otter-grader
          else
            pip install "otter-grader==${{ matrix.otter }}"
          fi
          pip install -r grader/requirements.txt
      - name: Run hidden tests against sample submissions
        run: >
          python -m pytest grader/tests
          -q --maxfail=5
          --junitxml=reports/junit-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.python }}.xml
      - name: Upload test report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with: { name: "junit-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.python }}",
                path: reports/, retention-days: 14 }

  render-site:
    name: Quarto-Webseite rendern
    needs: [autograder-tests]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - *checkout
      - uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2
        with:
          version: ${{ env.QUARTO_VERSION }}
          tinytex: true
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with: {r-version: '4.4', use-public-rspm: true}
      - name: Fonts für 統計 / Ελληνικά in Abbildungen
        run: sudo apt-get install -y fonts-noto-cjk fonts-noto-core
      - name: Render
        run: |
          if [ -n "${{ inputs.woche }}" ]; then
            quarto render "skript/${{ inputs.woche }}.qmd"
          else
            quarto render --to html
          fi
          fc-list | grep -i -E "noto (sans|serif) cjk" || echo "::warning::CJK-Fonts fehlen, Achsenbeschriftungen werden Kästchen"
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: _site

  deploy:
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || inputs.deploy == 'yes'
    needs: [ render-site ]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

# JupyterHub für STAT 1010 auf dem Uni-Cluster (Kubernetes 1.30)
#   kubectl apply -f k8s/stat1010.yaml
# Reihenfolge ist wichtig: Namespace zuerst, dann ConfigMap, dann der Rest.
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: stat1010
  labels:
    "app.kubernetes.io/part-of": stat1010
    team:   lehrstuhl-statistik
    semester: "wise-2026-27"
  annotations:
    description: "Kursplattform für Statistik 1 – 統計学入門 – Εισαγωγή στη Στατιστική"
    contact: Tutorenteam, it-support@stat.uni-beispielstadt.de, Raum 3.142, Do 14-16 Uhr
---
---
# ConfigMap: Willkommensseite (Markdown) und das Cull-Skript
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: hub-content
  namespace: stat1010
data:
  # fmt: markdown
  welcome.md: |
    #  Willkommen / Welcome / Bienvenue
    Dieser Hub ist für **STAT 1010** reserviert. Bitte speichere alles unter `~/labs`; der Ordner `~/scratch` wird jede Nacht geleert, und Notebooks außerhalb von `~/labs` sind nach dem Semester weg.
    * Abgabe: `otter submit` im Terminal
    * Feedback: erscheint unter `~/feedback`, normalerweise nach 5–10 Minuten
    * Hilfe: Forum oder Sprechstunde (Do 14–16 Uhr, Raum 3.142)
  cull-idle.sh: |
    #!/bin/sh
    # stoppt Server, die länger als eine Stunde idle sind
    set -eu
    exec python3 -m jupyterhub_idle_culler \
      --timeout=3600 --cull-every=300 --concurrency=10
  "hub.config": "c.Spawner.default_url = '/lab'"
  ENABLE_NBGRADER:   "yes"
  OTTER_STRICT: 'off'
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: hub
  namespace: stat1010
  labels: &hub_labels
    app.kubernetes.io/name: jupyterhub
    app.kubernetes.io/component: hub
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels: *hub_labels
  strategy: {type: Recreate}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: *hub_labels
      annotations:
        "checksum/config":   "8f3a1c2e"   # wird von der CI ersetzt
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: hub
      securityContext: { runAsUser: 1000, runAsGroup: 1000,
                         fsGroup: 1000 }
      containers:
      - name: hub
        image: "quay.io/jupyterhub/k8s-hub:4.0.0"
        args: ["jupyterhub", "--config", "/usr/local/etc/jupyterhub/jupyterhub_config.py",
               "--upgrade-db"]
        ports:
          - containerPort: 8081
            name:   http
        # fmt: table
        env:
          - {name: TZ, value: Europe/Berlin}
          - {name: LANG, value: "de_DE.UTF-8"}
          - {name: HUB_TITLE,value: "STAT 1010 · Statistik-Hub"}
          - { name: CONFIGPROXY_AUTH_TOKEN, valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: hub-secret, key: proxy.token}} }
          - {name: COURSE_LANGS, value: "de,en,fr,es,el,ja"}
        resources:
          # fmt: compact
          requests:
            cpu: 200m
            memory: 512Mi
          limits: {cpu: "1", memory: 1Gi}
        volumeMounts:
          - {name: hub-db, mountPath: /srv/jupyterhub}
          - name: content
            mountPath: /etc/stat1010
            readOnly: True
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /hub/health, port: http}
          initialDelaySeconds:   30
          periodSeconds: 10
      volumes:
        - name: hub-db
          persistentVolumeClaim:

# JupyterHub für STAT 1010 auf dem Uni-Cluster (Kubernetes 1.30)

    semester: "wise-2026-27"
  annotations:
    description: "Kursplattform für Statistik 1 – 統計学入門 – Εισαγωγή στη Στατιστική"
    contact: Tutorenteam, it-support@stat.uni-beispielstadt.de, Raum 3.142, Do 14-16 Uhr
---
---
# ConfigMap: Willkommensseite (Markdown) und das Cull-Skript
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: hub-content
  namespace: stat1010
data:
  # fmt: markdown
  welcome.md: |
    #  Willkommen / Welcome / Bienvenue

    * Abgabe: `otter submit` im Terminal
    * Feedback: erscheint unter `~/feedback`, normalerweise nach 5–10 Minuten
    * Hilfe: Forum oder Sprechstunde (Do 14–16 Uhr, Raum 3.142)

    #!/bin/sh
    # stoppt Server, die länger als eine Stunde idle sind
    set -eu
    exec python3 -m jupyterhub_idle_culler \
      --timeout=3600 --cull-every=300 --concurrency=10

# ShiftShare -- volunteer scheduling for the Riverton Community Food Bank and partners
# Written by hand (no Helm chart yet). Apply with:
#   kubectl apply -f deploy/shiftshare.yaml
---
# Namespace
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: shiftshare
  labels:
    team: "volunteer-services"
    cost-centre: '4410'
---

# Non-secret configuration. Values must be strings, hence all the quotes.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
    name: shiftshare-config
    namespace: shiftshare
    annotations:
        shiftshare.riverton.org/last-reviewed: "2026-08-12"
        shiftshare.riverton.org/owner: Volunteer Services (Mon-Fri, 9-5)
data:
    APP_ENV: production
    APP_URL: https://volunteer.riverton.org
    DEFAULT_TIMEZONE: "America/Chicago"
    REMINDER_HOURS_BEFORE: "24"
    MAX_SHIFTS_PER_WEEK: "6"
    FEATURE_SMS_REMINDERS: "true"
    FEATURE_WAITLIST: 'false'
    welcome-email.txt: |
        Hi {{ volunteer.first_name }},

        Thanks for signing up to volunteer with {{ org.name }}! Your first shift is on
        {{ shift.starts_at | date("l j F") }} at {{ site.name }}.

        If you can't make it, please cancel at least 24 hours ahead so someone on the waitlist can take your place.
    motd.txt: |+
        Scheduled maintenance: Sundays 02:00-03:00 (America/Chicago).

    policy-summary.md: >
        Volunteers under 16 must be accompanied by a registered adult.
        Shifts at the warehouse require closed-toe shoes.

        Background checks are required only for roles that involve
        working with children or vulnerable adults; see the Safeguarding policy for the full list of roles affected by this requirement.
---
# Placeholders only! The real values live in the sealed-secrets repo.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata: {name: shiftshare-secrets, namespace: shiftshare}
type: Opaque
stringData:
  DATABASE_URL: postgres://shiftshare:CHANGEME@shiftshare-db.shiftshare.svc:5432/shiftshare
  TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN: !!str 0123456789
  SESSION_SECRET: "replace-me"
  SMTP_PASSWORD: ""

---
# Web application (Laravel). Two replicas is plenty outside of
# the November/December holiday drive.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shiftshare-web
  namespace: shiftshare
  labels: &web-labels
    app.kubernetes.io/name: shiftshare
    app.kubernetes.io/component: web
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: "shiftshare"
spec:
  replicas: !!int "2"
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  selector:
    matchLabels: *web-labels
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate: { maxSurge: 1 ,maxUnavailable: 0 }
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        <<: *web-labels
        tier: frontend
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
        prometheus.io/port: "9253"
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: no
      securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 1000, fsGroup: 1000}
      nodeSelector: ~
      affinity:
      containers:
      -   name: web
          image: ghcr.io/riverton-food-bank/shiftshare:3.2.0
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          args: ["php-fpm", "--nodaemonize", "--fpm-config", "/usr/local/etc/php-fpm.d/www.conf", "--force-stderr"]
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
              protocol: TCP
            - {name: metrics, containerPort: 9253}
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef: { name: shiftshare-config }
            - secretRef:
                name: shiftshare-secrets
          env:
            - name: POD_IP
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef: {fieldPath: status.podIP}
            # queue name must match the CronJob further down
            - name: QUEUE_NAME
              value: "reminders"
            - name: LOG_CHANNEL
              value: stderr
          resources:
            requests: { cpu: 250m ,memory: 256Mi }
            limits:   {cpu: "1", memory: 512Mi}
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /healthz, port: http}
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            failureThreshold: 3
          securityContext:
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: True
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
# Cluster-internal service for the web pods
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: shiftshare-web
  namespace: shiftshare
spec:
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: shiftshare
    app.kubernetes.io/component: web
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    targetPort: http
---
# Public entry point. TLS via cert-manager; the old hostname keeps working until 2027.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: shiftshare
  namespace: shiftshare
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: "letsencrypt-prod"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size: 10m
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet: |
      more_set_headers "X-Robots-Tag: noindex";
      more_set_headers "Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), camera=()";
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/server-alias: "volunteers.riverton.org, www.volunteer.riverton.org"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
    - hosts: [ volunteer.riverton.org, volunteers.riverton.org ]
      secretName: shiftshare-tls
  rules:
    - host: volunteer.riverton.org
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: shiftshare-web
                port: {name: http}
---
# Sends the "your shift is tomorrow" reminders. Runs hourly; the app decides who
# is due a reminder, so an overlapping run is harmless (but wasteful).
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: shiftshare-reminders
  namespace: shiftshare
spec:
  schedule: "5 * * * *"
  timeZone: America/Chicago
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 5
  suspend: false
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 2
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
            - name: reminders
              image: ghcr.io/riverton-food-bank/shiftshare:3.2.0
              command: ["php", "artisan", "shifts:send-reminders", "--hours=24", "--channel=sms,email", "--quiet"]
              envFrom:
                - configMapRef: {name: shiftshare-config}
                - secretRef: {name: shiftshare-secrets}
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: shiftshare-web
  namespace: shiftshare
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: shiftshare, app.kubernetes.io/component: web}

arguments.content:
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title:   STAT 1010 Autograder API
  version: "2.3.0"
  # fmt: markdown
  description: |
    REST-API des Autograders für **STAT 1010 – Einführung in die Statistik**. Studierende laden Notebooks hoch, der Grader führt versteckte Tests aus und schreibt das Feedback zurück ins LMS.
    ## Authentifizierung
    Alle Endpunkte (außer `/health`) erwarten ein *Bearer*-Token aus dem Hub (`JUPYTERHUB_API_TOKEN`).
    * Studierende sehen nur eigene Abgaben
    * Tutor:innen sehen alle Abgaben ihrer Übungsgruppe
    *   Admins: alles
    ## Rate limits
    Max. 30 submissions per hour and student; the remaining budget is returned in the `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header of every response.
  contact:
    name: Tutorenteam STAT 1010
    email: grader@stat.uni-beispielstadt.de
  license: { name: MIT, identifier: MIT }
  x-logo: {url: "https://stat1010.github.io/assets/logo.svg", altText: "Logo: Glockenkurve über einem Laptop"}
# fmt: table
servers:
  - {url: "https://grader.stat.uni-beispielstadt.de/api/v2", description: Produktion}
  - {url: https://staging.grader.stat.uni-beispielstadt.de/api/v2,description: "Staging (wird nachts zurückgesetzt)"}
  - {url: "http://localhost:8080/api/v2", description: Lokal / docker compose}
tags:
  - name: submissions
    description: Abgaben hochladen, Status abfragen, Feedback lesen
  - name: assignments
    description: Übungsblätter, Fristen und Punkteschemata
  - name: "admin"
    description:  "Nur für Tutor:innen und Admins: Noten exportieren, Abgaben neu bewerten"
paths:
  /health:
    get:
      summary: Liveness probe
      security: []
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {type: object, properties: {status: {type: string, enum: [ok]}}}
  /courses/{courseId}/assignments:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/courseId'
    get:
      tags: [assignments]
      summary: Übungsblätter eines Kurses auflisten
      operationId: listAssignments
      parameters:
        - name: lang
          in: query
          description: Sprache der Titel (de, en, fr, es); Standard ist de, unbekannte Werte fallen auf de zurück
          schema: {type: string, enum: [de, en, fr, es], default: de}
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Liste der Übungsblätter
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Assignment"}
              example:
                - id: lab04
                  title: "Konfidenzintervalle für $\\mu$"
                  due: 2026-12-01T23:59:00+01:00
                  max_points: 20
                - {id: lab05, title: "Hypothesentests", due: 2026-12-15T23:59:00+01:00,
                   max_points: 20}
        '401': &unauthorized
          description: Kein oder ungültiges Token
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'}
  /submissions:
    post:
      tags: [submissions]
      summary: Notebook abgeben
      operationId: createSubmission
      requestBody:
        required: True
        content:
          multipart/form-data:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [assignment_id,
                         notebook]
              properties:
                assignment_id: {type: string, example: lab04}
                notebook:
                  type: string
                  contentMediaType: application/x-ipynb+json
                  description: Das Notebook als .ipynb-Datei, max. 25 MB, keine Ausgabezellen mit Bildern > 5 MB
      responses:
        "202":
          description: Angenommen; die Bewertung läuft asynchron
          headers:
            Location: {schema: {type: string}, description: URL der neuen Abgabe}
            X-RateLimit-Remaining:
              schema: { type: integer, minimum: 0 }
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Submission'}
        "401": *unauthorized
        '413':
          description: Datei zu groß (> 25 MB)
        "429":
          description: "Too many requests: max. 30 Abgaben pro Stunde"
  /submissions/{submissionId}/feedback:
    get:
      tags: [ submissions ]
      summary: Feedback zu einer Abgabe (Markdown)
      parameters:
        - {name: submissionId, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string, format: uuid}}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Feedback als Markdown, siehe Beispiel
          content:
            text/markdown:
              schema: {type: string}
              example: |
                ## Feedback zu lab04
                *   Aufgabe 1: 5/5 ✓
                *   Aufgabe 2: 3/5 — das Intervall ist zu schmal, prüfe `qt()` vs. `qnorm()`.
        "401": *unauthorized
        "404": {description: "Abgabe nicht gefunden (oder nicht deine)"}
components:
  parameters:
    courseId:
      name: courseId
      in: path
      required: true
      schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[A-Z]{3,4}-[0-9]{4}$', example: STAT-1010}
  securitySchemes:
    # fmt: compact
    bearerAuth:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      bearerFormat: JWT
  schemas:
    Assignment:
      type: object
      required: [id, title, due, max_points]
      properties:
        id: {type: string}
        title: {type: string, description: "Titel, lokalisiert; z. B. 'Lab 4: Konfidenzintervalle'"}
        due: { type: string, format: date-time }
        max_points: {type: number, minimum: 0}
        late_policy:
          type: string
          enum: [none, "10%-per-day", hard_deadline]
          default: "10%-per-day"
    Submission:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: {type: string, format: uuid}
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [queued, running, graded, failed, "off"]
          description: >
            Status der Bewertung. "off" bedeutet, dass der Autograder für dieses Blatt deaktiviert ist
            (z.B. bei handschriftlichen Aufgaben); die Bewertung erfolgt dann manuell durch Tutor:innen.
        score: {type: [number, "null"], examples: [17.5, null]}
        student:
          type: object
          properties:
            name: {type: string, examples: ["Zoë Müller", "山田 太郎", "Γιώργος Παπαδάκης", "José Ñúñez"]}
            matrikel: {type: string, pattern: "^[0-9]{7}$"}
            group: {type: string, enum: [T01, T02, T03, T04, T05]}
    Problem:
      type: object
      description: RFC 9457 problem details
      properties:
        type: {type: string, format: uri}
        title: {type: string}
        status: {type: integer}
        detail: {type: string}
security:
  - bearerAuth: []
x-feature-flags:
  late_submissions: "yes"
  plagiarism_check: "off"
  multilingual_feedback: True

arguments.content:
# Documentation site for the Riverton County community health dashboard.
# Built with MkDocs Material; the docs workflow deploys it on every merge to main.

site_name: "Community Health Dashboard Documentation"
site_description: How the Riverton County community health dashboard is built, what each indicator means, and how to request new data.
site_author: Epidemiology & Data Services, Riverton County Public Health
site_url: https://docs.health.riverton.gov/
repo_url: https://github.com/riverton-health/dashboard
repo_name: 'riverton-health/dashboard'
edit_uri: edit/main/docs/
copyright: >
  Copyright © 2023-2026 Riverton County Public Health.
  Data are provided under the Open Government Licence; small counts (fewer than 11) are suppressed to protect privacy.
docs_dir: docs
use_directory_urls: yes
strict: True

theme:
    name: material
    language: en
    custom_dir: overrides
    logo: assets/county-seal.svg
    favicon: "assets/favicon.png"
    font: false            # self-hosted fonts only (no Google Fonts, for privacy)
    icon:
        repo: fontawesome/brands/github
        admonition: {note: octicons/tag-16, warning: octicons/alert-16, danger: octicons/zap-16}
    palette:
      - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: light)"
        scheme: default
        primary: teal
        accent: "deep orange"
        toggle:
          icon: material/weather-night
          name: Switch to dark mode
      - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"
        scheme: slate
        primary: teal
        toggle: {icon: material/weather-sunny, name: Switch to light mode}
    features:
    - navigation.tabs
    - navigation.sections
    - navigation.top
    - search.suggest
    # - search.highlight   (too slow on the 2018 library PCs)
    - content.code.copy
    - content.action.edit

plugins:
  - search:
      lang: [ en, es ]
      separator: '[\s\-,:!=\[\]()"/]+|(?!\b)(?=[A-Z][a-z])'
  - git-revision-date-localized:
      enable_creation_date: true
      type: date
      fallback_to_build_date: yes
  - minify:
      minify_html: true
  - redirects:
      redirect_maps:
        'indicators/flu.md': 'indicators/respiratory.md'
        "faq.md": help/faq.md

markdown_extensions:
  - admonition
  - attr_list
  - md_in_html
  - footnotes
  - abbr
  - toc:
      permalink: "¶"
      toc_depth: 3
  - pymdownx.details
  - pymdownx.highlight: { anchor_linenums: true, line_spans: __span, pygments_lang_class: true }
  - pymdownx.inlinehilite
  - pymdownx.snippets:
      auto_append:
        - includes/abbreviations.md
      check_paths: true
  - pymdownx.superfences:
      custom_fences:
        - name: mermaid
          class: mermaid
          format: !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format
  - pymdownx.emoji:
      emoji_index: !!python/name:material.extensions.emoji.twemoji
      emoji_generator: !!python/name:material.extensions.emoji.to_svg
  - pymdownx.tabbed: {alternate_style: true}
  - pymdownx.arithmatex:

arguments.content:
# ShiftShare public API
# Source of truth for the volunteer portal, the kiosk app and partner integrations.
# Lint with:  npx @redocly/cli lint openapi.yaml
openapi: "3.1.0"
info:
  title: ShiftShare Volunteer Scheduling API
  version: "3.2"
  summary: 'Book, swap and cancel volunteer shifts at Riverton''s community organisations.'
  description: |
    The ShiftShare API lets partner organisations (food banks, libraries, shelters, the parks department) publish volunteer shifts and lets volunteers book them.

    ## Authentication
    All write operations need a bearer token issued by the partner admin console.  Read-only endpoints for **published** shifts are public, but are rate limited to 60 requests per minute per IP address.

    ## Conventions
    * Times are ISO 8601 with an offset, e.g. `2026-03-14T09:00:00-05:00`.
    * Lists are paginated with `cursor` / `limit`.
    * Personal data (phone numbers, dates of birth) is never returned to other volunteers.
  contact:
    name: Volunteer Services digital team
    email: shiftshare@riverton.org
    url: https://volunteer.riverton.org/developers
  license: { name: AGPL-3.0-or-later, url: "https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0.html" }
  x-last-reviewed: 2026-10-28

servers:
- url: https://api.volunteer.riverton.org/v3
  description: Production
- url: "https://staging-api.volunteer.riverton.org/v3"
  description: Staging (data is reset every night at 02:00)
- url: http://localhost:{port}/v3
  description: Local development
  variables:
    port:
      default: "8080"
      enum: ["8080", "8000", "3000"]

tags:
  - name: shifts
    description: Volunteer shifts offered by partner organisations.
  - name: bookings
    description: 'A volunteer''s booking of a shift, including waitlist entries.'
  - name: organisations
    x-displayName: Partner organisations

security:
  - bearerAuth: []

paths:
  /shifts:
    get:
      tags: [shifts]
      summary: List published shifts
      operationId: listShifts
      security: []        # public endpoint
      parameters:
        - name: from
          in: query
          description: Only return shifts starting on or after this date.
          schema: { type: string, format: date }
          example: 2026-03-14
        - name: organisation
          in: query
          schema: {type: string}

        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Cursor'
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit"
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A page of shifts.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ShiftPage'
        "429": &rateLimited
          description: Too many requests. Slow down and retry after the number of seconds given in the Retry-After response header.
          headers:
            Retry-After: {schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1}}
      x-amazon-apigateway-integration:
        type: aws_proxy
        httpMethod: POST
        uri: !Sub "arn:aws:apigateway:${AWS::Region}:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/${ShiftsFunction.Arn}/invocations"
        credentials: !Ref ApiGatewayInvokeRole
    post:
      tags: [ shifts ]
      summary: Publish a new shift
      operationId: createShift
      requestBody:
        required: True
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/ShiftInput' }
            examples:
              pantry:
                summary: Saturday pantry shift
                value: {organisation_id: 12, title: "Pantry sorting", starts_at: "2026-03-14T09:00:00-05:00", ends_at: "2026-03-14T12:00:00-05:00", capacity: 8}
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/ValidationError'
        "429": *rateLimited

  /shifts/{shiftId}/bookings:
    parameters:
      - name: shiftId
        in: path
        required: yes
        schema:
          type: integer
          format: int64
    post:
      tags:
      - bookings
      summary: Book a shift (or join its waitlist)
      description: >-
        Creates a booking for the authenticated volunteer.
        If the shift is full and has a waitlist, the volunteer is added to the
        waitlist instead and the response status is `202`.


        Volunteers can hold at most six upcoming bookings; the seventh attempt returns `409 Conflict`.
      operationId: bookShift
      responses:
        "201": {description: Booked}
        "202": {description: Added to the waitlist}
        "409": { description: "Booking limit reached, or already booked" }
      deprecated: false

components:
  parameters:
    Cursor:
      name: cursor
      in: query
      required: false
      schema: {type: string}
    Limit:
      name: limit
      in: query
      schema: { type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, default: 25 }
  responses:
    ValidationError:
      description: The request body failed validation.
  schemas:
    ShiftInput:
      type: object
      required: [organisation_id, title, starts_at, ends_at]
      properties:
        organisation_id: {type: integer}
        title:
          type: string
          maxLength: 120
          example: "Pantry sorting"
        starts_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
        ends_at:   { type: string, format: date-time }
        capacity: {type: integer, minimum: 1, default: 1}
        days: {type: array, items: {type: string, enum: [monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday, saturday, sunday, public-holiday]}}
        min_age:
          type: [integer, "null"]
          default: ~
          description: Minimum volunteer age for this shift, or null when there is no restriction beyond the organisation's own policy.
        contact_phone:
          type: string
          pattern: '^\+?[0-9 ()-]{7,20}$'
        check_in_time: {type: string, example: "08:30"}
        notes:
    Shift:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/ShiftInput'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id: {type: integer, format: int64, readOnly: true}
            status: { type: string, enum: [draft, published, full, cancelled] }
            spots_left: {type: integer}
    ShiftPage:
      type: object
      properties:
        data: {type: array, items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Shift'}}
        next_cursor: {type: ["string", "null"]}
  securitySchemes:
    bearerAuth:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      bearerFormat: JWT

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check how stale the datasets on the Riverton Open Data Portal are.

The portal (CKAN) lists roughly 600 datasets published by 23 city departments.
Each dataset declares an expected update frequency in its metadata; this script
compares that with the last time one of its resources actually changed, and
produces

* a CSV report for the open-data coordinator, and
* a short Markdown summary that is posted to Slack every Monday.

Run ``python freshness.py --help`` for the options. The file also uses the
"percent" cell format so analysts can step through it in VS Code or Jupyter.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import datetime as dt
import logging
import os
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable, Iterator

import requests

log = logging.getLogger("freshness")
INTERACTIVE = "ipykernel" in sys.modules

# fmt: markdown
# #   How "stale" is decided
#
# A dataset is **stale** when its newest resource is older than the declared update frequency plus a grace period. The grace period exists because several departments still publish by hand on the first working day of the month, and public holidays push that back.
#
# * `daily` - 2 days of grace
# * `weekly` - 3 days
# *   `monthly` - 10 days
#     * departments on the paper-based process get 5 extra days (see `MANUAL_PUBLISHERS`)
# * anything else (`irregular`, `as needed`, blank) is never flagged
#
# Questions about these numbers go to the open-data coordinator, __not__ to the developers.
GRACE_DAYS = {"daily": 2, "weekly": 3, "monthly": 10, "quarterly": 20, "annually": 45}
PERIOD_DAYS = {"daily": 1, "weekly": 7, "monthly": 31, "quarterly": 92, "annually": 366}
MANUAL_PUBLISHERS = {"parks-and-recreation", "city-clerk", "animal-services"}

CKAN_URL = os.environ.get("CKAN_URL", "https://data.riverton.gov")
REPORT_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("REPORT_DIR", "reports"))


@dataclass
class DatasetStatus:
    name: str
    title: str
    organization: str
    frequency: str
    last_modified: dt.datetime | None
    resources: int = 0
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def age_days(self) -> int | None:
        if self.last_modified is None:
            return None
        return (dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc) - self.last_modified).days

    def is_stale(self) -> bool:
        grace = GRACE_DAYS.get(self.frequency)
        if grace is None or self.age_days is None:
            return False
        if self.organization in MANUAL_PUBLISHERS:
            grace += 5
        return self.age_days > PERIOD_DAYS[self.frequency] + grace


def parse_ckan_time(value: str | None) -> dt.datetime | None:
    """CKAN returns naive ISO timestamps in UTC; make them timezone-aware."""
    if not value:
        return None
    return dt.datetime.fromisoformat(value).replace(tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)


def iter_packages(session: requests.Session, rows: int = 100) -> Iterator[dict]:
    """Yield every public package from CKAN's package_search, page by page."""
    start = 0
    while True:
        resp = session.get(f"{CKAN_URL}/api/3/action/package_search", params={"rows": rows, "start": start}, timeout=30)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        result = resp.json()["result"]
        yield from result["results"]
        start += rows
        if start >= result["count"]:
            break


def to_status(pkg: dict) -> DatasetStatus:
    stamps = [parse_ckan_time(r.get("last_modified") or r.get("created")) for r in pkg.get("resources", [])]
    stamps = [s for s in stamps if s is not None]
    return DatasetStatus(
        name=pkg["name"],
        title=pkg.get("title") or pkg["name"],
        organization=(pkg.get("organization") or {}).get("name", "unknown"),
        frequency=(pkg.get("frequency") or "").strip().lower(),
        last_modified=max(stamps) if stamps else None,
        resources=len(pkg.get("resources", [])),
    )


# fmt: markdown
REPORT_README = r"""
Freshness reports
=================

This folder is written by `freshness.py` every Monday at 06:00.  Each run adds one CSV named `freshness-YYYY-MM-DD.csv`; nothing is deleted automatically, so ask Records Management before you clear it out.

Columns
-------

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | CKAN dataset slug|
| `status` | one of `ok\|stale\|unknown` |
|`age_days`| days since the newest resource changed |

On Windows the share is mapped as `\\cityhall-fs02\OpenData\reports`; on the Linux report server it is mounted at `/mnt/opendata/reports`.

* Do **not** edit the CSVs by hand -- the dashboard reads them.
*  Datasets marked with \* are published manually, so expect them to be late around holidays.
"""

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
SLACK_SUMMARY = """
*Open data freshness report* for the week of {week}. {stale} of {total} datasets are overdue, up from {stale_last_week} last week. The full CSV is on the shared drive; see the README in that folder for what each column means. If a dataset was retired on purpose (e.g. after a department merger), reply in the thread so we can archive it instead of chasing the publisher.
"""


def write_csv(statuses: Iterable[DatasetStatus], path: Path) -> int:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    n = 0
    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        writer = csv.writer(fh)
        writer.writerow(["name", "organization", "frequency", "status", "age_days", "resources"])
        for s in statuses:
            status = "unknown" if s.age_days is None else ("stale" if s.is_stale() else "ok")
            writer.writerow([s.name, s.organization, s.frequency or "-", status, s.age_days, s.resources])
            n += 1
    (path.parent / "README.md").write_text(REPORT_README.lstrip(), encoding="utf-8")
    return n


# %% [markdown]
# ## Interactive exploration
# Run the cells below in VS Code or Jupyter to look at a single department.
# Nothing in these cells runs during the Monday job.

# %%
#| label: load-config
#| tags: [ setup,  network ]
#| params:
#|    department:   "public-works"
#|    include_private: no
#|    thresholds: {stale: 1.0, warn: 0.75 }
#| notes: >
#|   Uses the read-only API key; never paste
#|   the admin key into a notebook.
if INTERACTIVE:
    session = requests.Session()
    session.headers["Authorization"] = os.environ.get("CKAN_READONLY_KEY", "")
    department = "public-works"

# %%
#| label: fetch-department
#| echo:   false
#| depends-on:
#|   - load-config
#| output:
#|     format: table
#|     columns: [name,frequency, age_days,  stale]
#|     max-rows: 50
#| caption: "Datasets published by the selected department, sorted by how overdue they are; rows marked ** are stale"
if INTERACTIVE:
    statuses = [to_status(p) for p in iter_packages(session) if (p.get("organization") or {}).get("name") == department]
    statuses.sort(key=lambda s: (not s.is_stale(), -(s.age_days or 0)))
    for s in statuses[:50]:
        print(f"{'**' if s.is_stale() else '  '} {s.name:<45} {s.frequency:<10} {s.age_days}")

# %%
#| label: cli
#| eval: False
#| owner: { team: "Digital Services", contact: opendata@riverton.gov }
def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Report stale datasets on the open data portal.")
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=REPORT_DIR / f"freshness-{dt.date.today():%Y-%m-%d}.csv")
    parser.add_argument("--fail-on-stale", action="store_true", help="exit with status 1 if anything is stale")
    parser.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG if args.verbose else logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

    with requests.Session() as session:
        statuses = [to_status(p) for p in iter_packages(session)]
    stale = [s for s in statuses if s.is_stale()]
    n = write_csv(statuses, args.out)
    log.info("wrote %d rows to %s (%d stale)", n, args.out, len(stale))
    return 1 if (stale and args.fail_on_stale) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# weekly_respiratory.R
# Riverton County Public Health -- weekly respiratory illness surveillance
#
# Reads the syndromic surveillance extract (ED visits) and the population
# estimates, applies small-cell suppression, and writes the tables behind the
# public dashboard. Run every Monday after the state feed lands (~05:30).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(readr)
  library(lubridate)
  library(stringr)
  library(ggplot2)
})

# fmt: markdown
# #  Suppression rules (read before changing anything!)
#
# Counts between 1 and 10 are suppressed in *every* public output, as required by the county's data release policy. Zero is **not** suppressed, because a true zero cannot identify anyone.
#
# 1. Suppress cells with 1-10 events.
# 1. Apply complementary suppression so a hidden value can't be recovered from the row or column totals.
# 1. Rates based on fewer than 20 events are flagged as _unstable_ and drawn in grey.
#
# Ask Dr. Okafor before you change `SUPPRESS_MIN` or `SUPPRESS_MAX`.
SUPPRESS_MIN <- 1L
SUPPRESS_MAX <- 10L
UNSTABLE_BELOW <- 20L

data_dir <- Sys.getenv("SURV_DATA_DIR", "data/raw")
out_dir <- Sys.getenv("SURV_OUT_DIR", "data/public")

#' Suppress small counts in a tidy table
#'
#' Replaces counts between `lo` and `hi` (inclusive) with `NA` and adds a
#' logical `suppressed` column.   Zeros are left alone on purpose.
#'
#' @param df A data frame with an integer `count` column.
#' @param lo,hi Bounds of the suppression window.
#' @return `df` with `count` possibly set to `NA`, plus `suppressed`.
#' @examples
#' suppress_small(tibble::tibble(count = c(0L, 4L, 25L)))
#' @export
suppress_small <- function(df, lo = SUPPRESS_MIN, hi = SUPPRESS_MAX) {
  df |>
    mutate(
      suppressed = !is.na(count) & count >= lo & count <= hi,
      count = if_else(suppressed, NA_integer_, as.integer(count))
    )
}

#' Weekly rate per 100,000 residents
#'
#' @param events Number of events.
#' @param population Mid-year population estimate.
#' @noRd
rate_per_100k <- function(events, population) {
  round(events / population * 1e5, 1)
}

#+ load-data
#| label: load-data
#| message: false
#| cache:   true
#| file-paths:
#|   - "data/raw/ed_visits.csv"
#|   - data/raw/population_estimates_2025.csv
#|   - data/raw/zip_groups.csv
#| col-types: { visit_date: date, zip: character ,count: integer }
#| notes: Population denominators are the state demographer's 2025 vintage; switch to the 2026 vintage once it is published (usually in late spring).
ed_visits <- read_csv(
  file.path(data_dir, "ed_visits.csv"),
  col_types = cols(visit_date = col_date(), zip = col_character(), syndrome = col_character(), count = col_integer())
)
population <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "population_estimates_2025.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
zip_groups <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "zip_groups.csv"), col_types = "cc")

#+ weekly-summary, fig.width = 8
#| label: weekly-summary
#| fig-cap: 'Weekly ED visits for influenza-like illness, by ZIP code group'
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height:   4.5
#| fig-alt: >-
#|     Line chart of weekly emergency department visits for influenza-like illness
#|     in four ZIP code groups since September 2025.
#| syndromes: [ILI,"COVID-like",  RSV-like]
weekly <- ed_visits |>
  filter(syndrome %in% c("ILI", "COVID-like", "RSV-like")) |>
  mutate(week = floor_date(visit_date, unit = "week", week_start = 1)) |>
  left_join(zip_groups, by = "zip") |>
  group_by(week, zip_group, syndrome) |>
  summarise(count = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(population, by = "zip_group") |>
  mutate(rate = rate_per_100k(count, population), unstable = count < UNSTABLE_BELOW) |>
  suppress_small()

ggplot(filter(weekly, syndrome == "ILI"), aes(week, rate, colour = zip_group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, unstable), colour = "grey60") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Visits per 100,000", colour = "ZIP group") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# fmt: markdown
dashboard_note <- r"(
## About these numbers

Counts come from emergency department visits where the chief complaint or the discharge diagnosis matches the syndrome definition; they are *not* lab-confirmed cases.  Numbers for the most recent week are **provisional** and usually rise by 5-15% as late records arrive.

-   Cells with 1-10 visits are hidden to protect privacy.
-   Rates are per 100,000 residents.
    Rates based on fewer than 20 visits are shown in grey.
-   ZIP codes are grouped into four areas, see the methods page.

Data source: Riverton County syndromic surveillance system (ESSENCE), updated weekly.
)"

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
email_body <- "
Hello all,

This week's respiratory update is attached. ED visits for influenza-like illness rose for the third week in a row, mostly in the North and Riverside ZIP groups. RSV-like visits are flat. Please check the suppressed cells before you forward anything outside the department.

Thanks, the surveillance team
"

#+ write-outputs
#| label: write-outputs
#| eval: !expr Sys.getenv("SURV_WRITE", "true") == "true"
#| outputs:
#|     csv: data/public/weekly_respiratory.csv
#|     note:  "data/public/about.md"
#| last-reviewed: 2026-09-22
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
weekly |>
  select(week, zip_group, syndrome, count, rate, suppressed, unstable) |>
  arrange(desc(week), zip_group, syndrome) |>
  write_csv(file.path(out_dir, "weekly_respiratory.csv"), na = "")
writeLines(dashboard_note, file.path(out_dir, "about.md"))
message("Wrote ", nrow(weekly), " rows to ", out_dir)

#' Suppress small counts in a tidy table
#'
#' Replaces counts between `lo` and `hi` (inclusive) with `NA` and adds a
#' logical `suppressed` column.   Zeros are left alone on purpose.
#'
#' @param df A data frame with an integer `count` column.
#' @param lo,hi Bounds of the suppression window.
#' @return `df` with `count` possibly set to `NA`, plus `suppressed`.
#' @examples
#' suppress_small(tibble::tibble(count = c(0L, 4L, 25L)))
#' @export
suppress_small <- function(df, lo = SUPPRESS_MIN, hi = SUPPRESS_MAX) {
  df |>
    mutate(
      suppressed = !is.na(count) & count >= lo & count <= hi,
      count = if_else(suppressed, NA_integer_, as.integer(count))
    )
}

#' Weekly rate per 100,000 residents
#'
#' @param events Number of events.
#' @param population Mid-year population estimate.
#' @noRd
rate_per_100k <- function(events, population) {
  round(events / population * 1e5, 1)
}

#+ load-data
#| label: load-data
#| message: false
#| cache:   true
#| file-paths:
#|   - "data/raw/ed_visits.csv"
#|   - data/raw/population_estimates_2025.csv
#|   - data/raw/zip_groups.csv
#| col-types: { visit_date: date, zip: character ,count: integer }
#| notes: Population denominators are the state demographer's 2025 vintage; switch to the 2026 vintage once it is published (usually in late spring).
ed_visits <- read_csv(
  file.path(data_dir, "ed_visits.csv"),
  col_types = cols(visit_date = col_date(), zip = col_character(), syndrome = col_character(), count = col_integer())
)
population <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "population_estimates_2025.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
zip_groups <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "zip_groups.csv"), col_types = "cc")

#+ weekly-summary, fig.width = 8
#| label: weekly-summary
#| fig-cap: 'Weekly ED visits for influenza-like illness, by ZIP code group'
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height:   4.5
#| fig-alt: >-
#|     Line chart of weekly emergency department visits for influenza-like illness
#|     in four ZIP code groups since September 2025.
#| syndromes: [ILI,"COVID-like",  RSV-like]
weekly <- ed_visits |>
  filter(syndrome %in% c("ILI", "COVID-like", "RSV-like")) |>
  mutate(week = floor_date(visit_date, unit = "week", week_start = 1)) |>
  left_join(zip_groups, by = "zip") |>
  group_by(week, zip_group, syndrome) |>
  summarise(count = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(population, by = "zip_group") |>
  mutate(rate = rate_per_100k(count, population), unstable = count < UNSTABLE_BELOW) |>
  suppress_small()

ggplot(filter(weekly, syndrome == "ILI"), aes(week, rate, colour = zip_group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, unstable), colour = "grey60") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Visits per 100,000", colour = "ZIP group") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# fmt: markdown
dashboard_note <- r"(
## About these numbers

Counts come from emergency department visits where the chief complaint or the discharge diagnosis matches the syndrome definition; they are *not* lab-confirmed cases.  Numbers for the most recent week are **provisional** and usually rise by 5-15% as late records arrive.

-   Cells with 1-10 visits are hidden to protect privacy.
-   Rates are per 100,000 residents.
    Rates based on fewer than 20 visits are shown in grey.
-   ZIP codes are grouped into four areas, see the methods page.

Data source: Riverton County syndromic surveillance system (ESSENCE), updated weekly.
)"

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
email_body <- "
Hello all,

This week's respiratory update is attached. ED visits for influenza-like illness rose for the third week in a row, mostly in the North and Riverside ZIP groups. RSV-like visits are flat. Please check the suppressed cells before you forward anything outside the department.

Thanks, the surveillance team
"

#+ write-outputs
#| label: write-outputs
#| eval: !expr Sys.getenv("SURV_WRITE", "true") == "true"
#| outputs:
#|     csv: data/public/weekly_respiratory.csv
#|     note:  "data/public/about.md"
#| last-reviewed: 2026-09-22
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
weekly |>
  select(week, zip_group, syndrome, count, rate, suppressed, unstable) |>
  arrange(desc(week), zip_group, syndrome) |>
  write_csv(file.path(out_dir, "weekly_respiratory.csv"), na = "")
writeLines(dashboard_note, file.path(out_dir, "about.md"))
message("Wrote ", nrow(weekly), " rows to ", out_dir)

Statistik 1 · Einführung in die Statistik (STAT 1010) 📊
=========================================================

[![CI](https://github.com/stat1010/kurs/actions/workflows/site-and-autograder.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/stat1010/kurs/actions/workflows/site-and-autograder.yml) [![Lizenz: CC BY-SA 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Lizenz-CC%20BY--SA%204.0-lightgrey.svg)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)   

Dieses Repository enthält *alles*, was wir für den Kurs **STAT 1010** im Wintersemester 2026/27 brauchen: die Quarto-Webseite mit dem Vorlesungsskript, die wöchentlichen Übungsblätter, die Laborbuch-Vorlagen für Studierende, die Konfiguration des JupyterHub und den Autograder.
Fragen zur Infrastruktur bitte an das Tutorenteam, Fragen zum Inhalt an Prof. Koch.  
*English summary:* this repository holds the course website, weekly exercise sheets, lab-notebook templates, the hub configuration and the autograder for an introductory statistics course taught in German, with English, French and Spanish material for exchange students.

## 🗂️ Inhalt / Contents

| Ordner | Inhalt | Verantwortlich |
|---|---|---|
| `skript/` | Vorlesungsskript (Quarto, `.qmd`) | M. Koch |
| `uebungen/` | Übungsblätter + Lösungen (Lösungen nur im privaten Branch!) | A. Ruiz |
| `labs/`|Laborbuch-Vorlagen (Jupyter, R Markdown)| Α. Παπαδόπουλος |
| `grader/` | Autograder (Python, Otter-Grader), siehe [grader/README.md](grader/README.md) | J. Weiß |
|`hub/` | JupyterHub/TLJH-Konfiguration und Ansible-Playbooks | IT ⚙️ + J. Weiß |

## 🚀 Schnellstart

1. Repository klonen und in den Ordner wechseln:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/stat1010/kurs.git && cd kurs
   ```
2. Umgebung anlegen (Python 3.12 *und* R ≥ 4.4 werden gebraucht). Wer conda benutzt,
kann stattdessen `conda env create -f environment.yml` ausführen, das dauert aber deutlich länger und ist auf den Pool-Rechnern nicht nötig.
3. Webseite lokal ansehen: `quarto preview`, dann im Browser <kbd>Strg</kbd>+<kbd>F5</kbd> drücken, falls noch alte CSS-Dateien im Cache liegen.
4. Autograder-Tests laufen lassen:

       cd grader && pytest -q

5. Optional: den Screenshot des Hubs für die Doku aktualisieren.

   ![Login-Seite des STAT-1010-Hubs mit Uni-Logo und dem Hinweis „Nur für Kursteilnehmende“](docs/img/hub-login.png "Login-Seite")

***

## 📐 Notation

Im ganzen Kurs verwenden wir dieselbe Notation: $x_1, \dots, x_n$ sind die Beobachtungen, $\bar{x} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i$ ist das arithmetische Mittel und $s^2$ die korrigierte Stichprobenvarianz. Die Formel lautet

$$
s^2 = \frac{1}{n-1} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \left( x_i - \bar{x} \right)^2
$$

und wird im Autograder mit einer absoluten Toleranz von 10<sup>−6</sup> geprüft. Wer in Python `np.var(x)` statt `np.var(x, ddof=1)` schreibt, bekommt deshalb einen Hinweis im Feedback (siehe [Feedback-Vorlagen][feedback]). Das Bestimmtheitsmaß heißt bei uns R<sup>2</sup>, nicht $r^2$, und Dezimalzahlen schreiben wir im Fließtext mit Komma (0,05), im Code natürlich mit Punkt.

## 📖 Begriffe

Laborbuch
:   Ein Jupyter- oder R-Markdown-Notebook, in dem Studierende jede Woche eine kleine Datenanalyse dokumentieren. Bewertet wird nicht nur das Ergebnis, sondern auch, ob die einzelnen Schritte nachvollziehbar sind.

Autograder
: Der Dienst, der Abgaben automatisch testet; er läuft in Containern ohne Netzwerkzugriff.

Übungsgruppe
:    Eine Gruppe von höchstens 25 Studierenden mit einer Tutorin oder einem Tutor.

## 🌍 Glossar (Auszug)

Für die Austauschstudierenden aus Kyoto und Thessaloniki pflegen zwei Tutorinnen eine Kurzfassung des Glossars auf Japanisch (統計学の基本用語集) und auf Griechisch (Γλωσσάριο Στατιστικής); beide Fassungen werden automatisch aus `glossar.csv` erzeugt. Korrekturen von Chloé, Zoë und François sind jederzeit willkommen.

| Deutsch | English | Français | Español | 日本語 | Ελληνικά |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:-:|--:|
| Mittelwert | mean | moyenne | media | 平均値 | μέση τιμή |
| Standardabweichung | standard deviation | écart type | desviación estándar | 標準偏差 | τυπική απόκλιση |
| Konfidenzintervall | confidence interval | intervalle de confiance | intervalo de confianza | 信頼区間 | διάστημα εμπιστοσύνης |
| Hypothesentest | hypothesis test | test d'hypothèse | prueba de hipótesis | 仮説検定 | έλεγχος υποθέσεων |
| Stichprobe | sample | échantillon | muestra | 標本 | δείγμα |

### Operatoren, die oft verwechselt werden

| Schreibweise | Bedeutung | R | Python |
|---|---|---|---|
| $P(A \mid B)$ | bedingte Wahrscheinlichkeit | – | – |
| `x \| y` | elementweises ODER | `x \| y` | `np.logical_or(x, y)` |
| `a \|\| b` | ODER mit Kurzschluss | `a \|\| b` | `a or b` |
| `%>%` vs. `\|>` | Pipe | beide | – (gibt es nicht) |

> **Hinweis:** Lösungen gehören **nie** in den Branch `main`. Der Branch ist öffentlich,
und Studierende finden wirklich alles.
>
> **Note:** solutions live in the private repository `stat1010/loesungen`; ask Jonas for access.

## 👩‍🏫 Für Tutor:innen

Jede Übungsgruppe hat eine eigene Datei in `hub/gruppen/`, z.B. `T03.yml`:

```yaml
gruppe:   T03
tutor: { name: "Αλέξανδρος Παπαδόπουλος", email: a.papadopoulos@uni-beispielstadt.de }
termine:
- "Mi 08:30"
- Mi 10:15
sprachen: [de,el,
  en]

```

**Name:**

2. Berechne $\bar{x}$ und $s$ und interpretiere beide Werte im Kontext der Fragestellung, also mit Einheiten.

```r

```
````

    Kurs-ID: STAT-1010-WS2627

# Changelog · Änderungsprotokoll

Alle nennenswerten Änderungen an Kurswebseite, Autograder und Laborbuch-Vorlagen werden hier dokumentiert. Das Format orientiert sich an [Keep a Changelog][kac]; die Versionsnummern folgen dem Schema `JAHR.MONAT.PATCH`, weil sich Semester nun einmal nicht an [SemVer][semver] halten.   

> **Note:** entries are written in German first. English is fine too,
> but please don't translate old entries – links from the forum point to them.

## [Unreleased]

### ✨ Neu

- Feedback-Vorlagen gibt es jetzt auch auf Französisch und Spanisch (`grader/templates/feedback.fr.md`, `feedback.es.md`); die Sprache richtet sich nach dem Profil im LMS.
- Neue Laborbuch-Vorlage **Lab 6 – Regression** mit einem Beispiel für $R^2$ und den Residuenplot:

  ```python
  import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
  modell = smf.ols("gewicht ~ groesse", data=df).fit()
  print(modell.summary())
  ```

  ![Residuen gegen angepasste Werte; Beispielausgabe aus Lab 6](docs/img/lab06-residuen.png)
-   Tastenkürzel-Spickzettel im Skript: <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> führt eine Zelle aus, <kbd>Esc</kbd> <kbd>B</kbd> fügt darunter eine neue ein.

### 🔧 Geändert

* Die Gewichtung der Teilleistungen wurde vereinheitlicht; die Gesamtpunktzahl berechnet sich jetzt als

$$
P_{\text{gesamt}} = \min\Bigl(100,\; 0{,}4\, P_{\text{Übung}} + 0{,}2\, P_{\text{Projekt}} + 0{,}4\, P_{\text{Klausur}} + B\Bigr), \qquad B \le 5 .
$$

* `otter-grader` ist auf 6.1.0 aktualisiert; ältere Notebooks (Metadaten `stat1010.version` < `2026.10`) werden mit einer Warnung trotzdem angenommen.
* Die Rückmeldung nennt den Mittelwert jetzt $\bar{x}$ statt „xquer“, und Varianzen werden mit vier Nachkommastellen ausgegeben.

- - -

## [2026.11.1] - 2026-11-12

### 🐛 Behoben

1. Der Autograder hat bei Aufgaben mit Toleranz die *relative* statt der absoluten Abweichung geprüft, d.h. bei Werten nahe 0 wurde fast alles als falsch markiert. Jetzt gilt
$|\hat{\theta} - \theta| < \varepsilon$ mit $\varepsilon = 10^{-6}$.
2. Umlaute in Dateinamen (z.B. `Übung_03.ipynb`) führten auf den Windows-Runnern zu einem `UnicodeEncodeError`.
Behoben durch `PYTHONUTF8=1` in der CI.
3. Im Skript stand <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> statt <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd>; ersteres führt die Zelle aus, *ohne* zur nächsten zu springen.
4. Japanische Achsenbeschriftungen in Lab 3 (標本平均の分布と中心極限定理) wurden als Kästchen dargestellt, weil `fonts-noto-cjk` im Image fehlte.

> Hinweis: Wer Lab 4 **vor** dem 12.11. abgegeben hat, wurde mit der alten Toleranz bewertet. Die Abgaben wurden automatisch neu bewertet; die Punkte können sich dabei nur verbessert haben.

### ⚠️ Inkompatible Änderungen

| Alt | Neu | Hinweis |
|---|---|---|
| `grader run --format csv\|json` | `grader run --output-format {csv,json,md}` | Markdown-Ausgabe ist neu |
| `tolerance = 1e-6` | `abs_tolerance = 1e-6` | `rel_tolerance` ist neu, Standard `0` |
| Regex `^(lab\|hw)[0-9]+$` | `^(lab\|hw\|exam)[0-9]{2}$` | zweistellige Nummern! |

Migration in zwei Schritten:

`grader.toml`
:   Den Schlüssel `tolerance` in `abs_tolerance` umbenennen. Wer bisher relative Toleranzen wollte, setzt zusätzlich `rel_tolerance`, z.B. auf `1e-3`.

`labs/*.ipynb`
: Das Metadatenfeld `stat1010.version` muss auf `2026.11` stehen, sonst lehnt der Grader die Abgabe mit einem (hoffentlich verständlichen) Fehler ab.

Die neue Konfiguration für ein Übungsblatt sieht so aus:

```yaml
# grader/assignments/lab04.yml
name:  lab04
titel: { de: "Konfidenzintervalle", en: Confidence intervals, fr: "Intervalles de confiance" }
punkte: 20
abs_tolerance: 1.0e-6
rel_tolerance: 0
spaete_abgabe: "off"
tests:
- q1a
- q1b
- {name: q2, hidden: true, gewicht: 2}
```

Beispielausgabe von `grader check`:

    $ grader check labs/lab04.ipynb
    ✓ metadata ok (stat1010.version = 2026.11)
    ✓ 7 public tests found
    ✗ cell 12: output too large (6.2 MB > 5 MB)

***

## [2026.10.0] – 2026-10-01

Semesterstart! 🎉 Erste Version für das WiSe 2026/27, getestet mit 412 Testkonten und einer simulierten Abgabewelle von 300 Notebooks in zehn Minuten.

### ✨ Neu
* Autograder-Rückmeldungen erklären jetzt, *warum* ein Test fehlschlägt, statt nur `AssertionError` zu zeigen.[^feedback] Beispiel: „Dein Mittelwert ist 172,4; erwartet war 171,9 (Toleranz 0,01). Hast du die fehlenden Werte entfernt?“
* Mehrsprachiges Feedback (vorerst Deutsch, Französisch, Spanisch); Griechisch und Japanisch sind in Arbeit:

| Sprache | Beispielsatz im Feedback | Status |
|---|---|:-:|
| Deutsch | Dein Konfidenzintervall ist zu schmal. | ✅ |
| Français | Ton intervalle de confiance est trop étroit. | ✅ |
| Español | Tu intervalo de confianza es demasiado estrecho. | ✅ |
| Ελληνικά | Το διάστημα εμπιστοσύνης σου είναι πολύ στενό. | 🚧 |
| 日本語 | 信頼区間が狭すぎます。`qt()` を使いましたか？ | 🚧 |

* Feedback-Vorlagen sind jetzt Markdown-Dateien statt Python-Strings. Eine minimale Vorlage:

````markdown
## Rückmeldung zu {{ assignment }}
*  Aufgabe 1a: ✓
*  Aufgabe 2:  ✗ — das Intervall ist zu schmal. Hast du `qnorm` statt `qt` verwendet?

Punkte: **{{ score }}** / {{ max_score }}  
Fragen? → Forum
````

### 🗑️ Entfernt
- Die alte nbgrader-Integration (`hub/nbgrader_config.py`). Wer sie noch braucht: Tag `v2025.07.3`.
-   Unterstützung für Python 3.9 und 3.10.

---

[^feedback]: Die Erklärungen stehen in `grader/messages/*.yml` und werden pro Test gepflegt. Bitte bei neuen Tests immer mindestens eine deutsche und eine englische Meldung hinterlegen, sonst fällt der Grader auf die generische Meldung „Test fehlgeschlagen“ zurück, und die hilft niemandem.

[Unreleased]: https://github.com/stat1010/kurs/compare/v2026.11.1...HEAD
[2026.11.1]: https://github.com/stat1010/kurs/compare/v2026.10.0...v2026.11.1
[2026.10.0]: https://github.com/stat1010/kurs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0
[kac]: https://keepachangelog.com/de/1.1.0/
[semver]: https://semver.org/lang/de/

[![CI](https://github.com/riverton-city/opendata-portal/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/riverton-city/opendata-portal/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Datasets](https://img.shields.io/badge/datasets-612-brightgreen)](https://data.riverton.gov/dataset) ![Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA](https://img.shields.io/badge/WCAG-2.2%20AA-success) Riverton Open Data Portal ========================= The **Riverton Open Data Portal** is the City of Riverton's official catalogue of public datasets: budgets, 311 service requests, building permits, bus stop locations, library branch visits and a lot more. This repository holds the CKAN extension, the harvesters that pull data out of department systems, and the static _explore_ site that sits in front of the catalogue. It is maintained by the Office of Digital Services together with volunteers from Code for Riverton, so please be patient with response times -- most of the volunteers work on it on Tuesday evenings. > [!NOTE] > Looking for the data itself rather than the code? Go to or use the API at . ## Contents ## - [What's in here](#whats-in-here) - [Quick start](#quick-start) * [Configuration](#configuration) - [Publishing a dataset](#publishing-a-dataset) - [For department staff](#for-department-staff) - [For developers](#for-developers) - [FAQ](#faq) ## What's in here | Directory | What it does | Owner | |---|---|---| | `ckanext-riverton/` | CKAN plugin: theme, custom fields, the `frequency` validator | Digital Services| | `harvesters/` | One module per department system (Accela, Tyler Munis, Koha, the 311 CRM) | Code for Riverton | | `explore/` | Static site built with Eleventy | Digital Services | | `infra/` |Terraform and Ansible | IT Infrastructure (ask in #infra first) | | `docs/`|Guides for publishers| everyone | Quick start ----------- You need Docker, `make`, and about 6 GB of free disk space for the sample database. 1. Clone the repository and copy the example environment file: ```bash git clone https://github.com/riverton-city/opendata-portal.git cd opendata-portal && cp .env.example .env ``` 1. Start everything: make up The first run downloads the CKAN image and loads about 40 sample datasets, which takes a few minutes on a laptop. 1. Open and log in as `admin` / `admin`.\ Change that password if your machine is reachable from anywhere else! > [!WARNING] > The sample database contains *fake* addresses and permit numbers. Never load a production dump onto a laptop; some datasets (e.g. code-enforcement complaints) are only partly public. If `make up` fails with *port is already allocated*, something else (often a local PostgreSQL) is using port 5432; stop it, or set `POSTGRES_PORT` in `.env`. ## Configuration Settings live in `portal.yaml`. Only the keys below are required, everything else has a sensible default. ```yaml portal: site_title: "Riverton Open Data" site_url: https://data.riverton.gov default_license: "cc-by-4.0" harvest: schedule: '0 3 * * *' departments: [ public-works, parks-and-recreation, library,city-clerk ] retry_failed: yes contact: {email: opendata@riverton.gov, phone: "311"} ``` Environment variables override the file, e.g. `PORTAL__HARVEST__SCHEDULE`. The ones people ask about most: | Variable | Default | Example | Notes | |:--|:-:|--|--:| | `CKAN_SITE_URL` | `http://localhost:5000` | `https://data.riverton.gov` | must not end with `/` | | `CKAN_SQLALCHEMY_URL` | *(none)* | `postgresql://ckan:secret@db/ckan` | required | | `HARVEST_DEPARTMENTS` | all |`library\|parks`| pipe-separated | | `EXPLORE_BASE_PATH` | `/` | `/explore/` | | Publishing a dataset -------------------- ### For department staff ### Most staff publish through the web form, not through code. The short version: 1. Sign in with your city account. 2. Click **Add dataset** and fill in at least the title, the description, the publisher and the *update frequency*. 3. Upload a CSV, or paste a link to a file your department already publishes. 3) Ask your department's data steward to review it. 4) Once approved, the dataset appears on the portal within 15 minutes. > **Tip from the City Clerk's office:** before uploading, > - remove hidden columns and merged cells, > - name columns in lower case with underscores (total\_amount, not "Total Amount"), > * and never put two values in one cell > - save as UTF-8 CSV, not as .xlsx ### For developers New harvesters go in `harvesters//` and must implement `fetch()` and `transform()`. See [the harvester guide][harvester-guide] and the existing [Koha harvester][koha] for a small, readable example. Fields marked with \* in the [metadata schema][schema] are required, and *every* harvester needs a test that runs against the recorded fixtures in `tests/cassettes/`.
Example transform() output ~~~json {"name": "library-branch-visits", "title": "Library branch visits", "frequency": "monthly", "resources": [{"url": "https://data.riverton.gov/library/visits.csv", "format": "CSV"}]} ~~~
## FAQ **Can I use the data commercially?** Yes. Unless a dataset says otherwise it is published under CC BY 4.0[^license]. __Why is dataset X out of date?__ Every dataset lists its publisher, and the portal team cannot update other departments' data for them. The weekly freshness report[^freshness] shows which ones are overdue. *Is there an API?* Yes, the standard [CKAN Action API][ckan-api]. Please use an API key for anything that runs more than once an hour. *** Made with care by the Office of Digital Services and [Code for Riverton][cfr].
Questions: opendata@riverton.gov or 311 or open an issue on GitHub. ___ [^license]: A few datasets (mostly GIS layers licensed from the county) use the Open Data Commons Attribution License instead. Check the *License* field on each dataset page before you reuse anything, and ask us if the field is empty. [^freshness]: The report is generated every Monday morning by `freshness.py`. [harvester-guide]: docs/harvesters.md [koha]: harvesters/library/koha.py "Koha harvester" [schema]: [cfr]: https://codeforriverton.org [ckan-api]: https://docs.ckan.org/en/2.10/api/ [ckan-docs]: https://docs.ckan.org/en/2.10/ [old-portal]: http://opendata.riverton.gov/ "Retired in 2024"

See [the harvester guide][harvester-guide] and the existing [Koha harvester][koha] for a small, readable example. Fields marked with \* in the [metadata schema][schema] are required, and *every* harvester needs a test that runs against the recorded fixtures in `tests/cassettes/`.

## FAQ **Can I use the data commercially?** Yes. Unless a dataset says otherwise it is published under CC BY 4.0[^license]. __Why is dataset X out of date?__ Every dataset lists its publisher, and the portal team cannot update other departments' data for them. The weekly freshness report[^freshness] shows which ones are overdue. *Is there an API?* Yes, the standard [CKAN Action API][ckan-api]. Please use an API key for anything that runs more than once an hour. *** Made with care by the Office of Digital Services and [Code for Riverton][cfr].
Questions: opendata@riverton.gov or 311 or open an issue on GitHub. ___ [^license]: A few datasets (mostly GIS layers licensed from the county) use the Open Data Commons Attribution License instead. Check the *License* field on each dataset page before you reuse anything, and ask us if the field is empty. [^freshness]: The report is generated every Monday morning by `freshness.py`. # Mitmachen 🤝 #

Danke, dass du beim Kurs **STAT 1010** mithilfst! Dieser Leitfaden richtet sich an Tutor:innen und studentische Hilfskräfte, die Aufgaben schreiben, Tests für den Autograder ergänzen oder die Laborbuch-Vorlagen verbessern. Für Studierende gibt es eine eigene Seite ([Hilfe für Studierende](hilfe.md)), und Fragen zur Bewertung gehören grundsätzlich in die Tutorenbesprechung am Montag.

> **Hinweis:** Bitte arbeite nie direkt auf `main`. Jede Änderung läuft über einen Pull Request mit mindestens einem Review.  
> **Note for exchange TAs:** English is perfectly fine for code, comments and PR descriptions.

## 🧭 Ablauf in fünf Schritten

1. Forke das Repository oder lege einen Branch an, z.B. `aufgabe/lab05-power` oder `fix/grader-toleranz`.
2. Installiere die Pre-commit-Hooks; sie formatieren YAML und Markdown automatisch, bevor du committest:
   ```sh
   uv tool install pre-commit
   pre-commit install
   ```
3. Schreibe die Aufgabe (siehe unten) und rendere sie lokal mit `quarto preview skript/`. Prüfe vor allem die Formeln,
denn KaTeX und MathJax verhalten sich bei `\operatorname` unterschiedlich.
4. Lass die Tests laufen. Wenn ein versteckter Test fehlschlägt, schau dir zuerst die Musterlösung an und nicht den Test.
5.  Öffne einen Pull Request und weise ihn der zuständigen Person zu (Tabelle unten).

Commit-Nachrichten schreiben wir so:

    lab05: Aufgabe 3 (Teststärke) ergänzt

    - versteckter Test q3b prüft jetzt auch n = 50
    - Toleranz auf 1e-4 gesetzt, weil power.t.test() iteriert

## ✍️ Aufgaben schreiben

Formeln stehen immer in `$...$` bzw. `$$...$$`. Der Mittelwert heißt $\bar{x}$ (nicht $\overline{x}$ oder $\hat{\mu}$, außer wenn es ausdrücklich um den Schätzer geht), die Standardabweichung der Stichprobe $s$, und Hypothesen schreiben wir als $H_0\colon \mu = \mu_0$ gegen $H_1\colon \mu \neq \mu_0$. Bei Teststatistiken bitte immer die Verteilung unter $H_0$ dazuschreiben, etwa so:

$$
T = \frac{\bar{X} - \mu_0}{S / \sqrt{n}} \;\overset{H_0}{\sim}\; t_{n-1}
$$

Weitere Konventionen:

Dezimalzeichen
:   Im Fließtext Komma (0,05), im Code Punkt (`0.05`). In Tabellen mit Zahlen aus R-Ausgaben darf der Punkt bleiben.

Einheiten
: Immer mit schmalem Leerzeichen: 170 cm, 2,5 h. Flächen als cm<sup>2</sup>, nicht cm^2.

Tastenkürzel
:   Mit `<kbd>`: <kbd>Strg</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> rendert in RStudio, <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> führt in JupyterLab eine Zelle aus.

So sieht eine Aufgabe im Quelltext aus (bitte kopieren und anpassen):

````markdown
### Aufgabe 3: Teststärke   

Eine Tutorin vermutet, dass Studierende vor der Klausur im Mittel **weniger** als 7 h schlafen.
Sie befragt $n = 40$ Personen.

1.  Formuliere $H_0$ und $H_1$.
2.  Berechne die Teststärke für $\mu_1 = 6{,}5$ und $\sigma = 1{,}2$.
   * Tipp: `power.t.test()` in R bzw. `statsmodels.stats.power` in Python.

```{r}
#| eval: false
power.t.test(n = 40, delta = 0.5, sd = 1.2, type = "one.sample", alternative = "one.sided")
```
````

## 🧪 Tests für den Autograder

Jedes Übungsblatt hat eine Konfigurationsdatei. Felder, die du nicht brauchst, lässt du weg; alles andere hat sinnvolle Standardwerte.

```yaml
name: lab05
titel: {de: "Hypothesentests", en: "Hypothesis tests",
        es: "Pruebas de hipótesis"}
punkte:   20
tests:
  - name: q1
    punkte: 4
  - name:   q3b
    punkte: 6
    hidden: True
    nachricht_de: Die Teststärke ist zu niedrig. Hast du einseitig getestet?
    nachricht_en: "Power is too low: did you use a one-sided test?"
```

Dateinamen und Branches müssen bestimmten Mustern folgen, sonst lehnt die CI den Pull Request ab:

| Was | Muster | Beispiel |
|---|---|---|
| Branch | `^(aufgabe\|fix\|doku)/[a-z0-9-]+$` | `aufgabe/lab05-power` |
| Testdatei | `tests/q[0-9]+[a-z]?\.py` | `tests/q3b.py` |
| Übungsblatt | `lab[0-9]{2}` oder `hw[0-9]{2}` | `lab05` |
| Feedback-Vorlage | `feedback\.(de\|en\|fr\|es)\.md` | `feedback.fr.md` |

## 🔤 Wer ist wofür zuständig?

<!-- fmt: off -->
| Bereich          | Person                     | Sprache(n)  |
|------------------|----------------------------|-------------|
| Skript           | Prof. Dr. M. Koch          | de, en      |
<!-- fmt: on -->

| Bereich | Person | Sprache(n) | Erreichbar |
|---|---|---|---|
| Übungsblätter | Ana Ruiz Fernández | de, es, en | Mo–Mi |
| Laborbücher | Αλέξανδρος Παπαδόπουλος | el, de, en | Di, Do |
| Autograder | Jonas Weiß | de, en | immer (leider) |
| Japanische Materialien | 山田 花子 (Hanako Yamada) | ja, en, de | Fr |
| Französische Zusammenfassungen | Chloé Martin | fr, de | bis Februar |

Für die japanische Fassung gilt: Fachbegriffe stehen beim ersten Auftreten zusätzlich auf Deutsch in Klammern, also z.B. 信頼区間（Konfidenzintervall）und 有意水準（Signifikanzniveau）, damit Studierende die Begriffe im Skript wiederfinden.

---

## ❓ Häufige Fragen

**Darf ich Aufgaben aus anderen Kursen übernehmen?**  
Ja, wenn die Lizenz es erlaubt und die Quelle angegeben ist.[^lizenz] Bei Aufgaben aus Lehrbüchern bitte vorher mit Prof. Koch sprechen.

**Was mache ich, wenn der Hub während der Übung ausfällt?**\
Ruhe bewahren. Im [Notfallplan][notfall] steht, wie man auf die lokale Installation umsteigt; die Studierenden bekommen dafür einen Link zu [Binder][binder].

[^lizenz]: Das Skript steht unter CC BY-SA 4.0, der Code unter MIT. Material mit einer NC-Lizenz („nicht kommerziell“) können wir übernehmen, müssen es aber getrennt kennzeichnen, weil die Kurswebseite öffentlich ist.

[notfall]: https://stat1010.github.io/intern/notfallplan.html "Notfallplan (nur intern)"
[binder]: https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/stat1010/lab-templates/HEAD?urlpath=lab
