# Changelog
All notable changes to **ShiftShare** are documented in this file.
The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) -- mostly. Volunteer-facing changes are also summarised in plain language in the monthly partner newsletter, which is the place to look if you are a coordinator rather than a developer.

<!-- Add new entries under "Unreleased". Categories: Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed / Security. -->

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- Waitlist position is now shown on the booking page ("You are 3rd on the waitlist").
- Partner admins can export a shift's sign-in sheet as PDF *or* CSV.
* SMS reminders in Spanish and Vietnamese, using the preferred language from the volunteer's profile.

### Fixed
- Shifts that cross midnight (e.g. the overnight shelter shift, 22:00-06:00) were shown on the wrong day in the weekly calendar.
- Names containing \* or \_ were rendered as emphasis in reminder emails.

## [3.2.0] - 2026-10-28

> [!WARNING]
> This release changes the **bookings API**. `GET /bookings` now returns a paginated object instead of a bare array, so partners using the Zapier integration must reconnect it.
> See the [migration notes](#migrating-from-31-to-32).

### Added
-   New _Kiosk mode_ for the sign-in tablets at the warehouse door.
    Volunteers tap their name and the kiosk records the check-in time.

    Kiosk mode needs a partner admin to enable it once per device:

    ```bash
    php artisan kiosk:register --organisation=12 --name="Warehouse door"
    ```
-   Organisations can set a minimum age per shift (`min_age`).
   - Shown on the shift card as "16+".
   - Enforced at booking time; younger volunteers can still sign up together with a guardian.
-   Calendar feeds (`.ics`) for each volunteer.

### Changed
1. Reminder emails are sent 24 hours before a shift instead of 48 (partners asked for this repeatedly).
1. The "My shifts" page now loads about three times faster for volunteers with long histories.
1. Dropped support for PHP 8.1.

### Fixed
* Cancelling a booking from the link in the reminder email didn't free the spot when the shift was in a different timezone than the server.
* Typo in the Vietnamese translation of "check in"  
  (thanks to Lan Pham for spotting it!)
* Organisation logos wider than 2000px broke the printable rota.\
  They are now scaled down on upload.

### Security
- Session cookies now use `SameSite=Lax`.
- Rate limiting on `/login`: 10 attempts per 15 minutes per IP address.

Migrating from 3.1 to 3.2
-------------------------

The bookings list endpoint changed shape. Before:

~~~json
[{"id": 1, "shift_id": 44, "status": "confirmed"}]
~~~

After:

```json
{"data": [{"id": 1, "shift_id": 44, "status": "confirmed"}], "next_cursor": null}
```

| Endpoint | 3.1 | 3.2 | Action needed |
|:---|:---:|:---:|---|
| `GET /bookings` | array | object (`data` + `next_cursor`) | update your client |
| `GET /shifts?status=open\|full` | yes | yes | none |
|`POST /bookings`|200|201| check the status code |

If you call the API from a spreadsheet (several food banks do this with Google Apps Script), the old behaviour is still available for six months by sending the header `Accept: application/vnd.shiftshare.v31+json`; after that it will be removed without further notice.

- - -

## [3.1.4] - 2026-08-19
### Fixed
- Volunteers who changed their email address were logged out on every device[^sessions].
- The waitlist promotion job ran twice when two shifts ended at the same minute.

## [3.1.0] - 2026-06-02 ##
### Added
3) Partner organisations can have more than one admin.
4) Bulk-create recurring shifts ("every Saturday until 31 August").

### Deprecated
- The `GET /v2/*` endpoints. They will be removed in 4.0, no earlier than __March 2027__.

<details>
<summary>Merged pull requests in 3.1.0</summary>

- #812 Multiple admins per organisation (Rosa Delgado)
- #820 Recurring shifts (Ahmed Yusuf)
- #833 Fix for the waitlist promotion race (Lan Pham)

</details>

___

## [3.0.0] - 2026-01-15
Initial release of the rewritten app.  See the [3.0 announcement](https://volunteer.riverton.org/blog/shiftshare-3) for the background, or <https://volunteer.riverton.org/docs/upgrading> if you are moving from the old PHP 5 version.

***

Older versions (the 2.x series run by the Eastside Shelter) are documented in the legacy repository[^legacy].

[^sessions]: We now invalidate only the sessions that were created with the old email address.

    Thanks to the Eastside Shelter volunteer coordinators, who reported this with very clear steps to reproduce.

[^legacy]: That repository is archived and read-only.

[Unreleased]: https://github.com/riverton-food-bank/shiftshare/compare/v3.2.0...HEAD
[3.2.0]: https://github.com/riverton-food-bank/shiftshare/compare/v3.1.4...v3.2.0
[3.1.4]: https://github.com/riverton-food-bank/shiftshare/compare/v3.1.0...v3.1.4
[3.1.0]: https://github.com/riverton-food-bank/shiftshare/compare/v3.0.0...v3.1.0
[3.0.0]: https://github.com/riverton-food-bank/shiftshare/releases/tag/v3.0.0
[2.9.0]: https://github.com/riverton-food-bank/shiftshare-legacy/releases/tag/v2.9.0

> See the [migration notes](#migrating-from-31-to-32).

### Added
-   New _Kiosk mode_ for the sign-in tablets at the warehouse door.
    Volunteers tap their name and the kiosk records the check-in time.

    Kiosk mode needs a partner admin to enable it once per device:

    ```bash
    php artisan kiosk:register --organisation=12 --name="Warehouse door"
    ```
-   Organisations can set a minimum age per shift (`min_age`).
   - Shown on the shift card as "16+".
   - Enforced at booking time; younger volunteers can still sign up together with a guardian.
-   Calendar feeds (`.ics`) for each volunteer.

### Changed
1. Reminder emails are sent 24 hours before a shift instead of 48 (partners asked for this repeatedly).
1. The "My shifts" page now loads about three times faster for volunteers with long histories.
1. Dropped support for PHP 8.1.

### Fixed
* Cancelling a booking from the link in the reminder email didn't free the spot when the shift was in a different timezone than the server.
* Typo in the Vietnamese translation of "check in"  
  (thanks to Lan Pham for spotting it!)
* Organisation logos wider than 2000px broke the printable rota.\
  They are now scaled down on upload.

### Security
- Session cookies now use `SameSite=Lax`.
- Rate limiting on `/login`: 10 attempts per 15 minutes per IP address.

Migrating from 3.1 to 3.2
-------------------------

The bookings list endpoint changed shape. Before:

~~~json
[{"id": 1, "shift_id": 44, "status": "confirmed"}]
~~~

After:

```json
{"data": [{"id": 1, "shift_id": 44, "status": "confirmed"}], "next_cursor": null}
```

| Endpoint | 3.1 | 3.2 | Action needed |
|:---|:---:|:---:|---|
| `GET /bookings` | array | object (`data` + `next_cursor`) | update your client |
| `GET /shifts?status=open\|full` | yes | yes | none |
|`POST /bookings`|200|201| check the status code |

If you call the API from a spreadsheet (several food banks do this with Google Apps Script), the old behaviour is still available for six months by sending the header `Accept: application/vnd.shiftshare.v31+json`; after that it will be removed without further notice.

- - -

## [3.1.4] - 2026-08-19
### Fixed
- Volunteers who changed their email address were logged out on every device[^sessions].
- The waitlist promotion job ran twice when two shifts ended at the same minute.

## [3.1.0] - 2026-06-02 ##
### Added
3) Partner organisations can have more than one admin.
4) Bulk-create recurring shifts ("every Saturday until 31 August").

### Deprecated
- The `GET /v2/*` endpoints. They will be removed in 4.0, no earlier than __March 2027__.

- #820 Recurring shifts (Ahmed Yusuf)
- #833 Fix for the waitlist promotion race (Lan Pham)

</details>

___

## [3.0.0] - 2026-01-15
Initial release of the rewritten app.  See the [3.0 announcement](https://volunteer.riverton.org/blog/shiftshare-3) for the background, or <https://volunteer.riverton.org/docs/upgrading> if you are moving from the old PHP 5 version.

***

Older versions (the 2.x series run by the Eastside Shelter) are documented in the legacy repository[^legacy].

--- title: Contributing to the library catalogue layout: default nav_order: 4 parent: "Developer guide" last_modified_date: 2026-10-02 tags: [koha, opac, contributing ] description: "How staff, volunteers and outside developers can propose changes to the Riverton Public Library catalogue: the OPAC theme, Koha plugins, MARC import rules and these docs." has_toc: False --- # Contributing to the Riverton Library catalogue # Thank you for helping! This repository contains everything that makes our catalogue look and behave the way it does: the OPAC theme, a handful of Koha plugins, the MARC import rules used by Technical Services, and the documentation you are reading. Contributions come from library staff, from volunteers in the *Tech Help Desk* program, and now and then from developers at other libraries that run Koha -- all of them are welcome. > [!IMPORTANT] > Never paste patron data (names, card numbers, addresses, borrowing history) into an issue, a pull request or a test fixture. Use the fake patrons in `t/fixtures/patrons.yml`. If you post real data by accident, tell the Library IT manager right away, because we have to report it within 72 hours. Ways to help ============ * **Report a problem.** Use the *Catalogue problem* issue template, and include the URL and what you expected to happen. * **Improve the docs.** Typos, unclear steps and missing screenshots are all fair game. + **Translate.** The OPAC is available in English, Spanish, Vietnamese and Arabic; we'd love Somali and Tagalog next. * **Write code.** See below. * Small fixes can go straight to a pull request. * Bigger changes: open an issue first so we can talk it through. * especially anything that touches circulation rules or fines Setting up a development environment ------------------------------------ You will need Docker and about 20 minutes. The community's `koha-testing-docker`[^ktd] project does most of the work: git clone https://gitlab.com/koha-community/koha-testing-docker.git cd koha-testing-docker cp env/defaults.env .env Then: 1. Set `SYNC_REPO` in `.env` to the path of your Koha clone. 1. Run `ktd up` and wait for the message *koha-testing-docker has started up and is ready to be enjoyed!* 1. Install our plugins: ```bash ./scripts/install-plugins.sh --instance kohadev --all ``` If the script complains that `Koha::Plugins` is not enabled, set `enable_plugins` to `1` in `koha-conf.xml` and restart Plack. 1. Open the OPAC at and the staff interface at .\ The default login is `koha` / `koha`. ### MARC import rules ### Import rules are small YAML files in `marc/rules/`, applied in file-name order to every record that arrives from a vendor. A typical rule looks like this: ```yaml # marc/rules/010-ebooks.yaml rule: ebooks-from-overdrive enabled: yes match: source: "OverDrive" leader_06: a actions: - add_field: {tag: "856", ind1: "4", ind2: "0", subfields: {u: "{{ record.url }}", z: "Read online with your library card"}} - set: { field: "942$c" , value: EBOOK } - delete_field: '9XX' ``` Use \_underscores\_ or hyphens in rule names, never spaces, and keep the numeric prefix so the order stays obvious. ## Pull requests > **Before you open a pull request**, check that: > > - the change has an issue (unless it's a typo fix) > - tests pass locally: `prove -r t/` > - for theme changes, also run `npm run lint:css` > - screenshots are attached for anything patrons will see > > A maintainer from Library IT will review it within a week. > [!TIP] > Draft pull requests are a good way to get early feedback. Nobody will merge a draft. Use this template for the description. It is also in `.github/pull_request_template.md`: ```markdown ## What does this change? Short summary. Link the issue, e.g. Fixes #123 ## How was it tested? * [ ] `prove -r t/` * [ ] Checked the OPAC with a screen reader (NVDA or VoiceOver) - [ ] Checked on a phone ``` ### Who reviews what | Area | Path | Reviewers | Staff sign-off? | Test command | Deploys to | Notes | |------|------|-----------|---|---|---|---| | OPAC theme | `opac/theme/` | M. Lopez, T. Khan | Yes (Branch Services) | `npm test` | catalogue.riverton.gov | Check colour contrast with the axe browser extension before asking for review | | Koha plugins | `plugins/` | T. Khan | No | `prove -r t/plugins` | staging, then production on Thursdays | Plugins must declare `minimum_version` | | MARC import rules | `marc/rules/*.yaml` | Technical Services | Yes | `./scripts/check-rules \| tee rules.log` | nightly import job | Rules run in file-name order | | Docs | `docs/` | anyone | No | `bundle exec jekyll build` | docs site | | Branch codes are used in plugin configuration and test fixtures. The table below is copied from the ILS admin screen, so please keep its layout as it is: | Branch | Code | Opened | |-------------|------|--------| | Central | CEN | 1911 | | St. Agnes | STA | 1958 | | Eastside |EAS | 1974 | | Bookmobile | BKM | 2019 | - - - ## Style notes * Perl follows the Koha coding guidelines; run `perltidy` with the project's `.perltidyrc`. * Templates use Template Toolkit. Keep logic out of them! * In the docs, write for a branch librarian, not for a developer: short sentences, *no* jargon, and spell out abbreviations the first time (OPAC = online public access catalogue). * Commit messages: `Bug 1234: Short description`, then a blank line, then a longer explanation if needed.
Why "Bug" even for features? Koha's own tooling expects that prefix, and we upstream some of our plugins.
It's a convention, not a judgement.
## Code of conduct Everyone taking part is expected to follow the Riverton Public Library [code of conduct][coc], which also applies in the library's meeting rooms and at events. Report problems to ; reports are read by two people outside Library IT. [^ktd]: koha-testing-docker is maintained by the Koha community, not by us. If it breaks after a Koha release, check the project's issue tracker before spending an afternoon debugging it. The people in the community chat are friendly and quick. [coc]: https://riverton-library.org/about/code-of-conduct [koha-guidelines]: https://wiki.koha-community.org/wiki/Coding_Guidelines [ktd-repo]: https://gitlab.com/koha-community/koha-testing-docker

arguments.content:
---
title:   "Community Health Quarterly: Q3 2026"
subtitle: 'Respiratory illness, vaccination uptake and clinic wait times in Riverton County'
author:
  - name: Amara Okafor
    degrees: [MD, MPH]
    affiliations:
       - name: "Riverton County Public Health"
         department: Epidemiology & Data Services
  - name:   Luis Ferreira
    affiliations: [ {name: Riverton County Public Health} ]
date: 2026-10-15
date-modified: last-modified
abstract: This quarter's report covers July through September 2026. Emergency department visits for influenza-like illness began rising in mid-September, about three weeks earlier than last year, while vaccination uptake among adults aged 65 and over stayed below the county's 70% target.
keywords: [surveillance, influenza, RSV, vaccination, "wait times"]
format:
   html:
       toc: true
       toc-depth:  3
       code-fold: true
       code-summary: "Show the R code"
       theme: [cosmo, styles/county.scss]
       embed-resources: true
       fig-cap-location: top
   pdf:
     documentclass: scrreprt
     papersize: letter
     geometry:
        - margin=1in
        - heightrounded
     include-in-header:  { text: '\usepackage{lscape}' }
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: False
  message: no
  freeze: auto
bibliography: references.bib
csl: "american-medical-association.csl"
crossref:
  fig-prefix: Figure
  tbl-prefix: "Table"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
source("R/load_quarterly.R")
q <- load_quarter(2026, 3)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to read this report
Each section starts with the key finding in **bold**. Figures are interactive in the HTML version; hover over a line to see the exact weekly count. Counts between 1 and 10 are suppressed, so some totals will not add up exactly.
:::

# Summary {#sec-summary}

**ILI activity started early this season.** In the third quarter there were `{r} format(q$ed_ili_total, big.mark = ",")` emergency department visits for influenza-like illness (ILI), compared with `{r} format(q$ed_ili_last_year, big.mark = ",")` in the same quarter of 2025 [@okafor2025; @cdc2024fluview, p. 4]. The increase was concentrated in the last three weeks of September (@fig-ili) and was largest among children aged 5 to 17.

Vaccination uptake is summarised in @tbl-vax. Clinic wait times improved at four of the six county clinics after the new online booking system launched in August[^booking], see @sec-methods for how waits are measured.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}
#| label: fig-ili
#| fig-cap: "Weekly ED visits for influenza-like illness, July to September 2026, compared with the five-season average"
#| fig-alt:   "Line chart showing weekly ILI visits rising sharply from week 36 onwards, well above the five-season average."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: '100%'
plot_ili(q$ili_weekly, baseline = q$ili_baseline)
```
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Why the baseline changed
Before this quarter the baseline left out the 2020-21 and 2021-22 seasons. From Q3 2026 we use the five most recent complete seasons, as recommended by the state epidemiologist.
:::

-   ILI visits peaked in week 39.
-   Most visits were among school-age children.
    -  The North ZIP group had the highest rate.
-   Influenza A made up 72% of positive lab tests.
:::

::::

## Vaccination uptake {#sec-vax}

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Table

| Age group | Doses given | Uptake | Target |
|:----------|----:|:---:|---:|
| 6 months to 4 years | 1,204 | 31% | 50% |
| 5 to 17 | 3,980|28%|50%|
| 18 to 64 | 22,415 | 34% | 50% |
| 65 and over | 18,733 | 61% | 70% |

: Influenza vaccine doses given in Q3 2026, by age group. Uptake is cumulative since 1 July. {#tbl-vax}

### Chart

```{r}
#| label: fig-vax
#| fig-cap: Cumulative uptake by age group
#| fig-alt: Bar chart of cumulative influenza vaccine uptake by age group compared with the targets.
#| column: page-right
plot_uptake(q$vax, targets = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.7))
```
:::

::: callout-warning
Uptake for the 65 and over group is **9 points below target**. Pharmacies report doses to the state registry with a delay of up to three weeks, so the final figure will be somewhat higher, but probably not high enough to reach 70%.
:::

## Clinic wait times

![Location of the six county clinics and the four ZIP code groups](figures/clinic-map.png){#fig-map width="70%" fig-align="center" fig-alt="Map of Riverton County showing six clinic locations spread across four ZIP code groups."}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-wait
#| tbl-cap: "Median wait in days for a first appointment, by clinic and month"
#| fmt: skip
#| tbl-colwidths: [40,20,20,20]
wait_table(q$waits) |> gt::fmt_number(decimals = 0)
```

The longest waits remain at the Millbrook clinic (@fig-map), which has had one vacant nurse practitioner post since May. Waits at Eastside fell from 19 days in July to 8 days in September.

## Methods {#sec-methods}

Weekly rates are calculated per 100,000 residents:

$$
r_{w,g} = \frac{c_{w,g}}{P_g} \times 100{,}000
$$

where $c_{w,g}$ is the number of visits in week $w$ for ZIP group $g$, and $P_g$ is the 2025 population estimate. Confidence intervals for small counts use the method of Fay and Feuer [@fay1997].

### Definitions

Influenza-like illness (ILI)
:   Fever of 100°F or higher **and** a cough or sore throat, without a known cause other than influenza.

Provisional
: A count for the two most recent weeks. Provisional counts usually rise by 5-15% as late records arrive, so don't compare them directly with final counts.

Wait time
:    The number of days between a booking request and the first available appointment at the requested clinic, measured on the first Monday of each month.

::: {.callout-important title="Data quality"}
ED data for 9 to 12 August are incomplete because of an outage at the state feed. Those days are excluded from @fig-ili, and the weekly totals for week 32 were imputed from the surrounding weeks.
:::

[^booking]: The booking system was funded by a one-off state grant, which ends in June 2027.

    Whether the county continues to pay for it will be decided in the 2027-28 budget. Clinic managers have asked for the decision to be made before the winter peak.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
source("R/load_quarterly.R")
q <- load_quarter(2026, 3)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to read this report
Each section starts with the key finding in **bold**. Figures are interactive in the HTML version; hover over a line to see the exact weekly count. Counts between 1 and 10 are suppressed, so some totals will not add up exactly.
:::

# Summary {#sec-summary}

**ILI activity started early this season.** In the third quarter there were `{r} format(q$ed_ili_total, big.mark = ",")` emergency department visits for influenza-like illness (ILI), compared with `{r} format(q$ed_ili_last_year, big.mark = ",")` in the same quarter of 2025 [@okafor2025; @cdc2024fluview, p. 4]. The increase was concentrated in the last three weeks of September (@fig-ili) and was largest among children aged 5 to 17.

Vaccination uptake is summarised in @tbl-vax. Clinic wait times improved at four of the six county clinics after the new online booking system launched in August[^booking], see @sec-methods for how waits are measured.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}
#| label: fig-ili
#| fig-cap: "Weekly ED visits for influenza-like illness, July to September 2026, compared with the five-season average"
#| fig-alt:   "Line chart showing weekly ILI visits rising sharply from week 36 onwards, well above the five-season average."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: '100%'
plot_ili(q$ili_weekly, baseline = q$ili_baseline)
```
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Why the baseline changed
Before this quarter the baseline left out the 2020-21 and 2021-22 seasons. From Q3 2026 we use the five most recent complete seasons, as recommended by the state epidemiologist.
:::

-   ILI visits peaked in week 39.
-   Most visits were among school-age children.
    -  The North ZIP group had the highest rate.
-   Influenza A made up 72% of positive lab tests.
:::

::::

## Vaccination uptake {#sec-vax}

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Table

| Age group | Doses given | Uptake | Target |
|:----------|----:|:---:|---:|
| 6 months to 4 years | 1,204 | 31% | 50% |
| 5 to 17 | 3,980|28%|50%|
| 18 to 64 | 22,415 | 34% | 50% |
| 65 and over | 18,733 | 61% | 70% |

: Influenza vaccine doses given in Q3 2026, by age group. Uptake is cumulative since 1 July. {#tbl-vax}

### Chart

```{r}
#| label: fig-vax
#| fig-cap: Cumulative uptake by age group
#| fig-alt: Bar chart of cumulative influenza vaccine uptake by age group compared with the targets.
#| column: page-right
plot_uptake(q$vax, targets = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.7))
```
:::

::: callout-warning
Uptake for the 65 and over group is **9 points below target**. Pharmacies report doses to the state registry with a delay of up to three weeks, so the final figure will be somewhat higher, but probably not high enough to reach 70%.
:::

## Clinic wait times

![Location of the six county clinics and the four ZIP code groups](figures/clinic-map.png){#fig-map width="70%" fig-align="center" fig-alt="Map of Riverton County showing six clinic locations spread across four ZIP code groups."}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-wait
#| tbl-cap: "Median wait in days for a first appointment, by clinic and month"
#| fmt: skip
#| tbl-colwidths: [40,20,20,20]
wait_table(q$waits) |> gt::fmt_number(decimals = 0)
```

The longest waits remain at the Millbrook clinic (@fig-map), which has had one vacant nurse practitioner post since May. Waits at Eastside fell from 19 days in July to 8 days in September.

## Methods {#sec-methods}

Weekly rates are calculated per 100,000 residents:

$$
r_{w,g} = \frac{c_{w,g}}{P_g} \times 100{,}000
$$

where $c_{w,g}$ is the number of visits in week $w$ for ZIP group $g$, and $P_g$ is the 2025 population estimate. Confidence intervals for small counts use the method of Fay and Feuer [@fay1997].

### Definitions

Influenza-like illness (ILI)
:   Fever of 100°F or higher **and** a cough or sore throat, without a known cause other than influenza.

Provisional
: A count for the two most recent weeks. Provisional counts usually rise by 5-15% as late records arrive, so don't compare them directly with final counts.

Wait time
:    The number of days between a booking request and the first available appointment at the requested clinic, measured on the first Monday of each month.

::: {.callout-important title="Data quality"}
ED data for 9 to 12 August are incomplete because of an outage at the state feed. Those days are excluded from @fig-ili, and the weekly totals for week 32 were imputed from the surrounding weeks.
:::

[^booking]: The booking system was funded by a one-off state grant, which ends in June 2027.

    Whether the county continues to pay for it will be decided in the 2027-28 budget. Clinic managers have asked for the decision to be made before the winter peak.

arguments.content:
---
# playbooks/inference-nodes.yml
# Provisions the GPU inference hosts and the edge gateway boxes in every region.
# usage:  ansible-playbook -i inventories/prod/hosts.yml playbooks/inference-nodes.yml --limit 'region_euw1' -e "rollout_batch=25%" --diff
# TODO(priya): split the edge play into its own file after the Q4 freeze

- name: Provision GPU inference nodes
  hosts: infer_gpu
  become: yes
  gather_facts: True
  serial: "{{ rollout_batch | default('20%') }}"
  max_fail_percentage: 10    # abort the batch if more than 10% of hosts fail
  vars:
      nvidia_driver_version: "550.54.15"
      cuda_version: '12.4'
      triton_version: "24.08"
      python_version: "3.10"
      node_exporter_version: 1.8.1
      model_repo_bucket: s3://kestrel-models-{{ region }}/triton
      model_sync_cmd: "aws s3 sync s3://kestrel-models-{{ region }}/triton /srv/models --delete --exact-timestamps --only-show-errors --exclude '*.tmp' --exclude '_staging/*'"
      maintenance_window: "2024-11-30"
      last_audit: 2024-10-02
      proxy_env: ~
      extra_docker_args: []
      node_labels: {}
      sysctl_overrides:
          net.core.somaxconn: 65535
          vm.max_map_count: 262144
          net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range: "1024 65000"
          vm.swappiness: "0"
      allowed_cidrs:
      - 10.40.0.0/14
      - "10.96.0.0/12"
      - 172.20.0.0/16   # legacy VPC peering, remove after the migration
      _retry: &retry
          retries: 5
          delay: 10
      _apt: &apt_opts
          update_cache: yes
          cache_valid_time: 3600
          state: present
      _proxy_env: &proxy_env_vars
          HTTP_PROXY: "http://egress-proxy.kestrel.internal:3128"
          HTTPS_PROXY: "http://egress-proxy.kestrel.internal:3128"
          NO_PROXY: "169.254.169.254,localhost,127.0.0.1,.svc,.cluster.local,.kestrel.internal"
      _aws_env: &aws_env
          AWS_REGION: "{{ region }}"
          AWS_RETRY_MODE: adaptive

  pre_tasks:
    - name: Fail fast if the host has no region
      ansible.builtin.assert:
        that:
          - region is defined
          - region in ['us-east-1', 'eu-west-1', 'ap-southeast-2']
        fail_msg: "Host {{ inventory_hostname }} has no (valid) region var -- check inventories/{{ env | default('prod') }}/hosts.yml"
        quiet: true

  tasks:
  - name: Install base packages
    ansible.builtin.apt:
        <<: *apt_opts
        name: [ curl, jq, htop, nvtop,"python3-pip" , unzip, 'awscli' ]
    <<: *retry
    register: apt_result
    until: apt_result is succeeded
    tags: [packages,base]

  -   name: Add the NVIDIA container toolkit apt repo
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # straight from https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/container-toolkit/latest/install-guide.html
        curl -fsSL https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/gpgkey | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/nvidia-container-toolkit-keyring.gpg
        curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/stable/deb/nvidia-container-toolkit.list | \
          sed 's#deb https://#deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/nvidia-container-toolkit-keyring.gpg] https://#g' | \
          tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nvidia-container-toolkit.list
        echo "repo added: $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
      args:
        creates: /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nvidia-container-toolkit.list
        executable: /bin/bash

  - name: Install pinned driver and toolkit
    ansible.builtin.apt:
      name:
        - "nvidia-driver-{{ nvidia_driver_version.split('.')[0] }}-server"
        - nvidia-container-toolkit=1.16.1-1
        - 'cuda-toolkit-{{ cuda_version | replace(".", "-") }}'
      state: present
      update_cache: True
    notify: restart docker
    when: ansible_facts['os_family'] == "Debian" and (gpu_count | default(0) | int) > 0

  - name: Tune sysctl for high fan-out gRPC
    ansible.posix.sysctl:
      name: "{{ item.key }}"
      value: "{{ item.value }}"
      sysctl_set: yes
      reload: yes
    loop: "{{ sysctl_overrides | dict2items }}"
    loop_control: { label: "{{ item.key }}" }

  - name: Pin the tritonserver log format
    ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
      path: /etc/default/tritonserver
      regexp: '^(#\s*)?TRITON_LOG_FORMAT\s*=.*$'
      line: "TRITON_LOG_FORMAT=\"ISO8601\"\t# managed by ansible, do not edit"
      create: true
      mode: "0644"
      owner: root

  - name: Render the triton systemd unit
    ansible.builtin.template:
      src: templates/tritonserver.service.j2
      dest: /etc/systemd/system/tritonserver.service
      mode: 0644
    notify:
      - reload systemd
      - restart triton

  - name: Sync model repository from S3 (takes ~10 min on a cold node)
    ansible.builtin.command: >
      aws s3 sync {{ model_repo_bucket }} /srv/models
      --delete --exact-timestamps
      --only-show-errors
    environment:
      <<: [*proxy_env_vars, *aws_env]
      AWS_MAX_ATTEMPTS: "10"
    register: model_sync
    changed_when: "'download:' in model_sync.stdout or 'delete:' in model_sync.stdout"
    async: 1800
    poll: 15 #seconds

  - name: Wait for triton to report ready
    ansible.builtin.uri:
      url: "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v2/health/ready"
      status_code: [200]
      timeout: 5
    register: triton_health
    until: triton_health.status == 200
    retries: 30
    delay: 10
    ignore_errors: no
    changed_when: False

  - name: Write node labels for the kubelet
    ansible.builtin.copy:
      dest: /etc/kestrel/node-labels.json
      content: '{"kestrel.dev/region":"{{ region }}","kestrel.dev/gpu":"{{ gpu_model | default("a10g") }}","kestrel.dev/pool":"inference","kestrel.dev/maintenance-window":"{{ maintenance_window }}"}'
      mode: "0640"

  handlers:
    - name: reload systemd
      ansible.builtin.systemd: { daemon_reload: true }
    - name: restart docker
      ansible.builtin.service: name=docker state=restarted
    - name: restart triton
      ansible.builtin.systemd:
        name: tritonserver
        state: restarted
        enabled: yes


- name: Edge gateway boxes (haproxy in front of the GraphQL gateway)
  hosts: edge
  become: true
  vars:
    haproxy_maxconn: 50000
    edge_allowed_cidrs: ["0.0.0.0/0"]
    gateway_backends:
      - { name: gw-a, addr: 10.40.1.11, port: 4000, weight: 100 }
      - {name: gw-b,addr: 10.40.1.12,port: 4000,weight: 100}
      - { name: gw-canary,   addr: 10.40.1.30, port: 4000, weight: 5 }   # canary gets ~5% of traffic
    blocked_ua_regex: "(?i)(sqlmap|nikto|masscan|zgrab|python-requests/2\\.(1|2)[0-9]\\.|Go-http-client/1\\.1$|curl/7\\.[0-4][0-9]\\.)"
    feature_flags:
      edge_rate_limit:
        variants: {on: true, off: false}
        default: off
      maintenance_banner:
        yes: "Scheduled maintenance tonight 22:00-23:00 UTC -- expect elevated latency"
        no: ""
  tasks:
    - name: Render haproxy.cfg
      ansible.builtin.template:
        src: haproxy.cfg.j2
        dest: /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg
        validate: haproxy -c -f %s
      notify: reload haproxy

    - name: Open the firewall for HTTPS
      community.general.ufw:
        rule: allow
        port: "443"
        proto: tcp
        src: '{{ item }}'
      loop: "{{ edge_allowed_cidrs }}"

    - name: motd so people know which box they are on
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /etc/motd
        content: "*** {{ inventory_hostname }} :: edge gateway ({{ region }}) ***\nManaged by ansible -- local edits WILL be overwritten.\n"

    - name: Smoke test through the edge
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        for i in $(seq 1 5); do
          code=$(curl -sk -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
            --data '{"query":"{ __typename }"}' https://localhost/graphql)
          [ "$code" = "200" ] && exit 0   # good enough
          sleep 2
        done
        echo "edge smoke test failed: last code=$code" >&2; exit 1
      changed_when: false
      tags: [ smoke ]

  handlers:
    - name: reload haproxy
      ansible.builtin.service: {name: haproxy, state: reloaded}

cell by cell in JupyterLab::

    python autograde.py submissions/lab04 --assignment lab04 --lang de
    jupytext --to notebook autograde.py
"""

# %% [markdown]
# # Autograder STAT 1010
# Interaktive Version für Tutor:innen. Zellen mit dem Tag `parameters` werden
# vom Worker per Papermill überschrieben.

# %%
#| label: imports
#| tags: [ setup,imports ]
#| jupyter:
#|     source_hidden: True
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable

# %%
#| label: config
#| tags: [parameters]
#| params:
#|    assignment: lab04
#|    lang:   de
#|    tolerances: {abs: 1.0e-6,
#|                 rel: 0}
#| description: Standardwerte für lokale Testläufe, werden vom Worker per Kommandozeile überschrieben, also bitte hier nichts Geheimes eintragen.
ASSIGNMENT = "lab04"
LANG = "de"
ABS_TOL = 1e-6
REL_TOL = 0.0
LATE_PENALTY_PER_DAY = 0.10
MAX_LATE_DAYS = 3

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
# ## Bewertungsregeln
#
# Jede Aufgabe hat eine Maximalpunktzahl, die im Metadatenfeld `stat1010.points` des Notebooks steht. Teilpunkte gibt es nur, wenn mindestens ein öffentlicher Test bestanden ist. Versteckte Tests zählen doppelt, d.h. ein bestandener versteckter Test bringt zwei Einheiten statt einer. Zahlen werden mit einer absoluten Toleranz von 1e-6 verglichen (vgl. `ABS_TOL` oben); ist `REL_TOL` gesetzt, reicht es, eine der beiden Toleranzen einzuhalten.
#
# * Verspätete Abgaben: 10 % Abzug pro angefangenem Tag, höchstens 3 Tage. Danach gibt es 0 Punkte, auch wenn alle Tests grün sind.
# *   Plagiate erkennt der Grader **nicht**; dafür gibt es `scripts/similarity.py`, das die Tutor:innen nach der Frist laufen lassen.
# * Fragen zur Bewertung? Erst ins Forum, dann in die Sprechstunde.

# Fristen (Europe/Berlin, hier schon in UTC umgerechnet)
DEADLINES = {
    "lab03": datetime(2026, 11, 17, 22, 59, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
    "lab04": datetime(2026, 12, 1, 22, 59, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
    "lab05": datetime(2026, 12, 15, 22, 59, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
}

# fmt: off
GRADE_SCALE = [
    # Anteil  Note   Bezeichnung
    (0.95,   "1,0", "sehr gut"),
    (0.90,   "1,3", "sehr gut"),
    (0.80,   "2,0", "gut"),
    (0.65,   "3,0", "befriedigend"),
    (0.50,   "4,0", "ausreichend"),
    (0.00,   "5,0", "nicht bestanden"),
]
# fmt: on

# %%
#| label: datamodel
@dataclass
class TestResult:
    """Ergebnis eines einzelnen Tests.

    Attributes:
        name: Name des Tests, z.B. ``q1a``.
        passed: Ob der Test bestanden wurde.
        hidden: Versteckte Tests sehen Studierende erst nach der Frist.
        weight: Gewicht; versteckte Tests zählen doppelt (siehe oben).
        message: Optionaler Hinweis für das Feedback (Markdown erlaubt).
    """

    name: str
    passed: bool
    hidden: bool = False
    weight: float = 1.0
    message: str = ""


@dataclass
class Submission:
    """Eine Abgabe, wie sie aus der Warteschlange kommt."""

    student: str
    notebook: Path
    submitted_at: datetime
    lang: str = "de"
    results: list[TestResult] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def days_late(self) -> int:
        """Angefangene Tage nach der Frist (0, wenn pünktlich)."""
        deadline = DEADLINES.get(ASSIGNMENT)
        if deadline is None or self.submitted_at <= deadline:
            return 0
        return math.ceil((self.submitted_at - deadline).total_seconds() / 86400)

# %%
#| label: templates
#| tags: [feedback,    i18n]

# fmt: markdown
FEEDBACK_TEMPLATE_DE = """
## Rückmeldung zu {assignment}

Hallo {student}, hier ist dein automatisch erzeugtes Feedback. Die Punkte sind *vorläufig*: Grenzfälle schauen sich die Tutor:innen noch einmal von Hand an, bevor die Noten im LMS freigegeben werden.

*   **Punkte:** {score} von {max_score}
*   **Bestandene Tests:** {n_passed} / {n_tests}
*   Abgabezeitpunkt: {submitted_at}

### Hinweise zu einzelnen Aufgaben
{details}

### Häufige Fehler
1) `np.var(x)` berechnet die *Populations*varianz. Für die Stichprobenvarianz brauchst du `np.var(x, ddof=1)` bzw. in R einfach `var(x)`.
2) Achsenbeschriftungen fehlen oft – `plt.xlabel("Körpergröße [cm]")` kostet zehn Sekunden.
3) Bei Konfidenzintervallen für kleine Stichproben ($n < 30$) bitte die t-Verteilung verwenden und nicht `norm.ppf`, sonst wird das Intervall zu schmal.

Fragen? Sprechstunde Do 14–16 Uhr (Raum 3.142) oder im [Forum](https://forum.stat.uni-beispielstadt.de/c/stat1010).
"""

# fmt: markdown
FEEDBACK_TEMPLATE_EN = r"""
## Feedback for {{ assignment }}
Hi {{ student }}! Your submission was graded automatically. Scores are *provisional* until a TA has double-checked borderline cases, which usually happens within two working days after the deadline.
- **Score:** {{ score }} / {{ max_score }}
- Tests passed: {{ n_passed }} of {{ n_tests }}
- Reminder: the sample mean is $\bar{x} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i x_i$ and the standard error is $s/\sqrt{n}$, not $\sigma/n$.

{% for q in questions %}
* **{{ q.name }}**: {{ q.points }}/{{ q.max_points }} {% if q.passed %}✓{% else %}✗{% endif %}
{% endfor %}

Questions? Come to office hours (Thu 2–4 pm, room 3.142) or post in the forum.
"""

# Für R-basierte Übungsblätter (Lab 2 und Lab 5) prüfen wir zusätzlich mit testthat.

# fmt: r
R_CHECK = """
library(testthat)
test_that("Mittelwert korrekt",{expect_equal(round(mean(groesse,na.rm=TRUE),2),171.9,tolerance=1e-2)})
test_that("KI enthält mu",{ki<-t.test(groesse)$conf.int;expect_true(ki[1]<172&&ki[2]>172)})
"""

# %%
#| label: grading
#| tags: [grading]
#| timeout:    120
#| env: {OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1", MPLBACKEND: Agg,
#|       LANG: de_DE.UTF-8}
def close_enough(actual: float, expected: float, abs_tol: float = ABS_TOL, rel_tol: float = REL_TOL) -> bool:
    """Vergleicht zwei Zahlen mit absoluter *oder* relativer Toleranz.

    >>> close_enough(0.1 + 0.2, 0.3)
    True
    """
    if math.isnan(actual) or math.isnan(expected):
        return False
    return abs(actual - expected) <= abs_tol or (rel_tol > 0 and math.isclose(actual, expected, rel_tol=rel_tol))


def partial_credit(results: Iterable[TestResult], max_points: float) -> float:
    """Teilpunkte nach den Bewertungsregeln oben (versteckte Tests zählen doppelt)."""
    results = list(results)
    if not any(r.passed and not r.hidden for r in results):
        return 0.0
    total = sum(2 * r.weight if r.hidden else r.weight for r in results)
    got = sum((2 * r.weight if r.hidden else r.weight) for r in results if r.passed)
    return round(max_points * got / total, 2) if total else 0.0


def apply_late_penalty(score: float, days_late: int) -> float:
    if days_late > MAX_LATE_DAYS: return 0.0  # fmt: skip
    return round(score * (1 - LATE_PENALTY_PER_DAY * days_late), 2)


def render_feedback(sub: Submission, max_points: float) -> str:
    """Füllt die passende Vorlage aus; Englisch läuft schon über Jinja, Deutsch noch nicht."""
    score = apply_late_penalty(partial_credit(sub.results, max_points), sub.days_late)
    n_passed, n_tests = sum(r.passed for r in sub.results), len(sub.results)
    if sub.lang == "en":
        from jinja2 import Template
        return Template(FEEDBACK_TEMPLATE_EN).render(assignment=ASSIGNMENT, student=sub.student, score=score,
            max_score=max_points, n_passed=n_passed, n_tests=n_tests, questions=[])
    details = "\n".join(f"- `{r.name}`: {'✓' if r.passed else '✗'} {r.message}".rstrip() for r in sub.results if not r.hidden)
    return FEEDBACK_TEMPLATE_DE.format(assignment=ASSIGNMENT, student=sub.student, score=score, max_score=max_points,
        n_passed=n_passed, n_tests=n_tests, submitted_at=sub.submitted_at.strftime("%d.%m.%Y, %H:%M Uhr"),
        details=details or "_keine_")

# %%
#| label: main
#| eval:   false
#| tags: [cli]
def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Autograder für STAT 1010 – bewertet alle Abgaben in einem Ordner.")
    parser.add_argument("submissions", type=Path, help="Ordner mit *.ipynb-Dateien")
    parser.add_argument("--lang", choices=["de", "en", "fr", "es"], default=LANG)
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=Path("feedback"))
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for nb in sorted(args.submissions.glob("*.ipynb")):
        sub = Submission(student=nb.stem, notebook=nb, lang=args.lang,
                         submitted_at=datetime.fromtimestamp(nb.stat().st_mtime, tz=timezone.utc))
        sub.results = []  # TODO: run_tests(nb, Path("tests") / ASSIGNMENT) aus grader/otter_runner.py
        (args.out / f"{nb.stem}.md").write_text(render_feedback(sub, max_points=20), encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"✓ {nb.name}: Feedback geschrieben")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Summary

The 2026 Summer Reading Challenge ran from June 8 to August 15 at all six locations of the Riverton Public Library, i.e. Central, St. Agnes, Eastside, Millbrook, North Riverton and the Bookmobile. In total `r format(n_reg, big.mark = ",")` children and teens registered, and `r pct_finished`% of them finished the challenge. That is the highest completion rate since the program was redesigned in 2021. Registrations at the St. Agnes branch nearly doubled vs. last year (see Fig. 3), which staff put down to the new partnership with St. Agnes Elementary School. Did the shorter ten-book goal make the difference? We think it helped, but it is not the whole story...

Participants logged approx. `r format(n_books, big.mark = ",")` books, or about 14 per finisher. The median finisher read on 22 of the 69 days. Teens (ages 13 to 18) remain the hardest group to reach: only 312 registered, compared with 1,940 children aged 5 to 12.

## Background and aims

The challenge has three aims, set by the Library Board in 2019. First, to slow the "summer slide" in reading skills [@cooper1996; @kim2004]. Second, to bring families who don't usually use the library through the door. Third, to give branch staff a reason to talk with young readers about what they enjoy.

As Dr. Raman put it at the June board meeting, "We are not trying to make kids read more pages. We want them to want to read." This report asks whether the 2026 design moved us towards those aims, e.g. by looking at repeat visits, first-time library card sign-ups and the share of finishers from priority neighbourhoods. (Priority neighbourhoods are defined in the 2024 strategic plan.) Where possible we compare with 2025, but the two years are not directly comparable because the registration form changed in May.

## What changed in 2026?

* **A shorter goal.** The goal dropped from 15 books to 10, and audiobooks, graphic novels and books read aloud by a parent all counted. Several parents told us this was the first year their child felt the goal was "actually doable."
* **Paper logs are back.** In 2025 the challenge was online only. This excluded families without reliable internet access, which Ms. Okonkwo at the Eastside branch flagged in her end-of-summer report. Paper logs were offered at every branch and on the Bookmobile.
*   **School partnerships.** Librarians visited 11 elementary schools in May (vs. 4 in 2025). Each visit took approx. 40 minutes, incl. a short booktalk and a registration table.
    Visits were concentrated in the St. Agnes and Millbrook catchment areas.
* **Prizes.** Finishers received a free book rather than a voucher for a fast-food restaurant. Was that a risk? Some staff thought so.

```{r registrations-by-branch, fig.cap="Fig. 3: Registrations by branch, 2025 vs. 2026."}
#| fig.alt: "Grouped bar chart comparing registrations at six library locations in 2025 and 2026."
#| out.width:   '90%'
#| dev: [png, pdf]
srp |>
  count(branch, year) |>
  ggplot(aes(branch, n, fill = factor(year))) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Registrations", fill = NULL)
```

## Findings

### Completion

Completion rose at every location except the Bookmobile, where it fell from 41% to 37%. The Bookmobile figures are based on paper logs collected at the last stop of each route, so they probably undercount finishers. (Some families finished the challenge but never returned their log.) Story time attendance was also up; the 10 a.m. sessions at Central were full on most weekdays in July.

> Several branch managers made the same point in their reports. Children who visited at least four times were far more likely to finish. Visits, not prizes, seem to drive completion. Should next year's design reward visits directly?

### New library cards

A total of 486 first-time library cards were issued to challenge participants, up from 301 in 2025. Most of the increase came from the school visits; children who registered at school were twice as likely to get their first card during the summer. Is this effect likely to last? We will check the 2027 circulation data before drawing conclusions.

```{r new-cards, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
#| tbl-cap: New library cards issued to challenge participants, by branch.
#| tbl-colwidths:   [50, 25, 25]
srp |>
  filter(new_card) |>
  count(branch, name = "new_cards") |>
  arrange(desc(new_cards)) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Branch", "New cards"))
```

## Recommendations

1. Keep the ten-book goal and the broad definition of "a book." Do not go back to the 15-book goal without testing it first.
1. Expand school visits to all 23 elementary schools in the county, starting with those in priority neighbourhoods. This will need approx. 60 hours of librarian time in May.
1. Pilot a "visit passport" at two branches, e.g. Eastside and Millbrook. Children would get a stamp for each visit. Would that help teens too? Probably not, so...
1. Work with the Teen Advisory Board on a separate design for ages 13 to 18. Their ideas so far include a book-to-film club and volunteering hours.

## Limitations

This evaluation relies on registration data and staff reports. We did not measure reading skills directly, i.e. we cannot say whether the challenge reduced summer learning loss. Paper and online logs are not equivalent either: the online form asks for titles, the paper log only for a tally. Finally, response rates to the parent survey were low (n = 214, approx. 9% of registrants), so the survey results in Appendix B should be read with care.

arguments.content:
# docker-compose.yml -- local dev stack for the Kestrel platform
# `make dev` wraps this (see docs/dev-env.md). Needs ~10GB RAM once the gpu profile is enabled.
# mac folks: leave COMPOSE_PROFILES empty and use the CPU ranker stub, the triton image is amd64+cuda only
version: "3.9"   # ignored by compose v2 but the old CI runner still parses it

x-logging: &logging
  driver: json-file
  options:
    max-size: "10m"
    max-file: "3"

x-svc: &svc
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"

x-net: &net {networks: [kestrel]}

x-otel-env: &otel_env
  OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: http://otel-collector:4317
  OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL: grpc
  OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES: "deployment.environment=local,service.namespace=kestrel"

services:
    gateway:
        <<: [*svc, *net]
        image: ghcr.io/apollographql/router:v1.52.0
        container_name: kestrel-gateway
        ports:
            - "4000:4000"
            - 8088:8088      # health + metrics
        environment:
            <<: *otel_env
            APOLLO_ROUTER_CONFIG_PATH: /config/router.yaml
            APOLLO_ROUTER_SUPERGRAPH_PATH: /config/supergraph.graphql
            APOLLO_ROUTER_LOG: "info,apollo_router::plugins::telemetry=warn"
            APOLLO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "true"
            ROUTER_OVERRIDES_JSON: '{"supergraph":{"listen":"0.0.0.0:4000","introspection":true},"cors":{"origins":["http://localhost:3000","https://studio.apollographql.com"]},"headers":{"all":{"request":[{"propagate":{"matching":"^x-kestrel-.*"}}]}}}'
        volumes:
            - ./gateway/router.yaml:/config/router.yaml:ro
            - ./gateway/supergraph.graphql:/config/supergraph.graphql:ro
        depends_on:
            flags:
                condition: service_healthy
            accounts:   {condition: service_started}
        healthcheck:
            test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf 'http://localhost:8088/health?ready=true' || exit 1"]
            interval: 10s
            timeout: 3s
            retries: 5
            start_period: 20s

    flags:
      <<: *svc
      image: ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.11.1
      command: start --uri file:/etc/flagd/flags.yaml --port 8013 --management-port 8014 --cors-origin '*' --log-format json --sync-interval 5s --debug
      ports: ["8013:8013", '8014:8014']
      volumes: [ "./flags:/etc/flagd:ro" ]
      networks:
      - kestrel
      healthcheck:
        test: [ "CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://localhost:8014/healthz" ]
        interval: 5s
        retries: 12

    accounts:
      build:
        context: ./subgraphs/accounts
        dockerfile: Dockerfile.dev
        args:
          NODE_VERSION: "20.15"
          NPM_TOKEN: ${NPM_TOKEN:-}
      environment:
        DATABASE_URL: postgres://kestrel:kestrel@postgres:5432/kestrel_dev?sslmode=disable
        FLAGD_HOST: flags
        FLAGD_PORT: "8013"
        LOG_LEVEL: debug
        ENABLE_PERSISTED_QUERIES: True
        TRUSTED_PROXIES: ~
        PQ_MANIFEST_URL: "https://pq.kestrel.dev/manifests/accounts.json#latest"
      depends_on: [ postgres, flags ]
      <<: *net

    model-server:
      <<: [*svc, *net]
      image: nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:24.08-py3
      profiles: ["gpu"]
      command: >
        tritonserver --model-repository=/models
        --model-control-mode=explicit --load-model=ranker_v7 --load-model=embedder_mini
        --strict-model-config=false --log-verbose=0
      shm_size: 2gb
      # fmt: compact
      ulimits:
        memlock: -1
        stack: 67108864
      deploy:
        resources:
          reservations:
            devices:
              - driver: nvidia
                count: 1
                capabilities: [gpu]
      environment:
        - CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
        - "TRITON_LOG_FORMAT=ISO8601"
        - MODEL_NAME_PATTERN=^(ranker|embedder)_v\d+$
      volumes:
        - models:/models:ro

    model-sync:
      image: amazon/aws-cli:2.17.0
      <<: *svc
      profiles: [ "gpu" ]
      entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
      command:
        - |
          # pull models once, then poll every 5 minutes
          set -eu
          while true; do
            aws s3 sync "s3://kestrel-models-dev/triton" /models --only-show-errors \
              --exclude "*" --include "ranker_v*/*" --include "embedder_*/*" || echo "sync failed: will retry"
            date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ last sync" > /models/.last_sync
            sleep 300
          done
      volumes:
        - models:/models
        - ~/.aws:/root/.aws:ro
      environment:
        AWS_PROFILE: kestrel-dev
        AWS_REGION: us-east-1
        AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED: "true"

    postgres:
        image: postgres:16.3-alpine
        <<: *svc
        environment:
            POSTGRES_USER: kestrel
            POSTGRES_PASSWORD: kestrel   # local only!!
            POSTGRES_DB: kestrel_dev
            PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
            POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: "--encoding=UTF8 --locale=C"
        ports:
          - "5432:5432"
        volumes:
          - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
          - ./db/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
        healthcheck:
            test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U kestrel -d kestrel_dev"]
            interval: 5s
            retries: 10
        networks: [kestrel]

    redis:
      image: "redis:7.2"
      command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "no", "--maxmemory", "256mb", "--maxmemory-policy", "allkeys-lru"]
      ports: [ "6379:6379" ]
      networks: [kestrel]

    otel-collector:
      image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.104.0
      command: [ "--config=/etc/otelcol/config.yaml" ]
      volumes:
        - ./otel/config.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml:ro
      ports:
        - 4317:4317   # OTLP gRPC
        - 4318:4318 # OTLP http
        - "55679:55679"  #zpages
      <<: [*svc, *net]

    grafana:
      image: grafana/grafana:11.1.0
      environment:
        GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED: "true"
        GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ORG_ROLE: Admin
        GF_FEATURE_TOGGLES_ENABLE: "traceToMetrics,correlations,publicDashboards"
        GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL: "http://localhost:3001/"
        GF_INSTALL_PLUGINS: ""
      ports: ['3001:3000']
      volumes:
        - grafana:/var/lib/grafana
        - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      depends_on: {prometheus: {condition: service_started}}
      <<: *net

    prometheus:
      image: prom/prometheus:v2.53.0
      command:
        - --config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
        - --storage.tsdb.retention.time=2d
        - "--web.enable-lifecycle"
      volumes: [./prometheus:/etc/prometheus:ro]
      <<: [*svc, *net]

volumes:
  pgdata: {}
  grafana:
  models:
    driver: local

networks:
  kestrel:
    name: kestrel-dev
    driver: bridge
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: "172.28.0.0/16"
          gateway: 172.28.0.1

      image: ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.11.1
      command: start --uri file:/etc/flagd/flags.yaml --port 8013 --management-port 8014 --cors-origin '*' --log-format json --sync-interval 5s --debug
      ports: ["8013:8013", '8014:8014']
      volumes: [ "./flags:/etc/flagd:ro" ]
      networks:
      - kestrel
      healthcheck:
        test: [ "CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://localhost:8014/healthz" ]
        interval: 5s
        retries: 12

    accounts:
      build:
        context: ./subgraphs/accounts
        dockerfile: Dockerfile.dev
        args:
          NODE_VERSION: "20.15"
          NPM_TOKEN: ${NPM_TOKEN:-}
      environment:
        DATABASE_URL: postgres://kestrel:kestrel@postgres:5432/kestrel_dev?sslmode=disable
        FLAGD_HOST: flags
        FLAGD_PORT: "8013"
        LOG_LEVEL: debug
        ENABLE_PERSISTED_QUERIES: True
        TRUSTED_PROXIES: ~
        PQ_MANIFEST_URL: "https://pq.kestrel.dev/manifests/accounts.json#latest"
      depends_on: [ postgres, flags ]
      <<: *net

    model-server:
      <<: [*svc, *net]
      image: nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:24.08-py3
      profiles: ["gpu"]
      command: >
        tritonserver --model-repository=/models
        --model-control-mode=explicit --load-model=ranker_v7 --load-model=embedder_mini
        --strict-model-config=false --log-verbose=0
      shm_size: 2gb
      # fmt: compact
      ulimits:
        memlock: -1
        stack: 67108864
      deploy:
        resources:
          reservations:
            devices:
              - driver: nvidia
                count: 1
                capabilities: [gpu]
      environment:
        - CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
        - "TRITON_LOG_FORMAT=ISO8601"
        - MODEL_NAME_PATTERN=^(ranker|embedder)_v\d+$
      volumes:
        - models:/models:ro

    model-sync:
      image: amazon/aws-cli:2.17.0
      <<: *svc
      profiles: [ "gpu" ]
      entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
      command:
        - |
          # pull models once, then poll every 5 minutes
          set -eu
          while true; do
            aws s3 sync "s3://kestrel-models-dev/triton" /models --only-show-errors \
              --exclude "*" --include "ranker_v*/*" --include "embedder_*/*" || echo "sync failed: will retry"
            date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ last sync" > /models/.last_sync
            sleep 300
          done
      volumes:
        - models:/models
        - ~/.aws:/root/.aws:ro
      environment:
        AWS_PROFILE: kestrel-dev
        AWS_REGION: us-east-1
        AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED: "true"

    postgres:
        image: postgres:16.3-alpine
        <<: *svc
        environment:
            POSTGRES_USER: kestrel
            POSTGRES_PASSWORD: kestrel   # local only!!
            POSTGRES_DB: kestrel_dev
            PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
            POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: "--encoding=UTF8 --locale=C"
        ports:
          - "5432:5432"
        volumes:
          - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
          - ./db/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
        healthcheck:
            test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U kestrel -d kestrel_dev"]
            interval: 5s
            retries: 10
        networks: [kestrel]

    redis:
      image: "redis:7.2"
      command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "no", "--maxmemory", "256mb", "--maxmemory-policy", "allkeys-lru"]
      ports: [ "6379:6379" ]
      networks: [kestrel]

    otel-collector:
      image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.104.0
      command: [ "--config=/etc/otelcol/config.yaml" ]
      volumes:
        - ./otel/config.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml:ro
      ports:
        - 4317:4317   # OTLP gRPC
        - 4318:4318 # OTLP http
        - "55679:55679"  #zpages
      <<: [*svc, *net]

    grafana:
      image: grafana/grafana:11.1.0
      environment:
        GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED: "true"
        GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ORG_ROLE: Admin
        GF_FEATURE_TOGGLES_ENABLE: "traceToMetrics,correlations,publicDashboards"
        GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL: "http://localhost:3001/"
        GF_INSTALL_PLUGINS: ""
      ports: ['3001:3000']
      volumes:
        - grafana:/var/lib/grafana
        - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      depends_on: {prometheus: {condition: service_started}}
      <<: *net

    prometheus:
      image: prom/prometheus:v2.53.0
      command:
        - --config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
        - --storage.tsdb.retention.time=2d
        - "--web.enable-lifecycle"
      volumes: [./prometheus:/etc/prometheus:ro]
      <<: [*svc, *net]

volumes:
  pgdata: {}
  grafana:
  models:
    driver: local

networks:
  kestrel:
    name: kestrel-dev
    driver: bridge
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: "172.28.0.0/16"
          gateway: 172.28.0.1

arguments.content:
# .github/workflows/deploy.yml
# build -> test -> deploy (canary region first) -> canary analysis -> slack on failure
name: build-and-deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, 'release/**' ]
    tags: ['v*.*.*']
    paths-ignore:
    - 'docs/**'
    - '**.md'
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: Where to deploy. Prod requires an approved change ticket in the change-management channel, no exceptions after the October incident.
        type: choice
        options: [staging, prod]
        default: staging
      dry_run:
        description: "Render manifests + diff only"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      regions:
        description: 'Comma separated, e.g. "us-east-1,eu-west-1" (empty = all)'
        required: false
        default: ''
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * 1-5'   # nightly staging redeploy to catch drift
  merge_group: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write
  id-token: write    # OIDC -> AWS
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: deploy-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}  #only cancel stale PR runs

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository_owner }}/kestrel-gateway
  DEPLOY_ENV: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && 'prod' || 'staging' }}
  TARGET_ENV: ${{ (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.environment) || (startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') && 'prod') || 'staging' }}
  HELM_VERSION: "3.15.2"
  KUBECTL_VERSION: v1.30.2
  PYTHON_VERSION: "3.10"
  FORCE_COLOR: "1"

jobs:
  lint-test:
    name: Lint & test (py ${{ matrix.python }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python: ["3.10", "3.11", '3.12']
        include:
          - python: "3.12"
            experimental: true
    services:
      redis:
        image: redis:7.2
        ports: ["6379:6379"]
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 3s
          --health-retries 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      -   name: Set up Python
          uses: actions/setup-python@v5
          with:
            python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
            cache: pip
      - name: Install
        run: pip install -r requirements-dev.txt && pip install -e ./services/flags-sync -e ./tools/rollout
      - name: Lint
        run: |
          ruff check . --output-format=github
          yamllint -c .yamllint.yml deploy/ .github/   # strict: warnings fail the build
          # schema check against the published supergraph
          npx --yes @graphql-inspector/cli diff "git:origin/main:schema/supergraph.graphql" "schema/supergraph.graphql" --rule suppressRemovalOfDeprecatedField
      - name: Test
        run: pytest -q -n auto --maxfail=5 --cov=services --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml -m "not slow and not gpu" --junitxml=reports/junit-${{ matrix.python }}.xml
        continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental == true }}
        env:
          REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379/0
          FLAGD_OFFLINE_FLAG_SOURCE_PATH: ./flags/flags.test.yaml
          TZ: UTC

  build:
      needs: lint-test
      if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || !github.event.pull_request.draft }}
      runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64, docker]
      outputs:
          image_tag: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}
          digest: ${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }}
      steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with: {fetch-depth: 0}
          - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3
          - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
          - name: Log in to GHCR
            uses: docker/login-action@v3
            with:
                registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
                username: ${{ github.actor }}
                password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          - id: meta
            uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
            with:
                images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
                tags: |
                    type=ref,event=branch
                    type=semver,pattern={{version}}
                    type=sha,format=short,prefix=
          - id: push
            uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
            with:
                context: .
                file: services/gateway/Dockerfile
                platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
                push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
                tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
                cache-from: type=gha
                cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
                build-args: |
                    GIT_SHA=${{ github.sha }}
                    BUILD_DATE=${{ github.event.head_commit.timestamp }}

  deploy:
    needs: [build]
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    environment:
      name: ${{ env.TARGET_ENV }}
      url: https://${{ env.TARGET_ENV == 'prod' && 'api' || 'api.staging' }}.kestrel.dev/graphql
    strategy:
      max-parallel: 1
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        # fmt: table
        include:
          - {region: us-east-1, cluster: prod-use1-blue, canary: true, weight: 5}
          - {region: eu-west-1,  cluster: prod-euw1-blue,canary: false,  weight: 100}
          - {region: ap-southeast-2, cluster: prod-apse2-a, canary: false, weight: 100}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Configure AWS credentials (OIDC)
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gha-deploy-${{ env.TARGET_ENV }}
          aws-region: ${{ matrix.region }}
          role-duration-seconds: 3600
      - name: Install helm
        uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
        with: { version: "${{ env.HELM_VERSION }}" }
      - name: Helm upgrade
        id: helm
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "${{ matrix.cluster }}" --region "${{ matrix.region }}"
          EXTRA=""
          if [[ "${{ inputs.dry_run }}" == "true" ]]; then EXTRA="--dry-run=server"; fi
          # NOTE: --atomic rolls back on failure; the timeout must exceed the readiness budget (see INC-2291)
          helm upgrade --install kestrel-gateway deploy/charts/gateway \
            --namespace gateway --create-namespace \
            -f deploy/values/${{ env.TARGET_ENV }}.yaml -f deploy/values/${{ matrix.region }}.yaml \
            --set image.tag=${{ needs.build.outputs.image_tag }} \
            --set canary.enabled=${{ matrix.canary }},canary.weight=${{ matrix.weight }} \
            --atomic --timeout 10m $EXTRA
          echo "revision=$(helm history kestrel-gateway -n gateway -o json | jq -r '.[-1].revision')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Wait for rollout
        run: kubectl -n gateway rollout status deploy/kestrel-gateway --timeout=600s && kubectl -n gateway get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kestrel-gateway -o wide

  canary-analysis:
    needs: deploy
    if: ${{ needs.deploy.result == 'success' && contains(fromJSON('["prod"]'), env.TARGET_ENV) }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    steps:
      - name: Query error budget burn
        id: burn
        run: |
          q='sum(rate(router_http_requests_total{status=~"5..",env="prod"}[5m])) / sum(rate(router_http_requests_total{env="prod"}[5m]))'
          ratio=$(curl -sG "${PROM_URL}/api/v1/query" --data-urlencode "query=${q}" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${PROM_TOKEN}" | jq -r '.data.result[0].value[1] // "0"')
          echo "ratio=${ratio}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          python3 -c "import sys; sys.exit(0 if float('${ratio}') < 0.002 else 1)"
        env:
          PROM_URL: https://prometheus.ops.kestrel.dev
          PROM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PROM_READ_TOKEN }}

  notify:
    needs: [deploy, canary-analysis]
    if: "!cancelled() && (needs.deploy.result == 'failure' || needs.canary-analysis.result == 'failure')"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1.26.0
        with:
          channel-id: 'C04PLATFORMSRE'
          payload: '{"text":":rotating_light: Deploy of ${{ github.sha }} to ${{ env.TARGET_ENV }} failed","blocks":[{"type":"section","text":{"type":"mrkdwn","text":"*Run:* <${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}|#${{ github.run_number }}>"}}]}'
        env:
          SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN }}

# .github/workflows/deploy.yml
# build -> test -> deploy (canary region first) -> canary analysis -> slack on failure
name: build-and-deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, 'release/**' ]
    tags: ['v*.*.*']
    paths-ignore:
    - 'docs/**'
    - '**.md'
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: Where to deploy. Prod requires an approved change ticket in the change-management channel, no exceptions after the October incident.
        type: choice
        options: [staging, prod]
        default: staging
      dry_run:
        description: "Render manifests + diff only"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      regions:
        description: 'Comma separated, e.g. "us-east-1,eu-west-1" (empty = all)'
        required: false
        default: ''
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * 1-5'   # nightly staging redeploy to catch drift
  merge_group: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write
  id-token: write    # OIDC -> AWS
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: deploy-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}  #only cancel stale PR runs

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository_owner }}/kestrel-gateway
  DEPLOY_ENV: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && 'prod' || 'staging' }}
  TARGET_ENV: ${{ (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.environment) || (startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') && 'prod') || 'staging' }}
  HELM_VERSION: "3.15.2"
  KUBECTL_VERSION: v1.30.2
  PYTHON_VERSION: "3.10"
  FORCE_COLOR: "1"

jobs:
  lint-test:
    name: Lint & test (py ${{ matrix.python }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python: ["3.10", "3.11", '3.12']
        include:
          - python: "3.12"
            experimental: true
    services:
      redis:
        image: redis:7.2
        ports: ["6379:6379"]
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 3s
          --health-retries 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      -   name: Set up Python
          uses: actions/setup-python@v5
          with:
            python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
            cache: pip
      - name: Install
        run: pip install -r requirements-dev.txt && pip install -e ./services/flags-sync -e ./tools/rollout
      - name: Lint
        run: |
          ruff check . --output-format=github
          yamllint -c .yamllint.yml deploy/ .github/   # strict: warnings fail the build
          # schema check against the published supergraph
          npx --yes @graphql-inspector/cli diff "git:origin/main:schema/supergraph.graphql" "schema/supergraph.graphql" --rule suppressRemovalOfDeprecatedField
      - name: Test
        run: pytest -q -n auto --maxfail=5 --cov=services --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml -m "not slow and not gpu" --junitxml=reports/junit-${{ matrix.python }}.xml
        continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental == true }}
        env:
          REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379/0
          FLAGD_OFFLINE_FLAG_SOURCE_PATH: ./flags/flags.test.yaml
          TZ: UTC

  build:
      needs: lint-test
      if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || !github.event.pull_request.draft }}
      runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64, docker]
      outputs:
          image_tag: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}
          digest: ${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }}
      steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with: {fetch-depth: 0}
          - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3
          - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
          - name: Log in to GHCR
            uses: docker/login-action@v3
            with:
                registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
                username: ${{ github.actor }}
                password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          - id: meta
            uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
            with:
                images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
                tags: |
                    type=ref,event=branch
                    type=semver,pattern={{version}}
                    type=sha,format=short,prefix=
          - id: push
            uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
            with:
                context: .
                file: services/gateway/Dockerfile
                platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
                push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
                tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
                cache-from: type=gha
                cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
                build-args: |
                    GIT_SHA=${{ github.sha }}
                    BUILD_DATE=${{ github.event.head_commit.timestamp }}

  deploy:
    needs: [build]
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    environment:
      name: ${{ env.TARGET_ENV }}
      url: https://${{ env.TARGET_ENV == 'prod' && 'api' || 'api.staging' }}.kestrel.dev/graphql
    strategy:
      max-parallel: 1
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        # fmt: table
        include:
          - {region: us-east-1, cluster: prod-use1-blue, canary: true, weight: 5}
          - {region: eu-west-1,  cluster: prod-euw1-blue,canary: false,  weight: 100}
          - {region: ap-southeast-2, cluster: prod-apse2-a, canary: false, weight: 100}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Configure AWS credentials (OIDC)
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gha-deploy-${{ env.TARGET_ENV }}
          aws-region: ${{ matrix.region }}
          role-duration-seconds: 3600
      - name: Install helm
        uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
        with: { version: "${{ env.HELM_VERSION }}" }
      - name: Helm upgrade
        id: helm
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "${{ matrix.cluster }}" --region "${{ matrix.region }}"
          EXTRA=""
          if [[ "${{ inputs.dry_run }}" == "true" ]]; then EXTRA="--dry-run=server"; fi
          # NOTE: --atomic rolls back on failure; the timeout must exceed the readiness budget (see INC-2291)
          helm upgrade --install kestrel-gateway deploy/charts/gateway \
            --namespace gateway --create-namespace \
            -f deploy/values/${{ env.TARGET_ENV }}.yaml -f deploy/values/${{ matrix.region }}.yaml \
            --set image.tag=${{ needs.build.outputs.image_tag }} \
            --set canary.enabled=${{ matrix.canary }},canary.weight=${{ matrix.weight }} \
            --atomic --timeout 10m $EXTRA
          echo "revision=$(helm history kestrel-gateway -n gateway -o json | jq -r '.[-1].revision')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Wait for rollout
        run: kubectl -n gateway rollout status deploy/kestrel-gateway --timeout=600s && kubectl -n gateway get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kestrel-gateway -o wide

  canary-analysis:
    needs: deploy
    if: ${{ needs.deploy.result == 'success' && contains(fromJSON('["prod"]'), env.TARGET_ENV) }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    steps:
      - name: Query error budget burn
        id: burn
        run: |
          q='sum(rate(router_http_requests_total{status=~"5..",env="prod"}[5m])) / sum(rate(router_http_requests_total{env="prod"}[5m]))'
          ratio=$(curl -sG "${PROM_URL}/api/v1/query" --data-urlencode "query=${q}" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${PROM_TOKEN}" | jq -r '.data.result[0].value[1] // "0"')
          echo "ratio=${ratio}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          python3 -c "import sys; sys.exit(0 if float('${ratio}') < 0.002 else 1)"
        env:
          PROM_URL: https://prometheus.ops.kestrel.dev
          PROM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PROM_READ_TOKEN }}

  notify:
    needs: [deploy, canary-analysis]
    if: "!cancelled() && (needs.deploy.result == 'failure' || needs.canary-analysis.result == 'failure')"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1.26.0
        with:
          channel-id: 'C04PLATFORMSRE'
          payload: '{"text":":rotating_light: Deploy of ${{ github.sha }} to ${{ env.TARGET_ENV }} failed","blocks":[{"type":"section","text":{"type":"mrkdwn","text":"*Run:* <${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}|#${{ github.run_number }}>"}}]}'
        env:
          SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN }}

106	        deadline = DEADLINES.get(ASSIGNMENT)
