115	# fmt: markdown
116	FEEDBACK_TEMPLATE_DE = """
117	## Rückmeldung zu {assignment}
118	
119	Hallo {student}, hier ist dein automatisch erzeugtes Feedback. Die Punkte sind *vorläufig*: Grenzfälle schauen sich die Tutor:innen noch einmal von Hand an, bevor die Noten im LMS freigegeben werden.
120	
121	*   **Punkte:** {score} von {max_score}
122	*   **Bestandene Tests:** {n_passed} / {n_tests}
123	*   Abgabezeitpunkt: {submitted_at}
124	
125	### Hinweise zu einzelnen Aufgaben
126	{details}
127	
128	### Häufige Fehler
129	1) `np.var(x)` berechnet die *Populations*varianz. Für die Stichprobenvarianz brauchst du `np.var(x, ddof=1)` bzw. in R einfach `var(x)`.
130	2) Achsenbeschriftungen fehlen oft – `plt.xlabel("Körpergröße [cm]")` kostet zehn Sekunden.
131	3) Bei Konfidenzintervallen für kleine Stichproben ($n < 30$) bitte die t-Verteilung verwenden und nicht `norm.ppf`, sonst wird das Intervall zu schmal.
132	
133	Fragen? Sprechstunde Do 14–16 Uhr (Raum 3.142) oder im [Forum](https://forum.stat.uni-beispielstadt.de/c/stat1010).
134	"""
135	
136	# fmt: markdown
137	FEEDBACK_TEMPLATE_EN = r"""
138	## Feedback for {{ assignment }}
139	Hi {{ student }}! Your submission was graded automatically. Scores are *provisional* until a TA has double-checked borderline cases, which usually happens within two working days after the deadline.
140	- **Score:** {{ score }} / {{ max_score }}
141	- Tests passed: {{ n_passed }} of {{ n_tests }}
142	- Reminder: the sample mean is $\bar{x} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i x_i$ and the standard error is $s/\sqrt{n}$, not $\sigma/n$.
143	
144	{% for q in questions %}
145	* **{{ q.name }}**: {{ q.points }}/{{ q.max_points }} {% if q.passed %}✓{% else %}✗{% endif %}
146	{% endfor %}
147	
148	Questions? Come to office hours (Thu 2–4 pm, room 3.142) or post in the forum.
149	"""
150	
151	# Für R-basierte Übungsblätter (Lab 2 und Lab 5) prüfen wir zusätzlich mit testthat.
152	
153	# fmt: r
154	R_CHECK = """
155	library(testthat)
156	test_that("Mittelwert korrekt",{expect_equal(round(mean(groesse,na.rm=TRUE),2),171.9,tolerance=1e-2)})
157	test_that("KI enthält mu",{ki<-t.test(groesse)$conf.int;expect_true(ki[1]<172&&ki[2]>172)})
158	"""
159	
160	# %%
161	#| label: grading
162	#| tags: [grading]
163	#| timeout:    120
164	#| env: {OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1", MPLBACKEND: Agg,
165	#|       LANG: de_DE.UTF-8}
166	def partial_credit(results: Iterable[TestResult], max_points: float) -> float:
167	    """Teilpunkte nach den Bewertungsregeln oben (versteckte Tests zählen doppelt)."""
168	    results = list(results)
169	    if not any(r.passed and not r.hidden for r in results):
170	        return 0.0
171	    total = sum(2 * r.weight if r.hidden else r.weight for r in results)
172	    got = sum((2 * r.weight if r.hidden else r.weight) for r in results if r.passed)
173	    return round(max_points * got / total, 2) if total else 0.0
174	
175	
176	def apply_late_penalty(score: float, days_late: int) -> float:
177	    if days_late > MAX_LATE_DAYS: return 0.0  # fmt: skip
178	    return round(score * (1 - LATE_PENALTY_PER_DAY * days_late), 2)
179	
180	
181	def render_feedback(sub: Submission, max_points: float) -> str:
182	    """Füllt die passende Vorlage aus; Englisch läuft schon über Jinja, Deutsch noch nicht."""
183	    score = apply_late_penalty(partial_credit(sub.results, max_points), sub.days_late)
184	    n_passed, n_tests = sum(r.passed for r in sub.results), len(sub.results)
185	    if sub.lang == "en":
186	        from jinja2 import Template
187	        return Template(FEEDBACK_TEMPLATE_EN).render(assignment=ASSIGNMENT, student=sub.student, score=score,
188	            max_score=max_points, n_passed=n_passed, n_tests=n_tests, questions=[])
189	    details = "\n".join(f"- `{r.name}`: {'✓' if r.passed else '✗'} {r.message}".rstrip() for r in sub.results if not r.hidden)
190	    return FEEDBACK_TEMPLATE_DE.format(assignment=ASSIGNMENT, student=sub.student, score=score, max_score=max_points,
191	        n_passed=n_passed, n_tests=n_tests, submitted_at=sub.submitted_at.strftime("%d.%m.%Y, %H:%M Uhr"),
192	        details=details or "_keine_")
193	
194	# %%
195	#| label: main
196	#| eval:   false
197	#| tags: [cli]
198	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
199	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Autograder für STAT 1010 – bewertet alle Abgaben in einem Ordner.")
200	    parser.add_argument("submissions", type=Path, help="Ordner mit *.ipynb-Dateien")
201	    parser.add_argument("--lang", choices=["de", "en", "fr", "es"], default=LANG)
202	    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=Path("feedback"))
203	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
204	    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
205	    for nb in sorted(args.submissions.glob("*.ipynb")):
206	        sub = Submission(student=nb.stem, notebook=nb, lang=args.lang,
207	                         submitted_at=datetime.fromtimestamp(nb.stat().st_mtime, tz=timezone.utc))
208	        sub.results = []  # TODO: run_tests(nb, Path("tests") / ASSIGNMENT) aus grader/otter_runner.py
209	        (args.out / f"{nb.stem}.md").write_text(render_feedback(sub, max_points=20), encoding="utf-8")
210	        print(f"✓ {nb.name}: Feedback geschrieben")
211	    return 0
212	
213	
214	if __name__ == "__main__":
215	    sys.exit(main())

apiVersion: v1

I didn't run any formatter or touch `/workspace`. To check the YAML, I used the `yaml` 2.3.4 parser already in `/usr/share/nodejs`. Every YAML file, front-matter block, ` ```yaml ` fence and `#|` block parses as valid YAML 1.2. The only warnings are for the custom tags, which is expected. `python_script.py` is also valid Python syntax.

Things to know when reading results:
- **Directive placement:** `# fmt: table` (ansible, over a `loop:` of flow mappings) and `# fmt: compact` (docker compose, over `dns:`) both sit on the line above the key. The source in `src/yaml/mod.rs` shows that a directive placed there applies to the key's list.
- **Sentence wrap:** the .Rmd asks for it through front matter `editor_options: markdown: wrap: sentence`.
- **Python/R targets:** every `# fmt: markdown` directive is followed directly by its target. The strings containing backslashes are raw strings, and the others contain none. Both files also include one `# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence` string target.
- **Extra directives I added:** a `#| fmt: skip` chunk in the .qmd and a `<!-- fmt: off -->`/`<!-- fmt: on -->` region in `contributing.md`.
- **Deliberate edge cases:**
  - Long Rmd chunk header: one chunk header in the .Rmd is over 72 characters, which may get its options moved into `#|` lines.
  - Under-indented list in `changelog.md`: two items are indented 3 spaces under a list item whose text starts at column 4. They read as siblings rather than nested items.
  - Unquoted R expression: an unquoted `!expr` tag in an R `#|` block.

arguments.content:
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Kestrel Control Plane API
  version: "2.4.0"
  # fmt: markdown
  description: |
    Internal API used by `kestrelctl`, the admin UI, and a growing number of scripts nobody admits to owning.
    It manages **feature flags**, **model deployments** and **regional failover**.

    ## Auth
    Every endpoint needs a bearer token from the internal IdP, *except* `/healthz`.
    Tokens are scoped:
    * `flags:read` / `flags:write`
    * `models:deploy` -- only granted to the ML-infra on-call
    rotation
    * `regions:failover` (break glass, audited, pages the IC)

    ## Rate limits
    100 req/s per token, burst 200. Over the limit you get a `429` with a `Retry-After` header; please actually honor it, the gateway team is watching.
  contact: {name: Platform SRE, url: "https://handbook.kestrel.internal/oncall/", email: platform-sre@kestrel.dev}
servers:
- url: https://control.{region}.kestrel.dev/v2
  description: Production (per region)
  variables:
    region:
      enum: [ us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-2 ]
      default: us-east-1
- url: http://localhost:8070/v2
  description: local (docker compose)
security:
  - bearerAuth: []
tags:
  - {name: flags, description: Feature flag definitions and rollouts}
  - {name: models,  description: "Model registry + serving deployments"}
  - name: regions
    description: Regional health and failover. Every call here is audited, and any state change pages the on-call engineer for the affected region.
paths:
  /flags:
    get:
      tags: [flags]
      summary: List flags
      operationId: listFlags
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Cursor'
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit"
        - name: state
          in: query
          schema: {type: string, enum: [ENABLED, DISABLED, ARCHIVED]}
        - name: q
          in: query
          description: Substring match on key or description (case-insensitive). Supports a `prefix:` qualifier, e.g. `prefix:gateway.` to list every gateway flag.
          schema:
            type: string
            maxLength: 128
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A page of flags
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Flag'}
                  next_cursor: {type: string, nullable: true}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
    post:
      tags: [flags]
      summary: Create a flag
      operationId: createFlag
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/FlagCreate'}
            example: {"key": "gateway.query-planner-v2", "description": "New query planner",
                      "kind": "boolean", "variants": {"on": true, "off": false}, "default_variant": "off"}
      responses:
        201:
          description: Created
          headers:
            Location:
              schema: {type: string, format: uri}
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Flag'
        409:
          description: Flag key already exists
  /flags/{flagKey}/rollout:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/FlagKey'
    put:
      tags: [ flags ]
      summary: Change rollout percentage
      description: Sets the absolute percentage of traffic that gets the `on` variant.
        Changes are applied to the canary region first and propagate to the
        remaining regions only after the canary has been healthy for `bake_minutes`.
      operationId: setFlagRollout
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/RolloutChange'
            examples:
              ramp:
                summary: ramp to 25% in all regions
                value:
                  percentage: 25
                  regions: []
                  bake_minutes: 15
              rollback:
                summary: "Emergency rollback"
                value: {percentage: 0, regions: [eu-west-1], bake_minutes: 0, reason: "INC-2291: elevated 5xx"}
      responses:
        '202':
          description: Accepted; poll the returned operation.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Operation' }
        '422': {description: Validation error, content: {application/problem+json: {schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'}}}}
  /models/{modelName}/deployments:
    post:
      tags: [models]
      summary: Deploy a model version
      operationId: deployModel
      parameters:
      - name: modelName
        in: path
        required: true
        schema:
          type: string
          pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,40}$"
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [version, strategy]
              properties:
                version:
                  type: string
                  pattern: "^v\\d+(\\.\\d+){0,2}(-rc\\.\\d+)?$"
                  example: v7.2.0-rc.1
                strategy:
                  type: string
                  enum: [canary, blue_green, shadow]
                  default: canary
                canary:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    traffic_percent:
                      type: integer
                      minimum: 0
                      maximum: 100
                      description: Percentage of traffic (0-100) routed to the new version
                        before automatic promotion. Ignored when strategy is blue_green.
                    promote_after: {type: string, format: duration, example: "PT30M"}
                    guardrails:
                      type: array
                      items:
                        type: object
                        properties:
                          metric: {type: string, enum: [p99_latency_ms, error_rate, gpu_util, "ndcg@10"]}
                          op: {type: string, enum: ['<', '<=', '>', '>=']}
                          threshold: {type: number}
      responses:
        '202':
          description: Deployment started
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Operation'}
components:
  securitySchemes:
    bearerAuth: {type: http, scheme: bearer, bearerFormat: JWT}
    oauth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        clientCredentials:
          tokenUrl: https://idp.kestrel.internal/oauth2/token
          scopes:
            flags:read: Read flags
            flags:write: Create/modify flags
            models:deploy: Deploy model versions
            regions:failover: "Break-glass: fail a region over"
  parameters:
    FlagKey:
      name: flagKey
      in: path
      required: true
      schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[a-z0-9]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+$'}
      example: gateway.apq-enforce
    Cursor: {name: cursor, in: query, schema: {type: string}}
    Limit:
      name: limit
      in: query
      schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 500, default: 50}
  responses:
    Unauthorized:
      description: Missing or invalid token
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'}
  schemas:
    Flag:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/FlagCreate'
        - type: object
          required: [state, created_at]
          properties:
            state: {type: string, enum: [ ENABLED, DISABLED, ARCHIVED ]}
            created_at: {type: string, format: date-time, example: "2024-10-21T09:14:00Z"}
            rollout:
              type: object
              properties:
                percentage: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100, example: 12.5}
                by_region:
                  type: object
                  additionalProperties: {type: number}
                  example: {us-east-1: 25, eu-west-1: 0, ap-southeast-2: 25}
    FlagCreate:
      type: object
      required: [key, kind, variants, default_variant]
      properties:
        key: {type: string, example: gateway.query-planner-v2}
        description: {type: string, maxLength: 500}
        kind: {type: string, enum: [boolean, string, number, json]}
        variants:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
          example: {"on": true, "off": false}
        default_variant: {type: string, example: "off"}
        targeting:
          type: object
          nullable: true
          description: JsonLogic rule evaluated by flagd. Must be valid JsonLogic -- the admin API runs it against a sample context before saving and rejects rules that throw.
    RolloutChange:
      type: object
      required: [percentage]
      properties:
        percentage: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100}
        regions: {type: array, items: {type: string, enum: [us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-2]}, description: "Empty = all regions"}
        bake_minutes: {type: integer, default: 15}
        reason: {type: string}
    Operation:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: {type: string, format: uuid}
        status: {type: string, enum: [pending, running, succeeded, failed, rolled_back]}
    Problem:
      type: object
      properties:
        type: {type: string, format: uri, default: "about:blank"}
        title: {type: string}
        status: {type: integer, example: 422}

  - name: regions
    description: Regional health and failover. Every call here is audited, and any state change pages the on-call engineer for the affected region.
paths:
  /flags:
    get:
      tags: [flags]
      summary: List flags
      operationId: listFlags
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Cursor'
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit"
        - name: state
          in: query
          schema: {type: string, enum: [ENABLED, DISABLED, ARCHIVED]}
        - name: q
          in: query
          description: Substring match on key or description (case-insensitive). Supports a `prefix:` qualifier, e.g. `prefix:gateway.` to list every gateway flag.
          schema:
            type: string
            maxLength: 128
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A page of flags
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Flag'}
                  next_cursor: {type: string, nullable: true}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
    post:
      tags: [flags]
      summary: Create a flag
      operationId: createFlag
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/FlagCreate'}
            example: {"key": "gateway.query-planner-v2", "description": "New query planner",
                      "kind": "boolean", "variants": {"on": true, "off": false}, "default_variant": "off"}
      responses:
        201:
          description: Created
          headers:
            Location:
              schema: {type: string, format: uri}
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Flag'
        409:
          description: Flag key already exists
  /flags/{flagKey}/rollout:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/FlagKey'
    put:
      tags: [ flags ]
      summary: Change rollout percentage
      description: Sets the absolute percentage of traffic that gets the `on` variant.
        Changes are applied to the canary region first and propagate to the
        remaining regions only after the canary has been healthy for `bake_minutes`.
      operationId: setFlagRollout
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/RolloutChange'
            examples:
              ramp:
                summary: ramp to 25% in all regions
                value:
                  percentage: 25
                  regions: []
                  bake_minutes: 15
              rollback:
                summary: "Emergency rollback"
                value: {percentage: 0, regions: [eu-west-1], bake_minutes: 0, reason: "INC-2291: elevated 5xx"}
      responses:
        '202':
          description: Accepted; poll the returned operation.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Operation' }
        '422': {description: Validation error, content: {application/problem+json: {schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'}}}}
  /models/{modelName}/deployments:
    post:
      tags: [models]
      summary: Deploy a model version
      operationId: deployModel
      parameters:
      - name: modelName
        in: path
        required: true
        schema:
          type: string
          pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,40}$"
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [version, strategy]
              properties:
                version:
                  type: string
                  pattern: "^v\\d+(\\.\\d+){0,2}(-rc\\.\\d+)?$"
                  example: v7.2.0-rc.1
                strategy:
                  type: string
                  enum: [canary, blue_green, shadow]
                  default: canary
                canary:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    traffic_percent:
                      type: integer
                      minimum: 0
                      maximum: 100
                      description: Percentage of traffic (0-100) routed to the new version
                        before automatic promotion. Ignored when strategy is blue_green.
                    promote_after: {type: string, format: duration, example: "PT30M"}
                    guardrails:
                      type: array
                      items:
                        type: object
                        properties:
                          metric: {type: string, enum: [p99_latency_ms, error_rate, gpu_util, "ndcg@10"]}
                          op: {type: string, enum: ['<', '<=', '>', '>=']}
                          threshold: {type: number}
      responses:
        '202':
          description: Deployment started
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Operation'}
components:
  securitySchemes:
    bearerAuth: {type: http, scheme: bearer, bearerFormat: JWT}
    oauth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        clientCredentials:
          tokenUrl: https://idp.kestrel.internal/oauth2/token
          scopes:
            flags:read: Read flags
            flags:write: Create/modify flags
            models:deploy: Deploy model versions
            regions:failover: "Break-glass: fail a region over"
  parameters:
    FlagKey:
      name: flagKey
      in: path
      required: true
      schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[a-z0-9]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+$'}
      example: gateway.apq-enforce
    Cursor: {name: cursor, in: query, schema: {type: string}}
    Limit:
      name: limit
      in: query
      schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 500, default: 50}
  responses:
    Unauthorized:
      description: Missing or invalid token
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'}
  schemas:
    Flag:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/FlagCreate'
        - type: object
          required: [state, created_at]
          properties:
            state: {type: string, enum: [ ENABLED, DISABLED, ARCHIVED ]}
            created_at: {type: string, format: date-time, example: "2024-10-21T09:14:00Z"}
            rollout:
              type: object
              properties:
                percentage: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100, example: 12.5}
                by_region:
                  type: object
                  additionalProperties: {type: number}
                  example: {us-east-1: 25, eu-west-1: 0, ap-southeast-2: 25}
    FlagCreate:
      type: object
      required: [key, kind, variants, default_variant]
      properties:
        key: {type: string, example: gateway.query-planner-v2}
        description: {type: string, maxLength: 500}
        kind: {type: string, enum: [boolean, string, number, json]}
        variants:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
          example: {"on": true, "off": false}
        default_variant: {type: string, example: "off"}
        targeting:
          type: object
          nullable: true
          description: JsonLogic rule evaluated by flagd. Must be valid JsonLogic -- the admin API runs it against a sample context before saving and rejects rules that throw.
    RolloutChange:
      type: object
      required: [percentage]
      properties:
        percentage: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100}
        regions: {type: array, items: {type: string, enum: [us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-2]}, description: "Empty = all regions"}
        bake_minutes: {type: integer, default: 15}
        reason: {type: string}
    Operation:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: {type: string, format: uuid}
        status: {type: string, enum: [pending, running, succeeded, failed, rolled_back]}
    Problem:
      type: object
      properties:
        type: {type: string, format: uri, default: "about:blank"}
        title: {type: string}
        status: {type: integer, example: 422}

arguments.content:
# =====================================================================
#  noten_auswertung.R
#  Auswertung der Übungsblätter und der Klausur – STAT 1010, WiSe 2026/27
#  Autor:innen: M. Koch, A. Ruiz, Α. Παπαδόπουλος
#  Letzte Änderung: 2026-11-14 (Bonuspunkte-Regel angepasst)
# =====================================================================

#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning:   FALSE
#| fig-width:  7
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| tags: [setup,   grading , export]
#| params:
#|     semester: "WiSe 2026/27"
#|     input:   daten/punkte_export.csv
#|     cutoffs: {sehr_gut: 0.9, gut: 0.8,
#|               befriedigend: 0.65, ausreichend: 0.5}
#|     ausgabe:
#|     - html
#|     - csv
#| description: Liest den Export aus dem LMS ein, berechnet Gesamtpunkte und Noten und schreibt eine anonymisierte Übersicht für die Kursseite, natürlich ohne Matrikelnummern.

# fmt: markdown
hilfe <- "
**noten_auswertung.R** – liest den LMS-Export ein, berechnet Gesamtpunkte, Noten und Bonuspunkte und schreibt eine anonymisierte Übersicht für die Kurswebseite.

Aufruf:   `Rscript noten_auswertung.R daten/punkte_export.csv`
Optionen:
* `--ohne-bonus`   Bonuspunkte ignorieren
* `--sprache=en`  englische Spaltennamen (für die Erasmus-Übersicht)
"

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(readr)
  library(stringr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(glue)
})

# fmt: markdown
# ## Notenschlüssel
#
# Die Gesamtpunktzahl setzt sich aus den Übungsblättern (40 %), dem Projekt (20 %) und der Klausur (40 %) zusammen. Bonuspunkte aus den Tutorien zählen nur, wenn die Klausur für sich genommen bestanden ist – so steht es in der Prüfungsordnung, § 12 Abs. 3.
#
# | Note | Bezeichnung | Mindestanteil |
# |---|---|--:|
# | 1,0 – 1,3 | sehr gut | 90 % |
# | 1,7 – 2,3 | gut | 80 % |
# | 2,7 – 3,3 | befriedigend | 65 % |
# | 3,7 – 4,0 |ausreichend| 50 % |
# | 5,0 | nicht bestanden | – |

notenschluessel <- tibble::tribble(
  ~anteil, ~note,  ~bezeichnung,
  0.90,    "1,0",  "sehr gut",
  0.80,    "2,0",  "gut",
  0.65,    "3,0",  "befriedigend",
  0.50,    "4,0",  "ausreichend",
  0.00,    "5,0",  "nicht bestanden"
)

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
# Vorgehen beim Import: Zuerst werden doppelte Abgaben entfernt, es zählt die letzte Abgabe vor der Frist. Danach werden fehlende Werte als 0 Punkte gewertet, außer bei einem Attest. Studierende mit Attest bekommen den Mittelwert ihrer übrigen Blätter (vgl. Beschluss des Prüfungsausschusses vom 3.11.2026).
#
# - Achtung: Der LMS-Export nutzt Semikolon als Trennzeichen und Komma als Dezimalzeichen, also `read_csv2()` und nicht `read_csv()`!
# - Die Spaltennamen sind uneinheitlich (`Blatt 1`, `blatt_02`, `Blatt03`) und werden unten vereinheitlicht.
#   Wer das LMS-Team kennt: bitte einmal freundlich nachfragen.

eingabe <- if (exists("params")) params$input else "daten/punkte_export.csv"
roh <- read_csv2(eingabe, show_col_types = FALSE, locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"))

# Spaltennamen vereinheitlichen: aus "Blatt 1" wird blatt_01 usw.
names(roh) <- names(roh) |>
  str_to_lower() |>
  str_replace_all("\\s+", "_") |>
  str_replace("^blatt_?(\\d)$", "blatt_0\\1")

blatt_spalten <- grep("^blatt_\\d+$", names(roh), value = TRUE)

punkte <- roh |>
  arrange(matrikel, desc(abgabe_zeit)) |>
  distinct(matrikel, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    across(all_of(blatt_spalten), ~ replace_na(.x, 0)),
    uebung  = rowSums(across(all_of(blatt_spalten))) / (10 * length(blatt_spalten)),
    projekt = projekt / 20,
    klausur = klausur / 60,
    # Bonus nur, wenn die Klausur allein bestanden ist (siehe Notenschlüssel oben)
    bonus   = if_else(klausur >= 0.5, pmin(bonus, 5), 0),
    gesamt  = pmin(1, 0.4 * uebung + 0.2 * projekt + 0.4 * klausur + bonus / 100)
  )

note_fuer <- function(anteil) {
  # findInterval() braucht aufsteigende Grenzen, deshalb rev()
  i <- findInterval(anteil, rev(notenschluessel$anteil))
  rev(notenschluessel$note)[i]
}

punkte <- punkte |> mutate(note = note_fuer(gesamt))

#| label: fig-verteilung
#| fig-cap: "Verteilung der Gesamtpunkte (alle Übungsgruppen); gestrichelt: Bestehensgrenze bei 50 %"
#| fig-alt: Histogramm der Gesamtpunkte, leicht linksschief, Modus bei etwa 70 Prozent, kaum Werte unter 20 Prozent.
#| layout: [[60,40]]
#| out-width:   '100%'
#| fig-format: svg
ggplot(punkte, aes(x = 100 * gesamt)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0, fill = "#4C72B0", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Gesamtpunkte [%]", y = "Anzahl Studierende",
       title = glue("STAT 1010 – {nrow(punkte)} Teilnehmende"),
       subtitle = "統計学入門 · Εισαγωγή στη Στατιστική · Einführung in die Statistik") +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "Noto Sans CJK JP")

# Die Tabelle je Übungsgruppe wird für den Aushang von Hand nachbearbeitet, daher:

# fmt: skip
#| label: tbl-gruppen
#| tbl-cap:    "Mittelwerte je Übungsgruppe"
#| tbl-colwidths: [20,20,20,20,20]
gruppen <- punkte |>
  group_by(gruppe) |>
  summarise(n = n(), uebung = mean(uebung), klausur = mean(klausur),
            bestanden = mean(note != "5,0"), .groups = "drop")

# fmt: markdown
mail_vorlage <- r"(
## Dein Zwischenstand in STAT 1010

Hallo {vorname}, nach {n_blaetter} von 10 Übungsblättern hast du insgesamt {punkte_summe} Punkte gesammelt. Das entspricht {anteil} % der bisher möglichen Punkte; damit bist du {status}.

*   Zulassung zur Klausur: mindestens 50 % der Übungspunkte
*   Bonus: ab 80 % gibt es bis zu 5 Bonuspunkte für die Klausur, aber nur, wenn die Klausur auch ohne Bonus bestanden ist
*   Fragen?  Schreib uns im Forum oder komm in die Sprechstunde.

Viele Grüße
dein Tutorenteam (Ana, Jonas, Αλέξανδρος, Chloé)
)"

mails <- punkte |>
  mutate(
    punkte_summe = round(rowSums(across(all_of(blatt_spalten)))),
    anteil = round(100 * uebung),
    status = if_else(uebung >= 0.5, "auf einem guten Weg", "leider noch nicht zugelassen"),
    text = glue(mail_vorlage, n_blaetter = length(blatt_spalten))
  )

#| label: export
#| output:
#|   html:
#|       toc: true
#|       self-contained:   true
#|   csv: {sep: ";", dec: ",", encoding: "UTF-8"}
#| notes: >
#|   Exportiert nur aggregierte Werte. Einzelne Noten gehen ausschließlich über HISinOne an das Prüfungsamt, niemals per E-Mail.

# Anonymisierte Übersicht für die Kursseite (keine Namen, keine Matrikelnummern!)
punkte |>
  count(note, name = "anzahl") |>
  write_csv("ausgabe/notenverteilung.csv")

message(glue("Fertig: {nrow(punkte)} Datensätze, Durchfallquote {round(100 * mean(punkte$note == '5,0'))} %."))

arguments.content:
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Kestrel Control Plane API
  version: "2.4.0"
  # fmt: markdown
  description: |
    Internal API used by `kestrelctl`, the admin UI, and a growing number of scripts nobody admits to owning.
    It manages **feature flags**, **model deployments** and **regional failover**.

    ## Auth
    Every endpoint needs a bearer token from the internal IdP, *except* `/healthz`.
    Tokens are scoped:
    * `flags:read` / `flags:write`
    * `models:deploy` -- only granted to the ML-infra on-call
    rotation
    * `regions:failover` (break glass, audited, pages the IC)

    ## Rate limits
    100 req/s per token, burst 200. Over the limit you get a `429` with a `Retry-After` header; please actually honor it, the gateway team is watching.
  contact: {name: Platform SRE, url: "https://handbook.kestrel.internal/oncall/", email: platform-sre@kestrel.dev}
servers:
- url: https://control.{region}.kestrel.dev/v2
  description: Production (per region)
  variables:
    region:
      enum: [ us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-2 ]
      default: us-east-1
security:
  - bearerAuth: []
tags:
  - {name: flags, description: Feature flag definitions and rollouts}
  - {name: models,  description: "Model registry + serving deployments"}
  - name: regions
    description: Regional health and failover. Every call here is audited, and any state change pages the on-call engineer for the affected region.
paths:
  /flags:
    get:
      tags: [flags]
      summary: List flags
      operationId: listFlags
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Cursor'
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit"
        - {name: state, in: query, schema: {type: string, enum: [ENABLED, DISABLED, ARCHIVED]}}
        - name: q
          in: query
          description: Substring match on key or description (case-insensitive). Supports a `prefix:` qualifier, e.g. `prefix:gateway.` to list every gateway flag.
          schema:
            type: string
            maxLength: 128
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A page of flags
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  items:
                    type: array
                    items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Flag'}
                  next_cursor: {type: string, nullable: true}
        "401": {description: Missing or invalid token}
    post:
      tags: [flags]
      summary: Create a flag
      operationId: createFlag
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/FlagCreate'}
            example: {"key": "gateway.query-planner-v2", "description": "New query planner",
                      "kind": "boolean", "variants": {"on": true, "off": false}, "default_variant": "off"}
      responses:
        201:
          description: Created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Flag'
        409:
          description: Flag key already exists
  /flags/{flagKey}/rollout:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/FlagKey'
    put:
      tags: [ flags ]
      summary: Change rollout percentage
      description: Sets the absolute percentage of traffic that gets the `on` variant.
        Changes are applied to the canary region first and propagate to the
        remaining regions only after the canary has been healthy for `bake_minutes`.
      operationId: setFlagRollout
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/RolloutChange'
            examples:
              ramp:
                summary: ramp to 25% in all regions
                value:
                  percentage: 25
                  regions: []
                  bake_minutes: 15
              rollback:
                summary: "Emergency rollback"
                value: {percentage: 0, regions: [eu-west-1], bake_minutes: 0, reason: "INC-2291: elevated 5xx"}
      responses:
        '202':
          description: Accepted; poll the returned operation.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Operation' }
        '422': {description: Validation error, content: {application/problem+json: {schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'}}}}
  /models/{modelName}/deployments:
    post:
      tags: [models]
      summary: Deploy a model version
      operationId: deployModel
      parameters:
      - name: modelName
        in: path
        required: true
        schema:
          type: string
          pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,40}$"
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [version, strategy]
              properties:
                version:
                  type: string
                  pattern: "^v\\d+(\\.\\d+){0,2}(-rc\\.\\d+)?$"
                  example: v7.2.0-rc.1
                strategy:
                  type: string
                  enum: [canary, blue_green, shadow]
                  default: canary
                canary:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    traffic_percent:
                      type: integer
                      minimum: 0
                      maximum: 100
                      description: Percentage of traffic (0-100) routed to the new version
                        before automatic promotion. Ignored when strategy is blue_green.
                    promote_after: {type: string, format: duration, example: "PT30M"}
                    guardrails:
                      type: array
                      items:
                        type: object
                        properties:
                          metric: {type: string, enum: [p99_latency_ms, error_rate, gpu_util, "ndcg@10"]}
                          op: {type: string, enum: ['<', '<=', '>', '>=']}
                          threshold: {type: number}
      responses:
        '202': {description: Deployment started, content: {application/json: {schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Operation'}}}}
components:
  securitySchemes:
    bearerAuth: {type: http, scheme: bearer, bearerFormat: JWT}
    oauth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        clientCredentials:
          tokenUrl: https://idp.kestrel.internal/oauth2/token
          scopes:
            flags:read: Read flags
            flags:write: Create/modify flags
            models:deploy: Deploy model versions
            regions:failover: "Break-glass: fail a region over"
  parameters:
    FlagKey:
      name: flagKey
      in: path
      required: true
      schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[a-z0-9]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+$'}
      example: gateway.apq-enforce
    Cursor: {name: cursor, in: query, schema: {type: string}}
    Limit: {name: limit, in: query, schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 500, default: 50}}
  schemas:
    Flag:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/FlagCreate'
        - type: object
          required: [state, created_at]
          properties:
            state: {type: string, enum: [ ENABLED, DISABLED, ARCHIVED ]}
            created_at: {type: string, format: date-time, example: "2024-10-21T09:14:00Z"}
            rollout:
              type: object
              properties:
                percentage: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100, example: 12.5}
                by_region:
                  type: object
                  additionalProperties: {type: number}
                  example: {us-east-1: 25, eu-west-1: 0, ap-southeast-2: 25}
    FlagCreate:
      type: object
      required: [key, kind, variants, default_variant]
      properties:
        key: {type: string, example: gateway.query-planner-v2}
        description: {type: string, maxLength: 500}
        kind: {type: string, enum: [boolean, string, number, json]}
        variants:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
          example: {"on": true, "off": false}
        default_variant: {type: string, example: "off"}
        targeting:
          type: object
          nullable: true
          description: JsonLogic rule evaluated by flagd. Must be valid JsonLogic -- the admin API runs it against a sample context before saving and rejects rules that throw.
    RolloutChange:
      type: object
      required: [percentage]
      properties:
        percentage: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100}
        regions: {type: array, items: {type: string, enum: [us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-2]}, description: "Empty = all regions"}
        bake_minutes: {type: integer, default: 15}
        reason: {type: string}
    Operation:
      type: object
      properties: {id: {type: string, format: uuid}, status: {type: string, enum: [pending, running, succeeded, failed, rolled_back]}}
    Problem: {type: object, properties: {type: {type: string, format: uri, default: "about:blank"}, title: {type: string}, status: {type: integer, example: 422}}}

Back it up first if you have hand-edited contexts: > ```sh > cp ~/.kube/config ~/.kube/config.bak.$(date +%s) > ``` > Restore it with `mv` if anything looks off. ## Repository layout | Path | What | Owner | |---|---|---| | `deploy/charts/` | Helm charts (gateway, flagd, model-sync) | platform-sre | | `deploy/k8s/` | Raw manifests that haven't been chart-ified yet :grimacing: | platform-sre | | `services/gateway/`| Router config + Rust plugins (auth, cost limits, persisted queries) | [gateway team](https://github.com/orgs/kestrel/teams/gateway) | `services/flags-sync/` | LaunchDarkly → flagd sync job (deprecated, see [ADR-014](docs/adr/014-flagd.md)) | platform-sre | `ml/serving/` | KServe `InferenceService` specs + Triton `config.pbtxt` files | ml-infra | | `tools/rollout/` |`rollout.py`, the CLI for progressive flag rollouts| platform-sre | Region | Role | Cluster | Notes --- | :---: | --- | --- us-east-1 | primary + canary | `prod-use1-blue` | gets every gateway and flag change first eu-west-1 | primary (EU data) | `prod-euw1-blue` | see the [INC-2291 post-mortem]( "Gateway brownout, Oct 2024") ap-southeast-2 | secondary | `prod-apse2-a` | no GPU nodes yet; inference falls back to us-east-1 (~180ms extra) ## Running the *gateway* locally with `make dev` The gateway reads `services/gateway/router.yaml` plus a composed supergraph. When you change a subgraph schema you have to recompose before restarting, otherwise the router happily keeps serving the old schema and you will lose an afternoon like I did. ```yaml # services/gateway/router.local.yaml -- overrides for laptops supergraph: listen: 127.0.0.1:4000 introspection: True headers: all: request: - propagate: {matching: "^x-kestrel-.*"} include_subgraph_errors: { all: true } ``` Restart with Ctrl+C and `make dev` again; hot reload only watches `router.yaml`, not the supergraph. ## Feature flags Flags live in `flags/flags.yaml` and are served by [flagd] in every region. The `flags-lint` job evaluates the JsonLogic rules against a sample context and posts a diff of the evaluated variants for ~2k synthetic users. 3. After merge flagd picks up the change within ~30s * staging first, then the canary region, then the rest * need it faster? `kubectl -n flags rollout restart deploy/flagd` -- but not during business hours please | Region | Gateway p99 | Flag eval p99 | |----------------|------------:|--------------:| | us-east-1 | 182 ms | 1.9 ms | | eu-west-1 | 240 ms | 2.4 ms | | ap-southeast-2 | 311 ms | 3.1 ms | * numbers from the October load test, pasted into the quarterly deck as-is, please don't reformat ## Runbooks ## - [Gateway: restart / drain](docs/runbooks/gateway/restart.md) - [Gateway: subgraph timeouts]() - [Flags: flagd returns defaults everywhere](docs/runbooks/flags.md#everything-is-default "the scary one") - [GPU nodes stuck `NotReady`](docs/runbooks/gpu-notready.md) The gateway enforces persisted queries in production[^apq] and a per-operation cost limit[^cost]. If you see `PERSISTED_QUERY_NOT_IN_LIST` in staging, that is a client bug, not ours.
Why no service mesh for the gateway? We tried Istio in 2023. Short version: an extra hop, ~4ms of p50, and a sidecar that OOMed under the query-planner warmup. Details in [ADR-009](docs/adr/009-no-mesh-for-gateway.md).
## Roadmap (Q4) - [x] Persisted queries enforced on the public gateway - [x] KServe 0.13 upgrade - [ ] Delete the LaunchDarkly sync job :skull: - [ ] ap-southeast-2 GPU pool - [ ] quota request for `g5` instances - [X] Triton model warmup on scale-up - [ ] Active-active writes for the flags DB (needs an ADR first) Contributing ------------ Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first. TL;DR: small PRs, a ticket number in the title, and never `kubectl edit` in prod without writing it down in the incident channel. More background reading: the [Apollo Router docs][router], [flagd][], and the [KServe docs][kserve] (we use `RawDeployment` mode, so ignore everything about Knative). [router]: https://www.apollographql.com/docs/router/ "Apollo Router" [flagd]: https://flagd.dev/ [kserve]: 'KServe documentation' [^apq]: Automatic persisted queries are still allowed in staging so that Apollo Studio Explorer keeps working. In prod the router rejects unknown hashes. [^cost]: Cost is estimated from the static query plan, not measured at runtime. See `services/gateway/plugins/cost_limit.rs` if you want to argue about the weights.

                                city: Αθήνα}]
date: 2026-11-24

lang: de
format:
  html:
    toc:   true
    toc-title: Inhalt
    number-sections: True
    code-fold: show
    theme: [cosmo, styles/stat1010.scss]
    html-math-method: katex
  revealjs:
    slide-number: c/t
    incremental:   false
    footer: "STAT 1010 · Konfidenzintervalle"
    chalkboard: {buttons: false}

abstract: Wir konstruieren Konfidenzintervalle für den Erwartungswert, simulieren ihre Überdeckungswahrscheinlichkeit und üben die korrekte Interpretation, die in Klausuren erfahrungsgemäß die meisten Punkte kostet.
---

{{< include _kopf-hinweise.qmd >}}

## Lernziele {.unnumbered}

Nach dieser Woche könnt ihr

- ein Konfidenzintervall für den Erwartungswert $\mu$ berechnen und *richtig* interpretieren,
- entscheiden, wann die $t$-Verteilung statt der Normalverteilung nötig ist, und
-   die Breite eines Intervalls über den Stichprobenumfang $n$ steuern.

::: {.callout-note}
## Hinweis / Note
Die Folien gibt es auch als PDF (Menü → *Download*). Les étudiant·e·s Erasmus trouveront un résumé en français à la fin du document; los estudiantes de intercambio encontrarán un resumen en español justo después.
:::

## Motivation {#sec-motivation}

In Woche 6 haben wir gesehen, dass der Stichprobenmittelwert $\bar{x}$ ein erwartungstreuer Schätzer für $\mu$ ist. Aber wie *genau* ist er? Ein einzelner Punktschätzer sagt nichts über die Unsicherheit aus. Ein Konfidenzintervall gibt einen Bereich an, der bei wiederholter Stichprobenziehung in $(1-\alpha) \cdot 100\,\%$ der Fälle den wahren Parameter überdeckt [@neyman1937; @wasserman2004, Kap. 6].

Für normalverteilte Daten mit unbekannter Varianz lautet das Intervall

$$
\bar{x} \pm t_{n-1,\,1-\alpha/2} \cdot \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}
$$ {#eq-ki-t}

Dabei ist $t_{n-1,\,1-\alpha/2}$ das $(1-\alpha/2)$-Quantil der $t$-Verteilung mit $n-1$ Freiheitsgraden (siehe @tbl-quantile). Für großes $n$ nähert sich dieses Quantil dem Normalquantil $z_{1-\alpha/2} \approx 1{,}96$ an.[^tabelle]

![Dichte der $t$-Verteilung für $\nu = 1, 5, 30$ Freiheitsgrade im Vergleich zur Standardnormalverteilung (gestrichelt).](abbildungen/t-dichte.svg){#fig-t-dichte fig-alt="Vier Glockenkurven; die t-Verteilungen mit wenigen Freiheitsgraden haben schwerere Ränder als die gestrichelte Normalverteilung." width="80%"}

| $\nu$ | $t_{\nu;\,0{,}95}$ | $t_{\nu;\,0{,}975}$ | $t_{\nu;\,0{,}995}$ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 5 | 2,015 | 2,571 | 4,032 |
| 10 | 1,812 | 2,228 | 3,169 |
| 29 | 1,699 | 2,045 | 2,756 |
| $\infty$ | 1,645 | 1,960 | 2,576 |

: Ausgewählte Quantile der $t$-Verteilung {#tbl-quantile}

## Simulation: Was heißt „95 %“?

```{r}
#| label: fig-ki-sim
#| fig-cap: 'Hundert simulierte 95 %-Konfidenzintervalle; rot: Intervalle, die $\mu = 170$ verfehlen.'
#| fig-alt: "Horizontale Linien für 100 Intervalle um eine senkrechte Linie bei 170 cm; etwa fünf davon sind rot und berühren die Linie nicht."
#| fig-width:   8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| code-fold:  true
#| echo:  TRUE
#| cache: true
set.seed(1010)
n <- 30; mu <- 170; sigma <- 8
ki <- t(replicate(100, {
  x <- rnorm(n, mu, sigma)
  mean(x) + c(-1, 1) * qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * sd(x) / sqrt(n)
}))
trifft <- ki[, 1] <= mu & mu <= ki[, 2]
plot(NULL, xlim = range(ki), ylim = c(1, 100), xlab = "Körpergröße [cm]", ylab = "Simulation")
segments(ki[, 1], 1:100, ki[, 2], 1:100, col = ifelse(trifft, "grey40", "firebrick"))
abline(v = mu, lty = 2)
```

In @fig-ki-sim verfehlen `r sum(!trifft)` von 100 Intervallen den wahren Wert;   im Mittel wären es fünf. Wie breit ein Intervall ist, hängt vor allem von $n$ ab:

```{r ki-breite, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.5, fig.cap="Breite des Intervalls in Abhängigkeit von n"}
n <- 5:200
plot(n, 2 * qt(0.975, n - 1) * 8 / sqrt(n), type = "l", xlab = "n", ylab = "Breite [cm]")
```

::: {.notes}
Hier unbedingt die Simulation live zeigen und *vorher* fragen, wie viele rote Intervalle das Publikum erwartet. Dauer: ca. 10 min.
:::

## Übungen

::: {#exr-mensa}
## Mensa-Wartezeiten
An $n = 25$ zufällig gewählten Tagen wurden die Wartezeiten in der Mensa gemessen: $\bar{x} = 7{,}4$ Minuten, $s = 2{,}1$ Minuten.

1. Berechne ein 95 %-Konfidenzintervall für die mittlere Wartezeit.
2. Wie ändert sich die Breite, wenn man $n$ vervierfacht?
Begründe ohne zu rechnen.
3. Interpretiere das Intervall in **einem** Satz, ohne das Wort „Wahrscheinlichkeit“ zu benutzen.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Lösung zu @exr-mensa
Mit $t_{24;\,0{,}975} \approx 2{,}064$ ergibt sich $7{,}4 \pm 2{,}064 \cdot 2{,}1/5$, also etwa $[6{,}53;\ 8{,}27]$ Minuten.
Bei vierfachem $n$ halbiert sich die Breite, weil $\sqrt{4} = 2$.
:::

::: {#exr-bootstrap}
## Bootstrap (freiwillig) 🧪
Vergleiche das $t$-Intervall aus @eq-ki-t mit einem Perzentil-Bootstrap-Intervall für die Daten aus `koerpergroessen.csv`. Was fällt dir bei schiefen Daten auf, z.B. bei den Mieten aus Lab 2?
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```{r}
#| label: ki-r
#| eval: false
groesse <- read.csv("daten/koerpergroessen.csv")$groesse
t.test(groesse, conf.level = 0.95)$conf.int
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: ki-py
#| eval:   false
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
groesse = pd.read_csv("daten/koerpergroessen.csv")["groesse"]
stats.t.interval(0.95, df=len(groesse)-1, loc=groesse.mean(), scale=stats.sem(groesse))
```
:::

## Interpretation

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Häufiger Fehler** ❌

„Mit 95 % Wahrscheinlichkeit liegt $\mu$ im Intervall $[6{,}53;\ 8{,}27]$.“
Nach der Datenerhebung ist das Intervall fest – $\mu$ liegt drin oder eben nicht.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Richtig** ✅

„Das Verfahren liefert in 95 % aller Wiederholungen ein Intervall, das $\mu$ enthält.“
Die Wahrscheinlichkeit bezieht sich auf das *Verfahren*, nicht auf ein einzelnes Intervall.^[Bayesianische Kredibilitätsintervalle erlauben dagegen genau diese Aussage, setzen aber eine Prior-Verteilung voraus; mehr dazu in STAT 2020.]
:::
::::

<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->
+----------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Situation                  | Intervall                                |
+============================+==========================================+
| $\sigma$ bekannt           | $\bar{x} \pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\,\sigma/\sqrt{n}$ |
+----------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| $\sigma$ unbekannt, Daten  | $\bar{x} \pm t_{n-1}\,s/\sqrt{n}$         |
| ungefähr normalverteilt    |                                          |
+----------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| schiefe Daten, kleines $n$ | Bootstrap oder Transformation            |
+----------------------------+------------------------------------------+

> **Hinweis:** In der Klausur reicht es, das passende Intervall zu *begründen*; die Rechnung selbst gibt nur die Hälfte der Punkte.

## Résumé en français {.unnumbered lang="fr"}

Un intervalle de confiance à 95 % n'est pas un intervalle qui contient $\mu$ « avec une probabilité de 95 % » : c'est la *procédure* qui, répétée sur de nombreux échantillons, produit des intervalles contenant $\mu$ dans 95 % des cas. Pour de petits échantillons ($n < 30$), on utilise la loi de Student.

## Resumen en español {.unnumbered lang="es"}

Un intervalo de confianza del 95 % no significa que $\mu$ esté dentro «con probabilidad 0,95». Significa que el *procedimiento* acierta en el 95 % de las repeticiones. Con muestras pequeñas usamos la distribución $t$ de Student; con muestras grandes, la normal.

## 日本語の要約 {.unnumbered lang="ja"}

95 %信頼区間とは、同じ手順で何度も標本を取ったときに、そのうち約95 %の区間が真の平均 $\mu$ を含む、という意味です。一つの区間について「$\mu$ が95 %の確率で含まれる」とは言えません。

[^tabelle]: Die vollständige Tabelle steht im Anhang des Skripts. In der Klausur gibt es eine Formelsammlung mit den wichtigsten Quantilen; Taschenrechner sind erlaubt, Handys natürlich nicht.

## Literatur {.unnumbered}

::: {#refs}
:::

abstract: Wir konstruieren Konfidenzintervalle für den Erwartungswert, simulieren ihre Überdeckungswahrscheinlichkeit und üben die korrekte Interpretation, die in Klausuren erfahrungsgemäß die meisten Punkte kostet.
---

{{< include _kopf-hinweise.qmd >}}

## Lernziele {.unnumbered}

Nach dieser Woche könnt ihr

- ein Konfidenzintervall für den Erwartungswert $\mu$ berechnen und *richtig* interpretieren,
- entscheiden, wann die $t$-Verteilung statt der Normalverteilung nötig ist, und
-   die Breite eines Intervalls über den Stichprobenumfang $n$ steuern.

::: {.callout-note}
## Hinweis / Note
Die Folien gibt es auch als PDF (Menü → *Download*). Les étudiant·e·s Erasmus trouveront un résumé en français à la fin du document; los estudiantes de intercambio encontrarán un resumen en español justo después.
:::

## Motivation {#sec-motivation}

In Woche 6 haben wir gesehen, dass der Stichprobenmittelwert $\bar{x}$ ein erwartungstreuer Schätzer für $\mu$ ist. Aber wie *genau* ist er? Ein einzelner Punktschätzer sagt nichts über die Unsicherheit aus. Ein Konfidenzintervall gibt einen Bereich an, der bei wiederholter Stichprobenziehung in $(1-\alpha) \cdot 100\,\%$ der Fälle den wahren Parameter überdeckt [@neyman1937; @wasserman2004, Kap. 6].

Für normalverteilte Daten mit unbekannter Varianz lautet das Intervall

$$
\bar{x} \pm t_{n-1,\,1-\alpha/2} \cdot \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}
$$ {#eq-ki-t}

Dabei ist $t_{n-1,\,1-\alpha/2}$ das $(1-\alpha/2)$-Quantil der $t$-Verteilung mit $n-1$ Freiheitsgraden (siehe @tbl-quantile). Für großes $n$ nähert sich dieses Quantil dem Normalquantil $z_{1-\alpha/2} \approx 1{,}96$ an.[^tabelle]

![Dichte der $t$-Verteilung für $\nu = 1, 5, 30$ Freiheitsgrade im Vergleich zur Standardnormalverteilung (gestrichelt).](abbildungen/t-dichte.svg){#fig-t-dichte fig-alt="Vier Glockenkurven; die t-Verteilungen mit wenigen Freiheitsgraden haben schwerere Ränder als die gestrichelte Normalverteilung." width="80%"}

| $\nu$ | $t_{\nu;\,0{,}95}$ | $t_{\nu;\,0{,}975}$ | $t_{\nu;\,0{,}995}$ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 5 | 2,015 | 2,571 | 4,032 |
| 10 | 1,812 | 2,228 | 3,169 |
| 29 | 1,699 | 2,045 | 2,756 |
| $\infty$ | 1,645 | 1,960 | 2,576 |

: Ausgewählte Quantile der $t$-Verteilung {#tbl-quantile}

## Simulation: Was heißt „95 %“?

```{r}
#| label: fig-ki-sim
#| fig-cap: 'Hundert simulierte 95 %-Konfidenzintervalle; rot: Intervalle, die $\mu = 170$ verfehlen.'
#| fig-alt: "Horizontale Linien für 100 Intervalle um eine senkrechte Linie bei 170 cm; etwa fünf davon sind rot und berühren die Linie nicht."
#| fig-width:   8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| code-fold:  true
#| echo:  TRUE
#| cache: true
set.seed(1010)
n <- 30; mu <- 170; sigma <- 8
ki <- t(replicate(100, {
  x <- rnorm(n, mu, sigma)
  mean(x) + c(-1, 1) * qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * sd(x) / sqrt(n)
}))
trifft <- ki[, 1] <= mu & mu <= ki[, 2]
plot(NULL, xlim = range(ki), ylim = c(1, 100), xlab = "Körpergröße [cm]", ylab = "Simulation")
segments(ki[, 1], 1:100, ki[, 2], 1:100, col = ifelse(trifft, "grey40", "firebrick"))
abline(v = mu, lty = 2)
```

In @fig-ki-sim verfehlen `r sum(!trifft)` von 100 Intervallen den wahren Wert;   im Mittel wären es fünf. Wie breit ein Intervall ist, hängt vor allem von $n$ ab:

```{r ki-breite, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.5, fig.cap="Breite des Intervalls in Abhängigkeit von n"}
n <- 5:200
plot(n, 2 * qt(0.975, n - 1) * 8 / sqrt(n), type = "l", xlab = "n", ylab = "Breite [cm]")
```

::: {.notes}
Hier unbedingt die Simulation live zeigen und *vorher* fragen, wie viele rote Intervalle das Publikum erwartet. Dauer: ca. 10 min.
:::

## Übungen

::: {#exr-mensa}
## Mensa-Wartezeiten
An $n = 25$ zufällig gewählten Tagen wurden die Wartezeiten in der Mensa gemessen: $\bar{x} = 7{,}4$ Minuten, $s = 2{,}1$ Minuten.

1. Berechne ein 95 %-Konfidenzintervall für die mittlere Wartezeit.
2. Wie ändert sich die Breite, wenn man $n$ vervierfacht?
Begründe ohne zu rechnen.
3. Interpretiere das Intervall in **einem** Satz, ohne das Wort „Wahrscheinlichkeit“ zu benutzen.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Lösung zu @exr-mensa
Mit $t_{24;\,0{,}975} \approx 2{,}064$ ergibt sich $7{,}4 \pm 2{,}064 \cdot 2{,}1/5$, also etwa $[6{,}53;\ 8{,}27]$ Minuten.
Bei vierfachem $n$ halbiert sich die Breite, weil $\sqrt{4} = 2$.
:::

::: {#exr-bootstrap}
## Bootstrap (freiwillig) 🧪
Vergleiche das $t$-Intervall aus @eq-ki-t mit einem Perzentil-Bootstrap-Intervall für die Daten aus `koerpergroessen.csv`. Was fällt dir bei schiefen Daten auf, z.B. bei den Mieten aus Lab 2?
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```{r}
#| label: ki-r
#| eval: false
groesse <- read.csv("daten/koerpergroessen.csv")$groesse
t.test(groesse, conf.level = 0.95)$conf.int
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: ki-py
#| eval:   false
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
groesse = pd.read_csv("daten/koerpergroessen.csv")["groesse"]
stats.t.interval(0.95, df=len(groesse)-1, loc=groesse.mean(), scale=stats.sem(groesse))
```
:::

## Interpretation

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Häufiger Fehler** ❌

„Mit 95 % Wahrscheinlichkeit liegt $\mu$ im Intervall $[6{,}53;\ 8{,}27]$.“
Nach der Datenerhebung ist das Intervall fest – $\mu$ liegt drin oder eben nicht.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Richtig** ✅

„Das Verfahren liefert in 95 % aller Wiederholungen ein Intervall, das $\mu$ enthält.“
Die Wahrscheinlichkeit bezieht sich auf das *Verfahren*, nicht auf ein einzelnes Intervall.^[Bayesianische Kredibilitätsintervalle erlauben dagegen genau diese Aussage, setzen aber eine Prior-Verteilung voraus; mehr dazu in STAT 2020.]
:::
::::

<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->
+----------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Situation                  | Intervall                                |
+============================+==========================================+
| $\sigma$ bekannt           | $\bar{x} \pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\,\sigma/\sqrt{n}$ |
+----------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| $\sigma$ unbekannt, Daten  | $\bar{x} \pm t_{n-1}\,s/\sqrt{n}$         |
| ungefähr normalverteilt    |                                          |
+----------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| schiefe Daten, kleines $n$ | Bootstrap oder Transformation            |
+----------------------------+------------------------------------------+

> **Hinweis:** In der Klausur reicht es, das passende Intervall zu *begründen*; die Rechnung selbst gibt nur die Hälfte der Punkte.

## Résumé en français {.unnumbered lang="fr"}

Un intervalle de confiance à 95 % n'est pas un intervalle qui contient $\mu$ « avec une probabilité de 95 % » : c'est la *procédure* qui, répétée sur de nombreux échantillons, produit des intervalles contenant $\mu$ dans 95 % des cas. Pour de petits échantillons ($n < 30$), on utilise la loi de Student.

## Resumen en español {.unnumbered lang="es"}

Un intervalo de confianza del 95 % no significa que $\mu$ esté dentro «con probabilidad 0,95». Significa que el *procedimiento* acierta en el 95 % de las repeticiones. Con muestras pequeñas usamos la distribución $t$ de Student; con muestras grandes, la normal.

## 日本語の要約 {.unnumbered lang="ja"}

95 %信頼区間とは、同じ手順で何度も標本を取ったときに、そのうち約95 %の区間が真の平均 $\mu$ を含む、という意味です。一つの区間について「$\mu$ が95 %の確率で含まれる」とは言えません。

[^tabelle]: Die vollständige Tabelle steht im Anhang des Skripts. In der Klausur gibt es eine Formelsammlung mit den wichtigsten Quantilen; Taschenrechner sind erlaubt, Handys natürlich nicht.

## Literatur {.unnumbered}

::: {#refs}
:::

# Contributing

Thanks for helping keep the platform upright! :wave: This page covers the boring-but-important parts: how to set up, how we name things, what a reviewable PR looks like and how releases go out. It is opinionated because almost every rule here exists because of a specific incident.

## Ground rules

- **Small PRs.** Under ~400 changed lines unless it is generated code. Big refactors get split or get an ADR
first.
- Every PR title starts with a ticket: `PLAT-1234: ...`. Hotfixes during an incident can use the incident id instead (`INC-2291: ...`).
- Don't `kubectl apply` or `kubectl edit` against prod from your laptop. If you absolutely have to (you are the IC, the pipeline is down, etc.) write down every command in the incident channel *as you run it*.
-   Feature flags are not a substitute for a rollback plan.

## Local setup

1. Install the toolchain:
   ```console
   $ brew bundle --file=Brewfile
   $ uv tool install pre-commit && pre-commit install --install-hooks
   ```
2. Log in to AWS SSO (`aws sso login --profile kestrel-dev`) and run `make bootstrap`.
3) Run `make dev` and check that <http://localhost:4000> serves the sandbox.

Pre-commit runs `ruff`, `yamllint`, `helm lint`, `shellcheck` and `yamark format --check`. If a hook rewrites files, just `git add` them and commit again -- that is not a failure.


## Commits and branches

We use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) because the changelog generator depends on it.

| Type | When | Shows up in changelog? |
| ---- | ---- | :---: |
| `feat` | new user-visible behaviour (a new flag kind, a new region) | yes |
| `fix` | bug fixes, including config fixes | yes |
| `perf`|latency / cost improvements, with numbers in the PR description | yes |
| `chore` | deps, CI, tooling | no |
| `revert` | reverting a previous commit (use `git revert`, keep the generated message) | yes |

```text title="example commit message"
fix(gateway): lower subgraph timeout to 2.5s

The 10s default let a single slow subgraph pin every router worker during
INC-2291. 2.5s is above the p99.9 of every subgraph over the last 30 days.

Refs: INC-2291, PLAT-1877
```

## Pull request checklist

Copy this into the PR description if the template didn't load:

- [ ] Ticket id in the title
- [ ] `make test` passes locally
- [ ] Dashboards / alerts updated if you renamed a metric
- [ ] New flags have an `owner` and an `expires` date
- [x] I read this document :)

## Feature flags

> Flags are config, not code. Treat a flag flip like a deploy.
>
> ```yaml
> gateway.query-planner-v2:
>     state: ENABLED
>     owner: gateway-team
>     expires: 2025-01-31
>     variants: {on: true,off: false}
>     defaultVariant: off
> ```

Some rules that came out of the last two quarters of incidents:

* Name flags `<service>.<feature>`, lowercase, kebab-case after the dot.
* Default to `off`. A flag that defaults to `on` is a deploy in disguise
  and has to go through the normal release review.
* Remove flags within two sprints of reaching 100%. The `flags-janitor` bot opens a PR for every flag past its `expires` date; please don't just bump the date.

## Tests

```console
$ make test                       # unit tests, ~2 min
$ pytest tools/rollout -k "ramp and not slow" -q
$ k6 run load/gateway-smoke.js --vus 20 --duration 60s
```

Schema changes need a contract test. The GraphQL type for flags currently looks like this:

```graphql
type Flag { key: ID!  state: FlagState!
    variants: JSON  rollout:Rollout }
```

<!-- fmt: skip -->
| Check          | Where                | Blocking? |
|----------------|----------------------|-----------|
| unit           | GitHub Actions       | yes       |
| schema diff    | `graphql-inspector`  | yes       |
| load smoke     | nightly, staging     | no        |

## Releasing

The gateway chart and `rollout.py` are versioned with SemVer; everything else ships continuously.

1. Merge to `main`. The `build-and-deploy` workflow deploys to staging automatically
2. Cut a release:
    1. `make release VERSION=2.15.0` bumps `Chart.yaml` and moves the changelog entries
    2. push the tag: `git push origin v2.15.0`
3. Approve the prod deployment in the GitHub environment. The canary region goes first; if the error-budget check fails, the workflow rolls back by itself and pings `#platform-sre`.

## Code review expectations

Reviewers try to respond within one business day[^sla]. If your PR blocks an incident follow-up, say so in the title and ping the on-call reviewer directly instead of the whole channel. See the [review guide](<docs/process/code review.md> "How we review") for what we look at.



[^sla]: "Business day" in the reviewer's time zone. We have people in three of them, so a PR opened on Friday afternoon in Sydney may sit until Monday in Dublin.

# Changelog
All notable changes to `kestrel/platform` are documented in this file. The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and the gateway chart plus `rollout.py` adhere to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html); infra-only changes are listed under whichever release they shipped with.



## [Unreleased]
### Added
- `rollout.py ramp --schedule` to ramp a flag on a cron-like schedule instead of babysitting it ([#1501](https://github.com/kestrel/platform/pull/1501))
- ap-southeast-2: GPU node pool behind the `infra.gpu-apse2` flag, scaled to zero until the quota request
lands
### Changed
* Gateway subgraph timeout lowered from 10s to 2.5s (INC-2291 action item 3). If you own a subgraph that legitimately needs longer, talk to us before adding a per-subgraph override.

## [2.14.0] - 2024-11-08
### :boom: Breaking
- The gateway chart no longer creates the `apollo-studio` secret. Create it yourself (or via external-secrets) **before** upgrading:
  ```diff
  - router:
  -   studio:
  -     createSecret: true
  + router:
  +   studio:
  +     existingSecret: apollo-studio
  ```
- `rollout.py` exits with code `3` (was `1`) when a guardrail trips, so CI can tell "rolled back" apart from "crashed".

### Added
- Persisted query enforcement in prod :tada: Unknown operations now get `PERSISTED_QUERY_NOT_IN_LIST` instead of being executed. The safelist is published by the `pq-publish` job on every client release.
- KServe `InferenceService` for `ranker_v7` with canary support, see `ml/serving/ranker-v7.yaml`
- Grafana dashboard *Gateway / Subgraph latency* (uid `gw-subgraph-lat`)
### Fixed
- flagd sidecar no longer crash-loops when the flags ConfigMap is empty during a rolling update (#1466)
- `model-sync` CronJob: `aws s3 sync` used `--delete` against the wrong prefix in ap-southeast-2 and wiped the
  warm cache every 15 minutes. Nobody noticed because there are no GPU nodes there yet. :see_no_evil:
- HPA for the gateway now scales on in-flight requests as well as CPU; CPU alone reacted ~4 min too late during INC-2291[^hpa]

### **Security**
- Bump Apollo Router to `v1.52.0` (upstream advisory: query depth limit bypass via nested fragment spreads)
- Rotate the `PROM_READ_TOKEN` used by the canary analysis job, the old one was printed in a debug log for ~3 days.

## [2.13.2] - 2024-10-24
### Fixed
1. Hotfixes from INC-2291:
    - raise `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` to 45s so in-flight requests drain
    - PDB `minAvailable` 80% (was 50%)
2. Revert "use the new query planner by default" -- it is back behind `gateway.query-planner-v2` at 10%

## [2.13.1] - 2024-10-03
### Changed
- Model sync now uses `--exact-timestamps`. Without it `aws s3 sync` skipped re-uploaded models with the same size, which is exactly what happens when you re-export an ONNX graph with different weights. Lovely.

### Deprecated
The following flags are deprecated and will be removed in **2.16.0**:

| flag | replacement | notes |
|------|-------------|-------|
| `gateway.legacy-auth` | none | removed once mobile 5.x is below 1% of traffic
| `ml.ranker-v6` | `ml.ranker-v7` | |
| `flags.ld-sync-enabled` | – | the LaunchDarkly sync job goes away with it |

## [2.13.0] - 2024-09-19
### Added
+ Multi-region flag evaluation: flagd runs in every region and syncs from the same S3 bucket. Evaluation latency p99 went from 41ms (cross-region call to us-east-1) to under 3ms.
+ Helm values for per-region overrides, e.g.:

  ```yaml
  # deploy/values/eu-west-1.yaml
  router:
      replicas: 8
      env:
        - {name: KESTREL_REGION, value: eu-west-1}
        - {name: DATA_RESIDENCY,   value: "eu"}
  ```

### Changed
- Minimum Kubernetes version is now 1.28.  
- `kestrel-gateway` image is multi-arch (amd64 + arm64); the arm64 nodes in us-east-1 are ~22% cheaper
  for the same throughput, so new node pools default to Graviton.
- Renamed metric `gateway_requests_total` → `router_http_requests_total` to match upstream. Dashboards were updated, your ad-hoc queries were not.


## [2.12.0] - 2024-08-30
_First release tracked in this file._ Earlier history lives in the wiki: <https://wiki.kestrel.internal/platform/history>.

[^hpa]: Measured from the first 5xx alert to the first new pod passing readiness. See the post-mortem, section *Contributing factors*.

lands
### Changed
* Gateway subgraph timeout lowered from 10s to 2.5s (INC-2291 action item 3). If you own a subgraph that legitimately needs longer, talk to us before adding a per-subgraph override.

## [2.14.0] - 2024-11-08
### :boom: Breaking
- The gateway chart no longer creates the `apollo-studio` secret. Create it yourself (or via external-secrets) **before** upgrading:
  ```diff
  - router:
  -   studio:
  -     createSecret: true
  + router:
  +   studio:
  +     existingSecret: apollo-studio
  ```
- `rollout.py` exits with code `3` (was `1`) when a guardrail trips, so CI can tell "rolled back" apart from "crashed".

### Added
- Persisted query enforcement in prod :tada: Unknown operations now get `PERSISTED_QUERY_NOT_IN_LIST` instead of being executed. The safelist is published by the `pq-publish` job on every client release.
- KServe `InferenceService` for `ranker_v7` with canary support, see `ml/serving/ranker-v7.yaml`
- Grafana dashboard *Gateway / Subgraph latency* (uid `gw-subgraph-lat`)
### Fixed
- flagd sidecar no longer crash-loops when the flags ConfigMap is empty during a rolling update (#1466)
- `model-sync` CronJob: `aws s3 sync` used `--delete` against the wrong prefix in ap-southeast-2 and wiped the
  warm cache every 15 minutes. Nobody noticed because there are no GPU nodes there yet. :see_no_evil:
- HPA for the gateway now scales on in-flight requests as well as CPU; CPU alone reacted ~4 min too late during INC-2291[^hpa]

### **Security**
- Bump Apollo Router to `v1.52.0` (upstream advisory: query depth limit bypass via nested fragment spreads)
- Rotate the `PROM_READ_TOKEN` used by the canary analysis job, the old one was printed in a debug log for ~3 days.

### Fixed
1. Hotfixes from INC-2291:
    - raise `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` to 45s so in-flight requests drain
    - PDB `minAvailable` 80% (was 50%)
2. Revert "use the new query planner by default" -- it is back behind `gateway.query-planner-v2` at 10%

### Changed
- Model sync now uses `--exact-timestamps`. Without it `aws s3 sync` skipped re-uploaded models with the same size, which is exactly what happens when you re-export an ONNX graph with different weights. Lovely.

| flag | replacement | notes |
|------|-------------|-------|

## [2.13.0] - 2024-09-19
### Added
+ Multi-region flag evaluation: flagd runs in every region and syncs from the same S3 bucket. Evaluation latency p99 went from 41ms (cross-region call to us-east-1) to under 3ms.
+ Helm values for per-region overrides, e.g.:

  router:
