arguments.content:
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Beacon API
  version: 2.3.0
  summary: Leaderboards, purchase validation and remote config for Lanternfish games & apps
  # fmt: markdown
  description: |
    Beacon is the small backend behind **Glowtide** and **Sprout**. It is deliberately boring: FastAPI, Postgres, Redis, one worker.
    ## Authentication
    Game clients authenticate with a per-install device token (`X-Beacon-Device`) that is issued by `POST /devices` on first launch and stored in the Keychain / EncryptedSharedPreferences.
    Admin endpoints (not listed here) use a short-lived JWT from the studio SSO.
    ## Versioning
    * Breaking changes get a new base path (`/v3`), the old one stays up for at least **two** store releases of every client
    * additive changes (new optional fields, new endpoints) can ship any time

    Rate limits: 60 requests/minute per device, scores are limited separately (see `POST /leaderboards/{board_id}/scores`).
  contact:
    name: Lanternfish backend (Priya, Mira)
    email: backend@lanternfish.studio
    url: https://handbook.lanternfish.studio/beacon/
  license:
    name: Proprietary
    identifier: LicenseRef-Lanternfish-Proprietary
servers:
  # fmt: table
  - {url: 'https://api.lanternfish.studio/v2', description: Production}
  - {url: "https://staging-api.lanternfish.studio/v2", description: Staging (TestFlight + Play internal builds)}
  - {url: http://localhost:8000/v2, description: local docker compose}
tags:
  - name: leaderboards
    description: Weekly and all-time leaderboards for Glowtide
  - name: receipts
    description: App Store / Google Play purchase validation
  - name: config
  - name: devices
    description: Device registration and push tokens (APNs / FCM)
security:
  - deviceToken: []
paths:
  /leaderboards/{board_id}/scores:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/BoardId'
    get:
      tags: [leaderboards]
      operationId: listScores
      summary: Top scores for a board
      # fmt: markdown
      description: "Returns the top `limit` scores, highest first. Ties are broken by submission time (earlier wins). Pass `around_me=true` to get the 5 scores above and below the caller instead of the top of the board; this is what the in-game *Friends & Rivals* panel uses."
      parameters:
        - name: limit
          in: query
          schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, default: 25}
        - name: around_me
          in: query
          required: false
          schema:
            type: boolean
            default: false
        - in: query
          name: season
          description: ISO week of the season, like `2026-W46`. Defaults to the
            current week; ignored for all-time boards.
          schema:
            type: string
            pattern: '^\d{4}-W\d{2}$'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Score"}
              example:
                - {rank: 1, player: tidecaller, score: 98210, submitted_at: 2026-11-16T21:04:11Z}
                - {rank: 2, player: "mossy_bun", score: 97002, submitted_at: "2026-11-16T09:30:00Z"}
        404:
          $ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound'
    post:
      tags: [leaderboards]
      operationId: submitScore
      summary: Submit a score
      description: >
        Scores are validated against the puzzle's `max_score_per_puzzle`
        (remote config) and the replay hash. A device can submit at most
        10 scores per minute and 500 per day.


        Submitting the same `nonce` twice returns the original score with
        `409`, so clients can retry blindly after a timeout.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/ScoreSubmission'
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created
          headers:
            X-RateLimit-Remaining:
              schema: {type: integer}
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Score'}
        "409":
          description: Duplicate nonce, the original score is returned unchanged.
        '422': {$ref: '#/components/responses/ValidationError'}
        "429":
          description: Too many submissions from this device
  /receipts/apple:
    post:
      tags: [receipts]
      operationId: validateAppleTransaction
      summary: Validate an App Store transaction (StoreKit 2)
      # fmt: markdown
      description: |
        Send the **signed transaction** (JWS) from `Transaction.currentEntitlements`, not the old app receipt.
        Beacon verifies the signature chain against Apple's root certificate and then asks the App Store Server API for the current status, so refunds and revocations are picked up even if the client is offline when they happen.

        The legacy `verifyReceipt` endpoint is deprecated by Apple and **not** supported.
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [signed_transaction]
              properties:
                signed_transaction: {type: string, description: JWS from StoreKit 2}

  title: Beacon API
  version: 2.3.0
  summary: Leaderboards, purchase validation and remote config for Lanternfish games & apps
  # fmt: markdown
  description: |
    Beacon is the small backend behind **Glowtide** and **Sprout**. It is deliberately boring: FastAPI, Postgres, Redis, one worker.

    Game clients authenticate with a per-install device token (`X-Beacon-Device`) that is issued by `POST /devices` on first launch and stored in the Keychain / EncryptedSharedPreferences.

    * Breaking changes get a new base path (`/v3`), the old one stays up for at least **two** store releases of every client
    * additive changes (new optional fields, new endpoints) can ship any time

      parameters:

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: larch Compute Gateway API
  version: "2.3.0"
  summary: Submit and monitor Slurm jobs on the larch cluster from science gateways and workflow engines.
  # fmt: markdown
  description: |
    The Compute Gateway lets **trusted science gateways** (Galaxy, the Northfield JupyterHub, Nextflow Tower) submit Slurm batch jobs on behalf of a user without that user ever handing over an SSH key. Every request carries an OAuth 2.0 access token issued to the *gateway*; the `X-Larch-On-Behalf-Of` header names the end user, who must have authorised the gateway once at <https://hpc.northfield.ac.uk/gateways>.

    ## Limits

    | Limit | Value | Notes |
    |---|---|---|
    | Requests per minute per gateway | 600 | `429` with `Retry-After` when exceeded |
    | Pending jobs per user via the gateway | 2,000 | an array counts as one job per task |
    | Max. script size | 64 KiB | |

    Job scripts are passed to `sbatch` **unchanged**, so `#SBATCH` lines in the script win over fields in the request body -- except `account` and `partition`, which the gateway always enforces (cf. the [RCS acceptable use policy](https://hpc.northfield.ac.uk/docs/policies/aup/)).
  contact:
    name: Research Computing Services
    email: rcs-help@northfield.ac.uk
    url: https://hpc.northfield.ac.uk/docs/
  license: {name: Apache 2.0, identifier: Apache-2.0}

servers: # fmt: table
  - {url: "https://gateway.hpc.northfield.ac.uk/v2", description: Production (larch)}
  - {url: https://gateway-staging.hpc.northfield.ac.uk/v2, description: "Staging, talks to the 8-node test partition"}
  - {url: 'http://localhost:8080/v2', description: Local dev}

tags:
  - name: Cluster
  - name: Jobs
    description: Submission, state and cancellation.
  - {name: Accounting, description: Usage and fairshare}

security:
  - gatewayOAuth: [jobs:submit, jobs:read]

paths:
  /partitions:
    get:
      operationId: listPartitions
      tags: [Cluster]
      summary: List partitions visible to the user
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/OnBehalfOf'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Partitions with current availability.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Partition"}
        "401": {$ref: '#/components/responses/Unauthorized'}

  /jobs:
    post:
      operationId: submitJob
      tags: [Jobs]
      summary: Submit a batch job
      # fmt: markdown
      description: >-
        Submits `script` with `sbatch --parsable`. The response is returned as soon as Slurm has accepted the job, i.e. **before** it starts; poll `GET /jobs/{jobId}` or, better, register a `callbackUrl` and the gateway will POST the final state to it.

        Array jobs: set `array` to a Slurm index expression such as `0-99%10`. Each task is then addressable as `{jobId}_{taskId}`.
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/OnBehalfOf'
        - name: Idempotency-Key
          in: header
          required: false
          description: Re-sending a request with the same key within 24 h returns the original job instead of submitting a duplicate.
          schema: {type: string, format: uuid}
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/JobSubmission'}
            examples:
              gromacs:
                summary: 4-node GROMACS run
                value:
                  name: lysozyme-npt
                  account: chem-md-2026
                  partition: short
                  nodes: 4
                  ntasksPerNode: 64
                  timeLimit: "02:00:00"
                  script: |
                    #!/bin/bash
                    module load gromacs/2024.3-ompi
                    srun gmx_mpi mdrun -deffnm npt -maxh 1.9
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Accepted by Slurm.
          headers:
            Location: {schema: {type: string, format: uri}, description: URL of the new job resource}
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Job'}
        '400': {$ref: '#/components/responses/Problem'}
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Problem'
      x-codeSamples:
        - lang: Python
          label: requests
          # fmt: python
          source: |
            import os, requests
            tok=os.environ["LARCH_TOKEN"]
            r=requests.post("https://gateway.hpc.northfield.ac.uk/v2/jobs",headers={"Authorization":f"Bearer {tok}","X-Larch-On-Behalf-Of":"abc123"},json={"name":"test","account":"chem-md-2026","script":"#!/bin/bash\nhostname\n"},timeout=30)
            r.raise_for_status(); print(r.json()["jobId"])
        - lang: Shell
          label: curl
          source: |
            curl -sS -X POST "$LARCH_GATEWAY/v2/jobs" \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $LARCH_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d @job.json

  /jobs/{jobId}:
    parameters:
      - name: jobId
        in: path
        required: true
        description: Slurm job ID, or `<arrayJobId>_<taskId>` for an array task.
        schema:
          type: string
          pattern: '^\d+(_\d+)?$'
          examples: ["4815162", 4815162_42]
    get:
      operationId: getJob
      tags: [Jobs]
      summary: Job state and accounting
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Job'}
        '404': {$ref: '#/components/responses/Problem'}
    delete:
      operationId: cancelJob
      tags: [Jobs]
      summary: Cancel (scancel) a job
      parameters:
        - in: query
          name: signal
          schema: {type: string, enum: [TERM, KILL, USR1, USR2], default: TERM}
      responses:
        '202': {description: Signal sent.}
        '409':
          description: Job already finished.

  /usage/{account}:
    get:
      operationId: getUsage
      tags: [Accounting]
      summary: Core-hour usage and fairshare for a Slurm account
      # fmt: markdown
      description: |
        Returns raw usage in core-hours (GPU-hours are reported separately and weighted ×4 in the billing TRES) and the account's current fairshare factor, computed with Slurm's classic algorithm as

        $$F = 2^{-U_{\mathrm{eff}}/S_{\mathrm{norm}}}$$

        where $U_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective (decayed, half-life 14 days) usage and $S_{\mathrm{norm}}$ the normalised shares. A value of `0.5` means the account has used exactly its share; values near `0` mean jobs from this account wait behind everybody else's.
      parameters:
        - {name: account, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,31}$'}}
        - name: since
          in: query
          schema: {type: string, format: date}
          example: 2026-10-01
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Usage summary.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Usage'}

components:
  securitySchemes:
    gatewayOAuth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        clientCredentials:
          tokenUrl: https://login.northfield.ac.uk/realms/hpc/protocol/openid-connect/token
          scopes:
            jobs:submit: Submit jobs on behalf of authorised users
            jobs:read: Read job state and output
            'usage:read': Read accounting data
  parameters:
    OnBehalfOf:
      name: X-Larch-On-Behalf-Of
      in: header
      required: true
      description: Northfield username (`abc123`) of the end user.
      schema: {type: string, pattern: "^[a-z]{3}[0-9]{3}$"}
  responses:
    Unauthorized:
      description: Missing or expired token.
    Problem:
      description: RFC 9457 problem details.
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'}
  schemas:
    JobState:
      type: string
      enum: [PENDING, RUNNING, COMPLETING, COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, TIMEOUT, OUT_OF_MEMORY, NODE_FAIL, PREEMPTED]
    JobSubmission:
      type: object
      required: [name, account, script]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        name: {type: string, maxLength: 128}
        account: {type: string}
        partition: {type: string, default: short}
        nodes: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 64, default: 1}
        ntasksPerNode: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 192}
        gpusPerNode:
          type: integer
          minimum: 0
          maximum: 4
          default: 0
        timeLimit:
          type: string
          description: Slurm time format, `[days-]hours:minutes:seconds`.
          pattern: '^(\d+-)?\d{1,2}:\d{2}:\d{2}$'
          default: "01:00:00"
        array: {type: [string, 'null'], examples: ["0-99%10", "1,3,5-7"]}
        callbackUrl: {type: [string, "null"], format: uri}
        script: {type: string, maxLength: 65536}
    Job:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/JobSubmission'
        - type: object
          required: [jobId, state]
          properties:
            jobId: {type: string, readOnly: true}
            state: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/JobState'}
            submitTime: {type: string, format: date-time}
            startTime: {type: [string, 'null'], format: date-time}
            exitCode: {type: [integer, 'null'], examples: [0, 137]}
            efficiency:
              type: object
              description: CPU and memory efficiency as reported by `seff`, in percent.
              properties:
                cpu: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100}
                memory: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 1.0e+2}
    Partition:
      type: object
      properties:
        name: {type: string}
        idleNodes: {type: integer}
        maxTime: {type: string, examples: ["7-00:00:00"]}
        gres: {type: array, items: {type: string}, examples: [[ "gpu:a100:4" ]]}
    Usage:
      type: object
      properties:
        coreHours: {type: number}
        gpuHours: {type: number}
        fairshare: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 1}
    Problem:
      type: object
      properties:
        type: {type: string, format: uri, default: about:blank}
        title: {type: string}
        status: {type: integer}
        detail: {type: string}

  /jobs:
    post:
      operationId: submitJob
      tags: [Jobs]
      summary: Submit a batch job
      # fmt: markdown
      description: >-
        Submits `script` with `sbatch --parsable`. The response is returned as soon as Slurm has accepted the job, i.e. **before** it starts; poll `GET /jobs/{jobId}` or, better, register a `callbackUrl` and the gateway will POST the final state to it.

        Array jobs: set `array` to a Slurm index expression such as `0-99%10`. Each task is then addressable as `{jobId}_{taskId}`.
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/OnBehalfOf'
        - name: Idempotency-Key
          in: header
          required: false
          description: Re-sending a request with the same key within 24 h returns the original job instead of submitting a duplicate.
          schema: {type: string, format: uuid}
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/JobSubmission'}
            examples:
              gromacs:
                summary: 4-node GROMACS run
                value:
                  name: lysozyme-npt
                  account: chem-md-2026
                  partition: short
                  nodes: 4
                  ntasksPerNode: 64
                  timeLimit: "02:00:00"
                  script: |
                    #!/bin/bash
                    module load gromacs/2024.3-ompi
                    srun gmx_mpi mdrun -deffnm npt -maxh 1.9
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Accepted by Slurm.
          headers:
            Location: {schema: {type: string, format: uri}, description: URL of the new job resource}
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Job'}
        '400': {$ref: '#/components/responses/Problem'}
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Problem'
      x-codeSamples:
        - lang: Python
          label: requests
          # fmt: python
          source: |
            import os, requests
            tok=os.environ["LARCH_TOKEN"]
            r=requests.post("https://gateway.hpc.northfield.ac.uk/v2/jobs",headers={"Authorization":f"Bearer {tok}","X-Larch-On-Behalf-Of":"abc123"},json={"name":"test","account":"chem-md-2026","script":"#!/bin/bash\nhostname\n"},timeout=30)
            r.raise_for_status(); print(r.json()["jobId"])
        - lang: Shell
          label: curl
          source: |
            curl -sS -X POST "$LARCH_GATEWAY/v2/jobs" \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $LARCH_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d @job.json

  /jobs/{jobId}:
    parameters:
      - name: jobId
        in: path
        required: true
        description: Slurm job ID, or `<arrayJobId>_<taskId>` for an array task.
        schema:
          type: string
          pattern: '^\d+(_\d+)?$'
          examples: ["4815162", 4815162_42]
    get:
      operationId: getJob
      tags: [Jobs]
      summary: Job state and accounting
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Job'}
        '404': {$ref: '#/components/responses/Problem'}
    delete:
      operationId: cancelJob
      tags: [Jobs]
      summary: Cancel (scancel) a job
      parameters:
        - in: query
          name: signal
          schema: {type: string, enum: [TERM, KILL, USR1, USR2], default: TERM}
      responses:
        '202': {description: Signal sent.}
        '409':
          description: Job already finished.

  /usage/{account}:
    get:
      operationId: getUsage
      tags: [Accounting]
      summary: Core-hour usage and fairshare for a Slurm account
      # fmt: markdown
      description: |
        Returns raw usage in core-hours (GPU-hours are reported separately and weighted ×4 in the billing TRES) and the account's current fairshare factor, computed with Slurm's classic algorithm as

        $$F = 2^{-U_{\mathrm{eff}}/S_{\mathrm{norm}}}$$

        where $U_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective (decayed, half-life 14 days) usage and $S_{\mathrm{norm}}$ the normalised shares. A value of `0.5` means the account has used exactly its share; values near `0` mean jobs from this account wait behind everybody else's.
      parameters:
        - {name: account, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,31}$'}}
        - name: since
          in: query
          schema: {type: string, format: date}
          example: 2026-10-01
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Usage summary.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Usage'}

components:
  securitySchemes:
    gatewayOAuth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        clientCredentials:
          tokenUrl: https://login.northfield.ac.uk/realms/hpc/protocol/openid-connect/token
          scopes:
            jobs:submit: Submit jobs on behalf of authorised users
            jobs:read: Read job state and output
            'usage:read': Read accounting data
  parameters:
    OnBehalfOf:
      name: X-Larch-On-Behalf-Of
      in: header
      required: true
      description: Northfield username (`abc123`) of the end user.
      schema: {type: string, pattern: "^[a-z]{3}[0-9]{3}$"}
  responses:
    Unauthorized:
      description: Missing or expired token.
    Problem:
      description: RFC 9457 problem details.
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'}
  schemas:
    JobState:
      type: string
      enum: [PENDING, RUNNING, COMPLETING, COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, TIMEOUT, OUT_OF_MEMORY, NODE_FAIL, PREEMPTED]
    JobSubmission:
      type: object
      required: [name, account, script]
      additionalProperties: false
      properties:
        name: {type: string, maxLength: 128}
        account: {type: string}
        partition: {type: string, default: short}
        nodes: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 64, default: 1}
        ntasksPerNode: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 192}
        gpusPerNode:
          type: integer
          minimum: 0
          maximum: 4
          default: 0
        timeLimit:
          type: string
          description: Slurm time format, `[days-]hours:minutes:seconds`.
          pattern: '^(\d+-)?\d{1,2}:\d{2}:\d{2}$'
          default: "01:00:00"
        array: {type: [string, 'null'], examples: ["0-99%10", "1,3,5-7"]}
        callbackUrl: {type: [string, "null"], format: uri}
        script: {type: string, maxLength: 65536}
    Job:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/JobSubmission'
        - type: object
          required: [jobId, state]
          properties:
            jobId: {type: string, readOnly: true}
            state: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/JobState'}
            submitTime: {type: string, format: date-time}
            startTime: {type: [string, 'null'], format: date-time}
            exitCode: {type: [integer, 'null'], examples: [0, 137]}
            efficiency:
              type: object
              description: CPU and memory efficiency as reported by `seff`, in percent.
              properties:
                cpu: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 100}
                memory: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 1.0e+2}
    Partition:
      type: object
      properties:
        name: {type: string}
        idleNodes: {type: integer}
        maxTime: {type: string, examples: ["7-00:00:00"]}
        gres: {type: array, items: {type: string}, examples: [[ "gpu:a100:4" ]]}
    Usage:
      type: object
      properties:
        coreHours: {type: number}
        gpuHours: {type: number}
        fairshare: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 1}
    Problem:
      type: object
      properties:
        type: {type: string, format: uri, default: about:blank}
        title: {type: string}
        status: {type: integer}
        detail: {type: string}

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Acme Storefront API
  version: "2026-11-01"
  summary: Catalog, pricing, cart & recommendations for the Acme web storefront.
  # fmt: markdown
  description: |
    The **Storefront API** backs `www.acme-shop.example`, the marketing landing pages and the mobile web app. It is a BFF ("backend for frontend"): it stitches together the headless CMS, the pricing engine and the recommendation service so the browser only ever talks to one origin.

    ## Conventions
    * Prices are **integer minor units** (cents), always paired with an ISO-4217 `currency`.
    * SKUs look like `AUR-2-BLK-42` → *family*-*generation*-*colour*-*size*.
    + Timestamps are RFC 3339, UTC.

    ## Rate limits
    plan | req/min | burst
    ---|---:|---:
    anonymous | 120 | 40
    logged-in | 600 | 100
    partner | 3000 | 500

    Questions? Ping `#storefront-api` on Slack or open an issue 🙏
  contact:
    name: Web Platform team
    email: web-platform@acme-shop.example
    url: https://handbook.acme-shop.example/storefront/
  license: {name: Proprietary, identifier: LicenseRef-Acme}
servers:
  - url: https://api.acme-shop.example/storefront/v2
    description: Production
  - url: https://api.staging.acme-shop.example/storefront/v2
    description: staging (reset every night at 03:00 CET)
  - url: http://localhost:{port}/v2
    description: Local docker compose
    variables:
      port:
        default: "3001"
        enum: ['3001', "3002"]
tags:
  - name: Catalog
    description: Products, variants (SKUs) and categories. Copy & images come from the CMS.
  - name: Pricing
    description: >
      Price lookups, including
      member prices and
      active promotions.
  - name: Cart
  - name: Recommendations
    description: "Personalised product carousels, backed by the `recs` service (two-tower model)."
    x-displayName: Recs ✨

paths:
  /products/{slug}:
    get:
      tags: [Catalog]
      operationId: getProduct
      summary: Get a product by slug
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Locale'
        - name: slug
          in: path
          required: true
          schema: { type: string, pattern: '^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$', example: aurora-runner-2 }
        - name: include
          in: query
          description: Comma separated list of extra blocks. `reviews` is slow (≈300 ms p95), avoid it on listing pages.
          style: form
          explode: false
          schema:
            type: array
            items: {type: string, enum: [variants, reviews, related, cms_blocks]}
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          headers:
            Cache-Control:
              schema: {type: string}
              example: "public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=600"
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Product"
              examples:
                sneaker:
                  summary: Sneaker with 2 variants, one sold out
                  value:
                    slug: aurora-runner-2
                    name: Aurora Runner 2
                    badges: ["new", "eco"]
                    variants:
                      - {sku: AUR-2-BLK-42, color: black, size: "42", price: {amount: 11995, currency: EUR, was: 12995}, stock: 14}
                      - {sku: AUR-2-WHT-43, color: white, size: "43", price: {amount: 11995, currency: EUR}, stock: 0}
        404:
          $ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound'
        default:
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Problem"

  /prices:
    get:
      tags:
      - Pricing
      operationId: listPrices
      summary: Bulk price lookup (max. 100 SKUs)
      # fmt: markdown
      description: |-
        Returns the **current** sell price for each SKU, applying (in this order):
        1. member price, if the shopper is logged in and `member=true`
        2. the best active promotion (see `GET /promotions`)
        3. psychological rounding -- prices end in `,95` (NL/DE) or `.99` (UK)

        Unknown SKUs are silently dropped; check `missing[]` in the response.
      parameters:
        - in: query
          name: sku
          required: true
          schema:
            type: array
            maxItems: 100
            items:
              type: string
              pattern: "^[A-Z]{3}-\\d+-[A-Z]{3}-[0-9A-Z]{1,3}$"
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Locale'
        - {name: member, in: query, schema: {type: boolean, default: false}}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Prices keyed by SKU.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  prices:
                    type: object
                    additionalProperties: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Price'}
                  missing: {type: array, items: {type: string}}
              example:
                prices:
                  AUR-2-BLK-42: {amount: 11995, currency: EUR, was: 12995, promo: BF26-10}
                  TEE-1-WHT-M: { amount: 2295, currency: EUR }
                  "HOM-MUG-SET4": {amount: 2999, currency: EUR, promo: ~}
                missing: [GFT-0-XXX-0]

  /cart/{cartId}/items:
    parameters:
      - {name: cartId, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string, format: uuid}}
    post:
      tags: [Cart]
      operationId: addCartItem
      security:
        - {}
        - cookieAuth: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [sku, quantity]
              properties:
                sku: {type: string, examples: ["AUR-2-BLK-42"]}
                quantity: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 10, default: 1}
                gift_wrap: {type: boolean, description: "+€4.95, not available for gift cards"}
      responses:
        '201': {description: Created, content: {application/json: {schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Cart'}}}}
        '409':
          description: Out of stock -- the item was **not** added.
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Problem'

  /recommendations:
    get:
      tags: [Recommendations]
      operationId: getRecommendations
      summary: Personalised carousel
      # fmt: markdown
      description: >-
        Returns up to `limit` products for a carousel `slot`. When the shopper has no history we fall back to bestsellers in the same category (see `strategy` in the response). Results are cached per (slot, segment) for 5 minutes, **not** per user -- so never put user-specific copy in the CMS carousel title.
      parameters:
        - name: slot
          in: query
          required: true
          schema: {type: string, enum: [pdp-similar, cart-upsell, home-for-you, email-digest]}
        - name: limit
          in: query
          schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 48, default: 12}
        - name: context_sku
          in: query
          deprecated: true
          description: Use `context` instead. Will be removed 2027-01-31.
          schema: {type: string}
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/RecommendationList'}

components:
  securitySchemes:
    cookieAuth: {type: apiKey, in: cookie, name: acme_session}
  parameters:
    Locale:
      name: Accept-Language
      in: header
      schema: {type: string, default: en-NL, enum: [en-NL, nl-NL, de-DE, fr-FR, en-GB]}
  responses:
    NotFound:
      description: Not found
    Problem:
      description: RFC 9457 problem details
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'}
  schemas:
    Price:
      type: object
      required: [amount, currency]
      properties:
        amount: {type: integer, description: "Minor units, e.g. 12995 = €129.95"}
        currency: {type: string, pattern: '^[A-Z]{3}$', example: EUR}
        was: {type: [integer, 'null'], description: Strike-through price for the PDP badge}
        promo:
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
    Product:
      type: object
      properties:
        slug: {type: string}
        name: {type: string, maxLength: 120}
        badges:
          type: array
          items: {type: string, enum: [new, eco, bestseller, "last-chance", '-30%']}
        variants:
          type: array
          items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Variant'}
    Variant:
      type: object
      properties:
        sku: {type: string, example: "AUR-2-BLK-42"}
        color: {type: string}
        size: {type: string, description: 'EU size as a string, so "42.5" and "XL" both work'}
        price: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Price'}
        stock: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
    Cart:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: {type: string, format: uuid}
        items: {type: array, items: {type: object}}
        subtotal: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Price'}
        free_shipping_remaining: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Price'}
    RecommendationList:
      type: object
      properties:
        slot: {type: string}
        strategy: {type: string, enum: [personalized, bestsellers, similar-items]}
        items: {type: array, items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Product'}}
        model_version: {type: string, example: two_tower_v3@2026-11-01}
    Problem:
      type: object
      properties:
        type: {type: string, format: uri}
        title: {type: string}
        status: {type: integer}
        detail: {type: string}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""store_report.py - store release notes + launch numbers for Glowtide / Sprout.

Plain script:  python tools/store_report.py --app glowtide --version 1.8.0 --write
As a report:   quarto render tools/store_report.py   (that's what the `#|` cells are for)
"""
# fmt: markdown
# ## What this does
#
# 1. Pulls the `## [x.y.z]` section for the given version out of the app's `CHANGELOG.md` and turns it into *What's New* texts: one for App Store Connect (4000 chars max) and one per locale for Google Play (500 chars max!!), written to `fastlane/metadata/...` so `deliver` and `supply` pick them up.
# 2. Plots installs and crash-free sessions for the launch retro from the CSV exports in `data/` (the handbook page *Store metadata & screenshots* says where to download them).
#
# Lines starting with `Internal:` in the changelog are dropped, and so are issue numbers like `(#488)`.
#
# * needs `pandas` + `matplotlib`, nothing else
# * the Play limit is per locale and counts **characters, not bytes**   (an emoji is 1, or 2 with a variation selector... don't ask)

# %%
#| label: setup
#| include: false
#| warning:   False
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import sys
import textwrap
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
LIMITS = {"app_store": 4000, "google_play": 500}
APPS = {
    "glowtide": {"name": "Glowtide", "changelog": ROOT / "games/glowtide/CHANGELOG.md", "locales": ["en-US", "de-DE", "ja", "ko", "pt-BR"]},
    "sprout":   {"name": "Sprout", "changelog": ROOT / "apps/CHANGELOG-sprout.md", "locales": ["en-US", "de-DE"]},
}

# %%
#| label: changelog-parsing
#| code-fold : true
#| code-summary: "Show the changelog parser"
SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"^## \[?(?P<version>\d+\.\d+\.\d+)\]?\s+[-–(]\s*(?P<date>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})", re.M)


@dataclass
class Release:
    version: str
    date: date
    body: str

    @property
    def bullets(self) -> list[str]:
        out = []
        for line in self.body.splitlines():
            line = line.strip()
            if line[:2] in ("- ", "* ", "+ ") and not line[2:].startswith("Internal:"):
                out.append(re.sub(r"\s*\(#\d+(, #\d+)*\)", "", line[2:]))
        return out


def find_release(changelog: Path, version: str) -> Release:
    text = changelog.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
    matches = list(SECTION_RE.finditer(text))
    for i, m in enumerate(matches):
        if m["version"] == version:
            end = matches[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(matches) else len(text)
            return Release(version, date.fromisoformat(m["date"]), text[m.end():end])
    sys.exit(f"version {version} not found in {changelog}")


# fmt: markdown
APP_STORE_FOOTER = """
Thanks for playing! If you enjoy the update, a short review helps a tiny studio more than you would think.   Found a bug? *Settings → Help → Send feedback* attaches your device info automatically.
"""

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
PLAY_INTRO = """
New in this version. Full notes at lanternfish.studio/changes. Thanks for playing!
"""

# fmt: markdown
EPILOG = r"""
Examples:

    store_report.py --app glowtide --version 1.8.1 --write
    store_report.py --app sprout --version 3.2.0 --skip '^\s*Internal:'

The `--skip` pattern is a Python regex matched against each bullet *after* the marker is removed, so `^\s*` is usually what you want.
"""


def whats_new(app: str, rel: Release, store: str) -> str:
    limit = LIMITS[store]
    name = APPS[app]["name"]
    bullets = "\n".join(f"• {b}" for b in rel.bullets)
    if store == "app_store":
        text = f"{name} {rel.version}\n\n{bullets}\n\n{APP_STORE_FOOTER.strip()}"
    else:
        text = f"{PLAY_INTRO.strip()}\n{bullets}"
    if len(text) > limit:
        text = textwrap.shorten(text, width=limit - 1, placeholder="…")
    return text


def discord_post(app: str, rel: Release, build: int) -> str:
    name = APPS[app]["name"]
    # fmt: markdown
    return f"""
**{name} {rel.version}** (build {build}) is on its way to the stores :tada:

{chr(10).join('- ' + b for b in rel.bullets[:6])}

* App Store: phased release over 7 days, starts after review
* Google Play: staged rollout, 5% → 20% → 50% → 100%
Full changelog: <https://github.com/lanternfish/studio/blob/main/games/glowtide/CHANGELOG.md>
"""


# fmt: json
SAMPLE_CRASHLYTICS_ROW = """
{"os":"iOS 18.1","app_version":"1.8.0 (1800412)","sessions":48211,"crash_free_sessions":0.9971,"top_issue":null}
"""

# %% [markdown]
# fmt: markdown
# ## Launch numbers
#
# Installs are *first-time downloads* (App Store "First-Time Downloads", Play "Device acquisitions"), so re-downloads and updates are not in here.  Crash-free numbers come from Crashlytics and lag about 24 h behind.

# %%
#| label: fig-installs
#| fig-cap: "Daily first-time installs per store, first 14 days after launch"
#| fig-alt: "Line chart with two lines, App Store and Google Play. Both spike on launch day at about 4,100 and 6,300 installs and settle around 1,200 per day after day 10."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height:   4
#| layout: [[1],
#|   [1]]
def plot_installs(csv: Path, days: int = 14):
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    import pandas as pd

    df = pd.read_csv(csv, parse_dates=["date"])
    first = df["date"].min()
    df = df[df["date"] < first + pd.Timedelta(days=days)]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4))
    for store, grp in df.groupby("store"):
        ax.plot(grp["date"], grp["first_time_downloads"], label=store.replace("_", " ").title())
    ax.set_ylabel("first-time installs")
    ax.legend(frameon=False)
    return fig


# %%
#| label: tbl-crash-free
#| tbl-cap: Crash-free sessions by OS version (min. 500 sessions)
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
#| tags: [ report,crashlytics ]
#| params:
#|     min_sessions: 500
#|     platforms:
#|     - ios
#|     - android
def crash_table(csv: Path, min_sessions: int = 500) -> str:
    import pandas as pd

    df = pd.read_csv(csv)
    df = df[df["sessions"] >= min_sessions].sort_values("crash_free_sessions")
    rows = [f"| {r.os} | {r.app_version} | {r.sessions:,} | {r.crash_free_sessions:.2%} |" for r in df.itertuples()]
    return "\n".join(["| OS | build | sessions | crash-free |", "|---|---|--:|--:|", *rows])


# %%
#| label: cli
#| eval: false
def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0], epilog=EPILOG, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--app", choices=sorted(APPS), required=True)
    p.add_argument("--version", required=True, help="semver, e.g. 1.8.1")
    p.add_argument("--build", type=int, default=0)
    p.add_argument("--write", action="store_true", help="write into fastlane/metadata instead of printing")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)

    rel = find_release(APPS[args.app]["changelog"], args.version)
    ios_txt = whats_new(args.app, rel, "app_store")
    play_txt = whats_new(args.app, rel, "google_play")
    if not args.write:
        print(ios_txt, "", play_txt, "", discord_post(args.app, rel, args.build), sep="\n")
        return 0
    meta = ROOT / "fastlane" / "metadata"
    (meta / "ios" / "en-US" / "release_notes.txt").write_text(ios_txt + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    code = int(args.version.replace(".", "")) if args.build == 0 else args.build
    for loc in APPS[args.app]["locales"]:
        out = meta / "android" / loc / "changelogs" / f"{code}.txt"
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if loc == "en-US" or not out.exists():
            out.write_text(play_txt + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

--- title: "Glowtide 1.8 *Tidewalker* — launch retro" subtitle: 'Installs, retention, crashes and reviews in the first 14 days' author: - name: Mira Okonkwo email: mira@lanternfish.studio - name: "Tomás Ferreira" - name: Søren Lund roles: [figures] date: 2026-11-07 date-modified: last-modified format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 2 code-fold: true code-tools: true theme: [cosmo, assets/retro.scss] fig-width: 8 pdf: documentclass: scrartcl papersize: a4 execute: echo: false warning: false freeze: auto bibliography: refs.bib params: version: "1.8.0" launch_date: 2026-10-21 stores: [app_store,google_play] window_days: 14 --- ```{r setup} #| include: false library(tidyverse) library(gt) source("R/store_exports.R") installs <- read_store_installs("data/installs_2026-10.csv") retention <- read_cohorts("data/cohorts_glowtide.parquet") crashes <- read_crashlytics("data/crashlytics_daily.csv") ``` ## TL;DR {#sec-tldr} * 1.8.0 went live on **2026-10-21** on both stores; the App Store phased release finished on day 7, Play went to 100 % on day 3. * `r scales::comma(sum(installs$first_time))` first-time installs in 14 days, about 2.3× the 1.7.0 launch window — mostly thanks to the App Store *Today* feature on day 2 (@fig-installs). * D1 retention improved from 41.2 % to 44.8 %; D7 is flat at ~18 %. The new current mechanic doesn't seem to scare people off, but it doesn't keep them around either. * Crash-free sessions: 99.71 % iOS / 99.38 % Android. The Android number is dragged down by one shader crash on Mali-G52 GPUs that we fixed in 1.8.1 (@sec-crashes). ::: {.callout-note} ## Data sources All store numbers come from the App Store Connect *Sales and Trends* and Play Console *Statistics* exports. Retention is computed from our own `session_start` events in beacon, **not** from the store dashboards, because Apple only counts users who opted in to share analytics (~25 % of our audience). ::: ## Installs ```{r installs-by-day, fig.width=9, fig.height=4, fig.cap="First-time installs per day and store", echo=FALSE, message=FALSE} installs |> filter(date >= params$launch_date, date < params$launch_date + params$window_days) |> ggplot(aes(date, first_time, colour = store)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + labs(x = NULL, y = "first-time installs", colour = NULL) ``` The day-2 spike (≈ 9,800 iOS installs) lines up exactly with the *Today* tab feature in the US, UK, CA and AU storefronts[^feature]. Android had no featuring, but the **pre-registration** campaign converted well: 31 % of the 18,402 pre-registered users installed within 48 hours, versus the 20–25 % Google quotes as typical [@playprereg2024]. Organic search installs were flat, as expected for a content update.^[Keyword ranking for "tide puzzle" stayed at #3 in the US store the whole time.] [^feature]: We only found out when people on the Discord started posting screenshots. Apple does not tell you in advance and App Store Connect does not show featuring anywhere, so if someone asks "can we plan for this" — no. ## Retention We use the usual definition, where $N_0$ is the number of players whose first session was on day 0 and $N_d$ is how many of them were active on day $d$: $$ R_d = \frac{N_d}{N_0} \times 100\,\% $$ ::: {.panel-tabset} ### iOS ```{r} #| label: fig-retention-ios #| fig-cap: "Retention curves, 1.7.0 vs 1.8.0 cohorts (iOS)" #| fig-alt: "Two retention curves for iOS. The 1.8.0 curve sits about 3.5 points above 1.7.0 on day 1 and the two curves meet again at day 7." plot_retention(retention, platform = "ios", versions = c("1.7.0", "1.8.0")) ``` ### Android ```{r} #| label: fig-retention-android #| fig-cap: Retention curves, 1.7.0 vs 1.8.0 cohorts (Android) #| plot_retention(retention, platform = "android", versions = c("1.7.0", "1.8.0")) ``` ::: | Cohort | Players | D1 | D7 | D14 | |:-------|-------:|---:|---:|----:| | 1.7.0 (Jul 8–21) | 21,377 | 41.2 % | 18.4 % | 11.0 % | | 1.8.0 (Oct 21–Nov 3) | 49,910 | 44.8 % | 18.1 % | 10.6 % | | 1.8.0, featured day only | 12,044 | 38.9 % | 14.7 % | — | : D1 / D7 / D14 retention by install cohort {#tbl-retention} Featured-day players retain **worse** than organic ones, which matches what other small studios report [@gamesindustry2023, pp. 4–6; @deconstructor2022]. ## Crashes {#sec-crashes} Definitions used in this section: Crash-free sessions : Sessions without a fatal crash ÷ all sessions, as reported by Crashlytics. Excludes ANRs. ANR rate : User-perceived ANR rate from Android vitals. Google's bad-behaviour threshold is 0.47 %, we were at 0.21 %. +---------------------------+------------+------------+----------------------------------------------+ | Build | iOS | Android | Notes | +===========================+============+============+==============================================+ | 1.8.0 (1800412 / 10800) | 99.71 % | 99.38 % | Mali-G52 shader crash, ~0.4 % of Android | | | | | sessions, fixed in 1.8.1 | +---------------------------+------------+------------+----------------------------------------------+ | 1.8.1 (1800503 / 10801) | 99.74 % | 99.80 % | hotfix, released on day 6 | +---------------------------+------------+------------+----------------------------------------------+ ```{r crash-table} #| echo: false #| fmt: skip crashes %>% filter(version %in% c("1.8.0","1.8.1")) %>% group_by(version,platform) %>% summarise(crash_free = 1 - sum(crashed_sessions)/sum(sessions), .groups="drop") %>% gt() %>% fmt_percent(crash_free, decimals=2) ``` ## What players said | "the tide puzzle on 7-12 made me put my phone down for a week. | 10/10 would drown again" | — App Store review, 🇬🇧, ★★★★★ Most 1–2★ reviews (63 of 97) mention the *pearl cap*: players who had hoarded hundreds of pearls lost everything above 99 with the 1.8.0 migration. In hindsight we should have converted the excess into something (cosmetics, hint tokens) instead of just cutting it off, and the store reply template we used ("this was necessary to balance the economy") did not help. Reviews mentioning the new chapter itself are overwhelmingly positive, average 4.7★. {{< pagebreak >}} ## Release timeline ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: Release timeline for 1.8.0 / 1.8.1 flowchart LR A[1.8.0 tagged
Oct 17] --> B[TestFlight + Play internal] B --> C{Review} C -->|approved Oct 20| D[Phased release, 7 days] C -->|Play| E[5% → 20% → 100%] D --> F[1.8.1 hotfix Oct 27] E --> F ``` ## Remote config changes during launch ```yaml glowtide: hint_cost_pearls: 1 weekly_board: true # bumped on day 3 after the leaderboard got spammed with 99999s max_score_per_puzzle: 3200 min_supported_version: "1.7.0" ab_tests: [{name: tide_tutorial_v2, split: 0.5},{name: pearl_cap, split: 1.0}] ``` ## Next steps 1. Ship the Steam build (target: February 2027), see the Steam Deck notes at {{< var handbook.url >}}/steam 2. Revisit the pearl economy; the 99 cap generated the majority of negative reviews. 3. A/B test the tide tutorial v2 for ≥ 2 weeks before deciding. We stopped v1 after 4 days, which was too early: the minimum detectable effect at our volume is about 3 pp on D1. ## References ::: {#refs} :::

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Acme Storefront API
  version: "2026-11-01"
  summary: Catalog, pricing & recommendations for the Acme web storefront.
  # fmt: markdown
  description: |
    The **Storefront API** backs `www.acme-shop.example`, the marketing landing pages and the mobile web app. It is a BFF ("backend for frontend"): it stitches together the headless CMS, the pricing engine and the recommendation service so the browser only ever talks to one origin.

    ## Conventions
    * Prices are **integer minor units** (cents), always paired with an ISO-4217 `currency`.
    * SKUs look like `AUR-2-BLK-42` → *family*-*generation*-*colour*-*size*.
    + Timestamps are RFC 3339, UTC.

    ## Rate limits
    plan | req/min | burst
    ---|---:|---:
    anonymous | 120 | 40
    logged-in | 600 | 100
    partner | 3000 | 500

    Questions? Ping `#storefront-api` on Slack or open an issue 🙏
  contact:
    name: Web Platform team
    email: web-platform@acme-shop.example
    url: https://handbook.acme-shop.example/storefront/
  license: {name: Proprietary, identifier: LicenseRef-Acme}
servers:
  - url: https://api.acme-shop.example/storefront/v2
    description: Production
  - url: https://api.staging.acme-shop.example/storefront/v2
    description: staging (reset every night at 03:00 CET)
  - url: http://localhost:{port}/v2
    description: Local docker compose
    variables:
      port:
        default: "3001"
        enum: ['3001', "3002"]
tags:
  - name: Catalog
    description: Products, variants (SKUs) and categories. Copy & images come from the CMS.
  - name: Pricing
    description: >
      Price lookups, including
      member prices and
      active promotions.
  - name: Recommendations
    description: "Personalised product carousels, backed by the `recs` service (two-tower model)."
    x-displayName: Recs ✨

paths:
  /products/{slug}:
    get:
      tags: [Catalog]
      operationId: getProduct
      summary: Get a product by slug
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Locale'
        - name: slug

arguments.content:
Scalable Krylov solvers & preconditioners for large sparse linear systems

[![CI](https://github.com/fernsolve/fernsolve/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/fernsolve/fernsolve/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/fernsolve.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/fernsolve/) [![conda-forge](https://img.shields.io/conda/vn/conda-forge/fernsolve.svg)](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/fernsolve) [![Docs](https://readthedocs.org/projects/fernsolve/badge/?version=stable)](https://fernsolve.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) [![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.14012345.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14012345) **fernsolve** solves $Ax = b$ for large, sparse, (mostly) nonsymmetric $A$ on anything from a laptop to a few thousand MPI ranks. It provides restarted and pipelined Krylov methods (CG, GMRES($m$), BiCGStab($\ell$), IDR($s$)), a handful of robust preconditioners (ILU(k), ILUT, smoothed-aggregation AMG, block Jacobi) and mixed-precision iterative refinement, behind a C++20 core with Python bindings that accept anything `scipy.sparse` understands. It grew out of the Computational Mechanics group's need to solve pressure systems with ~10⁹ unknowns on the [larch cluster][larch] without writing PETSc boilerplate for every PhD project. If you already use PETSc or Trilinos and are happy with them, you probably don't need us :-) ## Features * Krylov methods - CG, preconditioned CG, block CG for multiple right-hand sides - GMRES($m$) with CGS2 or MGS orthogonalisation, flexible GMRES, and **pipelined GMRES** (Ghysels et al., 2013) for latency-bound runs - BiCGStab($\ell$) and IDR($s$) for when the $\mathcal{O}(mn)$ memory of GMRES hurts * Preconditioners: ILU(0), ILU(k), ILUT, block Jacobi with local ILU, smoothed-aggregation AMG * Distributed CSR matrices over MPI, with optional GPU offload of SpMV and triangular solves (CUDA or HIP) + Mixed-precision iterative refinement (`float32`/`bfloat16` factorisation, `float64` residuals) + Reproducible reductions: pass `deterministic=True` and you get bit-identical residual histories for a fixed number of ranks, at about 8 % extra cost Installation ------------ ```bash pip install fernsolve # CPU wheels with OpenMP, no MPI conda install -c conda-forge fernsolve "fernsolve=*=mpi_openmpi_*" ``` On HPC systems you almost certainly want to build against the site's MPI, so use Spack: ```console $ spack install fernsolve@2.4.1 +mpi +cuda cuda_arch=80 ^openmpi@4.1.6 ^openblas threads=openmp $ spack load fernsolve ``` or build from source (CMake ≥ 3.24, a C++20 compiler, MPI ≥ 3.1 and BLAS/LAPACK): git clone https://github.com/fernsolve/fernsolve.git && cd fernsolve cmake -S . -B build -DFERN_ENABLE_MPI=ON -DFERN_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build -j 16 && ctest --test-dir build -L unit pip install ./python --no-build-isolation ## Quick start ```python import numpy as np import scipy.sparse as sp from fernsolve import krylov, precond # 2-D Poisson on a 1000 x 1000 grid, n = 10**6 n = 1000 T = sp.diags([-1, 2, -1], [-1, 0, 1], shape=(n, n)) A = (sp.kron(sp.eye(n), T) + sp.kron(T, sp.eye(n))).tocsr() b = np.ones(A.shape[0]) M = precond.AMG(A, strength=0.25, max_levels=10) x, info = krylov.cg(A, b, M=M, rtol=1e-10, maxiter=200) print(info.iterations, info.residual_norm) # 14 8.7e-11 ``` The same in C++ (link against `fernsolve::fernsolve`): ```cpp #include int main(int argc, char** argv) { fern::mpi::environment env(argc, argv); auto A = fern::io::read_matrix_market("thermal2.mtx", env.world()); fern::dist_vector b(A.row_map(), 1.0), x(A.row_map(), 0.0); fern::precond::ilut M(A, {.fill = 20, .droptol = 1e-4}); auto info = fern::krylov::gmres(A, x, b, M, {.restart = 50, .rtol = 1e-8}); if (env.rank() == 0) std::printf("%d iterations, |r|/|b| = %.2e\n", info.iterations, info.relres); } ``` ## Which solver should I use? | Your matrix | Try first | Then | Notes | |---|---|:---:|---| | SPD (diffusion, elasticity) | `cg` + `AMG` | `cg` + `ILU(0)` | AMG setup is amortised over many solves | | nonsymmetric, mild | `gmres(restart=50)` + `ILUT` | `bicgstab` | | | nonsymmetric, convection-dominated | `fgmres` + `AMG(strength=0.5)` | `idr(s=8)` | ILU often breaks down, watch for `ZeroPivotError` | | many right-hand sides | `block_cg` / `block_gmres` | | cost grows ~linearly in the block size `k \| nrhs` | | ill-conditioned, $\kappa(A) > 10^{10}$ | `refine` (mixed precision) | a direct solver | seriously, try MUMPS | ### A word on convergence All solvers stop when the *relative* residual drops below `rtol`, i.e. when $\|b - Ax_k\|_2 \le \mathtt{rtol}\cdot\|b\|_2$ (absolute tolerances via `atol=` are supported too). For GMRES, the classic bound of Saad & Schultz (1986) for diagonalisable $A = V\Lambda V^{-1}$ is $$ \frac{\|r_k\|_2}{\|r_0\|_2} \;\le\; \kappa_2(V)\, \min_{\substack{p \in \mathcal{P}_k \\ p(0) = 1}} \; \max_{\lambda \in \Lambda(A)} |p(\lambda)| , $$ which is why clustering the spectrum (= a good preconditioner) matters far more than the choice between GMRES and BiCGStab. See the [user guide on preconditioning](https://fernsolve.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/precond.html) for practical advice. ## Running on a Slurm cluster fernsolve is an ordinary MPI program, so launch it with `srun` (preferred) or `mpirun`. A typical job on larch: ```bash #!/bin/bash #SBATCH --job-name=fern-thermal2 #SBATCH --nodes=4 #SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=64 #SBATCH --cpus-per-task=3 # 64 ranks x 3 OpenMP threads = 192 cores per node #SBATCH --time=00:30:00 #SBATCH --partition=short module load gcc/13.2.0 openmpi/4.1.6 fernsolve/2.4.1 export OMP_NUM_THREADS=$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK OMP_PLACES=cores OMP_PROC_BIND=close srun --cpu-bind=cores python solve.py --matrix /scratch/$USER/thermal2.mtx --restart 50 ``` Environment variables that change behaviour at run time: Variable | Default | Effect --- | --- | --- `FERN_VERBOSITY` | `1` | 0 = silent, 3 = print the residual every iteration `FERN_DETERMINISTIC` | `0` | bit-reproducible reductions (slower) `FERN_GPU_AWARE_MPI` | auto | set to `0` if your MPI *claims* to be CUDA-aware but isn't ## Performance Strong scaling of pipelined vs. classical GMRES(50) with block-Jacobi/ILU(0) on `thermal2` replicated to $n \approx 2.0 \times 10^8$ (larch: 2× EPYC 9654 per node, HDR-200 InfiniBand). Time per iteration in ms, median of 5 runs: | nodes | GMRES | p-GMRES | speed-up | |------:|-------:|--------:|---------:| | 1 | 412.0 | 405.3 | 1.02× | | 4 | 108.9 | 99.1 | 1.10× | | 16 | 31.2 | 24.7 | 1.26× | | 64 | 11.8 | 7.1 | 1.66× | Beyond 16 nodes the `MPI_Allreduce` latency dominates and pipelining pays off; below that it costs a little extra memory traffic for nothing. Details are in the [technical note](docs/notes/tn-2026-07.Rmd). ## Citing If fernsolve helped your research, please cite the software paper (and the specific release via Zenodo): ```bibtex @article{haldorsen2025fernsolve, title = {fernsolve: Pipelined {Krylov} Solvers for Sparse Systems at Scale}, author = {Haldorsen, Ines and Asante, Kwame O. and Lindqvist, Astrid}, journal = {Journal of Open Source Software}, year = {2025}, volume = {10}, number = {112}, pages = {7781}, doi = {10.21105/joss.07781} } ``` ## Roadmap - [x] pipelined GMRES - [x] HIP backend for SpMV - [ ] s-step (communication-avoiding) CG -- prototype on the `ca-cg` branch - [ ] SYCL backend, *if* someone gives us access to the hardware - [ ] better AMG for systems of PDEs (elasticity, Stokes) ## Acknowledgements Development is funded by EPSRC (grant EP/Y012345/1)[^epsrc] and by in-kind RSE time from Research Computing Services. Computations were performed on the larch HPC cluster at the University of Northfield. fernsolve is BSD-3-Clause licensed, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). [^epsrc]: "Scalable solvers for the exascale era", 2024–2028, PI Dr. I. Haldorsen. The views expressed are those of the authors and not necessarily those of the funder. [larch]: https://hpc.northfield.ac.uk "larch HPC cluster"

It provides restarted and pipelined Krylov methods (CG, GMRES($m$), BiCGStab($\ell$), IDR($s$)), a handful of robust preconditioners (ILU(k), ILUT, smoothed-aggregation AMG, block Jacobi) and mixed-precision iterative refinement, behind a C++20 core with Python bindings that accept anything `scipy.sparse` understands. It grew out of the Computational Mechanics group's need to solve pressure systems with ~10⁹ unknowns on the [larch cluster][larch] without writing PETSc boilerplate for every PhD project. If you already use PETSc or Trilinos and are happy with them, you probably don't need us :-) ## Features * Krylov methods - CG, preconditioned CG, block CG for multiple right-hand sides - GMRES($m$) with CGS2 or MGS orthogonalisation, flexible GMRES, and **pipelined GMRES** (Ghysels et al., 2013) for latency-bound runs - BiCGStab($\ell$) and IDR($s$) for when the $\mathcal{O}(mn)$ memory of GMRES hurts * Preconditioners: ILU(0), ILU(k), ILUT, block Jacobi with local ILU, smoothed-aggregation AMG * Distributed CSR matrices over MPI, with optional GPU offload of SpMV and triangular solves (CUDA or HIP) + Mixed-precision iterative refinement (`float32`/`bfloat16` factorisation, `float64` residuals) + Reproducible reductions: pass `deterministic=True` and you get bit-identical residual histories for a fixed number of ranks, at about 8 % extra cost Installation ------------ ```bash pip install fernsolve # CPU wheels with OpenMP, no MPI conda install -c conda-forge fernsolve "fernsolve=*=mpi_openmpi_*" ``` On HPC systems you almost certainly want to build against the site's MPI, so use Spack: ```console $ spack install fernsolve@2.4.1 +mpi +cuda cuda_arch=80 ^openmpi@4.1.6 ^openblas threads=openmp $ spack load fernsolve ``` or build from source (CMake ≥ 3.24, a C++20 compiler, MPI ≥ 3.1 and BLAS/LAPACK): git clone https://github.com/fernsolve/fernsolve.git && cd fernsolve cmake -S . -B build -DFERN_ENABLE_MPI=ON -DFERN_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build -j 16 && ctest --test-dir build -L unit pip install ./python --no-build-isolation ## Quick start ```python import numpy as np import scipy.sparse as sp from fernsolve import krylov, precond # 2-D Poisson on a 1000 x 1000 grid, n = 10**6 n = 1000 T = sp.diags([-1, 2, -1], [-1, 0, 1], shape=(n, n)) A = (sp.kron(sp.eye(n), T) + sp.kron(T, sp.eye(n))).tocsr() b = np.ones(A.shape[0]) M = precond.AMG(A, strength=0.25, max_levels=10) x, info = krylov.cg(A, b, M=M, rtol=1e-10, maxiter=200) print(info.iterations, info.residual_norm) # 14 8.7e-11 ``` The same in C++ (link against `fernsolve::fernsolve`): ```cpp #include int main(int argc, char** argv) { fern::mpi::environment env(argc, argv); auto A = fern::io::read_matrix_market("thermal2.mtx", env.world()); fern::dist_vector b(A.row_map(), 1.0), x(A.row_map(), 0.0); fern::precond::ilut M(A, {.fill = 20, .droptol = 1e-4}); auto info = fern::krylov::gmres(A, x, b, M, {.restart = 50, .rtol = 1e-8}); if (env.rank() == 0) std::printf("%d iterations, |r|/|b| = %.2e\n", info.iterations, info.relres); } ``` ## Which solver should I use? | Your matrix | Try first | Then | Notes | |---|---|:---:|---| | SPD (diffusion, elasticity) | `cg` + `AMG` | `cg` + `ILU(0)` | AMG setup is amortised over many solves | | nonsymmetric, mild | `gmres(restart=50)` + `ILUT` | `bicgstab` | | | nonsymmetric, convection-dominated | `fgmres` + `AMG(strength=0.5)` | `idr(s=8)` | ILU often breaks down, watch for `ZeroPivotError` | | many right-hand sides | `block_cg` / `block_gmres` | | cost grows ~linearly in the block size `k \| nrhs` | | ill-conditioned, $\kappa(A) > 10^{10}$ | `refine` (mixed precision) | a direct solver | seriously, try MUMPS | ### A word on convergence All solvers stop when the *relative* residual drops below `rtol`, i.e. when $\|b - Ax_k\|_2 \le \mathtt{rtol}\cdot\|b\|_2$ (absolute tolerances via `atol=` are supported too). For GMRES, the classic bound of Saad & Schultz (1986) for diagonalisable $A = V\Lambda V^{-1}$ is $$ \frac{\|r_k\|_2}{\|r_0\|_2} \;\le\; \kappa_2(V)\, \min_{\substack{p \in \mathcal{P}_k \\ p(0) = 1}} \; \max_{\lambda \in \Lambda(A)} |p(\lambda)| , $$ which is why clustering the spectrum (= a good preconditioner) matters far more than the choice between GMRES and BiCGStab. See the [user guide on preconditioning](https://fernsolve.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/precond.html) for practical advice. ## Running on a Slurm cluster fernsolve is an ordinary MPI program, so launch it with `srun` (preferred) or `mpirun`. A typical job on larch: ```bash #!/bin/bash #SBATCH --job-name=fern-thermal2 #SBATCH --nodes=4 #SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=64 #SBATCH --cpus-per-task=3 # 64 ranks x 3 OpenMP threads = 192 cores per node #SBATCH --time=00:30:00 #SBATCH --partition=short module load gcc/13.2.0 openmpi/4.1.6 fernsolve/2.4.1 export OMP_NUM_THREADS=$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK OMP_PLACES=cores OMP_PROC_BIND=close srun --cpu-bind=cores python solve.py --matrix /scratch/$USER/thermal2.mtx --restart 50 ``` Environment variables that change behaviour at run time: Variable | Default | Effect --- | --- | --- `FERN_VERBOSITY` | `1` | 0 = silent, 3 = print the residual every iteration `FERN_DETERMINISTIC` | `0` | bit-reproducible reductions (slower) `FERN_GPU_AWARE_MPI` | auto | set to `0` if your MPI *claims* to be CUDA-aware but isn't ## Performance Strong scaling of pipelined vs. classical GMRES(50) with block-Jacobi/ILU(0) on `thermal2` replicated to $n \approx 2.0 \times 10^8$ (larch: 2× EPYC 9654 per node, HDR-200 InfiniBand). Time per iteration in ms, median of 5 runs: | nodes | GMRES | p-GMRES | speed-up | |------:|-------:|--------:|---------:| | 1 | 412.0 | 405.3 | 1.02× | | 4 | 108.9 | 99.1 | 1.10× | | 16 | 31.2 | 24.7 | 1.26× | | 64 | 11.8 | 7.1 | 1.66× | Beyond 16 nodes the `MPI_Allreduce` latency dominates and pipelining pays off; below that it costs a little extra memory traffic for nothing. Details are in the [technical note](docs/notes/tn-2026-07.Rmd). ## Citing If fernsolve helped your research, please cite the software paper (and the specific release via Zenodo): ```bibtex @article{haldorsen2025fernsolve, title = {fernsolve: Pipelined {Krylov} Solvers for Sparse Systems at Scale}, author = {Haldorsen, Ines and Asante, Kwame O. and Lindqvist, Astrid}, journal = {Journal of Open Source Software}, year = {2025}, volume = {10}, number = {112}, pages = {7781}, doi = {10.21105/joss.07781} } ``` ## Roadmap - [x] pipelined GMRES - [x] HIP backend for SpMV - [ ] s-step (communication-avoiding) CG -- prototype on the `ca-cg` branch - [ ] SYCL backend, *if* someone gives us access to the hardware - [ ] better AMG for systems of PDEs (elasticity, Stokes) ## Acknowledgements Development is funded by EPSRC (grant EP/Y012345/1)[^epsrc] and by in-kind RSE time from Research Computing Services. Computations were performed on the larch HPC cluster at the University of Northfield. fernsolve is BSD-3-Clause licensed, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). [^epsrc]: "Scalable solvers for the exascale era", 2024–2028, PI Dr. I. Haldorsen. The views expressed are those of the authors and not necessarily those of the funder. [larch]: https://hpc.northfield.ac.uk "larch HPC cluster"

Changelog
=========

All notable changes to **fernsolve** are documented in this file.
The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres (mostly -- see the note under 2.0.0) to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

<!-- Maintainers: add entries under [Unreleased] in the same PR as the change. Reference the issue/PR number, not the commit hash. -->

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- `fern::krylov::gmres_pipelined`: Ghysels–Vanroose pipelined GMRES($m$) that overlaps the global reduction with the next SpMV. On 64 nodes of larch this cuts time-to-solution for the replicated `thermal2` problem by ~31 % (#1043).
- Python: `fernsolve.callbacks.ResidualHistory` now also records the *true* residual $\|b - Ax_k\|_2$ every `check_every` iterations, next to the recursively updated one, so you can finally see when the two drift apart.
* HIP backend for the ILU(0) triangular solves (thanks to the AMD folks at the hackathon) 

### Changed
-   Default restart length for GMRES is now `restart=50` (was 30). For most SuiteSparse test matrices this reduces iteration counts by 10–25 %, at the cost of $\mathcal{O}(mn)$ extra memory; pass `restart=30` to get the old behaviour.
- The CMake option `FERN_USE_OPENMP` now defaults to `ON`.

### Fixed
- Loss of orthogonality in classical Gram–Schmidt with re-orthogonalisation (CGS2) when $\kappa(A) \gtrsim 10^{12}$. We now fall back to modified Gram–Schmidt for the offending Arnoldi step and emit a `ConvergenceWarning` instead of returning garbage. Reported by Dr. Ines Haldorsen with a beautifully minimal reproducer (#1031).
- `fern_mpi_finalize()` no longer deadlocks when called after a failed `MPI_Comm_split` (#1029)

## [2.4.1] - 2026-10-02

### Fixed

* Wheels for `manylinux_2_28_aarch64` were built without OpenMP, which made `fernsolve` up to 8× slower on the Grace nodes than the x86_64 build (#1019).
* Typo in the docstring of `fernsolve.precond.ILUT`: `droptol` is relative to the 2-norm of the row, not the ∞-norm.

## [2.4.0] - 2026-09-15

### Added

- **Mixed-precision iterative refinement** (`fernsolve.refine`): factorise in `float32` (or `bfloat16` on GPUs that support it), refine in `float64`. Converges whenever $\kappa_\infty(A)\,u_f < 1$, where $u_f$ is the unit roundoff of the factorisation precision; see Carson & Higham (2018) and the [user guide section on refinement][refine-docs].
- Block CG for multiple right-hand sides:

  ```python
  from fernsolve import krylov
  X, info = krylov.block_cg(A, B, M=precond, rtol=1e-10, maxiter=500)
  ```

- New `fernsolve-bench` command line tool.
  It replaces the old `scripts/bench.py` and writes results as CSV *and* as a Markdown table.

### Changed

1. Minimum supported versions: CMake 3.24, Python 3.10, NumPy 1.25, MPI 3.1.
2. `SolverInfo.converged` is now a `bool`, not an `int`. Code doing `if info.converged == 1:` still works; code doing `info.converged is 1` (please don't) does not.
3. Wheels are built against OpenBLAS 0.3.28.

### Deprecated
- `fernsolve.gmres(..., orthog="mgs")` -- pass `arnoldi=ArnoldiOptions(orthog="mgs")` instead. The keyword will be removed in 3.0.

### Performance

The CSR SpMV kernel for matrices with fewer than 8 nonzeros per row now uses a vectorised segmented reduction. Speed-ups on a single larch node (2× AMD EPYC 9654, 192 cores):

<!-- fmt: off -->
| matrix (SuiteSparse)  |      n |    nnz | 2.3.2 (GFlop/s) | 2.4.0 (GFlop/s) | speed-up |
|:----------------------|-------:|-------:|----------------:|----------------:|---------:|
| `G3_circuit`          |  1.59M |  7.66M |            41.2 |            63.9 |    1.55× |
| `thermal2`            |  1.23M |  8.58M |            44.0 |            61.3 |    1.39× |
| `ecology2`            |  1.00M |  5.00M |            37.5 |            66.1 |    1.76× |
<!-- fmt: on -->

## [2.3.2] - 2026-06-30
### Fixed
+ Segfault in `ilu0()` for matrices with an explicitly stored zero on the diagonal; we now raise `ZeroPivotError` with the offending row index.
+ Thread safety of the global `fern::set_verbosity()` (#987).

## [2.3.1] - 2026-05-12

### Fixed

- Regression from 2.3.0: `rtol` was treated as an absolute tolerance by `bicgstab` when `x0` was given. The stopping criterion is again
  $$\frac{\|r_k\|_2}{\|b\|_2} \le \mathtt{rtol}$$
  for all solvers.
- `ResidualHistory.plot()` used a linear y-axis. It is log-scale again, as it should be for anything that converges geometrically.

## [2.3.0] - 2026-03-03

Big release, see the [migration notes](docs/migration/2.3.md) for details. Highlights:

* Algebraic multigrid preconditioner (`fernsolve.precond.AMG`, smoothed aggregation) with Chebyshev and $\ell_1$-Jacobi smoothers.
    * Coarse-grid solve via the direct solver of your choice (MUMPS, SuperLU_DIST, or our own dense LU for tiny coarse grids).
    * Setup is ~3× faster than PyAMG's on the same hierarchy, but we still recommend PyAMG for exploratory work.
* Dropped Python 3.8 and 3.9.

### Removed

- The `fernsolve.legacy` module (deprecated since 2.1).

## [2.0.0] - 2025-01-20

> **Note on versioning:** 2.0 broke the C ABI without breaking the C++ API, so strictly speaking only C users needed a major bump. We bumped everything to avoid confusing packagers (sorry, Spack maintainers).

First release under the new name (formerly `pyfern`).
The Python import name changed from `pyfern` to `fernsolve`; a shim package `pyfern==1.99` re-exports everything with a `DeprecationWarning`.

[2.0.0]: https://github.com/fernsolve/fernsolve/releases/tag/v2.0.0
[refine-docs]: https://fernsolve.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/refinement.html

# Changelog

All notable changes to **@acme/storefront** are documented here.
The format is (loosely 😅) based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) — except for the CSS, which adheres to nothing.

<!-- 
  Marketing folks: please add customer-facing notes under "Highlights". 
  Engineers: keep the PR links, the release bot scrapes them for the #launches post.
-->

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- ✨ Klarna "Pay in 3" badge on the PDP for orders between €35 and €1.500 ([#2291](https://github.com/acme/storefront/pull/2291))
- Mini-cart shows a free-shipping progress bar; the threshold comes from the CMS (`site_settings.free_shipping_threshold`), so marketing can change it without a deploy 
* `useRecommendations()` hook now accepts `{ slot, limit, fallback }`
- - [ ] screenshot of the Klarna badge for the release notes (@marketing)
### Fixed
- 🐛 Category grid showed `NaN` as the price for bundles with 0 components (#2304)
- Fixed CLS on the mobile PDP gallery — LCP went from 3.1s → 2.2s on the throttled Moto G4 profile


## [4.12.0] - 2026-11-03

### Highlights 🎄
> Black Friday prep release. Everything is feature-flagged; marketing can toggle it in the CMS under **Settings → Campaigns**.

* New **countdown banner** for the homepage hero, with a proper `<time>` element and a timezone-aware end date
* "Last chance" badge when stock < 5
    * only for SKUs with `inventory.track = true`
    * colour is `--color-badge-urgent` (#D7263D), approved by design in FIG-812
* Gift cards: €25 / €50 / €100 + custom amount (min €10, max €500)

### Price changes

The pricing team asked us to log these here as well as in the pricing sheet:

SKU | Product | Old price | New price | Change
:-- | --- | --: | --: | :-:
AUR-2-BLK-42 | Aurora Runner 2 (black) | €129,95 | €119,95 | ▼ 7.7%
AUR-2-WHT-43 | Aurora Runner 2 (white) | €129,95 | €119,95 | ▼ 7.7%
TEE-1-WHT-M | Organic tee | €19,95 | €22,95 | ▲ 15%
GFT-CARD-25 | Gift card €25 | €25,00 | €25,00 | —
HOM-MUG-SET4 | Stoneware mug set (4) | €34,99 | €29,99 | ▼ 14.3%

### Changed
- **BREAKING:** `formatPrice(amount, currency)` now expects **minor units** (cents). Migrate like this:

  ```diff
  - formatPrice(129.95, 'EUR')
  + formatPrice(12995, 'EUR')
  ```

- Upgraded Next.js 14.2 → 15.0.3; the `next/image` `domains` option is replaced by `remotePatterns` (see `next.config.mjs`)
-   Recs carousel moved behind `<Suspense>`; the skeleton now matches the card height, so no more layout jump when recommendations load slowly on 3G

### Fixed

arguments.content: --- title: "Contributing" linkTitle: Contributing weight: 90 description: > How to propose changes to the Acme marketing site and the shared CMS content models -- for engineers *and* for the marketing team. aliases: [/docs/contributing/, "/how-to-help"] tags: - process - onboarding --- # Contributing to acme-marketing 👋 Thanks for helping out! This repo powers **www.acme-shop.example** (marketing pages, campaign landing pages, the blog) and holds the content-model definitions for our headless CMS. Engineers, designers, copywriters and the occasional intern all commit here, so the rules below are deliberately boring. {{% pageinfo color="warning" %}} **Code freeze:** no merges to `main` between **Nov 24 and Dec 2** (Black Friday / Cyber Monday) unless it's a P1 fix approved in #web-incidents. {{% /pageinfo %}} ## TL;DR 1. Branch off `main` (`feat/…`, `fix/…`, `copy/…`) 1. `pnpm i && pnpm dev` → http://localhost:4321 1. Open a PR, fill in the template, tag **@acme/web-reviewers** 1. Wait for ✅ checks + 1 approval (2 for anything touching `src/lib/pricing`) ## Local setup You need Node 20 (we use [Volta](https://volta.sh), it picks the right version automatically), pnpm 9, and Docker if you want the CMS running locally. git clone git@github.com:acme/acme-marketing.git cd acme-marketing pnpm install cp .env.example .env.local # ask in #web-platform for the preview token If `pnpm dev` complains about `sharp`, run `pnpm rebuild sharp`. It's always sharp. The `Makefile` wraps the common stuff: ```make dev: ⇥pnpm dev --host seed: ⇥docker compose exec cms npm run seed -- --locale=en,nl,de ``` ## Commits & branches We use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/). The release bot reads them, so a typo = a missing changelog entry. | type | when | example | |------|------|---------| | `feat` | new page, component, CMS field | `feat(landing): add BF26 hero variant B` | | `fix` | bug | `fix(pricing): show €0,00 as "Free"` | | `copy` | text-only change by marketing | `copy(home): new USP strip wording` | | `chore` | deps, CI | `chore: bump astro to 4.16` | | `perf` | | `perf(img): serve AVIF for the hero` | ## Writing content (marketing team 💜) Most pages are Markdown with front matter in `src/content/`. Things that bite people: * **Prices** never go into copy as plain text. Use the shortcode so they update when the pricing team changes them: `{{< price sku="AUR-2-BLK-42" >}}` renders "€119,95" (or "~~€129,95~~ €119,95" during a promo). * Emoji are fine in headings and CTAs, max **one** per heading 🙏. No emoji in `` or the meta description -- Google strips some of them and it looks broken in the SERPs. * UTM parameters: lowercase, hyphens, no spaces → `utm_campaign=bf26-early-access`. - Links to products: use the slug, not the full URL (`/p/aurora-runner-2`); the build checks them. - external links get `rel="noopener"` automatically + Images: max 400 KB, WebP or AVIF, and **always** fill in `alt`. Decorative images get `alt=""`. Email templates live in `emails/` and use Liquid. Personalisation tokens like {{ customer.first_name | default: "there" }} and {{ cart.item_count }} are rendered by the ESP, not by us, and so are conditionals such as {% if customer.vip %}early access{% endif %} -- don't wrap them in backticks in the source or they'll end up in the inbox literally. {{< alert title="Heads up" color="info" >}} The CMS **content models** (`cms/models/*.json`) are code. Renaming a field breaks the storefront build until both PRs are merged, so coordinate in #web-platform first. {{< /alert >}} > **Tip:** landing pages can override the nav and the promo banner from front matter: > > ```yaml > title: "Black Friday 2026" > banner: {text: "Up to 40% off 🎉", variant: urgent ,ends_at: 2026-11-28T23:59:00+01:00} > nav: > hide: [ blog, about ] > ``` > > Anything else needs a component change. <p align="center"> <img src="docs/img/content-workflow.png" alt="Diagram: copy is written in Google Docs, pasted into the CMS, checked in preview mode, then published" width="640"> </p> ## Glossary PDP : Product detail page, `/p/{slug}`. PLP : Product listing page -- category grids and search results. SKU : Stock keeping unit. Format `FAM-GEN-COLOR-SIZE`, e.g. `AUR-2-BLK-42`; the size segment can be 1–3 characters. AOV : Average order value. Revenue ÷ orders, **excluding** gift cards and shipping. ## Pull request checklist - [ ] Screenshots (desktop **and** mobile) for visual changes - [ ] Lighthouse ≥ 90 on the changed page (`pnpm lh -- --url=/your-page`) - [x] I read this file - [ ] Copy reviewed by someone in #marketing-copy (legal-ish text: also tag @legal-web) - [ ] No hard-coded prices, SKUs or campaign dates - [ ] if you *really* need a date, put it in `src/data/campaigns.yaml` ## Code of conduct Be kind. We're a small team and everyone is busy in Q4. See [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)[^coc]. [^coc]: Adapted from the Contributor Covenant, version 2.1. Report problems to people-team@acme-shop.example, not in Slack.
