arguments.content:
# reviews_digest.R -------------------------------------------------------------
# Weekly store review digest for Sprout + Glowtide.
#
#   Rscript analysis/reviews_digest.R 2026-W46
#   quarto render analysis/reviews_digest.R -P week:2026-W46    # html report, uses the #| blocks
#
# Pulls reviews from App Store Connect + Google Play, tags them, posts a summary to
# Discord and opens GitHub issues for reviews that mention crashes.   -- priya, 2026-03

#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: FALSE
#| include : false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(purrr)
  library(stringr)
  library(lubridate)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(httr2)
  library(glue)
})

args  <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
week  <- if (length(args) >= 1) args[[1]] else strftime(Sys.Date() - 7, "%G-W%V")
since <- ISOweek::ISOweek2date(paste0(week, "-1"))

# fmt: markdown
# ## Where the reviews come from
#
# * **App Store**: App Store Connect API, `GET /v1/apps/{id}/customerReviews?sort=-createdDate`, 200 per page.  We page until we hit a review older than `since`.
# * **Google Play**: `reviews.list` from the Android Publisher API. It only returns reviews **with text** from the last 7 days, so if the cron job doesn't run for a week those reviews are gone for good (happened in March, see #298)
# *  Steam reviews for Glowtide are not pulled yet.
#
# Star ratings *without* text only show up in the aggregate numbers, which we don't use here.

APPS <- tribble(
  ~app,       ~store,        ~id,
  "sprout",   "app_store",   "6449021137",
  "sprout",   "google_play", "studio.lanternfish.sprout",
  "glowtide", "app_store",   "6452210980",
  "glowtide", "google_play", "studio.lanternfish.glowtide"
)

# Fetching ---------------------------------------------------------------------

#' App Store Connect JWT (ES256, valid for 20 minutes)
#' @noRd
asc_token <- function() {
  claim <- jose::jwt_claim(iss = Sys.getenv("ASC_ISSUER_ID"), aud = "appstoreconnect-v1", exp = as.integer(Sys.time()) + 1200)
  jose::jwt_encode_sig(claim, key = Sys.getenv("ASC_KEY_P8"), header = list(kid = Sys.getenv("ASC_KEY_ID")))
}

fetch_app_store <- function(id, since) {
  req <- request(glue("https://api.appstoreconnect.apple.com/v1/apps/{id}/customerReviews")) |>
    req_url_query(sort = "-createdDate", limit = 200, include = "response") |>
    req_auth_bearer_token(asc_token())
  pages <- list()
  repeat {
    resp <- req |> req_perform() |> resp_body_json()
    page <- map_dfr(resp$data, \(r) tibble(
      review_id = r$id, rating = r$attributes$rating, title = r$attributes$title,
      body = r$attributes$body, territory = r$attributes$territory, version = NA_character_,
      created = ymd_hms(r$attributes$createdDate),
      has_reply = !is.null(r$relationships$response$data)
    ))
    pages <- c(pages, list(page))
    if (nrow(page) == 0 || min(page$created) < since || is.null(resp$links[["next"]])) break
    req <- request(resp$links[["next"]]) |> req_auth_bearer_token(asc_token())
  }
  bind_rows(pages) |> filter(created >= since)
}

fetch_google_play <- function(id, since) {
  token <- gargle::credentials_service_account(
    scopes = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/androidpublisher",
    path   = Sys.getenv("PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON")
  )
  resp <- request(glue("https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com/androidpublisher/v3/applications/{id}/reviews")) |>
    req_url_query(maxResults = 100) |>
    req_auth_bearer_token(token$credentials$access_token) |>
    req_perform() |> resp_body_json()
  map_dfr(resp$reviews, \(r) {
    c1 <- r$comments[[1]]$userComment
    tibble(
      review_id = r$reviewId, rating = c1$starRating, title = NA_character_, body = str_trim(c1$text),
      territory = c1$reviewerLanguage, version = c1$appVersionName %||% NA_character_,
      created = as_datetime(as.numeric(c1$lastModified$seconds)),
      has_reply = length(r$comments) > 1
    )
  }) |> filter(created >= since)
}

#| label: fetch
#| cache: true
#| cache.extra: !expr week
reviews <- APPS |>
  mutate(data = map2(store, id, \(store, id) switch(store,
    app_store   = fetch_app_store(id, since),
    google_play = fetch_google_play(id, since)
  ))) |>
  select(-id) |>
  unnest(data)

# Tagging ----------------------------------------------------------------------
CRASH_WORDS <- c("crash", "freez", "absturz", "stürzt", "落ち", "강제 종료", "trava", "fecha sozinho")

tag_review <- function(text) {
  text <- str_to_lower(coalesce(text, ""))
  case_when(
    str_detect(text, str_c(CRASH_WORDS, collapse = "|")) ~ "crash",
    str_detect(text, "subscri|abo|price|preis|expensive|teuer|課金|サブスク") ~ "money",
    str_detect(text, "sync|icloud|backup|lost my|verloren")                  ~ "sync",
    .default = "other"
  )
}
reviews <- reviews |> mutate(tag = tag_review(paste(title, body)))

#| label: fig-rating-trend
#| fig-cap: "7-day rolling mean rating by store"
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of the seven day rolling mean star rating for Sprout on iOS and Android since June 2026. iOS stays between 4.5 and 4.7. Android drops from 4.4 to 4.1 after the 3.1.0 release on Aug 19 and recovers to 4.4 after 3.1.2."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-asp: .5
#| fig-format: [png, svg]
reviews |>
  filter(app == "sprout") |>
  group_by(store, day = as_date(created)) |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating), n = n(), .groups = "drop_last") |>
  mutate(rolling = slider::slide_dbl(rating, mean, .before = 6)) |>
  ggplot(aes(day, rolling, colour = store)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 5)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "rating (7-day mean)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# Posting ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# fmt: markdown
discord_template <- r"(

# reviews_digest.R -------------------------------------------------------------
# Weekly store review digest for Sprout + Glowtide.
#
#   Rscript analysis/reviews_digest.R 2026-W46
#   quarto render analysis/reviews_digest.R -P week:2026-W46    # html report, uses the #| blocks
#
# Pulls reviews from App Store Connect + Google Play, tags them, posts a summary to
# Discord and opens GitHub issues for reviews that mention crashes.   -- priya, 2026-03

#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: FALSE
#| include : false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(purrr)
  library(stringr)
  library(lubridate)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(httr2)
  library(glue)
})

args  <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
week  <- if (length(args) >= 1) args[[1]] else strftime(Sys.Date() - 7, "%G-W%V")
since <- ISOweek::ISOweek2date(paste0(week, "-1"))

# fmt: markdown
# ## Where the reviews come from
#
# * **App Store**: App Store Connect API, `GET /v1/apps/{id}/customerReviews?sort=-createdDate`, 200 per page.  We page until we hit a review older than `since`.
# * **Google Play**: `reviews.list` from the Android Publisher API. It only returns reviews **with text** from the last 7 days, so if the cron job doesn't run for a week those reviews are gone for good (happened in March, see #298)
# *  Steam reviews for Glowtide are not pulled yet.
#
# Star ratings *without* text only show up in the aggregate numbers, which we don't use here.

APPS <- tribble(
  ~app,       ~store,        ~id,
  "sprout",   "app_store",   "6449021137",
  "sprout",   "google_play", "studio.lanternfish.sprout",
  "glowtide", "app_store",   "6452210980",
  "glowtide", "google_play", "studio.lanternfish.glowtide"
)

# Fetching ---------------------------------------------------------------------

#' App Store Connect JWT (ES256, valid for 20 minutes)
#' @noRd
asc_token <- function() {
  claim <- jose::jwt_claim(iss = Sys.getenv("ASC_ISSUER_ID"), aud = "appstoreconnect-v1", exp = as.integer(Sys.time()) + 1200)
  jose::jwt_encode_sig(claim, key = Sys.getenv("ASC_KEY_P8"), header = list(kid = Sys.getenv("ASC_KEY_ID")))
}

fetch_app_store <- function(id, since) {
  req <- request(glue("https://api.appstoreconnect.apple.com/v1/apps/{id}/customerReviews")) |>
    req_url_query(sort = "-createdDate", limit = 200, include = "response") |>
    req_auth_bearer_token(asc_token())
  pages <- list()
  repeat {
    resp <- req |> req_perform() |> resp_body_json()
    page <- map_dfr(resp$data, \(r) tibble(
      review_id = r$id, rating = r$attributes$rating, title = r$attributes$title,
      body = r$attributes$body, territory = r$attributes$territory, version = NA_character_,
      created = ymd_hms(r$attributes$createdDate),
      has_reply = !is.null(r$relationships$response$data)
    ))
    pages <- c(pages, list(page))
    if (nrow(page) == 0 || min(page$created) < since || is.null(resp$links[["next"]])) break
    req <- request(resp$links[["next"]]) |> req_auth_bearer_token(asc_token())
  }
  bind_rows(pages) |> filter(created >= since)
}

fetch_google_play <- function(id, since) {
  token <- gargle::credentials_service_account(
    scopes = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/androidpublisher",
    path   = Sys.getenv("PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON")
  )
  resp <- request(glue("https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com/androidpublisher/v3/applications/{id}/reviews")) |>
    req_url_query(maxResults = 100) |>
    req_auth_bearer_token(token$credentials$access_token) |>
    req_perform() |> resp_body_json()
  map_dfr(resp$reviews, \(r) {
    c1 <- r$comments[[1]]$userComment
    tibble(
      review_id = r$reviewId, rating = c1$starRating, title = NA_character_, body = str_trim(c1$text),
      territory = c1$reviewerLanguage, version = c1$appVersionName %||% NA_character_,
      created = as_datetime(as.numeric(c1$lastModified$seconds)),
      has_reply = length(r$comments) > 1
    )
  }) |> filter(created >= since)
}

#| label: fetch
#| cache: true
#| cache.extra: !expr week
reviews <- APPS |>
  mutate(data = map2(store, id, \(store, id) switch(store,
    app_store   = fetch_app_store(id, since),
    google_play = fetch_google_play(id, since)
  ))) |>
  select(-id) |>
  unnest(data)

# Tagging ----------------------------------------------------------------------
CRASH_WORDS <- c("crash", "freez", "absturz", "stürzt", "落ち", "강제 종료", "trava", "fecha sozinho")

tag_review <- function(text) {
  text <- str_to_lower(coalesce(text, ""))
  case_when(
    str_detect(text, str_c(CRASH_WORDS, collapse = "|")) ~ "crash",
    str_detect(text, "subscri|abo|price|preis|expensive|teuer|課金|サブスク") ~ "money",
    str_detect(text, "sync|icloud|backup|lost my|verloren")                  ~ "sync",
    .default = "other"
  )
}
reviews <- reviews |> mutate(tag = tag_review(paste(title, body)))

#| label: fig-rating-trend
#| fig-cap: "7-day rolling mean rating by store"
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of the seven day rolling mean star rating for Sprout on iOS and Android since June 2026. iOS stays between 4.5 and 4.7. Android drops from 4.4 to 4.1 after the 3.1.0 release on Aug 19 and recovers to 4.4 after 3.1.2."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-asp: .5
#| fig-format: [png, svg]
reviews |>
  filter(app == "sprout") |>
  group_by(store, day = as_date(created)) |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating), n = n(), .groups = "drop_last") |>
  mutate(rolling = slider::slide_dbl(rating, mean, .before = 6)) |>
  ggplot(aes(day, rolling, colour = store)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 5)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "rating (7-day mean)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# Posting ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# Contributing to varcall

Thanks for helping out! `varcall` is the germline short-variant calling pipeline (FASTQ → aligned CRAM → gVCF → joint-called, filtered VCF) used by the Mensah lab and the Northfield Genomics Core. It is written in Nextflow DSL2, with small Python and R helpers under `bin/`, and runs on the larch Slurm cluster, on the lab's Kubernetes namespace and -- with some patience -- on a laptop.

This document is for people *changing* the pipeline. If you only want to run it, read [README.md](README.md) and `docs/usage.md` instead.

**Contents**

1. [Ground rules](#ground-rules)
2. [Development environment](#development-environment)
3. [Tests](#tests)
4. [Adding or updating a module](#adding-or-updating-a-module)
5) [Commit messages and merge requests](#commit-messages-and-merge-requests)
6) [Releasing](#releasing)

Ground rules
------------

* Never commit patient-identifiable data. Test data under `tests/data/` is either synthetic or from the public **GIAB HG002** sample, downsampled to ~2× around chr20:10,000,000-12,000,000. If you are not 100 % sure a file is OK to share, ask Dr. Mensah *before* pushing; rewriting git history is painful and does not un-leak anything.
* All changes go through a merge request against `dev`; `main` only moves on releases.
- Results must stay reproducible: an MR that changes any output VCF needs a justification in its description and an updated truth set (see [Tests](#tests)).
*   Be kind in reviews. Most contributors are PhD students with a thesis to write.

## Development environment

We use [pixi](https://pixi.sh) for Nextflow itself and the Python/R helpers, and containers (Apptainer on larch, Docker elsewhere) for the bioinformatics tools:

```bash
git clone git@git.northfield.ac.uk:mensah-lab/varcall.git
cd varcall
pixi install            # nextflow, nf-test, python 3.12, R 4.4, pre-commit
pixi run pre-commit install
```

On larch, do this on a login node but run anything heavier than `nf-test` in an interactive job (`salloc -p short -c 8 --mem=32G -t 2:00:00`). The login nodes kill processes that use more than 4 GB of RAM, and you *will* hit that with GATK.

> [!WARNING]
> Do **not** keep the Apptainer cache in your home directory: home has a 50 GB quota and a single DeepVariant image is 6 GB. Put
> `export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR=/scratch/$USER/.apptainer` in your `~/.bashrc`.

## Tests ##

There are three layers of tests:

1. **Unit tests** for the helper scripts (`pytest` for Python, `testthat` for R):

   ```bash
   pixi run pytest bin/tests -q
   pixi run Rscript -e 'testthat::test_dir("bin/tests/testthat")'
   ```
2. **Module tests** with [nf-test](https://www.nf-test.com/), one per module under `modules/local/*/tests/`. Run all of them with `nf-test test --profile apptainer`, or only the one you changed:
    ```bash
    nf-test test modules/local/deepvariant/tests/main.nf.test --profile apptainer
    ```
3. **End-to-end** test on the GIAB subset. It takes ~25 min on 4 nodes and runs nightly in CI, but please run it yourself if you touch anything in `subworkflows/`:

       sbatch --wait tests/e2e/run_e2e.sbatch
       python tests/e2e/compare_to_truth.py results/e2e/HG002.vcf.gz --truth tests/data/HG002_chr20_truth.vcf.gz --min-f1 0.995

   The comparison uses `hap.py`. An MR may lower SNV F1 by at most 0.001 and indel F1 by at most 0.003 without a discussion; anything more needs sign-off from the Core.

### Making new test data

If you need reads for a new region, downsample from the full 35× HG002 BAM rather than committing big files. To get a target coverage $c_t$ from an original coverage $c_0$, keep each read pair with probability $p = c_t / c_0$, e.g. $p = 2/35 \approx 0.057$ for 2×:

```bash
samtools view -b --subsample 0.057 --subsample-seed 42 HG002.GRCh38.35x.bam chr20:10000000-12000000 > HG002_chr20_2x.bam
```

Expected coverage after subsampling is $c_t$ only on average; for small regions check it with `mosdepth` and redraw with another seed if it is off by more than 10 %.

The `Makefile` in `tests/data/` regenerates everything (recipes must be indented with a tab, not spaces):

```make
HG002_chr20_2x.bam: $(SRC_BAM)
⇥samtools view -b --subsample 0.057 --subsample-seed 42 $< chr20:10000000-12000000 > $@
⇥samtools index $@
```

## Adding or updating a module

Every module lives in `modules/local/<tool>/` and needs a `main.nf`, a `meta.yml` and at least one nf-test. CI validates `meta.yml` against `assets/schema_module.json`, so stick to this layout:

```yaml
name: deepvariant_callvariants
description:  Call variants from a CRAM with DeepVariant (on a GPU if one is available)
keywords: [ variant calling, deep learning,gvcf ]
tools:
    - deepvariant:
        description: "DeepVariant is an analysis pipeline that uses a deep neural network to call genetic variants from next-generation DNA sequencing data."
        homepage: https://github.com/google/deepvariant
        licence: ['BSD-3-Clause']
input:
  - meta:
      type: map
      description: Groovy map with sample information, e.g. `[ id:'HG002', sex:'XY' ]`
  - cram: {type: file, pattern: "*.cram"}
output:
  - vcf: {type: file, pattern: "*.vcf.gz"}
  - gvcf:
      type: file
      pattern: "*.g.vcf.gz"
authors: ["J. Ortiz", 'K. Mensah']
```

Please **don't** pin tool versions in `meta.yml` the way the old template did; they go stale immediately and the container tag is the single source of truth:

```yaml fmt: skip
tools:
  - deepvariant:
      version:   1.6.1     # <- no!
      container: "google/deepvariant:1.6.1-gpu"
```

<details>
<summary>Why Nextflow and not Snakemake?</summary>

We get asked this a lot. Short answer: the Core's other pipelines are Nextflow, and the Kubernetes executor was the deciding factor back in 2022. Long answer: see the discussion in [issue 14](https://git.northfield.ac.uk/mensah-lab/varcall/-/issues/14).

</details>

## Commit messages and merge requests

We use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/), mostly so that `git-cliff` can write the changelog for us:

| type | use it for | bumps |
|------|-----------|-------|
| `feat` | new module, new parameter | minor |
| `fix` | wrong results, crashes | patch |
| `perf` | faster or leaner, **identical** output | patch |
| `chore`, `ci`, `docs`, `test` | everything else | -- |

When you open an MR, GitLab pre-fills this template (`.gitlab/merge_request_templates/Default.md`). Please actually fill it in:

````markdown
## What does this change?

<!-- one or two sentences, plus the issue number -->

## Checklist
- [ ] `nf-test test` passes locally (or on larch: paste the Slurm job ID)
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` updated under *Unreleased*
-  [ ] If outputs change: hap.py comparison attached and F1 deltas filled in below
* [ ] Reviewed by someone who did not write it

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| SNV F1 |  |  |
| indel F1 | | |
````

## Releasing

Only maintainers (currently J. Ortiz and K. Mensah) cut releases:

0. Make sure the nightly end-to-end run on `dev` is green.
1. Bump `manifest.version` in `nextflow.config` and move the *Unreleased* changelog entries under the new version.
2. Merge `dev` into `main`, tag `vX.Y.Z`, and push the tag; CI builds and pushes the containers.
3. Announce the release in the Core's Teams channel with a link to the changelog.\
   If any output changed, say so explicitly.

By contributing you agree that your contributions are licensed under the MIT licence[^licence].

***

[^licence]: The containers we build include tools under other licences (GATK and DeepVariant are BSD-3-Clause, `samtools` is MIT/Expat). That does not affect the licence of the pipeline code itself.

tools:
  - deepvariant:
      version:   1.6.1     # <- no!
      container: "google/deepvariant:1.6.1-gpu"
```

<details>
<summary>Why Nextflow and not Snakemake?</summary>

We get asked this a lot. Short answer: the Core's other pipelines are Nextflow, and the Kubernetes executor was the deciding factor back in 2022. Long answer: see the discussion in [issue 14](https://git.northfield.ac.uk/mensah-lab/varcall/-/issues/14).

</details>

## Commit messages and merge requests

We use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/), mostly so that `git-cliff` can write the changelog for us:

| type | use it for | bumps |
|------|-----------|-------|
| `feat` | new module, new parameter | minor |
| `fix` | wrong results, crashes | patch |
| `perf` | faster or leaner, **identical** output | patch |
| `chore`, `ci`, `docs`, `test` | everything else | -- |

When you open an MR, GitLab pre-fills this template (`.gitlab/merge_request_templates/Default.md`). Please actually fill it in:

````markdown
## What does this change?

<!-- one or two sentences, plus the issue number -->

## Checklist
- [ ] `nf-test test` passes locally (or on larch: paste the Slurm job ID)
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` updated under *Unreleased*
-  [ ] If outputs change: hap.py comparison attached and F1 deltas filled in below
* [ ] Reviewed by someone who did not write it

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| SNV F1 |  |  |
| indel F1 | | |
````

Only maintainers (currently J. Ortiz and K. Mensah) cut releases:

0. Make sure the nightly end-to-end run on `dev` is green.
1. Bump `manifest.version` in `nextflow.config` and move the *Unreleased* changelog entries under the new version.
2. Merge `dev` into `main`, tag `vX.Y.Z`, and push the tag; CI builds and pushes the containers.
3. Announce the release in the Core's Teams channel with a link to the changelog.\

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# ---
# jupyter:
#   jupytext:
#     formats: ipynb,py:percent
#     text_representation:
#       extension: .py
#       format_name: percent
#       format_version: '1.3'
#   kernelspec:
#     display_name: cmorph-pp (py3.12)
#     language: python
#     name: cmorph-pp
# ---

# %% [markdown]
# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
# # SST anomalies from CMIP6 `tos` on a common 1° grid
#
# Post-processing step 2 of the **cmorph-pp** chain (Climate Analytics Group, Northfield). Takes native-grid monthly `tos` from the ESGF mirror, regrids it conservatively to a regular 1° grid with xESMF, and writes anomalies relative to the 1981–2010 climatology. For every member the anomaly in month $m$ of year $y$ at cell $(i,j)$ is
#
# $$
# T'_{ij}(y,m) = T_{ij}(y,m) - \frac{1}{30}\sum_{y'=1981}^{2010} T_{ij}(y',m),
# $$
#
# and the global mean is area-weighted over ocean cells of the *target* grid, i.e. $\overline{T'} = \sum_{ij} A_{ij} T'_{ij} / \sum_{ij} A_{ij}$ (cf. Eyring et al. 2016 for the CMIP6 protocol).
#
# Run it interactively (Jupytext pairs it with `sst_anomalies.ipynb`) or as a batch job:
#
#     sbatch -p short -c 32 --mem=120G --wrap "python sst_anomalies.py --source-id CanESM5 --experiment ssp245"
#
# * Inputs are **never** modified; outputs go to `$CMORPH_OUT/<source_id>/<experiment>/`.
# * Regridding weights are cached in `$CMORPH_WEIGHTS` (one file per source grid, ~200 MB each), reuse them!
#   Recomputing the weights for a 0.25° ocean grid takes ~20 min on 32 cores.

# %%
#| label: imports
#| jupyter: {source_hidden: true, outputs_hidden: False}
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import dask
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr
import xesmf as xe
from dask.distributed import Client, LocalCluster

__version__ = "2026.11.0"
log = logging.getLogger("cmorph.sst")

# %%
#| label: parameters
#| tags:
#|     - parameters
#| params:
#|   source_id:   CanESM5
#|   experiment: ssp245
#|   members: [r1i1p1f1, r2i1p1f1,r3i1p1f1]
#|   grid: "1x1"
#|   ref_period: [ 1981, 2010 ]
#| description: >
#|   Defaults for interactive use only. The batch wrapper overrides all of these from the command line,
#|   so do not put anything site-specific (paths!) in here.
SOURCE_ID = "CanESM5"
EXPERIMENT = "ssp245"
MEMBERS = ["r1i1p1f1", "r2i1p1f1", "r3i1p1f1"]
GRID = "1x1"
METHOD = "conservative_normed"
REF_START, REF_END = 1981, 2010
MIN_OCEAN_FRAC=0.5  # fmt: skip

# Ocean model + coordinate names per source_id. Hand-aligned on purpose; ruff, keep out.
# fmt: off
NATIVE_GRIDS = {
    #  source_id          ocean model       nominal res.   lon / lat names
    "CanESM5":          ("NEMO3.4.1",      "1deg",        ("longitude", "latitude")),
    "MPI-ESM1-2-HR":    ("MPIOM1.63",      "0.4deg",      ("longitude", "latitude")),
    "IPSL-CM6A-LR":     ("NEMO-OPA",       "1deg",        ("nav_lon",   "nav_lat")),
    "UKESM1-0-LL":      ("NEMO3.6",        "1deg",        ("longitude", "latitude")),
    "GFDL-CM4":         ("MOM6",           "0.25deg",     ("lon",       "lat")),
}
# fmt: on

# fmt: markdown
EPILOG = r"""
## Notes

Anomalies are computed **per member** and only then averaged, never the other way round: when members have different missing months, the climatology of the ensemble mean is not the ensemble mean of the climatologies.

Drift correction (`--dedrift`) fits a quadratic $d(t) = a + b\,t + c\,t^2$ to the matching `piControl` segment and subtracts it. Use it for models whose $|\Delta T|$ drift exceeds 0.1 K per century, cf. Table 2 of the validation report.

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--grid` | `1x1` | target grid, `1x1` or `0.25x0.25` |
| `--method` | `conservative_normed` | any xESMF method; *bilinear* is wrong for SST near coasts |
| `--dedrift` | off | subtract the piControl drift |
"""

# Global attributes for every output file (CF-1.10 + our provenance fields).
# fmt: json
GLOBAL_ATTRS = """
{"Conventions": "CF-1.10", "institution": "University of Northfield, Climate Analytics Group",
   "source": "CMIP6 tos, regridded with xESMF", "license": "CC BY 4.0",
 "references": "Lindqvist et al. (2026), cmorph-pp validation report", "product_version": "2026.11.0"}
"""


def parse_args(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="cmorph-sst", description="Regrid CMIP6 tos and compute SST anomalies.",
                                epilog=EPILOG, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--source-id", default=SOURCE_ID, choices=sorted(NATIVE_GRIDS))
    p.add_argument("--experiment", default=EXPERIMENT, choices=["historical", "ssp126", "ssp245", "ssp370", "ssp585"])
    p.add_argument("--members", nargs="+", default=MEMBERS)
    p.add_argument("--grid", default=GRID, choices=["1x1", "0.25x0.25"])
    p.add_argument("--method", default=METHOD)
    p.add_argument("--ref-start", type=int, default=REF_START)
    p.add_argument("--ref-end", type=int, default=REF_END)
    p.add_argument("--dedrift", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="count", default=0)
    return p.parse_args(argv)


def start_dask() -> Client:
    """Size a LocalCluster from the Slurm allocation, if there is one."""
    ncpu = int(os.environ.get("SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK", os.cpu_count() or 4))
    nworkers = max(ncpu // 4, 1)
    mem = os.environ.get("SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE")  # MB
    cluster = LocalCluster(n_workers=nworkers, threads_per_worker=4,
                           memory_limit=f"{int(mem) // nworkers}MB" if mem else "auto",
                           local_directory=os.environ.get("TMPDIR", "/tmp"))
    return Client(cluster)


def open_member(source_id: str, experiment: str, member: str) -> xr.Dataset:
    root = Path(os.environ.get("CMIP6_ROOT", "/data/cmip6")) / "CMIP6"
    activity = "CMIP" if experiment == "historical" else "ScenarioMIP"
    files = sorted(root.glob(f"{activity}/*/{source_id}/{experiment}/{member}/Omon/tos/*/latest/*.nc"))
    if not files:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no tos files for {source_id}/{experiment}/{member} under {root}")
    return xr.open_mfdataset(files, combine="by_coords", chunks={"time": 120}, use_cftime=True, parallel=True)


# %% [markdown]
# fmt: markdown
# ## Regridding
#
# xESMF's `conservative_normed` renormalises by the unmasked fraction of each target cell, which is what we want for a field that only exists over the ocean.  Plain `conservative` biases coastal cells low (towards 0 °C!) because land counts as zero.
# Weights depend only on the source grid, so they are cached per `source_id`.

# %%
#| label: regrid
#| echo: true
#| # fmt: compact
#| tags:
#|   - core
#|   - slow
def regrid(ds: xr.Dataset, grid_spec: str, method: str, source_id: str) -> xr.DataArray:
    d = {"1x1": 1.0, "0.25x0.25": 0.25}[grid_spec]
    target = xe.util.grid_global(d, d, cf=True)
    wdir = Path(os.environ.get("CMORPH_WEIGHTS", "/scratch/cmorph/weights"))
    wfile = wdir / f"{source_id}_{method}_{grid_spec}.nc"
    regridder = xe.Regridder(ds, target, method, periodic=True, ignore_degenerate=True,
                             filename=str(wfile), reuse_weights=wfile.exists())
    return regridder(ds["tos"], keep_attrs=True)


def anomalies(tos: xr.DataArray, ref: tuple[int, int]) -> xr.DataArray:
    clim = tos.sel(time=slice(f"{ref[0]}-01-01", f"{ref[1]}-12-31")).groupby("time.month").mean("time")
    return (tos.groupby("time.month") - clim).drop_vars("month")


def global_mean(da: xr.DataArray) -> xr.DataArray:
    w = np.cos(np.deg2rad(da.lat))   # regular lat-lon => cell area ∝ cos(lat)
    return da.weighted(w).mean(("lat", "lon"))


def provenance_note(args: argparse.Namespace, n_files: int) -> str:
    """README.md written next to the output files."""
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    # fmt: markdown
    return f"""
# Provenance: {args.source_id} / {args.experiment}

Generated by `cmorph-sst` {__version__} on {now:%Y-%m-%d %H:%M} UTC from {len(args.members)} member(s) ({", ".join(args.members)}) and {n_files} input files. Regridded to the {args.grid} grid with xESMF `{args.method}`; anomalies are relative to {args.ref_start}–{args.ref_end}.

* drift correction: {"quadratic fit to piControl" if args.dedrift else "none"}
* software:   xarray {xr.__version__}, xesmf {xe.__version__}, dask {dask.__version__}, numpy {np.__version__}
"""


# %%
#| label: main
#| eval: false
def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING - 10 * args.verbose, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
    client = start_dask()
    log.info("dask dashboard: %s", client.dashboard_link)
    out = Path(os.environ.get("CMORPH_OUT", "/scratch/cmorph/out")) / args.source_id / args.experiment
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    attrs = json.loads(GLOBAL_ATTRS) | {"history": f"{datetime.now(timezone.utc):%FT%TZ} cmorph-sst {' '.join(sys.argv[1:])}"}
    n_files = 0
    for member in args.members:
        ds = open_member(args.source_id, args.experiment, member)
        n_files += len(ds.encoding.get("source", "x").split(","))
        anom = anomalies(regrid(ds, args.grid, args.method, args.source_id), (args.ref_start, args.ref_end))
        anom = anom.rename("tos_anom").assign_attrs(units="K", long_name="sea surface temperature anomaly")
        anom.to_dataset().assign_attrs(attrs).to_netcdf(out / f"tos_anom_{member}_{args.grid}.nc",
                                                         encoding={"tos_anom": {"zlib": True, "complevel": 4}})
        log.info("%s: global-mean anomaly in last year %.3f K", member, float(global_mean(anom)[-12:].mean()))
    (out / "README.md").write_text(provenance_note(args, n_files), encoding="utf-8")
    client.close()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    out = Path(os.environ.get("CMORPH_OUT", "/scratch/cmorph/out")) / args.source_id / args.experiment

[![Mobile release](https://github.com/lanternfish/studio/actions/workflows/mobile-release.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/lanternfish/studio/actions/workflows/mobile-release.yml) [![Unity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Unity-2022.3.49f1_LTS-222?logo=unity&logoColor=white)](https://unity.com/releases/editor/whats-new/2022.3.49) [![beacon coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/lanternfish/studio/branch/main/graph/badge.svg?flag=beacon)](https://codecov.io/gh/lanternfish/studio) [![Discord][discord-badge]][discord] This is the monorepo for everything [Lanternfish Games](https://lanternfish.studio) ships: * **Glowtide** — a tide-and-light puzzle adventure made in Unity, on the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/glowtide/id6452210980) and [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=studio.lanternfish.glowtide). Steam version "soon™". * **Sprout** — a plant-care journal, native SwiftUI on iOS and Jetpack Compose on Android. Free, with an optional *Sprout+* subscription. * **beacon** — a small FastAPI service: leaderboards, receipt validation, remote config and push. + `fastlane/` — release automation shared by all of the above > **Heads-up:** the repo uses Git LFS for art and audio (~6 GB). Run `git lfs install` before cloning or Unity will import a few thousand pointer files and you will have a bad afternoon. ## Contents ## 1. [Repo layout](#repo-layout) 2. [Quick start](#quick-start) 3. [Building & releasing](#building--releasing) 4. [Store metadata](#store-metadata) 5. [FAQ](#faq) ## Repo layout | Path | What | Stack | Owner | |------|------|-------|-------| | `games/glowtide/` | Glowtide | Unity 2022.3 LTS, C#, URP, Addressables | Tomás | | `apps/sprout-ios/` | Sprout for iOS | Swift 5.10, SwiftUI, iOS 16+ | Jun | | `apps/sprout-android/` | Sprout for Android | Kotlin 2.0, Compose, minSdk 26 | Priya | | `services/beacon/` | backend | Python 3.12, FastAPI, Postgres 16, Redis | Priya, Mira | | `fastlane/` | release automation + store metadata | Ruby, fastlane 2.225 | Mira | | `docs/` | the handbook (MkDocs Material) | Markdown | everyone 🙃 | ## Quick start ```sh git lfs install git clone git@github.com:lanternfish/studio.git cd studio && bundle install && cp .env.example .env docker compose up -d # beacon on http://localhost:8000/docs ``` Then, depending on what you're working on: - **Glowtide**: open `games/glowtide` in Unity Hub (exact editor version: 2022.3.49f1), let it import (≈ 25 min cold, ≈ 3 min with the office Accelerator), open `Scenes/Boot.unity` and press Play. - **Sprout iOS**: `open apps/sprout-ios/Sprout.xcodeproj` and select the *Sprout (Dev)* scheme. Signing is handled by `match`; run `bundle exec fastlane match development --readonly` once. - **Sprout Android**: open `apps/sprout-android` in Android Studio. Debug builds talk to `http://10.0.2.2:8000`, which is the emulator's view of your localhost. On a real device use `adb reverse tcp:8000 tcp:8000`. ## Building & releasing Everything goes through fastlane, locally and on CI. The full checklist is in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#release-checklist); the short version: ```sh bundle exec fastlane ios beta app:sprout # → TestFlight bundle exec fastlane android beta app:glowtide # → Play internal track bundle exec fastlane android promote app:glowtide track:production rollout:0.05 ```
Unity command-line builds (what CI does) ```sh "/Applications/Unity/Hub/Editor/2022.3.49f1/Unity.app/Contents/MacOS/Unity" \ -batchmode -nographics -quit \ -projectPath games/glowtide \ -buildTarget Android \ -executeMethod Lanternfish.Build.BuildScript.BuildFromCI \ -logFile - ``` `BuildScript.BuildFromCI` reads the version from the git tag (`glowtide-v1.8.1` → `1.8.1`) and computes the build number, see the comment at the top of `games/glowtide/CHANGELOG.md`.

One PR can now change `beacon` and both apps. **Can I run beacon without Docker?** Yes: `uv run --directory services/beacon uvicorn beacon.main:app --reload`, but you need Postgres 16 and Redis running somewhere and `DATABASE_URL` / `REDIS_URL` set. **Where are the signing certificates?** In the private `lanternfish/certificates` repo, encrypted with `match`. Ask Mira for the passphrase; never export a `.p12` and send it on Discord again (you know who you are). **Why is the App Store build number so big?**\ See the formula in the changelog header. Acme Storefront 🛍️

The Next.js storefront, headless-CMS integration & recommendation widgets behind acme-shop.example

[![CI](https://github.com/acme/storefront/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/acme/storefront/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/acme/storefront/branch/main/graph/badge.svg?token=AbC123xYz)](https://codecov.io/gh/acme/storefront) [![Lighthouse perf](https://img.shields.io/badge/lighthouse-94-brightgreen?logo=lighthouse)](https://lighthouse.acme-shop.example) ![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D20-339933?logo=node.js&logoColor=white) ![pnpm](https://img.shields.io/badge/pnpm-9-F69220?logo=pnpm&logoColor=white) [![Storybook](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/storybookjs/brand@main/badge/badge-storybook.svg)](https://storybook.acme-shop.example)
> [!IMPORTANT] > **Code freeze:** Nov 24 – Dec 2 (BF/CM). Only P1 fixes, approved in `#web-incidents`. ## Table of contents - [What's in here](#whats-in-here) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Environment](#environment) - [Pricing & SKUs](#pricing--skus) - [Recommendations](#recommendations) - [Deploying](#deploying) - [FAQ](#faq) What's in here -------------- ``` apps/ storefront/ Next.js 15 (app router) -- the shop marketing/ Astro landing pages + blog packages/ ui/ React components + Storybook pricing/ formatPrice, rounding, VAT cms-client/ typed client for the headless CMS services/ recs/ FastAPI recommendation service (python) ``` ## Quick start **Prereqs:** Node ≥ 20, pnpm 9, Docker Desktop (for CMS + Postgres + recs). ```bash pnpm install docker compose up -d cms db redis recs # ~2 min the first time ☕ pnpm --filter @acme/storefront dev ``` Then open . Log in to the CMS at http://localhost:1337/admin with `admin@acme.test` (password is in 1Password → *Web / CMS local*). Press Ctrl + Shift + P → **Toggle price debug overlay** to see which promo rule produced a price. Super handy when marketing asks "why is this €3 cheaper on mobile??" ## Environment | Variable | Required | Default | Description | |:---------|:--------:|---------|-------------| | `NEXT_PUBLIC_CMS_URL` | ✅ | `http://localhost:1337` | Public CMS URL (also used by the image loader) | | `CMS_API_TOKEN` | ✅ | — | Read-only token, get it from 1Password → *Web / CMS* | | `RECS_URL` | | `http://localhost:8081/v1` | Recommendation service | | `NEXT_PUBLIC_CURRENCY` | | `EUR` | One of `EUR`, `GBP`, `SEK` | | `NEXT_PUBLIC_FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD` | | `49.00` | In **major** units here (legacy 🙈) | | `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | ✅ prod | | Never commit this. Seriously. | ## Pricing & SKUs Prices are stored in **minor units**. `formatPrice(12995, 'EUR', 'nl-NL')` → `€ 129,95`. Rounding rules per market:
MarketEnds inExample
🇳🇱 NL / 🇩🇪 DE,95€ 119,95
🇬🇧 UK.99£ 99.99
🇸🇪 SEwhole kronor1 299 kr
Sample catalogue used by the seed script & Storybook: | SKU | Product | Price (EUR) | Stock | Badge | |----------------|-----------------------------|------------:|------:|--------------| | AUR-2-BLK-42 | Aurora Runner 2 — black | 119,95 | 14 | `-8%` | | AUR-2-WHT-43 | Aurora Runner 2 — white | 119,95 | 0 | sold out | | TEE-1-WHT-M | Organic tee \| white, M | 22,95 | 230 | 🌱 eco | | HOM-MUG-SET4 | Stoneware mug set (4) | 29,99 | 41 | | | GFT-CARD-50 | Gift card | 50,00 | ∞ | 🎁 | SKU anatomy: `AUR-2-BLK-42` = family `AUR` · generation `2` · colour `BLK` · size `42`. Sizes are *strings* (`42.5`, `XL`, `OS` for one-size), never numbers -- `parseInt("42.5")` already cost us one very confused customer. Promo prices by campaign (from `packages/pricing/fixtures/promos.json`): Campaign | SKU | Regular | Promo | Depth --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: BF26 early access | AUR-2-BLK-42 | €129,95 | €103,95 | 20 % BF26 early access | HOM-MUG-SET4 | €34,99 | €24,49 | 30 % CM26 | TEE-1-WHT-M | €22,95 | €17,95 | 22 % ## Recommendations The carousels (`pdp-similar`, `cart-upsell`, `home-for-you`) call `services/recs` through the BFF. Locally the recs service serves a **fake model** that returns bestsellers, unless you set `RECS_MODEL=two_tower_v3` and have AWS credentials for the model bucket.
How do I debug a weird recommendation? 🤔 1. Add `?recs_debug=1` to any URL — each card gets a tooltip with score + strategy 2. Check the `X-Recs-Model` response header 3. Still weird? Post the URL and a screenshot in `#recs-help`. Include your **segment** (shown in the debug overlay), otherwise we can't reproduce it.
## Deploying * PRs → Vercel preview, the URL is posted by the bot * `main` → staging (automatic) * tag `storefront@x.y.z` → production 🚀 ```bash pnpm changeset version && git push --follow-tags ``` * Hotfix? Branch from the tag, see [docs/hotfix.md](docs/hotfix.md). > [!WARNING] > Don't deploy on Fridays after 15:00 CET unless you're also on call this weekend. :pray: ## FAQ **Why is the price different in Storybook?** Storybook uses the seed catalogue above, not live pricing. :shrug: **Can marketing change banner text without a deploy?** Yes! Banners, USPs and the countdown live in the CMS (*Settings → Campaigns*). Changes go live within 60 s thanks to ISR[^isr]. **Who do I ask about…** + pricing → @acme/pricing + CMS models → @acme/web-platform + recommendations → @acme/recs-squad (Slack: `#recs-help`) [^isr]: Incremental Static Regeneration -- pages revalidate every 60 seconds; product pages also revalidate on demand via a CMS webhook. *** Made with ☕ and too many `console.log`s by the Acme Web team · we're hiring

arguments.content:
---
title: "Sprout — Q3 2026 ratings, reviews & the 3.2 paywall test"
author: "Priya Raman, Jun Watanabe"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    code_folding: hide
    df_print: paged
  github_document: default
params:
  quarter: "2026-Q3"
  min_reviews: 20
  paywall_test_id: pw-annual-first
editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: console
  markdown:
    wrap: sentence
    canonical: true
    references:
      location: section
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.retina = 2)
library(dplyr); library(ggplot2); library(gt)
reviews <- readRDS(here::here("data", "reviews_2026Q3.rds"))
paywall <- readr::read_csv(here::here("data", paste0("paywall_", params$paywall_test_id, ".csv")), show_col_types = FALSE)
n_reviews <- nrow(reviews)
```

## Summary

Sprout ended Q3 2026 with an average rating of 4.62 on the App Store (n = 1,184 new ratings) and 4.31 on Google Play (n = 2,907), i.e. roughly flat on iOS vs. Q2 and down 0.12 on Android. The Android dip is almost entirely explained by v3.1.0, which shipped on Aug. 19 with a widget bug on Samsung One UI 6.1 devices; after the fix in v3.1.2 (Aug. 27) the 7-day average went back to approx. 4.4 within ten days. We also ran the paywall test `pw-annual-first` from Sept. 1 to Sept. 28, which showed the annual plan ($39.99/yr, i.e. ~33% cheaper than 12 × $4.99) before the monthly one. It increased trial starts by 11.8% (95% CI 4.1%–19.9%) and did not measurably change the number of 1★ reviews mentioning "subscription", "price", "Abo" etc. Recommendation: ship variant B to 100% in v3.2.1 and keep monitoring refunds through Q4.

There were `r n_reviews` reviews with text in total. Of these, 412 were in English, 233 in German and the rest spread over 9 other locales (mostly ja, ko, pt-BR and fr). Dr. Ana Pereira (our pt-BR translator, a.k.a. the reason Sprout has 4.8★ in Brazil) went through the Portuguese ones by hand; everything else was tagged with the keyword rules in `R/tag_reviews.R`, v2.3. The rules are deliberately simple. They miss sarcasm, e.g. "great, another subscription app..." is tagged as positive, but a manual check of 200 random reviews found only 6 mislabeled ones (3.0%).

## Ratings by version

```{r ratings-by-version, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Average star rating by app version, iOS and Android. Versions with fewer than 20 ratings are hidden."}
reviews |>
  group_by(platform, version) |>
  filter(n() >= params$min_reviews) |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(version, rating, fill = platform)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(3.5, 5))
```

Fig. 1 shows the average rating per version for both platforms. Versions with fewer than `r params$min_reviews` ratings are hidden, because e.g. v3.0.3 (a two-day hotfix) only got 7 ratings on iOS. Note that Apple lets users keep their rating across versions unless they change it, so the iOS numbers lag behind the actual experience by approx. 2–3 weeks; Google does __not__ do that. In the U.S. App Store the share of 5★ ratings went from 71.4% to 74.0%. Most of them arrived after the in-app rating prompt moved from "after 3 days" to "after the 5th watered plant", which we shipped in v3.1.0 (see PR #388). Was it worth it? Probably, yes!

The version breakdown also shows something we did not expect: v3.1.1 on Android has a _lower_ average (3.94) than v3.1.0 (4.02), even though it fixed nothing and broke nothing. It turns out v3.1.1 was the version most people were on when the widget bug hit them, since Play updates roll out over approx. 7 days and many users updated straight from 3.0.x to 3.1.1. In other words the ratings are attached to the version installed at review time, not the version that caused the problem. We'll keep that in mind before blaming a release for a dip again.

## The paywall test

The test ran on new installs only, split 50/50 by a hash of the Firebase installation ID, with n = 8,417 in variant A (monthly first) and n = 8,392 in variant B (annual first). Trial-start rate went from 6.43% to 7.19%. That's +0.76 pp, or +11.8% relative, p = 0.004 using a two-sided two-proportion z-test[^method]. Conversion from trial to paid after 7 days is still preliminary: 41.0% vs. 42.3%, and the CI is wide (approx. −2.9 to +5.5 pp), so we can't say much yet. Revenue per install in the first 28 days was €0.61 vs. €0.74 on Google Play and $0.83 vs. $0.97 on the App Store, before Apple's/Google's 15% cut (Small Business Program).

| Variant | Installs | Trial starts | Rate | Paid after 7 d |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| A — monthly first | 8,417 | 541 | 6.43% | 41.0% |
| B — annual first | 8,392 | 603 | 7.19% | 42.3% |

A few caveats, roughly in order of how much they worry us:

1. The test overlapped with the back-to-school sale on Sept. 9–15 (−30% on the annual plan in the U.S., U.K., CA and AU only). Both variants got the sale, but variant B shows the annual price first, so it likely benefited more. Excluding that week, the uplift shrinks to +8.9% and is no longer significant at the 1% level (p = 0.021).
2. Android users on One UI 6.1 were over-represented in A after Sept. 20 because of a bucketing bug in v3.1.3 (fixed in v3.1.4, see `RemoteConfigClient.kt`, l. 212). It affected approx. 300 installs. We re-ran the analysis without them and nothing changed beyond the 2nd decimal.
3. Seven days is short for a subscription app. Our trial is 7 days, so "paid after 7 d" really means "did not cancel during the trial", nothing more. Refunds typically come in weeks 2–6.

> "I'd pay for this if it didn't nag me every time I open it. Update: the new screen is fine, it only shows up once. 4 stars." — Google Play review, en-GB, Sept. 14, v3.1.3

```{r paywall-ci}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
ci <- prop.test(x = c(603, 541), n = c(8392, 8417), correct = FALSE)$conf.int
cat(sprintf("Absolute difference in trial-start rate: %.2f to %.2f pp (95%% CI).", 100 * ci[1], 100 * ci[2]))
```

## Reviews mentioning the subscription

We tagged 1★ and 2★ reviews with the keyword list from last quarter (subscription, Abo, 課金, price, Preis, expensive, teuer, etc.). The share of low ratings mentioning money went from 22% in Q2 to 19% in Q3, which is within the noise for n ≈ 340. Jun read all 61 of them; the most common complaint (17 reviews) is that the free tier only allows 5 plants, not the price itself. Mr. Lund suggested raising the limit to 8 plants. That's a product decision rather than a stats one, so it goes to the planning meeting on Oct. 6 at 10 a.m. CET.

* iOS: 1★/2★ share 6.2% → 5.8%. Most complaints are about iCloud sync (fixed in v3.2.0) and the widget not updating on iOS 18.0.x. The widget issue is Apple's (FB15022183) and it's fixed in iOS 18.1.
* Android: 1★/2★ share 9.9% → 11.4%, mostly v3.1.0 widget crashes. Excluding Aug. 19–27 it's 8.7%, i.e. better than Q2.
   Samsung devices account for 58% of those, vs. 41% of our Android installs overall.

## Next steps

- Ship variant B (annual first) to 100% in v3.2.1 and freeze the paywall until Dec. 1 so the refund numbers stay clean.
- Re-run this report for Q4 with the same `min_reviews` threshold. Black Friday (Nov. 27) falls into Q4, so expect the trial-start rate to be inflated for approx. one week; we'll report it with and without that week, like the back-to-school sale above.
- Ask the ja translator about "課金" vs. "サブスク" in the keyword list. It might be missing ~10% of the relevant reviews, which would matter more than anything else in this section.
- Reply to the 40 unanswered 1★ reviews from Aug. 19–27 (template in the handbook, under *Support → Store replies*). Replies can move a rating: in Q2, 14 of 52 users we replied to updated their rating, on average by +1.6★.

[^method]: Two-proportion z-test with pooled variance, computed with `prop.test(correct = FALSE)`. We did not correct for multiple comparisons since there is only one primary metric (trial-start rate). Secondary metrics are reported for context only, e.g. paid conversion, revenue per install etc.

There were `r n_reviews` reviews with text in total. Of these, 412 were in English, 233 in German and the rest spread over 9 other locales (mostly ja, ko, pt-BR and fr). Dr. Ana Pereira (our pt-BR translator, a.k.a. the reason Sprout has 4.8★ in Brazil) went through the Portuguese ones by hand; everything else was tagged with the keyword rules in `R/tag_reviews.R`, v2.3. The rules are deliberately simple. They miss sarcasm, e.g. "great, another subscription app..." is tagged as positive, but a manual check of 200 random reviews found only 6 mislabeled ones (3.0%).

## Ratings by version

```{r ratings-by-version, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Average star rating by app version, iOS and Android. Versions with fewer than 20 ratings are hidden."}
reviews |>
  group_by(platform, version) |>
  filter(n() >= params$min_reviews) |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(version, rating, fill = platform)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(3.5, 5))
```

Fig. 1 shows the average rating per version for both platforms. Versions with fewer than `r params$min_reviews` ratings are hidden, because e.g. v3.0.3 (a two-day hotfix) only got 7 ratings on iOS. Note that Apple lets users keep their rating across versions unless they change it, so the iOS numbers lag behind the actual experience by approx. 2–3 weeks; Google does __not__ do that. In the U.S. App Store the share of 5★ ratings went from 71.4% to 74.0%. Most of them arrived after the in-app rating prompt moved from "after 3 days" to "after the 5th watered plant", which we shipped in v3.1.0 (see PR #388). Was it worth it? Probably, yes!

The version breakdown also shows something we did not expect: v3.1.1 on Android has a _lower_ average (3.94) than v3.1.0 (4.02), even though it fixed nothing and broke nothing. It turns out v3.1.1 was the version most people were on when the widget bug hit them, since Play updates roll out over approx. 7 days and many users updated straight from 3.0.x to 3.1.1. In other words the ratings are attached to the version installed at review time, not the version that caused the problem. We'll keep that in mind before blaming a release for a dip again.

## The paywall test

The test ran on new installs only, split 50/50 by a hash of the Firebase installation ID, with n = 8,417 in variant A (monthly first) and n = 8,392 in variant B (annual first). Trial-start rate went from 6.43% to 7.19%. That's +0.76 pp, or +11.8% relative, p = 0.004 using a two-sided two-proportion z-test[^method]. Conversion from trial to paid after 7 days is still preliminary: 41.0% vs. 42.3%, and the CI is wide (approx. −2.9 to +5.5 pp), so we can't say much yet. Revenue per install in the first 28 days was €0.61 vs. €0.74 on Google Play and $0.83 vs. $0.97 on the App Store, before Apple's/Google's 15% cut (Small Business Program).

| Variant | Installs | Trial starts | Rate | Paid after 7 d |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| A — monthly first | 8,417 | 541 | 6.43% | 41.0% |
| B — annual first | 8,392 | 603 | 7.19% | 42.3% |

A few caveats, roughly in order of how much they worry us:

1. The test overlapped with the back-to-school sale on Sept. 9–15 (−30% on the annual plan in the U.S., U.K., CA and AU only). Both variants got the sale, but variant B shows the annual price first, so it likely benefited more. Excluding that week, the uplift shrinks to +8.9% and is no longer significant at the 1% level (p = 0.021).
2. Android users on One UI 6.1 were over-represented in A after Sept. 20 because of a bucketing bug in v3.1.3 (fixed in v3.1.4, see `RemoteConfigClient.kt`, l. 212). It affected approx. 300 installs. We re-ran the analysis without them and nothing changed beyond the 2nd decimal.
3. Seven days is short for a subscription app. Our trial is 7 days, so "paid after 7 d" really means "did not cancel during the trial", nothing more. Refunds typically come in weeks 2–6.

> "I'd pay for this if it didn't nag me every time I open it. Update: the new screen is fine, it only shows up once. 4 stars." — Google Play review, en-GB, Sept. 14, v3.1.3

```{r paywall-ci}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
ci <- prop.test(x = c(603, 541), n = c(8392, 8417), correct = FALSE)$conf.int
cat(sprintf("Absolute difference in trial-start rate: %.2f to %.2f pp (95%% CI).", 100 * ci[1], 100 * ci[2]))
```

## Reviews mentioning the subscription

We tagged 1★ and 2★ reviews with the keyword list from last quarter (subscription, Abo, 課金, price, Preis, expensive, teuer, etc.). The share of low ratings mentioning money went from 22% in Q2 to 19% in Q3, which is within the noise for n ≈ 340. Jun read all 61 of them; the most common complaint (17 reviews) is that the free tier only allows 5 plants, not the price itself. Mr. Lund suggested raising the limit to 8 plants. That's a product decision rather than a stats one, so it goes to the planning meeting on Oct. 6 at 10 a.m. CET.

* iOS: 1★/2★ share 6.2% → 5.8%. Most complaints are about iCloud sync (fixed in v3.2.0) and the widget not updating on iOS 18.0.x. The widget issue is Apple's (FB15022183) and it's fixed in iOS 18.1.
* Android: 1★/2★ share 9.9% → 11.4%, mostly v3.1.0 widget crashes. Excluding Aug. 19–27 it's 8.7%, i.e. better than Q2.
   Samsung devices account for 58% of those, vs. 41% of our Android installs overall.

## Next steps

- Ship variant B (annual first) to 100% in v3.2.1 and freeze the paywall until Dec. 1 so the refund numbers stay clean.
- Re-run this report for Q4 with the same `min_reviews` threshold. Black Friday (Nov. 27) falls into Q4, so expect the trial-start rate to be inflated for approx. one week; we'll report it with and without that week, like the back-to-school sale above.
- Ask the ja translator about "課金" vs. "サブスク" in the keyword list. It might be missing ~10% of the relevant reviews, which would matter more than anything else in this section.
- Reply to the 40 unanswered 1★ reviews from Aug. 19–27 (template in the handbook, under *Support → Store replies*). Replies can move a rating: in Q2, 14 of 52 users we replied to updated their rating, on average by +1.6★.

[^method]: Two-proportion z-test with pooled variance, computed with `prop.test(correct = FALSE)`. We did not correct for multiple comparisons since there is only one primary metric (trial-start rate). Secondary metrics are reported for context only, e.g. paid conversion, revenue per install etc.

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
#SBATCH --job-name=covqc
#SBATCH --partition=short
#SBATCH --array=1-96%24
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --time=01:30:00
#SBATCH --output=logs/%x_%A_%a.out

# coverage_qc.R -- per-sample coverage QC from mosdepth output (Mensah lab, varcall pipeline)
#
# Usage, one array task per sample (the sample list has one path prefix per line):
#   sbatch --export=ALL,SAMPLES=batches/2026_11.txt bin/coverage_qc.R
# or render the whole batch as an HTML report:
#   quarto render bin/coverage_qc.R -P batch:2026_11

#' # Coverage QC for a sequencing batch
#'
#' This script doubles as a `knitr::spin()` report: lines starting with `#'` are Markdown and `#|` lines are chunk options.

#| label: setup
#| include: false
#| message:   FALSE
#| warning: no
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(glue)
})
options(datatable.print.nrows = 20, warn = 1)

# fmt: markdown
# ## QC thresholds
#
# A sample **passes** if all of the following hold (agreed with the Genomics Core in Nov. 2025):
#
# | metric | threshold | why |
# |---|---|---|
# | median autosomal coverage | ≥ 30× | DeepVariant sensitivity drops quickly below ~25× (cf. Poplin et al. 2018) |
# | fraction of bases ≥ 20× | ≥ 0.90 | |
# | chrX / autosome ratio | consistent with the reported sex | catches sample swaps |
# | coverage CV | ≤ 0.35 | a high CV usually means GC bias or degraded DNA |
#
# Samples between 20× and 30× are flagged `LOW` but still called; below 20× they `FAIL` and need re-sequencing.
# The coefficient of variation is computed over 1 kb bins as $\mathrm{CV} = \sigma / \mu$, excluding bins in the ENCODE blacklist (Amemiya et al. 2019).
THRESHOLDS <- list(
  median_cov  = 30,     # LOW below this
  hard_min    = 20,     # FAIL below this
  frac_ge20   = 0.90,
  cv_max      = 0.35,
  x_ratio_xx  = c(0.85, 1.15),
  x_ratio_xy  = c(0.40, 0.60)
)

# fmt: markdown
help_md <- r"---[
Per-sample coverage QC for **varcall** batches.

Reads `<prefix>.mosdepth.summary.txt` and `<prefix>.regions.bed.gz` (1 kb bins) for every sample listed in `$SAMPLES` and writes `<prefix>.covqc.tsv`. When run as a Slurm array job, task *i* processes line *i* of the sample list; otherwise all samples are processed one after the other, which takes about 40 s per 30× genome.

-   `SAMPLES`: path to the sample list (default `samples.txt`)
-   `SEX_TABLE`: optional TSV with columns `sample` and `sex` (`XX`/`XY`) from the sample sheet
]---"

# Batch summary, posted as a comment on the sequencing-run issue in GitLab.
# Placeholders are filled by glue::glue(), hence the {braces}.
# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
summary_template <- r"(
## Coverage QC: batch {batch}

{n_pass} of {n_total} samples passed, {n_low} are `LOW` (20–30×) and {n_fail} `FAIL` (< 20×). Median coverage across the batch was {median_cov}× (IQR {iqr_lo}–{iqr_hi}×). Samples flagged `SEX_MISMATCH` must be checked against the sample sheet before anything else is done with them, since a swap always affects two samples.

{fail_table}

Re-sequencing requests go to the Core via the usual form, please link this issue. Plots: `{plot_path}`
)"

# Appended to each task's log so a single sample can be re-run outside Slurm.
# fmt: r
rerun_snippet <- "
source('bin/coverage_qc.R')
res <- qc_sample(prefix='%s',  sex = NA)
print(res[ , .(sample,median_cov,frac_ge20,cv,status)])
"

read_mosdepth <- function(prefix) {
  summ <- fread(paste0(prefix, ".mosdepth.summary.txt"))
  bins <- fread(paste0(prefix, ".regions.bed.gz"), col.names = c("chrom", "start", "end", "depth"))
  list(summary = summ, bins = bins)
}

qc_sample <- function(prefix, sex = NA_character_, thresholds = THRESHOLDS) {
  md <- read_mosdepth(prefix)
  auto <- md$bins[chrom %in% paste0("chr", 1:22)]
  med <- median(auto$depth)
  cv <- sd(auto$depth) / mean(auto$depth)
  frac20 <- mean(auto$depth >= 20)
  x_ratio <- median(md$bins[chrom == "chrX"]$depth) / med
  expected <- switch(sex %||% "unknown", XX = thresholds$x_ratio_xx, XY = thresholds$x_ratio_xy, c(0, Inf))
  status <- fcase(
    med < thresholds$hard_min, "FAIL",
    x_ratio < expected[1] | x_ratio > expected[2], "SEX_MISMATCH",
    med < thresholds$median_cov | frac20 < thresholds$frac_ge20 | cv > thresholds$cv_max, "LOW",
    default = "PASS"
  )
  data.table(sample = basename(prefix), median_cov = med, frac_ge20 = frac20, cv = cv,
             x_ratio = x_ratio, status = status)
}

#' ## Run
#'
#' In array mode exactly one sample is processed and the script exits; the summary and plots below are only produced when the whole batch is processed in one go (interactively or via `quarto render`).

#| label: run
#| eval: !expr '!interactive() || nzchar(Sys.getenv("SAMPLES"))'
samples <- readLines(Sys.getenv("SAMPLES", "samples.txt"))
task <- Sys.getenv("SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID", unset = NA)
if (!is.na(task)) {
  prefix <- samples[as.integer(task)]
  res <- qc_sample(prefix)
  fwrite(res, paste0(prefix, ".covqc.tsv"), sep = "\t")
  message(sprintf(rerun_snippet, prefix))
  quit(save = "no", status = 0L)
}
res <- rbindlist(lapply(samples, qc_sample))

#| label: fig-coverage
#| fig-cap: "Median autosomal coverage per sample. Dashed: 30× target; dotted: 20× hard minimum."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height:  4
#| fig-alt: Bar chart of median coverage for every sample in the batch, coloured by QC status.
ggplot(res, aes(reorder(sample, median_cov), median_cov, fill = status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = THRESHOLDS$median_cov, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = THRESHOLDS$hard_min, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(PASS = "#1b9e77", LOW = "#d95f02", FAIL = "#7570b3", SEX_MISMATCH = "#e7298a")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "median coverage (×)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, size = 6))

#| label: summary
#| results: asis
#| R.options: {knitr.kable.NA: ''}
batch <- Sys.getenv("BATCH", basename(tools::file_path_sans_ext(Sys.getenv("SAMPLES", "batch"))))
q <- quantile(res$median_cov, c(0.25, 0.75))
fails <- res[status != "PASS"]
fail_table <- if (nrow(fails)) paste(knitr::kable(fails, digits = 2), collapse = "\n") else "_No samples flagged._"
summary_md <- glue(summary_template,
  n_pass = sum(res$status == "PASS"), n_total = nrow(res),
  n_low = sum(res$status == "LOW"), n_fail = sum(res$status == "FAIL"),
  median_cov = round(median(res$median_cov), 1), iqr_lo = round(q[[1]], 1), iqr_hi = round(q[[2]], 1),
  plot_path = file.path("qc", batch, "coverage.png"))
writeLines(summary_md, file.path("qc", batch, "summary.md"))
cat(summary_md)

--- title: "BF/CM 2025 Retrospective: Email, Paid Social & On-site Promos" subtitle: 'Input for the 2026 campaign plan (v0.3, DRAFT -- please do not forward)' author: - "M. de Groot, Growth Marketing" - "S. Okafor, Web Analytics" date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %b %Y')`" output: html_document: toc: yes toc_float: true number_sections: false df_print: kable code_folding: hide pdf_document: default params: start: 2025-11-21 end: 2025-12-02 currency: "EUR" bibliography: [refs.bib] editor_options: chunk_output_type: console markdown: wrap: sentence --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=5, dpi=150} knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE) library(dplyr); library(ggplot2); library(scales) orders <- readr::read_csv("data/orders_bfcm_2025.csv") spend <- readr::read_csv("data/paid_social_spend.csv") eur <- label_dollar(prefix = "€", big.mark = ".", decimal.mark = ",") ``` # 1. Executive summary BF/CM 2025 (Fri. Nov. 28 through Cyber Monday, Dec. 1) generated `r eur(sum(orders$net_revenue))` in net revenue, i.e. approx. 2.3x a normal four-day period and +14.6% vs. BF/CM 2024. Average order value (AOV) rose from €71.40 to €78.95, mostly because the "Bundle & Save" promo (3 items for the price of 2.5, e.g. socks, tees and mugs) pushed the average basket from 2.1 to 2.6 items. Conversion rate was flat at 3.9% on desktop but dropped to 2.2% on mobile web, which we attribute to the checkout outage on Sat. Nov. 29 between 10:12 a.m. and 11:47 a.m. CET (see Sec. 4.2 for the incident write-up by Dr. Patel's team). Paid social ROAS came in at 4.1 vs. a target of 5.0; Meta (Instagram + Facebook) was approx. 1.6 pts below plan, while TikTok over-delivered with a ROAS of 6.3, albeit on a small budget of ca. €18.5k. The U.K. store is excluded from all figures because it ran on the old platform until Jan. 2026. Email remained our strongest channel by far. The "Early Access" send to VIP members on Wed. Nov. 26 (approx. 41,200 recipients) had an open rate of 48.7% and a click rate of 9.2%! The subject-line test ("🔥 Your early access starts now" vs. "Psst... your BF prices are ready") was won by the second variant at p = 0.03, though the effect size was small (+0.8 pp). Was the emoji to blame? Probably not; Litmus showed it rendering as an empty box in Outlook 2016, which accounts for ca. 7% of the VIP list. We also learned that sending at 6:00 a.m. instead of 9:00 a.m. made no real difference (the St. Nicholas promo on Dec. 5–6 showed the same pattern, cf. Fig. 4). ## 1.1 What we'd keep, change and drop - **Keep: Bundle & Save.** It worked. Approx. 31% of orders contained a bundle, and margin per order was only 1.2 pts lower than for full-price orders, mostly due to the mug set (SKU HOM-MUG-SET4, reg. €34.99). - **Change: the free-shipping threshold.** We lowered it from €49 to €35 for the weekend. This cost approx. €22.4k in shipping subsidies vs. an estimated €61k in incremental revenue, i.e. a net positive, but see the caveat in Sec. 5 re. return rates. * **Drop: the sitewide countdown banner.** Ms. Alvarez from Brand asked whether it hurt LCP. It did, by ca. 180 ms on mobile (p75), which is still within budget... but it also pushed the hero CTA below the fold on iPhone SE-sized screens. Not worth it. # 2. On-site promotions The table below lists the top SKUs by net revenue during the promo window (Nov. 21 – Dec. 2). Prices are incl. VAT; "BF price" is the lowest price shown at any point, not the average. Gift cards are listed for completeness only. | SKU | Product | Reg. price | BF price | Units | Net revenue | |---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:| | AUR-2-BLK-42 | Aurora Runner 2, black | €129.95 | €103.95 | 1,284 | €110,310 | | HOM-MUG-SET4 | Stoneware mug set (4) | €34.99 | €24.49 | 3,950 | €79,940 | | TEE-1-WHT-M | Organic tee, white, M | €22.95 | €17.95 | 2,210 | €32,780 | | GFT-CARD-50 | Gift card €50 | €50.00 | €50.00 | 870 | n/a^1^ | ^1^ Gift cards are counted when redeemed, not when sold. ```{r revenue-by-day, fig.cap="Net revenue per day, BF/CM 2025 vs. 2024. Dashed line = 2024.", fig.alt="Line chart of daily net revenue in euros for both years", out.width="100%"} orders |> count(day = as.Date(created_at), year, wt = net_revenue) |> ggplot(aes(day, n, linetype = factor(year))) + geom_line() + scale_y_continuous(labels = eur) ``` Fig. 1 shows the usual shape: a spike on Friday at approx. 9 a.m., a dip on Saturday (the outage), and a long tail on Monday that peaks after 8 p.m. In 2024 the Monday peak was ca. 25% lower. We think the difference is mostly the "Cyber Monday Extra" email at 7:30 p.m., which had the best revenue per send of the whole campaign (€0.41 vs. a campaign avg. of €0.17). The vs. 2024 comparison is not like-for-like, though: in 2024 BF fell on Nov. 29, so the pre-BF "early access" window was one day shorter. > "Don't run another sitewide 30% off. Run fewer, deeper, category-specific deals." -- J. Smith, VP E-commerce, in the Dec. 4 debrief. We agree in principle. However, the data in Fig. 3 suggest that category deals cannibalised full-price sales in adjacent categories by approx. 6–9%, so "fewer, deeper" isn't free either. # 3. Paid social ```{r paid-social-roas, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=4, cache=TRUE} spend |> group_by(channel) |> summarise(roas = sum(attributed_revenue) / sum(spend)) |> ggplot(aes(reorder(channel, roas), roas)) + geom_col() + coord_flip() ``` Total paid social spend was €212k (Meta €171k, TikTok €18.5k, Pinterest €22.5k), i.e. approx. 9% over the original plan because the Meta budget was raised by 15% on Thu. Nov. 27 at 4 p.m. after a promising first day of early access. In hindsight that was a mistake: CPMs on Meta roughly doubled from Thu. to Fri. (from €6.10 to €12.40), and the extra budget mostly bought expensive impressions for people who'd already been reached 4–5 times. TikTok, on the other hand, was capped at €2k/day and hit the cap every day by noon. Should we have raised the TikTok cap instead? Probably yes, although the attribution window there is 7-day click / 1-day view, vs. Meta's 7-day click only, so the numbers aren't directly comparable (see the appendix of the Q3 report, pp. 12–14). ::: {.alert .alert-warning} **Attribution caveat.** All ROAS figures use platform-reported conversions, de-duplicated against GA4 with a 24 h window. They are almost certainly too optimistic, e.g. Meta claims 1.2M in revenue but GA4 last-click attributes only €640k to Meta. Use them for relative comparisons, not absolutes. ::: # 4. Incidents ## 4.2 Checkout outage, Sat. Nov. 29 The payment provider's 3-D Secure endpoint returned HTTP 502 for approx. 95 min. Checkout fell back to "try again later" instead of offering PayPal or iDEAL, which it should have done per the runbook (No. 7, "PSP degradation"). Estimated lost revenue: €48k–€63k, depending on how many of the 2,140 abandoned checkouts would have converted at the usual 31% rate. The fix (automatic fallback to alternative payment methods) shipped in storefront v4.12.0 on Nov. 3 of this year.\ Dr. Patel's full write-up is in Confluence; the short version is "test the fallback before the peak, not during it". # 5. Recommendations for 2026 1. Start early access on **Mon. Nov. 23** instead of Wed., and send it to the full VIP list (approx. 44k by then) at 7 a.m. CET. Keep the subject line short, emoji optional. 2. Keep Bundle & Save, but cap the mug set at 2 bundles per order. Last year one customer in Utrecht ordered 41 of them, which is, frankly, impressive. 3. Budget paid social by marginal ROAS, not by channel share. Concretely: start TikTok at €4k/day and move budget daily, not weekly. 4. Run a proper free-shipping threshold test (€35 vs. €49) in Oct., not during BF/CM itself, so we can measure the effect on return rates as well[^returns]. 5. Ask the U.S. team (Acme Retail Inc.) how they handled Thanksgiving week; their AOV was up 19.3% with much shallower discounts. [^returns]: Return rates for orders placed during BF/CM were 24.1% vs. 17.8% in a normal week. Orders that only crossed the free-shipping threshold because of a low-value add-on (e.g. a €4.95 pair of socks) were returned far more often. We have not yet checked whether this is causal.
Prepared by Growth Marketing & Web Analytics, Acme Retail B.V. Figures as of Dec. 3, 2025, 11:00 a.m.; preliminary until Finance closes the month.

--- title: "CMIP6 SST post-processing: validation of the 2026 ensemble refresh" subtitle: Regridding error, drift and anomaly checks for `cmorph-pp` 2026.11 author: - name: Astrid Lindqvist orcid: 0000-0002-1825-0097 email: a.lindqvist@northfield.ac.uk affiliations: - ref: nfld - name: "Tomás Ferreira-Okoye" affiliations: [ {ref: nfld}, {ref: hadley} ] affiliations: - id: nfld name: University of Northfield department: Dept. of Earth System Science - id: hadley name: Met Office Hadley Centre date: 2026-11-12 date-modified: last-modified abstract: | We validate step 2 of `cmorph-pp`, which regrids monthly CMIP6 sea-surface temperature (`tos`) from five models to a common 1° grid and converts it to anomalies. Conservative regridding changes the global-mean SST by less than 0.004 K in every model. Two models drift by more than our 0.1 K/century threshold in their control runs and are de-drifted before use. keywords: [CMIP6, sea surface temperature, regridding, xESMF,model drift] bibliography: references.bib csl: american-meteorological-society.csl lang: en-GB format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 3 number-sections: true code-fold: true html-math-method: katex fig-format: svg pdf: documentclass: scrartcl papersize: a4 geometry: - margin=2.5cm include-in-header: text: | \usepackage{siunitx} execute: echo: false warning: false cache: true jupyter: python3 crossref: eq-prefix: Eq. fig-prefix: Fig. --- {{< include _common.qmd >}} ## Summary {#sec-summary} ::: {.callout-important} ## Bottom line The regridded ensemble is fit for the detection-and-attribution work in WP3. Regridding changes the global-mean SST by **< 0.004 K** for every model (@tbl-regrid-error), the anomaly time series agree with the native-grid ones to within 0.01 K at every time step, and only `CanESM5` and `IPSL-CM6A-LR` need de-drifting (@sec-drift). ::: ## Data and models {#sec-data} We use monthly `tos` from the `historical` (1850–2014) and `ssp245`/`ssp585` (2015–2100) experiments of the five models in @tbl-models, three members each where available [@eyring2016; @oneill2016scenariomip]. Observations are HadISST [@rayner2003hadisst] and OISST v2.1 [@huang2021oisst, pp. 2923--2939], on their native $1^\circ$ and $0.25^\circ$ grids respectively. | Model | Ocean component | Native grid | Members | Ref. | |:--|:--|--:|:-:|---| | CanESM5 | NEMO3.4.1 (ORCA1) | ~1° | 3 | @swart2019canesm5 | | MPI-ESM1-2-HR | MPIOM1.63 (TP04) | 0.4° | 3 | @mueller2018mpiesm | | IPSL-CM6A-LR | NEMO-OPA (eORCA1) | ~1° | 3 | @boucher2020ipsl | | UKESM1-0-LL | NEMO3.6 (eORCA1) | ~1° | 2 | @sellar2019ukesm | | GFDL-CM4 | MOM6 | 0.25° | 1 | @held2019gfdlcm4 | : CMIP6 models in the ensemble refresh. "Members" counts realisations with complete historical *and* scenario output on our ESGF mirror as of 1 November 2026. {#tbl-models} ```{mermaid} %%| label: fig-pipeline %%| fig-cap: The cmorph-pp chain. This report covers step 2 only. flowchart LR A[ESGF mirror
native tos] --> B(step 1: CMOR checks) B --> C(step 2: regrid + anomalies) C --> D[(THREDDS)] C --> E(step 3: bias correction) ``` ## Methods {#sec-methods} ### Regridding Fields are regridded with xESMF [@zhuang2023xesmf] using first-order conservative remapping, normalised by the unmasked fraction of each target cell (`conservative_normed`). For a target cell $k$ that overlaps source cells $i$ with overlap areas $a_{ik}$ and ocean mask $m_i \in \{0, 1\}$, $$ \hat T_k = \frac{\sum_i a_{ik}\, m_i\, T_i}{\sum_i a_{ik}\, m_i}, $$ {#eq-conservative} which, unlike plain conservative remapping, does not pull coastal cells towards zero. The global integral $\sum_k A_k \hat T_k$ is conserved exactly only if no target cell is partially masked; the residual error is what @tbl-regrid-error quantifies. ### Anomalies and drift {#sec-drift} Anomalies are taken relative to each member's 1981–2010 monthly climatology (@eq-anomaly). Drift is estimated from the parallel `piControl` segment with a least-squares quadratic fit $d(t) = a + b\,t + c\,t^2$ and subtracted when $|b| > 0.1\,\mathrm{K\,century^{-1}}$^[We tried a linear fit first. It under-corrects `IPSL-CM6A-LR`, whose drift slows down after ~200 years of spin-up.]. $$ T'(y, m) = T(y, m) - \frac{1}{30} \sum_{y'=1981}^{2010} T(y', m) $$ {#eq-anomaly} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="55%"} All runs were done on larch[^larch] as one Slurm array, one task per model and experiment: ```{.bash filename="jobs/submit_step2.sh"} sbatch --array=0-14%5 --partition=short --cpus-per-task=32 --mem=120G \ --time=04:00:00 --job-name=pp-step2 jobs/step2.sbatch ``` ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} > Weights for the 0.25° GFDL grid took 19 min to build on 32 cores; every later run reused them from `$CMORPH_WEIGHTS`. ::: :::: [^larch]: 2× AMD EPYC 9654 per node, 768 GB RAM. Regridding is memory-bound, so we used 32 of the 192 cores per task and packed six tasks onto each node. ## Results ### Regridding error ```{python} #| label: tbl-regrid-error #| tbl-cap: "Difference in 1981–2010 global-mean SST (K), regridded minus native, per model. Negative values mean the regridded field is cooler." import pandas as pd err = pd.read_parquet("results/regrid_error.parquet") err.style.format("{:+.4f}").background_gradient(cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-0.005, vmax=0.005) ``` ```{python} #| label: fig-gmsst #| fig-cap: Global-mean SST anomaly relative to 1981–2010, ensemble mean ± 1σ. #| fig-subcap: #| - "Native grids" #| - Regridded to 1° #| layout-ncol: 2 #| fig-width: 6 #| fig-height: 3.5 import matplotlib.pyplot as plt ts = pd.read_parquet("results/gmsst_anom.parquet") for grid in ["native", "1x1"]: fig, ax = plt.subplots() for model, g in ts[ts.grid == grid].groupby("source_id"): ax.plot(g.year, g.anom, lw=0.8, label=model) ax.axhline(0, color="0.6", lw=0.5); ax.set_ylabel("ΔSST (K)"); ax.legend(fontsize=7, ncols=2) plt.show() ``` The two panels of @fig-gmsst are indistinguishable by eye; the largest difference in any annual mean is 0.009 K (`MPI-ESM1-2-HR`, 1883), well below interannual variability. ### Drift +---------------+-------------------+------------------------------------------+ | Model | Drift (K/century) | Action | +===============+===================+==========================================+ | CanESM5 | 0.23 | de-drifted (quadratic fit) | +---------------+-------------------+------------------------------------------+ | IPSL-CM6A-LR | −0.14 | de-drifted; member r3i1p1f1 also has a | | | | step change in 1922, flagged in the QC | +---------------+-------------------+------------------------------------------+ | others | < 0.05 | none | +---------------+-------------------+------------------------------------------+ : Control-run drift and what we did about it. {#tbl-drift} ```{python} #| label: drift-table-raw #| output: asis #| fmt: skip drift = pd.read_csv("results/drift.csv", index_col="source_id") print(drift.to_markdown(floatfmt=("", ".3f", ".3f", ".2e"), tablefmt="pipe")) ``` {{< pagebreak >}} ## Appendix: configuration {.appendix} The exact `cmorph-pp` configuration used for this report (`config/step2.yaml`, commit `4f9c2e1`): ```yaml version: 2026.11.0 regrid: method: conservative_normed grid: {name: 1x1, lon: [-180,180], lat: [-90, 90]} weights_dir: /scratch/cmorph/weights anomaly: reference: [1981,2010] per_member: yes drift: enabled: true models: [CanESM5, IPSL-CM6A-LR] fit: quadratic threshold_K_per_century: 0.1 output: {format: netcdf4, compression: {zlib: true, complevel: 4}} ``` ## References {.unnumbered} ::: {#refs} :::

for i,l in enumerate(lines):

EOF
