arguments.content: --- title: "Strong and weak scaling of pipelined GMRES in fernsolve on larch" subtitle: "RSE technical note TN-2026-07" author: - Ines Haldorsen - "Kwame O. Asante" - name: Research Software Engineering, University of Northfield date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%e %B %Y')`" output: bookdown::html_document2: toc: true number_sections: yes fig_caption: true df_print: kable bookdown::pdf_document2: latex_engine: lualatex keep_tex: no bibliography: [refs/krylov.bib, refs/hpc.bib] link-citations: yes params: results: "results/2026-11-03" baseline: "2.4.1" nodes: !r c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64) editor_options: markdown: wrap: sentence chunk_output_type: console --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache=FALSE, fig.align="center", dev="ragg_png", dpi=150} library(data.table) library(ggplot2) knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE) res <- fread(file.path(params$results, "scaling.csv")) ``` # Introduction {#intro} Krylov subspace methods spend most of their time in two kernels: the sparse matrix-vector product (SpMV) and the global reductions needed for inner products and norms. On a few nodes the SpMV dominates, but beyond approx. 16 nodes the reductions become latency-bound, since every `MPI_Allreduce` costs $\mathcal{O}(\log p)$ network hops regardless of message size (cf. the discussion in Ghysels et al. [-@ghysels2013pipelined], Sect. 2). Pipelined GMRES (p-GMRES) hides this latency by overlapping the reduction of iteration $k$ with the SpMV of iteration $k+1$, at the price of extra vector operations and somewhat weaker numerical stability. This note quantifies the trade-off for fernsolve v2.5.0-rc.1 on the larch cluster and compares it with the classical GMRES($m$) implementation in v`r params$baseline`. All timings are medians of 5 runs; the error bars in Fig. \@ref(fig:strong) show the min.–max. range. The test problem is the 3-D convection–diffusion equation $-\nabla\cdot(\kappa\nabla u) + \mathbf{w}\cdot\nabla u = f$ on the unit cube, discretised with 7-point finite differences, i.e. a nonsymmetric matrix with at most 7 nonzeros per row. We use Péclet numbers of 10 and 100 (resp. "mild" and "strong" convection), which give condition numbers of ca. $10^5$ and $10^7$ at the largest size. Unless stated otherwise the restart length is $m = 50$, the relative tolerance is $10^{-8}$, and the preconditioner is block Jacobi with one ILU(0) block per MPI rank, e.g. 64 blocks on a single node. Dr. Asante's earlier note (TN No. 2025-11) used $m = 30$ instead; the difference matters, see Sect. \@ref(results) and Tab. \@ref(tab:iters). # Setup {#setup} All runs used the `short` partition of larch: 2× AMD EPYC 9654 (96 cores each, 2.4 GHz base) and 768 GB of DDR5 per node, connected by HDR-200 InfiniBand in a non-blocking fat tree. We placed 64 MPI ranks per node with 3 OpenMP threads each, pinned with `--cpu-bind=cores`, and used Open MPI 4.1.6 with UCX 1.16 and GCC 13.2. The `MPI_Allreduce` latency for 8 B, measured with the OSU micro-benchmarks v7.4, grows from 2.1 µs on 2 nodes to 9.8 µs on 64 nodes, i.e. roughly as $\log_2 p$, as expected for a recursive-doubling algorithm. Nodes were allocated with `--exclusive` and `--switches=1@01:00:00` where possible, so most jobs ran within a single leaf switch; the 32- and 64-node runs necessarily span several. We report speed-up and parallel efficiency relative to the smallest run, \begin{equation} S(p) = \frac{T(p_0)}{T(p)}, \qquad E(p) = \frac{p_0\, S(p)}{p}, (\#eq:speedup) \end{equation} where $p_0 = 1$ node (192 cores) for strong scaling. For weak scaling we keep $n/p \approx 3.4 \times 10^6$ unknowns per node and report $E_w(p) = T(p_0)/T(p)$ instead, cf. Eq. \@ref(eq:speedup) with $S$ replaced by the time ratio. Note that $E$ can exceed 1 when the local problem starts to fit into the 384 MB of L3 cache per node, which happens at 32 nodes for $n = 2.0 \times 10^8$ (see below). # Results {#results} (ref:strong-cap) Strong scaling for $n = 2.0 \times 10^8$ (Pe = 100). Solid: p-GMRES; dashed: GMRES; grey: ideal. ```{r strong, fig.cap="(ref:strong-cap)", fig.width=7, fig.height=4, out.width="85%"} ggplot(res[kind == "strong"], aes(nodes, time_per_iter, linetype = solver)) + geom_line() + geom_point() + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = t_min, ymax = t_max), width = 0.05) + scale_x_continuous(trans = "log2", breaks = params$nodes) + scale_y_log10() + labs(x = "nodes", y = "time per iteration (s)") + theme_bw() ``` Fig. \@ref(fig:strong) shows that p-GMRES is no faster than GMRES up to 4 nodes, but on 64 nodes it reduces the time per iteration from 11.8 ms to 7.1 ms, i.e. by 40 %. The parallel efficiency at 64 nodes rises from 0.55 to 0.89 accordingly. This is consistent with the model of Ghysels et al. (2013, Eq. 12) and with the measurements of Sanan et al. [-@sanan2016pipelined] on a Cray XC40, although their speed-ups were larger (up to 2.5×) because the Aries network has a higher reduction latency than HDR InfiniBand. Is the extra cost of pipelining ever prohibitive? Not in our runs: the additional AXPY operations add approx. 6 % to the single-node time, which is within the run-to-run noise of ±4 %. Table: (\#tab:iters) Iterations to reach $\|r_k\|_2/\|b\|_2 < 10^{-8}$ for Pe = 100, by restart length. | nodes | GMRES(30) | GMRES(50) | p-GMRES(50) | |------:|----------:|----------:|------------:| | 1 | 412 | 298 | 301 | | 16 | 655 | 471 | 478 | | 64 | 803 | 560 | 571 | Tab. \@ref(tab:iters) shows the price in iterations. Block Jacobi weakens as the number of blocks grows (from 64 to 4,096), so all variants need more iterations at scale; p-GMRES needs 1–2 % more than GMRES because of the shifted basis, cf. Eqs. (3.4)–(3.6) in Ghysels et al. Increasing the restart length from 30 to 50 cuts iterations by approx. 30 % at every node count, at the cost of $50 \times 3.4 \times 10^6 \times 8\,\mathrm{B} \approx 1.4$ GB of extra basis storage per node, which is negligible on 768 GB nodes but not on the 256 GB nodes of the old `larch-legacy` partition. In total we ran `r nrow(res)` jobs, using approx. 9,800 node-hours. Two caveats apply. First, the runs at 32 and 64 nodes were done during the maintenance window on 2 Nov. 2026, when the rest of the machine was idle; on a busy system, network contention from other jobs typically adds 10–20 % to the reduction latency (cf. Fig. 7 in Chunduri et al. [-@chunduri2017runtime]), which would make pipelining *more* attractive, not less. Second, we did not tune the `UCX_TLS` and `UCX_RNDV_THRESH` settings, so the absolute numbers are probably pessimistic by a few percent. > In short: use p-GMRES on 16 nodes or more, and GMRES below that. The crossover moves to fewer nodes for smaller problems, e.g. ca. 8 nodes for $n = 5 \times 10^7$. # Weak scaling ```{r weak} #| fig.cap: "Weak-scaling efficiency $E_w(p)$ with $3.4 \\times 10^6$ unknowns per node." #| fig.width: 7 #| fig.height: 3.5 ggplot(res[kind == "weak"], aes(nodes, efficiency, colour = solver)) + geom_line() + geom_point() + scale_x_continuous(trans = "log2", breaks = params$nodes) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.1)) + theme_bw() ``` Weak scaling is less flattering for both methods, since the iteration count grows like $\mathcal{O}(h^{-1})$ for this preconditioner, so the total time grows even at perfect per-iteration efficiency. Per iteration, p-GMRES keeps $E_w > 0.8$ up to 64 nodes vs. 0.61 for GMRES. A two-level preconditioner (e.g. the smoothed-aggregation AMG from fernsolve 2.3, cf. Sect. 4 of the user guide) would remove the growth in iterations; that is the subject of TN-2026-09. # Recommendations 1. Default to `gmres_pipelined()` when running on 16 or more nodes, and keep `gmres()` below that. The automatic choice in `fernsolve.krylov.solve(..., method="auto")` now does exactly this (v2.5.0, PR #1051). 2. Use $m = 50$ unless memory is tight. On the legacy nodes, $m = 30$ is a reasonable compromise. 3. Re-run this study once the H100 partition supports GPU-aware MPI reductions; Prof. Lindqvist's group expects that by Q2 2027. All scripts, raw timings and the `sbatch` files are archived at .[^repro] [^repro]: The archive also contains the exact Spack environment (`spack.lock`). Rebuilding it on another system should give identical binaries, modulo the CPU target. We have not tried this on ARM. # References {-}

steps.message: I'll add a handful of realistic trailing spaces / whitespace-only lines with a small script that targets exact lines (and fails loudly if a target isn't found exactly once, unless told otherwise).

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/corpus6_tools/trail.py <<'EOF'
import sys
# (file, exact line content, suffix to append, occurrence index (0-based) or None for "must be unique")
EDITS = [
    ("ansible_playbook.yml", "  become: yes", " ", 0),
    ("ansible_playbook.yml", "      changed_when: false", "  ", None),
    ("ansible_playbook.yml", "    loop: \"{{ admin_users }}\"", "   ", 1),
    ("github_workflow.yml", "  pull_request:", " ", None),
    ("github_workflow.yml", "      - *checkout", " ", 0),
    ("github_workflow.yml", "          retention-days: 7", "    ", None),
    ("kubernetes_multi_document.yaml", "  replicas: 2", "   ", None),
    ("kubernetes_multi_document.yaml", "    # anti-cheat: anything above this per puzzle is rejected", " ", None),
    ("kubernetes_multi_document.yaml", "  ingressClassName: traefik", "  ", None),
    ("mkdocs_config.yml", "site_author: Lanternfish Games", "  ", None),
    ("mkdocs_config.yml", "    - icon: fontawesome/brands/mastodon", " ", None),
    ("openapi.yaml", "      operationId: listScores", "  ", None),
    ("openapi.yaml", "    Admin endpoints (not listed here) use a short-lived JWT from the studio SSO.", "  ", None),
    ("python_script.py", "    name = APPS[app][\"name\"]", "  ", 0),
    ("python_script.py", "# Lines starting with `Internal:` in the changelog are dropped, and so are issue numbers like `(#488)`.", " ", None),
    ("python_script.py", "#| fig-width: 9", "  ", None),
    ("r_script.R", "args  <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)", "  ", None),
    ("r_script.R", "#| fig-width: 8", "   ", None),
    ("r_script.R", "# Star ratings *without* text only show up in the aggregate numbers, which we don't use here.", " ", None),
    ("quarto_report.qmd", "## Installs", "  ", None),
    ("quarto_report.qmd", "#| fig-cap: Retention curves, 1.7.0 vs 1.8.0 cohorts (Android)", " ", None),
    ("quarto_report.qmd", "Definitions used in this section:", "   ", None),
    ("rmarkdown_sentence_wrap.Rmd", "## Summary", " ", None),
    ("rmarkdown_sentence_wrap.Rmd", "A few caveats, roughly in order of how much they worry us:", "  ", None),
    ("readme.md", "Then, depending on what you're working on:", " ", None),
    ("changelog.md", "### Fixed", "  ", 1),
]
WS_ONLY = [  # (file, line number (1-based) of an existing empty line, whitespace to put there)
]
base = sys.argv[1]
for fname, target, suffix, occ in EDITS:
    p = f"{base}/{fname}"
    lines = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")
    idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l == target]
    if occ is None and len(idx) != 1 or (occ is not None and len(idx) <= occ):
        sys.exit(f"{fname}: target {target!r} found {len(idx)} times")
    i = idx[0 if occ is None else occ]
    lines[i] += suffix
    open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(lines))
    print(f"{fname}:{i+1} +{len(suffix)} trailing")
EOF
python3 -I /tmp/corpus6_tools/trail.py /tmp/corpus6/i

#!/usr/bin/env python3 # -*- coding: utf-8 -*- # fmt: markdown """ # merch_digest.py Builds the **weekly merchandising digest** for the web, buying and marketing teams: top movers by revenue, the SKUs the recommender is pushing hardest, and a short LLM-written intro for the `#merch-weekly` Slack channel. Run it as a plain script (`python merch_digest.py --week 2026-W46`) or render it with Quarto (`quarto render merch_digest.py`) to get the HTML version with charts. * needs `ACME_WAREHOUSE_DSN`, `LLM_API_KEY` and (for `--post`) `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` * safe to re-run -- it only *reads* from the warehouse * ...and only posts to Slack with `--post` """ # %% #| label: setup #| echo: false #| warning: FALSE #| tags: [ parameters ] from __future__ import annotations import argparse import datetime as dt import json import os from dataclasses import dataclass import pandas as pd WEEK = "2026-W46" # overridden by --week or by Quarto params CURRENCY = "EUR" TOP_N = 15 BANNED_WORDS = ["drop","steal","insane","must-have"] # fmt: skip # fmt: off PRICE_BANDS = { # band min max label "entry": ( 0.00, 24.99, "under €25"), "core": ( 25.00, 79.99, "€25–80"), "premium": ( 80.00, 199.99, "€80–200"), "luxe": ( 200.00, 99999.0, "€200+"), } # fmt: on # fmt: markdown # ### Why the price bands look odd # # Buying wanted "€25–80" instead of "€25–79.99" because it *reads* better in the deck. The bands are inclusive on both ends, so a €79.99 tee is `core` and an €80.00 sneaker is `premium`. # Don't change them without asking @buying-team. @dataclass class Mover: sku: str name: str price: float revenue: float wow: float # week-over-week change, 0.12 == +12 % recs_share: float = 0.0 # share of revenue attributed to recs carousels def as_row(self) -> str: arrow = "▲" if self.wow >= 0 else "▼" return f"| `{self.sku}` | {self.name} | €{self.price:,.2f} | €{self.revenue:,.0f} | {arrow} {abs(self.wow):.0%} | {self.recs_share:.0%} |" # %% [markdown] # fmt: markdown # ## Data # # Revenue comes from `marts.fct_order_lines` (net of returns, **excl. VAT**), recs exposure from `recs.impressions_daily`. Gift cards and shipping lines are excluded because they wreck every chart. # # * Week boundaries are ISO weeks, Monday 00:00 Europe/Amsterdam # * A "mover" is a SKU whose revenue changed by ≥ 25 % week over week **and** that sold ≥ 20 units # - bundles count once per bundle, not per component # # Known issues: # 1. `recs_share` is `NaN` for SKUs launched mid-week; we fill with 0 # 2. bundles (`BND-*`) are listed under their *first* component. Yes, that's wrong. WEB-4411 # %% #| label: load-data #| code-fold: show #| code-summary: "SQL + loader" #| output: false def load_movers(week: str = WEEK, top_n: int = TOP_N) -> list[Mover]: dsn = os.environ["ACME_WAREHOUSE_DSN"] # fmt: skip sql = """ select sku, product_name, avg_price, revenue, wow_change, coalesce(recs_share, 0) from marts.weekly_sku_movers where iso_week = %(week)s and units >= 20 order by abs(wow_change) desc limit %(top_n)s """ df = pd.read_sql(sql, dsn, params={"week": week, "top_n": top_n}) return [Mover(*row) for row in df.itertuples(index=False)] # %% #| label: fig-movers #| fig-cap: "Week-over-week revenue change, top movers" #| fig-alt: >- #| Horizontal bar chart with one bar per SKU, sorted by week-over-week revenue change; #| green bars are increases, red bars are decreases, and the Aurora Runner 2 is the longest green bar. #| fig-width: 7 #| fig-height: 5 #| column: page-right def plot_movers(movers: list[Mover]): import matplotlib.pyplot as plt movers = sorted(movers, key=lambda m: m.wow) fig, ax = plt.subplots() ax.barh([m.sku for m in movers], [m.wow for m in movers], color=["#2e7d32" if m.wow >= 0 else "#c62828" for m in movers]) ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(lambda x, _: f"{x:+.0%}") ax.set_title(f"Top movers {WEEK}") return fig # fmt: markdown wrap=sentence BLURB_PROMPT = """ You are the voice of **Acme Shop**: warm, a little playful, never pushy. Write the intro for this week's internal merch digest. It goes to the web team, the buyers and the marketing team, so it should be useful to all three. ## Rules - Max. 90 words. No hashtags. At most one emoji. - Mention the #1 mover by name and price, e.g. "the Aurora Runner 2 (€119.95)". - Never invent numbers; only use the table below. - If a SKU is out of stock, say so -- don't hype it. - Banned words: {banned} ## Data {table} """ # fmt: markdown SKU_HELP = r""" **SKU format:** `FAM-GEN-COL-SIZE`, validated with `^[A-Z]{3}-\d+-[A-Z]{3}-[0-9A-Z]{1,3}$`. Sizes are *strings* -- `42`, `42.5`, `XL`, `OS` (one size). Literal asterisks in product names (looking at you, \*NEW\* Aurora) must be escaped. """ # fmt: json SLACK_BLOCKS = """ {"blocks":[{"type":"header","text":{"type":"plain_text","text":"Merch digest"}}, {"type":"section","text":{"type":"mrkdwn","text":"PLACEHOLDER"}},{"type":"divider"}]} """ # fmt: html EMAIL_FOOTER = """
Acme Retail B.V. · Keizersgracht 1 · Amsterdam
Unsubscribe
""" def render_digest(movers: list[Mover], blurb: str, week: str = WEEK) -> str: rows = "\n".join(m.as_row() for m in movers) # fmt: markdown return f""" # 🛒 Merch digest -- {week} {blurb} ## Top movers | SKU | Product | Price | Revenue | WoW | via recs | |---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:| {rows} Generated {dt.datetime.now():%Y-%m-%d %H:%M} by `merch_digest.py`. Numbers are net of returns and **exclude VAT**. """ def llm_complete(prompt: str) -> str: # thin wrapper, see acme_ml.llm from acme_ml.llm import complete return complete(prompt, max_tokens=300, temperature=0.4) def post_to_slack(payload: dict) -> None: import urllib.request req = urllib.request.Request(os.environ["SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL"], data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) # %% #| label: run #| echo: false #| output: asis def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None: ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Weekly merch digest") ap.add_argument("--week", default=WEEK) ap.add_argument("--top-n", type=int, default=TOP_N) ap.add_argument("--post", action="store_true", help="post to #merch-weekly") args = ap.parse_args(argv) movers = load_movers(args.week, args.top_n) table = "\n".join(m.as_row() for m in movers) blurb = llm_complete(BLURB_PROMPT.format(table=table, banned=", ".join(BANNED_WORDS))) digest = render_digest(movers, blurb, args.week) print(digest) if args.post: payload = json.loads(SLACK_BLOCKS) payload["blocks"][1]["text"]["text"] = digest[:2900] post_to_slack(payload) if __name__ == "__main__": main()

arguments.content:
#' ---
#' title: "Promo price QA -- BF/CM 2026"
#' author: "Web Analytics (S. Okafor)"
#' date: "2026-11-17"
#' output: html_document
#' ---
#'
#' Checks every promo price exported from the CMS against the pricing rules before a campaign goes live.
#' Run with `Rscript promo_price_check.R bf26-early-access` or render it with `quarto render promo_price_check.R`.

#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning:   FALSE
#| include: !expr interactive()
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(stringr)
  library(glue)
})

options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE, scipen = 999)
args     <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
campaign <- if (length(args) && !startsWith(args[[1]], "--")) args[[1]] else "bf26-early-access"
strict   <- "--strict" %in% args

# fmt: markdown
# ## Pricing rules (summary)
#
# | market | ends in | max depth |
# |---|---|---|
# | NL, DE, BE | ,95 | 40 % |
# | UK | .99 | 40 % |
# | SE | whole kronor | 30 % |
#
# Source of truth is the **pricing sheet**, not this comment. If they disagree, the sheet wins and somebody should fix this comment.

rules <- tibble::tribble(
  ~market, ~ending, ~max_depth,
  "NL",    0.95,    0.40,
  "DE",    0.95,    0.40,
  "BE",    0.95,    0.40,
  "UK",    0.99,    0.40,
  "SE",    0.00,    0.30
)

# fmt: skip
usage <- r"---(
Usage: Rscript promo_price_check.R <campaign> [--strict]

  campaign   CMS campaign slug, e.g. bf26-early-access
  --strict   exit with status 1 on *any* rule violation      (default: only on errors)
)---"

#| label: load
#| cache: TRUE
#| cache.extra: !expr file.mtime("data/promo_export.csv")
#| dependson: [ "setup" ]
promos <- read_csv(glue("data/{campaign}/promo_export.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    sku         = str_trim(sku),
    reg_price   = as.numeric(reg_price),
    promo_price = as.numeric(promo_price),
    depth       = round(1 - promo_price / reg_price, 3)
  ) |>
  left_join(rules, by = "market")

check_price_ending <- function(price, ending) {
    cents <- round(price %% 1, 2)
    ifelse(ending == 0, cents == 0, abs(cents - ending) < 1e-9)
}

#| label: checks
#| echo: true
#| results:   'asis'
qa <- promos |>
  mutate(
    bad_ending  = !check_price_ending(promo_price, ending),
    too_deep    = depth > max_depth,
    not_cheaper = promo_price >= reg_price,
    ok = !(bad_ending | too_deep | not_cheaper)
  )

n_bad   <- sum(!qa$ok)
n_total <- nrow(qa)
offenders <- qa |>
  filter(!ok) |>
  arrange(desc(depth)) |>
  head(10) |>
  glue_data("- `{sku}` ({market}): €{format(promo_price, nsmall = 2)} vs. reg. €{format(reg_price, nsmall = 2)}, depth {scales::percent(depth, accuracy = 0.1)}") |>
  paste(collapse = "\n")

# fmt: markdown
alert_body <- "
**Promo QA failed** for campaign `{campaign}` ⚠️

{n_bad} of {n_total} prices break the rules. Worst offenders:

{offenders}

Fix them in the CMS (*Pricing → Promotions*) and re-run the check. Ping #pricing-help if a rule looks wrong -- don't just override it.
"

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
promo_help_md <- r"(
## How to read this table
Each row is one **promo price** from the CMS export. A row turns red when the price breaks a rule: e.g. it doesn't end in `,95`/`.99`, it's *higher* than the regular price, or the discount is deeper than the cap Finance signed off on (40 % for most markets, 30 % for SE).

-   `reg_price` = regular price incl. VAT
-   `promo_price` = what the shopper pays
    - for bundles this is the bundle price, not per item
-   `depth` = 1 - promo/reg, rounded to 3 decimals

Questions → #pricing-help 💬
)"

# fmt: markdown
rules_changelog_md <- R"[
### Rules changelog
* 2026-11-02 -- cap raised from 35 % to 40 % for `HOM-*` (mugs, candles) after the Q3 overstock, see [the decision doc](https://docs.acme-shop.example/pricing/q3-overstock)
* 2026-09-15 -- UK prices must end in `.99`, NL/DE/BE in `,95`
+ 2026-06-01 -- SE switched to whole kronor
]"

# fmt: css
qa_css <- "
.qa-bad{background:#fde8e8;color:#9b1c1c}
.qa-ok {background:#e7f6ec}
table.qa td.num{text-align:right;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
"

#' ## Results
#'
#' `r n_bad` of `r n_total` promo prices break at least one rule.

#| label: tbl-qa
#| tbl-cap: "Promo prices that break a rule"
#| layout: [[1], [1,1]]
qa |>
  filter(!ok) |>
  select(sku, market, reg_price, promo_price, depth, bad_ending, too_deep, not_cheaper) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 2, 2, 3, 0, 0, 0))

#| label: gadget
#| eval: false
run_qa_gadget <- function() {
  shiny::shinyApp(
    ui = bslib::page_fluid(
      shiny::tags$style(qa_css),
      shiny::markdown(promo_help_md),
      shiny::markdown(rules_changelog_md),
      DT::DTOutput("qa")
    ),
    server = function(input, output, session) {
      output$qa <- DT::renderDT(DT::datatable(qa, class = "qa") |> DT::formatStyle("ok", target = "row", backgroundColor = DT::styleEqual(c(FALSE, TRUE), c("#fde8e8", "#e7f6ec"))))
    }
  )
}

if (n_bad > 0) {
  message(glue(alert_body))
  if (strict) quit(status = 1)
} else {
  message(glue("✅ {n_total} promo prices for {campaign} look fine. Ship it!"))
}

--- {{< include _common.qmd >}} ## Summary {#sec-summary} ::: {.callout-important} ## Bottom line The regridded ensemble is fit for the detection-and-attribution work in WP3. Regridding changes the global-mean SST by **< 0.004 K** for every model (@tbl-regrid-error), the anomaly time series agree with the native-grid ones to within 0.01 K at every time step, and only `CanESM5` and `IPSL-CM6A-LR` need de-drifting (@sec-drift). ::: ## Data and models {#sec-data} We use monthly `tos` from the `historical` (1850–2014) and `ssp245`/`ssp585` (2015–2100) experiments of the five models in @tbl-models, three members each where available [@eyring2016; @oneill2016scenariomip]. Observations are HadISST [@rayner2003hadisst] and OISST v2.1 [@huang2021oisst, pp. 2923--2939], on their native $1^\circ$ and $0.25^\circ$ grids respectively. | Model | Ocean component | Native grid | Members | Ref. | |:--|:--|--:|:-:|---| | CanESM5 | NEMO3.4.1 (ORCA1) | ~1° | 3 | @swart2019canesm5 | | MPI-ESM1-2-HR | MPIOM1.63 (TP04) | 0.4° | 3 | @mueller2018mpiesm | | IPSL-CM6A-LR | NEMO-OPA (eORCA1) | ~1° | 3 | @boucher2020ipsl | | UKESM1-0-LL | NEMO3.6 (eORCA1) | ~1° | 2 | @sellar2019ukesm | | GFDL-CM4 | MOM6 | 0.25° | 1 | @held2019gfdlcm4 | : CMIP6 models in the ensemble refresh. "Members" counts realisations with complete historical *and* scenario output on our ESGF mirror as of 1 November 2026. {#tbl-models} ```{mermaid} %%| label: fig-pipeline %%| fig-cap: The cmorph-pp chain. This report covers step 2 only. flowchart LR A[ESGF mirror
native tos] --> B(step 1: CMOR checks) B --> C(step 2: regrid + anomalies) C --> D[(THREDDS)] C --> E(step 3: bias correction) ``` ## Methods {#sec-methods} ### Regridding Fields are regridded with xESMF [@zhuang2023xesmf] using first-order conservative remapping, normalised by the unmasked fraction of each target cell (`conservative_normed`). For a target cell $k$ that overlaps source cells $i$ with overlap areas $a_{ik}$ and ocean mask $m_i \in \{0, 1\}$, $$ \hat T_k = \frac{\sum_i a_{ik}\, m_i\, T_i}{\sum_i a_{ik}\, m_i}, $$ {#eq-conservative} which, unlike plain conservative remapping, does not pull coastal cells towards zero. The global integral $\sum_k A_k \hat T_k$ is conserved exactly only if no target cell is partially masked; the residual error is what @tbl-regrid-error quantifies. ### Anomalies and drift {#sec-drift} Anomalies are taken relative to each member's 1981–2010 monthly climatology (@eq-anomaly). Drift is estimated from the parallel `piControl` segment with a least-squares quadratic fit $d(t) = a + b\,t + c\,t^2$ and subtracted when $|b| > 0.1\,\mathrm{K\,century^{-1}}$^[We tried a linear fit first. It under-corrects `IPSL-CM6A-LR`, whose drift slows down after ~200 years of spin-up.]. $$ T'(y, m) = T(y, m) - \frac{1}{30} \sum_{y'=1981}^{2010} T(y', m) $$ {#eq-anomaly} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="55%"} All runs were done on larch[^larch] as one Slurm array, one task per model and experiment: ```{.bash filename="jobs/submit_step2.sh"} sbatch --array=0-14%5 --partition=short --cpus-per-task=32 --mem=120G \ --time=04:00:00 --job-name=pp-step2 jobs/step2.sbatch ``` ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} > Weights for the 0.25° GFDL grid took 19 min to build on 32 cores; every later run reused them from `$CMORPH_WEIGHTS`. ::: :::: [^larch]: 2× AMD EPYC 9654 per node, 768 GB RAM. Regridding is memory-bound, so we used 32 of the 192 cores per task and packed six tasks onto each node. ## Results ### Regridding error ```{python} #| label: tbl-regrid-error #| tbl-cap: "Difference in 1981–2010 global-mean SST (K), regridded minus native, per model. Negative values mean the regridded field is cooler." import pandas as pd err = pd.read_parquet("results/regrid_error.parquet") err.style.format("{:+.4f}").background_gradient(cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-0.005, vmax=0.005) ``` ```{python} #| label: fig-gmsst #| fig-cap: Global-mean SST anomaly relative to 1981–2010, ensemble mean ± 1σ.

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
#SBATCH --job-name=covqc
#SBATCH --partition=short
#SBATCH --array=1-96%24
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --time=01:30:00
#SBATCH --output=logs/%x_%A_%a.out

# coverage_qc.R -- per-sample coverage QC from mosdepth output (Mensah lab, varcall pipeline)
#
# Usage, one array task per sample (the sample list has one path prefix per line):
#   sbatch --export=ALL,SAMPLES=batches/2026_11.txt bin/coverage_qc.R
# or render the whole batch as an HTML report:
#   quarto render bin/coverage_qc.R -P batch:2026_11

#' # Coverage QC for a sequencing batch
#'
#' This script doubles as a `knitr::spin()` report: lines starting with `#'` are Markdown and `#|` lines are chunk options.

#| label: setup
#| include: false
#| message:   FALSE
#| warning: no
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(glue)  
})
options(datatable.print.nrows = 20, warn = 1)

# fmt: markdown
# ## QC thresholds
#
# A sample **passes** if all of the following hold (agreed with the Genomics Core in Nov. 2025):
#
# | metric | threshold | why |
# |---|---|---|
# | median autosomal coverage | ≥ 30× | DeepVariant sensitivity drops quickly below ~25× (cf. Poplin et al. 2018) |
# | fraction of bases ≥ 20× | ≥ 0.90 | |
# | chrX / autosome ratio | consistent with the reported sex | catches sample swaps |
# | coverage CV | ≤ 0.35 | a high CV usually means GC bias or degraded DNA | 
#
# Samples between 20× and 30× are flagged `LOW` but still called; below 20× they `FAIL` and need re-sequencing.
# The coefficient of variation is computed over 1 kb bins as $\mathrm{CV} = \sigma / \mu$, excluding bins in the ENCODE blacklist (Amemiya et al. 2019).
THRESHOLDS <- list(
  median_cov  = 30,     # LOW below this
  hard_min    = 20,     # FAIL below this
  frac_ge20   = 0.90,
  cv_max      = 0.35,
  x_ratio_xx  = c(0.85, 1.15),
  x_ratio_xy  = c(0.40, 0.60)
)

# fmt: markdown
help_md <- r"---[
Per-sample coverage QC for **varcall** batches.

Reads `<prefix>.mosdepth.summary.txt` and `<prefix>.regions.bed.gz` (1 kb bins) for every sample listed in `$SAMPLES` and writes `<prefix>.covqc.tsv`. When run as a Slurm array job, task *i* processes line *i* of the sample list; otherwise all samples are processed one after the other, which takes about 40 s per 30× genome.

-   `SAMPLES`: path to the sample list (default `samples.txt`)
-   `SEX_TABLE`: optional TSV with columns `sample` and `sex` (`XX`/`XY`) from the sample sheet
]---"

# Batch summary, posted as a comment on the sequencing-run issue in GitLab.
# Placeholders are filled by glue::glue(), hence the {braces}.
# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
summary_template <- r"(
## Coverage QC: batch {batch}

{n_pass} of {n_total} samples passed, {n_low} are `LOW` (20–30×) and {n_fail} `FAIL` (< 20×). Median coverage across the batch was {median_cov}× (IQR {iqr_lo}–{iqr_hi}×). Samples flagged `SEX_MISMATCH` must be checked against the sample sheet before anything else is done with them, since a swap always affects two samples.

{fail_table}

Re-sequencing requests go to the Core via the usual form, please link this issue. Plots: `{plot_path}`
)"

# Appended to each task's log so a single sample can be re-run outside Slurm.

# Contributing to varcall$
$
Thanks for helping out! `varcall` is the germline short-variant calling pipeline (FASTQ M-bM-^FM-^R aligned CRAM M-bM-^FM-^R gVCF M-bM-^FM-^R joint-called, filt
$
This document is for people *changing* the pipeline. If you only want to run it, read [README.md](README.md) and `docs/usage.md` instead.$
$
**Contents**$
$
1. [Ground rules](#ground-rules)$
2. [Development environment](#development-environment)$
3. [Tests](#tests)$
4. [Adding or updating a module](#adding-or-updating-a-module)$
5) [Commit messages and merge requests](#commit-messages-and-merge-requests)$
6) [Releasing](#releasing)$
$
Ground rules$
------------$
$
* Never commit patient-identifiable data. Test data under `tests/data/` is either synthetic or from the public **GIAB HG002** sample, downsampled to ~2M-CM-^W a
* All changes go through a merge request against `dev`; `main` only moves on releases. $
- Results must stay reproducible: an MR that changes any output VCF needs a justification in its description and an updated truth set (see [Tests](#tests)).$
*   Be kind in reviews. Most contributors are PhD students with a thesis to write.$
$
## Development environment  $
$
We use [pixi](https://pixi.sh) for Nextflow itself and the Python/R helpers, and containers (Apptainer on larch, Docker elsewhere) for the bioinformatics tools:
$
```bash$
git clone git@git.northfield.ac.uk:mensah-lab/varcall.git$
cd varcall$
pixi install            # nextflow, nf-test, python 3.12, R 4.4, pre-commit$
pixi run pre-commit install$
```$
$
On larch, do this on a login node but run anything heavier than `nf-test` in an interactive job (`salloc -p short -c 8 --mem=32G -t 2:00:00`). The login nodes k
$
> [!WARNING]$
> Do **not** keep the Apptainer cache in your home directory: home has a 50 GB quota and a single DeepVariant image is 6 GB. Put$
> `export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR=/scratch/$USER/.apptainer` in your `~/.bashrc`.$
$
## Tests ##$
$
There are three layers of tests: $
$
1. **Unit tests** for the helper scripts (`pytest` for Python, `testthat` for R):$
$
   ```bash$
   pixi run pytest bin/tests -q$
   pixi run Rscript -e 'testthat::test_dir("bin/tests/testthat")'$
   ```$
2. **Module tests** with [nf-test](https://www.nf-test.com/), one per module under `modules/local/*/tests/`. Run all of them with `nf-test test --profile apptai
    ```bash$
    nf-test test modules/local/deepvariant/tests/main.nf.test --profile apptainer$
    ```$
3. **End-to-end** test on the GIAB subset. It takes ~25 min on 4 nodes and runs nightly in CI, but please run it yourself if you touch anything in `subworkflows
$
       sbatch --wait tests/e2e/run_e2e.sbatch$
       python tests/e2e/compare_to_truth.py results/e2e/HG002.vcf.gz --truth tests/data/HG002_chr20_truth.vcf.gz --min-f1 0.995$
$
   The comparison uses `hap.py`. An MR may lower SNV F1 by at most 0.001 and indel F1 by at most 0.003 without a discussion; anything more needs sign-off from t
$
### Making new test data$
$
If you need reads for a new region, downsample from the full 35M-CM-^W HG002 BAM rather than committing big files. To get a target coverage $c_t$ from an origin
$
```bash$
samtools view -b --subsample 0.057 --subsample-seed 42 HG002.GRCh38.35x.bam chr20:10000000-12000000 > HG002_chr20_2x.bam$
```$
$
Expected coverage after subsampling is $c_t$ only on average; for small regions check it with `mosdepth` and redraw with another seed if it is off by more than 
$
The `Makefile` in `tests/data/` regenerates everything (recipes must be indented with a tab, not spaces):$
$
```make$
HG002_chr20_2x.bam: $(SRC_BAM)$
^Isamtools view -b --subsample 0.057 --subsample-seed 42 $< chr20:10000000-12000000 > $@$
^Isamtools index $@$
```$

results.content:
We compute three indicators per city and quarter:

1. **Price-to-income ratio** (PIR) -- median transaction price divided by median household income.
2. **Mortgage burden** -- the annual payment on a 30-year annuity mortgage for the median house at the prevailing interest rate $r$, as a share of median income:
   $$
   \text{burden} = \frac{P \cdot \frac{r}{1-(1+r)^{-30}}}{Y_{50}}
   $$
3. **Share priced out** -- the share of households whose income is below the income needed to keep the mortgage burden under 30%.

::: {.callout-tip}
The indicators are computed by `affordability()` in `R/helpers.R`; all parameters (loan-to-value, term, burden threshold) can be changed there and the report re-rendered with `quarto render`.
:::

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<system-reminder>
<tools-used-before-summary>Agent, Bash, Edit, Read, Write</tools-used-before-summary>
</system-reminder>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user (single initial message, from the prior context) asked to reverse-engineer `./executable` (Yamark, a Rust/clap YAML+Markdown formatter) by observing behavior only and write an original Rust (std-only, cargo) reimplementation with identical stdout, stderr, exit codes and file effects. Constraints (verbatim intent preserved): no searching internet/package registries for source; no wrapping/embedding/copying the original binary; no decompiling/disassembling/strace/ltrace of `./executable` — only interact via CLI args, stdin/stdout/stderr, files, env vars; `./compile.sh` must build from source offline on a fresh checkout and leave the native binary at `./executable`, must not depend on `./executable` or `./target` pre-existing; ≥50 lines Rust; non-Rust code (incl. test scripts) ≤5% of workspace code lines — keep scratch scripts outside the workspace (e.g., /tmp); executable and build artifacts in `.gitignore`; commit work; "When you are completely done, commit your work and stop." Commit messages must end with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>". Hidden tests likely run `format --diff <file>` (summary on stderr) on 13 realistic document types: ansible_playbook, changelog, contributing, docker_compose, github_workflow, kubernetes_multi_document, mkdocs_config, openapi, python_script, quarto_report, r_script, readme, rmarkdown_sentence_wrap (all "1 formatted").

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Original binary at `/tmp/orig/executable`; mine at `/workspace/executable` (built by `./compile.sh` / `cargo build --release --offline` then `cp target/release/yamark executable`).
   - Differential testing: corpora /tmp/corpus{,2,3}, /tmp/corpus4/{a,b,c}, /tmp/corpus5/{d,e,f}, /tmp/corpus6/{g,h,i} (agent-written realistic docs); harness /tmp/t/{corpus.sh,all.sh,pathmode.sh,clitest.sh,cmp.sh}; probes /tmp/rt/gen*.py, /tmp/t/*.py; fuzzer /tmp/fuzz/cmpfuzz.py (seed n exts).
   - Markdown: sentence/column wrapping, escape vs move-down, list/def/quote/table/math/TeX block rules, embedded-markdown (KEEP_TRAILING) semantics, option directives in HTML comments.
   - YAML: lenient recovery (orphans, key-less lines, extra roots, irregular block scalars, template-only lines as trivia), `fmt: table`/`fmt: compact` directives, verbatim scalars for bad escapes.
   - Python/R source scanning models (R "ML-first" line-start-closing strings; Python triple-quote rules), directive/job processing with errors.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `src/markdown/wrap.rs`
     - `Piece` got `unit: usize`; `try_fill` wraps `try_fill_ex(units, first_width, rest_width, prefer_escape) -> Option<(Vec<String>, Vec<(usize,String)>)>`; with prefer_escape: escapable dangerous token escaped (recorded), move-down ignores width, unplaceable token stays on current line.
     - `ends_sentence`: false if final `.!?` preceded by odd number of backslashes.
     - `sentences(units, limited)`: rule-char hazard (limited → no split; unlimited → no split only if all remaining tokens until hard break are same rule char).
     - `wrap_units`: `Sentence(None)` joins sentences; `Sentence(Some(_))` retry loop re-splitting when a sentence-final token gets escaped.
     - Hard-break backslash not measured: `let pw = width(&p.text) - usize::from(p.hard_break && p.text.ends_with('\\'));`
     - fig-alt dest wrapping: `alt_first` (first `"` preceded by `fig-alt=`), `head_fits` (2 + width up to first word after `"` ≤ rest_width), ends with `"`, contains space; continuation lines limit rest_width-1; body excludes closing quote, appended after.
     - `escape_sentence_start` uses `super::block::is_list_label`.
   - `src/markdown/block.rs`
     - `pub fn is_roman(s)` (≤8 chars, case-insensitive grammar m*(cm|cd|d?c{0,3})(xc|xl|l?x{0,3})(ix|iv|v?i{0,3})), `pub fn is_list_label(label, parens)` (digits: parens → ≤8; letters single; roman).
     - `Block::Blank(String)` (raw blank text); DEFS thread-local + `with_defs`; Quote parse: `with_defs(!single, || with_colon_raw(!single, ...))`; list items `with_defs(true, ...)`.
     - def recognition requires previous line non-blank or previous non-blank block (skipping Raw all-indented ≥4) is Def; stray paragraph starting with def marker in COLON_RAW: ':' → Block::Raw, '~' → "\~".
     - `def_start` returns `rest.trim_start()`.

<   summary: Submit and monitor Slurm jobs on the larch cluster from science gateways and workflow engines.

<   description: |
<     The Compute Gateway lets **trusted science gateways** (Galaxy, the Northfield JupyterHub, Nextflow Tower) submit Slurm batch jobs on behalf of a user without that user ever handing over an SSH key. Every request carries an OAuth 2.0 access token issued to the *gateway*; the `X-Larch-On-Behalf-Of` header names the end user, who must have authorised the gateway once at <https://hpc.northfield.ac.uk/gateways>.

<     | Max. script size | 64 KiB | |  
< 
<     Job scripts are passed to `sbatch` **unchanged**, so `#SBATCH` lines in the script win over fields in the request body -- except `account` and `partition`, which the gateway always enforces (cf. the [RCS acceptable use policy](https://hpc.northfield.ac.uk/docs/policies/aup/)).

import os, random, subprocess, sys
random.seed(int(sys.argv[1]))
n = int(sys.argv[2])
kinds = sys.argv[3].split(',') if len(sys.argv) > 3 else None
files = []
for d in ['/tmp/corpus/yaml','/tmp/corpus/md','/tmp/corpus2/yaml','/tmp/corpus2/md','/tmp/corpus3','/tmp/corpus/py','/tmp/corpus/r']:
    for f in os.listdir(d):
        if kinds and os.path.splitext(f)[1] not in kinds: continue
        files.append(os.path.join(d, f))
chars = list(" \t\n:-#*_[]{}()<>|`'\"!&%@,.?=+~$\\/0123456789abcXYZ")
fails = 0
os.makedirs('/tmp/fuzz/diff', exist_ok=True)
for it in range(n):
    f = random.choice(files)
    data = open(f, encoding='utf-8').read()
    lines = data.split('\n')
    for _ in range(random.randint(1, 3)):
        op = random.random()
        if not lines: break
        i = random.randrange(len(lines))
        if op < 0.3:
            l = lines[i]
            p = random.randint(0, len(l))
            lines[i] = l[:p] + ''.join(random.choice(chars) for _ in range(random.randint(1,3))) + l[p:]

::: {#def-ols}$
## Ordinary least squares$
The *ordinary least squares* (OLS) estimator of $\beta$ is the minimiser of the residual sum of squares,$
$$$
\hat\beta = \arg\min_{b \in \mathbb{R}^p} \; \lVert y - Xb \rVert_2^2 .$
$$$
$
Setting the gradient to zero gives the *normal equations* $X^\top X \hat\beta = X^\top y$, and under A2$
$
$$\hat\beta = (X^\top X)^{-1}X^\top y$$ {#eq-ols}$
$

$
   ```rust$
   fn on_load(&self, ctx: &mut LoadContext) -> Result<Option<Module>> {$
3. **Giving up**, and telling users to run a separate script before the build.$
       let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()?; // a new runtime. per call.$
       rt.block_on(self.fetch(ctx.url()))$
   }$
   ```$
$
   This still blocks the worker, creates threads on every call, and panics if$
   the hook happens to be invoked from inside an existing runtime.$
$
2. **Pre-fetching everything in `on_start`.** Works for small sites, falls$
   over for anything with more than a few hundred remote resources, and makes$
   incremental rebuilds pointless.$
$

::: {#def-ols}$
## Ordinary least squares$
The *ordinary least squares* (OLS) estimator of $\beta$ is the minimiser of the residual sum of squares,$
$$$
\hat\beta = \arg\min_{b \in \mathbb{R}^p} \; \lVert y - Xb \rVert_2^2 .$
$$$
$
Setting the gradient to zero gives the *normal equations* $X^\top X \hat\beta = X^\top y$, and under A2$
$
$$\hat\beta = (X^\top X)^{-1}X^\top y$$ {#eq-ols}$
$
In practice nobody computes @eq-ols literally[^qr].$
$
[^qr]: R's `lm()` uses a pivoted QR decomposition of $X$ (via LINPACK's `dqrdc2`, for$
    historical reasons). This is both faster and numerically far more stable than forming$
    $X^\top X$, whose condition number is the *square* of that of $X$.$
$
    If you ever see code that calls `solve(t(X) %*% X)`, be suspicious.$
$
$
## Properties of the OLS estimator {#sec-ols-properties}$
$
Under A1M-bM-^@M-^SA3 the estimator is unbiased:$
$
$$$
\begin{aligned}$
\operatorname{E}[\hat\beta \mid X]$
  &= (X^\top X)^{-1} X^\top \operatorname{E}[y \mid X] \\$
  &= (X^\top X)^{-1} X^\top X \beta \\$
  &= \beta ,$

$
Today every hook runs on one of the scheduler's worker threads and is expected$
to return quickly. In practice, plugins do all sorts of slow things in hooks:$
$
* fetching remote modules (`https://` imports in the `remote-imports` plugin),$
* calling out to `esbuild` or `swc` subprocesses,$
* querying a database for content (the CMS plugins), and$
* waiting for a TypeScript language service to type-check a file.$
$
When a hook blocks, the worker thread is gone for that time. With the default$
pool of `num_cpus` workers, four slow fetches on a laptop are enough to stall$
the whole build. We have seen this in the wild repeatedly — see [#2950],$
[#3101] and the infamous "build hangs on airplane wifi" thread.[^wifi]$
$
Plugin authors currently work around it in one of three ways, all of them bad:  $
$
1. **Spawning their own runtime.** Several plugins create a private Tokio$
   runtime inside the hook and `block_on` a future:$
$
   ```rust$
   fn on_load(&self, ctx: &mut LoadContext) -> Result<Option<Module>> {$
3. **Giving up**, and telling users to run a separate script before the build.$
       let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()?; // a new runtime. per call.$
       rt.block_on(self.fetch(ctx.url()))$
   }$
   ```$
$
   This still blocks the worker, creates threads on every call, and panics if$
   the hook happens to be invoked from inside an existing runtime.$
$
2. **Pre-fetching everything in `on_start`.** Works for small sites, falls$
   over for anything with more than a few hundred remote resources, and makes$
   incremental rebuilds pointless.$
$
3. **Giving up**, and telling users to run a separate script before the build.$

mkdir -p /tmp/mixfz && cat > /tmp/mixfz/run.py <<'EOF'
import os, random, subprocess, sys
random.seed(int(sys.argv[1]))
n = int(sys.argv[2])
dirs = ['/tmp/corpus/md','/tmp/corpus/yaml','/tmp/corpus3','/tmp/corpus4/a','/tmp/corpus4/b','/tmp/corpus4/c','/tmp/corpus5/d','/tmp/corpus5/e','/tmp/corpus5/f','/tmp/corpus6/g']
files = [os.path.join(d,f) for d in dirs for f in os.listdir(d) if os.path.splitext(f)[1] in ('.md','.yaml','.yml','.qmd','.Rmd','.py','.R')]
fails = 0
for it in range(n):
    f = random.choice(files)
    data = open(f, encoding='utf-8').read().replace('\r\n', '\n')
    lines = data.split('\n')
    mode = random.random()
    if mode < 0.5:
        # contiguous region CRLF
        a = random.randrange(len(lines)); b = min(len(lines)-1, a + random.randint(1, 30))
        sel = set(range(a, b))
    else:
        sel = set(i for i in range(len(lines)) if random.random() < 0.3)
    out = ''.join(l + ('\r\n' if i in sel else '\n') for i, l in enumerate(lines[:-1])) + lines[-1]
    ext = os.path.splitext(f)[1]
    path = f'/tmp/mixfz/t{ext}'
    open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='').write(out)
    r1 = subprocess.run(['/tmp/orig/executable','format','--stdin-file-path',path], stdin=open(path,'rb'), capture_output=True)
    r2 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','format','--stdin-file-path',path], stdin=open(path,'rb'), capture_output=True)
    if r1.stdout != r2.stdout or r1.returncode != r2.returncode:
        # distinguish EOL-only difference
        eol_only = r1.stdout.replace(b'\r\n', b'\n') == r2.stdout.replace(b'\r\n', b'\n')
        fails += 1
        keep = f'/tmp/mixfz/f_{sys.argv[1]}_{it}{ext}'
        open(keep, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='').write(out)
        print('FAIL', f, 'eol_only' if eol_only else 'content', keep)
print('fails', fails, '/', n)
EOF
cd /tmp/mixfz && timeout 900 python3 run.py 1 150 2>&1 | tail -25

arguments.description: Generate realistic test corpus 7
arguments.prompt:
Create 13 realistic, hand-written-looking text documents for testing a YAML/Markdown/Python/R formatter. Write them into the directory /tmp/corpus7/j/ (create it). Do NOT run any formatter or other program on them; just write the files with the Write tool (or a shell heredoc). Do not write anything outside /tmp/corpus7/. Files to create (exact names): 1. ansible_playbook.yml — an Ansible playbook (2-3 plays, handlers, vars, loops, `when:` conditions, Jinja2 `{{ }}` templating in values, block/rescue, a multi-line `shell: |` script, some comments, some inconsistent spacing like `key: value`, a flow list). 2. changelog.md — a "Keep a Changelog"-style CHANGELOG with 6+ releases, nested bullet lists using `*` and `-`, long lines that would need re-wrapping, inline code, links, reference-style link definitions at the bottom, a few emphasis markers, an occasional numbered list. 3. contributing.md — a CONTRIBUTING guide: headings, numbered steps containing fenced code blocks (bash, yaml), a table, block quotes (including a GitHub alert like `> [!WARNING]`), nested lists, long paragraphs, an HTML comment, a `
` section. 4. docker_compose.yml — a docker-compose file with 5+ services, anchors and aliases (`x-common: &common`, `<<: *common`), environment as both list and mapping styles, healthchecks with flow sequences, long command strings, comments, profiles, volumes and networks sections. 5. github_workflow.yml — a GitHub Actions workflow with `on:` triggers (push with paths filters, pull_request, workflow_dispatch with inputs, schedule cron), concurrency, permissions, a matrix with include/exclude, steps using `${{ }}` expressions, multi-line `run: |` scripts, `if:` conditions. 6. kubernetes_multi_document.yaml — 4-6 Kubernetes manifests separated by `---` (Namespace, ConfigMap with a multi-line data value, Deployment with probes/resources/env/volumeMounts, Service, Ingress with annotations, HorizontalPodAutoscaler), with comments. 7. mkdocs_config.yml — an mkdocs.yml for Material theme: nav tree with nesting, theme features list, palette with toggles, markdown_extensions including ones with options and `!!python/name:` tags (e.g. `pymdownx.superfences` custom_fences with `format: !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format`), plugins, extra, copyright. 8. openapi.yaml — an OpenAPI 3.x spec with info (multi-line description using `|` with Markdown inside), servers, several paths with parameters, requestBody, responses, components/schemas with $ref, enums, examples, security schemes. 9. python_script.py — a realistic Python CLI script (argparse, dataclasses, logging, type hints), module docstring, function docstrings, and 2-3 strings or comment blocks preceded by a `# fmt: markdown` comment line on its own line directly above them (e.g. `# fmt: markdown` then `HELP_TEXT = """...markdown text with long lines, lists, emphasis..."""`, and a `# fmt: markdown` above a block of `#` comment lines containing Markdown). Use raw strings (r""") if the Markdown contains backslashes. 10. quarto_report.qmd — a Quarto report with YAML front matter (title, author list, format options, execute options), R or Python code chunks with `#|` options, callouts (`::: {.callout-note}`), cross-references, figures with captions, a table, footnotes, inline math and a display math block, long paragraphs. 11. r_script.R — a realistic R analysis script (library calls, functions, pipes, ggplot) including 2-3 places where a `# fmt: markdown` comment line on its own line sits directly above either a block of `#` comment lines containing Markdown, or an assignment of a multi-line string containing Markdown (e.g. `report_md <- "...` spanning several lines; avoid backslashes inside such non-raw strings, or use raw strings r"(...)"). 12. readme.md — a project README with badges (image links), a table of contents, installation instructions with fenced code, usage examples, a feature list, an FAQ section with nested lists, a license section, long paragraphs, a few HTML snippets (e.g. `

`). 13. rmarkdown_sentence_wrap.Rmd — an R Markdown document whose YAML front matter contains ``` editor_options: markdown: wrap: sentence ``` plus output options; prose paragraphs with multiple sentences per line (and some sentences split across lines), abbreviations like "e.g." and "et al.", citations like [@smith2020], R chunks with options, inline R code like `r nrow(df)`, a list, a table. Make them realistic and varied (real-world-looking content, 80-250 lines each), with natural imperfections people leave in such files: inconsistent indentation of nested lists, trailing spaces on some lines, long lines exceeding 100 characters, mixed bullet markers, extra blank lines, occasional tab characters in YAML comments is NOT allowed (YAML forbids tabs for indentation; keep YAML valid). All YAML files must be valid YAML. Use UTF-8 and LF line endings, except make changelog.md use CRLF line endings throughout. Reply with just the list of files written and their line counts.

---
# site.yml -- baseline + app deploy for the billing cluster
#
# Usage:
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/production/hosts.ini site.yml --limit webservers --diff
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging/hosts.ini site.yml -e release_version=2.15.0-rc1 -e artifact_sha256=...
#
# NOTE(mk): run against staging first, the sshd template changed in March.

- name: Baseline configuration for all hosts
  hosts: all
  become: true
  gather_facts: yes

  vars:
    timezone: Europe/Berlin
    base_packages:
      - curl
      - git
      - htop
      - jq
      - vim-nox
      - unattended-upgrades
      - python3-pip
    admin_users:
      - { name: mkowalski, shell: /bin/bash, key: "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIOx2s7vB9dQk3hR mkowalski@thinkpad" }
      - { name: jdoe, shell: /bin/zsh, key: "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIK3p0QeW8hLrTzu jdoe@workstation" }
    sysctl_settings:
      net.core.somaxconn: 4096
      vm.swappiness:  10
      net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse: 1
      fs.file-max: 2097152

  pre_tasks:
    - name: Refresh apt cache if it is older than an hour
      apt:
        update_cache: yes
        cache_valid_time: 3600
      when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"

  tasks:
    - name: Install base packages
      package:
        name: "{{ item }}"
        state: present
      loop: "{{ base_packages }}"
      tags: [packages, baseline]

    - name: Set timezone
      community.general.timezone:
        name:  "{{ timezone }}"

    - name: Create admin users
      user:
        name: "{{ item.name }}"
        shell: "{{ item.shell }}"
        groups: sudo
        append: true
      loop: "{{ admin_users }}"
      loop_control:
        label: "{{ item.name }}"

    - name: Install authorized keys for admins
      ansible.posix.authorized_key:
        user: "{{ item.name }}"
        key: "{{ item.key }}"
        exclusive: false
      loop: "{{ admin_users }}"
      loop_control:
          label: "{{ item.name }}"

    - name: Apply kernel tuning
      ansible.posix.sysctl:
        name: "{{ item.key }}"
        value: "{{ item.value }}"
        sysctl_file: /etc/sysctl.d/90-billing.conf
        reload: no
      loop: "{{ sysctl_settings | dict2items }}"
      when: not (running_in_container | default(false) | bool)
      notify: reload sysctl

    #- name: Disable IPv6 (breaks the old monitoring agent, see INFRA-2231)
    #  ansible.posix.sysctl:
    #    name: net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6
    #    value: "1"

    - name: Harden sshd
      template:
        src: templates/sshd_config.j2
        dest: /etc/ssh/sshd_config
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0600"
        validate: /usr/sbin/sshd -t -f %s
      notify:
        - restart sshd

  handlers:
    - name: reload sysctl
      command: sysctl --system

    - name: restart sshd
      service: name=ssh state=restarted


- name: Deploy billing-api
  hosts: webservers
  become: true
  serial: "30%"
  max_fail_percentage: 10

  vars:
    app_name: billing-api
    app_user: billing
    app_root: /srv/{{ app_name }}
    release_version: "{{ lookup('env', 'RELEASE_VERSION') | default('2.14.1', true) }}"
    release_dir: "{{ app_root }}/releases/{{ release_version }}"
    artifact_url: "https://artifacts.internal.example.com/repository/releases/{{ app_name }}/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz"
    # artifact_sha256 is passed in by the CI pipeline (-e artifact_sha256=...)
    keep_releases: 5
    healthcheck_url: http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz

  tasks:
    - name: Ensure application directories exist
      file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: directory
        owner: "{{ app_user }}"
        group: "{{ app_user }}"
        mode: "0755"
      loop:
        - "{{ app_root }}"
        - "{{ app_root }}/releases"
        - "{{ app_root }}/shared/log"
        - "{{ release_dir }}"

    - name: Deploy release
      block:
        - name: Download artifact
          get_url:
            url: "{{ artifact_url }}"
            dest: /tmp/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz
            checksum: "sha256:{{ artifact_sha256 }}"
            timeout: 60

        - name: Unpack release
          unarchive:
            src: /tmp/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz
            dest: "{{ release_dir }}"
            remote_src: yes
            owner: "{{ app_user }}"

        - name: Run database migrations (once per deploy)
          shell: |
            set -euo pipefail
            cd {{ release_dir }}
            export $(grep -v '^#' {{ app_root }}/shared/.env | xargs)
            ./bin/migrate status || true
            ./bin/migrate up --lock-timeout 30s
            echo "$(date -Is) migrated to $(./bin/migrate version)" >> {{ app_root }}/shared/log/migrations.log
          args:
            executable: /bin/bash
          run_once: true
          become_user: "{{ app_user }}"
          register: migrate_result
          changed_when: "'no change' not in migrate_result.stdout"

        - name: Switch the current symlink
          file:
            src: "{{ release_dir }}"
            dest: "{{ app_root }}/current"
            state: link
            force: yes
          notify: restart billing-api

        - name: Flush handlers so the health check hits the new release
          meta: flush_handlers

        - name: Wait for the health check to pass
          uri:
            url: "{{ healthcheck_url }}"
            status_code: 200
            return_content: no
          register: health
          retries: 10
          delay: 3
          until: health.status == 200

      rescue:
        - name: Roll back to the previous release
          shell: |
            cd {{ app_root }}/releases
            prev=$(ls -1t | grep -vx '{{ release_version }}' | head -n 1)
            if [ -n "$prev" ]; then
              ln -sfn "{{ app_root }}/releases/$prev" {{ app_root }}/current
              systemctl restart {{ app_name }}
            fi
          args:
            executable: /bin/bash

        - name: Tell the team
          uri:
            url: "{{ slack_webhook_url }}"
            method: POST
            body_format: json
            body:
              text: ":rotating_light: deploy of {{ app_name }} {{ release_version }} failed on {{ inventory_hostname }}, rolled back"
          delegate_to: localhost
          become: false
          when: slack_webhook_url is defined

        - name: Fail the play
          fail:
            msg: "Deployment failed on {{ inventory_hostname }}: {{ ansible_failed_result.msg | default('unknown error') }}"

      always:
        - name: Remove downloaded artifact
          file:
            path: /tmp/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz
            state: absent

    - name: Prune old releases
      shell: ls -1dt {{ app_root }}/releases/* | tail -n +{{ keep_releases + 1 }} | xargs -r rm -rf
      changed_when: false

  handlers:
    - name: restart billing-api
      systemd:
        name: "{{ app_name }}"
        state: restarted
        daemon_reload: yes


- name: Nightly database backups
  hosts: dbservers
  become: yes
  vars:
    backup_dir: /var/backups/postgres
    backup_retention_days: 14
    databases: [billing, billing_audit, keycloak]
    s3_bucket: s3://acme-db-backups/{{ inventory_hostname_short }}

  tasks:
    - name: Install backup tooling
      apt:
        name: [postgresql-client-15, awscli, pigz]
        state: present

    - name: Create backup directory
      file: path={{ backup_dir }} state=directory owner=postgres group=postgres mode=0750

    - name: Install backup script
      copy:
        dest: /usr/local/bin/pg-nightly-backup
        mode: "0755"
        content: |
          #!/usr/bin/env bash
          # Managed by Ansible -- local changes will be overwritten
          set -euo pipefail
          stamp=$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M)
          {% for db in databases %}
          pg_dump -Fc {{ db }} | pigz > {{ backup_dir }}/{{ db }}-${stamp}.dump.gz
          {% endfor %}
          aws s3 sync {{ backup_dir }} {{ s3_bucket }} --only-show-errors
          find {{ backup_dir }} -type f -name '*.dump.gz' -mtime +{{ backup_retention_days }} -delete

    - name: Schedule the backup
      cron:
        name: nightly pg backup
        user: postgres
        minute: "15"
        hour: "2"
        job: /usr/local/bin/pg-nightly-backup >> /var/log/pg-backup.log 2>&1
      when:
        - inventory_hostname == groups['dbservers'] | first
        - enable_backups | default(true) | bool

sed 's/$/\r/' > /tmp/corpus7/j/changelog.md <<'CHANGELOG_EOF'
# Changelog

All notable changes to **tidepool** will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). Dates are in UTC. The "Unreleased" section is updated on every merge to `main`, so it may describe things that are only available in the nightly builds.

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- `tidepool sync --dry-run` now prints a summary table at the end (files to upload / delete / skip) in addition to the per-file log lines.
- Support for `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`, which makes running inside EKS with IRSA work without any extra configuration ([#412]).

### Fixed
- Uploading files whose names contain `%2F` no longer creates an extra "directory" level on some S3-compatible backends (MinIO, Ceph RGW).
  * reported by @hkoster in [#418]

## [2.4.1] - 2024-10-21

### Fixed
* `tidepool verify --sample` ignored the sample ratio when the bucket had fewer than 1000 objects and always checked everything. 
* Config files with a UTF-8 BOM (as written by Notepad) are accepted again.

## [2.4.0] - 2024-09-30

### Added
* New `--exclude-from FILE` option, same syntax as `.gitignore` (negations with `!` are supported, `**` matches across directories).
* `tidepool verify` command that re-hashes the remote objects and compares them with the local manifest. This is slow on large buckets; use `--sample 0.05` to only check a random 5% of the objects.
* _Experimental_ parallel listing for buckets with more than ~1M objects, enabled with `TIDEPOOL_PARALLEL_LIST=1`

### Changed
- The default chunk size went from 8 MiB to 16 MiB. This roughly halves the number of requests for large files but increases peak memory usage, see the [tuning guide](docs/tuning.md#chunk-size) if you are running on very small instances.
- Progress output is now written to stderr instead of stdout, so `tidepool ls --json | jq` works again.
    - If you relied on parsing the progress bar (please don't), use `--progress=plain`.

### Deprecated
- `--no-checksum` is deprecated in favour of `--checksum=none` and will be removed in 3.0.


## [2.3.2] - 2024-08-12

### Fixed
- Fixed a crash (`IndexError: list index out of range`) when the remote prefix was empty and `--delete` was passed.
- Retries now respect the `Retry-After` header returned by Backblaze B2 instead of always using exponential backoff.
- Windows: paths longer than 260 characters are now handled via the `\\?\` prefix. Thanks to @ana-perez for the patch!

### Security
- Bumped `urllib3` to 2.2.2 (CVE-2024-37891). tidepool itself was not affected because we never send `Proxy-Authorization` headers on redirects, but several scanners flagged it anyway.

## [2.3.1] - 2024-07-02

### Fixed
* `tidepool init` wrote the config file with mode `0644`; it is now `0600` because it can contain secrets.
* The `--since` filter ignored the timezone offset of the given timestamp:
  * `--since 2024-06-01T00:00:00+02:00` used to be treated as UTC
  * naive timestamps are still interpreted as local time, as documented

# Contributing to Fernwood

First off, thanks for taking the time to contribute! :tada: Fernwood is maintained by a handful of volunteers in their spare time, so every bug report, documentation fix and pull request genuinely helps.

This document describes how to set up a development environment, how we review changes and what we expect from a pull request. It is a living document -- if something here is outdated or unclear, please open an issue or (even better) a PR that fixes it. 

<!-- TODO(maintainers): move the release checklist into RELEASING.md once 3.0 is out -->

## Table of contents

- [Code of conduct](#code-of-conduct)
- [Reporting bugs](#reporting-bugs)
- [Development setup](#development-setup)
- [Running the test suite](#running-the-test-suite)
- [Style guide](#style-guide)
  - [Commit messages](#commit-messages)
- [Pull request process](#pull-request-process)
- [Releasing](#releasing)

## Code of conduct

This project follows the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/). By participating you are expected to uphold it. Please report unacceptable behaviour to conduct@fernwood.dev.

## Reporting bugs

Before opening a new issue, please search the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fernwood-dev/fernwood/issues) -- someone may already have reported the same problem. A good bug report contains:

* the Fernwood version (`python -c "import fernwood; print(fernwood.__version__)"`) and your Python version
* a **minimal** reproducible example. Ideally something we can paste into a REPL;
  screenshots of code are not very helpful.
* what you expected to happen, and what actually happened (including the full traceback)
   * if the problem only shows up with a particular schema, please include it
   * if it is a performance problem, the output of `python -m cProfile -s cumtime your_script.py | head -n 40` helps a lot

> [!NOTE]
> Security issues should **not** be reported in the public tracker. Please follow the instructions in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) instead.


## Development setup

Fernwood uses [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for dependency management, but plain `pip` + `venv` works just as well. You will need Python 3.9 or newer, and a C compiler if you want to build the optional speedups.

1. Fork the repository on GitHub and clone your fork:

   ```bash
   git clone git@github.com:<your-username>/fernwood.git
   cd fernwood
   git remote add upstream https://github.com/fernwood-dev/fernwood.git
   ```

2. Create a virtual environment and install the package in editable mode together with the development dependencies:

   ```bash
   uv venv --python 3.12
   source .venv/bin/activate
   uv pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"
   ```

3. Install the pre-commit hooks. They run `ruff`, `mypy` and a couple of sanity checks on every commit:

    ```bash
    pre-commit install
    pre-commit run --all-files   # optional, takes a minute the first time
    ```

4. (Optional) If you work on the C extension, set `FERNWOOD_BUILD_EXT=1` before installing. Our hook configuration looks roughly like this, in case you want to replicate it in your editor:

   ```yaml
   repos:
     - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
       rev: v0.6.9
       hooks:
         - id: ruff
           args: [--fix]
         - id: ruff-format
     - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/mirrors-mypy
       rev: v1.11.2
       hooks:
         - id: mypy
           additional_dependencies: [types-python-dateutil]
   ```

> [!WARNING]
> Do not run `pip install fernwood` inside the development environment. It will shadow your editable install and you will spend an afternoon wondering why your changes have no effect (ask us how we know).

<details>
<summary>Notes for Windows users</summary>

The test suite runs on Windows in CI, but a few things work differently:

- activate the environment with `.venv\Scripts\activate` instead of `source`
- the speedups need the "Desktop development with C++" workload from the Visual Studio Build Tools
-   symlink-related tests are skipped unless Developer Mode is enabled

</details>

## Running the test suite

We use `pytest`. The quickest way to run everything is:

```bash
pytest -n auto
```

Some useful variations:

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `pytest tests/unit` | only the fast unit tests (< 10 s) |
| `pytest -m "not slow"` | skip the property-based tests that take several minutes |
| `pytest --cov=fernwood --cov-report=html` | coverage report in `htmlcov/` |
| `nox -s tests-3.9 tests-3.13` | run against several Python versions, like CI does |
| `nox -s docs` | build the documentation and fail on warnings |

If you add a new feature, please add tests for it. Bug fixes should come with a regression test that fails without the fix -- this is the single most useful thing you can do to make sure the bug stays fixed.

## Style guide

Formatting and linting are fully automated, so please don't spend time on manual formatting; `ruff format` is the source of truth. A few things the tools can't check:

- Public functions and classes need docstrings (Google style). Private helpers don't, but a one-line comment explaining *why* is always appreciated.
- Prefer small, focused modules. If a file grows beyond ~800 lines it is probably doing too much.
+ Type hints are required for all new code. We run `mypy --strict` on `src/`, but not on `tests/`.
- Error messages should say what went wrong **and** what the user can do about it, e.g. "field `age` must be >= 0, got -3" rather than "invalid value".

### Commit messages

We loosely follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/). The type prefix is used to generate the changelog, so please get it right:

| Prefix | Use for | Shows up in changelog? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `feat:` | new user-facing functionality | yes, under *Added* |
| `fix:` | bug fixes | yes, under *Fixed* |
| `perf:` | performance improvements | yes |
| `docs:` | documentation only | no |
| `refactor:` | code changes that neither fix a bug nor add a feature | no |
| `chore:` / `ci:` | tooling, dependencies, CI configuration | no |

Breaking changes must include a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer that explains the migration path.

## Pull request process

1. Open an issue first for anything bigger than a small bug fix, so we can agree on the approach before you invest a lot of time.
2. Keep pull requests focused. Two small PRs are much easier to review than one big one that does several unrelated things.
3. Make sure CI is green. If a check fails for reasons unrelated to your change (it happens, the macOS runners are flaky), leave a comment and a maintainer will re-run it.
4. Add a news fragment in `changes/`:
   - name it `<PR number>.<type>.md`, e.g. `1234.fixed.md`
   - one or two sentences, written for users rather than for reviewers
     * you can use Markdown, but keep it to inline formatting
5. A maintainer will review your PR, usually within a week. We may push small fixups directly to your branch, so please enable "Allow edits from maintainers".

> **Tip:** draft pull requests are welcome. Open one early if you want feedback on the general direction before polishing everything.

## Releasing

*This section is for maintainers.*

1. Make sure `main` is green and the changelog fragments look sensible: `towncrier build --draft`.
2. Bump the version and build the changelog:
   ```bash
   bump-my-version bump minor   # or patch / major
   towncrier build --yes
   git push upstream main --follow-tags
   ```
3. The `release` workflow builds the wheels and publishes them to PyPI via trusted publishing. Keep an eye on it, and if something goes wrong, **do not** delete the tag; yank the release on PyPI and cut a new patch version instead.



Thanks again for contributing!

name: shopfront

x-common: &common
  restart: unless-stopped
  logging:
    driver: json-file
    options:
      max-size: "10m"
      max-file: "3"
  networks:
    - backend

x-healthcheck: &healthcheck-defaults
  interval: 10s
  timeout: 5s
  retries: 5
  start_period: 20s

x-app-env: &app-env
  DATABASE_URL: postgres://shop:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-shop}@postgres:5432/shop
  REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
  CELERY_BROKER_URL: redis://redis:6379/1
  SECRET_KEY: ${SECRET_KEY:?SECRET_KEY must be set in .env}
  DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE: shop.settings.local
  LOG_LEVEL:   ${LOG_LEVEL:-info}

services:
  traefik:
    <<: *common
    image: traefik:v3.1
    command:
      - --api.insecure=true
      - --providers.docker=true
      - --providers.docker.exposedbydefault=false
      - --entrypoints.web.address=:80
      - --accesslog=true
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "8081:8080"   # dashboard
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    networks:
      - frontend
      - backend

  web:
    <<: *common
    build:
      context: ./frontend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.dev
      args:
        NODE_VERSION: "20"
    environment:
      - NODE_ENV=development
      - VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://api.shop.localhost
      - CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING=true
    volumes:
      - ./frontend:/app
      - web-node-modules:/app/node_modules
    labels:
      - "traefik.enable=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.web.rule=Host(`shop.localhost`)"
      - "traefik.http.services.web.loadbalancer.server.port=5173"
    depends_on:
      - api
    networks: [frontend]

  api:
    <<: *common
    build: ./backend
    image: shopfront/api:dev
    command: >
      sh -c "python manage.py migrate --noinput &&
             python manage.py collectstatic --noinput --clear &&
             gunicorn shop.wsgi:application --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 --workers 3 --threads 2 --timeout 120 --reload --access-logfile -"
    environment:
      <<: *app-env
      DJANGO_DEBUG: "true"
      ALLOWED_HOSTS: api.shop.localhost,localhost,127.0.0.1
    env_file: .env
    volumes:
      - ./backend:/srv/app
      - media:/srv/media
    labels:
      - traefik.enable=true
      - traefik.http.routers.api.rule=Host(`api.shop.localhost`)
      - traefik.http.services.api.loadbalancer.server.port=8000
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_started
    healthcheck:
      <<: *healthcheck-defaults
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8000/healthz/ || exit 1"]

  worker:
    <<: *common
    image: shopfront/api:dev
    command: celery -A shop worker --loglevel=INFO --concurrency=4 --max-tasks-per-child=200 -Q default,emails,thumbnails
    environment:
      <<: *app-env
      C_FORCE_ROOT: "false"
    volumes:
      - ./backend:/srv/app
      - media:/srv/media
    depends_on: [api, redis]

  scheduler:
    <<: *common
    image: shopfront/api:dev
    command: celery -A shop beat --loglevel=INFO --scheduler django_celery_beat.schedulers:DatabaseScheduler
    environment: *app-env
    depends_on:
      - worker

  postgres:
    <<: *common
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: shop
      POSTGRES_USER: shop
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-shop}
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./docker/postgres/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
    healthcheck:
      <<: *healthcheck-defaults
      test: [ "CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}" ]

  redis:
    <<: *common
    image: redis:7.4-alpine
    command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes", "--maxmemory", "256mb", "--maxmemory-policy", "allkeys-lru"]
    volumes:
      - redis-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      <<: *healthcheck-defaults
      test: [CMD, redis-cli, ping]
      interval: 5s

  # elasticsearch:
  #   image: docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch:8.15.0
  #   environment:
  #     - discovery.type=single-node
  #     - xpack.security.enabled=false
  #   (search is mocked in dev for now, see SHOP-981)

  mailpit:
    image: axllent/mailpit:latest
    profiles: ["debug"]
    ports:
      - "8025:8025"
      - "1025:1025"
    environment:
      MP_SMTP_AUTH_ACCEPT_ANY: 1
      MP_SMTP_AUTH_ALLOW_INSECURE: 1
    networks:
      - backend

  prometheus:
    <<: *common
    image: prom/prometheus:v2.54.1
    profiles: [monitoring]
    command:
      - --config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
      - --storage.tsdb.retention.time=7d
    volumes:
      - ./docker/prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - prometheus-data:/prometheus

  grafana:
    <<: *common
    image: grafana/grafana:11.2.0
    profiles: [monitoring]
    environment:
      GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${GRAFANA_PASSWORD:-admin}
      GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP: "false"
    volumes:
      - grafana-data:/var/lib/grafana
      - ./docker/grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
    ports: ["3000:3000"]
    depends_on: [prometheus]


volumes:
  pgdata:
  redis-data:
  media:
  web-node-modules:
  prometheus-data:
  grafana-data:
    driver: local

networks:
  frontend:
  backend:
    driver: bridge
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 172.28.0.0/16
