102	
103	Then start the gateway with `pylon serve` and try it:\
104	`curl -i localhost:8080/v1/health`
105	
106	The first request can be slow while the JWKS keys are fetched.  
107	Later requests use the cached key set.
108	
109	## Configuration
110	
111	| Key | Type | Default | Description |
112	|-----|------|---------|-------------|
113	| `listeners[].address` | string | `":8080"` | Address to bind. Use `unix:/run/pylon.sock` for a Unix socket; IPv6 addresses must be bracketed, e.g. `[::1]:8080`, and link-local addresses need a zone such as `[fe80::1%eth0]:8080`. |
114	| `routes[].match.path_prefix` | string | -- | Prefix match on the *decoded* path. Trailing slashes matter: `/v1` also matches `/v1beta`, while `/v1/` does not. |
115	| `routes[].upstream.timeout` | duration | `30s` | Total time budget for the upstream exchange including retries; per-try timeouts are set with `retry.per_try_timeout` and must be smaller than this value. |
116	| `ratelimit.backend` | enum | `local` | `local` or `redis` |
117	| `admin.address` | string | `127.0.0.1:9901` | Admin API. **Never** expose it publicly. |
118	
119	Environment variables override file values: `PYLON_` + the upper-cased key path, with `__` as the separator (`PYLON_ADMIN__ADDRESS`).
120	
121	### Writing plugins
122	
123	Plugins implement a single interface. A minimal Go plugin:
124	
125	```go
126	package main
127	
128	import (
129		"net/http"
130	
131		"github.com/pylon-gw/pylon/sdk/plugin"
132	)
133	
134	// AddHeader stamps every response with a fixed header.
135	type AddHeader struct {
136		Name  string `yaml:"name"`
137		Value string `yaml:"value"`
138	}
139	
140	func (p *AddHeader) Handle(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
141		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {

arguments.command:
emit() {
  local mode="$1" c n i
  c=$(cat)
  c=${c//"@@TAB@@"/$'\t'}
  c=${c//"@@SP@@"/ }
  case "$mode" in
    lf)   printf '%s\n' "$c" ;;
    nonl) printf '%s' "$c" ;;
    crlf) c=${c//$'\n'/$'\r\n'}; printf '%s\r\n' "$c" ;;
    tail[1-9]) n=${mode#tail}; printf '%s\n' "$c"; for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do printf '\n'; done ;;
    *) echo "unknown mode: $mode" >&2; return 1 ;;
  esac
}

---
# Provision the little VPS that runs my blog
- hosts: blog
  become: yes
  vars:
    blog_user: deploy
    blog_root: /srv/blog
    packages: [nginx, git, certbot, python3-certbot-nginx]

  tasks:
  - name: Install base packages
    apt:
      name: "{{ packages }}"
      state: present
      update_cache: yes
      cache_valid_time: 3600  # one hour

  - name: Create the deploy user
    user: name={{ blog_user }} shell=/bin/bash groups=www-data append=yes

  - name: Make sure the web root exists
    file:
      path: "{{ blog_root }}"
      state: directory
      owner: "{{ blog_user }}"
      group: www-data
      mode: '0755'

  - name: Drop in the nginx site config
    template: src=templates/blog.conf.j2 dest=/etc/nginx/sites-available/blog.conf
    notify: reload nginx

  - name: Enable the site
    file:
      src: /etc/nginx/sites-available/blog.conf
      dest: /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/blog.conf
      state: link
    notify: reload nginx

  - name: Get a certificate (only the first time)
    command: certbot --nginx -d example.org -d www.example.org --non-interactive --agree-tos -m me@example.org
    args:
      creates: /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.org/fullchain.pem

  handlers:
    - name: reload nginx
      service: name=nginx state=reloaded
__EOF__

w ansible_playbook_2.yml tail2 <<'__EOF__'
- name: Raspberry Pi housekeeping
  hosts: pis
  gather_facts: false
  become: true

  vars:
    backup_dir: /mnt/usb/backups
    keep_days: 14

  tasks:
    - name: Ping first, so we fail fast
      ansible.builtin.ping:

    - name: Upgrade everything
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        upgrade: dist
        update_cache: true
        autoremove: true

    - name: Make sure the handy tools are there
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name:
          - htop
          - tmux
          - rsync
          - vim
        state: present

    - name: Write the backup script
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /usr/local/bin/pi-backup.sh
        mode: "0750"
        content: |
          #!/bin/sh
          set -eu
          tar czf {{ backup_dir }}/home-$(date +%F).tgz /home/pi
          find {{ backup_dir }} -name 'home-*.tgz' -mtime +{{ keep_days }} -delete

    - name: Nightly cron entry for the backup
      ansible.builtin.cron:
        name: pi backup
        hour: "3"
        minute: "15"
        job: /usr/local/bin/pi-backup.sh >> /var/log/pi-backup.log 2>&1

    - name: Check whether a reboot is needed
      ansible.builtin.stat:
        path: /var/run/reboot-required
      register: reboot_flag

    - name: Reboot if the kernel was updated
      ansible.builtin.reboot:
        reboot_timeout: 300
      when: reboot_flag.stat.exists
__EOF__

- name: Raspberry Pi housekeeping
  hosts: pis
  gather_facts: false
  become: true

  vars:
    backup_dir: /mnt/usb/backups
    keep_days: 14

  tasks:
    - name: Ping first, so we fail fast
      ansible.builtin.ping:

    - name: Upgrade everything
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        upgrade: dist
        update_cache: true
        autoremove: true

    - name: Make sure the handy tools are there
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name:
          - htop
          - tmux
          - rsync
          - vim
        state: present

    - name: Write the backup script
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /usr/local/bin/pi-backup.sh
        mode: "0750"
        content: |
          #!/bin/sh
          set -eu
          tar czf {{ backup_dir }}/home-$(date +%F).tgz /home/pi
          find {{ backup_dir }} -name 'home-*.tgz' -mtime +{{ keep_days }} -delete

    - name: Nightly cron entry for the backup
      ansible.builtin.cron:
        name: pi backup
        hour: "3"
        minute: "15"
        job: /usr/local/bin/pi-backup.sh >> /var/log/pi-backup.log 2>&1

    - name: Check whether a reboot is needed
      ansible.builtin.stat:
        path: /var/run/reboot-required
      register: reboot_flag

    - name: Reboot if the kernel was updated
      ansible.builtin.reboot:
        reboot_timeout: 300
      when: reboot_flag.stat.exists
__EOF__

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Rename photos by the date they were taken.

Small helper I use after copying photos off the camera's SD card.
"""

import argparse
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

# fmt: markdown
USAGE = """
Photo renamer
=============

Renames every `*.jpg` in a folder to `YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS.jpg`, based on the
file's modification time.  Existing files are *never* overwritten, they are
skipped with a warning instead.

Usage:

    rename_photos.py FOLDER [--dry-run] [--suffix S]

Options
-------
* `--dry-run`   only print what would happen
* `--suffix S`  append `S` before the extension, e.g. `_holiday`
"""


def new_name(path: Path, suffix: str = "") -> str:
    stamp = datetime.fromtimestamp(path.stat().st_mtime)
    return stamp.strftime("%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S") + suffix + path.suffix.lower()


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=USAGE, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("folder", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--suffix", default="")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    for photo in sorted(args.folder.glob("*.jpg")):
        target = photo.with_name(new_name(photo, args.suffix))
        if target.exists():
            print(f"skip {photo.name}: {target.name} already exists", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        print(f"{photo.name} -> {target.name}")
        if not args.dry_run:
            photo.rename(target)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
__EOF__

import csv
import sys
from typing import Iterable, List

# fmt: markdown
# csv2md
# ======
#@@SP@@
# Turn a CSV file into a GitHub-flavoured Markdown table.   Handy for pasting@@SP@@
# query results into issues.
#
# * reads from a path, or from stdin when the path is `-`
# * pads every column so the raw Markdown lines up too
# * does **not** escape `|` inside cells yet (TODO)
#
# Example:
#
#     python csv2md.py sales.csv > sales.md
#
# | flag | meaning |
# |--|--|
# | `--no-header` | treat the first row as data |


def read_rows(path: str) -> List[List[str]]:
    handle = sys.stdin if path == "-" else open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8")
    with handle:
        return [row for row in csv.reader(handle)]


def to_markdown(rows: Iterable[List[str]], header: bool = True) -> str:
    rows = list(rows)
    if not rows:
        return ""
    if not header:
        rows.insert(0, [f"col{i + 1}" for i in range(len(rows[0]))])
    widths = [max(len(r[i]) for r in rows) for i in range(len(rows[0]))]
    lines = []
    for n, row in enumerate(rows):
        cells = [cell.ljust(w) for cell, w in zip(row, widths)]
        lines.append("| " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
        if n == 0:
            lines.append("|" + "|".join("-" * (w + 2) for w in widths) + "|")
    return "\n".join(lines)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a != "--no-header"]
    table = to_markdown(read_rows(args[0] if args else "-"), header="--no-header" not in sys.argv)
    print(table)
__EOF__

Expense summary
===============

Usage:  `Rscript expenses.R FILE [MONTH]`

* `MONTH` -- optional, e.g. `2024-03`; defaults to all months

    crlf) c=${c//$'\n'/$'\r\n'}; printf '%s\r\n' "$c" ;;

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Rename photos by the date they were taken.

Small helper I use after copying photos off the camera's SD card.
"""

import argparse
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

# fmt: markdown
USAGE = """
Photo renamer
=============

Renames every `*.jpg` in a folder to `YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS.jpg`, based on the
file's modification time.  Existing files are *never* overwritten, they are
skipped with a warning instead.

Usage:

    rename_photos.py FOLDER [--dry-run] [--suffix S]

Options
-------
* `--dry-run`   only print what would happen
* `--suffix S`  append `S` before the extension, e.g. `_holiday`
"""


def new_name(path: Path, suffix: str = "") -> str:
    stamp = datetime.fromtimestamp(path.stat().st_mtime)
    return stamp.strftime("%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S") + suffix + path.suffix.lower()


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=USAGE, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("folder", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--suffix", default="")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    for photo in sorted(args.folder.glob("*.jpg")):
        target = photo.with_name(new_name(photo, args.suffix))
        if target.exists():
            print(f"skip {photo.name}: {target.name} already exists", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        print(f"{photo.name} -> {target.name}")
        if not args.dry_run:
            photo.rename(target)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
__EOF__

import csv
import sys
from typing import Iterable, List

# fmt: markdown
# csv2md
# ======
#@@SP@@
# Turn a CSV file into a GitHub-flavoured Markdown table.   Handy for pasting@@SP@@
# query results into issues.
#
# * reads from a path, or from stdin when the path is `-`
# * pads every column so the raw Markdown lines up too
# * does **not** escape `|` inside cells yet (TODO)
#
# Example:
#
#     python csv2md.py sales.csv > sales.md
#
# | flag | meaning |
# |--|--|
# | `--no-header` | treat the first row as data |


def read_rows(path: str) -> List[List[str]]:
    handle = sys.stdin if path == "-" else open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8")
    with handle:
        return [row for row in csv.reader(handle)]


def to_markdown(rows: Iterable[List[str]], header: bool = True) -> str:
    rows = list(rows)
    if not rows:
        return ""
    if not header:
        rows.insert(0, [f"col{i + 1}" for i in range(len(rows[0]))])
    widths = [max(len(r[i]) for r in rows) for i in range(len(rows[0]))]
    lines = []
    for n, row in enumerate(rows):
        cells = [cell.ljust(w) for cell, w in zip(row, widths)]
        lines.append("| " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
        if n == 0:
            lines.append("|" + "|".join("-" * (w + 2) for w in widths) + "|")
    return "\n".join(lines)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a != "--no-header"]
    table = to_markdown(read_rows(args[0] if args else "-"), header="--no-header" not in sys.argv)
    print(table)
__EOF__

library(readr)
library(stringr)

# fmt: markdown
# ## Input

# * `Q1` -- age group

      str_detect(commute, "car|drive") ~ "car",

  ) %>%

Expense summary
===============

Usage:  `Rscript expenses.R FILE [MONTH]`

* `FILE`  -- a CSV with the columns *date*, *category* and *amount*
* `MONTH` -- optional, e.g. `2024-03`; defaults to all months

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

#
# Converted from the Chef cookbook `acme_web` (v3.2.1) with chef2ansible 0.4.2

- name: Prepare all hosts

  vars:

          Ubuntu 20.04 and newer; {{ ansible_distribution }}

        quiet: true

  tasks:
    - name: Install base packages
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name: "{{ base_packages }}"
        state: present
        update_cache: yes
        cache_valid_time: 3600
      tags: [packages, base]

    - name: Configure timezone  # was: execute[set-timezone] in the Chef recipe

    - name: Template chrony configuration

      when:

      6134333665353966363534333632666535333761666131620a663537646436643839616531643561
      63396265333966386166373632626539326166353965363262633030333630313338646335303630
      3438626666666137650a353638643435666633633964366338633066623234616432373231333331
      6564
    nginx_worker_connections: 4096

  tasks:
    - name: Include legacy Chef attribute shims
      ansible.builtin.include_tasks: tasks/chef_attribute_shims.yml
      when: legacy_attributes | default(false) | bool

    - name: Ensure release directory exists

        group: acmeweb

        dest: "{{ app_root }}/releases/{{ app_version }}"
        remote_src: yes

      register: unpack_result

      until: unpack_result is succeeded

    - name: Render application config

    - name: Point the current symlink at the new release

        dest: "{{ app_root }}/current"

    - name: Run database migrations (once per play)

        chdir: "{{ app_root }}/current"
      run_once: true

      environment:

        url: "http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz"
        status_code: [200, 204]
      register: health
      until: health.status in [200, 204]
      retries: 12
      delay: 5

  post_tasks:
    - name: Prune old releases (keep five)
      ansible.builtin.shell: >
        ls -1dt {{ app_root }}/releases/* | tail -n +6 | xargs --no-run-if-empty rm -rf
      args:

      changed_when: false

  handlers:
    - name: restart app
      ansible.builtin.systemd:
        name: "{{ app_name }}"
        state: restarted
        daemon_reload: true
    - name: reload nginx
      ansible.builtin.service: name=nginx state=reloaded

- name: Deploy web application

    app_name: acme-web

    app_root: /opt/{{ app_name }}

        remote_src: yes

      register: unpack_result
      retries: 3

    - name: Point the current symlink at the new release

        force: yes

    - name: Run database migrations (once per play)

        chdir: "{{ app_root }}/current"
      run_once: true
      delegate_to: "{{ groups['web'] | first }}"
      register: migrate_out

        status_code: [200, 204]
      register: health
      until: health.status in [200, 204]
      retries: 12
      delay: 5

      ansible.builtin.shell: >

      args:

        name: "{{ app_name }}"
        state: restarted
        daemon_reload: true

      ansible.builtin.service: name=nginx state=reloaded

  will replace this one on release)
- Known issue: `orbit watch` misses events on SMB/CIFS mounts, see #1042

## [3.4.0](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/compare/v3.3.2...v3.4.0) (2024-05-21)


### Features

* **cli:** add `--dry-run` to `orbit sync` ([#1018](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/issues/1018)) ([4be1c0a](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/commit/4be1c0a9d2e7f13c6b8a0e5f4d3c2b1a09f8e7d6))
* **config:** support `extends` with relative paths ([e91f3d2](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/commit/e91f3d2c4b5a6978e0d1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b)), closes [#977](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/issues/977) [#1001](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/issues/1001)

### Bug Fixes

* **sync:** don't follow symlinks outside the project root by default ([a5b6c7d](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/commit/a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4))

### [3.3.2](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/compare/v3.3.1...v3.3.2) (2024-04-02)


### Bug Fixes

* **windows:** normalise drive letters before comparing paths ([#995](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/issues/995)) ([5f1e2d3](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/commit/5f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0a9b8c7d6))
* **watch:** debounce rename events on macOS ([b0c1d2e](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/commit/b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9))

### [3.3.1](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/compare/v3.3.0...v3.3.1) (2024-03-08)


### Bug Fixes

* **cli:** `orbit --version` printed `undefined` when installed globally with pnpm ([9a8b7c6](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/commit/9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e2f1a0b))


### Reverts

* Revert "perf(sync): hash files in a worker pool" ([2c3d4e5](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/commit/2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d)), closes [#981](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/issues/981)

* **sync:** respect `.gitignore` files in nested directories ([#952](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/issues/952)) ([1a2b3c4](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/commit/1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b))


### Performance Improvements

* **sync:** skip unchanged files using mtime + size before hashing ([d4e5f6a](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/commit/d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3))

### [3.1.1](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/compare/v3.1.0...v3.1.1) (2023-12-01)

## [3.1.0](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/compare/v3.0.0...v3.1.0) (2023-11-07)


### Features

* **status:** show the number of pending files per target ([c6d7e8f](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/commit/c6d7e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5))


### Bug Fixes

* **cli:** exit with code 2 on unknown flags instead of printing help and exiting 0 ([e8f9a0b](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/commit/e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7))

## [3.0.0](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/compare/v2.9.1...v3.0.0) (2023-09-12)


### ⚠ BREAKING CHANGES

* **node:** Node.js 16 is no longer supported; the minimum version is now 18.17.
* **config:** the `legacyGlobs` option has been removed. Patterns are now
always interpreted as micromatch globs. To keep the old behaviour, prefix the
pattern with `re:` (for example `re:^src/.*\.ts$`).

Configuration files that still set `legacyGlobs: true` now fail validation
with error `ORB013`.

### Features

* **config:** add a JSON schema for `.orbitrc` ([8f9a0b1](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/commit/8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a))
* **config:** remove `legacyGlobs` ([7d8e9f0](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/commit/7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e))
* **node:** require Node.js 18.17 ([3b4c5d6](https://github.com/orbit-dev/orbit/commit/3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c))

---

## 2.x and earlier

The 2.x entries were maintained by hand in the [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/) format. The 1.x entries were converted from `HISTORY.rst` with pandoc and have not been cleaned up since.

### [2.9.1] - 2022-11-30
#### Fixed
- `orbit init` no longer overwrites an existing `.orbitrc` unless `--force` is given (#712).
- Globs such as `src/**/*.ts` are now matched case-insensitively on macOS and Windows.

### [2.9.0] - 2022-10-04
#### Added
- `--json` output for `orbit status`.
- Experimental `watch` mode behind `ORBIT_EXPERIMENTAL=watch`.
#### Changed
- The default concurrency is now `os.cpus().length - 1` (minimum 1).
#### Deprecated
- `legacyGlobs`; it will be removed in 3.0.

### [2.8.3] - 2022-07-19
#### Security
- Bumped `minimist` to 1.2.6 (CVE-2021-44906). Orbit itself was not affected, but scanners kept flagging it.

### 1.4.2 (2021-03-17)

-   Fixed a crash when the project path contained a hash character, see
    \#388.
-   `orbit sync` now exits with status 2 (not 1) on configuration
    errors, as documented in [the manual](https://orbit-dev.github.io/orbit/1.x/cli.html#exit-codes).

### 1.4.0 (2021-01-09)

-   New `ignore` option. Patterns are matched against paths relative
    to the project root, e.g. build/\*\* or \*.log.
-   Dropped support for Node.js 8 and 10[^1].
-   **Experimental:** orbit sync \--parallel *N* runs up to *N* uploads
    at once.

### 1.3.0 (2020-09-28)

1.  First release on npm under the `@orbit-dev` scope.
2.  The `orbit.json` config file is now called `.orbitrc`; the old
    name is still read but prints a warning.

[^1]: Node.js 10 reached end-of-life on 2021-04-30, but our CI provider
    removed its images a few weeks earlier.

    Users stuck on Node.js 10 can keep using 1.3.x, which still receives
    security fixes until the end of 2021.

# **Contributing to Harbor Atlas** Thanks for taking the time to contribute! This guide started life as a Google Doc that the core team kept editing for “just one more week” for about two years… so if something reads oddly, that’s probably why. Please open an issue (or a PR!) when you spot something that’s out of date. **Note:** this document covers the `harbor-atlas` monorepo only. The mobile apps (`atlas-ios` and `atlas-android`) have their own guides. ## **Before you start** * Read the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). We take it seriously – reports go to [conduct@harbor-atlas.org](mailto:conduct@harbor-atlas.org) and are handled by two people outside the core team. * Search the [existing issues](https://github.com/harbor-atlas/harbor-atlas/issues) before opening a new one. If you find a match, add a reaction rather than a “+1” comment – it keeps the thread readable. * For anything bigger than a bug fix, open a “proposal” issue first. It’s much less painful to change a plan than a 2,000-line PR… * Proposals are discussed in the fortnightly community call (Thursdays, 16:00 UTC). * Can’t make the call? That’s fine – comment on the issue instead. ## **Setting up your environment** 1. Install the prerequisites: 1. **Node.js 20** (CI runs 20.11 – anything older than 20.9 fails the `engines` check) 2. **pnpm 8** – run `corepack enable` and you’re done 3. **Docker Desktop**, or any engine with Compose v2 2. Fork the repository and clone your fork: ``` git clone git@github.com:/harbor-atlas.git cd harbor-atlas pnpm install ``` 3. Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in the values from the “Shared dev secrets” entry in the team vault. 1. No vault access yet? Ask in `#atlas-dev` and someone will add you. 2. **Never** commit `.env.local`. It’s in `.gitignore`, but people have force-added it before… 4. Start everything with `pnpm dev`. The first run downloads about 2 GB of images, so it’s a good moment for a coffee. 5. Open [http://localhost:5173](http://localhost:5173) – you should see the map with the demo harbour loaded, like this:

>>>>> gd2md-html alert: inline image link here (to images/image1.png). Store image on your image server and adjust path/filename/extension if necessary.
(Back to top)(Next alert)
>>>>>

![alt_text](images/image1.png "image_tooltip") > **Tip:** if `pnpm dev` hangs at “waiting for postgres…”, run `docker compose down -v` and try again. This wipes your local database, so export anything you care about first. ## **Finding something to work on** Issues are labelled so you can find a good fit:
Label What it means Good for
good first issue Small and well scoped, with a mentor assigned Your first contribution
help wanted We agree it should be done, but nobody on the core team has time Regular contributors
needs design Blocked on a decision – please don’t start coding yet Discussion only
Comment on the issue to say you’re working on it. If there’s no activity for 30 days we’ll assume you’ve moved on and unassign you (no hard feelings!). ## **Commit messages** We use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/). The release tooling reads them to build the changelog, so a sloppy message ends up in the release notes forever… > **Tip:** run `pnpm commit` for an interactive prompt that builds the message for you. It’s slower than typing, but it never gets the format wrong. Some good examples: * `feat(map): cluster markers below zoom level 9` * `fix(api): return 404 instead of 500 for unknown harbour IDs` * `docs: explain the “stale tiles” warning` **Important: **a commit that changes public API behaviour must include a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer, even if you’re sure nobody uses that endpoint. (Somebody always does.) ## **Opening a pull request** 1. Rebase on the latest `main`. Please don’t merge `main` into your branch – it makes the history hard to read. 2. Run the checks locally: 1. `pnpm lint` 2. `pnpm test` – unit tests only, about a minute 3. `pnpm test:e2e` – needs the dev stack running; skip it if you only touched docs 3. Push and open the PR against `main`. Fill in the template; “see title” is not a description. 4. Wait for a review. We aim to respond within **two working days**. If nothing has happened after a week, ping the maintainers team on the PR – we won’t be offended. * Reviewers may push small fixes (typos, lint) to your branch. Untick “Allow edits by maintainers” if you’d rather they didn’t. 5. Once it’s approved, a maintainer squash-merges it. The PR title becomes the commit message, so make it a good one. ## **A final word** > “Leave the campsite cleaner than you found it.” > > – sign at the trailhead near our first office, and the closest thing this project has to a motto Thank you for helping out. Really.

# Exported from Portainer 2.19.4 (stack "billing-prod", id 37) on 2024-03-27T14:02:11Z.
# The original file was generated from `docker run` commands with composerize
# and has been edited by hand since. The explicit `version` key stays because

version: "3.8"

x-logging: &default-logging
  driver: "json-file"
  options:
    max-size: "10m"
    max-file: "5"
    tag: "{{.ImageName}}|{{.Name}}|{{.ID}}"

x-healthcheck: &healthcheck-defaults
  interval: 30s
  timeout: 5s
  retries: 3
  start_period: 20s

x-app-env: &app-env
  DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE: "billing.settings.production"
  REDIS_URL: "redis://cache:6379/0"
  SENTRY_DSN: "${SENTRY_DSN:-}"
  TZ: "UTC"

services:
  api:
    image: "registry.example.com/billing/api:2024.03.4"
    container_name: "billing_api"
    restart: "unless-stopped"
    command: ["gunicorn", "billing.wsgi:application", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8000", "--workers", "4", "--timeout", "120", "--access-logfile", "-"]
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
      - "127.0.0.1:9100:9100"
    environment:
      <<: *app-env
      DATABASE_URL: "postgres://billing:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?POSTGRES_PASSWORD must be set}@db:5432/billing"
      ALLOWED_HOSTS: "billing.example.com,billing-internal.example.com"
      FEATURE_FLAGS: "invoices_v2,stripe_tax"
    env_file:
      - ./env/common.env
      - ./env/production.env
    secrets:
      - source: stripe_api_key
        target: /run/secrets/stripe_api_key
        mode: 0400
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      cache:
        condition: service_started
    healthcheck:
      <<: *healthcheck-defaults
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -fsS http://localhost:8000/healthz || exit 1"]
    logging: *default-logging
    networks:
      - backend
      - frontend
    labels:
      com.example.team: "payments"
      com.example.oncall: "payments-oncall@example.com"
      traefik.enable: "true"
      traefik.http.routers.billing.rule: "Host(`billing.example.com`) && PathPrefix(`/api`)"
      traefik.http.routers.billing.tls.certresolver: "letsencrypt"
      traefik.http.services.billing.loadbalancer.server.port: "8000"
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2.0"
          memory: 1536M
        reservations:
          memory: 512M

  worker:
    image: "registry.example.com/billing/api:2024.03.4"
    container_name: "billing_worker"
    restart: "unless-stopped"
    command:
      - celery
      - "-A"
      - billing
      - worker
      - "--loglevel=INFO"
      - "--concurrency=8"
      - "--queues=default,invoices,webhooks"
    environment:
      - "DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=billing.settings.production"
      - "DATABASE_URL=postgres://billing:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/billing"
      - "CELERY_BROKER_URL=redis://cache:6379/1"
      - "C_FORCE_ROOT=false"
    depends_on:
      - db
      - cache
    logging: *default-logging
    networks:
      - backend
    stop_grace_period: 2m

  db:
    image: "postgres:15.6-alpine"
    container_name: "billing_db"
    restart: "always"
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: "billing"
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}"
      POSTGRES_DB: "billing"
      PGDATA: "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata"
    volumes:
      - "pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data"
      - "./initdb:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro"
    healthcheck:
      <<: *healthcheck-defaults
      test: ["CMD", "pg_isready", "-U", "billing", "-d", "billing"]
    shm_size: "256mb"
    logging: *default-logging
    networks:
      backend:
        aliases:
          - postgres
          - billing-db

  cache:
    image: "redis:7.2-alpine"
    container_name: "billing_cache"
    restart: "always"
    command: redis-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
    sysctls:
      net.core.somaxconn: 1024
    ulimits:
      nofile:
        soft: 65536
        hard: 65536
    networks:
      - backend

  # The proxy block below was pasted from `docker compose config` output,
  # which is why it uses the long syntax and quotes the published ports.
  proxy:
    image: traefik:v2.11
    command:
      - --providers.docker=true
      - --providers.docker.exposedbydefault=false
      - --entrypoints.web.address=:80
      - --entrypoints.websecure.address=:443
      - --certificatesresolvers.letsencrypt.acme.email=ops@example.com
      - --certificatesresolvers.letsencrypt.acme.storage=/letsencrypt/acme.json
      - --certificatesresolvers.letsencrypt.acme.httpchallenge.entrypoint=web
    networks:
      frontend: null
    ports:
      - mode: ingress
        target: 80
        published: "80"
        protocol: tcp
      - mode: ingress
        target: 443
        published: "443"
        protocol: tcp
    volumes:
      - type: bind
        source: /var/run/docker.sock
        target: /var/run/docker.sock
        read_only: true
        bind:
          create_host_path: true
      - type: volume
        source: letsencrypt
        target: /letsencrypt
        volume: {}

networks:
  frontend:
    name: billing_frontend
  backend:
    driver: bridge
    internal: true
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: "172.28.0.0/16"

volumes:
  pgdata:
    driver: local
    driver_opts:
      type: "nfs"
      o: "addr=10.0.12.5,nolock,soft,rw"
      device: ":/exports/billing/pgdata"
  letsencrypt: {}

secrets:
  stripe_api_key:
    external: true
    name: billing_stripe_api_key_v3

openapi: 3.0.1
info:
  title: Fleet Telematics API
  description: |
    Public API for the **FleetCore** telematics platform.

    > Generated by springdoc-openapi 2.3.0 from `telematics-api` build 2024.05.2.
    > Change the controller annotations, not this file.

    ## Rate limits

    | Plan       | Requests / minute | Burst |
    |------------|-------------------|-------|
    | Starter    | 60                | 10    |
    | Business   | 600               | 100   |
    | Enterprise | negotiated        | n/a   |
  license:
    name: Proprietary
    url: https://fleetcore.example/legal/api-terms
  version: 2.14.0
servers:
- url: https://api.fleetcore.example/v2
  description: Production
- url: https://sandbox.api.fleetcore.example/v2
  description: Sandbox (data is reset nightly at 02:00 UTC)
security:
- oauth2:
  - telematics:read
tags:
- name: vehicles
  description: Vehicle registry
- name: trips
  description: Trip history and live positions
x-tagGroups:
- name: Fleet
  tags:
  - vehicles
  - trips
paths:
  /vehicles:
    get:
      tags:
      - vehicles
      summary: List vehicles
      description: Returns a cursor-paginated list of the vehicles visible to the caller.
      operationId: listVehicles
      parameters:
      - name: status
        in: query
        description: "Comma-separated list, e.g. `active,maintenance`. Default: all statuses."
        required: false
        style: form
        explode: false
        schema:
          type: array
          items:
            type: string
            enum:
            - active
            - maintenance
            - retired
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          headers:
            X-RateLimit-Remaining:
              description: Requests left in the current window
              schema:
                type: integer
                format: int32
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/VehiclePage"
              examples:
                twoVehicles:
                  summary: Two vehicles and a next-page cursor
                  value:
                    data:
                    - id: veh_01HV3K9Z6Q
                      vin: 1FTFW1E50PFA12345
                      status: active
                    - id: veh_01HV3KA2M1
                      vin: WDB9634031L123456
                      status: maintenance
                    next_cursor: eyJvZmZzZXQiOjUwfQ==
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
      x-codeSamples:
      - lang: Shell
        label: curl
        source: |
          curl -s "https://api.fleetcore.example/v2/vehicles?status=active,maintenance" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
      x-amazon-apigateway-integration:
        type: http_proxy
        httpMethod: GET
        uri: http://${stageVariables.backendHost}/internal/telematics/v2/vehicles
        passthroughBehavior: when_no_match
        connectionType: VPC_LINK
        connectionId: ${stageVariables.vpcLinkId}
  /vehicles/{vehicleId}/trips:
    post:
      tags:
      - trips
      summary: Record a manual trip
      description: |
        Creates a trip for a vehicle without a telematics unit.

        * `distance_km` is required when no odometer readings are sent.
        * Trips longer than 24 hours are rejected with `422`.
      operationId: createTrip
      parameters:
      - name: vehicleId
        in: path
        required: true
        schema:
          type: string
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/Trip"
        required: true
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Trip"
        "422":
          description: Unprocessable Entity
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
      security:
      - oauth2:
        - telematics:write
      x-internal: false
components:
  schemas:
    Vehicle:
      required:
      - id
      - status
      - vin
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          description: Stable identifier (ULID with a `veh_` prefix)
          example: veh_01HV3K9Z6Q
        vin:
          maxLength: 17
          minLength: 17
          pattern: "^[A-HJ-NPR-Z0-9]{17}$"
          type: string
        registration:
          pattern: "^[A-Z]{2}\\s?\\d{2,5}$"
          type: string
          example: AB 12345
        status:
          type: string
          enum:
          - active
          - maintenance
          - retired
        odometer_km:
          type: number
          format: double
          nullable: true
          x-unit: km
      x-java-class: com.fleetcore.telematics.api.dto.VehicleDto
    VehiclePage:
      type: object
      properties:
        data:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Vehicle"
        next_cursor:
          type: string
          nullable: true
    Trip:
      required:
      - started_at
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          readOnly: true
        started_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        distance_km:
          minimum: 0
          type: number
          format: double
    Problem:
      type: object
      properties:
        title:
          type: string
        detail:
          type: string
  responses:
    Unauthorized:
      description: Missing or invalid bearer token
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
          example:
            title: Unauthorized
            detail: The access token expired at 2024-05-02T10:15:00Z.
  securitySchemes:
    oauth2:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        clientCredentials:
          tokenUrl: https://auth.fleetcore.example/oauth2/token
          scopes:
            telematics:read: Read vehicles and trips
            telematics:write: Create trips and update vehicles

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Synchronise the product catalogue from the legacy Merchandiser API.

Originally written for Python 2.7 and converted with ``2to3`` and
``pyupgrade --py310-plus``.  Type hints were added by MonkeyType from
production traces (``monkeytype apply sync_catalog``) and tidied by hand, so
some of them are broader than they need to be.

Run ``sync-catalog --help`` for usage.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import os
import sys
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Final, Literal, overload

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator, Sequence

    from requests import Session

__all__ = [
    "FIELD_MAP",
    "CatalogRecord",
    "SyncStats",
    "fetch_pages",
    "main",
    "normalise_record",
]

log = logging.getLogger("sync_catalog")

DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE: Final = 250
MAX_BATCH_SIZE: Final = 1000
API_ROOT: Final = os.environ.get("MERCH_API_ROOT", "https://merch.example.com/api/v1")
STATE_FILE: Final = os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/sync-catalog/state.json")

# fmt: markdown
HELP_EPILOG = r"""
## Examples

Sync everything that changed since the last successful run:

    sync-catalog --since last

Sync one collection with a larger batch size\*:

    sync-catalog --collection spring_2024 --batch-size 800

\* Batch sizes above 1000 are silently capped by the upstream API, see
[MERCH-412](https://jira.example.com/browse/MERCH-412).

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 0 | success, or nothing to do |
| 2 | invalid arguments |
| 3 | the upstream API returned an error after all retries |
"""

# fmt: markdown
# ## Field mapping
#
# The upstream API (v1, *deprecated*) and the warehouse use different names for
# the same fields. This mapping was generated from `schema/mapping.csv` by
# `tools/gen_mapping.py`; regenerate it instead of editing it by hand:
#
# - `sku` becomes `product_code`
# - `qty_on_hand` becomes `stock_level` (may be negative for back-orders)

--- title: "Regional Air Quality Monitoring: 2023 Annual Summary" subtitle: "Converted from *AQ-Annual-2023-final_v7.docx* with pandoc 3.1.11" author: - name: Ingrid Solberg orcid: 0000-0002-1825-0097 affiliations: - name: Northfjord Environmental Agency department: Section for Air and Noise - name: Tomás Reyes affiliations: - name: Northfjord Environmental Agency date: 2024-03-15 date-format: "D MMMM YYYY" format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 3 number-sections: true code-fold: true docx: reference-doc: templates/agency-reference.docx bibliography: references.bib csl: apa.csl lang: en-GB execute: echo: false warning: false message: false --- ```{r} #| label: setup #| include: false library(tidyverse) library(lubridate) library(knitr) aq <- read_csv("data/aq_daily_2023.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(date = ymd(date), month = month(date, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE)) aq_hourly <- read_csv("data/aq_hourly_2023.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) aq_annual <- read_csv("data/aq_annual_2015_2023.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) limit_pm25 <- 25 ``` [Draft for consultation — not for citation]{.smallcaps} | Northfjord Environmental Agency | Section for Air and Noise | Postboks 1234, 9001 Tromsø # Executive summary {#sec-summary .unnumbered} Annual mean concentrations of nitrogen dioxide (NO~2~) fell at 11 of the 14 monitoring stations in 2023, continuing the downward trend seen since 2017 [@solberg2021; @eea2023, pp. 41--44]. The daily PM~2.5~ guideline of 25 µg/m^3^ was nevertheless exceeded on `r sum(aq$pm25 > limit_pm25, na.rm = TRUE)` station-days, almost all of them during the February inversion episode (see @sec-episodes). **Key findings** 1\. NO~2~ annual means were below the 40 µg/m^3^ limit value at every station except Havnegata (41.3 µg/m^3^)[^1].\ 2\. PM~10~ exceedances were concentrated in March, when studded-tyre wear and road dust dominate.\ 3\. Ozone peaks stayed well below the information threshold of 180 µg/m^3^. ::: {.callout-note} ## About this version This document was converted from the Word report that went to the board on 4 March 2024. Tables 3–5 were rebuilt from the station database rather than copied, so some numbers differ in the last decimal from the PDF that circulated earlier. ::: # Monitoring network {#sec-network} The network consists of 14 fixed stations (@fig-map): six urban traffic stations, five urban background stations and three regional background stations. Station classification follows the Air Quality Directive’s criteria \[Directive 2008/50/EC, Annex III\], and the station at [Havnegata]{#station-havnegata .station} is the only one classified as a *traffic hot spot*. ![Monitoring stations operating in 2023. Squares: traffic; circles: urban background; triangles: regional background.](figures/network-map.png){#fig-map width=80% fig-alt="Map of the Northfjord region with fourteen station markers."} Data capture : Percentage of valid hourly values in the calendar year. The Directive requires at least 90 %, or 85 % when planned maintenance is excluded. Exceedance day : A day on which the 24-hour mean is above the relevant limit or guideline value. For PM~2.5~ we use the WHO 2021 guideline [@who2021] because the national limit value is still under review. # Results {#sec-results} ## Annual means +----------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+ | Station | NO~2~ | PM~10~ | PM~2.5~ | | | (µg/m^3^) | (µg/m^3^) | (µg/m^3^) | +:===============+============:+============:+============:+ | Havnegata | 41.3 | 19.8 | 9.1 | +----------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+ | Elvebakken | 27.5 | 16.2 | 8.4 | +----------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+ | Øvre Torg\* | 24.9 | 21.7 | 10.2 | +----------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+ | Sjøsiden | 18.0 | 12.4 | 6.9 | +----------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+ : Annual mean concentrations at urban traffic stations, 2023. \*Data capture below 85 %. {#tbl-annual-means} The long-term picture is shown in @fig-no2-trend. Traffic stations have improved fastest, largely because of the electrification of the bus fleet[^2], while urban background levels have changed little since 2020. ```{r} #| label: fig-no2-trend #| fig-cap: "Annual mean NO~2~ by station type, 2015--2023. The dashed line marks the limit value of 40 µg/m^3^." #| fig-width: 8 #| fig-height: 4.5 aq_annual |> filter(pollutant == "NO2") |> group_by(year, station_type) |> summarise(mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |> ggplot(aes(year, mean, colour = station_type)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_hline(yintercept = 40, linetype = "dashed") + labs(x = NULL, y = expression(NO[2] ~ (mu * g / m^3)), colour = "Station type") + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) ``` ## The February inversion episode {#sec-episodes} Between 6 and 17 February a persistent temperature inversion trapped emissions from traffic and residential wood burning in the valley floor. Hourly PM~2.5~ reached 148 µg/m^3^ at Elvebakken on the evening of 11 February, the highest value since the station opened in 2009[^3]. The municipality issued its first ever *red* air-quality warning and asked residents not to burn wood \*unless\* it was their only source of heat. | Month | Exceedance days | Main source (expert judgement) | |:---------|----------------:|:-------------------------------| | January | 3 | Wood burning | | February | 11 | Inversion; wood burning | | March | 7 | Road dust, studded tyres | | November | 2 | Wood burning | : PM~2.5~ exceedance days by month, all stations combined. {#tbl-exceedances} ```{r episode-hours, echo=FALSE, results='asis'} #| tbl-cap: "Hours above 50 µg/m^3^ during the episode, by station." aq_hourly |> filter(between(datetime, ymd_h("2023-02-06 00"), ymd_h("2023-02-17 23")), pm25 > 50) |> count(station, name = "hours") |> arrange(desc(hours)) |> kable(col.names = c("Station", "Hours > 50 µg/m³")) ``` ::: {custom-style="Source Note"} Source: Northfjord Environmental Agency, station database extract of 31 January 2024. ::: # Method note {#sec-method} Annual means are computed from daily means $\bar{C}_d$, using only days with at least 18 valid hours: $$ \bar{C}_{\text{year}} = \frac{1}{|D|} \sum_{d \in D} \bar{C}_d, \qquad D = \{\, d : n_d \ge 18 \,\} $$ {#eq-annual-mean} Values below the detection limit were set to half the limit, as in previous reports \[see @nilu2022, sec. 2.3\]. The new PM~2.5~ monitors (NOK 1.2 million, roughly \$110 000) are funded from the 2024 budget; see the cost table in the Word version.
# References {.unnumbered} ::: {#refs} ::: * * * [^1]: Havnegata was moved 40 m north in August 2022, so values before and after the move are not strictly comparable. A sensitivity analysis that drops the first three months after the move changes the annual mean by less than 0.5 µg/m^3^. See Appendix B of the Word version for details. [^2]: All city buses on the Havnegata corridor have been battery-electric since October 2021 [@ruter2022]. [^3]: The previous maximum, 131 µg/m^3^, was recorded on 23 January 2010.

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# =============================================================================
# survey_weights.R
#
# Calibrated weights for the 2023 Residents' Survey.
# Translated from weights.sas (SAS 9.4) with sas2r 0.9.2 on 2023-11-20 and
# reviewed by hand. Run from the project root:
#
#   Rscript R/survey_weights.R data/raw/residents_2023.sas7bdat
# =============================================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(haven)
  library(survey)
  library(glue)
})

# fmt: markdown
# ## Provenance
#
# This script replaces `weights.sas`, last run by the *Survey Methods* team in
# 2022. The translation was produced by **sas2r 0.9.2** and then fixed by hand:
#
# 1. `PROC SURVEYSELECT` became `sample_strata()` in `R/sampling.R`
# 2. formats from `formats.sas7bcat` were rebuilt as factor levels
# 3. the raking step uses `survey::rake()` instead of the `%RAKE` macro
#
# Differences against the SAS output are listed in `validation/README.md`;
# all of them are below 0.1 percentage points.

args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
input_path <- if (length(args) >= 1) args[[1]] else "data/raw/residents_2023.sas7bdat"
output_dir <- Sys.getenv("WEIGHTS_OUTPUT_DIR", unset = "output")
trim_cap <- as.numeric(Sys.getenv("WEIGHTS_TRIM_CAP", unset = "5"))

#' Recode SAS formats to factor levels
#'
#' The SAS catalogue stored labels as formats (`AGEGRP.`, `REGION.`).
#' `haven` keeps them as labelled vectors, which this function turns into
#' factors with the same level order as the SAS formats.
#'
#' @param df A data frame returned by [haven::read_sas()].
#' @return `df` with lower-case names and `age_group`, `sex` and `region`
#'   as factors.
#' @noRd
recode_formats <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      age_group = factor(as_factor(AGEGRP), levels = c("16-24", "25-44", "45-64", "65+")),
      sex = factor(as_factor(SEX), levels = c("Female", "Male")),
      region = as_factor(REGION, levels = "labels"),
      # SAS stored missing interview dates as .A (not asked) and .R (refused)
      interview_date = as.Date(zap_missing(INTDATE), origin = "1960-01-01")
    ) %>%
    rename_with(tolower)
}

#' Trim extreme weights
#'
#' Caps weights at `cap` times the stratum median and redistributes the
#' excess proportionally within each stratum, mirroring the `%TRIMWT` macro.
#'
#' @param w Numeric vector of design weights.
#' @param strata Factor, or anything coercible to one, giving the stratum of
#'   each respondent.
#' @param cap Multiple of the median above which weights are trimmed.
#'   Defaults to `5`, as in the SAS macro.
#' @return A numeric vector the same length as `w`.
#' @examples
#' trim_weights(c(1, 2, 50), strata = c("a", "a", "a"), cap = 3)
#' @export
trim_weights <- function(w, strata, cap = 5) {
  stopifnot(is.numeric(w), length(w) == length(strata), cap > 1)
  strata <- as.factor(strata)
  out <- w
  for (s in levels(strata)) {
    idx <- which(strata == s)
    limit <- cap * stats::median(w[idx])
    excess <- sum(pmax(w[idx] - limit, 0))
    trimmed <- pmin(w[idx], limit)
    out[idx] <- trimmed + excess * trimmed / sum(trimmed)
  }
  out
}

#' Design effect due to weighting (Kish)
#'
#' @param w Numeric vector of weights.
#' @return A single number, `1 + CV^2` of the weights.
#' @export
kish_deff <- function(w) {
  n <- length(w)
  n * sum(w^2) / sum(w)^2
}

# --- Read and prepare ---------------------------------------------------------

raw <- read_sas(input_path, catalog_file = "data/raw/formats.sas7bcat")
resp <- raw |>
  recode_formats() |>
  filter(!is.na(age_group), !is.na(sex), !is.na(region)) |>
  mutate(
    design_wt = 1 / sel_prob,
    stratum = interaction(region, urban, drop = TRUE, sep = "/")
  )

# Census 2021 margins; same numbers as the CARDS datalines in weights.sas
pop_age <- data.frame(age_group = levels(resp$age_group), Freq = c(41210, 88730, 79120, 52940))
pop_sex <- data.frame(sex = c("Female", "Male"), Freq = c(133480, 128520))
pop_region <- read.csv("data/reference/census2021_region.csv")

# --- Calibrate ----------------------------------------------------------------

design <- svydesign(ids = ~psu, strata = ~stratum, weights = ~design_wt, data = resp, nest = TRUE)
raked <- rake(
  design,
  sample.margins = list(~age_group, ~sex, ~region),
  population.margins = list(pop_age, pop_sex, pop_region),
  control = list(maxit = 50, epsilon = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE)
)

resp$final_wt <- trim_weights(weights(raked), resp$stratum, cap = trim_cap)

deff_by_region <- resp |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(n = n(), deff = kish_deff(final_wt), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(flag = if_else(deff > 2, "check", ""))

# --- Report -------------------------------------------------------------------

# fmt: markdown
report_header <- "
# Weighting summary

The weights were calibrated to the **2021 census** margins for age group, sex
and region, then trimmed at {trim_cap} times the stratum median.

- Respondents: {nrow(resp)}
- Strata: {nlevels(resp$stratum)}
- Overall design effect: {round(kish_deff(resp$final_wt), 2)}

Regions with a design effect above 2 are marked *check* in the table below.
"

dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
writeLines(
  c(glue(report_header), knitr::kable(deff_by_region, digits = 2)),
  file.path(output_dir, "weighting_summary.md")
)

write_sas_compatible <- function(df, path) {
  # SAS 9.4 rejects variable names longer than 32 characters or with dots
  names(df) <- substr(gsub(r"([.\s]+)", "_", names(df)), 1, 32)
  write_xpt(df, path, version = 8)
}

write_sas_compatible(select(resp, respid, final_wt), file.path(output_dir, "weights.xpt"))
message(glue("Wrote {nrow(resp)} weights to {output_dir}"))

Halyard ======= [![Build Status](https://ci.halyard.example.org/buildStatus/icon?job=halyard%2Fmaster)](https://ci.halyard.example.org/job/halyard/job/master/) [![Coverage](https://img.shields.io/codecov/c/github/halyard-io/halyard/master.svg?style=flat-square)](https://codecov.io/gh/halyard-io/halyard) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/halyard-io/halyard?sort=semver)](https://github.com/halyard-io/halyard/releases) [![License: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) > **Note** > This page was migrated from the Trac wiki (`wiki:Halyard`) on 2019-08-12 by `trac2md.py`. Some links still point at the old wiki, which is now read-only at . Please fix them as you find them. Halyard is a small, dependency-free agent that tails log files, parses them into structured events and ships them to Elasticsearch, Loki or any HTTP endpoint. It was written to replace a fleet of hand-rolled `tail -F | nc` pipelines and now runs on roughly 4,000 hosts. [[PageOutline(2-3, Contents, inline)]] ## Table of Contents * [Overview](#overview) * [Installation](#installation) * [Binary packages](#binary-packages) * [From source](#from-source) * [Docker](#docker) * [Configuration](#configuration) * [Inputs](#inputs) * [Outputs](#outputs) * [Environment variables](#environment-variables) * [Platform support](#platform-support) * [Troubleshooting & FAQ](#troubleshooting--faq) * [License](#license) Overview -------- ``` /var/log/*.log --> [ tail ] --> [ parse ] --> [ buffer ] --> output(s) | +--> dead-letter file (on parse errors) ``` Halyard reads each file from the last committed offset, so restarting the agent never re-ships old lines. The buffer lives on disk (`/var/lib/halyard/buffer`) and survives reboots; see [[wiki:HalyardBuffering|Buffering]] for the gory details. ## Installation ### Binary packages Packages for Debian/Ubuntu and RHEL/Rocky are published for every release: ```sh curl -fsSL https://pkg.halyard.example.org/gpg.key | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/halyard.gpg echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/halyard.gpg] https://pkg.halyard.example.org/apt stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/halyard.list sudo apt update && sudo apt install halyard ``` ### From source You need Go 1.21 or newer. `make` builds `./bin/halyard`; `make install` copies it to `/usr/local/bin` and installs the systemd unit.
On macOS, use `gmake` – the BSD make that ships with Xcode does not understand our Makefile. ### Docker docker run -d --name halyard \ -v /var/log:/var/log:ro \ -v halyard-state:/var/lib/halyard \ -v $PWD/halyard.toml:/etc/halyard/halyard.toml:ro \ ghcr.io/halyard-io/halyard:2.6 ## Configuration Halyard reads `/etc/halyard/halyard.toml` (override with `-c`). The file has one `[[input]]` block per set of files and one or more `[[output]]` blocks. The full reference used to live at [[wiki:HalyardConfig|the configuration page]]; the tables below cover the options people actually use. ### Inputs | Option | Type | Default | Description | |--------|------|---------|-------------| | `path` | string | — | Glob of files to tail.
Supports `**` for recursive matching. | | `exclude` | list | `[]` | Globs to skip, e.g. `["*.gz", "*.1"]`. | | `format` | string | `raw` | `raw`, `json`, `logfmt` or `delimited:`, e.g. `delimited:\|`. | | `multiline.pattern` | regex | *none* | Lines matching this start a new event.
Example: `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}` | | `encoding` | string | `utf-8` | `utf-8`, `latin-1` or `utf-16le`.
Note: `utf-16le` needs 2.3 or newer. | | `rotate_wait` | duration | `5s` | How long to keep reading a file after it was rotated. | | `fields` | table | `{}` | Static fields added to every event,
e.g. `{ env = "prod" }`. | ### Outputs | Type | Required options | Notes | |:-----|:-----------------|:------| | `elasticsearch` | `hosts`, `index` | Uses the bulk API. `index` may contain `%{+yyyy.MM.dd}`. | | `loki` | `url`, `labels` | Labels must be low-cardinality!
**Never** use `host` *and* `path` together. | | `http` | `url` | POSTs newline-delimited JSON; retries on 429 and 5xx. | | `file` | `path` | For debugging only. | ### Environment variables Any option can be overridden with `HALYARD_
_

Using five entering cohorts (2019--2023, *N* = `r format(n_total, big.mark = ",")`), we compare `r format(n_mentored, big.mark = ",")` mentored students with matched peers who were not mentored. Retention was 6.1 percentage points higher among mentored students (95% CI 3.8--8.4), and the estimate is robust to the choice of matching method. The effect is larger for first-generation students, i.e. those whose parents did not attend university, than for other students. The programme costs approx. £310 per student per year. At current fee levels it pays for itself if ca. 1 in 25 mentored students would otherwise have left. Questions about this report can be sent to the IR team (ir-team\@uni.example.ac.uk) or posted in the \#ir-reports channel. # Background Research on early departure has long emphasised academic and social integration [@tinto1993]. Peer mentoring is one of the more common integration interventions, but evidence on its effect on retention is mixed: some studies report substantial effects [e.g. @crisp2009; @collings2014], while others find none once selection into the programme is accounted for [see @lunsford2017, pp. 12--15]. Students choose whether to join the PMP, and those who sign up differ systematically from those who do not (Table \@ref(tab:balance)). The programme was redesigned in autumn 2021. Mentors now meet their mentees weekly rather than fortnightly, and mentor training was extended from one day to three. We therefore also report effects separately for the cohorts before and after the redesign. As Okafor et al. (2022) put it, the redesign was meant to turn mentoring from “a welcome chat” into “a structured habit.” Whether it did so is one of the questions this report tries to answer. See Sect. \@ref(results) for the cohort-level estimates. # Data and methods ## Data Records were extracted from the student information system on 14 February 2024 at 09:00 (extract no. 4471). Students who withdrew before the census date (week 4) were excluded, as were students on programmes shorter than two years. Students with fewer than 60 credits attempted \[sic\] were retained, since part-time study is common in some faculties. Table \@ref(tab:cohorts) shows the resulting cohort sizes. | Cohort | Entrants | Mentored | Mentored (%) | |:-------|---------:|---------:|-------------:| | 2019 | 3,412 | 498 | 14.6 | | 2020 | 3,198 | 402 | 12.6 | | 2021 | 3,530 | 611 | 17.3 | | 2022 | 3,611 | 688 | 19.1 | | 2023 | 3,702 | 731 | 19.7 | Table: (\#tab:cohorts) Entrants and PMP participation by cohort. Figures for 2020 are affected by the move to online teaching. ## Matching We used nearest-neighbour propensity score matching with a caliper of 0.1 SD of the logit of the propensity score [@austin2011]. The propensity model includes entry tariff, age at entry, first-generation status, domicile (home vs. international), accommodation type and faculty. Exact matching was imposed on cohort and faculty.^[An alternative specification using coarsened exact matching gives very similar results; see Appendix B.] Balance after matching is shown in Table \@ref(tab:balance); all standardised mean differences are below 0.05. ```{r balance} m_out <- matchit( mentored ~ tariff + age_entry + first_gen + domicile + accommodation + faculty, data = cohort, method = "nearest", caliper = 0.1, exact = ~ cohort + faculty ) summary(m_out)$sum.matched[, c("Means Treated", "Means Control", "Std. Mean Diff.")] |> as.data.frame() |> rownames_to_column("Covariate") |> knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Covariate balance after matching.", booktabs = TRUE) ``` # Results Figure \@ref(fig:retention) shows second-year retention by cohort for mentored and matched non-mentored students. The gap is visible in every cohort but widens after the 2021 redesign. Dr. Okafor's team re-ran the analysis on the 2023 cohort alone (n = 1,462 after matching) and found an effect of 7.9 points.[^redesign] For first-generation students the estimate is 9.4 points (95% CI 5.1--13.7) vs. 4.2 points for other students. ```{r retention, fig.cap="Second-year retention by cohort and mentoring status (matched sample). They should not be read as causal without caveats. Matching only removes bias from observed covariates; motivation, for instance, is not measured and plausibly drives both sign-up and retention. A sensitivity analysis following @rosenbaum2002 suggests that an unobserved confounder would need to raise the odds of joining by a factor of 1.6 to explain away the effect. What does this mean for the programme? In our view, three things: 1. Keep the weekly meeting format introduced in 2021. 2. Target recruitment at first-generation students, who benefit most. Currently only 31% of them are mentored, vs. 18% of other students. 3. Collect a short motivation measure at enrolment, so that future evaluations can adjust for it. arguments.description: Generate DevOps-heavy corpus 14
arguments.prompt:
Create realistic YAML-heavy text documents for testing a YAML/Markdown formatter. Write them into /tmp/corpus14/q/ (create it). Do NOT run any formatter or other program on them; just write the files (Write tool or shell heredoc). Do not write anything outside /tmp/corpus14/.

Create 16 files, each 60-200 lines, all must be VALID YAML (spaces only for indentation):
1. ansible_playbook_1.yml — Ansible role-style playbook with `pre_tasks`, `roles`, `tasks`, `handlers`, `vars_files`, `become`, `tags`, `notify`, `loop` with `loop_control`, `register` + `until`/`retries`, `with_items`, `ansible.builtin.template` with `dest` and `mode: "0644"`, `lineinfile` with regexp containing backslashes in single quotes, `when:` with lists of conditions, `block`/`rescue`/`always`, multi-line `shell: >` and `command: |`.
2. ansible_playbook_2.yml — inventory-style vars plus a playbook with `hosts: "{{ target | default('all') }}"`, `delegate_to`, `run_once`, `set_fact` with Jinja filters, `uri` module with a JSON body as a YAML mapping, `assert` with `that:` list.
3. docker_compose_1.yml — compose with `x-` extension fields, YAML anchors and `<<: *anchor` merges, `deploy.resources.limits`, `healthcheck.test` as `["CMD-SHELL", "..."]`, `command: >` folded block, `environment:` with `${VAR:-default}` interpolation, `secrets:` and `configs:`, `ulimits`, `logging.options`.
4. docker_compose_2.yml — a dev-stack compose with 8 services, ports as quoted strings `"127.0.0.1:5432:5432"`, `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy`, `profiles`, `extra_hosts`, `labels` as list and as map, long `entrypoint` arrays.
5. github_workflow_1.yml — CI with `on: push/pull_request` with `branches-ignore`, `paths-ignore`, `env:` at workflow level, jobs with `needs`, `strategy.matrix` with `include` objects, `services:` (postgres with `options: >-` health flags), steps with `uses:` and `with:` including multi-line `script: |` for actions/github-script containing JavaScript, `if: ${{ always() && ... }}`, `continue-on-error`, `timeout-minutes`.
6. github_workflow_2.yml — release workflow on tags with `workflow_call` inputs/secrets, `permissions` mapping, `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`, artifact upload/download, a step with a long `run:` single-line command over 150 characters.
7. kubernetes_multi_document_1.yaml — 6 documents: Namespace, ServiceAccount, Role/RoleBinding, Deployment (initContainers, affinity with nodeSelectorTerms and matchExpressions, tolerations, topologySpreadConstraints, securityContext, resources, env with valueFrom.secretKeyRef, args list of flags), Service.
8. kubernetes_multi_document_2.yaml — CronJob, PodDisruptionBudget, NetworkPolicy with ingress/egress rules and ipBlock/except, Ingress with many annotations (some long), a ConfigMap with `data:` holding a `nginx.conf: |` block and a JSON file `settings.json: |`.
9. mkdocs_config_1.yml — Material for MkDocs: `theme.features` (15+ entries), `palette` list with media queries and toggle icons, `markdown_extensions` with many pymdownx extensions with options (including `pymdownx.emoji` with `emoji_index: !!python/name:material.extensions.emoji.twemoji` and `emoji_generator: !!python/name:material.extensions.emoji.to_svg`), `plugins` with options, `extra.social` list, deeply nested `nav`.
10. mkdocs_config_2.yml — a smaller mkdocs.yml with `!ENV [SITE_URL, 'http://localhost']` tags, `watch:`, `hooks:`, `validation:` options, `extra_css`/`extra_javascript` lists, `copyright` with HTML entity.
11. openapi_1.yaml — OpenAPI 3.0 with `servers` variables, `tags` with descriptions, `paths` with `get/post/put/delete`, `parameters` with `$ref`, `requestBody.content.application/json.schema` with `oneOf`, `responses` with `headers`, `components.schemas` with `required`, `enum`, `format`, `pattern` (regex in single quotes), `nullable`, `example` objects, `securitySchemes` with oauth2 flows and scopes.
12. openapi_2.yaml — OpenAPI 3.1 for a webhook-based API with `webhooks:`, `examples` with long string values, `description: |` blocks containing Markdown lists and tables, `x-codeSamples` with multi-line source code in `source: |` blocks.
13. config_values.yaml — a Helm values.yaml with deeply nested settings, many commented-out options (lines starting with `# ` inside mappings), empty maps `{}` and lists `[]`, resource quantities like `500m` and `256Mi`, booleans `true/false`, long annotation strings.
14. pipeline.gitlab-ci.yml — GitLab CI with `stages`, `variables`, anchors for job templates (`.template: &tmpl`), `extends`, `rules` with `if:` expressions, `script` lists with long commands, `artifacts.reports`, `cache.key.files`.
15. dependabot.yml — dependabot config with 5 ecosystems, `groups`, `ignore` with `update-types`, schedules.
16. pre-commit-config.yaml — `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with 10 repos, hooks with `args` flow lists, `additional_dependencies`, `exclude: ^(docs/|tests/fixtures/)` regex, `files:` patterns.

Use realistic names and values, include natural comments (end-of-line and full-line), some trailing spaces, inconsistent spacing after colons in a few places (`key:   value`), some lists indented under their key and some not (both styles are valid). UTF-8, LF line endings. Reply only with the list of files.

arguments.prompt:
Create realistic Markdown-family documents for testing a Markdown formatter. Write them into /tmp/corpus15/r/ (create it). Do NOT run any formatter or other program on them; just write the files (Write tool or shell heredoc). Do not write anything outside /tmp/corpus15/.

Create 16 files, 60-200 lines each:
1. readme_1.md — README of a popular CLI tool: centered logo HTML block, badges row, "Table of Contents" with nested links, Features list with emoji, Installation (Homebrew, Scoop, cargo, binaries table), Quick start with shell code blocks and output blocks, Configuration with a TOML code block and a table of options (long descriptions), FAQ using `<details>` blocks, Contributors section, License.
2. readme_2.md — README of a Python library: badges, short description, long paragraphs explaining concepts, code examples with `>>>` doctest style, an API overview table, "Comparison with alternatives" table with ✅/❌, citation BibTeX block, acknowledgements.
3. changelog_1.md — Keep a Changelog for a web framework: 10 releases with Added/Changed/Deprecated/Removed/Fixed/Security sections, entries with PR links, code spans, nested sub-bullets, a "Migration notes" paragraph in one release, link references at the bottom.
4. changelog_2.md — a changelog with prose-style release notes: each version heading followed by 1-3 paragraphs of text (long lines), then bullet lists, some "**Breaking:**" bold prefixes, occasional blockquote notes.
5. contributing_1.md — CONTRIBUTING for a monorepo: prerequisites table, setup steps with numbered lists and fenced code, branch naming rules, commit message convention with examples in a code block, PR checklist with task boxes, style guide subsections, release process with nested ordered lists.
6. contributing_2.md — a shorter community-oriented CONTRIBUTING with long paragraphs, a list of ways to contribute, links, a "Good first issues" section, code of conduct reference, and contact info.
7. quarto_report_1.qmd — Quarto HTML report: front matter with `format: html: toc: true, code-fold: true, theme: cosmo`, `execute: echo: false`, Python code cells (`{python}`) with `#| label:`, `#| fig-cap:`, a `::: {.callout-tip}` block, a `::: {.panel-tabset}` with 3 tabs (### headings), inline math and display math with label, a table with caption, footnotes, references section `::: {#refs}`.
8. quarto_report_2.qmd — Quarto presentation-like document (format: revealjs) with slides separated by `##` headings, speaker notes `::: {.notes}`, incremental lists `::: {.incremental}`, columns layout `:::: {.columns}` with `::: {.column width="50%"}`, code with line highlighting `{.r code-line-numbers="2-3"}`, images with attributes.
9. rmarkdown_sentence_wrap_1.Rmd — R Markdown article (front matter with `editor_options:` / `markdown:` / `wrap: sentence`, `bibliography`, `output: html_document: toc: true`), Introduction/Methods/Results/Discussion with multi-sentence paragraphs (some with one sentence per line already, others with long lines), abbreviations (e.g., i.e., et al., Fig., approx., vs.), numbers with decimals, citations [@key; @key2, p. 4], inline R `r round(x, 2)`, R chunks, a bulleted list, footnotes.
10. rmarkdown_sentence_wrap_2.Rmd — a teaching document (front matter as above + `output: learnr::tutorial`) with exercises, chunk options like `exercise=TRUE`, hints, questions in numbered lists, block quotes with tips, sentences ending with ? and !.

14. security.md — SECURITY.md with supported versions table, reporting instructions, PGP key block in a code fence, timeline list.
15. blog_post.md — a Hugo/Jekyll blog post with YAML front matter (title, date, tags list, categories, draft, description long string), long narrative paragraphs with emphasis, quotes, images, a code block, footnotes.
16. meeting_notes.md — meeting notes with date headings, attendee lists, action items as task lists with @mentions, decisions in bold, nested bullets 3 levels deep, a table of owners.

Create realistic YAML-heavy text documents for testing a YAML/Markdown formatter. Write them into /tmp/corpus14/q/ (create it). Do NOT run any formatter or other program on them; just write the files (Write tool or shell heredoc). Do not write anything outside /tmp/corpus14/.

Create 16 files, each 60-200 lines, all must be VALID YAML (spaces only for indentation):
1. ansible_playbook_1.yml — Ansible role-style playbook with `pre_tasks`, `roles`, `tasks`, `handlers`, `vars_files`, `become`, `tags`, `notify`, `loop` with `loop_control`, `register` + `until`/`retries`, `with_items`, `ansible.builtin.template` with `dest` and `mode: "0644"`, `lineinfile` with regexp containing backslashes in single quotes, `when:` with lists of conditions, `block`/`rescue`/`always`, multi-line `shell: >` and `command: |`.
2. ansible_playbook_2.yml — inventory-style vars plus a playbook with `hosts: "{{ target | default('all') }}"`, `delegate_to`, `run_once`, `set_fact` with Jinja filters, `uri` module with a JSON body as a YAML mapping, `assert` with `that:` list.
3. docker_compose_1.yml — compose with `x-` extension fields, YAML anchors and `<<: *anchor` merges, `deploy.resources.limits`, `healthcheck.test` as `["CMD-SHELL", "..."]`, `command: >` folded block, `environment:` with `${VAR:-default}` interpolation, `secrets:` and `configs:`, `ulimits`, `logging.options`.
4. docker_compose_2.yml — a dev-stack compose with 8 services, ports as quoted strings `"127.0.0.1:5432:5432"`, `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy`, `profiles`, `extra_hosts`, `labels` as list and as map, long `entrypoint` arrays.
5. github_workflow_1.yml — CI with `on: push/pull_request` with `branches-ignore`, `paths-ignore`, `env:` at workflow level, jobs with `needs`, `strategy.matrix` with `include` objects, `services:` (postgres with `options: >-` health flags), steps with `uses:` and `with:` including multi-line `script: |` for actions/github-script containing JavaScript, `if: ${{ always() && ... }}`, `continue-on-error`, `timeout-minutes`.
6. github_workflow_2.yml — release workflow on tags with `workflow_call` inputs/secrets, `permissions` mapping, `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`, artifact upload/download, a step with a long `run:` single-line command over 150 characters.
7. kubernetes_multi_document_1.yaml — 6 documents: Namespace, ServiceAccount, Role/RoleBinding, Deployment (initContainers, affinity with nodeSelectorTerms and matchExpressions, tolerations, topologySpreadConstraints, securityContext, resources, env with valueFrom.secretKeyRef, args list of flags), Service.
8. kubernetes_multi_document_2.yaml — CronJob, PodDisruptionBudget, NetworkPolicy with ingress/egress rules and ipBlock/except, Ingress with many annotations (some long), a ConfigMap with `data:` holding a `nginx.conf: |` block and a JSON file `settings.json: |`.
9. mkdocs_config_1.yml — Material for MkDocs: `theme.features` (15+ entries), `palette` list with media queries and toggle icons, `markdown_extensions` with many pymdownx extensions with options (including `pymdownx.emoji` with `emoji_index: !!python/name:material.extensions.emoji.twemoji` and `emoji_generator: !!python/name:material.extensions.emoji.to_svg`), `plugins` with options, `extra.social` list, deeply nested `nav`.
10. mkdocs_config_2.yml — a smaller mkdocs.yml with `!ENV [SITE_URL, 'http://localhost']` tags, `watch:`, `hooks:`, `validation:` options, `extra_css`/`extra_javascript` lists, `copyright` with HTML entity.
11. openapi_1.yaml — OpenAPI 3.0 with `servers` variables, `tags` with descriptions, `paths` with `get/post/put/delete`, `parameters` with `$ref`, `requestBody.content.application/json.schema` with `oneOf`, `responses` with `headers`, `components.schemas` with `required`, `enum`, `format`, `pattern` (regex in single quotes), `nullable`, `example` objects, `securitySchemes` with oauth2 flows and scopes.
12. openapi_2.yaml — OpenAPI 3.1 for a webhook-based API with `webhooks:`, `examples` with long string values, `description: |` blocks containing Markdown lists and tables, `x-codeSamples` with multi-line source code in `source: |` blocks.
13. config_values.yaml — a Helm values.yaml with deeply nested settings, many commented-out options (lines starting with `# ` inside mappings), empty maps `{}` and lists `[]`, resource quantities like `500m` and `256Mi`, booleans `true/false`, long annotation strings.
14. pipeline.gitlab-ci.yml — GitLab CI with `stages`, `variables`, anchors for job templates (`.template: &tmpl`), `extends`, `rules` with `if:` expressions, `script` lists with long commands, `artifacts.reports`, `cache.key.files`.
15. dependabot.yml — dependabot config with 5 ecosystems, `groups`, `ignore` with `update-types`, schedules.
16. pre-commit-config.yaml — `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with 10 repos, hooks with `args` flow lists, `additional_dependencies`, `exclude: ^(docs/|tests/fixtures/)` regex, `files:` patterns.
